cases.holding: A consumer challenging a finalized s.126 assessment, and the consequential disconnection and Tehsildar recovery, after the opportunity of personal hearing under Supply Code paragraph 6.8, has the statutory appeal to the Divisional Commissioner. If that appeal is filed in the manner prescribed, on payment of fees prescribed by the State Commission under s.82, it shall be decided on merits within six weeks. The writ was disposed of on that footing without examining the legality of the assessment or disconnection.

cases.title: Rajendra Nath Pal v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: unchallenged s.126 assessment; recovery certificate
cases.holding: A writ against a recovery certificate for alleged electricity theft will not be entertained where the Section 126 assessment order has not been challenged.

cases.title: Uttam Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: s.126 recovery withdrawn; fresh order after hearing
cases.holding: On the licensee's statement that the Section 126 recovery certificate dated 26.10.2023 and the final assessment had been withdrawn, the writ was disposed of with liberty to pass a fresh order after opportunity of hearing, strictly in accordance with the procedure prescribed under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2006.
cases.flag: Court referred to U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2006; the applicable Code is 2005.

cases.title: Ramrati v. State of U.P. and Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: provisional s.126 assessment — writ vs objection
cases.holding: A notice of provisional assessment under Section 126 of the Electricity Act, 2003 is not to be quashed in writ. The consumer may file an objection within two weeks; the Executive Engineer shall then decide it strictly in accordance with the procedure prescribed under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Praveen Kumar @ Praveen Chauhan v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: provisional assessment — prematurity of writ
cases.holding: A writ challenging a notice of provisional assessment is premature while the consumer's objections remain pending. The Assessment Officer, when passing the final assessment, shall follow the procedure under the Electricity Act and the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; until that order is passed, no coercive measure may be taken against the consumer on the basis of the provisional assessment.
cases.flag: Order cites 'the Act' and Electricity Supply Code, 2005 without numbering s.126 or a Code clause; keyed to EA2003::126 as the provisional/final assessment scheme.

cases.title: Sabir v. State of U.P. and Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: withdrawal of challenge to s.126/6.8 assessment
cases.holding: Counsel for the Electricity Department placed instructions that recovery was being made on an assessment dated 14.10.2018 passed under Section 126 of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Clause 6.8 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2006. On the petitioner's prayer to withdraw with liberty to assail that order, the writ was disposed of as withdrawn with that liberty. Validity of the assessment and the recovery was not decided.
cases.flag: order names Electricity Supply Code, 2006 (catalog key UP-2005::6.8)

cases.title: Mohammad Zubair v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: provisional-assessment-challenge-infructuous-after-final-assessment
cases.holding: Where a writ challenges a notice of provisional assessment dated 30 May 2024 under Section 126 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and Clauses 6.8 and 8.1 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and the licensee during pendency produces a final assessment order dated 31 August 2024, the challenge to the provisional notice is rendered infructuous. The petition is disposed of with liberty to challenge the final assessment, if aggrieved, in independent proceedings.

cases.title: No interference with Section 126 provisional assessment absent patent illegality
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: provisional assessment — writ interference
cases.holding: A writ court will not interfere with a notice of provisional assessment under Section 126 of the Electricity Act, 2003 in the absence of patent illegality or jurisdictional error. The consumer may file an objection, which the assessing officer must decide in accordance with the procedure prescribed under the Act and the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Pushpa Devi v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: writ against assessment notices — objection first
cases.holding: Where assessment notices had issued but the consumer had filed no objection and no assessment under Section 126 had yet been made, the High Court declined to entertain a writ to quash the notices. The petitioner was left to file an objection within two weeks, to be decided by the prescribed authority in accordance with Section 126 of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the notices remaining subject to the outcome of that proceeding.

cases.title: Smt. Ranjana Gupta v. Executive Engineer (Distribution), Asst. General Manager & Anr.
cases.topic: Two-stage hearing — UUE conclusion, then provisional assessment and quantum
cases.holding: The assessing officer must give a dual opportunity: first against unauthorised use of electricity; and, if not satisfied with the reply to that notice, a second opportunity by issuing a provisional assessment, with a further opportunity of objection, and then a final assessment, as explained in Ashok Kumar (paras 58-60) — a hearing before concluding unauthorised use (guilt) and a separate hearing on quantum. That procedure is to be completed within two months of production of a certified copy of this order.
cases.flag: Ashok Kumar's two-stage ratio (quoted from paras 58-60) is applied as s.126 procedure. The Court did not key the remand to Clause 6.8 or 8.1 of the 2005 Code, nor to Clause 6.17.2 of the 2002 Code (which the Appellate Committee had mentioned).

cases.title: Tejinder Singh v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Others
cases.topic: s.126 assessment must be at 1.5 times the applicable tariff, not thrice
cases.holding: No. Section 126(6), as quoted, requires assessment at a rate equal to one-and-half times the tariff applicable for the relevant category of services specified in subsection (5). The Executive Engineer's file showed the Rs. 9.28 lacs penalty computed on excess load at thrice that tariff. Counsel for the licensee admitted the overcharge. The orders dated 13.12.2004 and 12.05.2005 are set aside. The competent assessing authority must pass a fresh assessment applying the 1.5-times rate to the units assessed, and the petitioner is to pay that amount within one month.
cases.flag: Source PDF concatenates listing, substitution and adjournment orders (12.3.2013–13.11.2018); the operative judgment is 19.11.2018 (paras 1–7). Petitioner died; substitution allowed 7.7.2017. The assessment was said to be under s.126 r/w para 6.17.1 of the 2002 Code; the Court did not construe 6.17.1. Catalog hit UP-2002::6.17 is the Code vehicle pleaded, not a holding. Checking report of 24.11.2004 was challenged but not separately quashed. Keyed to catalog EA2003::126; the clause applied is 126(6).

cases.title: M/S Venus Stone Crushing Co. Thru' Partner & Another v. The U.P. Power Corpn. Ltd. Thru' Chairman & Others
cases.topic: s.126(6) 1.5-times tariff prevails over 2002-Code para 6.17.2 (thrice the units)
cases.holding: No. Following Sri Bhagwan Gupta, assessment in a theft case is to be at one-and-a-half times the tariff applicable under Section 126(6), not under paragraph 6.17.2 of the 2002 Code; Section 126(6) prevails over 6.17.2. Assessment here under 6.17.1 and 6.17.2 was held absolutely illegal. Those observations bind the restored appeal; the 24.12.2003 assessment itself was not quashed.
cases.flag: The judgment styles the statute 'U.P. Electricity Supply Act 2003'; recorded as stated. Catalog key EA2003::126; the clause applied is 126(6). Code vehicle is UP-2002::6.17 (6.17.2), not merged into the Act key. Catalog hits UP-2005::6.16 / 7.7 do not fit this 2002-Code assessment.

cases.title: M/S Mahavir Iron Foundry And Another v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. And Others
cases.topic: No designated assessing officer until the 27.6.2006 notification; 2005 inspection and assessment bad
cases.holding: No. Section 126(1) requires the assessing officer to be designated by the State Government. Paragraph 14 of the writ alleged that no such notification had issued; the counter did not show any designation and instead denied that no appellate authority had been constituted. The Court held that the assessing authority required to inspect had not been designated until Notification No. 173/2006-XXIV/P-3–27P/98,T.C dated 27 June 2006. The 12 September 2005 inspection and the assessments that followed could not stand.
cases.flag: Source PDF concatenates listing orders of 21.9.2022, 18.10.2022, 2.12.2022 and 9.12.2022 (judgment reserved) with the operative judgment of 28.4.2023 (Siddhartha Varma and Rajendra Kumar-IV, JJ.). Facts recite both 41.3 HP and 41.03 KW. Judgment OCR: 'Taz Trapezium Zone'.

cases.title: M/S Mahavir Iron Foundry And Another v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. And Others
cases.topic: Show-cause before provisional assessment; two-stage hearing (UUE conclusion, then quantum)
cases.holding: Yes. Following Ashok Kumar para 58, the assessing officer must, before making a provisional assessment, afford an opportunity on the allegation of unauthorised use and record a conclusion of unauthorised use, which confers jurisdiction to issue the provisional notice; a distinct opportunity is then required before final assessment on quantum. Kraipak is applied for the rule that natural justice supplements the statute. No show-cause was issued before the provisional assessment of 24 September 2005; that assessment was per se illegal. Independent witnesses were not present at the 12 September 2005 inspection, and the licensee had itself been raising minimum-consumption bills, so illegal use could not be presumed. The writ is allowed. The Court takes no action against the department because the matter is old. Allowing the writ does not preclude further action after giving an opportunity.
cases.flag: Petitioner invoked Clauses 8.1 and 8.2 of the 2005 Code; the Court did not cite a numbered Code clause and applied s.126 through Ashok Kumar and Kraipak. Not keyed to UP-2005::8.1.

cases.title: Akhalak Ahmad v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitaran Nigam Ltd. Thru' G.M. & Others
cases.topic: Non-supply of the 16.12.2003 survey vitiates proceeding on the provisional assessment; the report must be supplied and objections heard
cases.holding: Yes, on the narrow compass of natural justice. The checking was on 16.12.2003; the 2005 Code was not then in vogue. The petitioner's case was that the checking/survey report was never served, yet the Appellate Committee dismissed his appeal solely on that report. The Court directed the licensee to supply a copy of the survey report; the petitioner has three weeks thereafter to object to the provisional assessment. The appellate order (15.2.2005, served 22.6.2005) is quashed. The provisional assessment remains subject to the fresh decision.
cases.flag: Source PDF concatenates a 6.9.2014 listing order (Sunita Agarwal, J.) with this 22.1.2020 disposal. The challenge is first described as Appellate Committee dated 22.6.2005 and later as Appellate Order dated 15.2.2005 served through letter dated 22.6.2005; recorded as the judgment states it.

cases.title: Uco Bank v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.topic: Direct pole supply on a landlord's common-meter arrangement is unauthorised use assessable under section 126
cases.holding: Yes. The Court found there was admittedly unauthorised use of electrical energy. The respondents were therefore entitled to assess under section 126 read with Clause 6.8 of the Supply Code. The procedure for that assessment is Clause 6.8.

cases.title: Smt. Kalpana Agarwal v. Managing Director, Western Electricity & Others
cases.topic: Two-stage hearing: UUE conclusion then quantum, before a valid s.126 assessment
cases.holding: Yes. Following Ashok Kumar paras 56–64, a conclusion of unauthorised use under Section 126(1) is the condition precedent to a provisional assessment. Natural justice is not excluded; opportunity is required first on whether the consumer used electricity unauthorisedly (which confers jurisdiction to assess) and again on quantum before the final assessment under Section 126(3). A suo motu conclusion without that opportunity is arbitrary and would infringe Article 14. The 02.11.2007 demand, issued without that procedure, cannot sustain.

cases.title: Smt. Amna Khatoon v. PVVNL & Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: Writ court will not examine the validity of a Section 126(4) provisional assessment
cases.holding: No. Once a provisional assessment has been issued (here dated 7.3.2008, pursuant to an earlier Division Bench direction in W.P. No. 43872 of 2007), its validity cannot be gone into in writ. The consumer may file objections within 15 days; the respondents must then proceed in accordance with law to a final order. The 407-versus-180-day period is a question of calculation the writ court cannot go into.
cases.flag: Source PDF concatenates listing and substitution orders of 2.4.2010, 9.4.2010 and 4.8.2010 with the 6.12.2010 disposal. Paragraph numbers are of the disposing order. The Supreme Court SLP that vacated the 27.3.2008 stay is unnamed.

cases.title: M/S Sri Dauji Cold Storage Pvt Ltd And Another v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd And Others
cases.topic: s.126(6) as on 1.11.2004 caps assessment at 1.5 times the tariff, not three times
cases.holding: No. On 1.11.2004, the date of surprise inspection, Section 126(6) provided assessment at 1.5 times the normal tariff, not three times. The 15.6.2007 amendment raising the statutory multiple to twice did not govern that checking date. Following Vijay Pal Singh, and as licensee's counsel could not dispute, the Executive Engineer's 29.3.2008 demand at three times is illegal. That order is quashed and the writ allowed.
cases.flag: Source PDF concatenates stay-vacation, listing, dismissal for non-prosecution (22.9.2011) and restoration (31.1.2012) orders from 8.2.2010 to 6.12.2018; the operative judgment is 13.12.2018 (unnumbered). Checking on 1.11.2004 pre-dates the 2005 Code; the Court's own ratio is the unamended s.126(6) rate on that date. Catalog hits UP-2005::4.5(d), 6.12 and 8.2(x) do not fit.

cases.title: Raj Kumar v. KESCO and Others
cases.topic: Unamended s.126(6) 1.5-times tariff, not thrice, governs a 26.10.2004 theft/UUE assessment
cases.holding: At one-and-a-half times under Section 126(6) as it stood at the relevant time. The petitioner was assessed at thrice the per-unit tariff under Clause 6.17.2 of the 2002 Code. That could not be the applicable rate; the case is covered by unamended Section 126(6), making the assessment and the 29.3.2005 appellate dismissal vulnerable in law. The writ is allowed. Those orders are quashed. Respondent no. 2 (the assessing authority) is to re-determine the amount in the light of that holding and issue a fresh demand, if any, after adjusting deposits.
cases.flag: Para 6 quotes the later 'twice' text of s.126(6); para 7 applies 'one and half times' as the section stood at the 26.10.2004 inspection. Catalog key EA2003::126; the clause applied is 126(6). Paras 2–3 challenge a demand dated 5.12.2007; para 13 quashes orders dated 29.3.2005 and 5.10.2007. Recorded as the judgment states them.

cases.title: M/S Mayur Sheetgrah Pvt. Ltd. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. And Others
cases.topic: Statutory appeal is no bar where the theft assessment is in breach of natural justice
cases.holding: No. The licensee pressed a statutory appeal. The Court held it well established that, on a violation of natural justice, the petitioner cannot be compelled to avail the statutory remedy, and applied Whirlpool Corporation v. Registrar of Trade Marks (the three contingencies: fundamental rights, natural justice, want of jurisdiction or vires).
cases.flag: The Court described the appeal as 'under section 126 of the Act of filing appeal'. The appeal against a section 126 assessment is section 127; not silently corrected. The 4.2.2009 order in WP 6130 of 2009 had treated the then-pending objections as under section 126(3).

cases.title: Shabbir v. State of U.P. — recovery citation stayed on deposit; writ dismissed for default
cases.topic: provisional assessment and recovery citation
cases.holding: The Court recorded the petitioner's plea that no provisional assessment under section 126 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and paragraph 6.8(b)(i) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 had been served and that recovery had been started without opportunity to object; it stayed recovery pursuant to the citation dated 12 January 2010 subject to deposit of Rs 90,000 within four weeks, the stay to vacate automatically on default. The writ was later dismissed for want of prosecution, without a decision on that plea.

cases.title: Writ against provisional s.126 bill dismissed; vires of s.126 and cl.8.1/6.8 rejected
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: provisional assessment — writ and vires
cases.holding: A writ petition challenging a provisional assessment bill founded on a checking report, and the vires of s.126 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and clauses 8.1 and 6.8 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 vis-à-vis Article 14, is not to be entertained where the consumer has been noticed to file objections to the report and to the quantum of charges. The consumer must respond to that notice and pursue objections as advised and permissible in law. The vires challenge to s.126 and clauses 8.1 and 6.8 fails for want of any sustainable submission.

cases.title: Devi Lal @ Tutti Lal v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.topic: final assessment as precondition to recovery
cases.holding: A demand under Section 126(1) is a provisional assessment and must be served on the person found to have unauthorisedly consumed electricity. Section 126 confers a right to object; if objections are filed, the Executive Engineer must pass a final order, appealable under Section 127. Even if no objections are filed, a final assessment is still required after the officer satisfies himself from the record that the provisional assessment was served. Recovery cannot proceed on a provisional assessment alone. The 29 April 2010 Executive Engineer order did not show itself to be a final assessment and none was produced, so the citation dated 1 March 2012 was kept in abeyance, with a week to object and a Section 127 appeal if the objection is rejected.

cases.title: Ajay Kumar Jaiswal v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.topic: s.126 provisional assessment — commercial classification of Business Correspondent use
cases.holding: Without deciding whether a bank Business Correspondent’s village room is a commercial establishment, the Court directed that objections to the s.126(1) provisional assessment be decided by the Executive Engineer, and if still aggrieved the consumer may appeal under s.127. The assessing officer and the appellate authority must give reasons supporting any commercial-basis assessment and refer to the relevant provisions of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, keeping in mind the micro-banking nature of the work. Recovery was stayed for three months while that statutory course is exhausted.

cases.title: Executive Engineer, Kanpur Electricity Supply Co. (KESCO) v. Presiding Officer, Consumer Grievances Redressal Forum & Anr.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: CGRF jurisdiction where the complaint is billing after permanent disconnection, not s.126 assessment
cases.holding: Section 126 and the CGRF bar on assessment complaints do not prima facie oust the Forum where the grievance is billing after a permanent disconnection and there is no dispute of recorded consumption. The writ attacking the Forum's Clause 4.38 six-month post-PD billing cap was later dismissed for want of prosecution and the 2013 interim stay of the Rs.1,38,928 demand vacated.

EA2003::126(3).topic: Personal hearing is part of 'reasonable opportunity' before a final theft assessment

cases.title: Hazi Mohd. Yaseen v. P.V.V.N.L. & Another
cases.topic: Personal hearing is part of 'reasonable opportunity' before a final theft assessment
cases.holding: It requires a personal hearing. Merely taking note of written objections is not compliance; because supply (an essential service) has been disconnected and the theft charge carries penal consequences, a personal hearing is essential before a final assessment. The ex parte final assessment is quashed and remitted for a fresh reasoned order after personal hearing, conditioned on the consumer depositing 50% of the claim (25% cash + 25% security).

cases.title: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Appellate Authority/Addl. Commissioner & Anr. (Sunita Spat Pvt. Ltd.)
cases.topic: A final assessment order that has attained finality cannot be re-opened by the assessing authority except, under inherent authority, in cases of fraud or misrepresentation and after hearing
cases.holding: No. Assessment under Section 126 has two stages - a provisional assessment (Section 126(2)) and a final assessment to be made within thirty days of service of the provisional order (Section 126(3)), the mode of the order being declared by Section 126(5). Once a final order of assessment of the charges payable has been passed and has attained finality, there is no provision empowering the assessing authority to re-open it. This principle is subject only to the inherent authority to revive the assessment where fraud or misrepresentation is detected, and then only after affording an opportunity of hearing.

cases.title: Dinesh Kumar Gupta v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: Provisional and final assessment cannot be made simultaneously; a 'final' assessment made without an objection opportunity is treated as provisional
cases.holding: No. The respondents admitted in their counter affidavit that the provisional and final assessments were the same. The Court held that after making a provisional assessment the authorities are liable to issue notice to the petitioner/meter-holder to file objection, if any; a simultaneous provisional-cum-final assessment denies that opportunity. It therefore treated the impugned final order of assessment as a provisional assessment and permitted the petitioner to file objections within four weeks, to be dealt with by respondent no.2 by a final decision within a further month, the recovery citation dated 25.11.2011 to remain in abeyance for two months or till that final decision, which it is to abide.

cases.title: Vinod Kumar Agarwal v. State of U.P. And Others
cases.topic: A recovery citation under the U.P. Government Electricity Undertaking (Recovery of Dues) Act, 1958 for theft/unauthorised-use dues cannot be issued unless a final assessment order has first been passed under s.126(3) of the Electricity Act, 2003 (following Clause 6.8 of the Supply Code), after giving the consumer a reasonable opportunity of hearing on the provisional assessment (whether or not objections were filed)
cases.holding: The Court directed the Managing Director of U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. to issue strict instructions to all distribution corporations and Executive Engineers to comply with s.126 of the Electricity Act, 2003, and not to issue any recovery certificate unless and until a final assessment has been made after giving the consumer opportunity to object under s.126(1) — with s.126(3) requiring, even where no objection is filed, a recorded finding that the provisional assessment was duly served, followed by a reasoned final assessment order; where objections are filed, they must be considered before the final assessment and recovery certificate issue. The Court directed withdrawal of recoveries already issued without a final assessment, to be reissued only after a proper final assessment, and directed a compliance report to the Court. The Chairman & Managing Director's compliance affidavit (order dated 30.6.2012) accordingly directed all Corporations/Executive Engineers to follow s.126 and Clause 6.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, withdraw non-compliant recoveries forthwith (to be re-finalised within three months), and warned that non-compliant officers would face departmental action; the Court accepted this compliance and expected future adherence. In the underlying case, the petitioner's own provisional assessment was withdrawn, a final assessment order passed after considering his objections, and the connection reconnected, rendering the writ petition infructuous, with the petitioner permitted an appeal under s.127 and directed to complete the interim 50% deposit (adjusted for amounts already recovered), and with a direction that recovery-collection charges not be borne by the State where recoveries are withdrawn for Corporation non-compliance.

cases.title: Mohd. Sagir v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.topic: Reasonable opportunity of hearing before a final assessment
cases.holding: A final assessment order passed without affording a reasonable opportunity of hearing violates s.126(3) and natural justice and is liable to be set aside on that ground alone. Here the consumer's objection of 11/9/2009 was never decided, his request on 29/9/2009 for time (even short of the 15 days sought) was refused, and the one-month period contemplated by s.126(3) had not expired when the final order of 30/9/2009 was passed.

cases.title: Sarafraj v. Mandhyanchal Viduit Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: objection to provisional assessment
cases.holding: A writ against a provisional assessment notice issued on alleged theft of electricity is not decided on merits when the consumer has a remedy of filing an objection under Section 126(3) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with clause 6.8(b) of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the petition is disposed of with liberty to file that objection before the appropriate authority.

cases.title: Smt. Ranjana Gupta v. Executive Engineer (Distribution), Asst. General Manager & Anr.
cases.topic: Theft bill and s.3 demand without show-cause, provisional or final assessment
cases.holding: No. The 22 September 2003 bill and demand directing deposit of Rs. 7,48,560 were issued without any show-cause on the theft allegation and without a provisional or final assessment, in violation of Section 126(3). They are quashed.
cases.flag: Source PDF concatenates listing, restoration (14.5.2014), amendment (9.7.2018) and other interlocutory orders from 26.3.2014 to 17.4.2019; the operative judgment is 24.4.2019 (Siddharth, J.). The 2003 events predate the 2005 Code; the petitioner had appealed under Clause 7.20 of the 2002 Code. The Court applied s.126(3) of the 2003 Act, not a numbered 2002 or 2005 Code clause.

cases.title: Shamsul Qamar v. PVVNL and Others
cases.topic: Section 126(3) objections cannot be insisted on until the laboratory testing report is supplied
cases.holding: No. The counter affidavit did not deny the non-testing and non-supply of the report, and said only that the petitioner might object under section 126(3). Unless the meter-testing report is provided, the consumer cannot file those objections. Relegation to section 126(3) therefore does not sustain the bill.

cases.title: Raj Kumar v. KESCO and Others
cases.topic: Want of service of provisional assessment and opportunity to object cannot be raised for the first time in writ
cases.holding: No. The petitioner had not raised denial of opportunity to object to the provisional assessment before the assessing officer or in the appeal. The plea involves investigation of facts. The Court declined to entertain it for the first time in the writ petition and rejected that contention.
cases.flag: Source PDF concatenates listing and presence orders of 10.12.2012 (Sanjay Misra, J.), 6.9.2013 and 18.9.2013 (Pradeep Kumar Singh Baghel, J.); the operative judgment is 30.9.2013 (paras 1–13, Pankaj Naqvi, J.).

cases.title: Final s.126(3) assessment mandatory before recovery; notice-footer insufficient
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: final assessment before recovery; deemed-final notice
cases.holding: A note appended to a s.126(3) notice that if no reply is received the notice shall be treated as the final assessment does not serve s.126(3). The Executive Engineer must record whether the notice was served and, if objections have been filed, consider them; in either case a final assessment order must be passed before recovery of the assessed amount under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Where no final assessment had been made, the writ was disposed with a direction to pass a final order after considering the petitioner's objections dated 7.6.2011; recovery only after that order, which remains appealable.

cases.title: Triloki Mishra v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: final assessment before recovery of theft dues
cases.holding: Demand and citation to recover theft-assessment dues, including recovery charges and compounding, cannot proceed where the licensee has not shown service of the provisional assessment and has not made a final assessment under section 126(3). Compounding charges are payable only if the consumer admits the offence and cannot be recovered as arrears of land revenue. Treating the provisional order as served in Court, the consumer may file objections within 15 days, after which the licensee may pass a final assessment under section 126(3) subject to appeal under section 127.

cases.title: Shiv Baboo Yadav @ Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.topic: final assessment as precondition to recovery
cases.holding: A licensee cannot recover a theft-case electricity demand, including by citation under the U.P. Electricity Undertaking (Recovery of Dues) Act, 1958, unless the provisional assessment has been served and a final assessment has been made under section 126(3) after objections, which then carries a right of appeal under section 127. Compounding charges are to be deposited only if the consumer admits the offence and cannot be recovered as arrears of land revenue. The Court quashed the recovery, treated the provisional order as served in Court, and directed objections within 15 days, leaving the respondents free to pass a final assessment.

EA2003::126(5).topic: Assessment period — entire period of unauthorised use, or 12 months if unascertainable

cases.title: Hazi Mohd. Yaseen v. P.V.V.N.L. & Another
cases.topic: Assessment period — entire period of unauthorised use, or 12 months if unascertainable
cases.holding: Section 126(5) has two parts: assessment for the entire period during which unauthorised use took place, or, if that period cannot be ascertained, a period limited to twelve months preceding inspection. Whether the period (here 407 days) was properly ascertained is a factual question for the assessing/appellate authority.

EA2003::127.code: Electricity Act, 2003 (transition from U.P. Supply (Consumers) Regulations 1984 / U.P. Supply Code 2002)
EA2003::127.topic: Scope of the Section 127 appeal — confined to Section 126 orders; transitional assessments

cases.title: Aruna Bhargava v. PuVVNL & Another
cases.topic: Scope of the Section 127 appeal — confined to Section 126 orders; transitional assessments
cases.holding: No. Section 127(1) confines the appeal to a final order 'made under Section 126' of the 2003 Act; a pre-2003 assessment is not such an order, so neither Section 127 nor its pre-deposit condition applies. Section 185(2) & (5) (with Section 6 of the General Clauses Act) preserve the pre-2003 assessment and its appellate forum. The Commissioner's rejection under s.127(2) was without jurisdiction; the appeal is remitted to the forum under Regulations 1984 / Code 2002.
cases.flag: Multi-regime transitional case: it construes the pre-2005 U.P. regime (Regulations 1984 and U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2002), not the 2005 Code.

cases.title: Kapil Gupta v. U.P. Power Corpn. Ltd. & Anr.
cases.topic: Writ relegated to the statutory appeal where only factual disputes arise
cases.holding: Relegated to the appeal. Where the challenge to a Section 126 assessment raises only disputed questions of fact and no question of jurisdiction, vires, or breach of natural justice/fundamental rights, the writ court will not bypass the Section 127 appeal; the earlier decision on merits in this consumer's case turned on a four-year pendency, not any absolute rule, and Ashok Kumar (vires/jurisdiction) is distinguishable.

cases.title: Executive Engineer, Southern Electricity Supply Co. of Orissa Ltd. (SOUTHCO) v. Sri Seetaram Rice Mill
cases.topic: Sections 126-127 form a complete code; only a final Section 126(3) order is appealable; the High Court should not ordinarily interfere with a final assessment
cases.holding: Sections 126 and 127 together constitute a complete code. Only a final order of assessment under Section 126(3) is appealable under Section 127; a notice-cum-provisional assessment under Section 126(2) is not appealable. The High Court should normally decline to interfere under Article 226 with a final assessment — it may examine a jurisdictional challenge but must not travel into the assessing officer's exclusive domain of assessment and fact-finding.

cases.title: Lalit Kumar Kapoor v. Kanpur Electricity Supply Company & Anr.
cases.topic: Challenge to a final theft assessment relegated to the statutory appeal; pre-deposit not relaxed
cases.holding: Whether inspection or provisional assessment was properly made, and whether reasonable opportunity was given, are matters merged into the earlier writ proceeding that directed consideration of the representation (itself equivalent to the provisional stage) and cannot be reopened by a fresh writ against the final assessment; the final assessment must be challenged before the appellate authority under Section 127, and in a theft matter — given the public interest in the essential service of electricity — the Court will not relax the statutory deposit condition to enable the petitioner to avoid it.

cases.title: M/S Om Ice Factory Thru' Its Partner Satyapal Singh v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Anr.
cases.topic: Where an assessment challenge is purely factual/procedural (objections already considered) and raises no jurisdictional or vires issue, the writ is relegated to the s.127 appeal
cases.holding: The petitioner must be relegated to the Section 127 appeal. None of the three recognised exceptions to the alternative-remedy rule (want of jurisdiction, breach of natural justice, violation of fundamental rights) was made out: the assessing authority had already considered the petitioner's objections as directed in an earlier writ (disposed of 6.8.2013) and taken a decision not shown to be dehors the law or established procedure; mere allegation of a factual/procedural flaw in that decision does not permit bypassing the statutory remedy. Ashok Kumar is distinguishable since it involved a pure legal/jurisdictional challenge (validity of the notification appointing the assessing officer) that neither the assessing officer nor the appellate authority could decide — here, by contrast, only the correctness of the provisional assessment on facts was at issue. The governing precedent is Southco v. Sri Seetaram Rice Mill: the High Court may examine a jurisdictional challenge to a provisional assessment but must remand rather than decide the assessment itself, and should normally decline to interfere with a final assessment under Article 226.

cases.title: M/S Trikoot Iron & Steels Castings Ltd. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.topic: A theft-based assessment is made under Section 126 (via Clause 8.1-8.3 of the Code), not Section 135, and is always appealable under Section 127
cases.holding: An appeal always lies. Section 135 creates the criminal offence of theft but no independent assessment mechanism; its third proviso to sub-section (1A) (requiring restoration of supply on deposit of the 'assessed amount') itself presupposes that the assessment is made under Section 126. The Supply Code merely prescribes distinct procedures — para 8.1-8.3 for theft-based assessments, para 6.8 for other unauthorised use — but both are Section 126 assessments; the appeal lies under Section 127 in either case. Since Section 127 provides no separate parameters for deciding the appeal, the Appellate Authority's power is co-extensive with the Assessing Officer's, empowering it to examine on the merits whether the assessment (theft or otherwise) was correctly made. The Appellate Authority's rejection of the appeal on the ground that a theft-based assessment falls under Section 135 (and is hence non-appealable) was a jurisdictional error; the matter was remanded for decision on merits.

cases.title: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Appellate Authority/Addl. Commissioner & Anr. (Sunita Spat Pvt. Ltd.)
cases.topic: The appellate authority's power under Section 127 is co-extensive with the assessing authority's; it is competent to decide whether the case is one of theft, and a reasonable finding is not disturbed in writ
cases.holding: Yes, the appellate authority is competent. Section 127(1) provides an appeal against the final order made under Section 126 but prescribes no parameters for deciding it; the authority of the appellate forum is therefore co-extensive with that of the assessing authority. The appellate authority is free to decide whether the assessment was correctly made and whether the case is one of unauthorised use covering theft - the inevitable conclusion being that it is competent to go into the question of theft (assessable on the parameter in paragraph 8.1 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005) as against mere unauthorised use (paragraph 6.8) for judging the validity of the Section 126 assessment. Here the appellate authority examined the matter, found the meter tampered but, keeping in mind the mark in column 8, the meter not having been sent to the test laboratory and other circumstances, held it was not a case of theft; that view is not arbitrary or unreasonable, and the Court declined to interfere in judicial review merely because a second view was possible.

cases.title: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Appellate Authority/Addl. Commissioner & Anr. (Sunita Spat Pvt. Ltd.)
cases.topic: An appeal under Section 127 lies only against a final order; a revised provisional assessment during the appeal, on which no final order was passed, is not appealable and does not render the appeal infructuous
cases.holding: No. Even though the revised provisional assessment was made during the pendency of the appeal and the consumer filed no reply, a final order ought still to have been passed in black and white; in the absence of any final order the consumer was under no obligation to amend the memo of appeal, because an appeal under Section 127 is maintainable only against final orders and not against a provisional order. The pending appeal against the earlier final assessment therefore did not become infructuous, and the licensee's contention that the appellate authority should have declined to decide it on merits fails.

cases.title: Smt. Vimla Tiwari v. State of U.P. And Others
cases.topic: A s.127 appellate order is vitiated where the Commissioner (Appellate Authority) mechanically defers entirely to the Superintending Engineer's technical assessment without independently applying his own mind to the record, undermining the structural purpose of a statutory appeal
cases.holding: No. The Court critiqued the structural functioning of the s.127 Appellate Authority as constituted, observing that the Commissioner routinely defers wholesale to the Superintending Engineer on technical questions without independent application of mind, which defeats the object of a genuine, independent appellate review distinct from the original assessment. On the facts, the appellate order simply affirmed the assessment without meaningfully grappling with the checking report's internal inconsistencies, and was accordingly quashed along with the assessment order.
cases.paras: paras critiquing s.127 Appellate Authority's independence

cases.title: M/s Hind Industries Limited v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: Writ not entertained where the assessee bypassed the Section 127 appeal and the Area Level Committee
cases.holding: No. The appellant neither approached the Superintending Engineer nor the appellate authority under Section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003 after its enforcement, and did not approach the Area Level Committee; instead it kept the matter pending for nine years. A preliminary objection that the writ was liable to be dismissed for the statutory alternative remedy of appeal available under the Electricity Code was upheld, the learned Single Judge finding the grossest abuse of the process of the Court and relegating the appellant to the Area Level Committee. The Division Bench affirmed and dismissed the special appeal as being without merit.
cases.flag: Order-sheet: 38 pages, no printed page numbers or numbered paragraphs; pins are order dates. The reasoned disposal is the Division Bench order of 8.10.2013, which reproduces the learned Single Judge's order of 12.10.2011; the preceding pages are interim listing/stay-extension orders (2011-2013).

cases.title: M/s Hind Industries Limited v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: Interest at 16% per annum compounded every six months on the assessed amount
cases.holding: Section 127(6) of the Electricity Act, 2003 specifically provides for interest at 16% per annum compounded every six months on the assessed amount. Whether there was any provision for charging interest under the pre-2003 law was left to be raised before the appellate authority, and the applicability of the 2003 Act and the rate of interest were left open to the competent authority. Payment of interest is a necessary corollary to the retention of the amount and is neither penal nor confiscatory, following the Division Bench in Wig Brothers.

cases.title: Abdul Gaffar @ G. Hussian v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: Absent a Final Assessment Order under Section 126, the assessee is prima facie deprived of the Section 127 appeal
cases.holding: The Court treated the point as arguable. Section 127 provides for an appeal against the Final Order made under Section 126, and the petitioner contended that, no Final Assessment Order having been passed, he was deprived of his right of filing an appeal under Section 127. The Court held the matter required consideration, issued notice and granted interim protection against recovery, but did not finally decide the question, the petition being dismissed as infructuous on 2.2.2017.

cases.title: Ashok Kumar Ajmera v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: Final assessment order passed on a theft assessment: assessee relegated to the Section 127 appeal with all grounds open
cases.holding: Relegated to the appeal. The petitioner was found to be unauthorisedly drawing electricity even after disconnection, on which a theft case was registered and a final assessment order was passed on 24.10.2008. The petitioner has a right to file an appeal under Section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and to raise all the grounds raised in the writ petition, including his plea that the connection stood deemed disconnected so that no liability could be fastened on him. On the Hindustan Petroleum affidavit, the liability for the dues from the demand notice dated 25.11.2010 and the citation dated 11.12.2010 was upon the petitioner. The writ petition was accordingly dismissed with liberty to file a Section 127 appeal within one month, to be decided on merits, the appellate authority taking into account the Rs.1,25,000 deposited under the interim order.
cases.flag: Order-sheet: 25 pages, no printed page numbers or numbered paragraphs; pins are order dates. One interim order (25.7.2011) is in Hindi. The interim stay is of 26.4.2011 (Satya Poot Mehrotra and Rajesh Chandra, JJ.); the operative merits disposal is the 6.7.2012 order (Sunil Ambwani and Aditya Nath Mittal, JJ.).

cases.title: Ram Charan v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: Assessee relegated to the Section 127 appeal, to be decided on merits with limitation not examined
cases.holding: The remedy is a statutory appeal under Section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003. The Court disposed of the writ directing the petitioner to file a Section 127 appeal within four weeks; if so filed, the appeal would be decided by the appellate authority on merits, and that authority would not go into the question of limitation, so that the delay in resorting to the statutory remedy would not defeat the appeal.

cases.title: M/s Mayur Sheetgrah Pvt. Ltd. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: writ barred by section 127 appeal against theft assessment
cases.holding: Article 226 interference was refused against a theft assessment, including alleged illegal interest under Supply Code clause 6.8(e)(b) and section 127(6), because the same objections could be raised in the statutory appeal under section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003; the petitioner was directed to file that appeal as already ordered on 11 August 2014.

cases.title: Santosh Kumar Yadav v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: writ maintainability against final assessment
cases.holding: A writ petition challenging a final assessment order of the Executive Engineer will not be entertained when a statutory appeal under Section 127 is available; the petition is dismissed on that preliminary objection.
cases.flag: The Bench attributed Section 127 to the 'Electricity Supply Code, 2003'; the appeal lies under Section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003.

cases.title: Rajendra Prasad Yadav v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: writ barred by section 127 appeal against final assessment
cases.holding: A writ petition challenging a final assessment order of the Executive Engineer will not be entertained when a statutory appeal under Section 127 is available; the petition is dismissed on that alternative remedy.
cases.flag: Order attributes s.127 to the Electricity Supply Code, 2003; the provision is Electricity Act, 2003 s.127.

cases.title: Girish Kumar Agarwal v. State of U.P. — electricity recovery certificate
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: writ — alternative remedy if theft or unauthorised use
cases.holding: If the demand is an assessment on account of theft or unauthorised use of electricity, the statutory remedy is an appeal under Section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003; the writ is dismissed on the ground of that alternative remedy as well.

cases.title: Rajesh Kumar v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-quantum-alternate-remedy
cases.holding: Where the petitioner is not satisfied with the quantum of a bill issued by the electricity department, the remedies are an appeal under Section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003 or an objection under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the writ petition is dismissed with liberty to pursue those remedies.

cases.title: Mohd. Moobin @ Mohd. Muein v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: writ-bar-after-final-assessment
cases.holding: Where a final assessment has been made, the assessed amount remains unpaid, and the consumer has not preferred an appeal under Section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003, the High Court will not restore supply or decide pending applications in writ. The petition is dismissed without prejudice to remedies under the Act read with the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Mohd. Sagir v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.topic: Alternative statutory appeal as a bar to writ jurisdiction
cases.holding: The existence of a s.127 appeal against a s.126 final assessment does not bar a writ petition where the order is assailed for violation of natural justice; the rule of exhaustion is one of policy and discretion, not law. The Court also declined to relegate the petitioner because the writ had been entertained, an interim order passed, and it had been pending for about five years.

cases.title: Chotu Service And Washing Center v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: final assessment — relegation to statutory appeal
cases.holding: Once a final assessment has been passed, the consumer's remedy is the statutory appeal under Section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the High Court will not interfere in writ.

cases.title: Dayal Singh Kushwaha v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: alternate-remedy-section-127-appeal-bars-writ
cases.holding: Once a final assessment has been made by the Executive Engineer, a statutory alternative remedy of appeal is available under Section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003, read with the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and the High Court will not interfere in writ jurisdiction.

cases.title: Jai Laxmi Cement Company Ltd. v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.topic: Writ against a provisional assessment normally declined; only the final s.126(3) order is appealable
cases.holding: A provisional assessment under s.126(2) is not appealable under s.127 — only a final order under s.126(3) is — and the High Court should normally decline to interfere with a provisional assessment under Article 226, exercising jurisdiction only within the Whirlpool exceptions (a jurisdictional challenge, vires, or natural-justice breach). This case fell in none of those exceptions, so it was not fit to be entertained at the provisional stage; the petitioner's remedy is to file objections.

cases.title: Parmarth Steels & Alloys (Pvt.) Ltd. & Anr. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. (Transco) & Others
cases.topic: Alternative remedy is self-imposed discipline; not a bar after long pendency and completed pleadings
cases.holding: The s.127 appeal does not bar the writ. The bar of alternative remedy is a self-imposed discipline, a matter of discretion not jurisdiction; where the writ was entertained, pleadings exchanged, an interim order granted, and it remained pending over five years, it is not fit to be dismissed on that ground and should be decided on merits.

cases.title: Namepal v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: writ relegation to billing dispute or s.127 appeal
cases.holding: A writ against recovery of electricity dues on an alleged theft assessment is not decided on merits. The consumer's remedy is a billing-dispute application before the Executive Engineer or, if a final assessment has been made, an appeal under section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003 (styled in the order as the U.P. Electricity Act, 2003), read with the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If those forums are approached within fifteen days, the authority shall pass appropriate orders in accordance with law.

cases.title: Kamil v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.topic: Alternative remedy no bar where assessment breaches natural justice
cases.holding: The s.127 appeal does not bar the writ: an order passed in violation of natural justice is an established exception to the alternative-remedy rule (Whirlpool), and the writ had in any event been entertained with a conditional interim order and remained pending for six years. The petitioner was not relegated to the appeal.

cases.title: Jainullah v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: assessment-appeal-bars-writ
cases.holding: If the consumer questions an assessment already made after an allegation of theft, the remedy is an appeal under section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003; a writ seeking correction of that amount will not be entertained, without prejudice to that appeal being dealt with in accordance with law.

cases.title: Madan Pal v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: writ-against-final-assessment-relegated-to-s127-appeal
cases.holding: After inspection, a provisional assessment, and a final assessment, the High Court will not entertain a writ assailing that assessment: the consumer has a statutory alternative remedy of appeal under Section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003, and the petition is dismissed without examining the merits of the challenge.

cases.title: Munna Lal v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: appeal against final assessment; writ and recovery
cases.holding: The final assessment may be assailed by appeal under section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003 (styled in the order as the U.P. Electricity Act, 2003). The Court declined to interfere with consequential recovery. If an appeal is filed or any orders are passed, recovery shall abide the appellate order. The writ petition was consigned to records.

cases.title: Ashok Kumar Awasthi v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: residual appeal after assessing officer's order
cases.holding: If the consumer remains aggrieved after the assessing officer's order on the objections, it is open to file an appeal before the appropriate forum under Section 127 of the U.P. Electricity Act, 2003.

cases.title: Shyam Kumar v. Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitaran Nigam Ltd.
cases.topic: alternate-remedy-section-127-appeal
cases.holding: A writ petition challenging a final electricity assessment is not maintainable where a provisional assessment was in fact made, notice of hearing for the final assessment was given, and the consumer has not exhausted the statutory appeal under Section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with clause 6.8 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
cases.flag: The Court said the s.127/cl.6.8 appeal lay against the provisional assessment. Section 127 appeal lies against the final assessment; this petition challenged the final order dated 23.05.2018.

cases.title: Merino Industries Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: writ-maintainability-alternative-remedy
cases.holding: Where the licensee contends that a writ challenging a demand notice (and seeking a speaking order under the Supply Code, 2005 and consideration of rooftop-solar net-metering applications) is not maintainable because an appeal under s.127 lies, and the consumer does not dispute that alternative remedy, the writ is dismissed on the ground of alternative remedy without deciding the demand or the solar applications.
cases.flag: Order attributes the s.127 appeal to the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the statutory appeal is Electricity Act, 2003 s.127.

cases.title: Mahboob Ahmad v. Commissioner, Moradabad & Another
cases.topic: No writ re-examination of the quantum reduced by the s.127 appellate authority
cases.holding: No. The appellate authority having examined the assessment and reduced it from Rs. 73,920 to Rs. 17,520, the Court was not inclined to interfere with the quantum. The petition was disposed of allowing the consumer three months to deposit the reduced amount and directing regular bill payment.

cases.title: Abdul Ajij v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.topic: Whether a Code-prescribed deposit satisfies the s.127(2) pre-deposit — reserved
cases.holding: Not decided. The appeal had been rejected below for non-deposit of half the assessed amount under s.127(2); the petitioner claimed to have deposited the Code-prescribed amount. The Court merely listed the matter and directed affidavits, expressing no view on the point.
cases.flag: Listing/interlocutory order only — the s.127(2) pre-deposit question is reserved.

cases.title: Vikas Gupta & Another v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.topic: Disputed service of notice is for the s.127 appeal; instalments via Clause 6.14
cases.holding: The disputed question of service of notice depends on facts more appropriately dealt with in a s.127 appeal against the final assessments; and instalments, if desired, are for the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.14. Given these alternative remedies, the writ was dismissed with liberty to avail them.

cases.title: M/s Paliwal Alloys (Pvt.) Ltd. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Ors.
cases.topic: Recovery of a theft assessment cannot proceed while the s.127 appeal is pending under a restraint
cases.holding: The Corporation could not recover the theft assessment (Rs. 84,33,146) while the consumer's s.127 appeal — permitted by an earlier Division Bench (3.8.2006) on a Rs. 10 lakh deposit, with recovery restrained until the appeal was disposed of — was pending, the Corporation's SLP having obtained no interim stay. It ought instead to have pursued early disposal of the appeal.
cases.flag: The order of 19.11.2008 in the Corporation's special appeal did not direct recovery; it only called for details of liability.

cases.title: Moolchand Saini v. State of U.P. through Secretary, Power Corporation & Others
cases.topic: Consumer relegated to the s.127 statutory appeal against a final s.126 assessment order
cases.holding: No, ordinarily not. Section 126 provides for provisional assessment, objections and a final order after hearing; Section 127(1) gives any person aggrieved by the final order a right of appeal, and Clause 6.8 of the Code likewise provides for an appeal against the final assessment. Having regard to the nature of the controversy the Court accepted the licensee's preliminary objection and dismissed the writ petition on the ground of the availability of that alternative remedy, without deciding the merits.

cases.title: Ishwar Chandra v. U.P. Power Corporation Limited Thru' its M.D. & Another
cases.topic: Factual dispute over whether the objection was filed/considered is for the s.127 appeal, not Article 226
cases.holding: Relegate to the s.127 appeal. Whether the consumer filed an objection and whether it was considered is a disputed question of fact not amenable to Article 226. The Electricity Act, 2003 and the Supply Code, 2005 are a self-contained scheme with a remedy of appeal under s.127 against the final assessment; every contention raised in the writ can be raised in that appeal. The writ was disposed of on the ground of alternative remedy, leaving the consumer free to pursue it.

cases.title: Gopali v. State of U.P. through Secretary and others
cases.topic: Writ against a final s.126 assessment declined where the s.127 appeal is available and the dispute is factual
cases.holding: No. Section 126 provides for provisional assessment, objections and a final order after hearing; Section 127(1) gives a right of appeal against the final order, and Clause 6.8 likewise provides for an appeal. As the controversy was basically factual and better decided in appeal, the Court accepted the preliminary objection and dismissed the writ on the ground of the available alternative remedy.

cases.title: M/S Kamakhya Steels Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.topic: A Section 127 appellate order that brushes aside the grounds of appeal and affirms by reference to the checking report alone is sans reasons and unsustainable
cases.holding: No. Several grounds were raised in appeal questioning the conversion of 'possibility of theft' into a theft finding; the appellate authority brushed them aside, referred only to the checking and summary reports, and dismissed the appeal as devoid of merit. That order is sans reasons and unsustainable. Once the final assessment is itself held bad, an appellate order affirming it without discussing the grounds of appeal is also rendered irrelevant. The appellate order (Appeal No. 17 of 2007-08) and the consequential recovery order dated 09.04.2012 were quashed along with the assessment.

cases.title: Pradeep Singh v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: unmetered-energisation-versus-theft-is-disputed-fact-relegated-to-s.127
cases.holding: Whether the connection was energised on 4 September 2024 as the Connection Energisation Certificate states, or only after installation of the meter, is a disputed question of fact that cannot be adjudicated in writ jurisdiction. The petitioner is relegated to the statutory appeal under Section 127(1). If the appeal is filed within one month, the appellate authority shall decide it preferably within two months of filing, without entering into limitation. No coercive steps on the 28 March 2026 demand for four months from this order or until the appeal is decided, whichever is earlier, subject to the pre-deposit under Section 127.

cases.title: Saurabh Agarwal v. State of U.P. And 3 Others
cases.topic: Writ against a court-directed final s.126 assessment declined; consumer relegated to s.127 appeal
cases.holding: No. The 24 April 2025 order in Writ C No. 10132 of 2025 had, in place of a Section 127 appeal, directed a representation to the assessing authority, a 25% deposit, a hearing, and a reasoned order to be treated as the final assessment. That representation was rejected by the Executive Engineer's order dated 7 March 2026. The Court held that a statutory appeal under Section 127 to the Divisional Commissioner remained available and that the petition was liable to be dismissed on that ground. It disposed of the writ directing the petitioner to file that appeal within three weeks with a bank draft of Rs. 10 lakhs in addition to the 25% already deposited; the appellate authority is to consider and decide it expeditiously, preferably within two months of receipt; and no coercive action is to be taken on the impugned order until the appeal is disposed of.
cases.flag: The Court cited only Section 127, not a Supply Code clause (6.8 or 8.1). The extracted 2025 order referred to Section 126 'read with the Electricity Supply Code' without a numbered clause. Two paragraphs are numbered 3. Para 7's 'If it is so' conditions the two-month appellate timeline on filing the appeal with the Rs. 10 lakh draft. The statutory 50% pre-deposit under s.127(2) was not construed; the Court specified Rs. 10 lakhs plus the existing 25%.

cases.title: Gauri Prasad v. State of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Deptt. of Energy, Lko. & 4 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad (Lucknow Bench)
cases.topic: misaddressed appeal must be redirected; consumer directed to file a fresh appeal; recovery stayed
cases.holding: The licensee may not sit on it. Even if the representation/appeal dated 17.02.2026 was not before the appropriate authority, it was for the Electricity Department either to inform the petitioner or to re-direct it to the Appellate Authority; that was not done. Without entering into the merits, the Court directed the petitioner to prefer a fresh appeal before the competent authority within ten days. If such an appeal is preferred, the Appellate Authority shall consider and decide it after hearing, within a further four weeks. Recovery is stayed for six weeks or until the decision on the appeal, whichever is earlier. The Appellate Authority is to decide strictly in accordance with law.
cases.flag: The Court did not cite Section 127 by number. The direction is to a fresh appeal before the 'competent'/'Appellate' Authority. Petitioner's earlier representation (Annexure 6) was addressed to the Chief Engineer.

cases.title: Saurabh Agarwal v. State of U.P. And 3 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: Unused s.127 appeal (50% deposit) not treated as a bar; representation route with 25% deposit substituted
cases.holding: No such relegation was ordered. The Court recorded that the petitioner had approached it without going in appeal under Section 127, the reason cited being that a deposit of 50% of the amount was required. It did not send him to that appeal. It stayed the impugned order and demand for a limited period and substituted a fresh representation to the assessing authority, with a 25% deposit of the demand-notice amount, a hearing, and a reasoned order to be treated as the final assessment.
cases.flag: The Court cited Section 127 only as the unused statutory appeal. It did not decide whether that appeal was available or whether the 50% deposit justified bypassing it as a matter of law.

cases.title: M/S Chakradhari Cold Storage Pvt. Ltd. v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited And Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: Revised assessment by the Executive Engineer (Distribution) left to appeal without pre-deposit, with hearing and a reasoned order
cases.holding: Writ-C No. 59151 of 2007 is allowed only to the extent of granting liberty to appeal against the revised assessment order dated 3 September 2007 and the revised assessment bill dated 1 September 2007 within four weeks, without payment of any pre-deposit, a substantial amount having already been deposited. The authorities are to grant an opportunity of hearing and thereafter pass a reasoned order in accordance with law within eight weeks of filing of the appeal.
cases.flag: Keyed to s.127 as the statutory appeal against a final assessment. The Court said only 'file appeal'.

cases.title: Satyam Shukla v. State of U.P. and 3 Others
cases.topic: Writ against a provisional assessment on inspection infirmity; remand, not merits
cases.holding: No, not on this challenge. Following Seetaram Rice Mill, a Section 127 appeal lies only against a final Section 126 assessment; a provisional assessment is not appealable. The High Court may entertain a writ on an infirmity going to the root of the process, then remand; it must not decide the merits of the demand. The Court entertained the writ despite delay and the unused objection, hearing, and Section 127 path, because the sole ground urged was that the assessing officer had not inspected.

cases.title: M/S R.D. Ice & Cold Storage (P) Ltd. v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited And Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: Revised ex-parte assessment by the Executive Engineer (Distribution) left to appeal without pre-deposit, with hearing and a reasoned order
cases.holding: Writ-C No. 55908 of 2007 is allowed only to the extent of granting liberty to appeal against the revised assessment order dated 3 September 2007 and the revised assessment bill dated 1 September 2007 within four weeks, without payment of any pre-deposit, a substantial amount having already been deposited. The authorities are to grant an opportunity of hearing and thereafter pass a reasoned order in accordance with law within eight weeks of filing of the appeal.
cases.flag: Keyed to s.127 as the statutory appeal against a final assessment. The Court said only 'file appeal'. The 2007 order is described as ex-parte; the Court did not quash it on that ground.

cases.title: Keshari Nandan Rai v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.topic: writ vs s.127 appeal against s.126 assessment
cases.holding: A writ petition challenging a final assessment under s.126 of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 will not be examined on merits where the statutory appeal under s.127 is available and is not disputed; the petitioner is relegated to that alternative remedy.

cases.title: Smt. Ranjana Gupta v. Executive Engineer (Distribution), Asst. General Manager & Anr.
cases.topic: Appellate Committee cannot decide a s.127 appeal on an unauthorised counsel concession of theft
cases.holding: No. The 12 December 2003 order neither adjudicated the merits nor recorded any finding on the checking report or the assessment. The alleged concession does not appear in the body of the order; only the operative portion recites it. The petitioner disputes having authorised any such admission. Following Himalayan Coop. Group Housing Society, a doubtful or unauthorised concession, and a concession on a matter of law or one that surrenders substantial rights against the client's interest, does not bind the client; the Committee should have been cautious before accepting it. The appellate order is quashed.

cases.title: M/S Venus Stone Crushing Co. Thru' Partner & Another v. The U.P. Power Corpn. Ltd. Thru' Chairman & Others
cases.topic: Non-speaking statutory appeal is not an order in the eye of law; restored for a reasoned decision
cases.holding: No. The appellate authority performs judicial functions; after noting the arguments it must give reasons for accepting or rejecting them. The 7.7.2005 order (Annexure 14) contained neither discussion nor analysis of the grounds in the memorandum of appeal (Annexure 12) and is not an order in the eye of law. It is quashed. The appeal is restored to be decided afresh in accordance with law and in the light of the Court's observations, within two months of production of a certified copy. Recovery of the disputed dues remains stayed until that decision. The Court did not decide the merits of the 24.12.2003 order. On 20.8.2010 the direction was modified, without objection, so that the Divisional Commissioner, Jhansi, decides the restored appeal under the State notification dated 14.7.2006; records are to be transmitted within three weeks and the appeal decided within four weeks thereafter.
cases.flag: Source PDF concatenates listing/adjournment orders (18.8.2009–29.1.2010), the operative judgment of 23.2.2010, a modification of 20.8.2010, and a correction of 26.10.2010. The first writ (No. 10148 of 2004) was dismissed on 3.5.2005 for an appeal under paragraphs 17 and 19 of the 2002 Code. The 20.8.2010 modification recites a notification 'for the purpose of appeal under Section 197'; there is no s.197 in the 2003 Act — recorded as stated, not corrected. Keyed to catalog EA2003::127 as the statutory appeal later assigned to the Divisional Commissioner.

cases.title: M/S Mahavir Iron Foundry And Another v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. And Others
cases.topic: Writ maintainable despite s.127 where natural justice is extremely violated
cases.holding: No. The licensee argued that the High Court need not interfere because the consumer had not appealed under Section 127. Because there was an extreme violation of natural justice, the writ was maintainable and the petitioner was not to be relegated to the alternative remedy.

cases.title: Abdul Shakoor v. Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Ltd. And Others
cases.topic: Review of a writ dismissed for alternative remedy does not reopen Clause 8.2(h); appeal to the Commissioner remains, delay not a bar
cases.holding: Review refused. The 27.9.2011 writ was not dismissed on the petitioner's Clause 8.2(h) / acquittal point but because an appeal to the appellate authority was available. That is not a good ground for review. The petitioner still has the remedy of approaching the Commissioner. If an appeal is filed it shall not be rejected for delay, the petitioner having earlier approached a wrong forum, and it may be decided within two months of filing. The review petition was dismissed.
cases.flag: Source PDF concatenates expedite, listing, and review-notice orders (30.7.2010–10.5.2013) with the operative review of 11.7.2013. Petitioner cited 'Section 8.2(h)'; other corpus cases treat this as Clause 8.2(X)(h). Recorded as stated. Catalog key EA2003::127 for the Commissioner appeal; Clause 8.2(h) was raised but not decided.

cases.title: M/S Sijaria Ice Gramodhyog Sultanpura & Others v. State Of U.P. & Others
cases.topic: Non-speaking s.127 appeal is not an order in the eye of law; restored for a reasoned decision
cases.holding: No. The appellate authority, conferred appellate powers under a statute, performs judicial functions. After noting the arguments it must give reasons for accepting or rejecting them; an order with no process of reasoning is not an order in the eye of law. The 5.10.2007 order (Annexure-7) merely referred to the facts, reiterated the assessing authority's recitals, and dismissed Appeal No. 03/2006-07 because the inspection team had found unauthorised consumption. It did not advert to any of the thirteen grounds, including non-supply of the inspection report and denial of hearing. It is quashed. The appeal is restored to the Commissioner, Jhansi Division, to be decided afresh in accordance with law after hearing all concerned, within six weeks of production of a certified copy. Recovery of electricity dues remains stayed until that decision. The Court declined to decide the merits of the 23.02.2007 assessment.
cases.flag: The reasoning block is OCR-truncated at two sentence starts ('t is clear…'; 's the orders…'); recorded as the extract states them. Same judge and remand pattern as SCJ-640.

cases.title: Smt. Amna Khatoon v. PVVNL & Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: After the final assessment, the consumer's remedy is a Section 127 appeal
cases.holding: The earlier Division Bench in W.P. No. 43872 of 2007 had directed a provisional assessment under Section 126(4), objections, a final order, and then an appeal under Section 127 if aggrieved. This Court followed that path: it would not examine the provisional assessment in writ; after objections and the final order, the statutory appeal under Section 127 is the remedy.

cases.title: Satish Kumar Sharma v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: s.127 appeal against theft assessment
cases.holding: A final theft assessment and the Section 127 appellate order dismissing the consumer's appeal, if not consistent with the procedure required by Ashok Kumar and the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 (adequate show-cause and a speaking assessment), are liable to be quashed on writ, with remand to the Assessing Authority for a fresh order in accordance with law.

cases.title: Dr. Nirmal Kumar v. PVVNL
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: statutory appeal as alternative to writ against assessment
cases.holding: A writ challenging rejection of a representation against an electricity assessment will not be entertained where Section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003 gives a statutory appeal; issues including alleged non-consideration of U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 Clauses 6.8 and 8.1 and want of opportunity can be raised in that appeal. Counsel stated an appeal would be filed within three weeks; the Court directed that if an appeal is filed within three days it shall be considered on merits in accordance with law. The writ petition was dismissed.

cases.title: Dhirendra Pratap Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: statutory appeal as alternative remedy
cases.holding: A writ challenging such assessment and recovery is dismissed on the ground of alternative remedy; remaining grievance is to be raised in the statutory appeal under section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003.

cases.title: Sunder Lal Chaubey v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: s.127 appeal after EE decides theft-assessment objections
cases.holding: Once the Executive Engineer has decided objections to a theft-case assessment, the consumer’s remedy is an appeal under Section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003; a writ will be disposed of on that footing, with a direction that an appeal filed within 15 days shall be decided on merits expeditiously.

cases.title: Ramesh Chandra Gupta v. Kanpur Electricity Supply Company Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: alternate remedy against theft assessment
cases.holding: A writ petition challenging an Executive Engineer's order recording theft of electricity and raising an assessment will not be examined on merits; the consumer must proceed under Section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003 or before the appropriate forum under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Rajendra Kumar Gupta v. DVVNL
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: writ vs s.127 appeal from s.126(3) assessment
cases.holding: Where a consumer challenges a Section 126(3) assessment on disputed facts—no hearing; whether the case is unauthorised use or a defective-meter dispute under Supply Code clause 5.6(c)(iii); whether the meter should have been independently tested—the writ is not decided on merits. Availability of an alternative remedy depends on the circumstances of each case; those factual disputes are to be raised in a Section 127 appeal. The appellate authority does not lack jurisdiction. The petitioner is directed to appeal within seven days of obtaining a certified copy; if appealed, the authority shall hear all objections with a reasoned order preferably within one month, treating the writ petition and annexures as part of the appeal, and decide on merits.
cases.flag: Court cites s.126(3) as Electricity Act, 2003 and also as 2006, s.127 as Electricity Act, 2005, and refers to the 'U.P. Electricity Act, 2005'.

cases.title: M/s Shri Satguru Metalloys (Pvt.) Ltd. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: writ not entertained against final assessment when s.127 appeal available
cases.holding: Where a consumer challenges a detailed final assessment by writ, the High Court will not enter the facts or merits if a statutory appeal under section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003 is available. The petitioner was left to that appeal, with liberty to seek any document or report needed to file it (to be given within one week) and to request the competent authority for reconnection treatment similar to any concession already extended; the Court expressed no opinion on that disputed fact.

cases.title: M/s Avadh Alloys (Pvt.) Ltd. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: statutory appeal bars writ against final assessment
cases.holding: Where the consumer has a statutory appeal under section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003, the High Court will not entertain a writ against a final assessment on merits, including alleged want of adverse findings in checking and police reports, non-supply of documents for the reply, or a plea that the proceedings ought to have been dropped under paragraph 8.1.(G) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Those issues require entering into facts and belong in the appeal. Documents needed to file the appeal shall be given within one week; no direction is issued on reconnection against a lesser deposit.

cases.title: M/s Vehlna Steel & Alloys (Pvt.) Ltd. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.topic: statutory appeal bars writ against final assessment
cases.holding: A writ challenging a final assessment will not be entertained on merits when a statutory appeal lies under Section 127. The Electricity Act, 2003 is a self-contained code; the appellate authority has ample jurisdiction to consider all aspects, so the appeal is an efficacious remedy. The petitioner’s argument that no appeal lies against an assessment under Section 135 was rejected where the Corporation itself submitted that a Section 127 appeal was available.
