cases.title: Vinod Kumar Singh v. State of U.P. & 2 Ors.
cases.topic: Relisting of a criminal revision/appeal petition before the appropriate court after counsel confirmed the matter had not become infructuous
cases.holding: "Learned counsel for the petitioner states that the matter has not become infructuous. List in the next cause list before the appropriate court. Till the next date of listing, interim order, if any, shall continue." No facts or legal determination beyond this are recorded.
cases.flag: Bare procedural relisting order with no substantive content; recorded only for corpus completeness per this project's master-citation-ledger convention.

cases.title: Vinod Kumar v. State of U.P. & Another
cases.topic: Adjournment of an application for early listing of a second bail application, pending preparation of the paper book
cases.holding: "Learned counsel for the applicant states that the applicant/appellant is suffering for illness. Learned AGA shall seek necessary instructions... The paper book is stated to have not been prepared till date. List this matter after two weeks." No facts or legal determination beyond this are recorded.
cases.flag: Bare procedural adjournment order with no substantive content; recorded only for corpus completeness per this project's master-citation-ledger convention.

cases.title: M/s Ganga Devi Pyare Lal v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: withdrawal with liberty to competent authority
cases.holding: The writ was dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to approach the competent authority under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Outstanding bills and payments were not decided.

cases.title: Sanjeev Kumar v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: withdrawal of writ challenging recovery
cases.holding: After the licensee placed instructions on a May 2017 consumption dispute, the writ challenging recovery was dismissed as withdrawn, with liberty to file a proper petition if the law so permits in accordance with Ashok Kumar and the Electricity Act / U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The consumption and recovery dispute was not decided on merits.

cases.title: Consortium of Societies Ghaziabad v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: interlocutory listing of Clause 4.9 vires challenge
cases.holding: On a writ challenging Clause 4.9 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 (Thirteenth Amendment, 2018) as ultra vires for providing multiple-point supply, the Court issued notice and held that the matter required consideration. A later bench permitted the petitioners to apply to the competent authority for extension of time under Clause 4.9; subsequent listings extended the stay. Validity of Clause 4.9 was not decided.

cases.title: Kanpur Logistics Park Pvt. Ltd. v. Executive Engineer, Electricity Urban Distribution Division, KESCO
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: interim stay of HV-1 recategorisation arrears
cases.holding: The challenge to KESCO's 23.11.2018 order recategorising the consumer from HV-2 to HV-1 and raising 2012 arrears requires consideration. Effect and operation of that order are stayed until further orders; the licensee shall not insist on deposit of arrears of Rs.34,74,876.59 in the bill dated 16.12.2017 or interest thereon, provided the petitioners continue to deposit current electricity dues at Tariff HV-2.

cases.title: DVVNL v. Swati Kumari — PLA billing jurisdiction (notice)
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: PLA jurisdiction over billing — notice
cases.holding: The writ is entertained solely to examine whether the Permanent Lok Adalat had jurisdiction to entertain a billing dispute in view of Section 50 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and Clause 7(10) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The matter requires consideration; notice is issued; no merits determination is made.

cases.title: Vijay Kumar Agrawal v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: interlocutory stay of recovery citation
cases.holding: On the licensee's request for time to obtain instructions on the plea that a recovery citation issued without deciding clause 6.5 objections was illegal, the Court listed the writ and directed that no coercive steps be taken against the petitioner, later continuing that stay until further orders.

cases.title: Nagendra Singh Gautam & 2 Others v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.topic: Detachment of companion writ; listing; which connection-charge rate pending proof of notice
cases.holding: Writ C No. 27437 of 2025 cannot be tagged with this Division Bench petition because it is before the learned Single Judge; it is detached and to be placed before that Judge in the usual course. The supply company is to demonstrate that it informed the petitioners of the connection charge after 4 February 2024 and before February 2025. If it does, the petitioners are liable for the enhanced rate; on omission, they can be asked to pay only the earlier rate. Listed 3 July 2026 as fresh. No clause of the Supply Code was identified or construed.
cases.flag: Listing/interlocutory only. Counsel relied on a provision of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 but could not point it out from the 2025 publication; no clause applied. The Court's 4 February 2024 notice window is as stated in the order.

cases.title: M/s K.L. Concast Pvt. Ltd. v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: Notice on vires challenge; listing
cases.holding: Because the writ challenges the vires of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, notice for appearance is to go to the Advocate General of Uttar Pradesh, not the Attorney General of India (the 6 April 2011 notice to the Attorney General was inadvertent). An affidavit of deposits made under that order is to be filed, State respondents may object, and the petition is listed for the week commencing 17 August 2026.
cases.flag: interlocutory listing; no construction of the Supply Code

cases.title: M/s K.K. Duplex and Paper Mills Pvt. Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: listing; default of counter-affidavit
cases.holding: No decision on the vires challenge. The Court recorded that despite four weeks granted on 27.11.2025, no counter affidavit had been filed in a 2014 petition challenging Clauses 4.6 (h) (i) and 4.21 (a) of the 2005 Supply Code and Chapter 4 of the Cost Data Book, directed the Principal Secretary, Energy, Lucknow to appear and explain the twelve-year default, and listed the matter on 18.08.2026.
cases.flag: order cites Clauses 4.6 (h) (i); whether 4.6(h) and 4.6(i) or 4.6(h)(i) is unclear

cases.title: Vasnav Devi Aatta Chakki v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: listing
cases.holding: The Division Bench granted the licensee time to obtain instructions and listed the writ on 26.02.2026. No finding was recorded on the demand, the alleged absence of a criminal case or provisional assessment notice, or Supply Code 2005 compliance.

cases.title: Muzammil @ Meenu And 9 Others v. State Of U.P. And 4 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: FIR quash listing — alleged electricity misuse as BNS offences
cases.holding: The Court recorded that the petitioners had made out a case requiring consideration, issued notice to respondent no. 4, and directed counter and rejoinder affidavits. Arrest was stayed till the next date of listing or till submission of the police report, whichever is earlier. No finding was recorded on whether the FIR should be quashed or whether alleged electricity misuse had to be pursued under the Supply Code or the Electricity Act.

cases.title: Raj Kumar Ojha v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: interlocutory stay of criminal proceedings
cases.holding: Prima facie the s. 528 BNSS application to quash Criminal Case No. 80 of 2024 requires consideration. Notice issued to opposite party no. 2; further proceedings of that case stayed until further orders; listed after eight weeks.

cases.title: Executive Engineer, Urban Distribution Division, Munshi Puliya, Lucknow v. State of U.P. and Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: interlocutory stay of a Special Judge (EC Act) transformer-shifting miscellaneous case
cases.holding: Prima facie the s. 528 BNSS application requires consideration. The Court recorded that the Special Judge had entertained a private landowner's application to shift a transformer from the front of her plot — a person not covered by Section 11 of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955, on a subject not envisaged by Section 3 of that Act. Notice issued to opposite party no. 2; Criminal Misc. Case No. 761 of 2025 stayed till the next listing (second week of July 2025). The quash was not decided, nor was paragraph 4.5 of the Supply Code construed.
cases.flag: Interlocutory listing order. Applicant invoked paragraph 4.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 as the proper remedy; the Court did not cite or apply that clause.

cases.title: Lokesh v. Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Limited
cases.topic: writ disposed as relief already obtained
cases.holding: Once the purchaser had paid the vendor's arrears and the licensee had given the connection, no further order was required and the writ petition was disposed of.

cases.title: Najir Ahmad v. Managing Director, Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited
cases.topic: interim status quo on recovery of disputed demand
cases.holding: The Court did not decide the validity of the 8 October 2022 demand or whether clause 6.5 of the Supply Code is the exclusive remedy. It directed the supply company to file a counter-affidavit within three weeks, listed the writ, and ordered status quo on recovery till the next date of hearing.

cases.title: Faiju Uddin v. Purvanchal Vidhut Vitrana Nigam Ltd.
cases.topic: listing after bill-correction statement
cases.holding: The writ, brought after a Clause 6.5 bill-correction application, was listed for further hearing after the licensee's counsel stated on instructions that the bill had been corrected; the consumer's counsel was directed to examine the corrected bill and make submissions.

cases.title: Dinesh Chandra Sharma v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: listing
cases.holding: On a writ seeking mandamus for a temporary 1 KW construction connection under Section 43 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and Clause 4.29 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, the Court directed a short counter affidavit within two weeks and listed the petition as fresh on 08.12.2025. The claim was not decided.

cases.title: Gyan Prakash Gupta v. Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & 4 Others
cases.topic: listing after 6.5 rejection — counter and adjournments
cases.holding: The Court did not decide the 06.07.2022 bill, the 13.09.2022 disconnection, or the 23.01.2024 Executive Engineer order on the Rule 6.5 representation. On 28.08.2025 a Division Bench (Sangeeta Chandra and Brij Raj Singh JJ.) directed a counter affidavit within four weeks and listed the writ. Time for the counter was extended on 12.11.2025 on a peremptory basis. Later orders listed the matter from date to date. On 12.01.2026 none appeared for the petitioner; it was listed for 27.01.2026 and was not to be listed within top ten.
cases.flag: Thin interlocutory bundle of five orders (28.08.2025, 12.11.2025, 12.12.2025, 17.12.2025, 12.01.2026). Paras 5-6 are of the 28.08.2025 order. No construction of Clause 6.5.

cases.title: Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P. — 482 listed; coercive action stayed in s.138 case
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: s.482 listing and stay of coercive process
cases.holding: The Court did not decide the challenge to the bailable warrant or the Clause 8.1 Supply Code objection. Time was granted for a counter-affidavit; the application was listed; and no coercive action was to be taken against the applicant till the next date.

cases.title: Smt Omwati v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: s.482 CrPC interlocutory listing in s.135/138 prosecution
cases.holding: Without deciding whether the 19.03.2013 summoning order or the s.135/138 Electricity Act proceedings should be quashed, or whether Clause 6.15(b) of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 barred recovery after two years, the Court held that the matter required consideration, issued notice to opposite party no. 2, and directed that no coercive action be taken against the applicant till the next date of listing.

cases.title: Executive Engineer, Dakshinanchal Electricity Distribution Corporation Ltd. v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: PLA jurisdiction over bill dispute — listing
cases.holding: The Court recorded that the licensee's writ against a Permanent Lok Adalat electricity-bill award, on the plea that Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 occupies the field and that the PLA decided without conciliation under Section 22-C of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, requires consideration. Time was granted for counter and rejoinder affidavits and the matter was listed on 18.7.2024. No merits finding was recorded.

cases.title: Jaswant Nagar Cold Storage Pvt Ltd v. Appellate Authority Additional Commissioner
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: listing-and-interim-stay-of-assessment-dues
cases.holding: The writ challenging the Assessing Officer's 4.5.2021 demand (alleged non-compliance with s.126(1) EA 2003 and Clause 6.8(c)(i)) and the 7.3.2024 appellate order (alleged non-compliance with Clause 6.8(d)(v)) was held to require consideration. Realisation of electricity dues under those orders was stayed till the next listing and later extended till further orders. Merits were not decided.

cases.title: M/S My Car P Ltd. v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: interlocutory listing
cases.holding: The Court recorded the petitioner's plea that a change of category from HV-1 to HV-2 and the assessment were contrary to Clause 4.4 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and the licensee's objections of 1,309 days' laches and non-maintainability, held that the matter required consideration, directed a counter-affidavit and rejoinder, and listed the writ without deciding the Code or delay points.

cases.title: Ratan Industries Limited v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited And Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: listing after liberty to cite Clause 4.49
cases.holding: Without construing Clause 4.49 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 or deciding the writ, the Court granted the petitioner liberty to place judgments on that clause, later recorded that the matter required consideration, directed exchange of affidavits, took counters and rejoinders on record, directed notes of argument, and listed the petition from date to date. The last order of 27 July 2026 listed the matter for 10 August 2026 on the petitioner's prayer. The writ remains pending.
cases.flag: Thin interlocutory bundle of nine listing/adjournment orders (31.7.2024, 13.9.2024, 21.10.2024, 28.11.2024, 2.12.2024, 19.12.2024, 27.2.2025, 10.11.2025, 27.7.2026). Numbered paras 1-4 are of the 21.10.2024 order. Clause 4.49 is named only in the 13.9.2024 listing order; no construction.

cases.title: M/S Mohan Elctro Casting Pvt. Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: infructuous listing
cases.holding: The Registry classified and listed the writ as likely infructuous and invited objections; none were received. The Court dismissed the petition as infructuous, with liberty to move an appropriate application if the cause of action survives, and with no order as to costs.

cases.title: Rana Concat Limited v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: dismissal for want of instructions
cases.holding: The writ petition is dismissed because learned counsel for the petitioner has no instructions in the matter.

cases.title: Vijay Kumar Kesarwani v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: dismissal for want of prosecution
cases.holding: Called in the revised list with none appearing for the petitioner, the writ petition is dismissed for want of prosecution. Interim order, if any, stands discharged. The electricity dispute is not decided.

cases.title: M/s Babu Jagadish Singh Cold Storage Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: listing and delayed counter affidavit
cases.holding: The writ was not decided on merits. After noting that the electricity department had not filed a counter affidavit for eleven years, the Court granted three weeks and no more, on payment of Rs 5,000 recoverable from the Executive Engineer, and directed that the counter disclose the status of the final report and why the proceedings may not be dropped in terms of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. On joint request the matter was listed for July 2020.

cases.title: Dugdh Utpadak Sahkari Sangh Ltd. v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: dismissal as infructuous on listing
cases.holding: A writ listed under infructuous cases, with the petitioner absent even on a revised call of the cause list, is dismissed as infructuous and any interim order stands discharged, without adjudication of the supply dispute.

cases.title: Dhirendra Kumar v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: dismissal for want of prosecution after interlocutory PD-arrears stay
cases.holding: The writ was dismissed for want of prosecution when none appeared for the petitioners even in the revised call. An earlier interlocutory order (3.9.2009) had stayed recovery of Rs 1,35,529 towards permanent disconnection and directed the respondents to consider a fresh-connection application, with fees and charges, without insisting on that deposit, on a prima facie view that PD should have been directed within a reasonable time of the 1991 finding of non-use. Those directions were not a final merits grant; the electricity dispute was left undecided.

cases.title: Rakesh Kumar v. U.P. Power Corpn. Ltd. & Others
cases.topic: listing; instructions on cl. 8.1(b) theft assessment before recovery
cases.holding: Writ listed for 14 September 2009 in the supplementary list. Meantime, counsel for U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. to seek instructions whether the procedure in paragraph 8.1(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, for assessment as a theft case, was followed before recovery proceedings were initiated against the petitioner. Merits of the 8.1(b) challenge not decided.

cases.title: M/s. Mehak Metals Pvt. Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.topic: writ dismissed as infructuous
cases.holding: The writ against the para 4.20 additional-security demand was listed with similar 2009 matters and, without prejudice, respondents were restrained from demanding additional security until further orders, following the interim in Writ Petition No. 30582 of 2009. On 22 August 2016 the petition was dismissed as infructuous after counsel stated it had become infructuous by lapse of time. The demand was not decided on merits.

cases.title: Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. District Consumer Forum, Mainpuri
cases.topic: dismissal in default
cases.holding: After the list was revised and none appeared for the petitioner, the writ was dismissed in default and the 24.11.2009 interim stay of the District Consumer Forum (II), Mainpuri judgment dated 18.6.2009 in complaint case no. 136 of 2006 was vacated. The jurisdictional challenge was not adjudicated.

cases.title: Kishan Bahadur v. Electricity Distribution Division, P.V.V.N.L.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: dismissal for want of prosecution
cases.holding: Listed peremptorily, the writ was dismissed for want of prosecution when none appeared for the petitioner. Any interim order, including the 25 November 2009 stay of recovery on the theft-assessment citation, stood discharged. No finding was recorded on the Supply Code.

cases.title: M/s Rajendra Engineering Udyog Pvt. Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.topic: dismissal for want of prosecution
cases.holding: The writ challenging the additional-security demand was dismissed for want of prosecution and the 2009 interim restraint vacated, without any determination of paragraph 4.20.

cases.title: Shri Ghanshyam Das v. KESCO & Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: interlocutory stay, restoration, and listing
cases.holding: Pending the writ, recovery of the compounding demand remains stayed until further orders; respondents must restore electricity supply; the petitioner shall pay monthly bills regularly. Time was allowed for a counter affidavit. Later orders only listed the matter. The compounding-procedure challenge was not decided.

cases.title: Smt. Kalpna Khanna v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: 482 CrPC listing and interim protection in s.135 trial
cases.holding: The High Court did not decide the quashing prayer. It granted two weeks for the licensee's counter-affidavit and one week thereafter for rejoinder, directed listing with connected Application u/s 482 No. 6194/2010, and stayed coercive action against the applicant in Special Sessions Trial No. 57/2006 till the next date of listing.

cases.title: Dr. Rajeev Sinha v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: dismissal as infructuous
cases.holding: On revision of the list, nobody appeared for the petitioner. The Court held that from the pleadings and prayer the writ had become infructuous by efflux of time or the petitioner had no interest to prosecute it further, dismissed the petition as infructuous, and vacated any interim order.

cases.title: Santosh Kumar Sharma v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: dismissal in default of assessment writ
cases.holding: After an interlocutory stay of recovery on the 10 July 2010 demand notice, the writ was dismissed in default for non-prosecution and the interim order vacated, without deciding the Supply Code assessment or doubling issues.

cases.title: Irshad Hussain v. Executive Engineer, Vidyut Nagariya Vitaran Khand
cases.topic: infructuous listing
cases.holding: Listed as an infructuous case, the writ is dismissed as infructuous in the petitioner's absence even after a revised call; any interim order stands discharged. No Supply Code provision on portability of a connection in the same circle was identified or construed.

cases.title: Smt. Suman Lata v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: dismissal for default of theft-assessment writ
cases.holding: After notice pending admission and a conditional stay of recovery under the 28 February 2011 theft-assessment demand, the writ alleging non-compliance with mandatory requirements of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 was dismissed for default when none appeared for the petitioner on a revised list; the Code challenge was not adjudicated.

cases.title: Mool Chand Kushwaha v. State of U.P. and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: dismissal for default
cases.holding: The writ petition is dismissed for default, no one being present for the petitioner when the list was revised.

cases.title: Sita Ram v. State of U.P. and others
cases.topic: theft recovery — dismissal for want of prosecution
cases.holding: The writ petition challenging a recovery certificate for alleged theft of electricity was dismissed for want of prosecution. The Court did not decide whether the recovery complied with the Electricity Act, 2003 or the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. An earlier interim stay of recovery, conditional on deposit of Rs. 1,15,000, was overtaken by the dismissal.

cases.title: Dina Nath Saw v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: dismissal for want of prosecution; theft-assessment citation
cases.holding: The 2011 Division Bench issued notice and stayed recovery under the 9 May 2011 citation till the next date, conditional on deposit of Rs. 71,000 with the licensee within four weeks, without prejudice, the stay to stand automatically vacated on default. On 9 May 2023 none appearing to press even in revised call, the writ was dismissed for want of prosecution.

cases.title: Somil Ispat (Pvt.) Ltd. v. U.P. Power Corporation Limited And Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: dismissal in default of additional-security writ
cases.holding: The writ petition challenging a demand for additional security was dismissed in default for non-appearance of the petitioner at a listing of oldest pending cases. Any earlier interim order stood vacated. A party aggrieved was left free to move a recall application within one month. The Court did not decide the additional-security claim.

cases.title: Jai Prakash Dixit v. DVVNL
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: dismissal for want of prosecution
cases.holding: None appearing to press the writ against the 9 June 2011 recovery, the petition was dismissed for want of prosecution and any interim order, including the 2011 stay of recovery and direction to restore supply, stood vacated. The Clause 5.6(e) challenge was not decided.

cases.title: Writ challenging Supply Code vires dismissed as infructuous
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: infructuous writ
cases.holding: A writ left pending from 2011 is dismissed as infructuous by efflux of time where none appears for the petitioners; any interim order stands vacated. The Court did not construe the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: M/S Modinagar Paper Mills Pvt. Ltd. v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: want of prosecution
cases.holding: Where counsel holding brief states that the petitioner's advocate has no instructions, the writ is dismissed for want of prosecution, any interim order is discharged, and a recall application will be entertained only if supported by the petitioner's own affidavit.

cases.title: M/s Moolchand Steels Pvt. Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: writ dismissed as not pressed
cases.holding: The writ challenging the additional-security demand and the vires of Supply Code clause 4.20(l) vis-à-vis section 47(5) of the Electricity Act, 2003 was dismissed as not pressed. The 2012 interim stay of the demand, granted on an undertaking and without prejudice, decided nothing on the merits.

cases.title: Rajaram Singh @ Ram Swaroop v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: dismissal for want of prosecution
cases.holding: On revision of the list none appeared for the petitioner. The writ petition was dismissed for want of prosecution and the interim order, if any, was vacated. The Court did not decide whether the 25 May 2012 citation was supported by a provisional or final assessment under the Supply Code.

cases.title: M/s Torrent Power Ltd. v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: interlocutory stay of PLA award on theft assessment
cases.holding: Without deciding whether the Permanent Lok Adalat had jurisdiction to entertain a challenge to a theft-assessment demand under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, or whether its award was perverse, the Court issued notice, listed the writ for admission/hearing, and stayed operation of the Permanent Lok Adalat, Agra judgment dated 12 September 2012 till the next date of listing. Subsequent listings kept the interim order in force.

cases.title: M/s Shri Jai Balaji Rolling Mills Limited v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: want of prosecution
cases.holding: Listed among the High Court's oldest pending cases for priority hearing, the writ was dismissed for want of prosecution as none appeared to press it. The challenge to the additional-security demand and to clause 4.20 of the Supply Code was not decided.

cases.title: Shri Ramchander Straw Products Ltd. v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: interim stay of additional security demand
cases.holding: The writ is connected with Civil Misc. Writ Petition No. 51844 of 2009. Until further orders, the respondents shall not demand the additional security mentioned in the communication dated 4 October 2012, provided the petitioner files an undertaking on affidavit before respondent no. 4 within six weeks that the additional security will be furnished if the writ fails. The order is without prejudice to the parties' rights and contentions.

cases.title: Rakesh Kumar v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: dismissal for non-prosecution
cases.holding: The writ was dismissed for non-prosecution after none appeared for the petitioner on the revised list; any interim order stood discharged. The Court did not decide whether recovery of the remaining revised provisional assessment without deciding objections violated the Supply Code.

cases.title: Smt. Shakuntala Yadav v. Madhyanchal Vidhyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: interim stay and listing
cases.holding: The Court did not decide the Regulation 6.8 challenge. Pending the writ, if the licensee prepares and serves final dues in accordance with the appellate order, the consumer shall furnish security other than cash or bank guarantee within two weeks to the satisfaction of respondent no. 2, such security to abide the result of the petition; four weeks granted for counter-affidavit, list thereafter.

OFFTOPIC::rerc-open-access-regulations-v.code: Electricity Act, 2003 (ss.9, 42, 79(1)(c), 86(1)(c), 178, 181) — CERC/State Commission jurisdictional demarcation over open access; Rajasthan Open Access Regulations, 2016 (Regulations 21, 26(7))
OFFTOPIC::rerc-open-access-regulations-v.clause: ss.42/86(1)(c)/181 (State Commission's intra-state open-access jurisdiction) vis-a-vis s.79(1)(c) (CERC's inter-state transmission jurisdiction)
OFFTOPIC::rerc-open-access-regulations-v.topic: State Electricity Regulatory Commissions retain jurisdiction to regulate the intra-state aspects of open access (including deviation penalties and advance-scheduling requirements for captive power plants and inter-state consumers) even where the power originates outside the state; such regulatory measures are not ultra vires or unreasonable restrictions on the statutory open-access right

cases.title: Ramayana Ispat Pvt. Ltd. & Anr. v. State of Rajasthan & Ors. (with connected appeals)
cases.topic: State Electricity Regulatory Commissions retain jurisdiction to regulate the intra-state aspects of open access (including deviation penalties and advance-scheduling requirements for captive power plants and inter-state consumers) even where the power originates outside the state; such regulatory measures are not ultra vires or unreasonable restrictions on the statutory open-access right
cases.holding: The Court held: (i) RERC had jurisdiction to regulate the intra-state aspects of open access transactions under ss.42(2)/(3), 86(1)(c) and 181 of the Act of 2003, notwithstanding that the power might originate from outside Rajasthan or that CERC has jurisdiction under s.79(1)(c) over inter-state transmission — the key determinant is delivery/consumption within the state's intra-state grid, not the power's source; (ii) penalties under Regulation 21 for deviation/under-injection by captive power plants are a legitimate, uniformly-applied grid-discipline measure serving the Act's objectives (preventing gaming, ensuring frequency stability), not a discriminatory or unreasonable restriction on the s.9(1) proviso right to captive generation; (iii) Regulation 26(7)'s 24-hour advance-notice requirement for short-term inter-state open access is a reasonable procedural safeguard for grid stability and scheduling discipline, not an ultra vires or arbitrary barrier to open access, particularly since real-time/day-ahead market alternatives remain available for urgent procurement; and (iv) courts must exercise judicial restraint and defer to specialized regulatory commissions' technical/economic determinations, interfering only where a regulation is shown to be wholly irrational, ultra vires the parent statute, or violative of fundamental rights. All three appeals were accordingly dismissed and the High Court judgments upholding the Regulations of 2016 affirmed.
cases.flag: Recorded compactly given its scale (~2755 lines) and its subject (CERC/State Commission open-access regulatory jurisdiction and captive-generation deviation penalties), which is distinct from the U.P. Electricity Supply Code's retail billing/assessment/disconnection framework central to this project; not exhaustively digested.

OFFTOPIC::s156-3-crpc-tree-felling-dispu.topic: Criminal revision against dismissal of a s.156(3) Cr.P.C. application over a forged-consent tree-felling dispute between land co-sharers — no Supply Code nexus

cases.title: Shiv Murti Yadav v. State of U.P. & 6 Others
cases.topic: Criminal revision against dismissal of a s.156(3) Cr.P.C. application over a forged-consent tree-felling dispute between land co-sharers — no Supply Code nexus
cases.holding: The revisional court's jurisdiction is narrower than appellate jurisdiction, warranting interference only for gross error, non-compliance with law, unsupported findings, or perverse exercise of discretion; finding none of these, and noting the proper remedy for police inaction on an FIR is a complaint before the Magistrate (not a writ or revision), the revision was dismissed.
cases.flag: Recorded for completeness of the source corpus only; no jurisprudential content relevant to the Supply Code.

OFFTOPIC::s434-ipc-quashing-application.topic: s.482 Cr.P.C. application to quash a charge-sheet under s.434 IPC arising from an encroachment-demolition/extortion dispute — no Supply Code nexus

cases.title: Rakesh Kaushik v. State of U.P. & Another
cases.topic: s.482 Cr.P.C. application to quash a charge-sheet under s.434 IPC arising from an encroachment-demolition/extortion dispute — no Supply Code nexus
cases.holding: Notice issued to respondents with time for counter/rejoinder affidavits; interim protection granted restraining coercive action in the pending criminal case, without affecting separate encroachment-removal proceedings or permitting reconstruction of the demolished portion.
cases.flag: Recorded for completeness of the source corpus only; no jurisprudential content relevant to the Supply Code.

OFFTOPIC::s62-6-interest-generation-tari.code: Electricity Act, 2003 (s.62(6)) — wholesale generation-tariff dispute, unrelated to the retail Supply Code
OFFTOPIC::s62-6-interest-generation-tari.clause: s.62(6) construed narrowly: no interest on a provisional-vs-final tariff differential absent a specific regulation
OFFTOPIC::s62-6-interest-generation-tari.topic: Section 62(6) interest does not extend to the interim/provisional tariff period pending final determination, absent an express regulation; equity/restitution principles do not independently justify interest absent any statutory, contractual, or customary basis

cases.title: M/S NTPC Ltd. v. M.P. State Electricity Board & Ors. (with connected appeals)
cases.topic: Section 62(6) interest does not extend to the interim/provisional tariff period pending final determination, absent an express regulation; equity/restitution principles do not independently justify interest absent any statutory, contractual, or customary basis
cases.holding: Section 62(6) only prohibits recovery of a price 'exceeding the tariff determined under this section' — it does not address the interim period during which tariff determination is pending, nor deem a subsequently-reduced final tariff to retroactively convert prior lawful interim charges into 'excess' charges attracting interest. CERC's 2006 Regulation 5A (providing simple interest on provisional-vs-final tariff differentials) could not apply retrospectively to the 2001-2004 period in issue. The Appellate Tribunal erred in awarding interest on equity/justice/fair-play grounds, since there was no contractual, statutory, or regulatory basis for interest, no industry practice of paying it, and no finding that the generating company had coercively or unjustly extracted the interim tariff (which was charged strictly per the Commission's own continuing notifications).
cases.flag: SC's authoritative narrow construction of s.62(6) interest ('exceeding the tariff determined') — useful cross-reference for retail Supply Code cases construing the same provision (cf. SCJ-072 Kamla Cold Storage, which similarly held s.62(6) inapplicable to a delayed rebate).

OFFTOPIC::seb-contract-corruption-minist.code: Electricity (Supply) Act, 1948 (s.78A, Board guided by State Government policy directions only) read with IPC (ss.120-B, 409) and Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 (ss.5(1)(c), 5(2)) — criminal appeal against acquittal on corruption/breach-of-trust charges over an SEB contract award
OFFTOPIC::seb-contract-corruption-minist.clause: s.78A, Electricity (Supply) Act, 1948 — the State Government's role vis-a-vis the Board is confined to policy directions, not day-to-day contract-award interference
OFFTOPIC::seb-contract-corruption-minist.topic: The Minister for Electricity's persistent interference in a State Electricity Board's tender/contract-award process for a hydroelectric project (steering the contract to a favoured, unqualified late tenderer at 162-188% above the estimated rate, disadvantaging lower and more experienced tenderers) sustains criminal breach-of-trust and corruption convictions, notwithstanding the Board's formal 'collective decision' framing and the absence of direct evidence of personal monetary benefit to the Minister

cases.title: V.S. Achuthanandan v. R. Balakrishna Pillai & Ors.
cases.topic: The Minister for Electricity's persistent interference in a State Electricity Board's tender/contract-award process for a hydroelectric project (steering the contract to a favoured, unqualified late tenderer at 162-188% above the estimated rate, disadvantaging lower and more experienced tenderers) sustains criminal breach-of-trust and corruption convictions, notwithstanding the Board's formal 'collective decision' framing and the absence of direct evidence of personal monetary benefit to the Minister
cases.holding: Reversing the High Court's acquittal and restoring (with a moderated sentence, given nearly two decades' delay) the Special Court's conviction of the Minister (A1), a contractor's associate (A3) and a Board Member (A6), the Supreme Court held that s.78A of the Electricity (Supply) Act, 1948 confines the State Government's role to policy directions, not operational contract-award decisions; extensive witness evidence (of disadvantaged/excluded tenderers) established that the Minister pre-selected the eventual contractor before he even submitted a tender, procedurally manipulated the tendering timeline (repeated tender cancellations/re-invitations, selective notice to favoured tenderers, denial of a hearing opportunity to a disqualified rival tenderer) to eliminate more competitive bids, and rebuffed workers'/lower-cost alternatives, resulting in contracts awarded at 162-188% above the estimated rate with special conditions heavily favouring the contractor; the Board's 'collective decision' framing did not exculpate the accused given the absence of genuine deliberation (minutes dictated by the Chairman) and documented internal objections (Financial Adviser, Law Secretary) that were disregarded. An Appellate Court reviewing an acquittal has full power to reappraise evidence, subject to the double presumption of innocence, but need not defer to a High Court's contrary conclusion where that conclusion is not borne out by the evidence.
cases.flag: Recorded compactly given its criminal-law/corruption-prosecution character and absence of Supply Code nexus; the extensive witness-by-witness evidentiary analysis (paras 9-22) was not exhaustively catalogued.

OFFTOPIC::serc-composition-judicial-memb.code: Electricity Act, 2003 (ss.84(2), 85, 86(1)(f), 94-96, 112-113) — composition of State Electricity Regulatory Commissions
OFFTOPIC::serc-composition-judicial-memb.clause: s.84(2) ('may' appoint a Judge as Chairperson — enabling, not mandatory) read with the mandatory-legal-Member holding derived from ss.86(1)(f), 94-96 (adjudicatory functions/'trappings of a court')
OFFTOPIC::serc-composition-judicial-memb.topic: s.84(2)'s discretion to appoint a High Court Judge as SERC Chairperson is not mandatory, but given the SERC's adjudicatory functions and 'trappings of a court', it is mandatory that at least one Member possess legal/judicial qualifications, and that any adjudicatory Bench include such a Member

cases.title: State of Gujarat & Ors. v. Utility Users' Welfare Association & Ors.
cases.topic: s.84(2)'s discretion to appoint a High Court Judge as SERC Chairperson is not mandatory, but given the SERC's adjudicatory functions and 'trappings of a court', it is mandatory that at least one Member possess legal/judicial qualifications, and that any adjudicatory Bench include such a Member
cases.holding: No, s.84(2) is only an enabling provision permitting (not requiring) appointment of a Judge as Chairperson. But because the SERC discharges adjudicatory functions (chiefly under s.86(1)(f), adjudicating licensee-generating-company disputes) with civil-court-like powers under ss.94-96 and thus has the 'trappings of a court' (following the Constitution Bench's basic-structure reasoning in Madras Bar Association v. Union of India on separation of powers, rule of law, and judicial review), it is mandatory that the Commission include, as a Member, a person who is or has been holding judicial office or who possesses professional legal qualifications with substantial practice experience sufficient to qualify for appointment as a High Court or District Judge; and any Bench exercising adjudicatory functions must include such a legally-qualified Member. Prospective operation was directed (no disturbance of past Commission orders); vacancies must prospectively be filled to satisfy this requirement. The Tamil Nadu State Commission's specific appointments and its suo motu tariff-revision exercise were separately upheld on the facts (no established financial-bias disqualification under Rajesh Awasthi/Mor Modern Cooperative Transport Society).
cases.flag: Recorded compactly given scale (~84 pages) and subject-matter distance from the Supply Code's retail billing/assessment/disconnection framework; the extensive mid-judgment citation discussion (paras ~43-104, not fully read) was not exhaustively catalogued.

OFFTOPIC::service-law-natural-justice.code: Service law / departmental inquiry (not the Supply Code)
OFFTOPIC::service-law-natural-justice.topic: Burden on the Establishment to prove charges in a major-penalty inquiry

cases.title: Dhirendra Kumar Chaudhary v. State of U.P. & 5 Others
cases.topic: Burden on the Establishment to prove charges in a major-penalty inquiry
cases.holding: In a departmental inquiry carrying a major penalty, the Establishment must prove the charges by leading documentary and oral evidence through a Presenting Officer, with witnesses offered for cross-examination, before an inquiry tribunal that distances itself from the Establishment; relying on mere complaints and considering material (further inquiry/I.T.-cell reports) behind the employee's back vitiates the proceedings for breach of natural justice. Dismissal quashed; reinstatement, with liberty to hold a fresh inquiry from the charge-sheet stage.
cases.flag: Off-topic for the Supply Code: this is a service/disciplinary matter. The Supply Code, 2005 appears only as the backdrop of the misconduct charge (irregular bill revisions); no Code provision is construed. Retained in the corpus for completeness (and for its authorities).

cases.title: Umesh Chandra Verma v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. and 3 Others
cases.topic: Major-penalty inquiry — establishment must prove charges by oral and documentary evidence
cases.holding: No. The Court confined itself to fairness of procedure and the type of punishment, not the merits of the charges. The parties agreed that reduction by one step permanently in basic pay is a major penalty. In such an inquiry the committee must distance itself from the establishment; the establishment must first prove the charges by documentary and oral evidence through a Presenting Officer, witnesses must face cross-examination, and the delinquent must then be allowed to lead his own evidence. Here no witness was examined. The Committee gleaned the charge-sheet and reply and treated the documents as proved, as if at a preliminary inquiry. A plea that the petitioner had not disputed genuineness, and Regulation 7(7) (no named witness, so none need be produced), was rejected: the charges and cited documents were denied, and there was no endorsement of admission. The respondents' own later OM of 14.08.2023 directing officers to examine establishment witnesses first was treated as an acknowledgment of that principle. Punishment and appeal quashed; de novo from the charge-sheet if rules permit against a retired officer, to be concluded within three months if elected; no higher punishment.
cases.flag: Off-topic for the Supply Code. The 2005 Code appears only as the backdrop of the original 55 kW connection and load enhancement; no Code clause is construed. Same judge and authorities as SCJ-017. Source PDF also contains listing orders of 01.11.2023 (notice; petitioner cited Union of India v. S.C. Parashar on amalgam of minor and major penalties) and 20.11.2023 (admit; reserved); the judgment under record is 11.03.2024 (2024:AHC:44451).

cases.title: Tarun Kumar Pathak v. State of U.P. and others
cases.topic: Major-penalty inquiry — Establishment must prove charges by oral and documentary evidence through a Presenting Officer
cases.holding: No. The Court did not decide the merits of the ten charges relating to the M/s Three C Projects connection. For a major penalty the Inquiry Committee must convene as an impartial tribunal, distance itself from the Establishment, and require the Establishment to prove the charges from scratch through a Presenting Officer by documentary and oral evidence, with witnesses offered for cross-examination and then an opportunity to the delinquent to enter defence. Charges are dormant allegations, not proof of themselves. The delinquent cannot be made to prove innocence by a gruelling interrogation. Here only 21.12.2021 was scheduled; the petitioner averred that no inquiry was held that day and no later date was fixed, yet a report went to the Chairman. Documents appended to the charge-sheet are not evidence unless formally introduced and proved in the delinquent's presence. The proceedings are vitiated from the charge-sheet stage. Dismissal dated 20.05.2022 and the appellate order dated 04.03.2023 are quashed; reinstatement with current salary is directed. If the respondents proceed afresh from the charge-sheet, arrears abide that event and they may suspend pending an expeditious inquiry (subsistence without a non-alternative-engagement certificate). If they do not, the petitioner is entitled to 50% emoluments for the period out of service.
cases.flag: Off-topic for the Supply Code. Charge 1 alleged release of the 10000 KVA single-point Lotus Zing connection in teeth of the 13th Amendment to Clause 4.9 (10.08.2018) and UPERC's 17.05.2019 51% conversion direction; Charges 6–7 invoked Clauses 4.6 and 4.6(g). The counter cited Section 50 of the Electricity Act, 2003 as the source of the 4.9 amendment. No Code clause is construed. Same judge and authorities as SCJ-017 and SCJ-548. Source PDF also contains the 26.05.2023 stay of the Rs.4,66,764 recovery (Ashutosh Srivastava J.) and successive listing orders through reserved-on 08.12.2023; the judgment under record is 31.05.2024 (2024:AHC:99920). Hindi charge-sheet extract is OCR-garbled; English recitals in paras 2–5 and 14 and Charge 1's embedded UPERC quotation are used. Para 8 states the revised estimate as Rs.58,38,552; Charge 9 as Rs.58,34,552 — recorded as the judgment states it.

OFFTOPIC::sica-alternate-remedy-and-lach.topic: Writ not maintainable: unavailed statutory appeal under Section 25 SICA and inordinate delay

cases.title: U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. v. Appellate Authority for Industrial & Financial Reconstruction & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: Writ not maintainable: unavailed statutory appeal under Section 25 SICA and inordinate delay
cases.holding: No. An efficacious statutory remedy of appeal to the AAIFR under Section 25 SICA was available to the Corporation — including to assail the show-cause notice dated 25 February 2008 — which it did not avail; and the writ was filed in 2009, almost five years after the BIFR orders of 2004 and almost four years after the AAIFR order of 21 March 2005. On both counts the Court was not inclined to exercise its writ jurisdiction and dismissed the petition.

OFFTOPIC::transmission-scheme-siting-dis.code: Electricity (Supply) Act, 1948 (ss.28, 29) — transmission scheme preparation, publication, and sanctioning
OFFTOPIC::transmission-scheme-siting-dis.clause: ss.28-29 (scheme preparation/publication/sanctioning) — validity challenge and re-alignment claim by a subsequent purchaser
OFFTOPIC::transmission-scheme-siting-dis.topic: A subsequent land purchaser who neither made nor inherited a timely representation against a validly-published transmission scheme cannot belatedly seek re-alignment of an already-substantially-executed scheme; parallel pursuit of a civil suit and writ petition for the same relief is an abuse of process

cases.title: Orissa Power Transmission Corporation Ltd. & Ors. v. Asian School of Business Management Trust & Ors.
cases.topic: A subsequent land purchaser who neither made nor inherited a timely representation against a validly-published transmission scheme cannot belatedly seek re-alignment of an already-substantially-executed scheme; parallel pursuit of a civil suit and writ petition for the same relief is an abuse of process
cases.holding: The scheme (notified 1991, modified 1996) was validly published under ss.28/29 with full technical details available for inspection as specified; since neither the original landowner nor the respondent trust (which purchased the land and built on it 14+ years after publication) made any representation within the statutory window, they had no locus to belatedly challenge the scheme or seek re-alignment after ~150 towers had already been erected at a cost of over Rs. 14 crore. The Division Bench of the High Court erred in ordering re-alignment, having overlooked that the respondent stepped into the shoes of a party with no grievance, and in applying a half-baked feasibility analysis over the appellants' unrebutted technical objections. Additionally, pursuing a civil suit for injunction in parallel with two successive writ petitions seeking substantially the same relief, and withdrawing the suit only once the writ appeal was entertained, constituted an abuse of process; the second writ petition should have been dismissed on this ground, distinguishing S.J.S. Business Enterprises (which involved a suit withdrawn early, not maintained in parallel through appeal).
cases.flag: Recorded compactly given its subject (transmission-tower siting/land dispute under the wholesale infrastructure provisions of the 1948 Act), which has no nexus to the U.P. Electricity Supply Code's consumer billing/assessment/disconnection framework central to this project; not exhaustively digested.

PENALTY::retrospective-application-of-sc.code: General jurisprudence on retrospective/prospective operation of judicial precedent, applied to U.P. Power Corporation peak-hour-violation penalty circulars (Circulars dated 15.10.1998 and 07.04.1999)
PENALTY::retrospective-application-of-sc.clause: Doctrine of prospective overruling — applicability to a Supreme Court ruling reinterpreting departmental circulars governing electricity-penalty calculation
PENALTY::retrospective-application-of-sc.topic: A Supreme Court decision correcting an erroneous High Court interpretation of penalty-calculation circulars applies retrospectively to pending (not finally settled) disputes, since prospective overruling is an exception invoked only by express direction of the Supreme Court itself

cases.title: Sri Chandra Mohan Goyal v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Others
cases.topic: A Supreme Court decision correcting an erroneous High Court interpretation of penalty-calculation circulars applies retrospectively to pending (not finally settled) disputes, since prospective overruling is an exception invoked only by express direction of the Supreme Court itself
cases.holding: Yes. It is settled law that judicial decisions are retrospective unless the court expressly makes them prospective; the doctrine of prospective overruling (traced through Golak Nath, Mohd. Ramzan Khan, B. Karunakar, Waman Rao, Atam Prakash) may only be invoked by the Supreme Court itself and only by express direction, which the Lohia Brass Court did not give. On the facts, the Executive Engineer's purported reduction of the petitioner's penalty liability (from over Rs. 42 lakh across seven consumers including the petitioner, down to under Rs. 6 lakh) was never shown to have been approved by the Chief General Manager (Commercial), the officer competent to finally settle such liability, and was in fact under internal challenge via a show-cause notice to the Executive Engineer for having acted without authority; no binding settlement therefore arose. The demand notices recalculating penalty per the Lohia Brass interpretation (and the later Bonds and Beyonds (India) ruling) were accordingly valid, and the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum's and Electricity Ombudsman's orders upholding them were not infirm.

RATE-SCHEDULE-UP::LMV-9-Part-C.code: U.P. Electricity Rate Schedule LMV-9 (Temporary Supply), Part C
RATE-SCHEDULE-UP::LMV-9-Part-C.topic: Construction/civil-work supply is temporary (LMV-9 Part C): appropriate schedule rate + 25%

cases.title: Hyundai Engineering and Construction Co. Ltd. v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.topic: Construction/civil-work supply is temporary (LMV-9 Part C): appropriate schedule rate + 25%
cases.holding: The 25% additional charge is valid. Part C of Rate Schedule LMV-9 applies to power taken for construction purposes including civil work by all consumers, and applies by the nature/purpose of the supply, not the load factor; under clause (3) the rate is the net rate of the appropriate schedule (here HV-2) plus 25%. As the supply was for the Naini Bridge works and limited by the agreement, it was temporary, and by Clauses 7(a) and 7(d) of the agreement the consumer was liable for the applicable rates and any other charge.

TORT::compensation-assessment.code: Law of torts / Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (guidance)
TORT::compensation-assessment.clause: restitutio in integram; MV Act multiplier method
TORT::compensation-assessment.topic: Assessment of damages for electrocution disability

cases.title: Executive Engineer, Electricity Distribution Division-II v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.topic: Assessment of damages for electrocution disability
cases.holding: Damages for loss of limb/life flow from tort principles (restitutio in integram); the Permanent Lok Adalat rightly took guidance from the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 second schedule / multiplier method to compute compensation for a 100% disability, and ~Rs. 21 lakh was not excessive. A departmental circular capping compensation at Rs. 2 lakh binds the Corporation's officials but not the court.

UP-2002::(unspecified).topic: Theft assessment — notice, speaking order by the Executive Engineer, and a reasoned Appellate Committee order

cases.title: M/S I.G. Shoes Pvt. Ltd. v. U.P. Electricity Corporation Ltd. & Others
cases.topic: Theft assessment — notice, speaking order by the Executive Engineer, and a reasoned Appellate Committee order
cases.holding: No. Ashok Kumar holds that proper notice must be given to the consumer, that the Assessing Authority (Executive Engineer) must then pass a speaking and reasoned order, and that if the consumer appeals, the Appellate Committee must also pass a reasoned order. Here the Executive Engineer neither served a proper notice nor made a speaking assessment, and the Appellate Committee simply reiterated provisions of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2002 without discussing the grounds taken by the appellant. Neither order is sustainable. The writ is partly allowed; the impugned orders are set aside; the matter is remitted to the Assessing Authority to proceed afresh after a proper show-cause notice and opportunity of hearing.
cases.flag: Source PDF also contains listing, pass-over, impleadment and amendment orders from 6.1.2012 to 17.11.2014; the operative judgment is 29.11.2016 (paras 1-7). No numbered 2002 Code clause is cited. The raid (28.8.2002), bill (24.10.2002) and assessment (24.3.2003) predate the 2005 Code; the Appellate Committee referred to the 2002 Code. Ashok Kumar is applied for notice and speaking/reasoned orders. Not keyed to UP-2002::8.1 (used elsewhere for 2002-Code interest) or to 2005 Clauses 6.8/8.1.

cases.title: Joginder Singh v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.topic: Code theft definition is irrelevant to criminal prosecution under ss.135/138
cases.holding: No. Clause 2.2(av) was quoted from the 2002 Code. That Code has no relevance to a criminal revision against summoning. It details the obligations of the licensee and consumers towards each other so that the licensee may provide efficient, cost-effective and consumer-friendly service. The Division Bench decision in 2009 (2) AWC 1189 is likewise of no relevance on these facts.
cases.flag: The Court did not quote the text of Clause 2.2(av). Catalog has no UP-2002::2.2(av); keyed as UP-2002::(unspecified) with clause 2.2(av), matching SCJ-632's identification of that definition. Source PDF also contains a 24.11.2010 pass-over and stay-vacation of Ashok Kumar Roopanwal, J.; the reserved judgment is 3.12.2010 of Ashok Srivastava, J.

UP-2002::4.45.code: U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2002 (Clause 4.45, supervision charges for delegated electrification works) — predecessor to the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; framed under s.10, U.P. Electricity Reforms Act, 1999
UP-2002::4.45.clause: 4.45 (15% supervision charges on works executed by the applicant/delegate itself, as opposed to works executed by the Licensee) superseding an administrative office memorandum's lower rate
UP-2002::4.45.topic: A statutory Electricity Supply Code's supervision-charge rate (15% under Clause 4.45 of the 2002 Code) supersedes and displaces a pre-existing, merely administrative office-memorandum rate (5%) from the Code's date of statutory force, for electrification works a statutory development authority is permitted (by a separate relaxation-order) to execute itself in its own colonies

cases.title: U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad & Anr. v. U.P. Power Corpn. Ltd.
cases.topic: A statutory Electricity Supply Code's supervision-charge rate (15% under Clause 4.45 of the 2002 Code) supersedes and displaces a pre-existing, merely administrative office-memorandum rate (5%) from the Code's date of statutory force, for electrification works a statutory development authority is permitted (by a separate relaxation-order) to execute itself in its own colonies
cases.holding: Yes. The 1982 relaxation-order, though issued under statutory rule-making power (Rule 133(1) read with the proviso to Rule 45(1), Indian Electricity Rules, 1956), did not itself prescribe any supervision-charge rate — it merely relaxed the exclusivity otherwise vested in the 'designated licensee' to execute electrification works, subject to prescribed technical/safety conditions. Supervision charges were levied for the first time only via the 1984 office memorandum (5%), which, being a mere administrative order without statutory force, stood superseded by the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2002 (effective 7.6.2002, framed under s.10 of the U.P. Electricity Reforms Act, 1999, to carry out the U.P. Electricity Regulatory Commission's statutory functions), which prescribed 15% supervision charges under Clause 4.45. Since the relaxation-order and the charge-rate instrument address distinct subject matters, the Code's enhancement of the rate did not amend or supersede the relaxation-order itself. Separately, since the appellant had unilaterally accepted the analogous supervision-charge provision under the successor Electricity Supply Code, 2005 (effective 18.2.2005) without raising the same objections it now pressed against the 2002 Code, it could not consistently dispute the 2002 Code's applicability for identical reasons. The contention that higher supervision charges would raise construction costs passed on to the public was rejected as both factually speculative and legally irrelevant, given the legitimate safety/quality-assurance purpose of supervision (dangerous, safety-critical electrification work) and the appellant's freedom to instead deposit the full estimated cost and have the licensee perform the work itself.

Electricity Supply Code, 2005, which shall be considered and decided as per law, if possible before the next date.
