UP-2002::6.17.clause: 6.17 (theft assessment) r/w para 2.2(av) (definition of theft) and para 7.20 (Appellate Committee)
UP-2002::6.17.topic: Theft under para 6.17 requires bypass, meter-tampering, or illegal tapping; it cannot be inferred from higher-capacity equipment

cases.title: Mohan Dairy & Cold Storage Bulandshahar v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Others
cases.topic: Theft under para 6.17 requires bypass, meter-tampering, or illegal tapping; it cannot be inferred from higher-capacity equipment
cases.holding: No. Theft as defined in para 2.2(av) means abstraction by bypassing the meter, tampering with it so that it records less energy than actually passing, or illegal tapping from the licensee's network. The inspection of 8.7.2002 showed no such fact. The Corporation's inference of theft from a higher-capacity transformer and cable, and the Appellate Committee's confirmation of theft without a finding that the dairy was actually abstracting energy of a higher load, rest on surmises and conjectures rather than tangible evidence and cannot be sustained. The 18.1.2003 appellate order, the 8.7.2002 inspection order, and the 7.10.2002 final assessment bill are quashed.
cases.flag: Source PDF also contains listing orders of 29.7.2011 and 5.8.2011; the operative judgment is 12.8.2011. The prayer challenged orders dated 18.1.2003 and 27.9.2002 and a bill dated 7.10.2002 (Annexures 12, 9 and 9-A). The Court quashed 18.1.2003 (Annexure-12), the inspection dated 8.7.2002 (Annexure-1), and the 7.10.2002 bill (called Annexure-9 in the operative paragraph). Recorded as the judgment states them. Catalog hits UP-2005::6.2 / 7.10 do not fit; keyed from the 2002 Code clauses the Court applied.

cases.title: M/S Venus Stone Crushing Co. Thru' Partner & Another v. The U.P. Power Corpn. Ltd. Thru' Chairman & Others
cases.topic: When the period of theft is not ascertainable, para 6.17.1 treats it as 180 days
cases.holding: No. The period was not ascertainable, so it should have been treated as 180 days under paragraph 6.17.1. Assessment for 450 days, illegally and without material on record, is not tenable. That observation is for the restored appeal.

cases.title: Raj Kumar v. KESCO and Others
cases.topic: Clause 6.17.2 (thrice the tariff for theft) cannot be the assessment rate after 10.6.2003
cases.holding: No. Clause 6.17.2 (quoted with 6.17.1) billed assessed theft units at thrice the tariff of the consumer category. That rate is inconsistent with unamended Section 126(6) and, from 10.6.2003, is not the rate applicable to the petitioner. Assessment and appeal on that basis cannot stand.

UP-2002::6.18.clause: 6.18 (assessment for load in excess of the sanctioned limit)
UP-2002::6.18.topic: Consumption beyond sanctioned load is assessable under para 6.18, not as theft under para 6.17

cases.title: Mohan Dairy & Cold Storage Bulandshahar v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Others
cases.topic: Consumption beyond sanctioned load is assessable under para 6.18, not as theft under para 6.17
cases.holding: Yes. From the totality of the circumstances the only inference that can be drawn is that the dairy was consuming load in excess of the sanctioned limit, and it is liable to be assessed in accordance with para 6.18, not para 6.17. Under the interim order of 19.2.2003 the Corporation had already raised a para 6.18 demand, which the dairy paid, and amounts paid on the 6.17 assessment had been adjusted.

UP-2002::8.1.code: U.P. Electricity Supply Code (interest on delayed dues, Clause 8.1)
UP-2002::8.1.topic: Interest on a delayed/evaded assessment is a necessary corollary of retention, neither penal nor confiscatory

cases.title: M/S Hind Industries Limited v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.topic: Interest on a delayed/evaded assessment is a necessary corollary of retention, neither penal nor confiscatory
cases.holding: Payment of interest on money retained for years (here at the Clause 8.1 rate of 16% compoundable every six months) is a necessary corollary of retention and is neither penal nor confiscatory (following Wig Brothers). The question of whether the 2003 Act (rather than pre-2003 dues) governed the applicable rate, and the exact rate, was left to the competent authority, but the Court directed that in the facts of the case interest could not be less than the bank rate applicable for the relevant period.

UP-2002::area-committee.topic: monetary jurisdiction of internal committees on recovery representations

cases.title: Hind Industries Ltd. v. U.P. Electricity Power Corpn. Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: monetary jurisdiction of internal committees on recovery representations
cases.holding: Where recovery against the consumer exceeded Rs 10 lakhs, the representation directed by the earlier writ disposal could not be decided by the Superintending Engineer (Circle Level/DGM, limited to Rs 2 lakhs). The Supply Code 2002 required the Area Level Committee (CGM) to decide it. The Court allowed the modification and directed that Committee to decide within one month, if not already decided. The underlying recovery was not adjudicated.
cases.flag: order cites Supply Code 2002 committee limits without a clause number

UP-2002::area-level-committee-jurisdicti.clause: jurisdiction over representations against assessment (Area Level Committee/CGM vs. Superintending Engineer/DGM)
UP-2002::area-level-committee-jurisdicti.topic: Representations against an assessment exceeding Rs. 10 lakh lie before the Area Level Committee, not the Superintending Engineer (whose jurisdiction was capped at Rs. 2 lakh)

cases.title: M/S Hind Industries Limited v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.topic: Representations against an assessment exceeding Rs. 10 lakh lie before the Area Level Committee, not the Superintending Engineer (whose jurisdiction was capped at Rs. 2 lakh)
cases.holding: The Area Level Committee/CGM had jurisdiction, since under the Code, 2002 the Committee at circle level/DGM (Superintending Engineer) could decide representations only up to Rs. 2 lakh, while representations concerning recoveries above Rs. 10 lakh had to be decided by the Committee at area level/CGM; a 2010 modification order accordingly directed the representation to the Area Level Committee instead. However, even accepting the petitioner's own contention that the Superintending Engineer lacked jurisdiction, this meant only that the representation itself had been filed before an incompetent authority and any order thereon was of no consequence — it did not excuse the petitioner from approaching the Area Level Committee, which he never did even after the modification order, leaving the original assessment order unchallenged before any competent authority.
cases.paras: the jurisdiction discussion (unnumbered order, orders dated 12.10.2011 and 18-19.10.2011)

cases.title: Prakash Chandra v. State of U.P. & Anr.
cases.topic: alternative remedy against assessment
cases.holding: A writ against an assessment for alleged use of an agricultural connection for commercial purpose will not be entertained on merits where a remedy is available under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 and the consumer has already filed an objection before the licensee; the petition is dismissed. The Court did not identify a specific clause.

cases.title: Rajan Singh Yadav v. Dhakinanchal Electricity Distribution Corp. Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: provisional assessment objection and reconnection on part-deposit
cases.holding: Where a provisional assessment notice itself grants fifteen days to object, the High Court will not quash it for alleged non-compliance with the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; those points must be taken in the consumer's reply. If supply has been disconnected, reconnection shall be granted on deposit of one-third of the assessed amount, subject to final assessment after the objections are decided.

cases.title: Jay Prakash Yadav v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: new connection barred while theft dues unpaid
cases.holding: The U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 restricts grant of a new connection where there is a theft case and unpaid dues of that theft case. Mandamus for a new connection on an offer to pay the assessment in instalments was refused; if the petitioner does not dispute the assessment and wants a new connection, he must deposit the entire amount before applying.
cases.flag: order cites the Supply Code 2005 restriction on new connection for theft and unpaid theft dues without numbering the clause

cases.title: Ranveer Singh v. Powergrid Corporation of India Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: transmission line over private land without consent
cases.holding: Where a landowner alleges that a transmission line is being erected over his land without consent, the writ court may dispose of the petition by directing the concerned respondent to examine whether the line is required to be drawn over that land and to take immediate steps in accordance with the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, within a fixed time.
cases.flag: order invokes Electricity Supply Code, 2005 without citing a clause

cases.title: Peetam Singh v. State of U.P. and another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: delayed-billing-and-supply-code-forum
cases.holding: A writ agitating non-issuance of bills and payment grievances of 2004, after deposits and meter sealing under an earlier disposal for additional load, will not be used to examine such delayed billing. Current bills may be downloaded from the licensee's website; any grievance as to payment lies before the appropriate authority under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ is dismissed.

cases.title: Nand Kishore v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: forum for bill disputes and recovery citations
cases.holding: Where the dispute is as to assessment or electricity bills, the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 supplies the remedy; where the dispute is as to a recovery citation issued under the U.P.Z.A. & L.R. Act, a suit under Section 287-A of that Act is the contemplated remedy. A writ court will not, on affidavits, decide highly factual questions of quantum due or whether supply continued after 1998, especially when the consumer has already filed a civil suit for injunction against realisation of the same dues. Relief against the citation was refused and the petition was disposed of with liberty to pursue Section 287-A.

cases.title: Pooran Lal v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-assessment-dispute-forum
cases.holding: Where the controversy is as to assessment or the bills themselves, the remedy is under the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005; where it is as to a recovery citation issued under the U.P.Z.A. & L.R. Act, a suit under s.287-A of that Act is contemplated. The writ court will not, on affidavits, adjudicate a highly factual dispute as to the amount due or whether supply continued after 1998, particularly when the consumer has already filed a civil suit for injunction against realisation of the same dues. Relief against the citation is refused, with liberty to proceed under s.287-A.

cases.title: Gopal Gautam v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: application for new connection
cases.holding: Where the petitioner has not shown a proper application on record, the writ is disposed of with liberty to make a proper application for an electricity connection under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, to be disposed of expeditiously in accordance with law.
cases.flag: order invokes Supply Code 2005 generally; no clause numbered

cases.title: Rajvir v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: proposed assessment — premature writ
cases.holding: A challenge to a proposed-assessment notice under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is premature: unless the assessment has been finalised there cannot be any coercive action against the consumer. The writ was disposed of with a direction to the respondent authority to proceed strictly in accordance with law.
cases.flag: Order cites Supply Code 2005 generally; proposed assessment with 15-day objection, no clause numbered.

cases.title: Ruchi Agrawal v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: theft-assessment-objections
cases.holding: A consumer subjected to a theft assessment on which no final order has been passed may raise objections before the Executive Engineer under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; those objections are to be considered and disposed of in accordance with law. The writ was disposed of with a three-month outer limit from production of a certified copy.

cases.title: Ram Karan v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: consideration of consumer request after offer to clear dues
cases.holding: On the petitioner's undertaking to clear dues on connection no. 053658, the writ was disposed of with liberty to make the offer before the Executive Engineer, who shall consider the request and pass appropriate orders in accordance with the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Pushpa Jindal v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: conversion of domestic connection to commercial
cases.holding: A writ seeking mandamus to convert a domestic electric supply connection to a commercial connection was disposed of without merits adjudication, directing the licensee (respondent no. 3) to pass appropriate orders on the petitioner's application within three months provided it is in accordance with law and fulfils the terms and conditions of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Balak Ram v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: adjustment of electric wire obstructing construction
cases.holding: Respondent no. 3 shall examine the petitioner's request for adjustment of an obstructing electric wire, on the petitioner's offer to pay the required charges, in accordance with law and pass appropriate orders or issue necessary directions to the Executive Engineer concerned as per the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
cases.flag: order cites Electricity Supply Code, 2005 without a clause number

cases.title: Mukul Kumar v. General Manager, U.P.P.C. Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: new connection — third-party obstruction to poles
cases.holding: Where a third party obstructs installation of a pole needed for a new connection, the Executive Engineer shall, on the Junior Engineer's report, hear the objector and take appropriate action under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 including the Works Licensee Rules if orders of another authority are required, and inform the applicant within six weeks of production of a certified copy. The Court did not itself direct that the connection be granted.
cases.flag: No Supply Code clause numbered; order cites 'Works Licensee Rules' without a rule number.

cases.title: Madhu Singh v. State of U.P. — Permanent disconnection and No Dues Certificate left to Supply Code procedure
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: permanent disconnection and no-dues certificate
cases.holding: A writ seeking leave to deposit arrears and obtain a No Dues Certificate after permanent disconnection will be disposed of without a merits direction, leaving the consumer to the procedure prescribed under the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
cases.flag: order invokes the 2005 Code without identifying a clause

cases.title: Mohd. Mohsin v. State of U.P. and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: permanent disconnection — previous consumer's permission
cases.holding: A granted electricity connection cannot be permanently cancelled solely because a previous connection-holder of similar name did not permit the applicant to take supply, when it is not the licensee's case that the applicant does not own, jointly own or occupy the premises, is not running the factory, is in default of electricity dues, or is otherwise disqualified under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 or the Electricity Act, 2003. The Executive Engineer's order dated 29.08.2014 is set aside.
cases.flag: Order invokes the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 and Electricity Act, 2003 generally, without a numbered clause.

cases.title: Pappu Sharma v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-grievance
cases.holding: Where a writ petition in pith and substance questions the validity and correctness of an electricity bill, the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 furnishes the forum; the consumer must approach the authority concerned, and the High Court will not entertain the writ.
cases.flag: Court cited the Supply Code generally, without a clause number.

cases.title: Girish Kumar Agarwal v. State of U.P. — electricity recovery certificate
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: writ — alternative remedy for electricity dues
cases.holding: A recovery certificate issued on the Executive Engineer's demand of electricity charges is challengeable before the District Grievance Redressal Forum under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. That forum is an efficacious statutory alternative remedy, so a writ to quash the certificate and restrain coercive recovery will not be entertained and recovery is not interfered with.
cases.flag: The order names the District Grievance Redressal Forum under the 2005 Code but cites no clause number.

cases.title: M/s Simran Industries v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: alternative remedy for disputed electricity bill
cases.holding: If the consumer is not satisfied with the amount demanded under a bill issued by the distribution licensee, for whatever reason, the remedy is under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and a writ petition will be dismissed.

cases.title: Pooja Gupta v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: representation on disputed recovery of dues
cases.holding: Faced with a writ alleging that recovery ignored amounts already deposited, the Court held that disputed questions of fact should first be examined by the Executive Engineer (UPPCL), DVVNL, Raniya, Kanpur Dehat. The petitioner was given liberty to represent; that authority was to look into, examine and remedy the grievance in accordance with the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, preferably within three months of the representation with a certified copy of the order. The writ was disposed of on that direction. No specific Supply Code clause was cited.

cases.title: Rajendra Dev Tivari v. State of U.P. — electricity-bill recovery writ dismissed for Supply Code remedy
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: electricity-bill-recovery-writ
cases.holding: Where a petitioner is aggrieved by recovery of an electricity bill demanded by the Electricity Board, the remedy lies under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; a writ petition is dismissed with liberty to pursue that remedy.
cases.flag: Order invokes the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 without identifying any clause.

cases.title: Mahendra Pratap Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: Article 226 — factual dispute and Code remedies
cases.holding: Where the petitioner is aggrieved by an impugned order that raises a factual dispute, the High Court will not try those facts under Article 226; the petitioner may take such recourse as is available under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ petition was dismissed.

cases.title: Vinod Kumar Agarwal v. State of U.P. — representation for electricity connection to be considered under Supply Code
cases.topic: new-connection
cases.holding: Where the sole relief sought is disposal of a representation for grant of an electricity connection, the Court may dispose of the writ by directing the concerned Executive Engineer to consider that representation in accordance with law and the U.P. Electricity Supply Code within a fixed time, without adjudicating entitlement to the connection on the merits.

cases.title: Jeetu @ Jeet Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: assessment-objection
cases.holding: Once the consumer has already objected to an assessment demand, that objection cannot be adjudicated under Article 226. If half the demanded amount is deposited within fifteen days, the authority shall decide the objection within three months.
cases.flag: order cites U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 generally as the remedy to challenge assessment; no clause numbered

cases.title: M/S Krishna Auto Pvt. Ltd. v. U.P.P.C.L.
cases.topic: new-connection-application
cases.holding: On the licensee's assurance that a grievance of non-release of an electricity connection was being examined under the U.P. Electricity Act, 2003 and the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, the Court disposed of the writ by directing the Executive Engineer, Electricity Distribution Division-II, Purvanchal Vidyut Vitaran Nigam Ltd., Varanasi, to look into the grievance and try to redress it in accordance with law, preferably within six weeks of receipt of a certified copy.

cases.title: Shailendra Pratap Singh v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: prescribed application for a new connection
cases.holding: Mandamus to sanction a connection was refused on the papers. The petitioner was directed to submit, within two days, an application in the prescribed form and to complete the formalities required under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If those formalities were completed, the licensee was to process the application and pass appropriate orders within seven days. Entitlement to the connection was not decided.
cases.flag: order invokes the 2005 Supply Code generally; no clause number given

cases.title: M/s Bharti Flour Mills v. Executive Engineer, E.D.D., Meerut
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: successive writ; Code remedies saved
cases.holding: A second writ questioning subsequent electricity bills on technical grounds need not be entertained where the consumer has already invoked the writ court on outstanding dues, even if that earlier petition stands dismissed in default; the consumer may approach the first writ court. Dismissal of the successive petition does not affect recourse under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: M/s S.R. Preservation Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: withdrawal to Supply Code remedy
cases.holding: After the petition was heard at some length, the consumer was permitted to withdraw the writ so as to avail any remedy under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The petition was dismissed as withdrawn. Payments made under the Court's interim orders were directed to be adjusted against pending bills. The demand of Rs. 20,20,306 was not adjudicated.

cases.title: Naubahar Singh v. State of U.P. and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: assessment-alternative-remedy
cases.holding: Where theft of electricity is said to have been detected and an assessment raised, a writ petition challenging that assessment will not be entertained if departmental remedies before the appropriate Forum under the Electricity Act, 2003 and the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 remain available; the petition is consigned to the record.
cases.flag: No Code clause or Act section is identified. The order styles the statute as 'U.P. Electricity Act, 2003' and refers to an 'appropriate Forum' without distinguishing CGRF, assessing officer, or s.127 appellate authority.

cases.title: Kaushalendra Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-complaint-forum
cases.holding: A writ petition challenging electricity bills which also raises a general grievance of village residents, and is not filed as public interest litigation, will not be entertained on the writ side. The petitioner's billing grievance can be examined under the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the writ is disposed of with liberty to avail that remedy.

cases.title: Faizul Hasan v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: recovery citation without assessment
cases.holding: Where a recovery citation for electricity arrears is challenged as issued without a valid provisional or final assessment after due notice under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, the writ court need not keep the petition pending. The consumer may apply to the assessing authority; that application is to be treated as an objection to the proposed assessment and decided within a fixed time, and recovery shall abide the decision.
cases.flag: Supply Code 2005 invoked for provisional/final assessment without a clause number

cases.title: Raj Kumar Patel v. State of U.P. — demand notice / provisional assessment — representation directed
cases.topic: demand notice and provisional assessment — representation
cases.holding: Without expressing any opinion on merits, the petitioner was directed to appear before the Executive Engineer on 12 September 2018 and file a fresh representation or objection, enclosing a certified copy of the order and the writ papers. That authority was to consider and decide the representation by a speaking order in accordance with law after hearing, preferably within 30 days of receipt. No coercive action was to be taken for 45 days from the order or until disposal of the representation, whichever was earlier. The writ was disposed of.
cases.flag: Supply Code 2005 invoked without a numbered clause

cases.title: Sushmita Raghav v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: disconnection-independent-application-of-mind
cases.holding: The Executive Engineer, as the competent authority to grant or disconnect electricity, did not apply his own mind in the order dated 31 July 2018, which rested solely on the Additional City Magistrate (IInd), Allahabad's order dated 25 June 2018. That order cannot be sustained and is quashed. The matter is remanded to the Executive Engineer (Distribution), Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd., to reconsider on its own merits independent of the Magistrate's order, in accordance with law and especially the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, after hearing the petitioner and the landlord, expeditiously and if possible within one month. For one month from the date of the judgment or until a final decision, whichever is earlier, the authorities shall not refuse to recharge the petitioner's prepaid connection.
cases.flag: Court invoked the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 generally without citing a clause.

cases.title: Smt. Habibunissa v. State of Uttar Pradesh & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: objection before final assessment
cases.holding: Where only a notice calling for reply or objection to electricity dues has issued and no final assessment order has been passed, the writ is not decided on merits. The petitioner is directed to file objection to the 8 May 2024 notice under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 within four weeks; if she does, the authority shall deal with the objection and pass the final assessment order within a further month.
cases.flag: order cites the Supply Code 2005 without a clause number; context is objection before final assessment

cases.title: Sikandar Ali v. Executive Engineer, EUDD
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: new-connection-indemnity
cases.holding: Without examining the merits, the Court disposed of the writ and permitted the petitioner to file a fresh representation, with a certified copy of the order, before the Executive Engineer, EUDD, Kalyani Devi, Allahabad within one month. If such a representation is filed, the Executive Engineer shall consider and decide it in accordance with law within one month of receipt. No direction to grant the connection was issued.

cases.title: Ashwani Kumar v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing; cause of action
cases.holding: A writ does not lie where no cause of action is disclosed. The licensee's 24 April 2025 no-dues letter spoke only to billing cycles of November 2023, December 2023 and January 2024, and the bill dated 10 April 2025 had already been paid on 11 April 2025. Petition dismissed.

cases.title: Nisar Ahamad v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: withdrawal with liberty to Supply Code authority
cases.holding: On the petitioner's request, the writ petition is dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to approach the authority under the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code in accordance with law.

cases.title: Sanjay Chaurasiya v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: tenant commercial connection
cases.holding: Where a tenant’s occupation is protected by a subsisting civil injunction and the claim is covered by Guddi Kesarwani, the Executive Engineer’s rejection of a temporary electricity connection is set aside and remitted; if the petitioner applies for a commercial connection, it is to be processed in accordance with law.

cases.title: Anuj Kumar v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: writ vs statutory remedy (theft assessment)
cases.holding: Fact disputes on quantification of a theft-of-electricity assessment and an alleged excess deposit do not warrant interference in writ jurisdiction. The petition is disposed of, leaving the petitioner to avail the statutory remedy under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, in accordance with law.

cases.title: Jagdish Gaur v. Managing Director, Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.topic: new-connection
cases.holding: An application for grant of an electricity connection is to be examined by the concerned licensee officer under the applicable provisions of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, after notice to the affected private party, rather than in writ. The petitioner was directed to approach respondent no.2, who shall examine the claim in accordance with law within two months.
cases.flag: no clause numbered; order refers only to applicable provisions of the 2005 Code

cases.title: Ghanendra Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: theft-demand-fresh-order
cases.holding: Once the licensee withdraws a theft demand and undertakes to pass a fresh order after hearing, the Court issues no further direction, except that the fresh order must strictly follow the procedure prescribed under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
cases.flag: order cites the Supply Code generally; no clause numbered

cases.title: Gyanwati v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: provisional assessment — theft — objection before final order
cases.holding: On the licensee's statement that the Executive Engineer would consider the consumer's objection to a theft-based provisional assessment before passing the final assessment order, the writ was disposed of with a direction that the procedure prescribed under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 shall be strictly followed while considering the objection.

cases.title: Kunti Devi v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: objection to provisional assessment in alleged theft
cases.holding: On the licensee's statement that the consumer's objection to the notice of provisional assessment in an alleged theft case would be considered by the Executive Engineer before the final assessment order, the writ was disposed of with a direction that the procedure prescribed under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 shall be strictly followed while considering the objection.
cases.flag: order invokes the Supply Code 2005 generally; no clause numbered

cases.title: Rajesh Yadav v. State of U.P. and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: assessment-notice-procedure
cases.holding: Where the electricity department cancelled the impugned assessment notice and issued a fresh notice for making assessment, the writ cause of action does not survive. The consumer may file a reply to the fresh notice; the assessing officer must then proceed strictly in accordance with the procedure prescribed under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
cases.flag: Court invoked the Supply Code generally; no clause number given.

cases.title: Shilpi Pal v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: statutory forums
cases.holding: Where a fact dispute exists over rejection of a connection application, Article 226 interference is declined and the petitioner is left to the statutory forums under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
cases.flag: clause unspecified; court named only statutory forums under the 2005 Code

cases.title: Pappu Sharma v. State of U.P. and Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: application-for-new-connection
cases.holding: A writ seeking mandamus to decide a pending connection application and to grant supply is disposed of without examining the claim on merits; the petitioner may apply for electricity connection as per the Electricity Supply Code and the licensee shall consider and decide the application on its own merit preferably within two months.

cases.title: Ram Naresh @ Ram Rahees Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: theft-final-assessment-procedure
cases.holding: Once the licensee withdraws the impugned theft assessment and undertakes a fresh opportunity to file objections, the writ does not survive and is disposed of as infructuous, with liberty to pass a fresh final assessment strictly in accordance with the procedure prescribed under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
cases.flag: order cites the Supply Code generally, not a numbered clause

cases.title: Mewa Lal Ram v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: statutory remedies; Article 226; disputed facts
cases.holding: Where a fresh connection is refused for outstanding dues of an existing connection in the petitioner's father's name at the same premises, a fact dispute is involved and Article 226 interference is declined. The writ is disposed of leaving the petitioner to statutory remedies under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Ram Prasad Vishwakarma v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: final assessment after theft provisional notice
cases.holding: Where objections to a notice of provisional assessment in an alleged theft case have already been filed and remain undecided, no ground is made out to quash the notice. The petition is disposed of with a direction to the concerned Executive Engineer to pass the order of final assessment strictly in accordance with the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and to dispose of any still-pending compounding application in accordance with law.

cases.title: Birendra Singh Yadav v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: final assessment after provisional assessment
cases.holding: A writ challenging a checking report and notice of provisional assessment will not be entertained, nor will the Court decide whether the checking report is correct, while the consumer’s objection to the provisional assessment remains pending. The petitioner was given two weeks to file a supplementary objection. The assessing officer, while making the final assessment, must follow the procedure prescribed under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 and consider that supplementary objection.

cases.title: Chandrika Prasad Pandey v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: reconnection; disputed bills
cases.holding: Where the licensee filed no reply, the Court treated as correct that a final District Consumer Forum order dated 22.01.2002 required 7.5 H.P. billing and pump-set operation, yet supply had not been restored. It directed that the 7.5 H.P. connection be reconnected within a month of production of a certified copy before the Executive Engineer (Distribution), Kaushambi. The department may serve pending bills; if the consumer disputes them or the arrears, he may object under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and the Executive Engineer shall decide the objection in accordance with law and in compliance with the Forum order.

cases.title: Ashok Kumar v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: statutory remedy against demand
cases.holding: After argument, the petitioner elected to seek the statutory remedy under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 against the demand of Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd., Allahabad. The writ was dismissed with that liberty; the demand was not decided on merits.
cases.flag: order invokes Electricity Supply Code-2005 generally; no clause numbered

cases.title: Murari Lal v. Regional Appellate Committee/Supdt. Engg./D.G.M. & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: adjustment of assessment after acquittal
cases.holding: On the parties’ consensus and without examining merits, the Court recorded that after the petitioner’s criminal acquittal, the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 permits him to approach the concerned authority and claim adjustment of the assessed amount or penalty by showing the calculation was on the higher side. Respondent no.3 was directed to decide that claim on or before 31 March 2019, taking subsequent developments on record; recovery was not to be pressed until that decision. The writ was partly allowed. Prayer no.3 was not pressed.
cases.flag: Order invokes U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 generally; no clause number is given.

cases.title: Iqbal Ahmad v. Kanpur Electricity Supply Co. Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: alternative remedy — unauthorized-use inspection objection
cases.holding: A writ court will not interfere under Article 226 with an Executive Engineer's rejection of an objection to an unauthorized-use inspection report, the petitioner having an ample remedy under the Electricity Supply Code.
cases.flag: Court invoked the Electricity Supply Code generally; no clause was named.

cases.title: Kannu Lal v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: statutory remedy against electricity bill
cases.holding: A consumer disputing an electricity bill must avail the statutory remedy under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ court will neither quash the bill nor direct decision of a representation that is not referable to any statutory provision.

cases.title: Satyaveer Singh v. Executive Engineer, Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: writ forum; relegated to Supply Code
cases.holding: Writ proceedings are not the appropriate forum for a direction to survey and physically verify the existence of installations relating to a billed electricity connection. The petitioner may seek relief under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ petition was dismissed.

cases.title: Asaf Jahan v. Purwanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: new connection application
cases.holding: A writ seeking mandamus to issue an electricity connection is disposed of with a direction that the pending application be considered under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and decided within six weeks of production of a certified copy; the Court does not itself direct grant of the connection.

cases.title: Smt. Chandrawati v. Dakshinanchal Electricity Supply Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: representation on post-disconnection bill
cases.holding: The writ was disposed of with liberty to the petitioner to submit a representation to respondent no. 3 on the bill dated 1 October 2009, to be considered and decided in accordance with the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, expeditiously and preferably within three months of production of a certified copy. The Court did not decide the bill or restoration.

cases.title: Syed Qasim Husain v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-correction-alternate-remedy
cases.holding: Where the consumer disputes an electricity bill, the remedy is to take appropriate steps under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; a writ seeking permanent connection on that grievance is dismissed so the petitioner may pursue those Code remedies.
cases.flag: No clause number stated; court referred generally to the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Incorrect electricity bill directed to be corrected under Supply Code 2005

cases.holding: The electricity bill shall be corrected in accordance with the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 within one month of production of the certified copy of the order before the concerned authority.

cases.holding: Where a new-connection application was not being processed for want of a landlord's no-objection certificate under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and the applicant undertook to file that certificate, the writ was disposed of with a direction that if the applicant submits the landlord's NOC and completes all other formalities, the application shall be processed and appropriate action taken expeditiously in accordance with law.

cases.title: Pappu Singh v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: transfer of connection after death of consumer
cases.holding: Mandamus will not issue to compel the licensee to accept bills from a person in whose name the connection does not stand. Where the recorded consumer has died, the successor must apply for transfer of the connection under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; such an application is to be decided in accordance with law and consequential steps taken. The writ was disposed of on that footing without granting or refusing the bill-acceptance relief.
cases.flag: order cites U.P. Electricity Supply Code 2005 generally; no clause numbered

cases.title: Dr. Mohd. Israr v. State of U.P. and others

cases.topic: consideration of application for supply
cases.holding: Subject to fulfilment of the conditions prescribed under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, the petitioner's application for electricity supply may be considered and disposed of in accordance with law. The writ petition was disposed of finally; no notice was issued to the landlord.

cases.title: Buddha Ram v. U.P. Power Corporation
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: writ-maintainability-billing-disconnection
cases.holding: Where a consumer seeks a mandamus to decide an application alleging disconnection and wrong bills, the writ is not entertainable; the consumer must take the appropriate remedy under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Israr Ahmad v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-dispute-forum
cases.holding: A consumer seeking a mandamus to issue a correct electricity bill matching an on-spot checking report must raise the correctness of the bill under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the writ is dismissed with liberty to pursue that statutory remedy.
cases.flag: order cites U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 generally; no clause numbered

cases.title: Satendra Kumar Gupta v. State of U.P. And Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-dispute-writ
cases.holding: The correctness or incorrectness of electricity bills cannot be adjudicated in writ proceedings. Where a recovery citation is consequential to bills issued by the licensee, the consumer’s remedy is to approach the competent authority in accordance with the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ seeking to quash the citation dated 24 January 2011 was dismissed with that observation.

cases.title: Budhram v. State of U.P. — tubewell dues recovery

Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Rishal Singh v. State of U.P. And Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad

cases.holding: The High Court will not entertain a writ against excess billing and disconnection until the consumer first approaches the electricity department for correction of bills under the detailed procedure in the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the petition is dismissed for alternative remedy.
