cases.holding: Subject to inquiry into the petitioner's tenancy and possession, if an indemnity bond is submitted the licensee shall process it for grant of a separate electricity connection as per the Supply Code, especially clause 4.4, within four weeks. The order confers no right of possession or title and does not prejudice opposite parties 5 to 7.

cases.title: Mohammad Izlal Siddiqui v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: indemnity bond where ownership disputed
cases.holding: Even if the applicant claims to be owner, a pending partition suit and disputed title require an indemnity bond under clause 4.4 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The SDO/EE shall process the pending application, verify lawful possession, and decide the grant of connection in accordance with law, applying the principles in Seema Mansoor and Chandu Khamaru (though those were tenant-landlord cases). The direction has no bearing on title or possession and is unavailable if a court restraint forbids connection.

cases.title: Vijay Laxmi Yadav v. District Magistrate, Lucknow
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
cases.topic: occupier connection without owner consent
cases.holding: A writ for connection does not lie where the occupier has not proved tenancy or possession. If she applies with a lease, rent receipt or TDS and an indemnity bond, and possession is proved, the licensee may grant a connection in her name even without the owner's consent, after hearing the owner, if there is no legal impediment, and shall decide within three weeks.

cases.title: Jaya Ahuja v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.topic: occupant connection on indemnity bond
cases.holding: If the petitioner resides in the premises and seeks an electricity connection, the application shall be considered, subject to an indemnity bond under clause 4.4 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and needful done within three weeks. The order decides neither occupancy nor title or possession, and is without prejudice to the husband's or any third party's rights and to any pending proceeding.

cases.title: Arun Gupta v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
cases.topic: occupant connection on indemnity bond
cases.holding: Where inspection shows the applicant in part possession of the premises, outstanding electricity dues and a family dispute among occupants are not a bar to considering a new-connection application under clause 4.4 if the applicant clears the dues, furnishes an indemnity bond, and there is no other legal impediment (including any injunction). If a connection is granted it shall be prepaid. The order confers no title or possession and does not affect third-party rights. Clause 4.4 principles, though developed in landlord-tenant cases, apply because a person cannot live without electricity.

cases.title: Rabia Juneid v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
cases.topic: occupant prepaid connection on indemnity bond
cases.holding: If the petitioners are in possession of the premises (a fact the licensee must verify) and the first petitioner applies for a prepaid electricity connection with an indemnity bond referable to paragraph 4.4 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, the licensee shall consider that application and pass appropriate orders if she is otherwise eligible. Opposite party no. 4 shall be heard; her rights in the premises are not prejudiced. Consideration of her disconnection application is not barred, but the prepaid-connection application shall be considered simultaneously.

cases.title: Mohd. Nooruz Zaman v. Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitaran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad (Lucknow Bench)
cases.topic: occupant connection on indemnity bond
cases.holding: Where landlord consent is not available, a person claiming to be a tenant in occupation who seeks a separate connection may submit an indemnity bond. Subject to inquiry into tenancy and possession, the licensee shall process that application for grant of a separate connection as per clause 4.4 read with Annexure 4.2 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, within four weeks. The order confers no right of possession or title and does not prejudice the landlord.

cases.title: Smt. Neelam v. Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.topic: new connection barred by outstanding dues on premises
cases.holding: Unless outstanding dues on the premises are cleared, a new electricity connection cannot be granted in view of clause 4.4 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ was not a fit case for interference under Article 226 of the Constitution.

cases.title: Petitioner v. Chairman, Energy Deptt., U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad (Lucknow Bench)
cases.topic: new connection — process under clause 4.4
cases.holding: A writ seeking to restrain the licensee from granting a new electricity connection to a purchaser during pending civil and NI Act litigation was disposed of with a direction that the respondents follow paragraph 4.4 of the Electricity Supply Code in letter and spirit when processing any application for a new connection. The Court did not restrain the connection and did not decide whether the petitioner was entitled to a hearing.

cases.title: M/s Procapitus Business Park Pvt. Ltd. v. Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Ltd. & 4 Others
cases.topic: occupant connection on indemnity bond
cases.holding: No. The licensee having pointed out that the indemnity bond in Annexure 4.2 under clause 4.4 had not been submitted, the Court disposed of the writ with liberty to complete all legal formalities. As soon as those formalities are completed, the Department is to take an appropriate decision in accordance with law within two weeks, after hearing all concerned including the lessor. A modification dated 2 August 2024 deleted a recital of sub-letting but left the Department free to examine all aspects of the application for a connection in the petitioner's name.
cases.flag: Annexure 4.2 is cited as the indemnity-bond form under clause 4.4. Correction Application No. 2 of 2024 was rejected on 23.04.2024; Modification Application No. 3 of 2024 was allowed on 02.08.2024 only to delete the para-7 sub-letting recital.

cases.title: Smt. Babli Devi v. Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation
cases.topic: occupant connection on indemnity bond
cases.holding: Where the occupant of premises has no title deed, she may apply for a new connection under Clause 4.4 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, with an indemnity bond as provided by Annexure 4.2. If the petitioner so applies within one week, the licensee shall decide that application within one week thereafter. The writ was disposed of on that direction; connection was not ordered.

cases.title: Guddi Kesarwani v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: processing of application for new supply
cases.holding: Clause 4.4(a) of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 governs processing of applications for new supply and requires a complete application with proof of ownership or occupancy (including indemnity as per Annexure 4.2) and, among other documents, owner's consent. The Code is a self-contained enactment with a full-fledged grievance mechanism. The petitioner has a right to seek a new electricity connection under clause 4.4(a). The writ was disposed of without opinion on merits, leaving the petitioner to apply under that clause within a week, with the licensee to examine and remedy any such application strictly in accordance with law preferably within six weeks.

cases.title: Sharmila Prasad v. State of U.P. and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: occupier new connection on indemnity in lieu of owner consent
cases.holding: A lessee, tenant or occupier applying for supply cannot be refused a connection merely for want of the landlord's consent if an indemnity bond is furnished. Clause 4.4 read with Annexure 4.2 and Annexure 4.3 of the Electricity Supply Code 2005 provides for either the owner's consent letter or, in its absence, an indemnity bond. The writ was disposed of directing the competent authority to consider the petitioner's application, if not yet done, in accordance with law within three weeks after hearing parties having stake.

cases.title: Arun Kumar Kashyap v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: occupier connection on indemnity bond without owner consent
cases.holding: Clause 4.4 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, read with Annexures 4.2 and 4.3, provides for either the owner's consent letter or, in its absence, an indemnity bond by the lessee, tenant or occupier. Electricity being essential to life, a family-member occupier cannot be refused a connection merely for want of the father's or owner's NOC; the application is to be considered under that clause after hearing persons having a stake.

cases.title: Kiran v. State of U.P. and others
cases.topic: occupier new connection on indemnity application
cases.holding: The writ court will not itself grant a new connection to an occupier of premises standing in a deceased recorded owner's name. The applicant must move an application as per Annexure 4.2 of Clause 4.4 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, with the requisite indemnity bond; the licensee shall then consider it in accordance with law after hearing parties having stake.

cases.title: GTL Infrastructures Ltd. v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: occupancy documents for new connection to leased telecom-tower sites
cases.holding: Without deciding whether paragraph 4.4 of the 2005 Supply Code requires a registered lease deed, as opposed to owners' consent letters, for a new connection, the Court directed as an interim measure that if the petitioner produces owners' consent letters, requisite affidavits and complies with other conditions, electricity connection shall be provided provisionally, subject to the result of the writ.
cases.flag: Petitioner cited para 4.4(i); Standing Counsel para 4.4(1); sub-clause not identified or settled.

cases.title: Smt. Neelam Pandey v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: occupier connection without owner NOC
cases.holding: Where tenants sought a writ of mandamus for a commercial connection in their names and the licensee objected that no landlord no-objection certificate had been produced, the Court declined the mandamus and relegated the petitioners to an application under para 4.4 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 read with Annexure 4.2, to be acted upon in accordance with law.

cases.title: Alok Mohile v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: tenant connection; owner objection; indemnity bond
cases.holding: Where a tenant’s application for a new electricity connection was stalled on the landlady’s objection, and the licensee stated that the application would be processed on submission of an indemnity bond and other formalities, the Court disposed of the writ directing the respondents to consider the case for grant of connection subject to fulfillment of all necessary requirements. It did not hold that connection must be granted, and did not construe paragraph 4.4 read with Annexure 4.2.
cases.flag: Licensee’s counsel cited 'Paragraph 4.2' of the Supply Code for the indemnity bond; the petitioner relied on paragraph 4.4 read with Annexure 4.2. The Court did not resolve the clause number.

cases.title: Prem Kishore Mehrotra v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: tenant connection without landlord NOC
cases.holding: Recording the licensee's stand that if the tenant-petitioner re-submits his shop-connection application (earlier not accepted for want of landlord NOC) with a certified copy of this order, the Executive Engineer shall accept it, intimate the formalities within ten days, and install the connection immediately on completion of those formalities, the Court disposed of the writ and directed the respondents to consider grant of electricity connection subject to fulfillment of all necessary requirements. The petitioner had invoked para 4.4 read with Annexure 4.2 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: M/S Ratan Housing Development Ltd. v. Kanpur Electricity Supply Company And Others
cases.topic: developer NOC not a mandatory condition for new connection
cases.holding: Mandamus to restrain grant of electricity connections in the landowner's share of flats without the developer-petitioner's NOC was refused. Clause 4.4 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 does not impose a mandatory condition of a developer's no-objection certificate before a connection can be granted. The writ, including the prayer to quash the 14.10.2010 rejection of the petitioner's request, was dismissed.

cases.title: Ghanshyamdas Maheshwari v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: new connection — complete Clause 4.4 process
cases.holding: A writ complaining that a new-connection request is not being entertained will not yield a Court order on the connection. Petitioners may approach the competent authority and complete the process in Clause 4.4 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; that authority is to entertain the request and decide it on merits in accordance with law as expeditiously as possible.

cases.title: New connection refused for want of landlord NOC — fresh consideration on indemnity bond
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: new connection without landlord NOC — indemnity bond
cases.holding: Where a new-connection application is refused for want of the landlord's no-objection certificate, the licensee is to intimate the applicant of the Supply Code requirements including the indemnity bond contemplated by clause 4.4, and to consider the application afresh after those formalities, expeditiously and preferably within three months.

cases.title: Smt. Indu Chawala v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: new connection without landlord NOC; indemnity bond
cases.holding: Clause 4.4 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 permits the licensee, in the absence of the landlord's no-objection certificate, to supply energy on an indemnity bond. The Court did not grant or refuse the connection: it directed the licensee to intimate the indemnity-bond and other requirements under the Code and to consider the petitioners' application afresh, preferably within three months of production of a certified copy of the order.

cases.title: Sriram Dang v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: Clause 4.4 application — time-bound decision
cases.holding: A pending Clause 4.4 application for a new connection, left undecided for more than two and a half months after an earlier High Court direction to apply, is to be decided by the competent authority in accordance with law within a week of a certified copy being filed; the Court did not adjudicate entitlement on merits.

cases.title: Sriram Dang v. State of U.P. And Others
cases.topic: fresh connection application
cases.holding: The Court did not quash the 23 May 2012 rejection or mandamus a connection. It left it open to the petitioner to make a fresh application with all requisites, and directed that if made, the respondents shall consider it in accordance with clause 4.4 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Tanveer Azam v. State of U.P. and others
cases.topic: occupier fresh connection on indemnity without owner consent
cases.holding: Without deciding the occupation dispute, the Court directed the Executive Engineer, Allahabad Division, and the SDO, Sector Kalyani Devi, to provide a fresh electricity connection to the occupier-petitioner on his submitting the indemnity bond on Form 4.2 (Annexure 4.2 to clause 4.4). The application had been pending since 29 May 2012 for want of a rent deed; the connection was to be released within three days of the indemnity. Counsel for the licensee had accepted that sub-clause (a) of para 4.4 permits supply on proof of occupancy or on that indemnity where the owner does not consent.

cases.title: Rahulpuri v. General Manager, Kanpur Electricity Supply Co. Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: tenant connection withheld for landlord litigation
cases.holding: On first listing the Court directed the licensee to give the tenant-petitioner an electricity connection if he had completed the formalities under Clause 4.4 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and not to withhold it merely because of litigation with the landlord, or alternatively to show cause. The writ was later dismissed as infructuous and any interim order stood discharged, without a merits finding on those facts.

cases.title: Hanshraj v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: occupant-connection-on-indemnity-bond
cases.holding: Where a new-connection application is rejected for want of a landlord's no-objection certificate, the licensee is to intimate the applicant of the requirements for supply under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, including the indemnity bond contemplated by clause 4.4, and to consider the application afresh after those formalities, preferably within three months. The writ was disposed of on those observations; connection was not directed.

cases.title: Surjeet Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: occupant connection on indemnity bond without landlord NOC
cases.holding: Refusal of a new connection solely because the landlord has not granted a no-objection certificate does not exhaust the application. Under clause 4.4 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, the licensee may supply energy on an indemnity bond in the absence of that certificate. The licensee is to intimate the applicant of the necessary requirements, including that bond, and consider the application afresh after those formalities, preferably within three months. The writ was disposed of on that direction; the Executive Engineer's rejection was not quashed on the merits, and no connection was mandated.

cases.title: Sriram Dang v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: fresh connection after landlord-dispute disconnection
cases.holding: Where a person seeks a fresh electricity connection after disconnection arising from a landlord dispute, and no completed application has been submitted, it is open to him to apply afresh; the licensee may consider that application in accordance with clause 4.4 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. A writ to decide an earlier representation is disposed of on that footing without directing a connection.

cases.title: Nand Kishor v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.topic: new connection — prescribed-form application
cases.holding: Where no application for a new electric connection has been made in the prescribed form under clause 4.4 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, the Court will not mandamus supply; it will direct that if the petitioner files such an application, the licensee shall consider it in accordance with law within one month.

cases.title: Sanjeev Verma v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: independent connection by occupier without owner consent
cases.holding: A lessee, tenant or occupier who cannot obtain the owner's consent may apply for an independent electricity connection under Clause 4.4 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If the petitioner files a fresh application under that clause, the licensee shall consider it and decide within 15 days of submission.

cases.title: Petitioner v. Managing Director, Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad (Lucknow Bench)
cases.topic: new connection without owner NOC
cases.holding: Mandamus to grant a new connection without the landlord’s NOC was refused. The tenant-petitioner was directed to move an appropriate application in accordance with paragraph 4.4(a)(i) read with Annexure 4.2 of the Electricity Supply Code within two weeks; if so moved, the licensee shall consider it and pass appropriate orders within two weeks thereafter, in accordance with the rules, including inspection of the premises if required.

cases.title: Smt. Chanda v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.topic: processing of application for new supply — occupancy documents
cases.holding: The Court did not direct grant of the 2 kW connection. Liberty was given to apply in the prescribed form under clause 4.4(a)(i) within two weeks, with the documents listed in that clause (proof of ownership or occupancy, including rent receipt, lease, or indemnity in Annexure 4.2). The licensee shall process the application and pass an appropriate order after inspection of the formalities within two weeks thereafter.
cases.flag: Court cites '4.4 (a) (1)'; Code numbering is 4.4(a)(i).

cases.title: Tenant connection without owner NOC — consider under Supply Code 4.4(a)
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: tenant/occupier new connection — owner NOC or indemnity
cases.holding: Where a tenant seeks a new connection and the owner has not given a no-objection, the occupier must take recourse to para 4.4(a) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, including the indemnity-bond course prescribed where there is no NOC. The High Court will not direct the connection itself; if the petitioner completes the Code formalities, the licensee may consider the application and take an appropriate decision within two months in accordance with law.
cases.flag: Order cites para 4.4(a) generally, not sub-clause (i).

UP-2005::4.4(e).topic: delay in connection — right of way

cases.title: Hemant Kumar v. U.P. Electricity Regulatory Commission
cases.topic: delay in connection — right of way
cases.holding: Clause 4.4(e) provides that the licensee shall not be responsible if delay is on account of right of way, land acquisition, technical feasibility, or lack of transmission capacity, over which the licensee has no reasonable control. Villager interference with pole erection and line-laying, requiring police force that was not provided in time, is delay on account of right of way beyond the licensee’s control. UPERC’s waiver of the CGRF’s Rs 100 per day penalty, founded on the Electricity Ombudsman’s report to that effect, was therefore not illegal.

cases.title: Sarvesh Kumar v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
cases.topic: delay in new connection / right of way / suspension of supervising officer
cases.holding: Pending consideration of the writ, the Court treated admitted Right of Way hindrance—the ground in cl. 4.4(e) that the licensee is not responsible for such delay—together with the SDO’s supervisory role and his cooperation in the enquiry, as sufficient to stay the 29.10.2025 suspension until further orders; merits not decided.

cases.title: Anil Kumar v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad (Lucknow Bench)
cases.topic: right of way delay
cases.holding: Where a Sub Divisional Officer was suspended for delay in granting an electricity connection, and it was admitted that right-of-way hindrance caused the delay, the High Court—recording the invocation of clause 4.4(e) that the licensee is not responsible for ROW delay, the officer’s supervisory role, and his undertaking to cooperate in the enquiry—stayed the suspension pending consideration of the writ.

cases.title: Rajendra Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: time-bound disposal of clause 4.4(vi) objection
cases.holding: The Court allowed the writ prayer only to the extent of directing the respondent-authorities to dispose of the petitioner's pending objection under clause 4.4(vi) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 within 15 days in accordance with law, without deciding the merits of the objection.

cases.title: Krishna Murari Gupta v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: fresh application under Clause 4.40
cases.holding: The petitioner was directed to file a fresh application as per Clause 4.40 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, within two weeks; the respondent authorities were directed to act on that application expeditiously; the writ was disposed of without a merits grant or refusal of supply relief.

cases.title: Shahnaj Begum v. U.P. Electricity Regulatory Commission
cases.topic: load reduction
cases.holding: A successive writ seeking reduction of load under clause 4.41(a) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and a declaration that clause 4.41(a)(iv) (latest bill to be paid in full) is arbitrary, is not maintainable where an earlier writ for the same reduction was dismissed; pleas now raised could have been taken in that petition and are barred by constructive res judicata.

UP-2005::4.41(f)(ii).topic: tubewell connection / load reduction — writ vs Superintending Engineer

cases.title: Kaushal Kishore v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: tubewell connection / load reduction — writ vs Superintending Engineer
cases.holding: A writ against the Executive Engineer's refusal of a Sukh Rahat Package tubewell connection, the licensee having treated the matter as load reduction under sub-clause (f)(ii) of clause 4.41, cannot be resolved on the writ side. The consumer is to apply to the Superintending Engineer within seven days of the certified copy; the Superintending Engineer is to consider the cause as early as possible and within one month of the application.
cases.flag: clause recited as Sub-Clause f (ii) under Clause 4.41; numbering as in the order

UP-2005::4.43.topic: enhancement of contracted load — time for decision

cases.title: M/s Shree Radhey Radhey Ispat (Pvt.) Ltd. v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.topic: enhancement of contracted load — time for decision
cases.holding: Where an industrial consumer's application to enhance contracted load from 1500 KVA to 2500 KVA remained undecided despite a technical feasibility report, the Court directed the Chief Engineer, PuVVNL, Allahabad, to pass necessary orders on the application dated 10.7.2009 within 30 days of a certified copy, without examining the merits of the claim.

UP-2005::4.44.topic: mutation of connection after consumer's death

cases.title: Smt. Bhauneesh Singh Gaur v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: mutation of connection after consumer's death
cases.holding: Where the recorded consumer has died and heirs have been substituted in the writ, they must apply for mutation of the connection under clause 4.44; the competent authority is to decide that application within four weeks.

cases.title: Indra Pratap Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: transfer of connection after chak allotment
cases.holding: A claim to have an electricity connection transferred in the claimant's name, including a tube-well connection said to follow a chak allotment, is to be examined and disposed of by the Executive Engineer under clause 4.44(g) of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 in accordance with law; the High Court will not itself grant the transfer on writ.

cases.title: Janardan Dutt Shukla v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: mutation of deceased consumer's connection
cases.holding: Mutation of a deceased consumer's connection under Clause 4.44 requires the applicant to follow the prescribed procedure, furnish no-objection and clear the entire outstanding dues; if those formalities are completed, mutation may be carried out even suo motu. The Court disposed of the writ by directing the petitioner to complete the formalities within one month and apply with requisite fees, and directing the licensee to pass orders under Clause 4.44 within three weeks thereafter.

cases.title: Shakambhari Peetham v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: transfer of connection
cases.holding: Paragraph 4.44 confines transfer of a sanctioned electricity connection to two contingencies: death of the owner of the connection, or that person's consent to transfer in another name. Where the recorded consumer is alive and the document relied on as consent is found not to be genuine, the transfer is in contravention of clause 4.44. Concurrent CGRF and Ombudsman findings to that effect are findings of fact. The writ challenging those orders was dismissed as without merit.

cases.title: Meva Ram v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.topic: Transfer/mutation of a connection on clearance of all dues by the Executive Engineer
cases.holding: Mutation/transfer of a connection under Clause 4.44 requires the clearance of all dues and is to be done by the competent authority, the Executive Engineer of the Division, on completion of the requisite formalities. Here, by consent, the connection is to be transferred to the co-holder's son who undertook all liabilities, the Executive Engineer realising the entire dues before transfer and then forthwith restoring supply.

cases.title: Istiyak v. Superintendent Engineer, E.D.D., P.V.V.N.L. Amroha
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: transfer of connection / mutation of name
cases.holding: Transfer of an electricity connection and mutation of name is governed by Clause 4.44 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. A person seeking transfer or mutation must apply to the prescribed authority under that clause; the authority shall decide the application by a reasoned and speaking order, following the prescribed procedure, expeditiously. The writ was disposed of with those observations and without restoring the connection on the merits.

cases.title: Ganga Sharan v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: mutation of successor after death of recorded consumer
cases.holding: The recovery certificate dated 5 May 2018, issued in the name of a dead person, is quashed. Recovery of electricity dues against a deceased consumer is impermissible. The petitioner, who has inherited the connection, shall apply for mutation of his name under clause 4.44 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, with the requisite documents and an affidavit. After correcting the record, the licensee shall raise demand from the petitioner in accordance with law after considering objections, and conclude those proceedings within six weeks. If thereafter aggrieved by any imposition of liability, the petitioner may pursue remedies under the Electricity Act, 2003 read with the Supply Code. Writ petition allowed subject to those directions.

cases.title: Gopal Krishna v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: mutation of heir after recovery in deceased consumer's name
cases.holding: A recovery citation issued in the name of a deceased recorded consumer cannot be sustained. The heir shall apply under Clause 4.44 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 for correction and mutation of his name on the connection.

cases.title: Ganga Dayal v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.topic: Transfer/mutation of a connection on clearance of arrears by the Executive Engineer
cases.holding: Mutation/transfer of a connection under Clause 4.44 can be done only on clearance of all arrears and completion of the requisite formalities, the competent authority being the Executive Engineer of the Division. On the applicant's prescribed-form application (arrears said to be cleared under a one-time settlement), the competent authority must consider the prayer under Clause 4.44 in accordance with law within three weeks.
cases.flag: This 9.5.2014 order is the one reproduced in SCJ-174 (Meva Ram); the two petitions concern the same tubewell connection and Clause 4.44 transfer.

cases.title: Atiya Begum v. Chairman, U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.topic: mutation of deceased consumer's connection
cases.holding: Mutation of a deceased consumer's name in the electricity record is to be sought by application under Clause 4.44 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 in the Annexure-4.11 form. The writ is disposed of with liberty to file that application before respondent No. 3 within two weeks; if filed, respondent No. 2 shall decide it in accordance with law within four weeks.

cases.title: Naaz Fatima v. Purvanchal Vidhut Vitrana Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: mutation of connection
cases.holding: Where a mutation application under Clause 4.44 remains undecided despite a prior judicial direction to process it, the licensee must grant the applicant a hearing and pass an order under Clause 4.44 in accordance with law within the time fixed by the Court.

cases.title: Ashok Garg v. State of U.P. and Another
cases.topic: Failure to apply for mutation or transfer leaves the recorded consumer in the s.135 frame
cases.holding: No. Clause 4.44 requires an application, with documents and clearance of arrears, before a connection is transferred on change of ownership or occupancy. Admittedly no such mutation or transfer proceedings took place. The petitioner's name continued in U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. records. Combined with the case that he was the director and the owner of the factory who absconded when the meter was checked, and that he had not informed the department of any change of ownership, he cannot escape liability at the section 482 stage. Factual pleas may be raised at trial or on a discharge application.

cases.title: Ram Das v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: transfer of connection; recovery of arrears
cases.holding: The Court found no ground to quash recovery of Rs 1,45,232 on a tubewell connection used by the petitioner though still recorded in the name of his deceased father and others. It left it open to the petitioner to apply for transfer of the connection in his name under clause 4.44 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and disposed of the writ.

cases.title: Sudhir Kumar Mishra v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: shifting of transformer
cases.holding: Shifting of a transformer is governed by Clause 4.45 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ was disposed of with a direction to the Executive Engineer to examine the petitioner's shifting claim in accordance with the Rules and pass an appropriate order within two months; the Court did not grant or refuse shifting on merits.
cases.flag: ambiguous_clause

UP-2005::4.45-A.topic: consumer-funded works for wire change or transformer

cases.title: Dhruv Kumar v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: consumer-funded works for wire change or transformer
cases.holding: Writ disposed with a direction to respondent No. 2 to consider the petitioner's claim for change of wires or affixation of a transformer in accordance with the procedure prescribed under clause 4.45-A of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, within six weeks of production of a certified copy; the Court neither directed the work nor refused mandamus on merits.
cases.flag: Cited as 'section 4.45-A of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code Act, 2005'; the Code is not an Act, and hyphenated 4.45-A is recorded as spoken.

UP-2005::4.49.topic: Load reduction with disputed arrears — Bond acceptable; effective date; agreed reduction cannot be defeated

cases.title: Kanpur Electricity Supply Co. Ltd. & Anr. v. M/s L.M.L. Limited & Ors.
cases.topic: Load reduction with disputed arrears — Bond acceptable; effective date; agreed reduction cannot be defeated
cases.holding: No. The unamended Clause 4.49 (in force on 19.4.2006) allowed the consumer to secure disputed arrears by a Bank Guarantee OR a Bond OR any instrument to the licensee's satisfaction; the reduction took effect from the first day of the month after sanction (Clause 4.41(e), i.e. 1.5.2006). Having agreed to the reduction and known of the consumer's Relief-Undertaking/Sick-Company status and the BIFR order, the licensee acted unfairly in rejecting the Bond, insisting on a Bank Guarantee and continuing to bill on the higher (8 MVA) load; the load stood reduced.

cases.title: Sigma Castings Ltd. & Another v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Others (with Kundan Castings (P) Ltd.; PVVNL v. Vidyut Lokpal; M/s Shyam Ferrous Ltd.)
cases.topic: A condition requiring a bank guarantee for alleged 'arrears' as a precondition to releasing enhanced load is quashed where the underlying assessment giving rise to the alleged arrears was already conclusively revised and paid, with the revision having attained finality; the licensee may, however, later demand a guarantee for genuinely subsequently-arising dues
cases.holding: The Rs. 3.74 crore bank-guarantee condition imposed on Sigma Castings (and, derivatively, on its purported sister-concern Kundan Castings) was quashed, since the underlying 1995 theft-based assessment had been conclusively revised down (from Rs. 3.39 crore to Rs. 9.68 lakh) and paid, with the revision upheld and attained finality in a 2006-dismissed writ petition by UPPCL — a fact PVVNL's counter affidavit did not deny. However, it was left open to PVVNL to require the consumer to clear (or furnish a guarantee for) any dues genuinely accrued since the December 2007 office memorandum (e.g. dishonoured cheques, peak-hour penalties, unpaid current bills), since raising this did not amount to impermissibly supporting the original order on undisclosed grounds.

cases.title: Kamakhya Steels v. PVVNL — Clause 4.49 temporary-connection writ dismissed as infructuous
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: temporary connection — clause 4.49 as precondition
cases.holding: The writ challenging the licensee's insistence on Clause 4.49 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 as a precondition for a temporary 11 kV connection was dismissed as infructuous by efflux of time, and the 27 April 2015 interim restraining that insistence was vacated. Whether surplus already deposited with the licensee made the demanded bank guarantee unjustified was not decided.

cases.title: Maruti Papers Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.topic: additional load—stayed dues
cases.holding: The amounts claimed as due having been stayed in Writ Petition No. 25603 of 2007, which remained pending, the respondents cannot insist on a bank guarantee equivalent to those amounts and cannot on that ground refuse additional load under paragraph 4.49 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Additional load of 2000 KVA directed to be released without that bank guarantee; other charges payable by the petitioner.

cases.title: Silverton Pulp — cl. 4.49 cannot block additional load for stayed arrears
cases.topic: additional load refused for stayed arrears
cases.holding: While alleged arrears remain stayed and the related writ is sub judice, the licensee cannot, under clause 4.49, refuse additional load by demanding a bank guarantee equivalent to those stayed dues, or refuse the load on that ground alone; other charges shall still be paid.

cases.title: Shri Satguru Metalloys (Pvt.) Ltd. v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.topic: Bank-guarantee demand on load enhancement — interim stay; vires challenge
cases.holding: Prima facie the matter requires consideration. As the final assessment had been set aside on appeal and no fresh assessment passed, the Court stayed the direction to furnish the Clause 4.49 bank guarantee unless a fresh assessment is passed in terms of the appellate order. The challenge to Clause 4.49 as violative of Article 14 was left for consideration.
cases.flag: Interim order only; the vires of Clause 4.49 and the demand are reserved for final hearing.

cases.title: M/s L.M.L. Ltd. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.topic: A licensee's load-reduction decision stands approved; only ministerial steps remain; no UPERC approval needed; effective from the first day of the following month
cases.holding: The competent authority decided to reduce the load at the signed meeting of 19.4.2006 (Annexure-4) and pointed out no shortcoming in the application or non-compliance with Clauses 4.41 and 4.49; the reduction therefore stood approved and any further action was only ministerial. No approval of the U.P. Electricity Regulatory Commission was required for a licensee's decision to reduce load, so the reference to the Commission was a redundant exercise that could not affect the rights that accrued to the petitioner on 19.4.2006. Under Clause 4.41(b) the decision was to be communicated within thirty days, and under Clause 4.41(e) the effective date of the reduction is the first day of the month following the licensee's decision, i.e. 1.5.2006. Continuing to bill at 8 MVA after production had stopped was unjust and not in accord with the 19.4.2006 decision.
cases.flag: Source judgment is not paragraph-numbered; pins reference the printed page numbers of the source (the judgment runs on internal pages 2-20, preceded by three order-sheet pages). Clause 4.41 is reproduced at pp.7-8 and Clause 4.49 (unamended) at p.8.

cases.title: M/s L.M.L. Ltd. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.topic: The Code as at the application date governs; bond or 'any instrument' (including an affidavit) sufficed, not only a bank guarantee
cases.holding: The application dated 31.3.2006 is governed by Clause 4.49 as it then stood, which permitted submission of a bank guarantee, or a bond, or any instrument to the satisfaction of the licensee for an amount equivalent to the pending dues; since under Clause 4.41(b) the decision was due within thirty days, the unamended clause applied. The requirement of only a bank guarantee was introduced by the amendment of 14.9.2006 and did not govern this application. The word 'instrument', undefined in the Electricity Act, 2003 and the Supply Code, is wide enough to include the affidavit of undertaking filed by the company's whole-time director. The respondents' later demands for a bank guarantee (letters of 4.10.2006 and 20.3.2007, resting on the amended Code) were therefore of no consequence.

cases.title: Barnala Steel Industries Ltd. v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. and Anr.
cases.topic: Additional security is not 'dues' under Clause 4.49; no bank guarantee for it
cases.holding: No. Following the coordinate Division Bench in Tehri Girders Ltd. v. PVVNL (unchallenged by any SLP), Clause 4.49 is attracted only where recovery of 'dues' has been stayed; additional security is not a recoverable due (the sole consequence of its non-payment being non-release of the additional load and discontinuance of supply). The demand of a bank guarantee for the additional-security amount was therefore not in accordance with law and was quashed, the consumer being directed to comply with the sanction's other conditions.

cases.title: Tehri Girders Limited and another v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited and others (with R.A. Castings, Sikka Papers and connected petitions)
cases.topic: Clause 4.49 not attracted to additional security, which is not 'dues'; no bank guarantee for it
cases.holding: No. Clause 4.49 is attracted only where a court/forum has stayed the 'recovery of any dues'; the condition precedent is that the amount be a due recoverable by some process under the Act or the Code. Additional security is not such a due: its non-payment merely results in non-release of the additional load and discontinuance of supply, with no recovery process provided. Clause 4.49 is therefore not attracted, and the demand of a bank guarantee for the stayed additional-security amount was unjustified; the petitioners are entitled to release of any bank guarantee already furnished.

cases.title: M/s. Suvidha Engineers India Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.topic: Clause 4.49 is intra vires - a protective provision, not a recovery mechanism; does not offend s.127(2), s.56(2) or judicial review
cases.holding: No. Clause 4.49 is intra vires. It is a protective provision to insulate the licensee against apprehended future loss, triggered only because the consumer applied for enhancement of load; it neither enforces recovery of the stayed amount nor overrides the court's stay, so it does not abridge judicial review (Cauvery, S.S. Bola, Indian Aluminium distinguished). It does not violate Section 127(2) (which governs the one-third pre-deposit for an assessment appeal), nor Section 56(2) (the two-year recovery bar is inapplicable, since a stay of recovery presupposes a recoverable amount). The vires challenge was refused and the petitions dismissed, with liberty to represent on the bank-guarantee quantum.

cases.title: M/s Shree Gopala Iron India Pvt. Ltd. v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: reduction of load where arrears stayed
cases.holding: Rejection of an application to reduce contract load solely because arrear dues had not been paid and other writ petitions were pending is not in consonance with clause 4.49 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Where recovery of dues is stayed, the licensee shall permit reduction or enhancement of load (and release new connection, reconnection or permanent disconnection) subject to a bank guarantee of the pending dues, an agreement on extension or invocation of the guarantee, and levy of surcharge, and shall not keep the application pending. The rejection was set aside and a fresh order directed in accordance with law.

UP-2005::4.4f(i).topic: gift deed does not wipe electricity dues; application processed after clearing dues

cases.title: Kirti Kushwaha v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: gift deed does not wipe electricity dues; application processed after clearing dues
cases.holding: Mere execution of a gift deed in the applicant's favour does not exclude liability to pay electricity dues on the premises. Clause 4.4f(i) of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 provides that an application can be processed only after dues are cleared. The writ petition seeking a fresh connection without paying remaining dues was dismissed.
cases.flag: Cited as Clause 4.4f(i); unpunctuated numbering is ambiguous (possibly 4.4(f)(i)). Not silently recast as catalog 4.44 or 4.4(e).

UP-2005::4.5(d).code: U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 (Clause 4.5(d)) read with the Works of Licensees Rules, 2006 (Clause 3)
UP-2005::4.5(d).clause: 4.5(d) (landowner's right to object to a supply line over his land) read with Works of Licensees Rules, 2006, Clause 3 (resolution mechanism)
UP-2005::4.5(d).topic: A landowner's objection to an electric pole/line erected on his private property to supply neighbouring residents is to be resolved by the District Magistrate/Commissioner of Police/authorised officer under Clause 3 of the Works of Licensees Rules, 2006, balancing his Clause 4.5(d) right against the public interest in the electrification work

cases.title: Priy Shankar Pandey v. State of U.P. & 4 Others
cases.topic: A landowner's objection to an electric pole/line erected on his private property to supply neighbouring residents is to be resolved by the District Magistrate/Commissioner of Police/authorised officer under Clause 3 of the Works of Licensees Rules, 2006, balancing his Clause 4.5(d) right against the public interest in the electrification work
cases.holding: The landowner has a right under Clause 4.5(d) of the Supply Code to object to a supply line being laid over his land; that objection is to be resolved under Clause 3 of the Works of Licensees Rules, 2006 by the District Magistrate, Commissioner of Police, or other authorised officer, who must balance the landowner's rights against the public interest in not unduly stalling the electrification work. The petitioner was directed to file an application under Clause 3 (with a supporting affidavit, documents, and photographs) within three weeks; the authority was directed to decide the application within eight weeks after hearing all necessary parties, with status quo to be maintained in the interim.

cases.title: Shivmahraj v. State of U.P. & 6 Others
cases.topic: Companion ruling to SCJ-104 — identical holding on a parallel landowner objection to a new power line/pole for village electrification
cases.holding: As in SCJ-104: the landowner has a right under Clause 4.5(d) of the Supply Code to object to a supply line/pole being erected over his land; that objection is to be resolved under Clause 3 of the Works of Licensees Rules, 2006 by the District Magistrate or other authorised officer, balancing the landowner's rights against the public interest in the electrification work. The petitioner was directed to appear before the District Magistrate (already scheduled to hear similar grievances) with all relevant material, to be heard and a decision passed after hearing all parties including the licensee respondents, with status quo maintained in the interim.
cases.flag: Near-identical companion order to SCJ-104; recorded compactly given the substantially duplicate reasoning and holding.

cases.title: Rizwan Ahmad v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: landowner objection to supply line
cases.holding: A grievance that a supply line being installed for a colony is hazardous to the petitioner's residence, and that an objection under clause 4.5(d) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 has not been considered, is to be examined by the concerned electricity officer (respondent no.4), who shall pass appropriate orders on installation of the line; the writ petition is disposed of with that direction and without a finding on the alignment.

cases.title: Hridesh Kumar v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: landowner objection to supply line
cases.holding: Without deciding whether clause 4.5(d) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 barred the licensee from laying a tubewell supply line over the landowners’ plot without a third-party no-objection, the Court disposed of the writ by directing the Executive Engineer to consider and decide the pending representation in accordance with law, after hearing, within one month, and restrained the respondents from taking the electricity line over the plot until that decision.

cases.title: Abhimanyu Singh v. State of U.P. & 7 Others
cases.topic: Alternate-route cost differential on a third-party objection is borne by the applicant
cases.holding: Direct transmission from the distribution main to the point of supply is at the licensee's cost. Under Clause 4.5(d), where the supply line would go over a third party's property and an objection requires an alternate route, the applicant must obtain the no-objection or bear the cost differential of the different route. The licensee must furnish particulars of the cost of the direct and the longer route, and demand only the differential; any excess already deposited is adjusted against future bills, and the supply given within two weeks.

cases.title: Kumar Ajay Singh v. State of U.P. & 10 Others
cases.topic: Pending a title dispute over the land a proposed supply line would cross, the licensee is to seek a no-objection from the revenue authority in seisin and also to cost an alternative route
cases.holding: The Court did not decide the title or grant the connection. Clause 4.5(d) was reproduced: if the supply line would go over third-party property the applicant shall obtain a no-objection, failing which the licensee may adopt a different route and the applicant bears the cost differential. Because the Tehsildar is already in seisin of the ownership controversy on remand from an appeal, the licensee is to apply to that Tehsildar for a no-objection; the Tehsildar is to decide after notice to the private respondents and the Gram Sabha, and to file an affidavit enclosing the decision. Independently, the licensee is to work out an alternative route and the cost differential on affidavit. Both affidavits are to be accepted on the adjourned date (6 July 2026).
cases.flag: Interlocutory only — listed 6.7.2026. Not a final holding that Clause 4.5(d) requires the licensee (rather than the applicant) to obtain the NOC, though the direction in this case is that the supply company apply to the Tehsildar. Companion cluster: SCJ-104 / SCJ-120 (landowner objection; those went to the DM under the Works of Licensees Rules) and SCJ-169 (cost differential of the longer route). This order does not invoke the 2006 Rules.

cases.title: Smt. Mewati And Anr. v. Anil Kumar Singh, Executive Engineer, M.V.V.N.L., Tanda, Ambedkar Nagar
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
cases.topic: Contempt of a Clause 4.5(d) representation-direction is not made out once the intervening connection-charge letter is revoked and that is accepted as compliance
cases.holding: No. The 02.11.2020 writ in Writ Petition No. 18654 (M/B) of 2020 directed the Executive Engineer to decide the representation in the light of Clause 4.5(d) of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 within six weeks. The 05.01.2022 letter asking the applicants to deposit Rs. 1,36,350 as the charge for issuance of electricity connections was revoked by order dated 06.04.2024 of Shri Mohit Kumar, Executive Engineer, MVVNL, Tanda, Ambedkar Nagar. Opposite-party counsel submitted that the writ had thereby been complied with; applicants' counsel did not dispute that. No contempt was made out. The application was dismissed and consigned to record.
cases.flag: Contempt dismissed as having lost efficacy. The Court recites the earlier writ's Clause 4.5(d) direction and treats revocation of the 05.01.2022 deposit letter as compliance; it does not construe 4.5(d) or decide the pole objection. Source PDF also contains listing orders of 03.12.2022 (Rajeev Singh J.), 07.02.2024, 15.02.2024 and 12.03.2024 (Shree Prakash Singh J.), and 10.04.2024 (Rajeev Singh J., bailable warrant / personal presence); the judgment under record is 21.05.2024 (2024:AHC-LKO:38354).

cases.title: Shiv Shankar Pandey v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: landowner objection to supply line over private land
cases.holding: Clause 4.5(d) of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 gives any person over whose land an electricity supply line may be laid a right to object. Clause 3 of the Works of Licensees Rules, 2006 then empowers the District Magistrate (or Commissioner of Police or other authorised officer) to resolve the objection so that land rights are not violated and public work is not unduly stalled. Without deciding the line's location or the objection on merits, the Court directed the petitioner to apply under Clause 3 to the District Magistrate within one week; the Magistrate was to hear all necessary parties, call for reports, and decide within three weeks of compliance, with status quo meantime.

cases.title: Bhikari Lal Pal v. U.P. Power Corporation
cases.topic: alternative route where landowner withholds NOC
cases.holding: Where the applicant cannot obtain a no-objection from the person across whose property the supply line must be drawn, clause 4.5(d) requires the line to be drawn by an alternative route on deposit of the additional estimated amount. The petitioner may obtain a no-objection from Ram Sewak or apply for an alternative route with a fresh estimate; if he so applies with a certified copy of the order, the respondents shall decide the matter within four weeks. The writ is disposed of on that direction, without mandating the original alignment.

UP-2005::4.6.topic: Breach of paragraph 4.6(h): non-transparency and harassment in releasing a new connection

cases.title: Kanpur Electricity Supply Company Ltd. & Another v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: Breach of paragraph 4.6(h): non-transparency and harassment in releasing a new connection
cases.holding: Yes. The DCGRF recorded a finding of fact that the department had shown no transparency in releasing the new connection and that the consumer had been unnecessarily harassed by non-compliance with the requirement of paragraph 4.6(h) of the Supply Code, 2005; the connection had been denied for reasons not at all applicable to the grant of a new connection. The High Court found this approach legally unsustainable and untenable and affirmed the finding.

cases.title: Smt. Madhu Rani Agrawal v. State of U.P. & 5 Others
cases.topic: Licensee performs the installation (within 500 m); consumer cannot self-supply equipment
cases.holding: No. Under the regulations and the Cost Data Book, installation up to 500 metres from the pole is done by the Department; and Clause 4.6 provides that the new-connection estimate includes the charges of laying the line, distribution mains, material and system-loading charges, which covers poles and transformer. The Department is obliged to carry out the installation and the consumer to pay for it; the plea to self-install (the installation being within 500 metres) fails.

cases.title: Executive Engineer, Electricity Urban Distribution Division IInd v. Electricity Ombudsman, Lucknow & Ors.
cases.topic: Departmental delay cannot shift the consumer to a costlier feeder or a fresh estimate; connection on the old estimate
cases.holding: No. The estimate is valid for three months (Clause 4.6(a)) and the connection ought to have been drawn and metered within the stipulated period after the applicant completed formalities and deposited the amount; the department's own delay and the consequential change of area cannot authorise it to change the feeder or demand a fresh estimate. Proviso 4.6(g) bars charging estimates in excess where they were sanctioned before a revision of charges. The Ombudsman rightly directed connection to the tube well on the old estimate from the urban feeder (no restriction in the Code against supplying a private tube well from an urban feeder), billed under rate schedule LMV-5.3(b).

cases.title: Ram Kishun v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: new connection — full deposit work / private tube well
cases.holding: Where the licensee contends that no proper application under clause 4.6(e) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 has been made for a private tube-well connection on full-deposit-work (15% supervision charge) terms, the writ court will not keep the mandamus pending or call for a counter-affidavit. It remains open to the consumer to make a proper application under clause 4.6(e), which the licensee shall consider.

cases.title: M/s Ganesh Polytex Ltd. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: estimate disputes — alternative remedy
cases.holding: Disputes regarding an estimate, including every factor in the estimate such as system loading charges, must be referred under clause 4.6(f) to the authority one level higher than the sanctioning authority and, if the applicant remains aggrieved, to the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum. A writ seeking refund of system loading charges and demand charges, without exhausting those remedies and without pleading any ground to overreach them, is not maintainable; the consumer is relegated to that statutory hierarchy.

cases.title: M/s Silverton Paper Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: supervision of line shifting after road widening
cases.holding: A consumer of an independent feeder cannot, while lines are still being relocated for road widening, invoke writ jurisdiction to supervise pole placement or quality of work under para 4.6 of the Supply Code. Shifting of the line and assurance of uninterrupted supply is a purely administrative matter. Directions will not issue unless delay, negligence, or a genuine and apparent apprehension is shown.
cases.flag: Order cites 'Para 4.6 (e) and (ii)' of the Electricity Supply Code 2005 (mixed lettered and roman sub-clauses); keyed to catalog hit UP-2005::4.6 without resolving sub-clause numbering.

cases.title: Pradeep Kumar v. State of U.P. and others
cases.topic: CGRF forum for revised-estimate disputes
cases.holding: A dispute about a revised estimate, as distinct from a bill, is to be considered by the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum under clause 4.6 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the High Court will not interfere in writ jurisdiction. Dismissal does not affect any right to approach the Forum.

cases.title: Shail Upadhyay v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: private land used for private-industry feeder
cases.holding: The writ challenging the ADM (City) Bareilly's compensation and sale-deed directions over 58 sq m used, without consent, for a re-aligned feeder to a private industry was dismissed as not pressed/infructuous after the parties reported a compromise. The Court did not examine the compromise or the petitioners' case under Supply Code cl. 4.6(E)(ii) and s.67 of the Electricity Act, 2003, and vacated the interim stay of the ADM order and of energising the line.
cases.flag: Petitioners cited Clause 4.6(E)(ii); catalog also maps 4.6(f) and 4.66.

UP-2005::4.6(e).topic: fresh consideration after removal of oversized transformer

cases.title: Smt. Sai Kiran Khanna v. State of U.P. And 4 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: fresh consideration after removal of oversized transformer
cases.holding: On the parties’ statements that the petitioner had removed or would remove a 160 kVA transformer, the Court disposed of the writ by directing the Executive Engineer to inspect the site and, if that transformer had already been removed, to consider the petitioner’s case afresh in accordance with law. The Court did not decide the petitioner’s claim under Clause 4.6(e) that LT load up to 50 kW must be developed by the licensee without supervision charges.

cases.title: Karuna Nidhi Tiwari v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.topic: connection charges — next higher authority
cases.holding: Issues as to the total money demanded for providing an electricity connection can be examined by the authority one step higher than the authority who made the impugned order, under clause 4.6(f) of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The petitioner was permitted to approach that higher authority within two weeks; on such representation the higher authority shall consider and decide the same in accordance with law by a reasoned speaking order, preferably within eight weeks.

cases.title: Munni Lal Patel v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: estimate-bill-dispute-alternative-remedy
cases.holding: Where the consumer doubts the correctness of a bill or estimate, Clause 4.6(f) supplies the remedy: refer the dispute to the authority one level higher than the sanctioning authority, and if still aggrieved, to the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum. A writ under Article 226 for bill correction is not to be entertained unless an exceptional circumstance is shown; the consumer is relegated to that Code path, and any application so made is to be heard and disposed of in accordance with law without delay.

cases.title: Gajendra Prasad Bhatnagar v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: estimate disputes
cases.holding: Disputes over the estimate for grant of a new connection, being purely factual, are to be adjudicated under Clause 4.6(f) by the competent authority one level higher than the sanctioning authority and thereafter the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum; the writ court will not decide them and will relegate the consumer to that authority (here, the Superintending Engineer) to consider and decide the representation by a reasoned speaking order in accordance with law.

cases.title: Dharmendra Singh Chauhan v. State of U.P. and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: pole on consumer land / shared deposit / CGRF
cases.holding: A writ court will not decide on merits a dispute over a deposit demanded because a distribution pole has been installed on the petitioner's land, where the licensee says the estimate is payable by all consumers and not by the petitioner alone. The petitioner is to apply to the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum within seven days of obtaining a certified copy; the Forum shall call representatives of the Electricity Department, Nagar Nigam and Gram Panchayat and finalise the issue under clause 4.6(f) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 in their presence within one month thereafter.

UP-2005::4.66.topic: temporary disconnection without hearing; 50% deposit and grievance application

cases.title: Mohd. Zubair v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: temporary disconnection without hearing; 50% deposit and grievance application
cases.holding: Applying Clauses 4.66, 4.66.1 and 4.66.2 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2002, where supply was allegedly disconnected temporarily without hearing, the writ was disposed of directing that if the consumer deposited 50% of the 29 January 2011 bill with a grievance application within one month of the certified copy, the authority would decide within one month after fullest opportunity of hearing by a reasoned order, and reconnect within 72 hours if the consumer succeeded.
cases.flag: ambiguous: court cited Supply Code-2002 Clauses 4.66, 4.66.1 and 4.66.2 (2005 Code in force in 2011; numbering unverified).

cases.title: Allahabad U.P. Gramin Bank v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: new connection — clause 4.8 compliance
cases.holding: Compliance with clause 4.8, together with clause 4.4, is the condition upon which the licensee is to consider a new-connection application in accordance with law.

cases.title: KPB Metals Private Limited v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.topic: Extending a sanctioned connection to newly-acquired adjoining plots is a barred change of site, not an internal change within the premises
cases.holding: It is a change in the site of the sanctioned load, which Clause 4.8(d)(i) does not permit. Clause 4.45(c) applies only to changes in wiring/apparatus/service line within the premises for which the connection was accorded; 'premises' under Clause 2.2(ss) is the area (here khasra 267M) for which the connection was applied for/sanctioned for a single consumer. Plots 265 and 266, acquired after the sanction, did not become part of those premises merely by being contiguous, so Clause 4.45(c) was inapplicable and the Executive Engineer rightly invoked Clause 4.8(d) to reject the request. The consumer may apply afresh for the new premises, or seek disconnection and a fresh connection for the entire premises.

UP-2005::4.9.topic: metering before bush bar; housing-society separate connection

cases.title: Smt. Rajeshwari Pandey v. Kanpur Electric Supply Co. Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: metering before bush bar; housing-society separate connection
cases.holding: The letter of the Director (Commercial), U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. dated 6 July 2013 on installation of a metering system before the bush bar is strictly in conformity with clause 4.9 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Sub-clause (g) of clause 4.9 only permits an individual resident of a housing society to seek an electrical connection separate from the licensed supplier. The letter, written to avoid theft of electrical energy, is in the larger public interest. The writ petition was dismissed.

cases.title: Jasbeer Kaur v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: individual connection in multi-storeyed building
cases.holding: Without entering the merits, an occupier's claim to a fresh individual electricity connection in a multi-storeyed colony after disconnection of the builder-provided supply is to be redressed under Clause 4.9. The Court recited Clause 4.9(a) as permitting a person residing in such a plot or multi-storeyed building, multiplex, marriage hall, cooperative group housing society or colony, with load exceeding 25 kW, to apply for an individual connection, and directed the Executive Engineer to decide the pending application in accordance with law, preferably within one month.

cases.title: M/s Pawan Putra Floor Mill v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.topic: pole reinstallation after accidental damage
cases.holding: A consumer grievance of disconnection after accidental damage to an electricity pole, including reinstallation of the pole, can be redressed by approaching the competent authority under clause 4.9 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, read with clause 6.5; the Executive Engineer shall decide the matter within two months of production of a certified copy of the order.

cases.title: Gaurav Arya v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: New connection in a multi-storied complex
cases.holding: Where a shop occupant in a multi-storied complex seeks a new electricity connection and the licensee invokes Clause 4.9 as requiring the applicant to bear expenses, the Court, without deciding that clause, directed the licensee to examine the claim in accordance with the rules and issue instructions for such connection as may be permissible, within six weeks.

cases.title: Devanshu Bose v. Electricity Ombudsman, Lucknow and 4 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: gated-colony-prepaid-meters-reference-meter-and-permitted-line-loss
cases.holding: Under clause (j) of amended Part A (Electricity Supply Code (Thirteenth Amendment), 2018), separate connections to individuals follow a prescribed new-connection application; the licensee may install a reference meter; energy difference up to 4%/5% is allowed for transformation and LT losses; difference beyond that for a billing cycle is added to common-services consumption. A resident alleging that the difference is theft must demonstrate the theft and indicate the point from which it is taking place; the negative cannot be proved. The supply company must inspect and file an affidavit that there is no theft in the residences. Rejoinder and that affidavit to be taken on the adjourned date. Listed 9 July 2026 at 2:00 p.m. The 28 April 2026 direction for disclosure of the developer/RWA common-facility application under Clause 4.9 Part A(j) remains part of the interlocutory record. No final view on recoverability.
cases.flag: Interlocutory. The 21 May 2026 order cites the Thirteenth Amendment, 2018, clause (j) under amended Part A (reference meter; 4%/5% loss). The 28 April 2026 order cited Clause 4.9 Part A(j) of the 2005 Code (developer/RWA common-facility application). Keyed to UP-2005::4.9. No final ratio.

cases.title: Dr. Mohammad Afsar Khan And Another v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited, Varanasi And Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: 51% of consumers on a single-point supply must apply together for conversion to multi-point; a lone shop-buyer has no cause of action for a direct connection
cases.holding: No. The building already had a single-point connection availed by the owner/builder on prior consent of unit buyers. The Electricity Supply Code (Thirteenth Amendment), 2018 requires that conversion of that single-point supply to individual (multi-point) connections be applied for by 51% of the consumers drawing from the single point. The petitioners, with only 10% of such consumers, and without a pleaded case that they had not agreed to the single-point arrangement — their sale deed of 17 February 2024 (clause 21) recording the vendor's one-point connection and the vendees' obligation to install a prepaid meter — had no cause of action for a direct connection. The writ petition is dismissed.
cases.flag: Operative dismissal is the unnumbered 8 September 2025 order (Arindam Sinha and Prashant Kumar JJ.), which reproduces paras 1–3 of the 26 August 2025 order. Licensee relied on 'clause 4.28 in part-B'; UPERC said the application was under Clause 4.9, not 4.28(d). The Court applied the 13th Amendment 51% conversion rule without resolving that numbering dispute. Source PDF also contains listing/impleadment orders of 28.4.2025, 7.5.2025 and 21.5.2025 (Saraf and Srivastava JJ.) and a 10.2.2026 order on Civil Misc. Correction Application No. 4 of 2025 (respondent description corrected to 'and others'; no change to the 28.4.2025 'builders' label).

cases.title: Nagendra Singh Gautam v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: new-connection estimate; application-date rate versus later Code amendment
cases.holding: No. The Court did not decide whether the petitioner is liable at Rs.35 or Rs.70 per square foot. It disposed of the writ by permitting a representation to the Managing Director of the supply company within two weeks; the MD is to decide strictly in accordance with law after notice and hearing within two weeks of receipt. If the grievance is genuine, the estimate is to be modified, deposited, and the connection installed without delay; if not, a reasoned speaking order is to be passed.
cases.flag: Source PDF also contains 14.07.2025 (Arindam Sinha and Dr. Y.K. Srivastava JJ.: no reason to interfere with the 19.05.2025 PLA order; adjournment for the licensee to be heard or rectify charges) and 30.10.2025 (Prakash Padia and Vivek Saran JJ.: list 04.11.2025; respondents 2 and 3 to remain present). Application date is internally inconsistent: 12.11.2025 para 3 says 04.09.2024; paras 4 and 8 say 04.09.2025 (para 4 also '04.09.20225'). The 19.05.2025 PLA order is consistent only with an application before that date. Licensee on 14.07.2025 placed the amendment in 'January last'; the 12.11.2025 order dates it 27.02.2025.

cases.title: Vijay Kumar Sarin v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: application for reconnection or fresh connection
cases.holding: A writ of mandamus directing reconnection or a new electricity connection will not be entertained where the occupier has not made an application to the licensee in accordance with the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If such an application is made, the licensee is to consider it expeditiously.

cases.title: Dr. Vinay Kumar Goyal v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: load calculation for new commercial connection
cases.holding: After the Chief Engineer rejected, during pendency, the petitioner's application for release of 24 KW load, the Court dismissed the writ (which had challenged a 109 KW sanction against a 24 KW application, invoking Clause 4.9) and the amendment application. Liberty was reserved to challenge both that subsequent rejection and the originally impugned 19.1.2012 memorandum and 8.2.2012 TC letter. The Clause 4.9 load-calculation dispute was not decided.

cases.title: Mohd. Afzal v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing complaint
cases.holding: Where an electricity bill and subsequent demand are challenged on the plea that no connection stands in the petitioner's name and the notice records a wrong father's name, and the controversy requires adjudication of facts, the High Court will not decide the dispute in writ jurisdiction. The consumer is to file a written objection before the Executive Engineer, who shall consider it and take a decision within the time fixed; coercive steps on the demand are stayed for two months.

cases.title: Takesh Kumar v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: instalment of arrears
cases.holding: A petitioner seeking to deposit unpaid electricity dues in instalments after the consumer’s death may avail the instalment remedy under clause 5.14 of the Electricity Supply Code; the writ is disposed of leaving that course open.

cases.title: Jay Narayan v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill correction on pending representation
cases.holding: Where a consumer disputes a bill on the ground that previous payments were not adjusted and a representation is pending when a recovery citation issues, the Executive Engineer is to treat that representation as an application for correction of the bill under Clause 5.5 and decide it by a reasoned speaking order within two weeks of production of a certified copy; recovery remains in abeyance for four weeks.
cases.flag: Clause 5.5 cited for bill-correction of unadjusted payments; recorded as stated, not recast.

UP-2005::5.6.topic: Check-meter procedure under Clause 5.6 is triggered only by the consumer's request; silence on the meter's slow-running finding forfeits the objection

cases.title: M/S Krown Bakers India Pvt. Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam & Anr.
cases.topic: Check-meter procedure under Clause 5.6 is triggered only by the consumer's request; silence on the meter's slow-running finding forfeits the objection
cases.holding: No. Clause 5.6 gives the licensee the right to test a meter on reasonable doubt of accuracy, and separately gives the consumer the right to request testing (including installation of a check meter) if he doubts the meter's accuracy; the obligation to install a check meter arises only on the consumer's request. Since the consumer had full knowledge from the sealing certificate that the meter was found running slow, never disputed that finding or sought a check-meter test — his representations and applications (including a request for installment payment) challenged only the bill, not the meter's operational status — he cannot now contend that the bill is vitiated for non-compliance with Clause 5.6.

cases.title: M/S Modern Rice Mill v. MVVNL & Anr.
cases.topic: Clause 5.6 applies to testing of 'any meter', not only a known-defective one; meter-manufacturer's own lab is not an 'independent laboratory'; procedural safeguards must be followed
cases.holding: (a) No, the heading does not confine the clause: a marginal heading/side-note is not a legitimate aid to statutory construction (Chandler v. DPP; Chandroji Rao v. CIT; Padmaraje R. Kadambande v. CIT; Guntaiah v. Hambamma; followed in Ghanshyam Gupta v. United India Insurance). Clause 5.6(a) gives the licensee the right to test 'any meter' on reasonable doubt of accuracy, which includes a meter that has stopped recording despite continued consumption. (b) No — testing by the meter's own manufacturer is not testing by an 'independent laboratory'; a commercial manufacturer with a business interest in its product's reputation for being tamper/pilfer-proof cannot be an unbiased arbiter, offending the principle that no one may be a judge in his own cause (following the Patna High Court's JMD Alloys Ltd. v. Bihar SEB, which deprecated testing of Secure Meters by their own manufacturer as creating a strong bias). Further, the Clause 5.6(d) safeguards (advance notice of the testing date, opportunity for the consumer/representative to be present, signature on the test result sheet) were not followed before the manufacturer's report was obtained, and this defect was never addressed by either the Assessing Officer or the Appellate Authority.

cases.title: M/S Santosh Preservation Pvt. Ltd. & Anr. v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Anr.
cases.topic: Independent-laboratory testing right under Clause 5.6(c)(iii) applies only where the tampering/defect conclusion rests on a test report, not where tampering is patent on inspection
