cases.holding: No. Clause 5.6(c)(iii)'s independent-testing option exists to rule out bias where the conclusion of a fast/slow-running or tampered meter is arrived at on the basis of a test report (i.e. where the defect is not visible on inspection and needs laboratory ascertainment) — as in Mohd. Sagir and Smt. Amrawati Devi, both distinguished here. Where, as here, tampering is obvious to the naked eye at inspection itself (window/TP seals tampered, R and B phase wires cut, the meter recording nil consumption though the transformer showed live current on all three phases), the conclusion of theft does not depend on any test report; the licensee's subsequent sending of the meter for testing (for record purposes) does not confer a Clause 5.6(c)(iii) right that never arose. Since the tampering was a foregone conclusion on the inspection report itself, the assessment order was not vitiated for want of independent testing or for being non-speaking, and interference under Article 226 was declined.

cases.title: M/S Venus Stone Crushing Co. & Anr. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Ors.
cases.topic: Mandatory pre-testing notice (now final per SC's SLP dismissal in Amrawati Devi); licensee bears the burden of proving the consumer, not an intervening cause, caused the irregularity; manufacturer's lab is not independent
cases.holding: No. Paras 5.17/5.18/5.20 of the 2002 Code (materially identical to Clause 5.6 of the 2005 Code) mandate seven days' advance notice of any laboratory testing so the consumer may be present; this is a mandatory procedure per Amrawati Devi v. PVVNL, a ruling since rendered final by the Supreme Court's dismissal of the SLP against it (3.8.2009) — a test report obtained without this procedure cannot ground any action against the consumer. Since the sealing certificate at removal recorded only a burnt meter (no tampered/defective seals) and unrelated CT/PT phase errors that were also technically explicable and had self-corrected without any external intervention, the subsequent 'tampering' finding of the manufacturer's own lab (obtained ex parte, undated, and after the meter had left the consumer's custody) could not be relied upon; the licensee bears the burden of proving with cogent evidence that the consumer, rather than some cause arising after the meter's removal, caused the alleged irregularity. Following Modern Rice Mill v. MVVNL and JMD Alloys v. Bihar SEB, a meter manufacturer's own laboratory is not an 'independent laboratory'. Since the assessment's very basis (the test report) was vitiated, and the Clause 6.8/Ashok Kumar assessment procedure was also not followed, the entire assessment fell.

cases.title: Smt. Vimla Tiwari v. State of U.P. And Others
cases.topic: Before an assessment is finalised on the basis that a meter was found missing, tampered, or otherwise defective, Clause 5.6 requires the meter to be sent for testing to verify the checking report's claim, rather than the Assessing Officer relying solely on the (here, internally contradictory) field checking report
cases.holding: No. Following Smt. Amrawati Devi v. PuVVNL and M/s Modern Rice Mill v. MVVNL (both already part of this corpus's Clause 5.6 line of authority), the Court held the Assessing Officer was obliged to ensure the meter was tested/verified per Clause 5.6 before relying on the checking report's contested factual claim; reliance on an internally inconsistent, unverified report without such testing further vitiated the assessment.
cases.paras: paras discussing Clause 5.6 and meter-testing precedent

cases.title: Smt. Shakuntla Devi v. State of U.P. — bill dispute relegated to Clause 5.6
cases.topic: bill-dispute-relegated-to-clause-5.6
cases.holding: A consumer dissatisfied with a bill raised for electricity consumption has a remedy under Clause 5.6 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; a writ petition challenging such a bill is dismissed with liberty to pursue that remedy.

cases.title: Jaydev Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-dispute-clause-5.6-remedy
cases.holding: A consumer dissatisfied with a consumption bill raised by the distribution corporation has a remedy under clause 5.6 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; a writ petition challenging that bill is dismissed with liberty to pursue that remedy.

cases.title: Mohd. Sagir v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.topic: Whether the 'Defective Meters' heading confines Clause 5.6 to non-tampered meters
cases.holding: Clause 5.6 applies to tampered meters too. The heading cannot control the clear substantive provision: Clause 5.6(a) gives the licensee the right to test 'any meter' on reasonable doubt, and Clause 5.9(b)(ii) expressly treats a meter 'rendered defective due to tampering or any other deliberate act' within the same scheme. Read together, a tampered meter is a defective meter for Clause 5.6; the licensee's contention that Clause 5.6 was not attracted is incorrect.

cases.title: M/s Vikas Cool Industries v. Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: defective-meter-testing
cases.holding: Clause 5.6 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 governs checking of defective meters. A consumer who doubts meter accuracy must apply to the licensee under that clause; the licensee shall decide and, if necessary, issue a fresh bill. Where supply has already been disconnected and a recovery citation issued, the Court directed that if the consumer deposits ₹4 lakh within ten days and files a Clause 5.6 testing application, the licensee shall restore supply, decide in accordance with law, and take no further coercive action for the balance; failure to deposit withdraws that protection. The writ was disposed of on those directions without a finding that the meter was defective or that the demand was wrong.

cases.title: Shri Krishna Kumar Bhargava v. State of U.P. & 4 Others
cases.topic: Defective meter is not per se theft; distinct assessment regime — interim stay
cases.holding: Prima facie, no. Where the checking report finds the meter defective without finding that the consumer rendered it defective, it may not be a case of theft/UUE under s.126; a defective meter is governed by the distinct defective-meter rules (Clauses 5.6 and 5.8), and assessment must follow that regime. Coupled with a demand notice predating the 'final assessment' (suggesting the show-cause was treated as final, contra Ashok Kumar) and an unexplained computation, a prima facie case was made out and recovery was stayed.
cases.flag: Interim order only (stay of recovery); the merits await final hearing on affidavits.

cases.title: Shri Gautam Motors Pvt. Ltd. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Others
cases.topic: No bill can be raised on the basis of a check meter
cases.holding: No. There is no provision under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code or the Electricity Act, 2003 permitting a bill to be raised on the basis of a check meter (as the licensee's counsel fairly admitted). The demand of Rs. 5,93,227 raised on the strength of the inspection report / check meter is set aside.

cases.title: M/s Madhuvan Properties (P) Ltd. v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Another
cases.topic: Slow-meter difference chargeable only for the previous three months; testing in consumer's presence
cases.holding: Prima facie, no. Clause 5.6 requires the meter to be tested in the consumer's presence with an opportunity to object, and Clause 5.6(c)(ii) permits charging the difference of energy consumed only for the previous three months (with an instalment option). A demand for more than two-and-a-half years could not be made; as interim relief, restoration of supply was ordered on a Rs. 15 lakh deposit, the balance not to be recovered pending the petition.
cases.flag: Interim order only; final view reserved after counter affidavit.

cases.title: Retrospective OMF charges — unreasoned order quashed
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: retrospective assessment / meter multiplier (OMF)
cases.holding: An order reiterating retrospective charges without dealing with the consumer’s objection—including alleged non-compliance with clause 5.6 (no check meter; MRI not properly supplied) and the sealing-certificate CT ratio/OMF of 10/5 and 2 versus the claimed 1000/5 and 200—suffers from lack of reasons and is set aside. The Executive Engineer must pass a fresh order on the retrospective claim after the consumer pays outstanding arrears on current bills.

cases.title: M/s Kamakhya Steels Pvt. Ltd. & Another v. PVVNL & Another
cases.topic: Before treating a slow-running meter as theft, the licensee must send it for technical assessment to distinguish tampering from a manufacturing defect
cases.holding: No. The authority ought to have sent the meter for technical assessment to find out whether any tampering was done or whether it was a manufacturing defect. That not having been done, the conclusion that the petitioners were liable for additional units equal to the difference between the check meter and the original meter was hypothetical and unsustainable.
cases.flag: The Court did not cite Clause 5.6. It directed a 'technical assessment' of the meter to distinguish tampering from a manufacturing defect. Keyed to Clause 5.6 (meter testing) for indexing.

cases.title: Chaudhary Nursing Home Pvt. Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: slow-meter supplementary bill — Article 226 vs CGRF
cases.holding: Whether a slow-metering supplementary bill may run for 18 months on a check-meter report, or only three months under clause 5.6, is a question of fact that cannot be enquired into under Article 226. The consumer must approach the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum under the UPERC (CGRF and Electricity Ombudsman) Regulations, 2007, which may also hear an HV-2 tariff dispute. The writ is disposed of without entering the merits; interim protection continues for three weeks and stands vacated if the Forum is not approached.

cases.title: Abdul Hameed Alias Abdul Haneef v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: check meter for alleged defective meter
cases.holding: Where a domestic consumer disputes a high-consumption bill and seeks a check meter alleging the installed meter is defective, the licensee must install a check meter in terms of clause 5.6 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 and, depending on the inspection result, pass appropriate orders for correction of bills.

UP-2005::5.6(c)(iii).topic: Consumer's option on the venue of meter testing; illegality of testing without it

cases.title: Mohd. Sagir v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.topic: Consumer's option on the venue of meter testing; illegality of testing without it
cases.holding: Yes. Clause 5.6(c)(iii) requires the meter, after sealing in the consumer's presence, to be tested 'at licensee's lab/Independent lab/Electrical Inspector, as agreed by consumer', the option once exercised not to be changed and the resulting report to be final. The licensee has a corresponding duty to apprise the consumer of this right; failure to offer the option renders the sealing and testing irregular and illegal, and vitiates the assessment built upon it.

cases.title: Dr. Umesh Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: independent laboratory testing of defective meter
cases.holding: Where a consumer had invoked Clause 5.6(c)(iii) for independent laboratory testing of a defective meter after exercising that option at sealing, and a representation to the Executive Engineer remained undecided, the writ was disposed of with a direction to the Executive Engineer, Bareilly, to decide the representation in accordance with law, preferably within one month of a certified copy being filed. The Court made it clear that it had not adjudicated the merits.

cases.title: Rituraj v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.topic: Meter manufacturer's lab is not an 'independent laboratory'; duty to offer the venue option
cases.holding: No to the first, yes to the second. Applying Amrawati Devi and Mohd. Sagir, the licensee must apprise the consumer of the Clause 5.6(c)(iii) right to have the sealed meter tested at an independent agency; failure renders the proceedings illegal. Applying Modern Rice Mill, a report of a non-independent lab cannot be relied upon: the meter manufacturer (Secure Meters Ltd.) has a commercial interest and cannot be a judge in its own cause, and its lab is not an 'independent laboratory' under Clause 5.6(b)(iii).
cases.flag: Follows the corpus cases SCJ-162 (Amrawati Devi) and SCJ-153 (Mohd. Sagir), and Modern Rice Mill, on Clause 5.6.

cases.title: Smt. Amrawati Devi v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Anr.
cases.topic: Duty to apprise the consumer of the testing-venue option before testing a sealed meter
cases.holding: Yes. Clause 5.6(c)(iii) requires the sealed meter to be tested at the licensee's lab, an independent lab or by the electrical inspector 'as agreed by the consumer'; the consumer's agreement is essential and, once exercised, the option cannot be changed. The clause operates harshly and is construed strictly, so the licensee has a corresponding duty to apprise the consumer of the right — including the right to independent testing. Failure to do so renders the sealing and testing proceedings irregular and illegal, and a notice intimating only licensee-lab testing is contrary to law.
cases.flag: Leading DB authority on Clause 5.6(c)(iii); followed in SCJ-153 (Mohd. Sagir). The SLP against this judgment was dismissed by the Supreme Court on 3-8-2009 (as noted in SCJ-153).

UP-2005::5.6(d).topic: Meter-testing procedure vs a compounded theft offence

cases.title: Abhinav Seva Sansthan Mahavidyalaya v. U.P. Power Corporation Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.topic: Meter-testing procedure vs a compounded theft offence
cases.holding: No. Once the sum is paid under Section 152(1) and the offence is deemed compounded, the tampering stands admitted-compounded and the question of following the meter-testing procedure (para 5.6(d)) does not arise. The theft assessment was made on the Code's formula (Annexure 6.3); the procedural challenge fails.

cases.title: Saurabh Agrawal & Another v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.topic: Continued s.135 theft prosecution is quashed as an abuse of process where the underlying consumer inspection report does not itself allege theft, the licensee's own subsequent conduct treated the matter as slow metering (fully paid under Clause 5.6(c)(ii)), the Clause 5.6(d) meter-testing procedure (including MRI/proper laboratory testing) was not followed, and the s.127 appellate authority already conclusively held (with finality) that s.135 was inapplicable on the same facts
cases.holding: Yes — quashed. The consumer inspection report dated 2.8.2007, the sole evidentiary basis for the FIR/charge-sheet, did not itself record an allegation of theft (the relevant column was struck through); the licensee's parallel conduct — assessing and fully recovering the disputed amount (Rs. 71,95,449) as slow-metering charges under Clause 5.6(c)(ii) — was inconsistent with treating the same facts as theft. The Clause 5.6(d) procedure (notice of testing date, opportunity to be present, right to dispute per 5.6(c)) was never followed; no MRI report was obtained, and the seized meter was left at the police station rather than sent for proper laboratory testing, undermining any theft finding. The appellate authority under s.127 (Additional Commissioner, Judicial-II, Saharanpur) had, in a final order dated 24.10.2008 (upheld by a separate writ petition and never further challenged), held that s.135 was inapplicable and directed revision of the bills — a finding of finality directly negating the criminal prosecution's premise. Continuing the s.135 prosecution on the same consumer inspection report, after these developments, amounts to an abuse of the process of law within the settled Prakash P. Hinduja standard, and the charge-sheet, cognizance order, and pending proceedings were accordingly quashed.

cases.title: Rituraj v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.topic: Assessment based on meter/seal testing without the Clause 5.6(d) intimation is illegal
cases.holding: No. Clause 5.6(d) makes it imperative to inform the consumer of the proposed date of testing, give him an opportunity to be present, obtain his signature and preserve his right to dispute the result. Here no intimation was given for the alleged testing of the meter seals; the assessment order is per se illegal and, with the demand notice and the test-lab report, is quashed.

cases.title: Akriti Food Industry LLP v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: disputed bill; check meter
cases.holding: Clause 5.6(e) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 requires that, where the consumer disputes the correctness of a bill, a check meter be installed parallel to the main meter and the bill be made as per energy consumption reflected in the check meter, with check-meter readings recorded 7–15 days after installation. The check meter here was installed on 08.08.2025 and the impugned order was passed on 12.08.2025, before that period expired. The order dated 12.08.2025 was set aside, with liberty to the Executive Engineer to pass a fresh order after following Clause 5.6(e) within one month.

cases.title: Prakash Chandra Gupta v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.topic: CGRF must apply Clause 5.6(e) and hear the consumer on a check-meter slow-meter arrear
cases.holding: No. The petitioner's 6.9.2010 objection and the parallel check-meter history engaged Clause 5.6(e). CGRF's order dated 26.9.2016 showed no proper consideration of that clause and no proper opportunity of hearing, and those defects vitiated the order (and the recovery founded on it). The Court quoted Clause 5.6(e) in full: after a 7–15 day test, if the existing meter is fast or slow beyond permissible limits and the consumer does not dispute the results, the check meter remains and bills of the previous three months are adjusted; if the results are disputed, Clause 5.6(c) is to be followed. It did not itself apply the three-month adjustment or decide whether the test results were disputed. The CGRF order is set aside and the complaint remitted for a fresh decision after hearing, in the light of that observation, preferably within six weeks.
cases.flag: Petitioner described the licensee's reliance as '56 (ii) of the U.P. Electricity Act, 2003'; that is s.56(2) of the Electricity Act, 2003 — the Court did not construe it. Caption is 'State of U.P. And 2 Others', but the reserved judgment treats respondent no. 2 as the Ombudsman, no. 3 as CGRF, no. 4 as the distribution division, and also sets aside a citation dated 31.5.2021 of 'respondent no. 6' that is not in the prayer. Two consecutive paragraphs are numbered 13. The source PDF also contains listing/amendment/stay orders from 7.4.2021 to 22.8.2024; the judgment under record is 23.9.2024 (2024:AHC:154585).

cases.title: Deepak Mishra v. M.D. Kanpur Electricity Supply Co. Ltd.
cases.topic: check-meter billing adjustment
cases.holding: Para 5.6(e) does not authorise billing on check-meter consumption. Where a check meter shows the existing meter fast or slow beyond permissible limits, bills of the previous three months prior to the month in which the dispute arose are to be adjusted as per the test results. Applying that window to the petitioner's 1999 bill would fall before the 2005 Code was in force, and successive meter replacements broke any continuous consumption pattern. The CGRF/Ombudsman assessment at 180 units per month for 1991–2010 was just and equitable and was not interfered with.

cases.title: Mukhtar Ahmad v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: defective meter
cases.holding: A consumer's complaint that the electricity meter at his premises is defective, and that the licensee has taken no steps despite being informed, warrants examination by the concerned authority under the procedure in Clause 5.9 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The High Court will not decide that grievance on a writ petition and will dispose of the petition, leaving the consumer to seek redressal under that clause.
cases.flag: Order cites Clause 5.9 generally, not sub-clause 5.9(c).

cases.title: Pramod Kumar v. State of U.P. and 3 Others
cases.topic: Burnt-meter bypass and Clause 5.9(c) bar on booking direct theft — raised; not decided
cases.holding: No construction. Counsel submitted that Clause 5.8 required the licensee to restore supply immediately by bypassing a burnt meter (providing a 'direct light'), and that Clause 5.9(c) provided that if the meter is found burnt and there is reason to believe an official of the licensee gave a direct connection pending replacement, a case of direct theft shall not be booked. The Court recorded those submissions on 21.02.2024, called for an affidavit from the Executive Engineer who lodged the FIR, and later stayed coercive measures. It never applied or interpreted either clause. On 16.07.2026 the writ was dismissed for non-prosecution.
cases.flag: Clauses 5.8 and 5.9(c) are not catalog keys; 5.9(c) is keyed as the theft-booking bar counsel invoked, with 5.8 recorded in the clause field. The 21.02.2024 order cites 'Electricity Act, 2023' (read 2003) and 'floor will' (read flour mill). Counsel dated the FIR as 09.12.2022; the petition describes it as 10.12.2022. Source PDF also contains orders of 21.02.2024 (Arvind Singh Sangwan and Shiv Shanker Prasad JJ.) and 21.03.2024 and 22.03.2024 (Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Gajendra Kumar JJ.); the operative disposal is 16.07.2026 (Ajay Bhanot and Divesh Chandra Samant JJ.). Paragraph 8 is of the 21.02.2024 order.

cases.title: Umesh Nath Pandey v. P.V.V.N.L.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: name-and-bill-correction-writ
cases.holding: A writ seeking correction of consumer name and electricity bill under clause 6.1 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 will not be entertained where the petitioner has not paid the electricity dues; the consumer may pursue the statutory forum under the Electricity Act read with clause 6.1.

cases.title: Mahadev Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: provisional-assessment-show-cause-notice-and-hearing-date
cases.holding: Clause 6.1(b) of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 requires that a provisional assessment be issued with a show-cause notice giving 15 working days for reply and fixing a date and time. An assessment that grants only seven days and fixes no date or time for appearance is contrary to the Code and is liable to be quashed together with the consequent demand or recovery certificate, with a direction to hear the consumer and pass a speaking order.
cases.flag: Court cited Clause 6.1(b) for 15 working days' notice and a fixed hearing date on provisional assessment/show-cause. That machinery is Clause 6.8 of the 2005 Code (catalog UP-2005::6.8 / 6.8(b)); 6.1(b) is recorded as cited, not silently corrected. One sentence also refers to the assessment as dated 7.2.2012; the rest of the order treats it as 7.2.2017.

cases.title: Sequel Alloys And Wires Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: para-6.1-representation-energy-arrears
cases.holding: Whether the licensee may impose billed energy arrears is for the competent authority on a representation under Para 6.1 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ court will not decide chargeability; if a representation is filed within one month, the authority shall decide it strictly in accordance with law after notice and hearing within one month thereafter.
cases.flag: Cited as Para 6.1 without a sub-clause.

UP-2005::6.1(g).topic: Billing/disconnection window — 15-day bill dispatch plus disconnection notice

cases.title: Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Others v. M/s Prakancha Metal Works Pvt. Ltd.
cases.topic: Billing/disconnection window — 15-day bill dispatch plus disconnection notice
cases.holding: No. Clause 6.1(g) requires the bill to be dispatched at least 15 days before the due date, and a further seven days' notice is contemplated before disconnection; here the bill (issued 28.03.2011, due 31.03.2011) gave only three days and the disconnection (08.04.2011) preceded the statutory window, rendering it illegal. Ante-dating the payment receipt to 31.03.2011 was also illegal manipulation of the record.

cases.title: M/s Vimla Gramodyog Sansthan v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.topic: various-charges-not-underbilling-demand
cases.holding: A demand recovering the difference because the consumer was billed at half the applicable rate is a demand for wrongful billing, not recovery of 'various charges' within clause 6.1(g). A vires challenge to clause 6.1(g) vis-à-vis section 55 of the Electricity Act, 2003 therefore does not arise on such a demand.

cases.title: M/S Rathi Super Steel Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: time-for-payment-of-bills
cases.holding: The Court did not decide whether the provisional bills violated the fifteen-day payment window in clauses 6.1(g) and 4.36(a) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, or when they were served. Because the consumer was willing to deposit the entire amount, the writ was disposed of directing that if the bill raised on 27 February 2013 was not paid by 15 March 2013 the licensee could take action permitted by law, and that respondents make effort to adhere to those two provisions when raising bills.
cases.flag: Clause 4.36(a) was invoked with 6.1(g) for a fifteen-day payment period; the Court did not quote either clause.

cases.title: M/s Supreme Ceramics Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: due-date-for-bill-payment
cases.holding: Where the consumer challenged bills for want of the 15-day payment period under clause 6.1(g) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 (counsel also citing clause 4.36(a)) and offered to pay if that time were allowed, the Court disposed of the writ by directing that the entire bill dated 22.3.2013 be deposited by 10.4.2013 as a small protection for time consumed in litigation, observing that the licensee should follow the statutory provisions henceforth.

UP-2005::6.12.topic: Clause 6.12 governs appropriation of a consumer's bill payment, not adjustment of duty already realised

cases.title: M/s Shri Radhey Iron (Pvt.) Ltd. v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.topic: Clause 6.12 governs appropriation of a consumer's bill payment, not adjustment of duty already realised
cases.holding: No. Clause 6.12 applies to the appropriation of a payment made by the consumer (arrear, then current charges, then miscellaneous, with duty/LPS in proportion); it does not govern the adjustment claimed here, which is of duty already realised from the consumer, and cannot be used to defer that adjustment.

UP-2005::6.14.topic: Consumer may seek payment of outstanding dues in installments under Clause 6.14

cases.title: Kripa Shanker v. State of U.P. Thru. Distt. Collector, Unnao & Ors.
cases.topic: Consumer may seek payment of outstanding dues in installments under Clause 6.14
cases.holding: Clause 6.14 of the Code already provides for payment of outstanding dues in installments; on an application by the consumer, the Executive Engineer must consider and decide the request expeditiously. By consent, the Court directed the petitioner to deposit Rs. 15,000 and move a Clause 6.14 application, staying recovery pending decision, conditional on the deposit being made.

cases.title: Satyendra Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: instalment facility for financial distress
cases.holding: Clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, provides instalment facility to consumers in financial distress. Where the consumer does not dispute the amount and only seeks instalments, the proper course is to apply to the Executive Engineer (Prescribed Authority), who shall decide the request on the record; the High Court will not itself accord the facility.

cases.title: M/S Savari Ice Factory v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: installment facility in financial distress
cases.holding: Under clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, installment facility for a consumer in financial distress may be extended by the authority concerned, not by the High Court. The Court declined to itself accord installments and granted liberty to apply under clause 6.14; any such application is to be dealt with and decided in accordance with law on the records within two months of production of a certified copy of the order.

cases.title: Satendra Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: successive writ after clause 6.14 direction
cases.holding: Where an earlier writ against a recovery notice was disposed of with a direction to apply under Clause 6.14 before the Executive Engineer, a second writ challenging the same notice is not maintainable merely because that application has not been decided.

cases.title: Ram Ratan v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: installment facility for admitted electricity arrears
cases.holding: On the parties' submission that clause 6.14 of the Supply Code permits installment facility, the Court disposed of the writ by directing the petitioner to deposit the entire admitted dues of Rs. 1,90,434 in three equal quarterly installments (1 June, 1 September and 1 December 2014). Current electricity bills remain payable independently of the installments. On default in paying the entire dues, the order stands automatically vacated and the competent authority is at liberty to recover.

cases.title: Shyamdutt v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: instalment facility for financial distress
cases.holding: Clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 provides that the licensee may extend an instalment facility to consumers in financial distress. The writ seeking instalment payment after disconnection for arrears was disposed of by directing the petitioner to apply to the competent authority, which shall consider and decide the application within two weeks.

cases.title: M/s Raja Ram Ispat Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: instalment facility
cases.holding: Instalment facility to deposit the amount sought to be realised is available if the consumer tenders an offer under paragraph 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If such an application is made, the competent authority shall pass appropriate orders on it.

cases.title: Nawal Singh @ Lovil v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: installment facility for electricity dues
cases.holding: Clause 6.14 of the 2005 Electricity Supply Code empowers the Executive Engineer to extend an installment facility for electricity dues. Where the consumer offers to pay arrears in installments, the writ court will not itself grant that facility: the petitioner is to produce a certified copy of the order before the Executive Engineer, who shall within six weeks extend any benefit to which the consumer is entitled under clause 6.14. If the consumer then complies with that order, the Engineer shall restore a farming tubewell connection forthwith, having regard to drought.

cases.title: Raj Kumar Sharma v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: instalment facility for financial distress
cases.holding: Clause 6.14 itself provides for payment of outstanding dues in instalments in deserving cases of financial distress. A consumer seeking that facility must apply to the competent authority (not below Executive Engineer). The authority is to decide the application by a speaking and reasonable order, taking a sympathetic view; coercive recovery may be withheld pending that decision. The court does not itself grant instalments on a writ.

cases.title: Manoj Tomar v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: instalment facility for consumers in financial distress
cases.holding: Clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 empowers the Executive Engineer, DGM and General Manager to extend instalment facility to a consumer in financial distress. A writ against a recovery citation, where the consumer offered to pay in instalments, was dismissed with liberty to represent under Clause 6.14 within three weeks; the authority is to decide that representation in accordance with law preferably within one month.

cases.title: Mahaveer v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: instalment facility for financial distress
cases.holding: Where a consumer challenges a recovery citation for electricity dues and seeks to pay in instalments, the writ court may dispose of the petition with liberty to make a representation under Clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, which empowers the Executive Engineer, D.G.M. and General Manager to extend an instalment facility to a consumer in financial distress; if a representation is made within the time allowed, the authority shall decide it in accordance with law.

cases.title: Ayub v. State of U.P. and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: instalment facility for consumers in financial distress
cases.holding: Where a consumer facing recovery of electricity dues offers to pay in instalments, the writ court will not itself grant instalments but will relegate the consumer to the Executive Engineer, D.G.M. or General Manager, who under Clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 are empowered to extend instalment facility to consumers in financial distress; any representation so made is to be decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: Dhirendra Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: installment-payment-clause-6.14
cases.holding: Where a consumer facing an electricity recovery citation offers to pay in instalments, the writ is disposed of with liberty to represent under Clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005—under which the Executive Engineer, D.G.M. and General Manager may extend instalment facility to consumers in financial distress—and the authority must decide that representation in accordance with law, expeditiously.

cases.title: Dinesh Chandra v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: instalment facility for consumers in financial distress
cases.holding: Where a consumer facing a recovery citation for electricity dues is ready to pay in instalments, the writ court will not examine the citation on merits but will relegate him to Clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, under which the Executive Engineer, DGM and General Manager may grant instalments to consumers in financial distress; any representation made within three weeks is to be decided in accordance with law, preferably within one month.

cases.title: Smt. Rama Devi v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.topic: installment facility for arrears
cases.holding: If the petitioner files a certified copy of this order before respondent no. 2 within 15 days along with her claim, that officer shall examine her grievance and extend such installment benefits as may be permissible under Clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and shall decide the bill-correction grievance within two months.

cases.title: Murari Lal v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: instalment facility and re-energisation
cases.holding: Where a defaulting consumer facing permanent disconnection is prepared to pay the arrears, the Executive Engineer may permit clearance of dues by easy instalments under Clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and upon such clearance the connection shall be re-energised in accordance with the rules within three weeks, subject to no other legal impediment.

cases.title: Natthoram v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: installment facility for financial distress
cases.holding: Clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 empowers the Executive Engineer to extend the installment facility to consumers found to be in financial distress. The writ was disposed of with liberty to the petitioner to approach the Executive Engineer with a fresh application under clause 6.14; if made, the Executive Engineer shall pass a reasoned and speaking order expeditiously in accordance with law.

cases.title: Gufran v. State of U.P. and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: instalment facility for financial distress
cases.holding: Clause 6.14 empowers officers not below Executive Engineer to extend an instalment facility to consumers in financial distress. The petitioner, who did not dispute electricity-charge liability, was given liberty to apply under that clause within one week; the authority was directed to consider and decide any such application by a reasoned speaking order in accordance with law within three weeks, with no coercive recovery for four weeks or until that decision, whichever was earlier.

cases.title: Clause 6.14 instalments — representation directed, recovery stayed
cases.topic: instalment facility for financial distress
cases.holding: Without deciding the demand, the Court disposed of the writ with liberty to the consumer to apply under Clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 (Executive Engineer, D.G.M. and General Manager being empowered to grant instalments in financial distress) within three weeks; the authority was to decide the representation in accordance with law, preferably within one month; recovery was to remain in abeyance until that decision.

cases.title: Ashish Kesarwani v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: instalment facility for electricity dues
cases.holding: Where the licensee has no objection under clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, the Court may as a special case stay recovery of vigilance-penalty electricity dues and allow the consumer to pay the demanded amount in four monthly instalments—50% within fifteen days and the balance in three equal monthly instalments—adjusting deposits already made, waiving collection charges if the schedule is kept, and automatically vacating the stay on default.

cases.title: Smt. Rani Rajpoot v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: instalment facility for outstanding electricity dues
cases.holding: On the licensee's concession that Clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 permits instalments, the Court, as a special case, stayed recovery, attachment and auction of electricity dues provided the consumer deposited the claimed amount in four monthly instalments (first of Rs 60,000 within one month; balance in three equal monthly instalments), with amounts already paid adjusted, collection charges waived on compliance, automatic vacation of the order on default, and the order inoperative if an earlier writ on the same bill had proceeded or auction had already taken place.

cases.title: Siya Ram v. State of U.P. — recovery citation; liberty under clause 6.14
cases.topic: instalment facility for dues
cases.holding: Clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 empowers the Executive Engineer, DGM and General Manager to extend instalment facility to consumers in financial distress. A writ challenging a recovery citation, where the consumer offers to pay in instalments, is disposed of with liberty to represent under that clause; the authority shall decide the representation in accordance with law, preferably within one month.

cases.title: Rajveer Singh v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: installment payment of disputed demand
cases.holding: It is open to the consumer to seek payment of the disputed demand in installments. The Executive Engineer, if so permissible, shall invoke Clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Raj Kumar v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: installment facility on recovery citation
cases.holding: Where a consumer facing a recovery citation for electricity dues seeks time to pay in installments, the proper course is an application to the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The Court will not itself quash the citation; it may direct that such an application, if moved within a stated time, be decided expeditiously and stay coercive steps for a short period.

cases.title: Vijay Kumar Saraswat v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: installment facility
cases.holding: Paragraph 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is a self-contained provision for extending installment facility. Where the consumer does not dispute the billed amount and only asks the High Court to fix installments, the Court will not itself grant that relief; the remedy is to approach the concerned official under paragraph 6.14.

cases.title: Maa Kaila Foundries Pvt. Ltd. v. Dakhsinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.topic: instalment facility for electricity dues
cases.holding: A writ to quash recovery initiated for failure to deposit electricity dues within time will not be entertained where the consumer can take recourse to clause 6.14, which allows the licensee to extend instalments to consumers in financial distress without waiver of surcharge. If an application for that facility is filed, the licensee shall pass an appropriate order expeditiously.

cases.title: Harikesh Yadav v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: instalment facility for financial distress
cases.holding: Where electricity arrears are outstanding and recovery has been initiated, a writ seeking instalments on the ground of financial distress is not to be entertained. The consumer must approach the authority under Clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, which permits the licensee to extend instalments only to consumers in financial distress.

cases.title: M/s Jai Maa Laxmi Sheetgrah Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: reconnection of supply
cases.holding: A writ seeking reconnection under clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, after disconnection for non-deposit of billed charges, was disposed of without a merits determination: if the consumer applied within ten days with a certified copy of the order, the competent authority was to take an appropriate decision expeditiously, preferably within two weeks, in accordance with law.

cases.title: Pyare Lal v. Chief Engineer
cases.topic: installment-payment-clause-6.14
cases.holding: Clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 provides an instalment facility for payment of electricity dues. A consumer who seeks to discharge a recovery demand in instalments must apply to the Executive Engineer under that clause; the High Court will not itself direct an instalment schedule in writ. The petition was disposed of, leaving that recourse open.

cases.title: M/S Krishna Gears Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: Installment facility as an alternative remedy
cases.holding: Where a consumer aggrieved by a recovery citation for unpaid electricity dues seeks only permission to pay in installments, the writ court declines to entertain the petition because an alternative remedy exists under clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, which provides the installment facility; the petition is dismissed on that ground.

cases.title: M/s Ganga Devi Pyare Lal Cold Storage Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: instalments of electricity arrears
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity recovery notice and permission to pay arrears in instalments is not entertained when Clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is available before the department for fixing instalments.

cases.title: Devendra Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: installment of electricity bill
cases.holding: Where the only relief sought is that installments be fixed for depositing an electricity bill, the High Court will not entertain a writ petition because the consumer can apply to the competent authority under Clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ is dismissed.

cases.title: Bhagwati Prasad v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: writ-alternative-remedy-bill-installments
cases.holding: Where the only relief pressed in a writ petition is that installments be fixed for deposit of an electricity bill, the consumer has a statutory alternative remedy under clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and the High Court will decline to entertain the petition.

cases.title: Iqbal Ahmad v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: instalment facility for electricity dues
cases.holding: A consumer seeking to deposit electricity bills in instalments must invoke Clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code; a writ confined to that prayer is disposed by leaving the petitioner to that alternative remedy.

cases.title: Rashid Siddiqui v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: installment payment of bills
cases.holding: Where the only relief sought is permission to deposit electricity bills in installments, the consumer may invoke Clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code; the writ petition is disposed of leaving that alternative remedy open.

cases.title: Wahid Siddiqui v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: installment facility for billed dues
cases.holding: Where the only relief sought in a writ is permission to deposit electricity bills in installments, the consumer must invoke Clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code. The High Court will not grant that facility itself and will dispose of the petition leaving the petitioner to that alternative remedy.

cases.title: Iqbal Ahmad v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: installment facility — competent authority of the licensee
cases.holding: Clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 permits installment facility only to consumers in financial distress, and only an officer of the licensee not below the rank of Executive Engineer may grant it. A consumer of Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited who applies to the Chairman/Managing Director of U.P. Power Corporation Limited — a separate company — has not approached the appropriate authority, so the licensee cannot be faulted for non-consideration. The writ was disposed of with liberty to apply to respondent no. 4 within three weeks, to be decided under Clause 6.14 by a reasoned speaking order within two months.

cases.title: Jeevan Sahara Hospital v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: instalment facility for electricity dues
cases.holding: A consumer who, after rejection of a Clause 6.5 representation against the bill, seeks only to deposit electricity dues in instalments must invoke Clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the High Court will not itself direct the Executive Engineer to fix instalments.

cases.title: Shri Pal Singh v. State of U.P. — writ disposed with liberty under Clause 6.14
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: Clause 6.14 remedy before Executive Engineer
cases.holding: Clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is an adequate remedy before the Executive Engineer. A writ petition may be disposed of with liberty to the consumer to approach that authority, who shall pass appropriate orders on the representation strictly in accordance with law within four weeks of filing.

cases.title: M/S U.S. Foods Private Limited And Another v. State of U.P. And Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: instalment facility for electricity dues
cases.holding: Where a consumer facing recovery of electricity dues seeks time and instalments, clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 supplies the procedure. The writ is disposed of by directing the consumer to approach the Executive Engineer, who shall on receipt of a certified copy within 15 days pass an appropriate order on the request for fixing instalments.

cases.title: Mohammad Shafeeq v. U.P. Power Corporation
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: installments of electricity dues
cases.holding: A billing dispute is not to be decided in writ jurisdiction, without prejudice to the consumer raising it before the Consumer Grievances Redressal Forum. If the consumer applies under Clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 to clear dues in installments, the Executive Engineer shall consider the request sympathetically and make provision for easy installments, having regard to the domestic nature of the connection.

cases.title: Gopi Ram v. Dakshinanchal Vidhyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: installment-payment-clause-6.14
cases.holding: Where recovery of electricity dues is underway and the consumer offers to deposit the amount due with the Executive Engineer, that officer may consider granting easy installments as contemplated under Clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; an application moved in that regard shall be disposed of within three weeks of its filing. The Court will not, in such a writ, enter into the consumer's disputes on the dues themselves.

cases.title: Kaluwa v. State of U.P. and others
cases.topic: instalment facility for assessed dues
cases.holding: The writ was disposed with liberty to approach the second respondent, who shall look into the petitioner's grievances; if the petitioner is found liable to pay the assessed dues, the Executive Engineer shall pass an appropriate order keeping in view Clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, extending the benefit of instalments.

cases.title: Ashwini Kumar Tiwari v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: installment facility for agriculturist tubewell dues after theft assessment
cases.holding: If the consumer is prepared to pay electricity dues that are due, the Executive Engineer shall invoke clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 to facilitate installments, keeping in view that the consumer claims to be an agriculturist and the dues relate to tubewell operation, even where those dues arise after Section 135 theft proceedings and a claimed provisional assessment. Assessment grievances, where it is unclear whether a final assessment has been made, are to be examined by the concerned authority, which shall pass appropriate orders.

cases.title: Abdul Sattar v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: installment facility for electricity dues
cases.holding: Where the consumer seeks time to pay electricity dues in installments, Clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is the statutory provision; the consumer may apply to the Executive Engineer, who shall pass an appropriate order within three weeks of presentation of a certified copy of the writ court's order. The High Court did not itself grant or refuse the installment facility.

cases.title: Nagendra Singh v. State of U.P. (theft demand; billing officer and Clause 6.14)
cases.topic: billing grievance and instalment facility
cases.holding: Without deciding the theft-based recovery or the claim of full payment, the Court directed the petitioner to approach respondent no.3, the officer empowered under the 2005 Code to look into billing grievances, who shall examine the claim and pass an appropriate order. If dues are found cleared, appropriate directions shall issue; if any dues remain, respondent no.3 may facilitate payment keeping in view Clause 6.14 of the 2005 Code in accordance with law.

cases.title: Ram Lal v. Southern Electricity Distribution Corp. Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: installment-payment-clause-6.14
cases.holding: Where the only relief sought in a writ is permission to deposit an electricity bill in instalments, the consumer is to avail the statutory request under clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the petition is disposed of leaving that remedy open.

cases.title: Laxmi Grits — remaining bill installments relegated to Clause 6.14
cases.topic: installment of remaining electricity bill
cases.holding: Where the sole relief pressed is permission to deposit the remaining amount of an electricity bill in installments, the writ is disposed of leaving the consumer to avail the remedy under Clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Purshotam Dass v. D.V.V.N.L. — installment writ dismissed where settlement already provided post-dated cheques
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: installment facility for settlement dues
cases.holding: Where a settlement letter for electricity dues already provides for payment by post-dated cheques, the High Court will not grant a further writ directing deposit in installments. The petition was dismissed. In any event the consumer may still avail the installment remedy under Clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Surendra v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: installments of assessment liability
cases.holding: Assessment of electricity actually consumed is a proceeding separate from the Section 135 offence. A request for installments of that liability is to be made to the Executive Engineer of the area under Clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: S.S. Industries v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: instalment of arrears after disconnection
cases.holding: Clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 empowers the concerned licensee officer to extend the benefit of instalments. Where supply has been disconnected without considering a request to pay arrears in instalments, the writ court will not decide entitlement on merits but will direct that officer to consider the request and pass an appropriate order within a fixed time, and, if the consumer complies, to pass further orders on reconnection and regular supply in accordance with law.

cases.title: Arimadam Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: instalment facility for recovery of dues
cases.holding: Clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 confers on the Executive Engineer the power to allow payment of recovered dues in instalments. The High Court did not itself fix an instalment plan; it directed that if a certified copy of the order is filed before the Executive Engineer within one week, the Executive Engineer shall within two weeks pass an appropriate order providing such instalments as may be necessary on the facts, and that recovery proceedings shall remain subject to that order.

cases.title: Punit Kumar Gupta v. State of U.P. and others
cases.topic: instalment facility for payment of dues under recovery
cases.holding: Clause 6.14 confers on the Executive Engineer power to allow payment of electricity dues in instalments. Where the consumer offers to deposit the amount under recovery and seeks that facility, the Court will not itself structure the instalments but will direct the Executive Engineer, on production of a certified copy within one week, to pass an appropriate instalment order within two weeks on the facts of the case, recovery remaining subject to that order.

cases.title: M/s Nutek Overseas Pvt. Ltd. v. Pachimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.topic: instalment facility for arrears after disconnection
cases.holding: A writ seeking time to deposit dues after disconnection for non-payment is not granted on the merits; the consumer is left to apply under clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: S.S. Industries v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: instalment facility and restoration after disconnection
cases.holding: On the licensee's failure to extend Clause 6.14 instalments as previously directed, and after disconnection despite a Rs.40,000 deposit, the Court itself fixed three equal instalments for the balance electricity dues. Restoration was ordered forthwith subject to deposit of the next instalment within one week (by 25 November 2017); the remaining two instalments were payable on the 25th of each succeeding month. The writ was disposed of on those terms.

cases.title: Vijay Singh v. State of U.P. (cl. 6.14 instalments)
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: instalment facility for financial distress
cases.holding: A consumer seeking recovery of electricity dues in easy instalments must first apply to the licensee under clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, which permits the licensee to extend that facility to consumers in financial distress. The writ was disposed of with a direction that if such an application is filed within two weeks, the licensee shall consider it sympathetically.

cases.title: Prime Gold International Ltd. v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: installment of electricity dues
cases.holding: Where the sole relief claimed is permission to deposit electricity dues in installments, the consumer has a statutory remedy under Clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 and the writ is disposed of leaving the consumer to invoke that clause.

cases.title: Meenu Gupta v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: instalment facility; writ not entertained
cases.holding: Paragraph 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 authorises the licensee to grant instalments having regard to relevant facts; where the consumer is willing to pay in easy instalments, the High Court will not entertain a writ and will leave the consumer to that Code remedy.

cases.title: Virendra Kumar Srivastava v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: instalment facility for recovery-citation dues
cases.holding: Where a consumer seeks in writ to deposit a recovery-citation amount in instalments, the High Court will not grant that facility itself; the consumer may invoke Clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and the petition is disposed of leaving that Code remedy open.

cases.title: M/s Parmarth Steel & Alloys Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: installment facility for financial hardship
cases.holding: Where an electricity-duty demand follows dismissal of the consumer's earlier writ and vacation of Supreme Court interim protection, the High Court will not entertain a fresh writ against that demand, nor fix installments for financial hardship; that installment request is to be raised by invoking clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Clause 6.14 installment facility — recovery citation not quashed
cases.topic: installment facility for arrears
cases.holding: Admission of electricity arrears and a request for easy installments is no ground to quash a recovery citation. The consumer may apply to the Executive Engineer under clause 6.14 of the Supply Code, 2005 (installments only for consumers in financial distress; no surcharge waiver; first installment not less than 40% of the total; grant limited by the rank of the officer). The Executive Engineer shall, within three weeks of presentation of a certified copy, pass an appropriate order extending the maximum relief admissible; recovery proceedings abide that order.

cases.title: Neeraj v. State of U.P. — recovery citation not quashed; Clause 6.14 installments
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: installment facility for admitted arrears
cases.holding: Admission of electricity arrears and a prayer only for easy installments is no ground to quash a recovery citation. On the consumer approaching the Executive Engineer with that request, the Engineer shall consider the application under Clause 6.14 (installments only for consumers in financial distress; no surcharge waiver; grant restricted by rank, with the first installment not less than 40% of the total) and pass an appropriate order extending the maximum relief admissible and permissible; recovery proceedings shall abide by that order.

cases.title: Karan Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: installment facility
cases.holding: A request to pay an assessed electricity recovery in installments is to be made to the Executive Engineer under clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the Engineer shall consider it in accordance with law, and recovery proceedings abide that order.

cases.title: M/S M.D. Ice And Cold Storage v. Executive Engineer (Prescribed Authority) DVVNL
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: installment-payment-clause-6.14
cases.holding: Where a recovery certificate has issued for electricity dues, recovery proceeds in accordance with law, but a consumer prepared to deposit may approach the Executive Engineer for instalments as contemplated under Clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Kurri Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: court-fixed installments and stay of coercive recovery
cases.holding: Even though Clause 6.14 vests installment facility in the Executive Engineer, the Court, treating the outstanding as petty, itself directed the petitioner to deposit Rs 10,000 within one month and the balance within six months thereafter. On that deposit and in the absence of further default, coercive steps remain stayed; on default the Electricity Department may realise the dues in accordance with law. The writ petition was disposed of on those terms.

cases.title: Syed Muzaffar Ali v. M.D. Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: instalment facility for outstanding dues
cases.holding: Clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 confers power on the licensee to extend an instalment facility to consumers in financial distress. A consumer who does not contest outstanding dues on merits but seeks to pay in instalments must apply to the Executive Engineer or other competent authority under that clause. The writ was disposed of with a direction that if such an application is made within two weeks, the authority shall decide it in accordance with law by a reasoned speaking order within four weeks; coercive action on the impugned recovery citation is stayed for six weeks or until disposal of the application, whichever is earlier.

cases.title: Gopal Krishna v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: installment facility after mutation
cases.holding: After mutation under Clause 4.44, the heir may apply for payment of dues in installments under Clause 6.14. The licensee shall pass an appropriate order thereon within six weeks of presentation of a certified copy of the order.

cases.title: Sukhpal v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: instalment of outstanding dues
cases.holding: Where outstanding electricity dues are in issue, Clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is an efficacious remedy to apply to the appropriate authority for payment in instalments. The writ was dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to invoke that clause.

cases.title: Mohd. Yameen v. U.P. Power Corporation / Paschimanchal Electricity Distribution Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: installment payment of admitted dues
cases.holding: Where the consumer accepts the electricity dues and seeks easy installments, and the licensee has no objection because paragraph 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 contemplates installment payment, the writ is disposed of by directing the consumer to approach the Executive Engineer, who shall consider and decide the installment claim under paragraph 6.14, as far as possible within one month.

cases.title: Phool Singh v. State of U.P. — recovery citation relegated to Code 6.14
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: instalment facility / alternative remedy
cases.holding: Where a consumer challenges a demand notice and recovery citation and seeks instalment relief (including after an alleged one-time settlement), the writ court will not decide the merits and will relegate the consumer to apply under clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, directing that an application filed within 15 days be decided by a reasoned speaking order within 30 days.

cases.title: Kunwar Singh v. State of U.P. (recovery citation; cl. 6.14 instalments)
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: instalment facility for outstanding dues
cases.holding: The writ challenging the demand notice and recovery citation is disposed of without a merits decision. The petitioner is directed to move an application under Clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 within 15 days; if so presented, the concerned respondent shall decide it by a reasoned and speaking order within 30 days of presentation of a certified copy of this order.

cases.title: Raj Kumar @ Ram Kumar Sharma v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: alternative remedy — installment/relief against demand and recovery
cases.holding: A writ challenging an electricity demand notice and recovery citation, and seeking installment relief, is disposed of without merits examination where the licensee points to clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005: the consumer is directed to apply under that clause within 15 days, and the authority is to decide any such application by a reasoned speaking order within 30 days of presentation of the certified copy of the order.

cases.title: Ram Sumer v. State of U.P. — demand and recovery citation relegated to clause 6.14
cases.topic: instalment-facility
cases.holding: A consumer impugning a demand notice and recovery citation, and seeking instalment facility, is to apply under clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 rather than obtain writ relief on merits. If the application is made within 15 days, the concerned authority shall decide it by a reasoned speaking order within 30 days of presentation of a certified copy of the High Court order.

cases.title: Banshi Wale v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: installment payment of electricity dues
cases.holding: Where the consumer accepts the entire electricity dues and seeks to pay them under paragraph 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, the Court will not itself grant the installment facility on the writ; if an application for payment of the dues is made, the Executive Engineer is to consider and decide it in accordance with law.

cases.title: Uma Shankar v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: recovery certificate; representation; cl. 6.14 on accepted liability
cases.holding: A writ challenging a recovery certificate for electricity dues, where the consumer disputes the bill and quantum, may be disposed by directing the Executive Engineer to consider a representation in accordance with law within a fixed time. If the consumer accepts liability and is ready to pay, the Executive Engineer may consider the claim under clause 6.14 of the Supply Code, 2005; coercive recovery may be stayed meanwhile.

cases.title: Mohammad Waseem v. State of U.P. & Another
cases.topic: Instalment facility for consumers in financial distress
cases.holding: Under Clause 6.14 the licensee may extend instalments only to consumers in financial distress, with no surcharge waiver. Only an officer of the rank of Executive Engineer or above may grant them — the Executive Engineer, DGM and General Manager up to two, three and four monthly instalments respectively — the first instalment being at least 40% of the total, with post-dated cheques required above Rs. 10,000. The Executive Engineer was directed to consider and decide the consumer's representation accordingly.

cases.title: Vinod Kumar Gupta v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: instalment facility for outstanding dues
cases.holding: Where the connection number had been corrected, a bill issued, and the consumer had in writing accepted the quantified liability while praying for instalments, the Court did not quash the recovery citation. It disposed of the writ by directing the Executive Engineer to consider an instalment application under paragraph 6.14 and pass orders in accordance with law within one month of a certified copy being presented, and stayed coercive steps on the 26 February 2018 recovery for that period.

cases.title: Manveer Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: instalment facility for outstanding dues
cases.holding: Clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 confers power on the licensee to extend an instalment facility to consumers in financial distress; sub-clause (2) provides the procedure. A consumer facing recovery of undisputed outstanding dues who seeks instalments must apply to the concerned authority under clause 6.14. The writ court will dispose of the petition by directing that authority to consider and decide any such application in accordance with law and the prescribed procedure expeditiously.

cases.title: Salman @ Mohd. Salman v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: instalment facility for electricity arrears
cases.holding: It is not the business of the High Court to fix instalments of electricity dues, that being a matter between the consumer and the licensee. The consumer may apply to the Executive Engineer under clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 with an offer to pay the entire amount in instalments; if the application is moved within one week, the Executive Engineer shall decide it in accordance with law within one month, and coercive recovery on the citation shall remain stayed till that order.

cases.title: Salman @ Salman Qureshi v. State of U.P. and Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: installment facility — High Court will not fix terms
cases.holding: It is not the business of the High Court to fix installments for electricity arrears; that is a matter between the consumer and the Electricity Department. The consumer may apply under paragraph 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, with an offer to pay the entire amount in installments, and the Executive Engineer shall decide the application in accordance with law. Coercive steps pursuant to the demand notice shall remain stayed until that decision.

cases.title: Naresh Devi v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: installment-facility-restoration
cases.holding: Clause 6.14 empowers the Executive Engineer to grant installment facility for outstanding electricity dues. Where the consumer is willing to pay and seeks restoration after a bill-cum-disconnection notice, the writ is disposed with liberty to apply to the Executive Engineer within two weeks; the Executive Engineer shall pass a speaking order fixing installments and shall consider restoration of supply on payment of such initial amount as may be considered proper. The High Court does not itself determine the disputed demand or direct restoration.
cases.flag: Court cited 'Section 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2014'; clause 6.14 is of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Hem Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: installment facility for recovery of electricity dues
cases.holding: Clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 provides an installment facility for electricity dues. The writ against a recovery certificate for Rs 1,70,813 plus miscellaneous expenses is disposed of by directing the consumer to deposit Rs 50,813 within one month; on that payment, recovery of the balance remains in abeyance if Rs 1,20,000 is paid in four equal installments of Rs 30,000 by 10 February, 10 April, 10 June and 10 August 2019, the last installment to include miscellaneous charges and any further accrual. Default in any installment automatically vacates the stay and permits the respondents to recover in accordance with law.

cases.title: Ishwar Dayal v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: instalments of electricity dues
cases.holding: A consumer who does not dispute electricity dues but seeks time and instalments to pay a recovery certificate may approach the Executive Engineer under clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ was disposed of with liberty to so apply; if approached, the Executive Engineer shall consider the application in accordance with clause 6.14, simplistically and most expeditiously, if possible within one month.

cases.title: Installment facility for electricity dues under clause 6.14
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: installment facility for electricity arrears
cases.holding: Where a consumer is willing to discharge electricity arrears if installments are allowed, the proper course is an application under clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 to the Executive Engineer, who is competent to grant installment facility. The writ is disposed of with liberty to apply within two weeks; the Executive Engineer shall consider and decide any such application in accordance with law within the next two weeks.

cases.title: Jai Maa Laxmi Cold Storage v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: withdrawal with liberty to pursue instalment remedy
cases.holding: The writ petition was dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to the petitioner to pursue the remedy under Clause 6.14 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005, the respondent Corporation having no objection.

cases.title: Sultan Khan v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.topic: Instalment facility for undisputed dues to be decided by the Executive Engineer
cases.holding: The Executive Engineer, under Clause 6.14, is to consider and pass an appropriate order on the instalment application within four weeks; the dues being undisputed, no other issue arises.

cases.title: Udayveer Singh v. State of U.P. and 3 Others
cases.topic: Easy-instalment facility for a consumer in financial distress
cases.holding: Yes. Clause 6.15 requires the licensee to extend the facility of easy instalments to consumers in financial distress, and Clause 6.14 supplies the mechanism. Without adverting to the merits, the Court directed the petitioner to deposit Rs. 50,000 within three weeks, on which the Sub Divisional Officer must proceed strictly in accordance with law under Clause 6.14 and fix easy instalments.

cases.title: Usha Devi v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.topic: Easy-instalment facility for a residential consumer in financial distress
cases.holding: Yes. Clause 6.14 provides for payment of outstanding dues in instalments to consumers in financial distress (no waiver of surcharge; the first instalment not below 40%). The consumer was directed to apply under Clause 6.14 within three weeks, the appropriate authority to decide sympathetically by a speaking and reasoned order within a further three weeks, with no coercive recovery for two months or until disposal.

cases.title: Spencer Retail Limited v. State of Uttar Pradesh And 4 Others
cases.topic: Confining a writ to Clause 6.14 instalments accepts the bill; CGRF cannot later waive interest
cases.holding: No. The order of 11.06.2025 in Writ-C No. 18379 of 2025 recorded that although the bill dated 07.05.2025 was assailed on various grounds, the consumer confined the prayer to instalment benefits; the writ was disposed of without going into merits, on a 10% deposit, restoration within 24 hours, and consideration of an instalment application. The consumer thereby stood satisfied with the bill. Going to the CGRF to reduce the amount by waiving interest, instead of availing instalments, and then seeking a writ against the Forum's refusal, would amount to reviewing that consent judgment. The Forum rightly recorded the earlier order. Interest waiver, if any, is for the Electricity Department, not the Forum or a second writ. Petition dismissed.
cases.flag: The extracted 11.06.2025 order cites Clause 6.14 / 'Section 6.14'. Paras 4, 5 and 7 of this order paraphrase the same confinement as 'Clause 6.1(4)'. Catalog has UP-2005::6.14 (instalments) and no 6.1(4). Keyed to 6.14; the 6.1(4) paraphrase is recorded, not silently corrected. The Court also records that CGRF had permitted four equal instalments.

cases.title: Sandhya Kumari v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: installment payment of electricity dues
cases.holding: A writ seeking mandamus to accept electricity arrears in a stated number of installments is disposed of by directing the consumer to apply under Clause 6.14 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005; if the application is filed within a week, the concerned authority shall decide it within six weeks and allow payment of the balance electricity dues in installments.

cases.title: Satya Prakash Katara v. Junior Engineer, Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.topic: instalment facility for reconnection
cases.holding: Without interfering with the Permanent Lok Adalat order, the Court directed the DISCOM to provide a new electricity connection and reconnect supply if the petitioner deposits Rs 40,000 within one month, with the remaining arrears in three easy monthly instalments, having regard to clause 6.14 (no officer below Executive Engineer may grant instalments; EE/DGM/GM may grant up to two, three or four monthly instalments respectively; first instalment not less than 40%).

cases.title: Spencer Retail Limited v. State of Uttar Pradesh
cases.topic: installments and restoration on part payment
cases.holding: Without deciding the bill on merits, if the consumer deposits 10% of the amount demanded under the bill dated 07.05.2025 within ten days, the licensee shall restore the electricity connection within 24 hours of that deposit, and the consumer's application under Clause 6.14 of the UP Electricity Supply Code, 2005 shall be considered in accordance with law.

cases.title: Sunita v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: instalment facility for arrears
cases.holding: A consumer who wishes to pay electricity arrears in instalments may apply under Clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If the application is made within two weeks, the relevant authority is to consider fixing instalments within the next one month. Coercive action stayed for two months. The writ was disposed of on that footing.

cases.title: Devendra Singh v. State of U.P. And 4 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: instalment facility for bill payment
cases.holding: Clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 provides complete machinery for getting instalments of an electricity bill fixed.
