A consumer seeking that facility must approach the relevant authority under that clause; the Court did not itself accept the bill in instalments, but directed that if the petitioner approached within ten days the exercise of granting the facility would be completed within ten days thereafter.

cases.title: Brijpal @ Brijpal Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: instalment of electricity dues
cases.holding: Where the consumer admitted a bill of Rs. 1,45,166/- and sought instalments for financial inability to pay in one go, the writ was disposed of by permitting a representation to the Executive Engineer, who shall consider and decide it in light of Clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 within two weeks, and is expected to take a sympathetic view and grant instalment facility.

cases.title: Rajendra Nath Pal v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: installment facility for dues
cases.holding: The petitioner may apply to the Executive Engineer under clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 for installments to pay the dues, or pursue other permissible remedies.

cases.title: M/s Baba Ice and Cold Storage Pvt. Ltd. v. Ram Chandar, Tehsildar, Kirawali, Agra
cases.topic: No collection charges after full instalment payment under a Clause 6.14 order and recall of the demand notice
cases.holding: No. The applicant deposited the entire dues within the four-month schedule fixed by the writ order — the 2003 security deposit, adjusted on the applicant's request for permanent disconnection, together with the first payment meeting the 40% first instalment — and the Electricity Department itself recalled the demand notice confirming full payment. The writ order having waived collection charges on such compliance, and collection charges being leviable only where the Tehsil authorities actually effect recovery (not where the consumer deposits directly with the Department), the Tehsildar's recovery of Rs.63,335 as collection charges eight months later, with arrest and without notice, was unjustified and malafide. The opposite party admitted the amount had been inadvertently recovered and refunded it; the contempt notice was discharged on compliance.
cases.flag: Source is a contempt order-sheet across several dates (19.03.2010-31.08.2010); not paginated, so pins reference the order dates. Substantive reasoning by Vikram Nath, J. (28.04.2010); final disposal by Shashi Kant Gupta, J. (31.08.2010).

cases.title: Pratap Singh v. State of U.P. Electricity Deptt.
cases.topic: instalment facility for outstanding electricity dues
cases.holding: A consumer who seeks to deposit outstanding electricity dues in instalments may make a written request to the Executive Engineer under clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, which the authority shall consider. Mandamus to compel acceptance of dues in easy instalments was not granted on merits; the writ was disposed of with liberty to pursue that Code route.

cases.title: Nawab Ali v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: instalment facility for financial distress
cases.holding: Clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 provides that the Executive Engineer or any officer higher in rank may extend instalment facility to consumers in financial distress. The petitioner being ready to pay and the licensee having no objection, the Court directed the entire billed amount to be paid in four equal instalments (31.07.2012, 31.10.2012, 31.01.2013 and 30.04.2013), stayed recovery pending each deposit, and provided that default in any instalment would restore the respondents' right to recover the entire amount.

cases.title: Panna Lal v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: instalment facility for financial distress
cases.holding: Paragraph 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 provides that the Executive Engineer or any officer higher in rank may extend instalment facility to customers in financial distress. The petitioner being ready to pay outstanding bill arrears, the Court directed payment of the entire arrears in three equal instalments (on or before 31.7.2012, 30.9.2012 and 30.11.2012), with 50% of collection charges waived if paid on time and the respondents free to recover the entire amount on default; stayed the recovery proceeding pending timely instalments; and, the petitioner having already applied and paid for permanent disconnection on 29.4.2010, directed respondent 4 to finalise that disconnection within 15 days.

cases.title: Installment facility under clause 6.14 for outstanding electricity bills
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: installment facility for financial distress
cases.holding: Paragraph 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 empowers the Executive Engineer or any officer higher in rank to extend installment facility to consumers in financial distress. Where the consumer was ready to pay outstanding electricity bills and the licensee had no objection to realization in installments, the Court directed payment of the entire demanded amount in three equal installments (by 31.7.2012, 30.09.2012 and 30.11.2012), with recovery of the whole sum on default of any installment and stay of recovery in the meantime, the stay continuing stepwise on deposit of each installment.

cases.title: Garib Das v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.topic: instalment facility for consumers in financial distress
cases.holding: Paragraph 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 empowers the Executive Engineer or any officer higher in rank to grant an instalment facility to consumers in financial distress. Where arrears are admitted and the licensee does not object, the Court may schedule payment in three equal instalments, waive half the collection charges on timely deposit, stay recovery pending those deposits (with default restoring the right to recover the whole), and require the Executive Engineer to finalise a pending application for permanent disconnection.

cases.title: Ganga Prasad v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing objection and deposit pending decision on the bill
cases.holding: Without deciding whether the final assessment of Rs 2,64,532 was correct or whether provisional-assessment information had been served, the Court directed the petitioner to deposit Rs 50,000 with the concerned Executive Engineer within 15 days; on such deposit, no coercive measure was to be taken to recover the remaining amount; and the representation/objection as to correctness of the bill was to be entertained and decided on merits in accordance with law under Clause 6.14 read with Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ petition was disposed of.

cases.title: Maa Kaila Devi Sheet Grah Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: instalment facility for electricity dues
cases.holding: On the licensee's statement that the Executive Engineer is empowered under Clause 6.14 read with Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 to permit payment of electricity dues in instalments, the Court disposed of the writ against a recovery citation by permitting the consumer to deposit Rs 50,000 within 15 days and then apply to the Executive Engineer, who may adopt a liberal approach in settling the dispute.

cases.title: M/S Anurag Pisai Kendra v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: instalment facility on recovery citation
cases.holding: The Executive Engineer is empowered under Clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 to consider a request for payment of electricity dues in instalments. The High Court will not itself grant the instalment schedule against a recovery citation; it may dispose of the writ by directing a specified deposit and relegating the consumer to that officer.

cases.title: Ram Lakhan Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: restoration on deposit; representation under 6.14 read with 6.5
cases.holding: Without entering into merits, a consumer who had accepted electricity charges but whose connection stood disconnected was directed to deposit ₹30,000 within a month; if deposited, the connection is to be restored without delay after necessary formalities, and the representation is to be considered expeditiously in the light of Clause 6.14 read with Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

UP-2005::6.15.clause: 6.15(b) (recovery of arrears; two-year limitation) read with s. 56 of the Electricity Act, 2003
UP-2005::6.15.topic: Two-year limitation on recovery of electricity arrears; continuity of demand must be established

cases.title: Rajee Steels Pvt. Ltd. & Anr. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: Two-year limitation on recovery of electricity arrears; continuity of demand must be established
cases.holding: No. Under Clause 6.15(b), no sum due from a consumer is recoverable after two years from when it first became due unless the sum has been continuously shown as recoverable as arrears of charges for electricity supplied. The two-year period may be extended only where the licensee establishes continuous demand on just and proper grounds; where the Corporation keeps silent and fails to establish such efforts, the dues are not recoverable after two years. Here the counter-affidavit was silent on whether, after the first (wrongly issued) recovery notice, any demand notice showed the dues as continuously recoverable, and no date of permanent disconnection or final bill was disclosed. Recovery initiated against petitioner no. 1 in 2010, after disconnection in 1997, was therefore barred by limitation and was quashed.

cases.title: Satya Narayan v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. thru. its Managing Director & Others
cases.topic: The Clause 6.15/s.56(2) two-year recovery bar imposes a positive obligation on the licensee to act (notice, then temporary disconnection under Clause 4.36) within that window; prolonged licensee silence (here, ~12 years with no demand notice) forfeits the right to recover, and Clause 4.38(c)'s affidavit requirement for permanent disconnection cannot be invoked in isolation to defeat this bar
cases.holding: No, not beyond the two-year window contemplated by Clause 6.15(1)(b)/s.56(2), absent evidence the sum was continuously shown as recoverable arrears. Reading the Supply Code as a whole (not piecemeal), Clause 4.36 casts a mandatory obligation on the licensee to issue notice and proceed with temporary disconnection upon non-payment within the statutory window; a licensee's total silence for ~12 years, without a single demand notice, forecloses reliance on Clause 4.38(c) (permanent disconnection contingent on the consumer's own affidavit clearing dues) to justify a stale recovery — that clause operates subject to, not independent of, the licensee's own Clause 4.36/6.15 obligations. The Court moulded relief: the petitioner was permitted to seek refund of any amount paid in excess of what would be recoverable for a proper two-year period, and the Corporation was directed to issue a circular/order sensitising its employees to their Supply Code duties, given the demonstrated departmental negligence.

cases.title: Nitin Kumar Gupta v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: time-bound disposal of pending clause 6.15 application
cases.holding: Inaction by the Executive Engineer on a consumer's clause 6.15 application filed pursuant to an earlier High Court direction is treated as contemptuous; the Court nonetheless granted one further opportunity and directed the Executive Engineer, Pukhrayan, Kanpur Dehat, to consider and decide the application dated 21.12.2013 in accordance with the order dated 26.11.2013 in Writ-C No. 64415 of 2013 within one month of production of a certified copy.

cases.title: Joginder Singh v. D.V.V.N. Ltd. thru' its Managing Director & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: Para 6.15(b) is read with Section 56(1); it does not independently fix a two-year limitation, even in theft cases
cases.holding: Prima facie, no. Para 6.15(b) of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 has to be read in the context of sub-clause (1) of Section 56 and cannot be read in isolation to fix the period of limitation for two years, even in a theft case. The petitioner's reliance on Para 6.15(b) to defeat the recovery as time-barred accordingly failed at the prima facie stage.

cases.title: Mohammad Zaheer v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: delayed recovery as arrears of land revenue
cases.holding: After a 2015 interlocutory order directing a counter affidavit and staying further recovery under the 16 March 2015 citation on deposit of Rs.45,000, the writ challenging that recovery as barred by paragraph 6.15 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 was dismissed in default for non-appearance of the petitioner, and the interim order was discharged.

cases.title: Muneshwar Prasad Baranwal v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Another
cases.topic: Recovery ~19 years after permanent disconnection — interim stay
cases.holding: Prima facie, the plea has substance: a recovery notice issued about 19 years after permanent disconnection (27.5.1999), relying on Clause 6.15(b), cannot readily be sustained, and the consumer cannot be liable for a period after supply had ceased. The Court stayed the recovery notice pending affidavits; the matter requires consideration.
cases.flag: Interim order only; final view on the Clause 6.15(b) bar reserved.

cases.title: M/s Paliwal Alloys (Pvt.) Ltd. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Ors.
cases.topic: Two-year bar on recovery of arrears; a reasoned order required to recover after two years
cases.holding: No. Under s.56(2) of the Act and Clause 6.15 of the Code, arrears are not recoverable after two years from the date they first became due (unless continuously shown as recoverable). The peak-hour penalty (imposed 27.11.2006 for 24.11.2002-8.2.2003) could not be recovered after two years without the Corporation adverting to s.56(2)/Clause 6.15 and passing a reasoned order explaining recovery beyond that period; the 10.6.2009 notice gave no such reason, so the recovery of the peak-hour penalty was unjustified.

cases.title: M/s. Zaz Leather Complex Pvt. Ltd. v. Kanpur Electricity Supply Co. Ltd. and Another
cases.topic: Two-year recovery bar applies to a fresh bill for the licensee's own metering (MF) error
cases.holding: No. Section 56(2) and Clause 6.15(b) bar recovery of a sum after two years from when it first became due unless shown continuously as recoverable as arrears. The MF error was the licensee's own and the consumer had bona fide paid all bills; the fresh demand of 6.6.2011 could therefore reach back only two years (to 6.6.2009). The bill was quashed and the licensee directed to re-bill only for that two-year period.

cases.title: Sewa Suraksha Sahkari Awas Samiti Ltd. v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: occupier dues not recoverable by auction of owner's land
cases.holding: Where the temporary connection was taken by an occupier who had disclosed the petitioner as owner, the Court was unable to see how the owner's land could be sold in auction for the occupier's unpaid dues. Clause 6.15, as relied on, entitled the licensee to recover from the person who had taken the connection, as arrears of land revenue. Coercive action against the petitioner stayed till the next listing; the Department remained free to proceed against respondent no. 7.
cases.flag: Court described cl. 6.15 as recovery of the connection-holder's dues as arrears of land revenue, not the two-year billing bar.

cases.title: Executive Engineer, Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. The Electricity Consumer Grievances Redressal Forum & Anr.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: Explanation to Clause 6.15(b): inspection-based charges first due on the bill, to be issued within two billing cycles
cases.holding: No. The explanation to Clause 6.15(b) provides that charges or penalties levied as a result of meter reading or inspection of the consumer's installation become first due from the due date of payment of such a bill, and that bill shall be provided to the consumer not later than two billing cycles for that category. The Forum, relying on Clause 6.15 and Section 56, held the consumer could not be made liable for 51 months of overload arrears. The High Court found no infirmity in that order.

cases.title: Chandrapal v. U.P. Power Corporation
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-amount challenge relegated to Code remedy
cases.holding: Where the consumer challenges the amount shown in an electricity bill, the High Court will not examine the bill on writ and will leave the petitioner to pursue the remedy available under clause 6.15 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
cases.flag: Order treats para 6.15 as the consumer's bill-dispute remedy; catalog maps 6.15 to the two-year recovery bar.

cases.title: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Mohammad Khalid
cases.topic: recovery of arrears / two-year limitation
cases.holding: On the licensee's Article 227 challenge to a Permanent Lok Adalat award that treated all but Rs.1,11,829 of a CT-multiplier differential bill as time-barred under clause 6.15(b), the Court held that the limitation issue required consideration, issued notice to the consumer, and did not decide whether 6.15(b)'s two-year bar or the six-year period urged under the 1958 dues-recovery Rule 5-A governed.

UP-2005::6.16.topic: Protective treatment of sick industrial companies / relief undertakings

cases.title: Kanpur Electricity Supply Co. Ltd. & Anr. v. M/s L.M.L. Limited & Ors.
cases.topic: Protective treatment of sick industrial companies / relief undertakings
cases.holding: Clauses 4.41 and 4.49 are Rules framed to help industries in difficulty; read with Annexure 6.5 / Clause 6.16 (disconnected units seeking revival) and Clause 9.5 (Relief Undertaking regime under s.23), only current dues are realized from a sick/relief undertaking, with past dues recovered in instalments and no coercive disconnection — harmonised with the BIFR/SICA order.

cases.title: Allauddin v. Electricity Distribution Division
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-dispute-statutory-complaint
cases.holding: A writ challenging an electricity bill as incorrect or excessive is not decided on merits where clause 6.16 supplies a complaint to the Executive Engineer (R); the petition is disposed of with liberty to file that complaint, and the Executive Engineer is to decide it on merits in accordance with law within the time fixed.
cases.flag: Order cites clause 6.16 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2002; the catalogued provision is UP-2005::6.16.

cases.title: Gulzar Ahmad v. Electricity Ombudsman
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: writ against Ombudsman billing order
cases.holding: A writ challenging an Electricity Ombudsman order and a subsequent electricity demand on the plea that charges for a disconnected period violated Clause 6.2 will not be entertained where the petition raises disputed questions of fact that cannot be adjudicated under Article 226, the consumer has not deposited the bill properly, and the consumer was caught in theft of electricity; if the authorities have proceeded as per law, the writ is dismissed.

cases.title: Vineet Plastics Ltd. v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. and Another
cases.topic: No series of provisional assessment bills may be issued without a statutory or Code basis
cases.holding: No. A series of provisional assessment bills cannot be given unless the Statute or the Supply Code so provides. A provisional assessment under Section 126 follows an inspection and requires an opportunity to object; the only Code provision for a provisional bill is Clause 6.2(b), confined to cases where the meter reading cannot be taken; and disputes over a regular bill lie under Clause 6.5. As the licensee could point to no provision for the serial provisional monthly bills issued without deciding the consumer's objections, the bills for October, November and December 2013 were quashed, with liberty to issue rectified bills per law (excess payable / shortfall adjusted with interest) and any check-meter to be installed at the licensee's own expense.

UP-2005::6.3.clause: Annexure 6.3 (period of assessment for unauthorised use); interim relief pending final decision
UP-2005::6.3.topic: Interim restoration of supply on deposit of one year's assessed amount, pending decision on the assessment period

cases.title: Vijay Krishna Agrawal & Anr. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: Interim restoration of supply on deposit of one year's assessed amount, pending decision on the assessment period
cases.holding: By interim order, the Division Bench directed that the electricity connection be restored subject to the consumer depositing, within a week, the amount assessed under the order dated 19 May 2010 limited to a period of one year before the inspection dated 24 February 2010, with liberty to pay regular bills as raised. The deposit was confined to one year's assessment, prima facie reflecting the consumer's contention that under Annexure 6.3 of the Supply Code, 2005 the assessment period is capped at 365 days, while the validity of the assessment (and the competing reading that Annexure 6.3 applies only when the period cannot be ascertained) was expressly left to be decided finally.
cases.flag: Source is an order-sheet compilation without printed page numbers or numbered paragraphs; pins are order dates. Coram is the bench that passed the substantive interim order dated 20.7.2010; the matter has since travelled through later benches (most recently Atul Sreedharan, J. and Siddharth Nandan, J.).

cases.title: Ramveer Singh v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Another
cases.topic: UUE assessment must be at 1.5 times the tariff, not thrice
cases.holding: At one-and-a-half times the tariff rate per unit applicable to the consumer category, per Clause 2 of Annexure 6.3 (this amount not being counted for computing minimum monthly/annual charges). An assessment made at thrice the tariff rate is erroneous and illegal to that extent; the assessment and the unreasoned appellate order are set aside and the matter remanded for a fresh order at the correct rate.

cases.title: Kalicharan Yadav v. U.P. Electricity Regulatory Commission
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: 6.3(B)(1) classification for assessing officer; s.142 premature
cases.holding: Mandamus to the Commission to conclude a s.142 (read with s.146) complaint was refused. A pending Commission complaint does not relieve the consumer of the duty to reply to an assessment show-cause. Even if the consumer claims treatment under 6.3(B)(1) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, that is a fact pleading for the assessing officer, who must pass a reasoned order. The Commission complaint was wholly premature and misconceived. Petitioner given three weeks to reply to the 5 September 2023 notice; assessment to be finalized within two weeks thereafter.
cases.flag: Court refers both to Annexure 6.3(B)(1)/(II) and to Section 6.3(B)(1) of the Code.

cases.title: Chameli Devi v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: hearing on disputed bill
cases.holding: Once restoration of supply is conceded, a remaining dispute that the bill raised has not been waived is to be decided by the licensee after granting the consumer an opportunity of hearing under clause 6.4 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, followed by a reasoned order; the writ is disposed of on that direction without a merits finding on the bill.

cases.title: Sushila Upadhyay v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: new connection; infructuous writ
cases.holding: Where the consumer has completed the U.P. Electricity Supply Code formalities and deposited the charges, and the licensee has commenced supply and issued a sealing certificate, a writ seeking mandamus for that new connection no longer survives and is dismissed as infructuous.

cases.title: Satya Narain Gupta v. State of U.P. and others
cases.topic: alternative remedy to Executive Engineer
cases.holding: A writ challenging electricity bills and a recovery certificate, including previous-owner arrears, was held to have an alternative remedy of approaching the concerned Executive Engineer under para 6.4 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
cases.flag: ambiguous

cases.title: Smt. Tasneem Ahmad v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: grievance-before-executive-engineer
cases.holding: Where the licensee represents that the consumer may place her grievance before the concerned Executive Engineer under Rule 6.45 of the Electricity Supply Code 2005, the writ may be disposed of with a direction that the move will be attended by a speaking order preferably within three weeks, and disconnection stayed till that decision or three weeks, whichever is earlier.
cases.flag: Court cited 'Rule 6.45'; UP-2005 has no clause 6.45 (likely 6.4/6.5).

UP-2005::6.5.topic: Billing disputes — alternative remedy of complaint before the Competent Authority

cases.title: Chandrika v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.topic: Billing disputes — alternative remedy of complaint before the Competent Authority
cases.holding: A dispute as to the correctness of a bill is to be raised by complaint before the Competent Authority (the Executive Engineer) under Clause 6.5 of the Code; the writ petition is disposed of by relegating the consumer to that remedy, with a direction to decide by a speaking order after hearing and interim protection from coercive recovery conditioned on a part-deposit (Rs. 20,000).

cases.title: Lala Ram Batham v. U.P. Power Corporation Nigam & Ors.
cases.topic: Disputed meter reading relegated to a Clause 6.5 representation, with mandatory inspection of the removed meter
cases.holding: Under Clause 6.5 of the Code, the consumer may raise the grievance by representation before the licensee, who must decide it expeditiously by a speaking order after hearing the consumer; before deciding, the licensee must personally inspect the removed (old) meter to verify the correctness of the disputed reading. The writ court did not adjudicate the claim on merits.

cases.title: Indra Dutt Pandey v. M.D., Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.topic: billing complaint as alternative to writ
cases.holding: Where a consumer seeks quashing of an electricity bill, including on the ground that arrears of more than two years have been included, and a complaint under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is available, the writ petition will be dismissed and the consumer left to file that complaint.

cases.title: Mohd. Chand Pisar v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: A writ petition seeking quashing of an electricity bill will be disposed of without a merits decision where the consumer has an appropriate complaint under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the consumer may avail that complaint.

cases.title: Ram Dularey v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: clause 6.5 complaint as alternative to writ for bill quash
cases.holding: A writ to quash a monthly electricity bill will not be entertained where the consumer has an appropriate complaint under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the petition is dismissed with liberty to file that complaint.

cases.title: Sri Krishna v. State of U.P. — pending consumer complaint without stay does not bar recovery
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection
cases.holding: Pending Consumer Forum proceedings, without a stay, do not bar recovery of electricity dues. A prayer to correct bills according to meter reading is to be pursued under clause 6.5 of the Supply Code, not by writ. Petition dismissed.

cases.title: Roop Narain v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: electricity bill — statutory complaint under clause 6.5
cases.holding: Where a consumer seeks quashing of an electricity bill, the available statutory remedy is a complaint under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and the High Court will not entertain a writ petition in the face of that remedy.

cases.title: Navin Kumar v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: writ against assessment; alternative remedy
cases.holding: A writ petition seeking quashing of an Executive Engineer’s assessment order is dismissed where the consumer has a statutory alternative remedy under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 and Section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003, and where years of pendency without interim relief mean consequential recovery must be taken to have followed.
cases.flag: Court cites Clause 6.5 and s.127 in the alternative against an ‘assessment order’ without saying whether the demand was a billing objection (6.5) or a s.126 assessment (s.127).

cases.title: Prem Singh v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.topic: Dispute over assessment of an electricity bill relegated to the Clause 6.5 authority
cases.holding: The petitioner is permitted to approach the Executive Engineer (Rural), Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd., Fatehgarh, District Farrukhabad by invoking Clause 6.5 of the Supply Code for redressal of the billing assessment dispute.

cases.title: Hari Narayan Patel v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing objection
cases.holding: A consumer who challenges electricity bills and seeks quashing of a recovery citation has a statutory remedy under Para 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, where those objections can be raised, considered and decided; the writ petition is dismissed with liberty to avail that remedy.

cases.title: Vishwanath Sharma v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: complaint against inspection bill before Executive Engineer
cases.holding: A consumer aggrieved by an electricity bill issued after inspection has a statutory remedy of complaint under paragraph 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 before the Executive Engineer, who is to consider and decide the complaint in accordance with law. A request for reconnection may also be made and considered in accordance with law. The writ is disposed of on that footing without quashing the bill.

cases.title: Mohan Kumar Agrawal v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer
cases.holding: Where the writ petitioner is aggrieved by an electricity bill and the demand notice issued consequent to it, the remedy is to file a complaint under paragraph 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, to the Executive Engineer; the High Court will not quash the bill and instead directs that such a complaint, if filed in accordance with paragraph 6.5, be considered and expeditiously disposed of preferably within one month.

cases.title: Kunwar Pal Singh Raghav v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: A grievance regarding an electricity bill or demand notice is to be raised by filing an appropriate complaint under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 before the concerned Executive Engineer; a writ petition raising that grievance is dismissed on the ground of alternative remedy.

cases.title: M/s Mehak Metals Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: writ dismissed with liberty to pursue clause 6.5 first
cases.holding: On the petitioner's statement that it would first seek the clause 6.5 Electricity Supply Code, 2005 remedy, the writ petition was dismissed with that liberty and any interim order was discharged.

cases.title: Kamal Kant Dixit v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: A consumer’s grievance against an electricity bill and consequent recovery or demand is to be raised as a complaint under para 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 before the concerned Executive Engineer; the writ is dismissed as not maintainable in view of that alternative remedy, with a direction that any such complaint be disposed of expeditiously.

cases.title: Anil Kumar Singh v. M.D., U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: recovery-citation-and-bill-complaint
cases.holding: A recovery citation for electricity dues, issued on the Executive Engineer's recovery certificate, is not illegal where the writ does not challenge any electricity bill or assessment. Deposit of the demanded amount as directed is without prejudice to a complaint against an incorrectly issued bill under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, or any other statutory remedy under that Code.

cases.title: Satya Prakash v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: complaint for correction of electricity bill
cases.holding: A consumer who seeks correction of an electricity bill must file an appropriate complaint under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the High Court will not issue a writ of mandamus directing the licensee to correct the bill.

cases.title: Jakesh Singh Alias Kewal v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing objection to Executive Engineer
cases.holding: A demand notice will not be quashed in writ where the licensee states that a connection has already been sanctioned and the demand relates to it; any remaining grievance about the electricity bill may be raised by an appropriate complaint under clause 6.5 of the Supply Code, 2005 before the concerned Executive Engineer.

cases.title: Hukum Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer
cases.holding: Where the writ petitioner's grievance is against an electricity bill, the remedy is a complaint under paragraph 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, before the concerned Executive Engineer. The Court did not quash the bill and disposed of the petition observing that if such a complaint is filed, it shall be considered and decided accordingly.

cases.title: Awadh Narayan Mishra v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing dispute — complaint before Executive Engineer
cases.holding: Where a consumer disputes the correctness of an electricity bill and seeks in a writ petition to quash a demand notice for outstanding dues, the available remedy is a complaint under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 before the Executive Engineer, who shall consider the complaint, take an appropriate decision, and communicate it to the consumer.

cases.title: Badami Devi v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing complaint to Executive Engineer
cases.holding: Where a consumer is aggrieved by an electricity bill alleged to have been wrongly issued, it is open to the consumer to submit a complaint under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 before the Executive Engineer, who may consider and decide the objection in accordance with law; the writ petition was disposed of on that observation.

cases.title: Ram Soojan v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer
cases.holding: A writ challenging an electricity bill is disposed by relegating the consumer to file an objection under Clause 6.5 before the Executive Engineer, who may consider and decide it in accordance with law.

cases.title: Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: Where a consumer challenges an electricity bill in writ, the available remedy is to file a complaint under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, before the Executive Engineer, who may look into the grievance and take appropriate action; the writ is disposed of on that footing without a merits decision on the bill.

cases.title: Anayatur Rahman v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd./P.V.V.N. Ltd. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: disputed bills — complaint before competent authority
cases.holding: Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 deals with disputed bills and accuracy in the bill; the consumer's remedy is a complaint before the competent authority, which must proceed to redress the grievance. The writ was not entertained. Liberty was given to raise the grievance under that provision, to be dealt with in accordance with law preferably within three months from presentation of a certified copy of the order.

cases.title: Ashok v. State of U.P. — bill-dispute writ relegated to clause 6.5
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: Where a consumer disputes the correctness of an electricity bill and seeks quashing of a notice of outstanding dues, the writ court will not decide the dispute on merits if a complaint under Para 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 lies before the Executive Engineer; the petition is disposed of with a direction that any such complaint be considered, decided and communicated.

cases.title: Haneef v. State of U.P. — outstanding-dues notice relegated to para 6.5
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: Where a consumer seeks to quash an Executive Engineer's notice of outstanding electricity dues by disputing the correctness of the bill, the High Court will not decide the bill on a writ petition. The available remedy is a complaint under paragraph 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, before the Executive Engineer; if such a complaint is filed, it shall be considered, decided, and the decision communicated to the consumer.

cases.title: Jai Prakash Maurya v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: alternative remedy
cases.holding: The writ was dismissed for want of prosecution after none appeared for the petitioner on a revised call. The Court recorded that, even otherwise, clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 afforded an efficacious statutory alternative remedy.

cases.title: Smt. Kamlesh Sharma v. Executive Engineer, Dakshinanchal Electricity Distribution Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-correction-application
cases.holding: A consumer who seeks correction of an electricity bill must file an appropriate application before the authority competent under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; a writ of mandamus for that correction is not decided on merits and is disposed of with liberty to take that remedy.

cases.title: Mohan Singh v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.topic: complaint-to-executive-engineer
cases.holding: A consumer aggrieved by an electricity bill that includes miscellaneous charges must file a complaint under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 before the Executive Engineer, who may consider it; the writ is disposed of on that observation without a merits decision on the bill.

cases.title: Smt. Saroj v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: Where a consumer challenges an electricity bill by writ and a complaint against that bill is available under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 before the Executive Engineer, the writ is disposed of with liberty to file that complaint, which is to be decided accordingly.

cases.title: Kisan Sahkari Chini Mills Ltd. v. Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.topic: billing dispute to Executive Engineer
cases.holding: Without examining the merits of the consumer's claim, a writ asking the licensee to decide billing-dispute representations is disposed of by directing the Executive Engineer (Prescribed Authority) to decide those representations in accordance with law under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, preferably within six weeks of production of a certified copy of the order and photocopies of the representations.

cases.title: Manisha Cold Storage (Pvt.) Ltd. v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. &
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Sanjay Parashar v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: alternative remedy for billing dispute
cases.holding: A writ petition raising a grievance as to the correctness of electricity bills or otherwise is not to be entertained, the petitioner having an alternative remedy under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 before the competent authority.

cases.title: M/s Pawan Putra Floor Mill v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.topic: disputed bills and arrears
cases.holding: Disputed bills and arrears arising with a reconnection or pole-reinstallation grievance are to be taken to the competent authority under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, read with clause 4.9; the Executive Engineer shall decide within two months.

cases.title: Sanjay Kumar Gupta v. Consumer Grievances Redressal Forum & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is a complete mechanism for redressal of grievances of incorrect billing and non-communication of correct meter-reading status; the petitioner may approach respondent No. 2, who may consider the same in accordance with law.

cases.title: Prem Kishor Trivedi v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-dispute-clause-6.5-forum
cases.holding: A writ challenging a recovery citation and electricity bill after an alleged permanent disconnection, issued in a deceased consumer's name, is not to be decided on affidavits where the facts are highly disputed. Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is the remedy: the consumer is to apply to the competent authority within one month, and that authority is to decide within the time stipulated in the clause. The Court expressed no opinion on merits. On the licensee's statement, coercive measures are not to be taken until that decision if the consumer complies.
cases.flag: Court directed Clause 6.5; the licensee had invoked Clause 6.5(b).

cases.title: Ram Asrey v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: pending-billing-objection
cases.holding: Where a consumer's application under Clause 6.5 remains pending before the competent authority, a writ seeking to restrain recovery of dues and to have that application decided will be disposed of by leaving it to that authority to consider and decide the application in accordance with law, within the time stipulated in Clause 6.5, without the Court expressing any opinion on the merits of the claim.

cases.title: Smt. Bhauneesh Singh Gaur v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: revision of unmetered electricity bills
cases.holding: A dispute over revision of electricity bills raised while supply was unmetered is to be decided on an application under clause 6.5 by a reasoned and speaking order within four weeks; the writ court does not revise the bills itself.

cases.title: Kamlesh Kumar Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill quantum dispute — clause 6.5 remedy
cases.holding: Where a consumer disputes the quantum of a bill, the dispute is purely factual and the writ court will not appraise evidence on annexures. The consumer has a more appropriate remedy under clause 6.5 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and the writ petition cannot be maintained at that stage; the petitioner may avail that remedy if so desired.

cases.title: Mohammad Khalid v. Pashchimanchal Vidhyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. and 2 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Raghubir v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing dispute — writ vs Clause 6.5
cases.holding: Where a writ petition disputes an electricity bill and raises disputed questions of fact, those questions are better decided by the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ is disposed of with liberty to the petitioner to avail that remedy.

cases.title: Chhannu Lal Dwivedi v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: M/S. Pooja Aata Chakki v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing-objection-forum
cases.holding: Where a consumer assails an electricity bill as incorrect, the proper forum is the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, which is better placed to decide because the entire connection record is available before it. The writ was disposed of directing that authority to decide the petitioner’s existing objection dated 8 May 2014; the petitioner was to file a certified copy of the order with that objection within two weeks, after which the authority was to proceed in accordance with Clause 6.5.

cases.title: Mukesh Singh Chaturvedi v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: clause-6.5-alternate-remedy
cases.holding: A writ challenging an electricity consumption bill, including on the plea that the meter was defective, raises highly disputed questions of fact which the authority holding the connection records must decide under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the High Court will not interfere with the bill and will relegate the consumer to that remedy.

cases.title: Mohd. Tahir v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: bill-dispute-alternate-remedy
cases.holding: The Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is a self-contained code. A dispute as to the validity of an electricity bill is to be raised under clause 6.5; once that mechanism is provided, the consumer is to avail it and the writ petition will not be entertained.

cases.title: Ram Sagar v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: recovery without assessment after disconnection
cases.holding: Where the consumer's grievance is that a recovery certificate was issued without assessment after disconnection in 2007, the Executive Engineer is the competent authority under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the writ is disposed of with a direction to consider and decide the representation by a reasoned speaking order in accordance with law within six weeks, coercive action remaining stayed for two months or until that decision, whichever is earlier.

cases.title: Shiv Kumar v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing dispute; writ relegated to statutory objection
cases.holding: A consumer disputing the correctness of electricity bills may raise the dispute under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 or before the consumer grievance redressal forum. The High Court will not examine the bills on a writ petition.

cases.title: Prabandhak (C/M) Adarsh Rashtriya Inter College v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer
cases.holding: Power to revise an electricity bill vests in the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. A writ seeking only a direction to revise the bill in accordance with law is to be left to that authority, which shall decide the grievance within two months of production of a certified copy if no revision has yet been made.

cases.title: Jamuna Prasad v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: bill-accuracy-dispute
cases.holding: Where a consumer disputes the accuracy of an electricity bill and the controversy is purely factual, the writ court will not adjudicate the demand. The consumer is to apply under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the competent authority must decide the complaint by a speaking and reasoned order in accordance with the procedure in clause 6.5(b). Recovery proceedings remain in abeyance until that application is decided and thereafter follow the authority's order.

cases.title: Ex. Eng. E.D. Division v. Ashish Purohit
cases.topic: Permanent Lok Adalat jurisdiction vis-à-vis Clause 6.5
cases.holding: The High Court admitted the licensee's writ, recorded that the Permanent Lok Adalat's jurisdiction to entertain a dispute said to be raisable under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 required consideration, directed affidavits, listed the matter after 16 October 2014, and stayed operation of the Lok Adalat's order dated 31.7.2014 till further orders.

cases.title: Smt. Mithilesh Gupta v. Consumer Grievances Redressel Forum At Commissionary & Ors
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing and meter-accuracy dispute — Clause 6.5 remedy
cases.holding: Where a consumer disputes the correctness of an electricity demand on the ground that the meter is operating erroneously, Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is the available forum for redressal. The writ petition is disposed of with liberty to approach the competent authority (respondent no. 2), who shall examine the complaint and pass an appropriate order in accordance with law.

cases.title: Smt. Tripti Das v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-accuracy-dispute-remedy
cases.holding: Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 provides a remedy to a consumer disputing the accuracy of any bill; a writ petition raising that dispute is disposed of by leaving the petitioner to take that recourse.

cases.title: Brij Kishore Rai v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: Where the consumer had admittedly not paid electricity bills for almost two years, disconnection was not unjustified. Grievances about non-installation or malfunction of the meter and about the bills lay before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5. The writ was disposed of directing that if the petitioner filed a suitable application with a certified copy of the order, the Executive Engineer would consider and decide it in accordance with law by a reasoned speaking order, preferably within three weeks; if any bill was found payable, the line would be reconnected within one week of payment.

cases.title: Lalit Ram Tripathi v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: recovery-certificate-alternative-remedy
cases.holding: Against a recovery certificate the appropriate remedy is an appeal under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; a writ petition is dismissed on that alternative remedy.
cases.flag: Court called Clause 6.5 an 'appeal' against a recovery certificate; 6.5 is the billing-objection route.

cases.title: Sudesh Mishra v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: pending billing objection to Executive Engineer
cases.holding: Where a consumer has filed an objection purported to be under clause 6.5 against a revised bill and alleges disconnection and a demand notice without decision of that objection, the writ court may dispose of the petition by directing the Executive Engineer to decide the objection within a fixed time, without adjudicating disconnection or the demand on merits.

cases.title: Vaid Nath Vishwakarma v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing-objection
cases.holding: A consumer disputing the accuracy of a bill and a citation issued thereon has an alternative remedy of filing an objection under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the writ is dismissed, and an objection filed within six weeks of the order shall be entertained.

cases.title: Deepak Kumar Bansal v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: dual-bills-same-month
cases.holding: A consumer who receives two bills for the same month in different amounts must first file an appropriate application under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the writ court will not decide the discrepancy and, if such an application is filed, the authority shall consider and decide it by a reasoned speaking order within four weeks of production of a certified copy of the order.

cases.title: Krishan Gopal v. Dakhidanchal Vidut Vitaran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: meter installation and billing as per reading
cases.holding: A grievance seeking decision of an application for installation of a meter and for raising the bill as per the meter reading is redressable under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the licensee was directed to decide the application within six weeks of a certified copy of the order being filed, and the writ was disposed of without a merits determination.

cases.title: Lala Ram v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: Where a recovery citation is issued for electricity dues on a connection not standing in the petitioner's name and an objection before the Collector remains pending, the High Court will not decide the dispute on merits and will relegate the consumer to an application before the Executive Engineer under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, with a direction to consider and decide that application within two weeks of production of a certified copy of the order.

cases.title: Kunwar Pal Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing-objection-disconnected-period
cases.holding: Where the consumer objects to the correctness of a bill covering a period of disconnection, the writ court will not itself decide liability; the competent authority under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is to pass appropriate orders and correct the bill, if required.

cases.title: Mitthu Lal v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection
cases.holding: A consumer who seeks correction of an electricity bill said to include arrears of a One Time Settlement cannot obtain that relief in the form of a writ. The proper course is an application under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If such an application is moved, the authority concerned will consider it and correct the bill if any arrear is shown.

cases.title: Arun Kumar v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing objection — writ relegated to Supply Code remedy
cases.holding: A consumer who disputes the correctness of electricity arrears shown in a bill and seeks their deletion has a remedy of filing an application under paragraph 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ is disposed of with a direction that if such an application is made, the competent authority shall consider and decide the matter by a reasoned speaking order after due opportunity of hearing, within three weeks of production of a certified copy of the order.

cases.title: Gopal Babu v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection
cases.holding: A pending application for correction of electricity bills is to be treated as an objection under paragraph 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 and decided by a reasoned and speaking order after opportunity of hearing; the consumer shall pay the corrected amount.

cases.title: Swati Kakkar v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited And Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: alternative remedy for assessment bill
cases.holding: A writ challenging an assessment bill is not maintainable where the consumer has not first disputed the bill under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and has also not availed the further remedies before the District Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum and the Ombudsman.

cases.title: Mahavir Singh v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: A writ petition filed at a belated stage is liable to be dismissed on laches; any dispute relating to the bill may be raised by an application under paragraph 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Sarvjeet Singh v. State of U.P. & Another
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Anil Kumar v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: bill-correction-application-to-executive-engineer
cases.holding: A writ seeking correction of an electricity bill is disposed of by directing the petitioner to make an appropriate application before the Executive Engineer; such application shall be treated as filed under paragraph 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, decided within three weeks, and an appropriate corrected bill issued.

cases.title: Chandra Pal v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing dispute — statutory objection
cases.holding: Where a consumer is not satisfied with the amount claimed towards electricity dues, the proper course is the remedy under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; a writ petition challenging such a demand is dismissed with liberty to pursue that remedy.

cases.title: M/s Vimla Gramodyog Sansthan v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer
cases.holding: A consumer aggrieved by a demand issued on the ground of past underbilling (billing at half the applicable rate) has a remedy under clause 6.5 of the Supply Code, 2005. The writ court will relegate the party to that forum without expressing any opinion on the merits. Restoration of supply may be sought from the competent authority subject to the prescribed terms.

cases.title: Lekhraj Gambhir v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-under-clause-6.5
cases.holding: A consumer dissatisfied with an electricity demand notice must first approach the authority under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; a writ petition is dismissed with liberty to pursue that remedy.

cases.title: Rajveer Singh v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: disputed electricity bill and arrears
cases.holding: A disputed electricity demand on a tube-well connection, where the consumer has already approached the Executive Engineer for rectification, is to be dealt with under Clause 6.5. The High Court directed the petitioner to place a certified copy before respondent no.2, who shall examine the request and issue necessary orders in accordance with law within six weeks, without deciding the bill on merits in writ.

cases.title: Jor Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: Where a consumer disputes the correctness of outstanding electricity charges that are the subject of a recovery notice, clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 supplies a complaint before the competent authority. A writ petition raising a factual billing dispute will be disposed of with liberty to file that complaint, which the authority shall consider and decide in accordance with the Code.

cases.title: Brij Mohan Agrawal v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Another
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 1 month, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.
cases.flag: The order cites 'Clause 6.5 of the UP Electricity Supply Code, 2004'. The Code in force is the 2005 Code. Recorded, not silently corrected.

cases.title: Krishna Tyagi v. U.P.P.C.L.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: Where electricity bills are challenged and basic questions of fact are involved, the writ is dismissed and consumers are relegated to the statutory alternative remedy of raising objections under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; upon such objections being raised, the authorities are expected to deal with them in accordance with law.

cases.title: Virendra v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: A consumer who seeks quashing of an electricity bill in a writ petition has a remedy under paragraph 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and the High Court will decline to entertain the petition on that account.

cases.title: M/s Kundan Castings (Pvt.) Ltd. v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing dispute — statutory alternative remedy
cases.holding: A consumer who is not satisfied with the total demand raised in an electricity bill has a statutory alternative remedy under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ petition is dismissed with liberty to pursue that remedy.

cases.title: Sigma Casting Ltd. v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: alternative remedy against billed demand
cases.holding: A consumer dissatisfied with the total demand raised under an electricity bill has a statutory alternative remedy under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; a writ petition is dismissed with liberty to pursue that remedy.

cases.title: Sulabi Devi v. State of U.P. & Another
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Jokhu Lal v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing-objection-forum
cases.holding: If a consumer is not satisfied with a bill of demand raised by the Electricity Department, the challenge lies by an appropriate application under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, or before the Electricity Consumer Forum; a writ petition is not the forum and stands dismissed.

cases.title: R.S. Savita @ Ravindra Kumar v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-of-demand-challenge-clause-6.5
cases.holding: A consumer who is not satisfied with a bill of demand raised by the Electricity Department may challenge it by an appropriate application under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, or by approaching the Electricity Consumer Forum; a writ petition raising that grievance is dismissed.

cases.title: Ajab Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: demand-bill-objection-under-clause-6.5
cases.holding: If a consumer is not satisfied with a demand bill raised by the Electricity Department, for whatever reason, the remedy is under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ petition is dismissed with liberty to seek that remedy.

cases.title: Shesh Mani v. State of U.P. and 3 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: M/S Shiv Ganga Aata Mill v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: decision of pending Clause 6.5 billing objections
cases.holding: Where the consumer has already filed objections to electricity bills under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 and those objections remain undecided, the writ petition is disposed of with a direction that the distribution licensee make all endeavours to decide the objections within the stipulated time; the bills are not examined on merits.

cases.title: Dimber Singh v. Dakshinachal Vidhyut Vitaran Ltd.
cases.topic: decision of clause 6.5 objection
cases.holding: Where the consumer's sole prayer is that an objection already filed under clause 6.5 be decided, the writ may be disposed of by directing the licensee to decide that objection expeditiously, preferably within three weeks of a certified copy being filed, without adjudicating the merits, which the competent authority is to examine in accordance with law.

cases.title: Natthan Singh v. U.P.P.C.L. And 2 Others
cases.topic: billing dispute — writ not entertained where Clause 6.5 remedy available
cases.holding: Where a consumer disputes bills raised by the Power Corporation, the High Court will not entertain a writ petition if the consumer can take recourse to Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the petition is dismissed and the consumer is left to that remedy.

cases.title: Krishan Kumar v. U.P.P.C.L. And Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-dispute-forum
cases.holding: Where the consumer disputes bills raised by the Power Corporation, the High Court will not entertain a writ petition if the remedy under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is available; the petition is dismissed with liberty to avail that remedy.

cases.title: Ashu Rathi v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: alternate remedy for disputed demand and recovery
cases.holding: A writ that disputes the amount of an electricity demand and assails only the recovery citation, without challenging the principal demand of charges, is not to be entertained; Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 furnishes the alternative remedy.

cases.title: Rajendra Singh Baghel v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: If the consumer has any objection to a bill raised by the distribution licensee, the proper remedy is to challenge the bill in accordance with clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; a writ petition is dismissed for availability of that statutory alternative remedy.

cases.title: Suraj Pal v. Dakshinachal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: pending 6.5 correction application
cases.holding: Where a consumer has filed an application for correction under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, the writ may be disposed of by directing the competent authority to decide that application within four weeks of production of a certified copy of the order, without any finding on the bill.

cases.title: Rakesh Chandra Mishra v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: pending bill-rectification application before Executive Engineer
cases.holding: Where a consumer's application for rectification of electricity bills under Clause 6.5 of the Supply Code, 2005 is pending, the writ court will not examine the veracity of the billing claim and will instead direct the Executive Engineer to process that application within a stipulated time.

cases.title: Chandra Shekhar v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: bill-correctness-challenge
cases.holding: Where a consumer seeks to challenge the correctness of a bill issued by the Electricity Department, the proper remedy is an application under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, before the competent authority; a writ petition for that purpose is dismissed.

cases.title: M/s Shiv Ganga Aata Mill v. Srikant Pandey, Executive Engineer
cases.topic: contempt of direction to decide Clause 6.5 billing objections
cases.holding: Where a prior writ had directed the licensee to decide the consumer's Clause 6.5 objections to electricity bills within the stipulated seven days, the contempt court, without recording wilful disobedience, afforded the opposite parties one further opportunity to comply within two weeks of production of a certified copy of the contempt order, and disposed of the application at that stage with liberty to the applicant to move a fresh application if the writ direction was still not complied with.

cases.title: Narayan Singh Kardam v. U.P.P.C.L.
cases.topic: billing-objection-alternative-remedy
cases.holding: A dispute that alleged electricity arrears are not due, where supply has been temporarily disconnected for those dues, is to be raised under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and a writ petition on that controversy is not to be entertained at that stage.

cases.title: Jamadar Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing objection to Executive Engineer
cases.holding: A writ challenging a billed demand is disposed of where clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 affords an adequate remedy before the Executive Engineer; the consumer may approach that authority, which shall take an appropriate decision in accordance with law.
cases.flag: Court called clause 6.5 an 'appeal'; 6.5 is the billing objection to the Executive Engineer.

cases.title: Virendra Kumar v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: A consumer who disputes only the amount indicated in a bill raised by the licensee must pursue an objection under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; a writ raising that dispute is disposed of by leaving the petitioner to that remedy.

cases.title: M/S S.R. Preservation Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P. and 3 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Ravendra Singh v. U.P.P.C.L.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-representation
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of a disputed electricity demand and restoration of supply may be disposed of by relegating the consumer to a representation under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. A timely representation must be considered and a fresh corrected bill issued; supply is to be restored on payment of that bill within the time allowed, or, if the consumer remains aggrieved by the correction, on compliance with the formalities for filing an appeal, subject to the appellate proceedings.

cases.title: Ashu Rathi v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing-objection-alternate-remedy
cases.holding: A second writ seeking quash of a demand notice and recovery citation and a mandamus to decide an objection under clause 6.5(d) was disposed of without examining the bill. If clause 6.5(d) was satisfied, the consumer must appeal the demand to the appellate authority; it is for him to approach the concerned authority. An earlier writ had already been dismissed directing him to avail the clause 6.5 remedy.
cases.flag: order recites clause 6.5(d) as pleaded; catalogued sub-clauses are 6.5(a), 6.5(b) and 6.5B, not 6.5(d)

cases.title: Smt. Chameli Devi v. State of U.P. and 3 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Sm. Neelima Tiwari v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: Clause 6.5 billing-objection conditions and deposit
cases.holding: Interference was refused because the recovery notice was challenged without attacking the main assessment or consumption bill. The consumer may dispute a bill only under Clause 6.5, and only after complying with that clause’s conditions, including deposit of the requisite money; unless those conditions are satisfied the objection is not competent. If a compliant objection is filed, the authority shall consider and decide it by a reasoned order, preferably within four weeks.

cases.title: Mitthu Lal v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: duty to decide clause 6.5 application; restoration pending decision
cases.holding: Once the Court has granted liberty to apply under clause 6.5, the Executive Engineer is obliged to decide that application; unexplained inaction, with disconnection and continued demand of arrears, is non-compliance and prima facie contemptuous. The writ was disposed of with liberty to make a fresh application within two weeks, a direction to decide it by a reasoned speaking order within four weeks, and a further direction that supply be restored forthwith if the petitioner deposited Rs.50,000 within two weeks.

cases.title: Virendra Kumar v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: time for decision on billing objection
cases.holding: Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 stipulates seven days for deciding a consumer's billing objection; where that objection remains pending, the writ is disposed of by directing the licensee (respondent no. 3) to decide it within a week of production of a certified copy, without restoring supply or adjudicating the bill.

cases.title: Shesh Mani v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: time-bound consideration of clause 6.5 application
cases.holding: Where the licensee stated that the consumer’s earlier clause 6.5 application was not available on its record, the writ was disposed of by granting liberty to file a fresh application under clause 6.5 within two weeks, with a direction that the competent authority shall consider and decide any such application within four weeks of its making.

cases.title: Ajay Kumar Jaiswal v. Uttar Pradesh Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-correction-application
cases.holding: Where the consumer disputes the correctness of an electricity bill, the remedy is an application for correction of the bill under Regulation 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The Executive Engineer must consider and decide that application by a reasoned speaking order within two weeks of production of a certified copy of the Court's order. If the consumer deposits 50% of the amount, the balance shall not be recovered till disposal of the application.

cases.title: Satish Chandra v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing dispute; alternative remedy
cases.holding: A consumer disputing the correctness of electricity bills and a demand notice has a statutory alternative remedy under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 by raising the dispute before the competent authority, and the High Court will not interfere under Article 226.

cases.title: Brijesh Kumar v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection
cases.holding: A writ challenging correction of an electricity bill on the ground that a different connection number has been written in the bill is not entertained on merits; the consumer has a remedy of applying under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and if that application is filed the concerned authority is to pass an appropriate order within six weeks of production of a certified copy of the Court's order.

cases.title: Smt. Shamim Fatima v. State of U.P. and 3 Ors.
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Surendra Pratap Singh v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.topic: billing-grievance-executive-engineer
cases.holding: A grievance against an electricity bill is to be resolved by the Executive Engineer (Distribution) under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Where the consumer has already represented, the writ court will not examine the bill on merits and will instead direct the Executive Engineer to look into and redress the grievance in accordance with law (here, within eight weeks).

cases.title: M/S Prayan Ispat & Steel Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: pending Clause 6.5 billing objections
cases.holding: Where objections to electricity bills have been filed under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 and remain undecided, the competent authority is to decide them expeditiously, preferably within four weeks of a certified copy of the order, in accordance with law; the Court does not adjudicate the merits of the billing claim.

cases.title: Vaidya Nath Vishwakarma v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: Where an earlier objection under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 has been decided and a revised bill issued, the consumer must first clear those arrears before a subsequent Clause 6.5 application on a later bill will be considered afresh.

cases.title: Sudhir Kumar v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill rectification — Clause 6.5 forum
cases.holding: A consumer who seeks rectification of an electricity bill must file an appropriate application before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the writ court will not itself rectify the bill.
