If such an application is made, the authority shall consider and dispose of it within four weeks of production of a certified copy of the order.

cases.title: Reena Devi v. Chairman, U.P. Power Corp. Ltd.
cases.topic: bill-correction
cases.holding: A consumer disputing billed arrears and pole disconnection is to apply under clause 6.5 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005 for correction of the bill; the Executive Engineer must consider the application after hearing and pass an order within one week of production of a certified copy of the High Court's order, and if there are no electricity arrears, supply is to be restored forthwith.

cases.title: M/S Mb Rubber Pvt. Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited & Another
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Smt. Shahida Begum v. State of U.P. and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: alternate-remedy
cases.holding: A second writ seeking similar electricity reliefs is not maintainable after an earlier petition for the same reliefs was dismissed as withdrawn. The consumer may still approach the concerned authority under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Om Prakash Puri v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-dispute-article-226
cases.holding: A factual dispute as to the correctness of an electricity bill cannot be adjudicated under Article 226. The Electricity Act, 2003 and the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 are self-contained; the consumer must pursue the statutory billing-objection remedy available under those enactments.

cases.title: Mahendra Kumar v. State of U.P. and 3 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Yogeshwar Singh v. State of U.P. and Another
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 2 weeks, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: Ram Sewak v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: The third respondent shall decide the petitioner's application dated 10 July 2016 as a dispute under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, as expeditiously as possible and preferably within four weeks of receipt of the order, subject to the petitioner complying with conditions and formalities mandated by law; the petitioner must produce a copy of the order before the competent authority within ten days; until those conditions are complied with and the application is decided, no coercive action shall be taken against the petitioner.

cases.title: Ajay Gupta v. M.D., Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitaran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: Where a consumer questions the correctness of an electricity bill and seeks disposal of a representation raising that objection, Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is a complete machinery for redressal; the writ court will not examine the merits and will leave the consumer to institute appropriate proceedings under Clause 6.5.

cases.title: Yogesh Kumar v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing-dispute-redressal
cases.holding: Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 lays down a complete machinery for redressal of grievances questioning the correctness of an electricity bill. A writ seeking disposal of a representation against such a bill is disposed of without examining merits, leaving the consumer to institute appropriate proceedings under Clause 6.5.

cases.title: M/s S.R. Preservation Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill correction under clause 6.5
cases.holding: Where a consumer already remitted to Clause 6.5 challenges a subsequent demand alleging non-adjustment of cash deposits, the writ court may dispose of the petition by directing the Executive Engineer to pass a reasoned speaking order on the pending application within a fixed time, intimating the amount payable or refundable, and may keep the demand in abeyance until that order.

cases.title: Bill challenge dismissed with liberty under clause 6.5 ESC
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-dispute-forum
cases.holding: Where a consumer is dissatisfied with the correctness of electricity bills, the remedy is under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; a writ will not be entertained when counsel cannot even show that an application under that clause is competent.

cases.title: M/s Sanjeevani Cold Storage v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: disputed bills; writ vs clause 6.5 remedy
cases.holding: If a consumer is not satisfied with the correctness of electricity bills, the remedy is under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; a writ is dismissed with liberty to pursue that remedy, including where an objection under clause 6.5 has already been filed.

cases.title: Rajendra Singh Yadav v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: installment payment after clause 6.5 bill correction
cases.holding: Once the electricity bill had been corrected under clause 6.5, the Court did not reopen that correction. On the consumer's willingness to pay Rs. 4,48,311, it directed a deposit of Rs. 2 lakh within four weeks and the balance in three equal installments (30 November 2016, 31 January 2017 and 31 March 2017), default entitling the licensee to recover the amount forthwith.

cases.title: M/S Vinay Foods and Another v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited and
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 2 months, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: Manish Gulati v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: pending representation treated as Clause 6.5 application
cases.holding: A consumer representation against alleged inflated bills, left undecided while disconnection is threatened, is to be treated by the Executive Engineer as an application under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 and decided by a reasoned speaking order; coercive disconnection remains in abeyance for six weeks or until that disposal, whichever is earlier.

cases.title: Vishwanath Sharma v. State of U.P. and 3 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Kumar Share Brokers Ltd. v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill rectification via Executive Engineer
cases.holding: Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is the forum for rectification of an electricity bill, including a dispute that the multiplying factor is incorrect. A pending application before the Executive Engineer is to be treated as a Clause 6.5 application, processed after hearing, and decided by an appropriate order within four weeks; the writ is not the forum for that merits inquiry.

cases.title: Kuldip Dubey v. U.P. Power Corporation — pending representation treated as Clause 6.5 bill-correction application
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-correction-application
cases.holding: Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 provides for correction of the electricity bill. A representation already pending before the Executive Engineer against unexplained arrears is to be treated as an application under Clause 6.5; the Executive Engineer must pass an appropriate order within two weeks after giving the consumer an opportunity of hearing. Recovery of the disputed September 2016 arrears remains in abeyance until that representation is disposed of.

cases.title: M/S Vinay Foods v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.topic: clause-6.5-statutory-alternative-remedy
cases.holding: Where a consumer disputes the accuracy of a demand notice or bill, Clause 6.5 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is a statutory alternative remedy, including a complaint required to be decided within seven days, and a writ petition seeking quashing of the demand will not be entertained.

cases.title: Mohd. Haleem Khan v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: pending bill-correction application
cases.holding: The petitioner’s application for correction of the electricity bill under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 being pending before the concerned authority, the writ petition is disposed of by directing the competent authority to decide that application by a speaking and reasoned order within four weeks, without examining the bill on merits.

cases.title: Pending bill-correction representation treated as Supply Code clause 6.5 application
cases.topic: bill-correction representation treated as clause 6.5 application
cases.holding: A pending representation for correction of an electricity bill is to be treated as an application under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and the Executive Engineer is directed to decide it by a reasoned and speaking order within six weeks of production of a certified copy of this order.

cases.title: Smt. Shashi Lata v. Superintending Engineer, P.V.V.N. Ltd.
cases.topic: billing-complaint
cases.holding: A pending representation for correction of an electricity bill is to be treated as an application under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and the Executive Engineer is to decide it within six weeks of production of a certified copy of the order.

cases.title: Kusum Mishra v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing objection to Executive Engineer
cases.holding: A representation seeking correction of an electricity bill is to be treated as an application under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and the Executive Engineer is to pass an appropriate order thereon within the time fixed by the Court.

cases.title: Ravindra Nath Pandey v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: disputed-bills
cases.holding: Correction of an electricity bill is required to be done under Section 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. A pending consumer objection to a bill is to be treated as an application under that provision and decided by the Executive Engineer by a reasoned and speaking order; the writ court will not itself correct the bill.

cases.title: Mona Singh v. State of U.P. — bill correction treated as Clause 6.5
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking electricity bill correction is disposed of by treating the consumer's application as one under Clause 6.5, with a direction to the Executive Engineer to decide it within ten days of production of a certified copy of the order.

cases.title: Smt. Sharda Tripathi v. U.P. Power Corporation Limited
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing complaints
cases.holding: An application moved by a consumer for correction of her electricity bill is to be treated as an application under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and the competent authority must decide it by a speaking and reasoned order.

cases.title: Krishna Agrawal v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: disputed bills — representation to Executive Engineer
cases.holding: Billing disputes, including alleged factually incorrect bills, are remediable under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, which provides for disputed bills and arrears. Treating the Executive Engineer as the competent authority, and noting that a representation was already pending, the Court declined to examine the bills on merits and disposed of the writ by directing the Executive Engineer, Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Khand, Naini/Jhusi, to decide that representation in accordance with law within two months.
cases.flag: Court also cited 'paragraph 7.4' of the Supply Code as making the Executive Engineer the competent authority to redress the billing grievance. Clause 6.5 is the disputed-bills provision; 7.4 is retained as stated and is not treated as 7.7.4.

cases.title: Ajay Gupta v. M.D., Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitaran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: pending bill-correction application — time-bound disposal
cases.holding: Where a consumer’s application under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 for correction of the bill remains pending, the High Court will not decide the billing dispute in writ jurisdiction and will dispose of the petition by directing the competent authority to decide that application by a speaking and reasoned order within a fixed time.

cases.title: Allauddin v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: dues dispute after disconnection
cases.holding: Whether electricity dues remain recoverable after disconnection is a factual dispute to be raised under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the writ court will not decide the claim on merits and will direct the competent authority to examine and decide any such dispute expeditiously in accordance with law.

cases.title: Ravi Upadhyay v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: A remaining dispute over connection bills after the representation-order is not to be decided on a writ; the consumer must invoke the remedy under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Namita Katara v. Managing Director, Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: pending representation against disputed bills
cases.holding: Where the consumer's sole grievance is that a Clause 6.5 representation against disputed bills remains undecided, the writ is disposed of by directing the Executive Engineer to decide that representation expeditiously, preferably within one month of a certified copy, without the Court adjudicating the merits.

cases.title: Dileep Kumar v. State of U.P. — pending clause 6.5 bill-correction application directed to be decided
cases.topic: pending billing-objection application
cases.holding: A writ seeking correction of an electricity bill is disposed of without a merits determination where a clause 6.5 application is already pending; the competent authority is directed to decide that application within a fixed time.

cases.title: Nagendra Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: alternative remedy against demand notice
cases.holding: A writ petition challenging a notice to deposit balance electricity dues will not be entertained when the consumer has a statutory alternative remedy under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Hetram v. U.P.P.C.L.
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: Consumers have an adequate remedy of raising objections under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 before the Executive Engineer; a writ petition will be disposed of with liberty to file an appropriate representation/objection before that authority, who shall decide it and pass appropriate orders within one month of submission together with a certified copy of the Court's order.

cases.title: Babu Ram v. M.D., Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitaran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: accuracy of bills — statutory forum
cases.holding: Where the Electricity Act, 2003 read with the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is a self-contained code and paragraph 6.5 provides a statutory remedial forum for settling disputes pertaining to accuracy of bills, a consumer cannot bypass that forum and approach the High Court directly. The writ petition is disposed of, leaving the petitioner free to get the dispute redressed under paragraph 6.5.

cases.title: M/S Radhey Ice Factory v. Dakshinanchal Vidhut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-correctness-alternate-remedy
cases.holding: A consumer not satisfied with the correctness of electricity bills must seek remedy under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; a writ to quash a recovery citation or to enforce a Permanent Lok Adalat award on bill quantum is not maintainable. Following Anis Ahmad, PLA proceedings in such matters are without jurisdiction.
cases.flag: Court referred to the 'Electricity Act, 2005'; the statute is the Electricity Act, 2003.

cases.title: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Anr. v. The Electricity Ombudsman & Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.date: 15 March 2023 (dismissed for want of prosecution; order-sheet 11.9.2012 to 15.3.2023; interim stay 17.2.2016)
cases.topic: Prima facie, the correctness of a supplementary consumption bill is challengeable only under clause 6.5, and the CGRF / Electricity Ombudsman lacks competence to decide bill-correctness (Anis Ahmad); the Lokpal's order stayed pending enquiry, but the point was left undecided on dismissal for want of prosecution
cases.holding: The Court took only a prima facie view and did not finally decide the question. It recorded the licensee's submission that the Supply Code, 2005 provides under clause 6.5 the mechanics for challenging the correctness of bills, that the consumer's proceedings before the CGRF questioning the supplementary bill were not maintainable, and that for the same reason the Electricity Lokpal had no competence to enter into the correctness of the bill, relying on U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. v. Anis Ahmad. Holding that 'the matter does require enquiry by this Court', the Bench stayed the Electricity Lokpal's order dated 23 June 2011 pending the next date. This was an interim, prima facie view: the writ was ultimately dismissed for want of prosecution on 15 March 2023 without the competence point being decided, and the interim order stood vacated.
cases.flag: Order-sheet of 11 pages, dated orders from 11.9.2012 to 15.3.2023, no printed page numbers; pins are order dates. The prima facie observation and stay are of the 17.2.2016 order (Arun Tandon and Harsh Kumar, JJ.); the operative disposal is the dismissal for want of prosecution of 15.3.2023 (Suneet Kumar and Rajendra Kumar-IV, JJ.). Here the petitioner is the licensee, the respondents the Ombudsman and the consumer.

cases.title: Yogesh Kumar Jain v. Krishna Pal Puri, Executive Engineer
cases.topic: Contempt disposal directing consideration of a billing objection
cases.holding: Where a compliance affidavit shows that the Executive Engineer has fixed a date to consider the applicant's billing objection, the contempt application is disposed of with a direction that the claim be considered under clause 6.5 within three weeks of the fixed date, on the applicant's undertaking to appear and place his material. No contempt is recorded and the merits of the objection are left to that statutory consideration.
cases.flag: The notice order dated 22 August 2017 refers to the applicant's claim as arising under 'Clause 6.25' of the Code, while the disposing order dated 11 October 2017 refers to 'para 6.5'. The operative direction is under clause 6.5.

cases.title: Farjand Ali v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking restoration of electricity supply, not pressed, is disposed of with liberty to pursue Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the appropriate authority shall consider and decide the consumer's application for interim order/restoration of connection on merits in accordance with law.

cases.title: Sanjay Kumar Sharma v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Competent Authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Girija Shankar v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: writ not entertained for electricity charge demand
cases.holding: A consumer disputing a demand of electricity charges must avail the remedy under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; a writ petition raising that dispute is not entertained.

cases.title: Smt. Ayesha v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing-dispute-alternative-remedy
cases.holding: A consumer’s writ petition disputing the amount charged in electricity bills is not to be entertained when Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 affords a statutory alternative remedy; the petition is dismissed.

cases.title: Sarad Kumar Gupta v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing dispute — alternative remedy
cases.holding: A writ petition disputing the amount charged by the distribution licensee in electricity bills will not be entertained when the consumer has the statutory alternative remedy under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Sanjay Bajaj v. U.P.P.C.L.
cases.topic: billing dispute — writ not entertainable; remedy under clause 6.5
cases.holding: Where the consumer disputes a bill raised by the distribution licensee, the High Court will not entertain a writ petition; the consumer must avail the remedy provided in clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Petition dismissed.

cases.title: Rajendra Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing dispute remedy
cases.holding: Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 may be invoked to settle a dispute about electricity bills. The writ petition challenging bills allegedly raised from 2014 though a new connection was given only in January 2017 was disposed of, leaving that Code remedy open, without deciding the bills on merits.

cases.title: Jaiveer Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing-dispute-forum
cases.holding: A challenge to bills raised on a 10 H.P. formula against a sanctioned 5 H.P. load is a disputed question of fact which the High Court will not decide in writ. Under the Electricity Act, 2003 read with the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, paragraph 6.5 is the remedial forum for settling a billing dispute. The writ is not entertained; the competent authority already seized of the representation on bills and arrears is directed to look into the grievance in accordance with law, preferably within two months of production of a certified copy.

cases.title: Shyam Lal and Another v. State of U.P. and 3 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 2 weeks, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: Devi Dayal v. State of U.P. and 2 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Mahendra Singh v. State of U.P. and 2 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 7 days, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: Ravindra Bhushan Singh v. Kanpur Electricity Supply Company
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing dispute
cases.holding: A consumer disputing the correctness of an electricity bill and recorded arrears has a remedy under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 before the appropriate authority. The writ was disposed of with liberty to approach that authority, who shall decide any such application in accordance with law within six weeks of the application.

cases.title: M/s Shiv Ganga Aata Mill v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: consideration of clause 6.5 billing objections
cases.holding: An order on a Clause 6.5 billing objection that does not consider the objections raised is unsustainable. The Court held that the 11 January 2016 rejection of the representation, requiring payment of Rs. 12,66,096 before restoration, considered none of the objections (including alleged unaccounted deposits and LMV-6 benefits). The Court referred to Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Act, 2005; the 2015 order had cited the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. That order was quashed as contrary to the 2 December 2015 direction, with a fresh decision in accordance with law within three weeks.
cases.flag: Court referred to Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Act, 2005; the quoted 2015 order correctly cites Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Salik Ram & Another v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 2 weeks, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: Jaya Kumari v. State of U.P. & Another
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 10 days, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: Ram Chandar v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-dispute-writ-not-maintainable
cases.holding: A writ petition whose dispute is about electricity bills is not to be entertained, because such a dispute can be resolved under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the petition is dismissed.

cases.title: Vrindavan & Another v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 2 weeks, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: Jeevan Sahara Hospital v. State of U.P. Thrul& Another
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Mahesh Kumar Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing objections as alternate remedy
cases.holding: A writ petition disputing a demand bill is not entertained when the consumer has a statutory remedy of filing objections under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the petition is dismissed with liberty to avail that remedy.

cases.title: Naushad Husain v. State of U.P. and 3 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 10 days, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: Smt. Sudha Malviya v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing dispute forum
cases.holding: A dispute over electricity bills and recovery of consumption charges, including a plea that no connection was ever given, is to be raised before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ was disposed of with a direction that if such an application is filed within ten days, the authority shall pass an appropriate order within six weeks, and no coercive recovery shall be taken till then.

cases.title: Abdul Kadir v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-statutory-remedy
cases.holding: Where a consumer aggrieved by an electricity bill seeks a writ directing decision of a representation but cannot point to the provision under which it was filed, the High Court will not issue that direction and will leave the consumer to the statutory remedy under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Ramashray Dubey v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.topic: billing-objection-statutory-remedy
cases.holding: Where a consumer challenges an electricity bill by a representation whose statutory basis is not shown, the High Court will not direct the licensee to decide that representation; the consumer is to avail the statutory remedy under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Smt. Manna Devi v. U.P. Electricity Regulatory Commission
cases.topic: billing-and-meter-grievance-relegation
cases.holding: A writ challenging electricity bills and alleging a defective meter after disconnection is disposed by leaving the consumer to Clauses 6.5 and 5.9 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; supply shall be restored if ₹25,000 is deposited within a week, the balance depending on orders in those proceedings.

cases.title: Ved Prakash Jaiswal v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. and 2 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Mulayam Singh v. U.P. Power Corporation, Lucknow
cases.topic: billing disputes
cases.holding: All billing disputes are to be decided by the Executive Engineer under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If the consumer is aggrieved, an appeal may be filed or the Consumer Grievances Redressal Forum approached under clause 7.10. Where the factum of consumption and billing is disputed, those remedies are to be availed. If the consumer does not dispute the quantum and proposes to deposit the amount, the Executive Engineer may be approached for instalments under clause 6.14.

cases.title: Satish Sharma v. State of U.P. — writ against 30.7.2017 notice withdrawn with liberty under clause 6.5
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: dispute-against-notice
cases.holding: A notice of the kind dated 30 July 2017 may be the subject of a dispute under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ challenging that notice was disposed of as withdrawn with liberty to raise such a dispute.

cases.title: Ramesh Nath Pandey v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: notice-dispute-forum
cases.holding: A notice issued by the distribution licensee of the kind dated 16.7.2017 may be challenged by raising a dispute under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the writ challenging that notice was withdrawn with liberty to pursue that remedy.

cases.title: Musharraf v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing dispute — Executive Engineer under clause 6.5
cases.holding: A billing dispute alleging incorrect calculation of electricity consumption charges is to be examined by the Executive Engineer under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ was disposed with liberty to approach the fourth respondent, who shall pass an appropriate order within three weeks of presentation of a certified copy; recovery remains in abeyance until that order.

cases.title: Mukta Prasad Mishra v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-error correction under Clause 6.5
cases.holding: If there is an error in an electricity bill issued by the Electricity Department, the consumer's remedy for correction of the bill is to move an application under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; a writ seeking that correction is dismissed with that observation.

cases.title: Chandrabhan Gupta v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-dispute-executive-engineer
cases.holding: A writ petition raising a billing dispute on electricity consumption charges is disposed of by relegating the consumer to the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The pending representation/application is to be decided within six weeks of receipt of a certified copy of the order. If the consumer is found liable to pay, easy instalments may be sought from the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.14.

cases.title: Mohar Singh v. State of U.P. and 3 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: M/S Laxmi Oil Mill Thru Proprietor v. State of U.P. and 4 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Arun Kumar Shilpkar v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-dispute-executive-engineer
cases.holding: A writ alleging that an electricity bill is an incorrect assessment of consumption is essentially a billing dispute for the Executive Engineer under clause 6.5. The petition was disposed with liberty to file a certified copy before the Engineer, who was directed to consider the grievance, any deposits, and any indication of incorrect billing, and to pass an appropriate order in accordance with law within three weeks; if the dispute is resolved and the consumer pays the settled dues, the Engineer may pass a consequential order on continuance of the connection.

cases.title: Ajay Kumar Vishwakarma v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing-dispute-executive-engineer
cases.holding: Where the consumer disputes electricity consumption after assessment and alleges inflated bills, the remedy is to approach the Executive Engineer under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the writ is disposed with liberty to file a certified copy before the third respondent, who shall then pass an appropriate order within two weeks.

cases.title: Jamal Abdul Qadir v. Chief Engineer, Vidyut Vitaran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-complaint
cases.holding: Without deciding the bill, the Court recorded the consumer's undertaking to deposit 50% of the demand dated 4.9.2017 (after credit for amounts already paid) within two weeks. A dispute raised under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 within two weeks of that deposit is to be considered and dealt with on merits in accordance with law expeditiously; if no such dispute is raised, the licensee may recover the entire amount. Upon the 50% deposit, the electricity connection is to be restored within three days.

cases.title: Mohan Lal Kesarwani v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: disputed electricity bills
cases.holding: On the petitioner’s offer to deposit 50% of the demand under electricity bills dated 31.8.2017, the Court directed that if that deposit is made and a dispute of those bills is raised under cl. 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 within two weeks thereafter, the licensee shall consider and deal with it on merits in accordance with law expeditiously; if no such dispute is raised, the respondents may recover the balance in accordance with law. The writ was disposed of on that footing without deciding the bills.

cases.title: Jainullah v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer
cases.holding: Where the consumer essentially raises a billing dispute over a demand, the remedy is to approach the Executive Engineer under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the writ court will not correct the bill.

cases.title: Arti Singh v. M.D., U.P. Power Corporation
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: relegation to competent authority
cases.holding: Where the prayer in a writ petition is of a nature that the licensee’s counsel undertakes that the grievance will be considered if the consumer applies under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, the High Court may dispose of the petition with liberty to make that application, directing the competent authority to decide it expeditiously, without examining the merits.

cases.title: Dinesh v. State of U.P. — enhanced demand relegated to clause 6.5
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-forum
cases.holding: A writ challenging recovery of an allegedly erroneous enhanced electricity demand is not to be examined on the High Court side; the consumer is to take recourse to clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The second respondent shall examine the claim on presentation of a certified copy of the order and pass an appropriate order within three weeks.

cases.title: Mewalal v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: Whether the petitioner applied for or took an electricity connection, and whether recovery of consumption charges can be fastened on him, is a disputed question of fact which cannot be decided in writ jurisdiction under Article 226. Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 itself prescribes the fact-finding modality: the petitioner may approach the area officer (respondent no. 2), who, on being apprised of the dispute with a certified copy of the order, shall pass an appropriate order in accordance with law within six weeks of presentation.

cases.title: Mohd. Daud v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.topic: Billing-correctness dispute must first go to the competent authority under Clause 6.5
cases.holding: No. The subject matter is the raising of the bill, which is a billing dispute to be raised in the first instance before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the Code. The writ is not entertained on the ground of alternative remedy; the petitioner may raise the dispute before the competent authority, who will redress it in accordance with law.

cases.title: Maan Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: bill-correctness-remedy
cases.holding: A consumer disputing the correctness of an electricity bill has a remedy under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The Court recorded that remedy but, as none appeared for the petitioners, listed the writ in the next cause list without relegating the petitioners or deciding the bill.

cases.title: Dinesh Kumar Vishwakarma v. M.D. (Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitaran Khand) Agra
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill correction — clause 6.5 remedy
cases.holding: A writ disputing electricity bills was disposed of without examining the bills, leaving it open to the consumer to invoke clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 for correction of those bills.

cases.title: Baij Nath Prasad v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing dispute — Clause 6.5 remedy
cases.holding: Where the petitioner disputes a bill issued by the Power Corporation, a writ petition is dismissed because a remedy exists under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The consumer remains free to avail that remedy, and if he does so a decision is expected at an early date.

cases.title: Shishir Kumar Singh v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: inflated bills — objection under Clause 6.5
cases.holding: Where the consumer claims that bills issued by the licensee are inflated, the objection is to be pursued under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ is disposed of, leaving that remedy open.
cases.flag: original order cited Clause 6.54; Civil Misc. Correction Application No. 393852 of 2017 (4.12.2017) substituted Clause 6.5

cases.title: Lalji Tiwari v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: bill correction and restoration pending Clause 6.5
cases.holding: The writ was disposed of with liberty to invoke Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 for rectification of the bill. If the petitioner deposits Rs. 25,000 within one week, the electricity connection shall be restored; payment of the balance shall depend on the bill as corrected in the Clause 6.5 proceedings.

cases.title: Smt. Renu v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-rectification-and-restoration
cases.holding: A consumer disconnected for unpaid bills, who alleged regular payment and a pending correction application, was given liberty to invoke Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 for rectification of the bill. Restoration was directed if Rs 50,000 was deposited within ten days; payment of the balance would depend on the bill as corrected in those Clause 6.5 proceedings.

cases.title: Devendra Singh v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing dispute — alternate remedy
cases.holding: Where the petitioner disputes an electricity bill issued by the licensee, the remedy is to invoke Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the writ petition is disposed of leaving that remedy open, without examining the bill on merits.

cases.title: M/S Kumar Engineering, Ghaziabad v. Executive Engineer, P.V.V.N.L. Muradnagar
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 10 days, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: M/s Nourishing Food (Pvt.) Limited v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing-objection-tariff-category
cases.holding: A dispute over whether a multiplex is to be billed under HV-1 or HV-2, including reliance on a State notification treating multiplex halls as industry, is to be raised under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ is disposed of with a direction that, if the petitioner invokes clause 6.5, the authority shall decide in accordance with law, preferably within three months of a certified copy being filed. Merits were not adjudicated; any deposit remains subject to that decision.

cases.title: Habeeb Shah v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: alternative remedy for disputed bill and arrears
cases.holding: Where the grievance is a disputed electricity bill and arrears underlying a tehsildar recovery citation, clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is an effective remedy; the High Court will not interfere in writ jurisdiction and the consumer may pursue that objection.

cases.title: Vinod Kumar v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: alternative remedy for disputed demand
cases.holding: A consumer who disputes the amount demanded in a notice to deposit has an alternative remedy under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and a writ petition challenging that notice is dismissed on that ground.

cases.title: Subhash Yadav v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing dispute — statutory objection under clause 6.5
cases.holding: A dispute about an electricity bill is to be raised by invoking Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the writ is disposed of leaving that remedy open to the petitioner.

cases.title: Dhirendra Singh v. State of U.P. — writ for bill correction declined for clause 6.5
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: writ-jurisdiction-bill-correction
cases.holding: A writ petition filed primarily for correction of an electricity bill will not be entertained where Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 furnishes a statutory remedy; the petition is dismissed on that ground.

cases.title: Vijay Kumar v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: bill-correction-alternative-remedy
cases.holding: A consumer who disputes the correctness of the amount indicated in an Executive Engineer’s electricity notice has a statutory alternative remedy under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 for correction of the bill, and a writ petition raising that dispute will not be entertained.

cases.title: Shashi Kant Srivastava v. State of U.P. (billing dispute; clause 6.5)
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-dispute-under-clause-6.5
cases.holding: Billing disputes under the Electricity Act, 2003 read with the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 are to be settled by the competent authority under Chapter 6.5 of the 2005 Code. Where the consumer has already approached that authority and the grievance remains pending, the writ court will not decide the bill on merits and will instead direct the competent authority to decide the matter in accordance with law on the available records, preferably within three months.
cases.flag: Court refers to 'Chapter 6.5' of the 2005 Code; the Supply Code numbers 6.5 as a clause, not a chapter. The Act is cited as the 'Indian Electricity Act, 2003'.

cases.title: Meenu Gupta v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing dispute; alternative remedy
cases.holding: A consumer who disputes recovery of electricity consumption charges, including where no statement of how the amount was determined has been given, has a remedy under paragraph 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Mashooq Ahmad v. State of U.P. and 3 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Sandeep Mishra v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-dispute-alternative-remedy
cases.holding: A writ petition disputing an electricity bill and challenging recovery proceedings will not be entertained where the consumer has the alternative remedy under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Satish Chandra Gaur v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-dispute-statutory-remedy
cases.holding: A consumer who disputes an electricity bill is to invoke the statutory remedy under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the writ is disposed of with liberty to do so.

cases.title: Gee Pee Cycle Balls Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: assessment-objections-consideration-and-stay
cases.holding: Where a consumer has already raised objections under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 and undertakes to complete the formalities mandated for hearing those objections, the assessing authority is to consider the objections and pass appropriate orders within four weeks of compliance; if the consumer so complies, no coercive action is to be taken until the objections are decided. The Court does not decide the objections on merits.

cases.title: Saktu Lal v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: alternative statutory remedy for bill dispute
cases.holding: Where a consumer is aggrieved by an electricity bill raised by the Power Corporation, clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 furnishes a statutory remedy, and the High Court will decline to entertain a writ petition assailing the bill.

cases.title: Triveni Prasad v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing dispute alternative remedy
cases.holding: Where the consumer disputes an electricity bill raised by the power corporation, clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is a statutory alternative remedy, and the High Court will decline to entertain a writ petition on that dispute.

cases.title: Yogesh Kumar Jain v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-dispute-forum
cases.holding: Where a writ petition in pith and substance raises the validity or adjustment of an electricity bill, the consumer must invoke Paragraph 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, rather than High Court writ jurisdiction. If a Paragraph 6.5 complaint is already pending, the concerned Executive Engineer is to take a final call on that application.

cases.title: Rakesh Kumar v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing dispute — writ not entertained
cases.holding: A consumer's dispute about electricity dues shown in bills issued by the licensee is to be raised under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the High Court will not entertain a writ petition on that dispute.

cases.title: M/S Satya Flour Mill v. Sanjeev Kumar Singh, Executive Engineer
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: assessment grievance; Clause 6.5 machinery
cases.holding: Where a revised bill is placed on record in contempt, a consumer aggrieved by that assessment must pursue Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, which furnishes adequate machinery for redressal; the contempt petition does not survive.

cases.title: Salik Ram v. Jhabbu Lal (Exe. Engineer South Division)
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: pre-deposit for Clause 6.5 billing representation
cases.holding: A representation under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, cannot be decided unless the consumer has made the pre-deposit contemplated by Clause 6.5 read with Clause 6.7, or has applied for waiver of that deposit. A contempt petition alleging non-decision of such a representation is not entertainable without evidence that this mandated procedure was followed.

cases.title: M/s Bansal Agro Farm v. Pradeep Kumar Agrawal
cases.topic: contempt after clause 6.5 decision
cases.holding: Where the writ court directed the consumer to raise a dispute under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 and the competent authority to decide it, and the Executive Engineer has thereafter passed an order deciding that claim, civil contempt will not continue merely because the consumer says the decision did not deal with all issues raised; the contempt stands disposed of, leaving the consumer free to challenge that decision in appropriate proceedings.

cases.title: Ramashrey v. Chandresh Upadhyay
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: contempt of direction to decide clause 6.5 objection
cases.holding: Where the parent writ had declined to quash the 29.8.2017 and 3.11.2017 orders and directed respondent no. 2 to decide the consumer's 13.2.2018 objection under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, the contempt court recorded a prima facie case of willful disobedience for non-decision, issued no notice, granted two months further time from receipt of a certified copy to comply, and disposed of the contempt application with liberty to re-approach if the objection remained undecided.

cases.title: Abdul Kalaam @ Lalla Miyan v. State of U P and 2 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Asha Singh v. State of U.P. and 4 Ors.
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 2 weeks, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: Bela Devi v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: clause-6.5-alternative-remedy
cases.holding: Where a consumer disputes electricity issued by the distribution licensee, Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is a statutory alternative remedy, and a writ petition on that dispute will not be entertained.

cases.title: Fixed charges remain payable during temporary disconnection
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: fixed-charges-during-temporary-disconnection
cases.holding: Unless supply has been permanently disconnected, the consumer must pay fixed charges even for a period of temporary disconnection; a contrary objection is not tenable. Residual billing disputes may be raised under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 within 15 days, during which no coercive action is to be taken, and the objection is to be decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: Paschimanchal Electricity Distribution Division E.D.D. Iind v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: pla-restoration-without-clause-6.5-deposit
cases.holding: The Court issued notice and stayed operation of the Permanent Lok Adalat's 24.1.2018 restoration order till the next date of listing, holding that the licensee's plea required consideration: under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 a claim petition was not maintainable without deposit of the billed amount, and restoration without ensuring that deposit was illegal.

cases.title: Kriti Scanning Center Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P. and 3 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 1 week, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: Sayeem Khan v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-dispute-relegation-to-6.5
cases.holding: Where consumers dispute the amounts raised in the licensee's electricity bills, the High Court may dispose of the writ by leaving it open to them to avail the remedy under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, without adjudicating the billed amounts.

cases.title: Ram Kumar v. State of U.P. and another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing dispute
cases.holding: A writ petitioner disputing the amount raised in bills of the Power Corporation may avail the remedy under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the petition is disposed of leaving that remedy open.

cases.title: Renu v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: particulars of bill raised after Clause 6.5 liberty
cases.holding: Where, after the consumer deposits the restoration amount fixed in an earlier order granting liberty to seek bill correction under Clause 6.5, the licensee raises a further bill without disclosing the basis of calculation, the writ may be disposed of by directing the respondents to furnish the consumer the details of the amount raised in that bill.

cases.title: Udayvir Singh v. State of U.P. — writ against Consumer Forum bill order dismissed
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill and arrears dispute — alternative remedy
cases.holding: Where a consumer disputes electricity bills and the arrears determined, Paragraph 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 itself prescribes a remedy. Together with the statutory appeal under the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 against a District Consumer Forum order, a writ petition questioning that Forum judgment is not the proper course; the petitioner remains at liberty to avail those remedies.

cases.title: Dhirendra Singh v. State of U.P. and Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: pending bill-correctness objection before Executive Engineer
cases.holding: Where a consumer has filed an application under Clause 6.5 of the Supply Code objecting to the correctness of a bill and that application remains undecided, the writ court may dispose of a mandamus petition by directing the Executive Engineer to decide the application in accordance with law by a reasoned and speaking order within a fixed time, without examining the bill on merits.

cases.title: Rajendra Prasad Verma v. State of U P and 3 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 2 weeks, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: Yogesh Sharma v. State of U.P. Through M.D., U.P.P.C.L. and Another
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 15 days, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: Soran Singh v. State of U.P. and another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: incorrect bill — alternative remedy
cases.holding: A writ petition seeking quashing of a notice alleging an incorrect electricity bill will not be entertained where the controversy involves disputed questions of fact; the consumer must take the statutory remedy under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. An application to the appropriate authority may be considered in accordance with law.

cases.title: Sarva Deo Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing-dispute
cases.holding: A writ to quash recovery of electricity dues on a provisional theft assessment will not be entertained where the petition does not show that the assessment has been made final as prescribed. The consumer may approach the Executive Engineer for an appropriate assessment order and, for a billing dispute, under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Recovery shall abide by the Engineer's order, to be passed within three weeks of presentation of a certified copy.

cases.title: Israr Husain v. State of U.P. — Clause 6.5 billing dispute; recovery to abide Executive Engineer
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing dispute — Executive Engineer competent; recovery to abide his order
cases.holding: A billing dispute under Clause 6.5 is to be resolved by the Executive Engineer as the competent authority; he must himself enquire into the correctness of the alleged wrong bill and not call upon the Sub Divisional Officer to examine it. An assessment dispute would lie under the Electricity Act. Recovery on the impugned citation shall be carried out only after the Executive Engineer passes an appropriate order following enquiry, and shall abide that order.

cases.title: Smt. Rajkumari v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing dispute; recovery of arrears
cases.holding: A challenge to recovery of alleged electricity arrears, including a claim of no consumption after a pole-shifting application, is a billing dispute. The Executive Engineer under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is the competent authority to decide such a dispute even if it arises out of any assessment. The writ court declined to interfere and relegated the petitioner to that forum, directing that recovery proceedings abide the Engineer's decision. A civil court order on shifting of double poles does not decide consumption.

cases.title: Jai Prakash v. U.P. Power Corporation Limited, Lucknow and 3 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 2 weeks, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: Suman Gupta v. Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.topic: billing-dispute-writ-barred-clause-6.5
cases.holding: A dispute as to the amount of electricity dues or the bill is a fact-intensive matter requiring evidence and cannot be tried in extraordinary writ jurisdiction. Recourse lies under paragraph 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The petition is dismissed on that alternative remedy.

cases.title: Mohd. Jameel v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing dispute — application to licensee
cases.holding: A writ challenging a recovery citation for electricity dues, being essentially a billing dispute, is to be pursued by an application to the licensee under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The Court disposed of the petition with a direction that such an application, if filed within 10 days with a certified copy of the order, be considered and decided within six weeks, and that the recovery citation not be enforced until then.

cases.title: Phool Chand v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing dispute — Clause 6.5 statutory remedy
cases.holding: Where a consumer’s writ concerns a pending electricity bill and the dispute involves questions of fact, the High Court will not entertain the petition because Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 affords a statutory remedy; the petitioner may approach the appropriate authority, whose application is to be considered in accordance with law.

cases.title: Smt. Asma Begam v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.topic: Reopening/review of a decided Clause 6.5 order — interim stay
cases.holding: The Court held the question requires consideration and, as interim relief, stayed proceedings under the reopening notice of 23.11.2012 pending admission, on condition the petitioner keeps depositing future electricity charges. No final view was expressed on whether the authority has power to review its Clause 6.5 order.
cases.flag: Interim order only — the issue (power to review a Clause 6.5 order) is left for final hearing.

cases.title: Kisan Inter College, Gurgawan v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing dispute — alternate remedy
cases.holding: A dispute that an electricity bill is incorrect is to be raised under Paragraph 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; a writ petition will not be entertained when that statutory alternate remedy is available.

cases.title: Vijay Kumar Agrawal v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing-dispute
cases.holding: The writ petition, seeking correction of disputed electricity bills, was not pressed. Liberty was granted to the petitioner to make a complaint under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The Court recorded that it had not examined the merits.

cases.title: Banshi Wale v. State of U P and 3 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Mithilesh Kumar Tiwari v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing-dispute
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of a recovery citation for consumption charges alleged to have been levied during disconnection is disposed by relegating the consumer to the Executive Engineer, who shall treat the certified copy as a billing dispute and decide it under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 within three weeks of presentation; recovery proceedings shall abide the Executive Engineer's order.

cases.title: Ram Bhajan Singh v. State of U.P. and 2 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Sandeep Saxena v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: disputed-bill-representation
cases.holding: On the licensee's pointing to clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, the High Court declined to examine the consumer's claim for bill correction, restoration and restraint against recovery, and disposed of the writ by directing a representation to the Executive Engineer, EUDD-III, Patel Nagar, Ghaziabad within three weeks, to be decided in accordance with law preferably within three months, without any opinion on merits.

cases.title: Prahlad Singh v. Dashchianchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing objection to recovery citation
cases.holding: A consumer who challenges a recovery citation on the ground that the billed load is incorrect has a remedy of representation/objection before the Executive Engineer under paragraph 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ court will not decide that billing dispute on merits; if the objection is filed within a week with a certified copy of the order, the Executive Engineer shall consider it and pass an appropriate order within one month, and coercive recovery is stayed for one month or until that decision, whichever is earlier.

cases.title: Bablu @ Ramakant v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-correctness-statutory-remedy
cases.holding: A writ raising only the correctness of an electricity bill, being a disputed question of fact, will not be entertained; the consumer is left to Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and any application to the appropriate authority is to be considered in accordance with law.

cases.title: Aniruddha Kumar Pandey v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: bill correctness — statutory remedy
cases.holding: Where the consumer disputes correctness of the bill, the High Court will not entertain a writ in view of the statutory remedy under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The petitioner was left to approach the appropriate authority within 10 days; that authority was to decide by a speaking order within 7 days, with recovery stayed for 20 days or until decision, whichever earlier.

cases.title: Tuni v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-correctness-statutory-remedy
cases.holding: A dispute as to the correctness of an electricity bill is to be pursued under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the High Court will not entertain a writ while that statutory remedy is available. If the consumer approaches the appropriate authority within the time fixed, the authority is to decide the application by a speaking order, and supply is not to be disconnected pending that disposal provided the application is filed in time.

cases.title: Ram Autar Singh v. U.P. Power Corporation
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-correctness-statutory-remedy
cases.holding: A writ petition raising a dispute as to the correctness of an electricity bill is not to be entertained when Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 provides a statutory remedy. The consumer may approach the appropriate authority, whose application is to be considered and decided expeditiously in accordance with law.

cases.title: Stay of Permanent Lok Adalat refund of electricity-arrears deposits; Clause 6.5 noted
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: recourse-against-assessment-or-recovery
cases.holding: Where a consumer obtained a Permanent Lok Adalat award for refund of amounts deposited pursuant to recovery of electricity-bill arrears, the High Court, observing that Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 was the available recourse against assessment or recovery, issued notice on the licensee's jurisdictional challenge and stayed the award pending consideration.

cases.title: Ikbal Hussain v. Managing Director, Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitaran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-correctness-statutory-remedy
cases.holding: A writ petition challenging the correctness of an electricity bill is not entertained when Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 furnishes a statutory remedy. The consumer may apply to the appropriate authority under that clause; the authority is to consider and decide the application in accordance with law by a speaking order after opportunity of hearing. Coercive action was stayed for forty days to enable that recourse.

cases.title: Riyasat v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: bill correctness — alternate remedy
cases.holding: A writ raising a dispute as to correctness of an electricity bill is not to be entertained where a statutory remedy is available under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The consumer may approach the appropriate authority under that clause; if he does so within one week, the application shall be considered and decided expeditiously in accordance with law.

cases.title: M/S Maa Narheji Agro Industries v. State of U.P. and Another
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 7 days, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: Raja Ram Sharma v. State of U.P. and 3 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 7 days, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: Murtuja v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: pending bill-correction application before Executive Engineer
cases.holding: Where a consumer's application for correction of an electricity bill is pending before the Executive Engineer, the writ may be disposed of by directing that officer to decide the application under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 within a fixed time, without adjudicating the bill on merits.

cases.title: Gomti Devi v. State of U.P. (Secretary, Vidyut)
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: Where a consumer's representation for correction of bills issued after alleged transformer failure and non-supply, and for replacement of the transformer, remains pending, the writ is disposed of by treating that representation as an application under clause 6.5 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and directing the Executive Engineer to enquire, visit the spot personally, and pass an appropriate order within four weeks of production of a certified copy.

cases.title: Satya Prakash Sharma v. Dakshinanchal Viddyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.topic: billing objection to Executive Engineer
cases.holding: Where electricity dues forming the subject of a recovery certificate are disputed, including on the footing that the connection is not in the petitioner's name, the writ court will relegate the petitioner to the Executive Engineer under paragraph 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, directing that if so approached the claim be considered and decided in accordance with law within a specified time, and may stay coercive recovery for that period.

cases.title: Devendra Arya v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: not pressed; liberty to approach licensee under 6.5
cases.holding: Where the petitioner did not press the writ and sought liberty to approach the second respondent under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, the Court disposed of the petition as not pressed, with that liberty, without deciding the claim on merits.

cases.title: Smt.Saroj Devi v. State of U.P. and 2 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 10 days, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law. For 1 month the respondent officers shall not disconnect.

cases.title: Chetendra Singh v. State of U.P. and Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing objection to Executive Engineer
cases.holding: A dispute as to electricity dues is to be raised before the Executive Engineer under Paragraph 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ is disposed of with a direction that if the consumer files such an application within a week, the Executive Engineer shall consider and decide it in accordance with law, as far as possible within one month of presentation of a certified copy of the order.

cases.title: Arvind Kumar v. State of U.P. and 06 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 1 month, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law. For 1 month the respondent officers shall not disconnect.

cases.title: Jogendra Singh v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-correctness
cases.holding: A writ raising a dispute as to the correctness of an electricity bill is not to be entertained where the consumer has a statutory remedy under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the consumer may approach the appropriate authority under that clause.

cases.title: Vindeshwari Parsad v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing objection before Executive Engineer
cases.holding: Under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 a consumer may object to the bill before the Executive Engineer. The writ was disposed of with the direction that if the petitioner files a fresh objection with a certified copy of the order, the Executive Engineer shall consider and decide it in accordance with law within one month; coercive action on the recovery citation dated 8.8.2018 shall remain stayed for that period.

cases.title: Tikaram v. State of U.P. and 3 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 2 months, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law. For 2 months the respondent officers shall not disconnect.

cases.title: Umesh Nath Pandey v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: writ not pressed — liberty to clause 6.5
