cases.holding: The writ petition against the distribution licensee was disposed of as not pressed, with liberty to the petitioner to take a remedy under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The Court did not adjudicate the underlying consumer grievance.

cases.title: Harish v. State of U.P. and 2 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 2 weeks, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: Pancham Singh v. Chairman, U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: A consumer disputing a recovery/demand notice must first represent under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 before the Executive Engineer; the High Court will dispose the writ with a time-bound direction to consider and decide that representation in accordance with law, staying coercive action on the notice meanwhile.

cases.title: Srikant Yadav v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer
cases.holding: A consumer who alleges that an electricity bill is incorrect and excessive has a remedy under Paragraph 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 by complaint to the Executive Engineer, to be considered in accordance with law. The writ was disposed of with liberty to raise that dispute within two weeks, and any such application is to be considered most expeditiously within six weeks of filing.

cases.title: Bashu Gupta v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing objection before Executive Engineer
cases.holding: Where a consumer challenges recovery of a bill and the Executive Engineer has already decided the matter without giving an opportunity of hearing or receiving an objection under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, the writ court will not quash the recovery challans on merits. The consumer has liberty to file a clause 6.5 objection before the Executive Engineer, who shall decide it within the time fixed; coercive action on the impugned challans is stayed until that decision.

cases.title: Ashok Kumar v. Uttar Pradesh Power Shakti Bhawan
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: incorrect-bill-alternative-remedy
cases.holding: If an electricity bill issued to a consumer is incorrect, including where two bills are said to have been issued for the same period, the consumer may raise the grievance under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 before the Executive Engineer; the High Court will not intervene in writ jurisdiction in view of that alternative remedy.

cases.title: Smt. Santosh Kumari v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing objection to Executive Engineer
cases.holding: A consumer aggrieved by an electricity demand, including one raised after disconnection of supply, has a remedy of filing an objection before the Executive Engineer under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the writ petition is dismissed with liberty to approach the Executive Engineer.

cases.title: Mool Chand @ Mantri v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: Where recovery of electricity charges is sought, the consumer's remedy is to file an objection before the Executive Engineer under paragraph 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; a writ to quash the recovery certificate will not be entertained if that officer has not even been approached, though liberty remains to file the statutory objection.

cases.title: Ramesh Nath Pandey v. State of U.P. and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing objection to Executive Engineer against recovery/disconnection notice
cases.holding: A consumer disputing a recovery-cum-disconnection notice for alleged bill arrears may file an objection before the Executive Engineer under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ was disposed of directing that if objections to the 27.09.2018 notice were filed before the Executive Engineer, KESCO, Kanpur Nagar, within a week, that officer shall consider and decide them in accordance with law within one month after hearing, and that no coercive steps shall be taken on the demand notice until that decision.

cases.title: M/s Subhash Stone Product v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing dispute — objection to Executive Engineer
cases.holding: A consumer who disputes an electricity bill being recovered as arrears must file an objection before the concerned Executive Engineer under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; a writ seeking quashing of the recovery is dismissed with liberty to pursue that remedy.

cases.title: Ram Pat Ram v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer
cases.holding: A consumer challenging a provisional assessment electricity bill and demand notice, even where theft of electricity is alleged and an FIR has been lodged, has an alternative remedy of filing an objection before the Executive Engineer under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ is dismissed; if the objection is filed within one week with a certified copy of the order, the Executive Engineer shall consider and decide it in accordance with law within a further one month.

cases.title: Brij Bilash Gupta v. State of U P and 2 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 1 month, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: Mukesh Singh Chaturvedi v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.topic: A Clause 6.5 objection must be in proper form to require decision
cases.holding: No. An objection that does not mention the details of any amount deposited or set out a specific objection to the bill does not conform to Clause 6.5 and cannot be treated as a Clause 6.5 objection; the authority cannot be blamed for not deciding it. As the consumer then agreed to pay in instalments without disputing the bill, the Court disposed of the petition with instalment directions.

cases.title: Deepa Erasmus v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing objection to Executive Engineer
cases.holding: A consumer complaining of inflated bills and undecided surcharge objections is relegated to a fresh representation before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code; the Engineer shall consider the claim, including late-payment surcharge, and pass orders in accordance with law as far as possible within one month of presentation of a certified copy.

cases.title: Gopal Krishna Chaturvedi v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: A consumer who disputes an electricity bill sought to be recovered as arrears has a remedy by filing objection before the Executive Engineer under paragraph 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the writ court will not quash the recovery citation on merits and will dispose of the petition leaving that forum open, with a time-bound decision in accordance with law and a stay of coercive action until the objection is decided.

cases.title: Ramdayal v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: bill-correctness-statutory-remedy
cases.holding: A writ seeking to quash an electricity recovery citation, where the consumer disputes correctness of the bill, is not entertained because Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 furnishes a statutory remedy. If the consumer approaches the appropriate authority within 15 days, the application may be considered and decided by speaking order within 15 days. Recovery remains stayed for 30 days or until the authority decides, whichever is earlier.

cases.title: Sarojini v. State of U.P. Through D.M.
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 15 days, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: Ram Lautan v. Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation and 3 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Lala Ram v. State of U.P. and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-correctness dispute; statutory remedy
cases.holding: A writ seeking waiver of an allegedly inflated bill, reconnection and a PD certificate is not entertained where the consumer disputes bill correctness; the statutory remedy is Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. An application filed within 10 days is to be decided by a speaking order after hearing, within 30 days; coercive action is stayed for 40 days or until that decision, whichever is earlier.

cases.title: Sri Krishna Chikitsalaya v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-correctness statutory remedy
cases.holding: A writ seeking mandamus to the Executive Engineer to rectify an electricity bill, including surcharge, is not entertained where the consumer has the statutory remedy under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The consumer may approach the appropriate authority under that clause; if the application is made within ten days, the authority is to consider and decide it in accordance with law by a speaking order after hearing, within thirty days of receiving a certified copy of the order.

cases.title: Rajesh Kumar Agarawal v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: A writ petition raising a dispute as to the correctness of an electricity bill is not entertained where Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 affords a statutory remedy; the consumer may approach the Executive Engineer, and the application is to be considered and decided by a speaking order after hearing, in accordance with law.

cases.title: Gayatri Devi v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: bill-correctness dispute — statutory objection to Executive Engineer
cases.holding: A writ petition raising a dispute as to the correctness of an electricity bill will not be entertained where the consumer has the statutory remedy of approaching the Executive Engineer under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; if the consumer so applies, the authority is to consider and decide the application in accordance with law by a speaking order after hearing.

cases.title: Farjand Ali v. State of U.P. and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection
cases.holding: Even if the authority gave no receiving of a Clause 6.5 application, the consumer ought to have sent it by registered post. The writ against KESCO's recovery notice dated 17.09.2018 is disposed of without examining the demand: the petitioner shall appear before the Executive Engineer, KESCO Urban Distribution Division, Kanpur Nagar on 11.01.2019 with a certified copy of this order and his representation, which the Executive Engineer shall consider and decide in accordance with law within 15 days.

cases.title: Kunwar Sain v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: disputed bills — alternative remedy
cases.holding: A consumer who disputes the accuracy of an electricity bill has an efficacious alternative remedy under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 (payment under protest of the amount claimed or six-month average, whichever is less, and complaint to the competent authority). The High Court will not entertain a writ under Article 226 until that remedy is invoked; the petition is disposed of with liberty to apply under clause 6.5, the authority to decide in accordance with law expeditiously.

cases.title: M/s Padam Atta Chakki v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing dispute — alternate remedy before Executive Engineer
cases.holding: Where the consumer seeks a writ restraining recovery of a disputed electricity bill and arrears, and clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 furnishes a remedy before the Executive Engineer, the writ is dismissed with liberty to pursue that statutory objection.

cases.title: Sheetal Singh v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: disputed bill — alternative remedy before Executive Engineer
cases.holding: Where a writ seeks quashing of a demand notice for electricity arrears and the dispute is a disputed bill, the petition is not maintainable; the consumer must approach the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Om Prakash v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: disputed-bills
cases.holding: A writ seeking quash of a recovery citation for electricity dues, where the consumer asserts the amount has already been deposited, is a disputed-bill controversy. The consumer has a remedy under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ court will direct the Executive Engineer/Prescribed Authority to consider and decide a representation within 15 days; recovery under the citation remains in abeyance until that decision, but the interim protection automatically vacates if the representation is not submitted in time.

cases.title: Sudhir Baboo v. State of U.P. and Another
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 2 weeks, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: M/S Baleshwer Floor Mill Industries v. State of U.P. and 2 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 2 weeks, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: Mohd. Rafi v. State of U.P. Through Secretary Home, Govt of U.P. At
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Ram Bihari and 5 Others v. State of U.P. and 2 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 10 days, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: Ram Padarath Gupta v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & 4 Others
cases.topic: Rate-category/billing objection to be decided by the Executive Engineer before recovery
cases.holding: No, not before the objections are decided. The matter (a domestic 2KW connection allegedly billed at commercial rates) must be examined by the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 read with s.126, and an order passed on the objections within three weeks; the recovery proceedings are subject to the outcome of that order.

cases.title: Awadhesh Kumar Yadav v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.topic: Disputed factual billing dispute belongs to the Clause 6.5 / Consumer Forum remedy
cases.holding: No. Whether the consumer continued to receive supply after the transformer was shifted (department's case) or ceased to (consumer's case) is a disputed question of fact unfit for Article 226. The consumer has an alternative remedy under Clause 6.5 before the Executive Engineer, and was already before the District Consumer Forum; he was relegated to those remedies.

cases.title: Smt. Shanti Devi v. Managing Director, Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran & Anr.
cases.topic: No free consumption; disconnection for non-payment inevitable, dispute to be resolved under the Code
cases.holding: No. A consumer who has consumed electricity cannot use it without clearing the bills; on non-payment disconnection is inevitable, and the plea that no bill was raised gives no right to free consumption. The Court did not interfere, relegating the consumer to the billing-dispute remedy under the Act and the Code.

cases.title: M/s Shree Radhey Ice Factory v. State of U.P. & 4 Others
cases.topic: Billing objections must be raised before, and decided by, the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A billing grievance must be raised under Clause 6.5 before the Executive Engineer; approaching the Permanent Lok Adalat or the Managing Director is misconceived. Where the consumer's objections had not received the attention of the competent authority owing to his wrong approach, the Court directed the Executive Engineer to consider the objections and pass an appropriate reasoned order in accordance with law under Clause 6.5 within three weeks.

cases.title: Shashi Bhushan Singh v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.topic: Dispute over a current/revised bill pursued by representation before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5
cases.holding: Relegate to Clause 6.5. A consumer disputing the current bill has the remedy of a representation before the concerned Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5. The Court disposed of the writ directing a deposit of Rs. 4,00,000 within 30 days, liberty thereafter to file a Clause 6.5 representation to be decided within one month, and restoration of the disconnected supply on the deposit (backed by an indemnity bond for any balance found due on revision).

cases.title: Buddhesh Patel v. State of U.P. and Another
cases.topic: Dispute over a direct-connection/theft recovery pursued by objection before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5
cases.holding: Relegate to Clause 6.5. As the petitioner was disputing the recovery proceeding, he is at liberty to move an objection before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5; if filed within a week the authority should pass an appropriate order within a further three weeks, and no coercive action is to be taken meanwhile.

cases.title: Mohammad Khalid v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Another
cases.topic: Billing grievance decided by representation under Clause 6.5 within seven days; deposit under protest
cases.holding: The remedy is a representation before the competent authority under Clause 6.5, to be decided within seven days, with a deposit under protest under Clause 6.5(b). The disconnection here was attributable solely to the consumer, who took more than a month and a half to approach the authority despite an earlier order (8.5.2014). The Court directed the competent authority to decide the pending representation within seven days of service, the under-protest deposit to be adjusted per that decision.

cases.title: Chandrapal v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & 4 Others
cases.topic: Fresh recovery while a Clause 6.5 representation lies undecided is arbitrary
cases.holding: No. The consumer was pursuing his Clause 6.5 remedy under an earlier order (28.4.2010) and filed a representation on 17.5.2010 which the Corporation never decided; issuing a fresh demand and a Section 3 recovery notice in that situation is arbitrary. The Court directed the competent authority to decide the representation within one month and kept the Section 3 demand in abeyance, to abide that decision.

cases.title: Smt. Jama Begum v. Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & 2 Others
cases.topic: Bill dispute to be raised under Clause 6.5 — as held in the underlying writ, recited on a contempt application
cases.holding: No. The writ order of 14.07.2025 in Writ-C No. 14446 of 2025 itself recorded Clause 6.5 as the provision for dispute on bills and directed the petitioner to raise the dispute as per the prescribed procedure, disposing of the writ with that observation. That is not a direction to the licensee whose breach founds civil contempt. The contempt application was dismissed as misconceived.
cases.flag: This Court only recites and characterises the earlier writ order; it does not independently construe Clause 6.5. Indexed here because the writ holding it recites is a Clause 6.5 relegation (the underlying writ is not itself in the corpus).

cases.title: Devendra Nath Dubey v. Executive Engineer, Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.topic: Bill-dues dispute relegated to a time-bound Clause 6.5 representation before the Executive Engineer — contempt dismissed once that representation was decided
cases.holding: No. The writ order of 06.11.2024 itself treated Clause 6.5 as the effective statutory remedy, granted liberty to file a representation within 15 days to be decided on merits by the Executive Engineer preferably within one month, and stayed coercive recovery for two months (auto-vacating if the representation was not filed in time). A compliance affidavit of 01.09.2025 showed the claim had been decided on 24.07.2025. The writ order having been complied with, the contempt application was infructuous and was dismissed; the notice was discharged.
cases.flag: This Court recites the earlier writ's Clause 6.5 relegation and decides only that it has been complied with. Indexed under 6.5 because that is the provision the writ order applied (the underlying writ is not itself in the corpus). No independent construction of the clause.

cases.title: Krishna Kant Dubey v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.topic: Prepaid-meter arrears after regular payment of consumption bills — Clause 6.5 relegation not applied; licensee to explain the arrears by affidavit, else interim interference
cases.holding: The Court did not relegate to Clause 6.5 and did not decide maintainability. It queried how accumulated arrears can arise on supply made through a prepaid meter; licensee's counsel was unable to satisfy the Court. The supply company is to file an affidavit explaining that query, to be accepted on the adjourned date upon advance copy served. On omission there will be interim interference. Listed 10 April 2026 as fresh.
cases.flag: Interlocutory only — listed 10.4.2026. Clause 6.5 was invoked by the licensee as the consumer bill-dispute channel (SCJ-013, SCJ-046, SCJ-083); this order does not apply it. Companion: SCJ-283 (same pattern: demand after bills paid; licensee to demonstrate the authorizing provision).

cases.title: Mohd. Ibrahim Khan v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: Billing objection — alternative remedy before Executive Engineer
cases.holding: A writ seeking correction of a disputed electricity bill under Clause 6.5, and restoration of supply disconnected for non-payment of that bill, is disposed of where the licensee raises, and the consumer does not dispute, the alternative remedy under Clause 6.5. The consumer may file a fresh representation before the Executive Engineer within one month; the Engineer shall decide it strictly in accordance with law within one month of receipt.

cases.title: Ashok Yadav v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: Billing objection — alternative remedy; representation directed to Junior Engineer
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of disputed electricity bills is disposed of without examining merits where the licensee invokes Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 as the forum for disputing bill correctness. The consumer may file a fresh representation under Clause 6.5, raising all grievances, before the Junior Engineer within one month; the Engineer shall consider and decide it in accordance with law within one month of receipt.
cases.flag: The Court directed the Clause 6.5 representation to respondent no.4, Junior Engineer, PVVNL, Ghazipur. The ordinary 6.5 channel (catalog: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5) is the Executive Engineer. The order does not explain why the Junior Engineer is the deciding authority. Not silently corrected.

cases.title: Manoj Kumar Sinha v. State of U.P. and 2 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5; ten-day stay on disconnection
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an exaggerated electricity bill and a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5. If he applies under that clause after completing the formalities within ten days, the application shall be considered and decided in accordance with law. For ten days the respondent officers of the electricity department shall not disconnect.
cases.flag: The order cites 'Clause 6.5 of the UP Electricity Supply Code, 2006'. The Code in force is the 2005 Code. Recorded, not silently corrected. The deciding authority under 6.5 is not named.

cases.title: Mohan Lal v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: Recovery of unpaid bills — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ challenging recovery of unpaid electricity bills is disposed of without examining the bills. The consumer may apply to the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 with relevant documents; the grievance is to be considered in accordance with law expeditiously.
cases.flag: The Court records that the dispute arises out of Section 135, yet points the consumer to Clause 6.5. Recorded, not silently corrected.

cases.title: Smt. Vidyavati Devi v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: Provisional assessment — objections to be decided under Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ that seeks certiorari to quash a provisional assessment bill and mandamus to decide written objections under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is finally disposed of without examining the bill. The assessing officer is directed to decide those objections in accordance with law expeditiously, if there is no legal impediment.

cases.title: Mohd Hameed v. State of Uttar Pradesh
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: After restoration of supply, a consumer who alleges incorrect billing and several disconnections followed by restoration is to raise a comprehensive dispute under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The Court does not examine the bills. The writ is disposed of.

cases.title: Nazirun Nisha v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5 before permanent disconnection
cases.holding: A writ seeking a mandamus to consider an application for permanent disconnection, where the consumer disputes outstanding bills and arrears, is disposed of by directing the consumer to file objections under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 before the third respondent within four weeks. If she does so, those objections are to be considered and disposed of within two months. The department is to take a pragmatic view where the petitioner is a widow, issue a fresh bill after meeting the objections, and allow deposit in four equal instalments. The Court does not decide the bills or order disconnection.

cases.title: Anju Devi v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection
cases.holding: A writ petitioner seeking correction of an allegedly excessive electricity bill is to raise objections under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 (here, within two weeks). If objections are raised, the departmental team may visit the premises; the consumer shall provide full access for taking the meter reading and inspecting the meter. After the meter is checked, the concerned officer shall consider and decide the objections (here, within a further one month).

cases.title: Jogendra v. State of Uttar Pradesh
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: alternative remedy under Clause 6.5
cases.holding: Where an alternative statutory remedy under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is raised, the writ is dismissed with liberty to approach the Executive Engineer under that clause; any such application shall be decided in accordance with law within four weeks of production of a certified copy, and the High Court does not adjudicate the petition on merits.

cases.title: Jamadul Hasan v. State of U.P. and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-clause-6.5
cases.holding: A consumer challenging a demand to the extent of late payment surcharge is to lodge a complaint under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The Court did not quash the demand in writ. It directed the petitioner to lodge that complaint by 29 August 2026, enclosing a certified copy of the order; on it being made, the supply company through the appropriate authority shall deal with it and inform the result of consideration within three weeks.

cases.title: Nitin Kumar Nishad v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing dispute — apply under clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking a direction to the supply company to raise a correct bill is disposed of without merits examination; the consumer must apply under clause 6.5 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and may enclose a certified copy of the order with that application.

cases.title: Kallu Urf Genderpal v. State of U.P. and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: alternative statutory remedy before Executive Engineer
cases.holding: A writ petition challenging an electricity-department notice is dismissed where Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 provides an alternative statutory remedy. The petitioner may approach the Executive Engineer under that clause; any such application shall be decided in accordance with law within four weeks of filing along with a certified copy of the order.

cases.title: Mangal Dev Prasad Arya v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: alternative-remedy-clause-6.5
cases.holding: A writ petition challenging an electricity-department notice is not entertained where an alternative statutory remedy lies under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The petition is dismissed with liberty to approach the Executive Engineer; if the application is filed within one week, the authority shall grant a hearing and pass an order in accordance with law within two weeks of filing.

cases.title: Mohammad Jafar Ali Khan v. Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection
cases.holding: A consumer disputing a demand notice must raise the bill dispute by objection under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ is disposed of with a direction to file the objection within two weeks; if filed, the authority shall consider and dispose of it within two months. The demand shall not be pressed until that disposal or for three months, whichever is earlier.

cases.title: Mohammad Jafar Ali Khan v. Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing objection
cases.holding: Where a consumer questions a demand notice as a bill dispute, the writ court will not decide the legality of the demand on merits and will relegate the consumer to file an objection under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, with a time-bound direction for disposal and an interim stay of the demand until the objection is decided or a specified period expires, whichever is earlier.

cases.title: Executive Engineer, Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Riyasat Ali and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: Disputed bill — Clause 6.5 remedy not exhausted before the Permanent Lok Adalat
cases.holding: The Court did not finally decide whether Clause 6.5 bars or conditions Permanent Lok Adalat jurisdiction. It recorded that the claimant had disputed the genuineness of the bill, against which he had a remedy under Clause 6.5 which was not resorted to before approaching the Permanent Lok Adalat, and treated that as a further reason the writ requires consideration.
cases.flag: Interlocutory. Not a relegation or disposal. The Court cited Clause 6.5 only, not 6.5(b) or 6.5B.

cases.title: Lalita Kumari v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad (Lucknow Bench)
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: The competent authority to consider a consumer's challenge to an electricity bill and consequent disconnection is the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The petitioner was directed to apply to that officer (opposite party no. 2), who shall verify the facts and take a reasoned decision within three weeks of presentation of a certified copy of the order; consequences follow as per law. The writ was disposed of without a merits determination.

cases.title: M/s Abacus India Agencies Pvt. Ltd. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: A writ against the licensee may be disposed of as withdrawn with liberty to the petitioner to file an application under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the Court does not then decide the supply dispute on merits.

cases.title: Ram Chandar @ Ram Chandar Pasi v. Executive Engineer, Electricity Supply Division 4th, Pratapgarh
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: clause-6.5-application
cases.holding: Without examining the 2015 demand on merits, and noting the consumer forum's earlier liberty and the dispute over receipt of a Clause 6.5 application, the Court disposed of the writ by granting two weeks to apply under Clause 6.5 of the Code of 2005 and directing the authority to hear the consumer and pass a reasoned order within eight weeks of filing.

cases.title: Shri Sai Industries v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad (Lucknow Bench)
cases.topic: clause-6.5-application
cases.holding: A writ petitioner in a Supply Code dispute may be directed to make a fresh application under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 within a week; if made, the authorities must grant a hearing and pass a reasoned order in accordance with law within eight weeks, and no coercive measure is to be taken until that order.

cases.title: Anuj Singh v. Managing Director, U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad (Lucknow Bench)
cases.topic: billing dispute — objection under Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking correction of an electricity bill and decision of a billing representation is a billing dispute. The petitioner is to apply under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; if such application is made within a week, the concerned authority shall hear and decide it expeditiously.

cases.title: Laxmi Narayan Mishra v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: A consumer's billing dispute over electricity consumption is to be raised before the Executive Engineer under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ is disposed of with liberty to make a fresh representation, which the Executive Engineer shall consider and decide in accordance with law within six weeks.

cases.title: Suresh Singh v. State of Uttar Pradesh
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing objection
cases.holding: A consumer who approaches the High Court to quash a current electricity bill is directed to file an application under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; if that application is filed within two weeks, the authority shall grant a hearing and pass a reasoned order in accordance with law within eight weeks.

cases.title: Sahdeo Singh v. State of Uttar Pradesh and 4 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 2 weeks, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: Vijay Kumar Pandey v. State of U.P. and 2 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 2 weeks, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: Shiv Mohan v. State of U.P. and others
cases.topic: alternative remedy for billing dispute
cases.holding: Where the consumer disputes the correctness of a theft-related electricity bill and seeks assessment and restoration by writ, Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is an effective alternative remedy. The writ is disposed of with liberty to apply under Clause 6.5; if the application is filed within two weeks, the respondent authority shall consider and dispose of it within six weeks of filing.

cases.title: Smt. Laxmi Chaurasiya v. Dakshinanchal Electricity Distribution Corporation Ltd. and 4 Others
cases.topic: billing dispute — relegation to Clause 6.5; time-bound statement of liability, objection, and reasoned order
cases.holding: The writ court will not enter the factual dispute. The consumer is relegated to Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 for resolution of the billing dispute. The petitioner may approach the concerned authority with a copy of the order; the authority shall furnish details of the petitioner’s liability within one week; the petitioner may submit an objection within two weeks; the authority shall pass a reasoned order within six weeks thereafter. The writ petition is disposed of.
cases.flag: Source PDF also contains orders of 2.4.2018 (interim restoration on deposit of Rs 5,000), 10.5.2018 (dismissed for non-prosecution), 13.7.2018, 16.7.2018 (restored), 1.4.2024, 8.4.2024, 19.4.2024, 2.7.2024 and 30.8.2024; the operative disposal is 1.7.2025 (Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Jayant Banerji JJ.). The 2.4.2018 order described the arrears as those of the ‘erstwhile tenant’; the 1.7.2025 order treats them as the landlord’s default at the same premises. Clause 6.5 is cited without sub-clause.

cases.title: Smt. Ranjana Devi v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing objection under clause 6.5
cases.holding: Where a consumer writ is brought against the licensee, the Court may dispose of it by directing the petitioner to file an application/objection under Clause 6.5 of the Supply Code; if filed within two weeks, the concerned authority shall decide it within six weeks after granting a hearing.

cases.title: Suresh Prajapati v. State of U.P. And 3 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing objection
cases.holding: The writ petition was disposed of with a direction that the petitioner file an application/objection under Clause 6.5 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If such application/objection is filed within two weeks, the concerned authority shall decide it within six weeks of filing, after granting the petitioner an opportunity of hearing. The Court did not grant or refuse relief on the merits of the electricity dispute.

cases.title: Suman Tara v. State of U.P. and 2 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 2 weeks, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: M/S P.S.S. Taxcon Sadikpur v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection
cases.holding: Where disconnection of supply is challenged and a representation remains undecided, the authority dealing with Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is directed to treat that representation as one under Clause 6.5 and to pass a reasoned order in accordance with law after hearing the consumer, within four weeks; the writ is disposed of without deciding the merits of disconnection or restoration.

cases.title: Alakh Prakash Sharma v. State of U.P. and 2 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 2 weeks, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: Rajendra Prasad Memorial Trust v. State of U.P. and 3 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 2 weeks, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: Smt. Jama Begum v. State of U.P. And 4 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-dispute-procedure
cases.holding: Where a consumer disputes an electricity bill, the dispute must be raised in accordance with the prescribed procedure under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the writ court will not direct issuance of a corrected bill when that mechanism is in place.

cases.title: Jyoti Prakash Dubey v. State of Up and 3 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Nisa Parveen v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing objection under Clause 6.5
cases.holding: The authority is directed to decide the petitioner's electricity-bill objection, treating it as an application under Clause 6.5 of the Supply Code, 2005, within twelve weeks by a reasoned order after granting an opportunity of hearing. The writ is disposed of without examining the merits of the bill.

cases.title: Ramchandra v. State of U.P. and 4 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 2 weeks, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: Kanak Srivastava v. State of U.P. and others
cases.topic: hearing before Clause 6.5 order
cases.holding: An order under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, passed without affording the consumer opportunity of hearing is liable to be quashed; the consumer shall appear before the Executive Engineer on a fixed date and a fresh order shall be passed after hearing and considering the material produced.

cases.title: Sudhanshu Dhar Tripathi v. State of Uttar Pradesh
cases.topic: writ interference with reasoned Clause 6.5 order
cases.holding: Where the order under challenge is a reasoned order passed under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 and an alternative remedy is available, the writ court should not interfere.

cases.title: Swabhiman Breweries Private Limited v. Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Limited
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: disconnection pending Clause 6.5 application
cases.holding: Disconnection of a consumer's electricity supply while an application under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 remains pending is arbitrary. The authorities must reconnect immediately, preferably within three days; decide the pending Clause 6.5 application within two months after granting the consumer a hearing; and take no coercive measures until that application is decided.

cases.title: Ratan Prakash v. State of Uttar Pradesh
cases.topic: incorrect-bill-grievance
cases.holding: Grievance redressal for an incorrect electricity bill is provided in clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Where the petitioner has not disclosed the allegedly incorrect bill, the High Court is not called upon to interfere in writ jurisdiction.

cases.title: Ghangas Breeding Farm And Hatchery v. State of Uttar Pradesh
cases.topic: Clause 6.5 billing objection — time-bound adjudication
cases.holding: An unadjudicated application under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 must be decided by the relevant authority within one month of production of a certified copy of the order. Coercive action against the consumer is stayed for six weeks or until that decision, whichever is earlier.

cases.title: Om Narayan Tripathi v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-correction complaint
cases.holding: On a writ seeking a direction to decide a clause 6.5 complaint for electricity-bill correction, and on the licensee's statement that the application will be duly dealt with, the Court disposes of the petition directing respondent no. 2 to decide the application within four weeks. The bill is not adjudicated on merits.

cases.title: Phool Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing-objection
cases.holding: A consumer challenging an electricity bill and recovery certificate in writ should file the challenge under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If that application is made within two weeks, the authorities shall grant a hearing and thereafter pass a reasoned order in accordance with law within six weeks of filing.

cases.title: Usha Agnihotri v. State of Uttar Pradesh and Another
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Babu Khan v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing-objection-under-6.5
cases.holding: A representation already made against an alleged inflated bill, after disconnection for non-payment, is to be dealt with under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The consumer is to communicate a certified copy of the order and the representation to the licensee; the result of consideration is to be made known within three weeks of that communication. The writ is disposed of without directing restoration.

cases.title: Ritesh Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: restoration and installment application
cases.holding: The writ for installment payment of dues and restoration of supply was not decided on merits. The petitioner was directed to file an application under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; if filed within two weeks, the authority was to grant a hearing and pass a reasoned order in accordance with law within eight weeks. A later order, describing the same provision as “Section 6.5”, extended the filing time by two further weeks and barred any further extension.
cases.flag: The 16.5.2025 extension order refers to “Section 6.5” of the Supply Code; the 7.3.2025 disposal correctly calls it “Clause 6.5”.

cases.title: M/S Ishita Cold Storage And Ice P Ltd v. State of Uttar Pradesh
cases.topic: billing objection
cases.holding: Where, after the writ was filed, the licensee withdrew the earlier order and issued a show-cause notice on the arrears dispute, the Court disposed of the petition without deciding the billing merits and directed the Executive Engineer to conclude the proceeding on that notice preferably within two months.

cases.title: Abdul Jabbar v. State of Uttar Pradesh and 2 Others
cases.topic: Lok Adalat award vs Clause 6.5
cases.holding: Where a Lok Adalat has already directed correction of electricity bills, the licensee's submission that the consumer must raise a Clause 6.5 dispute does not prevail. Section 22-A of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 includes supply of power as a public utility service. The Court directed the supply company to comply forthwith with the 11 December 2024 award and to make the result known within two weeks of communication of this order.

cases.title: Dharmveer Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: grievance-redressal
cases.holding: Where a consumer disputes a tehsildar recovery citation and seeks correction of the recorded status of a connection alleged to have been permanently disconnected, the Court, without deciding the merits, directed him to apply under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the Electricity Department to decide that application within a month; and stayed recovery for two months or until the application is decided, whichever is earlier.

cases.title: M/S Subodh Gautam Aarya Rice Mile v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection
cases.holding: A consumer disputing a recovery citation and seeking bill rectification may be relegated to Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005: if an objection to the bill is filed within ten days, the Electricity Department shall decide it within one month, and no recovery shall be made for two months.

cases.title: Punit Kumar Srivastava v. State of U.P. And 4 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: restoration-on-deposit-and-clause-6.5-objection
cases.holding: If the petitioner deposits Rs.75,000 with the Electricity Department within seven days, the Department shall reconnect supply forthwith. The petitioner shall file an application/objection under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 within seven days; if so filed, the authority shall decide it in accordance with law within six weeks after hearing. After the Clause 6.5 order the petitioner shall deposit dues as determined (the Rs.75,000 to be adjusted); on default the Department may proceed in accordance with law.

cases.title: Kanak Srivastava v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: application under clause 6.5
cases.holding: A consumer who has approached the High Court in a writ should file an application under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; if that application is made within two weeks, the authorities shall grant a hearing and thereafter pass an order in accordance with law within eight weeks of filing.

cases.title: Vimala Singh v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd and Another
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Sudhanshu Dhar Tripathi v. State of U.P. and 4 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Niyaz Ahmad v. State of U.P. and 2 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 1 month, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: Zubair Ahmad v. State of U.P. and Another
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 10 days, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: Gupreet Singh v. State of U.P. And 2 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection
cases.holding: Where a recovery certificate for unpaid electricity bills is challenged in writ, the consumer may approach the relevant authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; if that application is made within ten days, it shall be decided within two months, and no coercive action shall be taken for three months or till the application is decided, whichever is earlier.

cases.title: Dharam Pal Sharma v. State of U.P. and others
cases.topic: forum for restoration and outstanding dues
cases.holding: A grievance regarding disconnection of an earlier electricity connection, restoration of supply, and outstanding dues on the previous connection is to be examined by the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The petitioner was permitted to approach respondent no. 3 under Clause 6.5 within two weeks; that authority shall pass a reasoned speaking order in accordance with law within six weeks.

cases.title: Pinki Singh v. State of U.P. And 3 Others
cases.topic: billing objection after disconnection
cases.holding: A consumer aggrieved by demand and assessment orders on which the connection has been disconnected may be relegated to raise an objection before the competent authority under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, with supporting material; the authority is to examine the claim and pass a reasoned order, and the plea of restoration of connection is also to be considered.

cases.title: Ram Narayan v. Managing Director, Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-dispute
cases.holding: A consumer who seeks a court-directed decision on an electricity-bill dispute and reconnection must raise all grievances by application under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; if that application is filed within two weeks, the concerned authority shall grant a hearing and pass a reasoned order in accordance with law within six weeks.

cases.title: Asma Begum v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: pending 6.5 objection
cases.holding: Where an objection under Rule 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 has not been decided, the writ court will dispose of the petition by directing the authority concerned to decide that objection expeditiously, preferably within six weeks.

cases.title: Smt. Rajesh Saini v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing objection to Executive Engineer
cases.holding: Where the connection and consumer name have been restored during the writ and only a disputed bill remains, the consumer is to prefer an objection under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 before the Executive Engineer, who shall decide it after notice and hearing; recovery of the disputed amount stays until that decision, while current bills must continue to be paid.

cases.title: Shree Badri Kedar Papers Private Limited v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: An order of the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 that is devoid of reasons and shows no application of mind is liable to be quashed. The billing objection is remitted to the Executive Engineer to decide afresh in accordance with Clause 6.5, after affording a full hearing, within two months of a certified copy.

cases.title: Dharampal v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing objection — address, load factor, quantification
cases.holding: Objections that a consumption bill records a wrong address or load factor, or wrongly quantifies dues, require determination of facts and are to be raised before the competent authority under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ court will not decide those issues on merits.

cases.title: Lalit Kumar v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-under-6.5
cases.holding: Factual issues in a billing dispute over electricity dues will not be entertained in writ at first instance. The consumer may approach the competent forum by filing a proper claim under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; if such a claim is raised, the forum shall decide it expeditiously in accordance with law.

cases.title: Arif Ali Khan v. State of U.P. And 2 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: A writ petitioner seeking a direction against coercive action on an Executive Engineer's order is to file an objection under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; if filed within one week, the Executive Engineer shall grant a hearing and pass a reasoned order in accordance with law within four weeks.

cases.title: Ram Kumar Gupta v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: A grievance regarding load factor on an electricity connection and consequential billing can more appropriately be examined by the concerned authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The petitioner was permitted to approach the third respondent, who shall consider and examine that grievance and do the needful within four weeks. The writ petition was disposed of without a merits determination.

cases.title: Imamun Nisha v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing objection treated as Clause 6.5 representation
cases.holding: An objection to a demand notice already moved before the Electricity Department is to be treated as a representation under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and decided within ten days; no coercive action is to be taken until the representation is decided or that period expires, whichever is earlier.

cases.title: Sharmila Begum v. Purvanchal Vidhut Vitrana Nigam Ltd. & Anr.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing objection under clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ challenging recovery of unpaid electrical dues need not be examined on merits where the dispute can more appropriately be raised before the competent authority under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The consumer was permitted to approach the second respondent under that clause within a week; the authority was directed to pass a reasoned order within six weeks, and coercive action was stayed until disposal of the application.

cases.title: Manoj v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: objection under clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ petition raising an electricity grievance may be disposed of by directing the petitioner to file an application/objection under Rule 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; if filed within two weeks, the concerned authority shall decide it after granting an opportunity of hearing, completing the exercise within two months.

cases.title: Parvati Devi v. Purvanchal Vidhut Vitrana Nigam, Varanasi
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: pending billing objection
cases.holding: A writ seeking a single bill from inception on the meter's final reading, while a Clause 6.5 objection to disconnection and arrears remains pending, is disposed without examining merits; the consumer may submit a fresh representation to the Executive Engineer, who shall consider and decide it strictly in accordance with law after notice and opportunity of hearing.

cases.title: Deep Chandra v. State of U.P. and Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill correction under clause 6.5
cases.holding: A consumer aggrieved by a wrong electricity bill may get the bill corrected under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ court may dispose of the petition by directing the consumer to apply before the concerned authority within ten days and directing that authority to decide the application in accordance with law within one month, while staying recovery under the impugned notice for two months.

cases.title: Ekta Malviya v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing objection pending before authority
cases.holding: Where a consumer's claim against a bill is already pending before the concerned authority, the writ court will not decide the bill on merits and will dispose of the petition by directing that authority to determine the claim in accordance with Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, within a stipulated period.

cases.title: Rambali v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing objection to Executive Engineer
cases.holding: A consumer disputing a demand notice as erroneously raised on a long-disconnected connection must first approach the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5; the High Court will not decide the billing objection on writ and will instead direct time-bound consideration of a representation.

cases.title: Ritu Verma v. State of U.P. And 4 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection
cases.holding: A consumer disputing a demand notice is to approach the authority under Clause 6.5 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is filed within two weeks, the authority shall consider and decide it in accordance with law within six weeks of filing, after hearing the consumer. The connection shall not be disconnected until that decision.

cases.title: Mahendra Singh v. State of U.P. and 2 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Rishikesh Madi Tripathi v. State of U.P. and Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing objection under clause 6.5
cases.holding: The writ is disposed of by directing the petitioner to file an application/objection under Clause 6.5 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005; if filed within two weeks, the authority concerned shall decide it within six weeks of filing after granting the petitioner an opportunity of hearing.

cases.title: Mustari Begam v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: pending 6.5 objection — direction to decide; stay of disconnection
cases.holding: Where an objection under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 has not been decided, the authority is directed to decide it expeditiously, preferably within six weeks, and the consumer's electricity connection is not to be disconnected until that objection is decided.

cases.title: Smt. Usha Shukla v. State of U.P. And 3 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: pending 6.5 objection — time-bound decision; disconnection stayed
cases.holding: Where the petitioner's objection under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 has not been decided, the authority concerned is directed to decide that objection expeditiously, preferably within six weeks; until the 6.5 objection is decided, the petitioner's electricity connection shall not be disconnected. The writ petition is disposed of on those directions.

cases.title: Wali Mohd. @ Wali Ahmad v. Managing Director, Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection
cases.holding: A consumer who disputes an electricity bill is to approach the authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ was disposed of with a direction that if the petitioner approaches that authority within one week, the grievance shall be looked into within one month, and no coercive action shall be taken on the demand notice dated 9 October 2024 for two months.

cases.title: Balram v. State of U.P. And 3 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: A writ petitioner may be directed to file an application/objection under Clause 6.5 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005; if filed within two weeks, the concerned authority shall decide it within six weeks of filing after granting an opportunity of hearing. The writ is disposed of without a merits grant or refusal.

cases.title: Shahabuddin v. State of U.P. and Another
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the executive engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Imami v. the Managing Director, Paschimanchal Vidyut
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 10 days, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: Rashid v. State of U.P. and 4 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 2 weeks, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: Smt. Najma Bano v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: A grievance of incorrect imposition of bill and disconnection is more appropriately examined by the third respondent under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If the consumer approaches that authority with a certified copy of the order, the claim is to be examined and appropriate orders passed within four weeks, and the claim for restoration of electricity is to be considered within a week of the representation. The writ is disposed of on those directions without a merits determination.
cases.flag: Clause 6.5 cited for both the billing objection and disconnection/restoration; the order does not specify a sub-clause.

cases.title: Rahul Trivedi v. State of U.P. and others
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: Without going into merits, the Court directed Respondent No. 3 (Executive Engineer, PuVVNL, Fatehpur) to decide the petitioner's representation dated 21.07.2022 within one month of presentation of a certified copy of the order, the Electricity Department having undertaken to treat it as a representation under Clause 6.5 of the Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Sandeep Kumar v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-objection
cases.holding: A writ seeking decision of a bill objection and restoration of supply is disposed of by directing the petitioner to approach the concerned authority under Clause 6.5 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005; if an application is filed within two weeks, the authority shall consider and decide it in accordance with law within six weeks after giving the petitioner a hearing.

cases.title: Lakhiya v. State of Uttar Pradesh
cases.topic: bill-reduction-on-permanent-disconnection
cases.holding: On the licensee's statement that payment of the amount due for permanent disconnection would be followed by consideration, permanent disconnection and bill reduction under clause 6.5, the Court directed the petitioner to pay that amount within four weeks and disposed of the writ without a merits grant or refusal.

cases.title: Sujeet Singh Chauban v. and 3 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 2 weeks, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: Petitioner v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer
cases.holding: Where the connection has already been restored after the writ was filed, a remaining billing dispute is to be raised before the Executive Engineer under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, by an application in the prescribed format after paying the prescribed fees; the writ is disposed of with liberty to that statutory remedy.

cases.title: Sandeep Kumar @ Sandeep Gupta v. State of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Energy Deptt.
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 1 month, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: Smt. Durgawati Pandey v. State of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Energy Lko and 2
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Brijesh Singh v. State of Uttar Pradesh
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
cases.topic: billing-dispute-forum
cases.holding: A challenge to a revised electricity bill is a billing dispute referable to para 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Unless that remedy has already been availed, in which case the consumer is to go to the concerned Consumer Forum, a maintainable application under para 6.5 shall be considered and decided expeditiously. The writ court will not decide the bill on merits.

cases.title: Musheer Khan v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
cases.topic: billing-objection
cases.holding: The remedy for a disputed electricity bill lies in clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Where the consumer has already approached the Executive Engineer, that authority is to look into the matter and do the needful as per that provision and the law, with expedition (here, within three weeks of receipt of a certified copy). A pending application for permanent disconnection is to be considered in the same period by the competent authority. The writ is disposed of on that direction; the bill is not quashed and connection is not ordered.

cases.title: Neelu Srivastava v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.topic: billing-objection-alternate-remedy
cases.holding: Where the consumer remains aggrieved by a rectified electricity bill, disputed questions of fact cannot be adjudicated under Article 226; the remedy lies before the Executive Engineer under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, or before the concerned consumer forum or other prescribed authority.

cases.title: Kadir Ahmad @ Dr. Q.A. Khan v. Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: A writ petitioner aggrieved by a demand notice has a remedy under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and may be directed to approach the designated officer, who shall decide the demand as per law; a connected grievance regarding an electricity connection may likewise be considered and decided by that officer within two weeks of an application with a certified copy of the order.

cases.title: Amit Yadav v. State of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Energy U.P. Lko. And 6 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
cases.topic: billing dispute before Executive Engineer
cases.holding: A dispute as to electricity bills is to be raised before the concerned Executive Engineer under Para 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The petitioner may approach that officer. The writ petition is disposed of without deciding the bills on merits.

cases.title: M/s Om Sai Ram Rice Mill v. Chairman, Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.topic: billing dispute (clause 6.5)
cases.holding: A writ court will not examine a billing dispute. The consumer may avail the statutory remedy under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; any application filed or pending before the Executive Engineer shall be considered and decided as per law within six weeks. Once the billing dispute is resolved, the consumer may approach the authorities for off-season benefit in terms of the impugned order.

cases.title: Mithilesh Kumari v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing objection — Executive Engineer remedy
cases.holding: The remedy for a grievance against electricity bills, if at all, is before the Executive Engineer under paragraph 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The petitioner was directed to avail that remedy and the writ was disposed of without a merits decision on the bills.

cases.title: Shakuntala v. Managing Director Madhyanchal Vidyut Veteran
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Saleem v. State of U.P. Thru. the Prin. Secy. Energy Civil
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Ram Sufal v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection
cases.holding: A consumer's pending application for correction of an electricity bill is to be decided by the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the High Court does not itself correct the bill in writ jurisdiction and instead directs that officer to decide the application within a fixed time.

cases.title: Shiv Kumar Dubey v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
cases.topic: billing dispute
cases.holding: Where the petitioner raises a billing dispute, he is to approach opposite party no. 2, who shall get the facts verified in terms of para 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 and do the needful within one month; the writ is disposed of without deciding the bill.

cases.title: Abhishek Chand Kaushik v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: Chapter 6 bill-correction is a Code mechanism; a junior employee not shown authorised to correct bills — PC Act bail
cases.holding: Yes, at the bail stage and without comments on the merits. Chapter 6 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is a detailed mechanism for correction of bills; the AGA could not show the applicant was authorised to correct the bill. Combined with a load enhancement from 5 kW to 13 kW (beyond the applicant's competence upto 9 kW), the Court held that no demand of alleged bribery could have been raised, that Neeraj Datta was squarely attracted, and that prima facie no offence under sections 7, 13(1)(B) and 13(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 was made out. Charge-sheet already filed; clean antecedents; incarceration since 30.04.2024; no circumstance shown necessitating custodial arrest. Bail allowed on conditions.
