cases.flag: The Court cited 'Chapter 6' without a clause number; keyed to clause 6.5 as the Code's bill-correction complaint procedure. Source PDF also contains a 10.06.2024 listing order of Samit Gopal J. (AGA given two weeks for instructions; listed 16.07.2024); the operative bail grant is 16.07.2024 (2024:AHC:113876). The charge-sheet is recorded as submitted on 26.04.2024 though the trap is 30.04.2024 and the FIR 01.05.2024 — recorded as the order states it. Counsel's citation 'Neeraj Datta' 2022 Online SC 1724 is the Constitution Bench in Neeraj Dutta. Bail is not an adjudication of the bill or of guilt.

cases.title: Avinash Kumar Gautam v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: Chapter 6 bill-correction mechanism — contractual bill-feeder not shown authorised to correct a bill
cases.holding: Yes, at the bail stage and without comments on the merits. The applicant, a contractual computer operator in Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitaran Nigam, was named in Case Crime No. 05 of 2024 under sections 7, 13(1)(B) and 13(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, over alleged demand and recovery of Rs. 5,000 to correct a residential electricity bill. Counsel said he could not independently correct a bill without an order of the authority under the Code. The Court held that Chapter 6 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 provides a detailed mechanism for correction of bills; the AGA could not point out that the applicant was authorised to correct the bill. Applying Neeraj Datta, there was prima facie no legal basis for the alleged demand, so no PC Act offence was made out at this stage. Bail was allowed on a personal bond and two sureties, with standard conditions.
cases.flag: The Court cited 'Chapter 6' for bill correction, not a clause number. Keyed to Clause 6.5 (the Code's billing-complaint / bill-correction channel used in this corpus); not Clause 6.7 (late-payment surcharge). Source PDF also contains the 05.07.2024 listing order (neutral citation 2024:AHC:115345) connecting this matter with Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 22586 of 2024; the operative grant is 16.07.2024. Para 9 recites co-accused load-enhancement facts (5 kW to 13 kW; competence up to 9 kW) copied from the reproduced Kaushik order, and a chemical test 'against' the applicant, while para 5 records counsel as saying the test was 'in the negative' — recorded as the order states it.

cases.title: Vijay Shukla v. Shri Shadab Ahmad, Executive Engineer, Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. and Another
cases.topic: A Clause 6.5 relegation is not disobeyed where the consumer never filed a 6.5 objection and instead sought OTS
cases.holding: No. The 10.08.2022 writ in Writ-C No. 22798 of 2022 gave liberty to submit an objection under para 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, to be decided in accordance with law if filed in time. The applicant never filed any such objection. His 05.09.2022 application only sought One Time Settlement; the Executive Engineer on 21.10.2022 and again on 20.12.2023 (after the 27.04.2023 first-contempt order granting three more months) told him OTS is availed by applying on UP.ENERGY.IN. He did not so apply. His conduct was held questionable. The second contempt application was dismissed as misconceived and devoid of merits.
cases.flag: Contempt dismissed as misconceived. The Court recites the earlier writ's para 6.5 relegation and finds no 6.5 objection was ever filed; it does not parse sub-clauses 6.5(a)/(b)/6.5B. An OTS request is treated as not a para 6.5 billing objection. Source PDF also contains listing orders of 08.01.2024 and 23.01.2024 (Vikas Budhwar J.) and 27.02.2024 (Dinesh Pathak J., time to file compliance affidavit); the judgment under record is 05.03.2024 (2024:AHC:39563).

cases.title: Nagesh Pati Tripathi v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing objection as alternate remedy
cases.holding: Where the consumer disputes the quantum of bills and has not invoked Clause 6.5 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005, the writ court relegates him to that remedy. The petitioner may file proceedings under Clause 6.5 within two weeks; the respondents must pass an appropriate order in accordance with law within three weeks thereafter after hearing him. Until those proceedings are decided, the recovery demand shall not be enforced.

cases.title: M/s Hotel Pride Inn v. Purvanchal Vidhut Vitrana Nigam Ltd. and Another
cases.topic: M.R.I. readings to enable Clause 6.5 billing objections; writ will not quash a reiterating demand
cases.holding: No. A prior writ (Writ-C No. 16127 of 2023) had already disposed of a challenge to adding Rs. 2,02,581 to the regular bill, with liberty to file objections under Clause 6.5. The petitioner had not filed those objections and instead sought documents, submitting that without M.R.I. readings it could not object. Counsel for the licensee stated that the department had sought an e-mail ID and would supply the M.R.I. once it was provided. The Court permitted the petitioner to supply that ID so the readings could be emailed, and disposed of the petition without quashing the demand or deciding the quantum.
cases.flag: Paras 1-6 are the 22.04.2024 Order on memo of petition (electricity disposal). Source PDF is composite: 02.04.2024 (slogan-shouting interrupting the hearing; Returning Officers directed to appear), 02.04.2024 after recess (Bar election Code of Conduct; adjourned), 03.04.2024 (CCTV; main matter listed 22.04.2024), 22.04.2024 (this disposal, plus a sealed-cover list of identified advocates), 13.05.2024 (list 29.05.2024), and 29.05.2024 (Neutral Citation 2024:AHC:98461-DB: disturbance proceedings dropped taking a lenient view after peaceful elections; petition consigned). No Code clause other than 6.5 is cited. Section 35 of the Advocates Act appears only in the Bar Code of Conduct, not as an electricity holding.

cases.title: M/S Super Texcones v. State of U.P. and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-correctness dispute; alternative remedy
cases.holding: Where the petitioner disputes the correctness of electricity bills, Clause 6.5 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is the alternative remedy, and the writ petition is disposed of with liberty to avail that remedy, if so advised.

cases.title: Seema Devi Widow v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill dispute — alternate remedy
cases.holding: A writ petition raising a live electricity-bill dispute is disposed of by directing the consumer to approach the appropriate authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; that application is to be decided on its own merits as expeditiously as possible, preferably within three months from the date of compliance.

cases.title: Deo Dutt Kumar v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitaran Nigam Limited
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing objection under clause 6.5
cases.holding: Counsel not disputing that the demand arising from an alleged mistake in a previously issued bill could be decided under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, the Court relegated the petitioner to that remedy. If an objection is filed under Clause 6.5, respondent No. 3 shall decide it by a speaking order in accordance with law, preferably within three weeks, and shall not enforce the impugned demand until then. Amounts already deposited pursuant to the demand will abide the Clause 6.5 decision. The writ petition was disposed of.

cases.title: Dinesh Chauhan v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill dispute — Clause 6.5 remedy
cases.holding: Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 affords a sufficient remedy to a consumer seeking to dispute a bill; Article 226 interference is declined and the petitioner is left to avail that remedy in accordance with law.

cases.title: M/s Harivansh Gupta Rice Mill v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing objection as alternate remedy
cases.holding: Where a consumer challenges an electricity bill in writ and agrees to avail the statutory objection under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, the petition is disposed of with liberty to follow that procedure; the Court does not decide the bill on merits.

cases.title: Gaurav Masala Udhyog v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: objection to recovery of electricity dues
cases.holding: A consumer challenging a recovery certificate for electricity dues has an alternative remedy of filing an objection under Clause 6.5 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005 before the authority that issued the certificate; the writ is disposed of with liberty to avail that remedy.

cases.title: Pancham v. State of Up and 2 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 2 weeks, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: Ajeet Kumar Verma v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: 6.5 pre-deposit after permanent disconnection
cases.holding: Without expressing any opinion on merits, the writ is disposed of directing respondent No. 3 to decide the petitioner's objection dated 06.02.2024 within three weeks of communication of this order, on merits, without insisting on any clause 6.5 pre-deposit, the dispute relating not only to correctness of the bill but to the very jurisdiction to issue any bill after permanent disconnection.

cases.title: Smt Sayra Bano v. State of U.P. and Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: alternative remedy — billing objection
cases.holding: A writ petition challenging the correctness of an electricity consumption bill will not be entertained where the consumer has the remedy of filing an objection as prescribed by clause 6.5 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The petition was disposed of with liberty to avail that remedy.

cases.title: Rajeev Kumar Yadav v. State of U.P. and Another
cases.topic: billing objection under clause 6.5
cases.holding: The writ is disposed of by directing the Executive Engineer to decide the petitioner's 4 May 2024 billing-objection application by treating it as one under clause 6.5 of the Supply Code, 2005, within three weeks of communication of the order. If the petitioner deposits the disputed amount as per the recent bill, the respondents are to restore electricity supply pending that clause 6.5 consideration.

cases.title: Smt Kafia v. Purvanchal Vidhut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.topic: billing-objection
cases.holding: Where a consumer seeks revision of an existing electricity bill and permanent disconnection, the writ is disposed of by directing that, if she applies under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 within two weeks, the application shall be dealt with and decided on its own merits within one month; subject to compliance with that resolution, she may apply for permanent disconnection in accordance with law.

cases.title: Shiva Puri Goswami v. Purvanchal Vidhut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: pending Clause 6.5 application
cases.holding: A pending application under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is to be decided by the licensee in accordance with law; the High Court will not itself adjudicate the dispute while that application remains pending and will only direct expedition, here preferably within three months.

cases.title: Narsingh v. State of U.P. and others
cases.topic: billing objection after permanent disconnection
cases.holding: Without expressing any opinion on merits, the writ was disposed of with a direction to respondent no. 3 to decide the petitioner’s representation, to be filed within two weeks with a true attested copy of the order after hearing him, under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Any further demand of electricity dues would abide by that decision.

cases.title: Sharafat Ulla (since deceased) v. Purvanchal Vidhut Vitrana Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing objection under Clause 6.5
cases.holding: Where a consumer aggrieved of a recovery certificate and disconnection elects to approach the licensee under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, the writ petition is disposed of with a direction that if such an objection is made, it shall be decided as expeditiously as possible, preferably within four weeks.

cases.title: Smt. Lata Devi v. State of U.P. and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing objection
cases.holding: The writ is disposed by directing respondent no. 3 to decide the petitioner’s application dated 1 April 2024 treating it as filed under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, within the time stipulated therein, provided she deposits 50% of the disputed amount within a week. On such deposit the electricity connection is to be restored subject to that decision. If the deposit is not made, the order is of no avail and the authority may proceed in accordance with law. The recovery certificate is not quashed on merits.

cases.title: M/S Nirmala Dairy v. State of U.P. and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: alternate-remedy-clause-6.5
cases.holding: Where a writ petition challenged a recovery citation for electricity dues and the licensee's counsel invoked Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 as an efficacious remedy, which the petitioner did not dispute, the Court declined to examine the challenge and left the petitioner to approach respondent No. 2 under Clause 6.5.

cases.title: Rajendra Kumar v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing-dispute-objection
cases.holding: A writ challenging an electricity demand notice as illegally and arbitrarily calculated is disposed of without examining the merits, with liberty to the consumer to file an objection against the demand; the issuing officer shall then decide that objection as provided under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: M/s Durga Cold Storage v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing objection to amended bill
cases.holding: Where the licensee has already corrected original electricity bills on the consumer's representation, a writ may be withdrawn with liberty to challenge the correctness of the amended bill under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Gurunam Singh v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: objection to recovery citation
cases.holding: A consumer challenging a recovery citation for electricity dues has the remedy of filing an objection under Clause 6.5. The writ was disposed of with two weeks to file the objection, to be decided by respondent no.2 within the next two weeks; recovery remains in abeyance for four weeks and thereafter abides that decision. If no objection is filed within time, the order lapses and the licensee may proceed in accordance with law.

cases.title: Ram Sewak v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: objection to recovery of electricity dues
cases.holding: A consumer challenging a recovery citation for electricity dues has an efficacious remedy of filing an objection under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ is disposed of with liberty to file objections within two weeks before respondent no.3, who shall decide them by a speaking order within the next two weeks. Recovery remains in abeyance for four weeks and thereafter abides by that decision; if no objection is filed, the order is of no avail and respondents may proceed in accordance with law.

cases.title: Satish Chandra v. State of U.P. and Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: reasoned decision on pending representation
cases.holding: Where a representation filed before the designated authority remains undecided, the High Court may dispose of the writ by directing that authority to pass a reasoned order on the representation in terms of Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, within a stipulated period after granting the consumer an opportunity of hearing, without examining the merits of the grievance.

cases.title: Noorjaha Begum v. State of U.P. and Another
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Barkat Frozen Foods Pvt Ltd v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: objection under clause 6.5
cases.holding: Where a writ challenging a demand notice and recovery certificate, with an alternative prayer for reconnection, is founded on non-supply of the MRI report, and that report is produced in Court and supplied to the petitioner, the High Court will not keep the petition pending; the consumer remains free to press an objection under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: M/s Vinayak Roller Flour Mills v. Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection
cases.holding: Where a Clause 6.5 complaint remains undecided, the Executive Engineer must pass a reasoned order on it within eight weeks after granting the consumer a hearing; the High Court will not itself decide the billing objection on a writ complaining only of inaction.

cases.title: Radheshyam Bhaskar v. State of Up and 3 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Barsatu Yadav v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: alternate-remedy-clause-6.5
cases.holding: A writ against a recovery citation for electricity dues is not entertained on merits where Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, furnishes an efficacious alternative; the petition is disposed of with liberty to avail that remedy.

cases.title: M/s Mangalam Agro Foods v. State of U.P. and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing dispute; objection to recovery demand
cases.holding: A writ against a Section 3 recovery demand for disputed electricity dues is disposed of with liberty to file a Clause 6.5 objection within two weeks; the competent authority shall decide it by a speaking order within four weeks. Until that decision the recovery remains in abeyance and thereafter abides the objection decision. If no objection is filed within two weeks, the licensee may proceed in accordance with law.

cases.title: Ajay Kumar Pandey v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing objection under clause 6.5
cases.holding: On the licensee's statement that the petitioner's representations would be treated as objections under Clause 6.5, the writ was disposed of directing the third respondent to decide the objections dated 20.09.2023, 22.09.2023 and 16.10.2023 by a speaking order within four weeks, and not to take coercive action on the impugned bills until that decision.

cases.title: Vijay Kumar Gupta v. State of Up and 3 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If an application is made after completing the formalities within 2 weeks, it shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.

cases.title: Narendra Singh v. State of U.P. and 5 Others
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Roop Narayan Tripathi v. Kanpur Electric Supply Company, Kanpur Nagar Thru' Its M.D.
cases.topic: Incorrect-billing / wrong-person demand — relegation to the Executive Engineer; coercive recovery stayed pending a timely representation
cases.holding: The writ court will not decide whether the purchasers obtained the connection by a false declaration. Prima facie the 29.7.1988 sale deed supports the petitioner's contention, but it is not prudent to decide that issue in writ jurisdiction. A dispute as to incorrect billing can be raised before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If the petitioner represents to the Executive Engineer, KESCO, within 15 days, the representation is to be decided within six weeks of production of a certified copy and supporting documents. Until that decision, no coercive steps are to be taken on the recovery certificate; if the representation is not filed within 15 days, that protection lapses.
cases.flag: Source PDF also contains listing, pass-over and service orders from 28.9.2010 to 15.2.2011; the operative judgment is 4.7.2011 (unnumbered; paras are of that order's logical paragraphs). Connection (November 1991) and the billed period (31.12.2000–31.5.2003) predate the 2005 Code; the Court applied Clause 6.5 as the 2011 forum.

cases.title: Maula Bux v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.topic: Bill and arrears dispute must go first to the supplier under Clause 6.5
cases.holding: No. Where the dispute is about bills and the arrears shown in them, Clause 6.5 gives the consumer a remedy before the supplier's competent authority. That remedy had not been availed. The Court declined extra-ordinary jurisdiction under Article 226 and dismissed the writ on alternative remedy, without deciding whether the post-disconnection bill was erroneous.
cases.flag: The operative order numbers paragraphs 1, 2, 3 then 5 (no paragraph 4). The Court applied Clause 6.5 of the 2005 Code to a 28.9.2003 demand without discussing the Code's temporal application.

cases.title: Awadhesh Pratap v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.topic: interlocutory direction to settle old ice-factory bills under Clause 6.5; overtaken by later dismissal
cases.holding: Yes, as an interlocutory measure. On 17.4.2017 a Division Bench (Bharati Sapru and Shashi Kant JJ.) recorded that the ice factory had remained shut from 2002 when the connection was permanently disconnected, and directed the petitioner to appear before the concerned authority within two weeks to settle his bills as provided in Clause 6.5, with a decision within one month and a proper hearing. The Executive Engineer, Electricity Distribution Division I, Mau, then passed an order dated 24.8.2017 adjusting ten receipts and quantifying Rs. 5,35,490 still recoverable. The 5.12.2019 judgment recited that order but dismissed the writ on disputed facts and the pending civil suit, without applying Clause 6.5 as the disposing forum.
cases.flag: Unnumbered interlocutory order of 17.4.2017; the 12.12.2017 order recites the 24.8.2017 Executive Engineer quantification. Overtaken by the 5.12.2019 dismissal.

cases.title: Pankaj Katiyar v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection
cases.holding: A small dispute over payment of electricity dues, for which a recovery certificate has been issued, is referable to the concerned Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The consumer may file a fresh representation with details to that authority within one month; the Engineer shall decide it within two months of production of a certified copy of the order. Till then the recovery certificate remains in abeyance. The writ is disposed of without deciding the dues on merits.

cases.title: M/S. Mohan Electrocasting Pvt. Ltd. And Another v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. And Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: check-meter billing dispute is a Clause 6.5 objection, not for the writ court
cases.holding: No. Counsel for the licensee submitted that because the petitioners were disputing the correctness of the electricity bill, they have the remedy of filing an objection under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, to be decided by respondent no. 2. The Court permitted the petitioners to file that objection within two weeks, directed respondent no. 2 to decide it by a speaking order within the next four weeks, and held that the impugned bill will abide that decision. No further amount is to be recovered on the bill until the objections are decided. The petition is disposed of accordingly.
cases.flag: Source PDF concatenates listing orders of 9.11.2021, 27.1.2023, 17.2.2023, 13.3.2023 and 21.3.2023; the operative disposal is 12.4.2023 (unnumbered). Petitioner relied on unnamed 'various decisions of this Court'; none are identified.

cases.title: Ram Lautan v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: writ-not-proper-remedy-for-electricity-bills
cases.holding: A writ petition is not the proper remedy to challenge electricity bills. Factual issues as to whether electrical energy was supplied, where the bills carry a connection number, are to be raised first under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The petition was dismissed with liberty to challenge the bills; any interim order stood discharged.

cases.title: The Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Anr. v. The Electricity Ombudsman of U.P. & Anr.
cases.topic: Licensee's failure to settle a billing complaint within seven days under paragraph 6.5 opens CGRF
cases.holding: Yes. Once a complaint had been filed with the licensee and the licensee failed to settle it within seven days in terms of paragraph 6.5, it could not be said that there was no complaint, and CGRF was competent to entertain the consumer's complaint.

cases.holding: A consumer who only disputes the amount of an electricity bill has an alternative remedy under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 before the competent authority; a writ petition raising that dispute is dismissed on the ground of alternative remedy.

cases.title: Dinesh Chandra v. State of U.P. & Ors.

Electricity Supply Code, 2005, the licensee shall decide the consumer's representation, if filed within one week of obtaining a certified copy of the order, within two further weeks after fullest opportunity of hearing and by a reasoned order; if the authority finds the case genuine and that all amounts have been paid with no arrear, it may take steps for reconnection as early as possible irrespective of that consideration.

cases.holding: A consumer disputing electricity bills and arrears must pursue the statutory remedy under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, after making the deposit required by the rules; the High Court will not decide the disputed bills on a writ challenging recovery.

cases.title: Rakesh Kumar v. State of U.P. Thru The Ministry Of Energy And Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: restoration of supply on deposit of billed amount
cases.holding: Clause 6.5 permits a consumer who is ready to pay the claimed charges to deposit the entire demand or electricity charges calculated on the average of the preceding six months' bills, whichever is less, and to have any complaint considered by the competent authority. Where the consumer elects to deposit the entire amount, deposit is to be made within two months of a certified copy; on an application for restoration the licensee, after considering the matter, is to restore supply without delay and not later than 72 hours. The direction does not affect any independent theft proceeding, in which the licensee may act in accordance with law if theft is established.

cases.title: Smt. Rajni Verma v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: reconnection on deposit pending billing complaint
cases.holding: Under clause 6.5, a billing complaint is to be considered on deposit of the entire claimed amount or electricity charges calculated on the average of the preceding six months' bills, whichever is less. The petitioner having undertaken to deposit the entire claimed amount, the Court directed deposit within two months of a certified copy and a restoration application thereafter; the licensee, after considering the matter, is to restore supply without delay and not later than 72 hours of the application. The order is irrespective of any theft case, which if established may be proceeded with independently. A modification application seeking further time to pay was dismissed.

cases.title: Sabhajeet Tiwari v. U.P. Power Corporation and Another
cases.topic: Billing objection — relegation to Clause 6.5
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of an electricity bill and/or a restraint on disconnection is disposed of without examining the bill. The consumer has a remedy before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Ishtiyak Ahmad v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: incorrect bills / meter reading
cases.holding: A complaint that electricity bills are not based on actual meter reading is to be considered under paragraph 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ seeking a mandamus to furnish a correct bill is dismissed, with a direction that the pending complaint before the Executive Engineer be decided expeditiously within two months of production of a certified copy.

cases.title: Ajay Kumar v. State of U.P. and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-correction-remedy

cases.title: Tauqeerul Islam v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-revision-and-reconnection-after-6.5-deposit
cases.holding: A consumer challenging an Executive Engineer's demand to deposit a revised MRI-based bill is to seek revision under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; after deposit of the amount required under that clause, the licensee shall consider reconnection. The writ is disposed without deciding the bill on merits.

cases.title: Bidha v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill dispute
cases.holding: Where the electricity bill is not under challenge, consequential recovery cannot be subjected to change in writ. A consumer dissatisfied with the bill’s correctness must seek the remedy under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ was dismissed with that liberty and any interim order was discharged.

cases.title: Jagdish Pal Singh v. State of U.P. and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: Where the consumer pressed only a grievance that a bill included amounts already deposited without adjustment, and the licensee pointed to the clause 6.5 remedy before the Executive Engineer, the writ was disposed of by consent directing that officer to consider and decide any complaint in accordance with law, preferably within six weeks of filing, without a delay objection, and restraining disconnection for non-payment of that bill until decision if the complaint was filed within two weeks.

cases.title: Pawan Kumar v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing objection inapplicable where consumption and bill not disputed
cases.holding: Clause 6.5 of the Supply Code is not attracted where the consumer does not dispute consumption of electricity or the bill. A plea that the bill should be shared with a co-heir after the consumer's death would require a fact-finding enquiry, which a writ court will not undertake. There is no provision under the U.P. Electricity Act or the regulations made thereunder to bifurcate bills among legal heirs.
cases.flag: The order refers to the 'U.P. Electricity Act'; the governing statute is the Electricity Act, 2003.

cases.title: Sant Swaroop v. Dakhinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing objection; alternative remedy
cases.holding: A writ against disputed electricity bills is not entertained where the consumer has the statutory alternative of approaching the Executive Engineer under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If a complaint is made, it is to be decided as provided under clause 6.5(b) within seven days of the complaint, on the consumer depositing before the due date an amount equal to the sum claimed or charges calculated on the average of the preceding six months' bills, whichever is less.
cases.flag: Operative observation cites 'Para 6.5 (b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Act, 2005'; the clause is in the Supply Code, 2005, not an Act.

cases.title: Rajveer Sharma v. State of U.P. — arrears recovery; writ dismissed
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer
cases.holding: Electricity bills are to be paid as soon as they become due on the date fixed under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If the consumer still disputes the bill, it is open to approach the Executive Engineer under clause 6.5, or the Electricity Consumers Redressal Forum; a writ for instalments or to stall recovery, without any representation or paid bill on record, is dismissed.

cases.title: Pratap Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: exhaustion of clause 6.5 before writ
cases.holding: A consumer who disputes electricity bills, a recovery citation, and post-disconnection minimum-guarantee charges must first raise the grievance before the Executive Engineer under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and may thereafter approach the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum. A writ petition filed in the High Court to correct such bills without first exhausting those statutory remedies under the Electricity Act, 2003 is not maintainable and is dismissed.

cases.title: Mohd. Azahar v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: A consumer seeking correction of electricity bills, including after disconnection and meter dismantling, must first approach the Executive Engineer under para 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and thereafter the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum. A writ petition filed in the High Court to correct bills without exhausting those statutory remedies under the Electricity Act, 2003 is dismissed.

cases.flag: Court called clause 6.5 an 'appeal' and did not specify 6.5(a), 6.5(b) or 6.5B.

If such a complaint is filed before the competent officer, it shall be decided in accordance with law by a reasoned and speaking order within seven days of filing, provided the petitioner complies with the terms of clause 6.5(b). The writ petition was disposed of on that basis.

cases.title: Smt. Asma Begam v. State of U.P.

cases.holding: Where a consumer disputes an arrears notice or electricity bill, the High Court will not issue mandamus to withdraw the notice; the statutory remedy is an application under paragraph 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, to be decided in accordance with that Code.

cases.title: M/S Malhotra Ice Factory v. State of U.P. and Others

cases.topic: statutory remedy under clause 6.5
cases.holding: Where the consumer states that it will seek the statutory remedy under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 at the first instance, the writ is dismissed with that liberty and any interim order stands discharged.

cases.title: Panna Lal Vishwakarma v. State of U.P. And Others
cases.topic: billing-complaint-on-recovery-citation
cases.holding: Where a recovery citation for electricity dues turns on disputed facts, including alleged undecided bill objections, the writ court will not adjudicate the bills. The consumer's remedy is a complaint under paragraph 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, which the Executive Engineer is to decide within four weeks of filing. If half the amount mentioned in the citation is deposited with the Executive Engineer within two weeks, no coercive steps shall be taken until that complaint is decided; thereafter the licensee may proceed in accordance with law. The complaint is to be filed within two weeks, and current bills remain payable.

cases.title: Narain Singh v. State of U.P. and others
cases.topic: bill-challenge-relegated-to-clause-6.5
cases.holding: If the consumer is not satisfied with a bill issued by the electricity department, the remedy is under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; a writ petition is dismissed with liberty to pursue that remedy and any interim order stands discharged.

cases.title: Kunwar Pal v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-complaint-statutory-remedy
cases.holding: A consumer aggrieved by an electricity bill must file a complaint under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; a writ seeking to restrain recovery without notice cannot be entertained when that statutory remedy is available.

cases.title: Vimla Devi v. Purvanchal Vidyut Bitaran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-dispute-complaint-to-executive-engineer
cases.holding: A writ seeking quash of a recovery citation for disputed electricity dues was disposed of by directing the consumer to deposit Rs 15,000 and to file a complaint before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the Engineer is to decide the complaint and may then recover any amount still due, coercive steps under the citation remaining stayed until that decision, with recovery reviving on the consumer's default.

cases.title: Suresh v. State of U.P. & Anr.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: Where a consumer challenges an electricity demand notice in writ, and clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 provides a statutory complaint in which all grievances can be raised, the writ is not entertainable and the petitioner must avail that remedy.

cases.title: Govind Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: recovery demand after permanent disconnection
cases.holding: A writ challenging a recovery citation after permanent disconnection, on the plea that no hearing was given and no particulars of the demand were furnished, will not be entertained where clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 supplies a statutory remedy. The consumer may file a clause 6.5 application within 30 days of a certified copy, and the authority shall decide it expeditiously without unnecessary adjournment.

cases.title: Bhola v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer
cases.holding: A consumer aggrieved by an electricity bill is to pursue a complaint before the Executive Engineer under paragraph 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the writ court will not decide the bill and will direct that if an appropriate complaint is filed, the Executive Engineer shall consider and dispose of it expeditiously, preferably within one month of a certified copy of the order.

cases.title: M/S Tarunika Gaur Housing & Commercial Ltd. v. State of U.P. and others
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: Where the grievance is against electricity bills, Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is the specific statutory remedy; a writ for mandamus to decide informal objections will be disposed of with liberty to invoke Clause 6.5 in accordance with law, and any complaint so submitted is to be considered and disposed of.

cases.title: Riyasat Hussain v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-objection
cases.holding: A consumer who challenges the correctness of an electricity bill must raise objections under para 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 and seek redressal from the concerned Executive Engineer; a writ filed two years after the disputed bill without adequately explaining the delay is dismissed both for that alternative remedy and for unexplained laches.

cases.title: Achhelal v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer
cases.holding: A consumer seeking correction of electricity bills has a right to file a complaint under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 before the Executive Engineer; the High Court will not decide the representation itself, and any such complaint may be considered and decided expeditiously, preferably within two months of filing together with a certified copy of the order.

cases.title: Yogeshwar Singh v. State of U.P. (through Secretary) and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing dispute — Permanent Lok Adalat / clause 6.5
cases.holding: A consumer not satisfied with the correctness of electricity bills must seek remedy under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Following U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. v. Anis Ahmad, the consumer’s remedy lies within the Supply Code and the Electricity Act; proceedings before the Permanent Lok Adalat are without jurisdiction. The writ to quash a recovery citation and to decide the claim in light of a Permanent Lok Adalat order is dismissed with that liberty.
cases.flag: The Court referred to the Electricity Act, 2005; the statute is the Electricity Act, 2003.

cases.title: Chhotey Lal v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.topic: billing complaint must be lodged before the Executive Engineer
cases.holding: Under para 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 a complaint against electricity bills is to be lodged before the Executive Engineer, not the Chief Engineer. The writ challenging the bills and disconnection notice is disposed of by directing the petitioner to submit a Clause 6.5 complaint before the Executive Engineer (respondent no. 3). Pending disposal of that complaint, supply shall be restored if the petitioner deposits the entire dues; if the Executive Engineer permits payment in instalments, supply shall be restored on payment of the first instalment.

cases.title: Madhukar Shukla v. State of U.P. and others
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer-under-6.5
cases.holding: Where a consumer challenges electricity bills on the ground that the multiplying factor is incorrect, the writ court will not entertain the petition in the face of the specific statutory remedy of a complaint under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; any such complaint filed in accordance with Clause 6.5 is to be considered and disposed of by the competent authority.

cases.title: M/S Anurag Pisai Kendra v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: relegation to Executive Engineer to settle dues dispute
cases.holding: Read with Clause 6.5, a consumer facing a recovery citation may, after the directed deposit, approach the concerned Executive Engineer with a representation and the Court's order. If the application is moved within the stipulated period, the Executive Engineer may adopt a liberal approach in settling the dispute. The citation is not examined on merits.

cases.title: M/S. Shyam Forging (P) Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: payment facility and stay of disconnection pending clause 6.5 consideration
cases.holding: Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 permits the competent authority to grant facility after considering the consumer's financial stress and other aspects. The petitioner was allowed to make a fresh representation with a certified copy of this order; the authority was to decide within three weeks, after which compliance was for the petitioner. Pending that decision, the petitioner was to deposit 40% of the total dues and pay regular current bills, and no disconnection was to take place.

cases.title: Jitendra Sharma (Minor) v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: facility-in-payment-of-assessment-bill
cases.holding: Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 permits the competent authority to grant facility in payment of an assessment bill, considering the consumer's financial stress and other aspects placed before it. Liability not being disputed, the writ court did not examine the bill on merits and disposed of the petition by permitting a fresh representation, with a certified copy of the order, to be decided preferably within three weeks.
cases.flag: ambiguous: court treated cl. 6.5 as payment-facility/financial-stress power

cases.title: Brahmpal Singh v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: payment facility on assessment bill (financial stress)
cases.holding: Where the consumer does not dispute an assessment bill and seeks only a facility in payment, clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is the alternative remedy: the competent authority may grant that facility and is to consider financial stress and other aspects placed by the consumer. The writ court will not decide the request on merits and will dispose of the petition with liberty to make a fresh representation, to be decided preferably within three weeks.
cases.flag: Court treated cl. 6.5 as authorising payment facility for financial stress; catalog hits treat 6.5 as billing-objection.

cases.title: Poonam Dixit v. State of U.P. And 3 Others
cases.topic: consumer grievance redressal
cases.holding: Without examining merits, a writ complaining that no electricity connection was ever taken in the petitioner's name is disposed of by directing that if she applies under Clause 6.5(a) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code within ten days, the authority shall decide the application within one month.

UP-2005::6.5(b).code: U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 (Clauses 5.5, 5.6, 5.6(c)(iii), 6.5(b)) read with s.162, Electricity Act, 2003
UP-2005::6.5(b).clause: 6.5(b) (Disputed Bills and Arrears) read with 5.6 (meter testing)
UP-2005::6.5(b).topic: A supplementary bill grounded in a disputed/defective meter or transformer reading is a 'disputed bill' under Clause 6.5(b); the consumer must first invoke the Clause 5.6 meter-testing procedure (and thereafter the Electrical Inspector) rather than approaching the writ court directly

cases.title: Mohamdabad Cold Storage Private Ltd. (& Anr.) v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.topic: A supplementary bill grounded in a disputed/defective meter or transformer reading is a 'disputed bill' under Clause 6.5(b); the consumer must first invoke the Clause 5.6 meter-testing procedure (and thereafter the Electrical Inspector) rather than approaching the writ court directly
cases.holding: A supplementary bill founded on a disputed meter/transformer reading falls within Clause 6.5(b)'s 'disputed bills' notwithstanding its heading; since the bill cannot be assessed without first resolving the accuracy of the underlying meter/instrument reading, the consumer must invoke the Clause 5.6 (and 5.6(c)(iii)) meter-testing procedure, and if unresolved, approach the Electrical Inspector under s.162 of the Electricity Act, 2003 (the modern successor, per Bombay Electric Supply and Transport Undertaking v. Laffans (India) Pvt. Ltd., to the Electrical Inspector's statutory-arbitration role under the 1910 Act). The writ petition, filed without first exhausting this route, is premature and dismissed without costs, without prejudice to the petitioners' right to raise their grievance before the authority concerned or the Electrical Inspector.

cases.title: Mother India Refrigeration Industries (& Anr.) v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.topic: Companion ruling to SCJ-083 — identical holding on a parallel supplementary-bill dispute grounded in a defective transformer
cases.holding: As in SCJ-083: a supplementary bill founded on a disputed/defective transformer reading is a 'disputed bill' under Clause 6.5(b); the consumer must first invoke the Clause 5.6 meter-testing procedure and, if unresolved, the Electrical Inspector under s.162 of the Electricity Act, 2003, rather than approach the writ court directly. The writ petition is premature and dismissed without costs, without prejudice to the petitioners' right to raise their grievance before the authority concerned or the Electrical Inspector.
cases.flag: Near-verbatim companion order to SCJ-083; recorded compactly to avoid duplicating the identical reasoning.

cases.title: Smt. Shiv Devi Tiwari v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-accuracy-alternative-remedy
cases.holding: A writ petition challenging the correctness of an electricity bill on the plea that the meter is defective and inflated bills are being raised is not liable to be entertained, because clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 provides an alternative remedy to approach the competent authority for redressal of that grievance.

cases.title: Mazzoo Khan v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: alternative remedy for billing dispute
cases.holding: A consumer aggrieved by electricity bills on various grounds has an alternative remedy under clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 before the competent authority; a writ seeking a direction to decide a representation is not liable to be granted and the petition stands dismissed, with liberty to avail that remedy.

cases.title: M/s Raja Ram Ispat Private Ltd. v. State of U.P. and others
cases.topic: bill-accuracy dispute before Executive Engineer
cases.holding: Clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 empowers the Executive Engineer to resolve disputes regarding accuracy of bills. Where the writ challenge to a post-disconnection demand raises questions of fact, the consumer must pursue that complaint/representation under Clause 6.5; the authority is to decide it by a reasoned speaking order in accordance with law, expeditiously. The High Court will not adjudicate the bill on a writ.

cases.title: Dayanand Public School v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: bill accuracy complaint
cases.holding: Where a consumer disputes the correctness or accuracy of an electricity bill, clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 supplies the complaint remedy before the competent authority. The writ court will not decide the bill on merits and will dispose of the petition with liberty to file that complaint, directing the Executive Engineer to consider and decide it in accordance with law and the prescribed procedure.

cases.title: Gaurav Gupta v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing-objection
cases.holding: Clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 requires the competent authority to decide a consumer's complaint disputing the accuracy of a bill. A writ against recovery of such bills as arrears of land revenue may be disposed of by relegating the consumer to that complaint before the Executive Engineer, keeping recovery in abeyance until a reasoned speaking order, and providing that the stay lapses if the complaint is not filed within the time fixed.

cases.title: M/s Maa Vindhyavasini Stone Works v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.topic: clause-6.5b-quantification-dispute
cases.holding: Correctness of electricity bills and a recovery certificate under Section 3 of the U.P. Government Electrical Undertaking (Recovery of Dues) Act, 1957, may be challenged under clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. A writ petition is not the proper remedy. A new-unit benefit claim and grievance against the bills can be raised in that quantification challenge.

cases.title: Ramdeep Singh v. State of U.P. — bill challenge relegated to clause 6.5(b)
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-objection-to-executive-engineer
cases.holding: A writ challenging the amount disclosed in an electricity bill is not entertained where the consumer has a statutory remedy of objection before the Executive Engineer under clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the petition is dismissed with liberty to pursue that objection strictly in accordance with the clause.

cases.title: Sajid Ali v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: bill accuracy — 6.5(b) complaint
cases.holding: Where a consumer disputes the correctness or accuracy of a bill for electrical energy, clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 supplies the remedy of a complaint to the competent authority. The writ was disposed of with liberty to file that complaint before the Executive Engineer, Electricity Distribution Division-II, PuVVNL, Ghazipur, who shall consider and decide it in accordance with law and the prescribed procedure.

cases.title: Mohsin Siddique v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: disputed-bill-complaint
cases.holding: Where a consumer disputes the correctness or accuracy of an electricity bill, the remedy is a complaint to the competent authority under clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the writ was disposed with liberty to file that complaint, and the Executive Engineer was directed to consider and decide it in accordance with law.

cases.title: Smt. Shashi Kala v. State of U.P. and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-accuracy dispute; payment under protest or complaint to competent authority
cases.holding: Where a consumer disputes the accuracy of an electricity bill, Clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 supplies the remedy of payment under protest or a complaint to the competent authority, which is to be decided within seven days; the High Court will not examine the billing dispute in writ jurisdiction and will relegate the consumer to that remedy, with a direction that if Clause 6.5 is invoked an appropriate decision be taken expeditiously.

cases.title: Rajendra Singh Yadav v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: bill-accuracy-objection
cases.holding: Where a consumer disputes the accuracy of electricity bills, Clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 supplies the remedy—payment under protest or a complaint to the competent authority, to be decided within seven days—and the writ court will dispose of the petition with liberty to invoke Clause 6.5, directing that an appropriate decision be taken expeditiously.

cases.title: Rajendra Singh Yadav v. Rang Lal Pal, Executive Engineer, Power Distribution Division
cases.topic: expeditious-decision-of-clause-6.5(b)-application
cases.holding: Where a writ court has directed that a consumer's application under Clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 be decided expeditiously, and the consumer alleges non-compliance in civil contempt, the High Court may, without recording a finding of wilful disobedience, afford the licensee officer one further opportunity to decide the application within a stipulated time and dispose of the contempt at that stage with liberty to move a fresh application if the order remains uncomplied.

cases.title: Mohd. Ramjan v. Kanpur Electricity Supply Company Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing complaint for disputed bill accuracy
cases.holding: Where a consumer challenges recovery of electricity dues by disputing the accuracy of the bill, and disputed questions of fact arise, the writ court will not decide the billing dispute on merits. The consumer is to make a complaint before the competent authority under clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Recovery remains in abeyance for four weeks or until disposal of that complaint, whichever is earlier, and shall abide by the authority's order. After the consumer deposits the amount, the electricity connection shall be restored forthwith.

cases.title: Salig Ram Gupta v. State of U.P. (KESCO bill recovery)
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-accuracy dispute — statutory complaint
cases.holding: Where the consumer disputes the accuracy of a bill and recovery of outstanding dues has been initiated, disputed questions of fact are to be raised by complaint before the competent authority under clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, not in writ. The petitioner was given one week to complain and the authority two weeks to decide in accordance with law; recovery remains in abeyance for four weeks or till disposal of the complaint, whichever is earlier, and the connection is to be restored forthwith after the petitioner deposits the amount.

cases.title: Ram Chandra Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: complaint against accuracy of bill
cases.holding: Clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 provides the complaint before the competent authority where the consumer disputes the accuracy of the bill. Because disputed questions of fact were involved and that statutory remedy was available, the writ was disposed of with liberty to complain under Clause 6.5(b) within one week; the authority was directed to consider and pass orders in accordance with law within two weeks of the complaint; recovery was to remain in abeyance for four weeks or till disposal of the complaint, whichever was earlier, and to abide by the authority's orders; after the petitioner deposited the amount, the electricity connection was to be restored forthwith.

cases.title: Chhotey Lal v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: bill-accuracy complaint as forum for disputed recovery
cases.holding: Clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 provides the complaint to the competent authority where a consumer disputes the accuracy of the bill. Because disputed questions of fact were involved and that remedy was available, the writ challenging recovery of outstanding dues was disposed of with liberty to complain under clause 6.5(b) within one week; the authority was directed to consider and pass orders in accordance with law within two weeks of the complaint; and no coercive action was to be taken on the recovery citation until disposal of that complaint under clause 6.5.

cases.title: Shashank Gupta v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-accuracy dispute; deposit of six-month average and complaint to competent authority
cases.holding: Clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code 2005 is the statutory remedy where a consumer disputes the accuracy of a bill. The consumer may deposit charges calculated on the average of the preceding six months' bills and file a complaint with the competent authority (here, the Executive Engineer), who shall decide it within seven days. This writ against a recovery certificate of Rs.4,54,461 is disposed of on those directions; recovery remains stayed until disposal of a representation made within 15 days, failing which the order will not benefit the petitioner.

cases.title: Inayat Khan v. State of U.P. — disputed bill relegated to cl. 6.5(b)
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-accuracy complaint as alternative to writ
cases.holding: Where the consumer disputes the accuracy of a bill and recovery of outstanding dues has been initiated, the writ court will not decide disputed questions of fact and will relegate the consumer to a complaint before the competent authority under clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, with a short time to complain, a corresponding direction to decide in accordance with law, and an interim stay of recovery until that decision or a brief outer limit, whichever is earlier.

cases.title: Shailendra Singh v. Dhakshinanchal Vidhut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: accuracy of bill / recovery of dues
cases.holding: Clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is the forum for a consumer who disputes the accuracy of a bill. Where recovery of outstanding dues is challenged on that footing, disputed questions of fact are to be raised by an appropriate complaint before the competent authority under clause 6.5(b), not in a writ petition. The petition was disposed of with liberty to complain within one week; the authority was directed to pass orders in accordance with law within two weeks; recovery was kept in abeyance for four weeks or till disposal of the complaint, whichever earlier, to abide the authority's order; and the connection was directed to be restored forthwith after the petitioner deposits the amount.

cases.title: Shailendra Kumar Dwivedi v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-accuracy-complaint
cases.holding: Clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 provides the complaint before the competent authority where a consumer disputes the accuracy of a bill. Because disputed questions of fact were involved and that remedy was available, the writ was disposed of with liberty to complain under clause 6.5(b) within one week; the authority was directed to consider and pass orders in accordance with law within two weeks; recovery was kept in abeyance for four weeks or until disposal of the complaint, whichever earlier; and the connection was to be restored forthwith after the petitioner deposited the amount.

cases.title: Babu Ram v. M.D., Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.topic: disputed bill — complaint under clause 6.5(b)
cases.holding: Where a consumer challenges recovery of electricity dues by disputing the accuracy of the bill and disputed questions of fact are involved, the writ court will not examine the bill on merits. Clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 furnishes the remedy of a complaint before the competent authority. The writ is disposed of with liberty to make that complaint, a time-bound direction to decide it in accordance with law, stay of recovery pending that process, and restoration of supply upon deposit of the amount.

cases.title: Jai Karan Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: bill-accuracy-complaint
cases.holding: A consumer who disputes the accuracy of an electricity bill has a complaint remedy under clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Finding disputed questions of fact and that statutory remedy, the Court disposed of the writ with liberty to complain under clause 6.5(b) within one week, directed the competent authority to decide the complaint within two weeks, stayed recovery for four weeks or until disposal of the complaint whichever was earlier, and directed that supply be restored forthwith after the petitioner deposits the amount.

cases.title: Ramesh Chandra v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: bill-accuracy-complaint-as-alternative-to-writ
cases.holding: Where the consumer disputes the accuracy of the bill for which recovery has been initiated, disputed questions of fact are to be raised by complaint before the competent authority under clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and the writ court will not decide those facts; recovery may be kept in abeyance pending that complaint and supply restored on a specified deposit subject to the authority's decision.

cases.title: Chhena v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-accuracy-dispute
cases.holding: Clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 provides the complaint before the competent authority where a consumer disputes the accuracy of a bill. Because disputed questions of fact were involved and that statutory remedy was available, the writ petition was disposed of with liberty to complain under clause 6.5(b) within one week; the authority was directed to consider and decide the complaint in accordance with law within two weeks. Recovery was to remain in abeyance for four weeks or until disposal of the complaint, whichever was earlier, and to abide the authority's order. Upon the petitioner depositing the amount, the electricity connection was to be restored forthwith.

cases.title: Anil Sharma v. Managing Director, U.P.P.C.L. & Anr.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-accuracy-dispute
cases.holding: Clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 provides the complaint to the competent authority where a consumer disputes the accuracy of a bill. Because disputed questions of fact were involved and that remedy existed, the writ challenging recovery of outstanding dues was disposed of with liberty to complain under clause 6.5(b) within one week; the authority was to consider and pass orders in accordance with law within two weeks; recovery remained in abeyance for four weeks or till disposal of the complaint, whichever earlier, and was to abide by that order.

cases.title: Ram Prasad v. P.V.V.N.L.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-accuracy-complaint
cases.holding: Where a consumer challenges recovery of outstanding dues by disputing the accuracy of the bill and disputed questions of fact are involved, clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 supplies the complaint before the competent authority. The writ court will dispose of the petition with liberty to make that complaint within a stipulated time, direct the authority to decide it in accordance with law, and keep recovery in abeyance for a short period pending that decision.

cases.title: Ganga Prasad Soni v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-accuracy-complaint
cases.holding: Clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 provides a complaint to the competent authority where the consumer disputes the accuracy of the bill. Because disputed questions of fact were involved and that statutory remedy existed, the writ challenging recovery of outstanding dues was disposed of with liberty to complain under clause 6.5(b) within one week, the authority being directed to consider and pass orders in accordance with law within two weeks. Recovery remained in abeyance for four weeks or until disposal of the complaint, whichever was earlier, and was to abide that decision. After the petitioner deposited the amount, the electricity connection was to be restored forthwith.

cases.title: Rakesh Kumar v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: bill-accuracy complaint as alternate remedy
cases.holding: Where a consumer disputes the accuracy of a bill and recovery has been initiated, clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 supplies the complaint before the competent authority. Because disputed questions of fact are involved, the writ is disposed of with liberty to make that complaint within one week; the authority is to consider and pass orders in accordance with law within two weeks; recovery remains in abeyance for four weeks or until disposal of the complaint, whichever is earlier; and after the petitioner deposits the amount, the electricity connection is to be restored forthwith.

cases.title: Ganesh Shankar Tiwari v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: bill-accuracy-complaint
cases.holding: Where the consumer disputes the accuracy of the bill and recovery has been initiated, clause 6.5(b) furnishes the complaint before the competent authority. Disputed questions of fact being involved, the writ is disposed with liberty to complain under clause 6.5(b) within one week; the authority shall consider and pass orders in accordance with law within two weeks of the complaint; recovery remains in abeyance for four weeks or until disposal of the complaint, whichever is earlier, and shall abide by that order; upon deposit of the amount, the connection shall be restored forthwith.

cases.title: Naval Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: bill-accuracy-complaint
cases.holding: Clause 6.5(b) provides a complaint before the competent authority where the consumer disputes the accuracy of the bill. Because disputed questions of fact were involved and that remedy was available, the writ was disposed of with liberty to complain under clause 6.5(b) within one week; the authority was directed to consider and pass orders in accordance with law within two weeks; recovery was to remain in abeyance for four weeks or till disposal of the complaint, whichever was earlier; and the connection was to be restored forthwith after the petitioner deposited the amount.

cases.title: Jaipal Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: excessive-bill dispute; alternative remedy
cases.holding: Where a consumer disputes an electricity bill as excessive, clause 6.5(b) of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005 furnishes a statutory alternative remedy, and the High Court will not in the first instance examine the correctness of the bill. The writ petition was dismissed with liberty to avail that remedy.

cases.title: Sohan Pal Singh v. State of U.P. — excessive bill relegated to Clause 6.5(b)
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: excessive-bill alternative remedy
cases.holding: Where a consumer disputes an electricity bill as excessive, including charges for a period of disconnection, Clause 6.5(b) of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is the statutory alternative remedy. The High Court will not, in the first instance, examine the correctness of the bill. The writ petition is dismissed with liberty to avail that remedy.

cases.title: Bhoop Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: excessive-billing
cases.holding: Where a consumer disputes an electricity bill as highly excessive, including for a period of disconnection, Clause 6.5(b) of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is the statutory alternative remedy. The High Court will not examine the correctness of the bill in the first instance and will dismiss the writ with liberty to avail that remedy.

cases.title: Poshaki Lal v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: excessive bill — alternative remedy
cases.holding: Where the consumer disputes an electricity bill as excessive, including charges for a disconnection period, Clause 6.5(b) of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005 furnishes a statutory alternative remedy, and the High Court will not in the first instance examine the correctness of the bill; the writ is dismissed with liberty to avail that remedy.

cases.title: Daya Shanker v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: excessive-bill-dispute
cases.holding: Where the consumer disputes the entire bill as excessive, including charges for a period of disconnection, Clause 6.5(b) of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005 furnishes a statutory alternative remedy, and the writ court will not in the first instance examine the correctness of the bill.

cases.title: Hetram v. State of U.P. — excessive bill writ dismissed for Clause 6.5(b) remedy
cases.topic: excessive bill — statutory alternative remedy
cases.holding: Clause 6.5(b) of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is a statutory alternative remedy for a consumer disputing an excessive electricity bill; the High Court will not examine the correctness of such a bill in the first instance, and the writ is dismissed with liberty to avail that remedy.

cases.title: Chandra Pal v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-accuracy complaint; statutory remedy
cases.holding: A consumer disputing the accuracy of any bill has a statutory remedy under paragraph 6.5(b): pay under protest the lesser of the amount claimed or charges calculated on the average of the preceding six months' bills, and file a complaint with the competent authority before the due date. Where that remedy is available, the writ court will not decide the billing dispute (here, whether a private tube-well motor's approved 5 H.P. load was wrongly billed as 10 H.P.) and will relegate the consumer to opposite party no. 3, directing a complaint within two weeks for disposal in accordance with law within four weeks.

cases.title: Smt. Badam Shree v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: time-bound decision of 6.5(b) objection on deposit
cases.holding: Subject to the consumer depositing the amount contemplated by clause 6.5(b) of the Supply Code, 2005, the competent authority shall consider and decide the consumer's objection or complaint under that clause within six weeks of the deposit. The writ is disposed of on that direction without adjudicating the bill or ordering restoration.

cases.title: Ram Prasad v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill-accuracy-complaint
cases.holding: Where the consumer disputes the accuracy of the electricity bill and recovery of outstanding dues, the proper forum is a complaint before the Executive Engineer under clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. A second writ repeating the same billing grievance after an earlier disposal with liberty to complain under clause 6.5(b) will not be entertained; the petitioner remains free to approach the Executive Engineer.

cases.title: M/s Laxmi Oil Mill v. Awdhesh Kumar Shukla, Executive Engineer
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: clause 6.5(b) compliance on disputed bill
cases.holding: On a contempt listing arising from a disputed bill of Rs.1,53,502, the Court recorded that counsel was unable to satisfy it that clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 had been complied with, granted further time to study the Code, and later passed the matter over on an illness slip, without deciding contempt or the bill.

cases.title: Smt. Sahil Devi v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: liberty to approach 6.5(b) authority
cases.holding: Where the consumer does not press a writ and seeks liberty to approach the concerned authority under clause 6.5(b) of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 for similar relief, the petition is disposed of as not pressed with that liberty.

cases.title: Smt. Vijay Kumari Srivastava v. Purvanchal Electricity Distribution Corporation Ltd.
cases.topic: not-pressed writ; liberty to consumer grievance forum
cases.holding: The writ petition was disposed of as not pressed, with liberty to the petitioner to take a remedy under clause 6.5(b) of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, raising the same challenge as in the writ. The Court made clear that it had not examined the merits.

cases.title: Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P. — recovery of vendor's electricity dues
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: objection-to-recovery-citation
cases.holding: On the licensee's stand that an objection to a recovery demand lies under paragraph 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, the writ was disposed of with liberty to file that objection within four weeks; the licensee was directed to decide it by a speaking and reasoned order within a further four weeks, the Court expressing no opinion on merits.

cases.title: Sophiya Khan @ Safi Ahamad Khan v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: disputed-bills
cases.holding: Writ interference with an electricity recovery certificate is refused where the consumer has not invoked clause 6.5(b) by paying under protest (the claimed sum or six-month average, whichever is less) and filing a complaint with the competent authority before the due date.

cases.title: Smt. Mamata Verma v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.topic: Clause 6.5(b) is a self-contained mechanism for bill-accuracy disputes; writ not entertained
cases.holding: Relegate to Clause 6.5(b). That clause is a self-contained full-fledged mechanism: pay under protest the sum claimed or the six-month-average charges (whichever is less) and complain to the competent authority before the due date; the complaint is to be decided within seven days, a revised bill issued within seven days with no late-payment surcharge (and timely-payment rebate) if the complaint is correct, or the original bill enforced with surcharge if incorrect. As a statutory forum was available, the Court did not entertain the writ and dismissed it on the ground of alternative remedy, leaving the petitioner to invoke Clause 6.5(b).

cases.title: Gul Mohammad v. U.P. Power Corporation and 2 Others
cases.topic: Bill-accuracy dispute pursued via the Clause 6.5(b) pay-under-protest-and-complain mechanism; recovery stayed
cases.holding: Clause 6.5(b) provides the remedy: the consumer may pay under protest either the sum claimed or the six-month-average charges (whichever is less) and complain to the competent authority (here the Executive Engineer / respondent no. 2), the complaint to be decided within seven days. The Court directed that, on such a representation with deposit of the six-month-average charges, it be decided within seven days, and stayed recovery under the demand notice until its disposal.

cases.title: Parvati Devi v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Another
cases.topic: Writ court will not examine an LPS challenge on a revised bill if the consumer refuses to deposit the undisputed billed amount
cases.holding: The Court did not decide Clause 6.5(b)(i). It had narrowed the controversy to the surcharge of Rs. 2,24,241.30 and directed deposit of the difference (Rs. 1,44,253) as a precondition to looking into the surcharge, with the licensee to disclose particulars of the 21.03.2025 disconnection memo. The petitioner refused to deposit, recasting the case as a demand for permanent disconnection. The Court would not be drawn into a dispute on the billed amount and dismissed the writ.
cases.flag: Clause 6.5(b)(i) is indexed because it was the consumer's surcharge ground; this order is not a construction of that sub-clause.

cases.title: Sharafat Ulla (since deceased) v. Purvanchal Vidhut Vitrana Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: Seven-day late-payment-surcharge holiday after bill revision — inapplicable to persistent defaulter
cases.holding: Clause 6.5(b)(i) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 makes only a small allowance: on revision of a bill upon the consumer's objection, seven days are allowed for payment, and late payment surcharge does not run in that interval. The petitioner's case is not of that kind. He is a persistent defaulter. The Court declined to interfere. Writ petition dismissed.

cases.title: Prema Devi v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
