cases.topic: Admitted commercial billing of a domestic-load connection — single bill without surcharge
cases.holding: Where the licensee admits that a consumer with domestic-category load was kept under commercial categorization, the Court will order generation of one bill from the last fully-paid date to date on the readings of all meters, treating the connection as domestic and without surcharge, giving the benefit of clause 6.5(b)(i). Compliance within three weeks of communication of a certified copy to the Executive Engineer.

cases.title: M/S Shivam Rice Mill v. U.P. Electricity Regulatory Commission
cases.topic: complaint-handling
cases.holding: Where a consumer has dispatched a complaint under clause 6.5(b), the writ court may dispose of the petition by directing the concerned respondent to consider the complaint and inform the petitioner of the decision within a fixed time of communication of the order and complaint, without deciding the merits.

cases.title: Managing Director, D.V.V. Nigam Ltd. & 2 Others v. Sri Kartar Singh & Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: Non-exhaustion of Clause 6.5(b) is a technical ground; not a basis to set aside a CGRF billing order after long delay
cases.holding: Not so as to warrant interference after long delay. The only contention in the writ was that the complaint was not maintainable and was premature for want of a Clause 6.5(b) objection. The consumer's case before the Forum was that he had repeatedly approached the Executive Engineer's office. The dispute is of 2013 and nearly twelve years have passed. The licensees failed to show how the Forum's order is illegal on merits. It is not in the interest of justice to interfere solely on technical grounds after a substantial lapse of time.

cases.title: Petitioner v. Managing Director, Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
cases.topic: billing complaint; alternate remedy
cases.holding: A consumer who disputes the accuracy of a bill must proceed under paragraph 6.5(b) of the Supply Code, 2005: pay under protest the amount claimed or the average of the preceding six months' bills, whichever is less, and file a complaint with the competent authority. The writ was disposed of with a direction to lodge that complaint within ten days with the Code deposit; the Executive Engineer is to pass a reasoned order within ten days thereafter, and the impugned recovery remains in abeyance for four weeks or until that decision.

cases.title: Rizwan v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing complaint / disputed bill
cases.holding: A consumer aggrieved by an electricity bill may file an objection under Regulation 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the writ court will not decide the bill on merits and will instead require the concerned authority to decide that objection expeditiously in accordance with law.

cases.title: Matloob v. Managing Director, Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: appeal against assessment; alternate remedy
cases.holding: Where an assessment is raised on a finding that the electricity meter was tampered, a consumer who accepts the liability and seeks only to pay in instalments still has a statutory appeal against the assessment under Clause 6.5.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the writ court will not interfere.
cases.flag: Court cited 'Clause 651.14' of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; read as 6.5.14 (assessment appeal). Meter tampering may engage cl. 6.8 (theft) rather than cl. 6.5 (unauthorized use); not classified. The writ (Writ-C 22089/2018) is dismissed in terms calling it 'the appeal'.

UP-2005::6.5B.topic: Dispute over the quantum of a demand notice is relegated to the authority under Clause 6.5B

cases.title: Madarsa Dargah Aaliya Islamiya Shareef Nagar & Anr. v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.topic: Dispute over the quantum of a demand notice is relegated to the authority under Clause 6.5B
cases.holding: The consumer is permitted to approach the authority concerned under Clause 6.5B of the Code, which must examine the objection raised as to quantification and pass a reasoned order within six weeks of presentation of a certified copy of the court's order.

UP-2005::6.7.topic: Late payment surcharge — not leviable on a Liquidator who had no funds and was not a defaulter

cases.title: U.P. State Cement Corporation Ltd. (In Liquidation), In re
cases.topic: Late payment surcharge — not leviable on a Liquidator who had no funds and was not a defaulter
cases.holding: No. Late payment surcharge is part of the statutory tariff, but it presupposes a defaulting consumer. The Official Liquidator had no money in the company's account until the assets were realised and could raise no dispute, so there was no default or wilful non-payment by the OL or the Court. The actual bills (in the supplementary affidavit) are admitted to proof, but the large late-payment-surcharge component is excluded.

cases.title: M/s Tej International Pvt. Ltd. v. U.P. Power Corporation
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: assessment-appeal-reasons
cases.holding: The appellate order dated 26.3.2004 dismissing the petitioner's challenge to the unauthorized-use assessment without assigning any reason is an order of non-application of mind. Administrative authorities are duty bound to record reasons; without them the consumer cannot assail the illegality in further proceedings. The writ is allowed, that order is quashed, and the appeal is remanded to the appellate authority to decide on merits after full opportunity and detailed reasons within three months of production of a certified copy.
cases.flag: Court applied Electricity Supply Code, 2002 cl. 6.20 to the assessment, not 2005 numbering.

cases.title: Om Sons India Handicraft Manufacturers & Others v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.topic: surcharge-levyability-remitted-to-executive-engineer
cases.holding: No. The Court recorded the Clause 6.7 hearing contention and the unnamed Supreme Court argument that surcharge was not levyable, but did not decide either. Because no counter affidavit had been filed and the 2006 writ had long been pending, it remitted the applications dated 30.10.2006 and 3.11.2006 to the concerned Executive Engineer. If those applications were not traceable, the petitioners could move a fresh representation within a month; any such representation was to be decided within two months of a certified copy of the order and the representation. The petition was disposed of with that observation.
cases.flag: Petitioner treated Clause 6.7 as requiring a hearing before surcharge; Clause 6.7 is the late-payment surcharge provision, not a hearing clause. The Court said 'Be that as it may' and did not construe 6.7. Source PDF concatenates six 2017 listing/adjournment orders (illness slips; showing Power Corporation counsel) with this 19.7.2017 disposal. Docket styles the first petitioner 'Manfufacturers'.

UP-2005::6.8.topic: Reasonable opportunity of hearing before a theft-based final assessment; procedural defect condoned where opportunity was in substance given

cases.title: Lalit Kumar Kapoor v. Kanpur Electricity Supply Company & Anr.
cases.topic: Reasonable opportunity of hearing before a theft-based final assessment; procedural defect condoned where opportunity was in substance given
cases.holding: Reasonable opportunity of hearing in a theft assessment is governed by Clauses 6.8(b)(i), 6.8(c)(iii) read with 8.1(b) of the Code (citing Khem Chand v. Union of India and Transmission Corporation of A.P. v. Sri Rama Krishna Rice Mill on the nature of 'reasonable opportunity'). Provisional assessment, reply, and final assessment together form a single process reaching finality; where the authority afforded an opportunity for hearing (including through consideration of a representation directed by an earlier writ order) before making the final assessment, any procedural defect at the provisional stage is condoned, since procedural law cannot override the substantive law.

cases.title: Latif v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.topic: Mandatory Clause 6.8 procedure for unauthorised-use assessment; bypassing it via the 1958 Recovery of Dues Act is illegal
cases.holding: No. Following Ashok Kumar & Others v. State of U.P., Clause 6.8 requires: (a) a site inspection report disclosing the irregularity, handed to the consumer or pasted/posted if refused; (b) a show-cause notice with the provisional assessment, giving 15 working days for reply and fixing a hearing date; and (c) after personal hearing, a speaking final order within 7 working days recording whether unauthorised use is established and the assessed amount. Since no such show-cause notice was issued and no final order under Clause 6.8(c) was passed, a bill-cum-notice and demand notice issued instead under Section 5 of the 1958 Act is illegal and inconsistent with the prescribed procedure; it is set aside, without prejudice to the licensee proceeding afresh in accordance with the Clause 6.8/Ashok Kumar procedure.

cases.title: M/S Kissan Chilling Udyog & Anr. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.topic: A theft assessment resting on a misreading of the checking report (conflating the main meter and a separately-installed double/test meter) cannot sustain
cases.holding: No. Following Ashok Kumar's Clause 6.8 procedure (inspection report, 15-working-day show-cause notice, hearing, speaking final order), the impugned orders were quashed for two independent defects: (1) no valid Clause 6.8 notice/final order was issued disclosing the manner of the alleged unauthorised use or the basis for the assessed quantum, and (2) the notice and final order misread the checking report by attributing tampering ('all seals found tempered') to the main meter and treating the double meter's contents as equally condemnatory, when the checking report showed the body-seal defect recorded only for the main meter and the foreign device only inside the double meter (installed by the respondents themselves to test the main meter, under no averred common sealing certificate) — a misreading respondent's own counsel conceded justified remand. The Assessing Authority was given liberty to reassess afresh strictly per Clause 6.8 and Ashok Kumar.

cases.title: M/S Modern Rice Mill v. MVVNL & Anr.
cases.topic: A Section 126 assessment (being penal/fiscal-preventive) cannot include dues not contemplated by the statute (e.g. electricity duty), and minimum-charge liability during disconnection requires fault attributable to the consumer
cases.holding: Since a Section 126/Clause 6.8 assessment amount is expressly excluded from computation of the consumer's monthly/annual charge liability, the assessment being penal in scope cannot be enlarged to add other dues (here, electricity duty) not contemplated by the statute. Separately, minimum consumption/guarantee charges for a period of disconnection can be demanded only where the disconnection is attributable to the consumer's own fault (e.g. an established theft justifying disconnection); where the fault (or its absence) is unresolved, the licensee cannot claim such charges, and the billing authority must determine responsibility for the disconnection before raising the demand.

cases.title: M/S Sartaj Rice Mill Thru' Its Partner Maqsood Ali v. Paschimanchal Vidhyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.topic: An assessment accepted by the consumer's own offer to pay in instalments becomes final/binding; opportunity of hearing was satisfied where the consumer was present but failed to substantiate his objection, and an adjournment could not override a court-mandated deadline
cases.holding: No. The consumer's own written offer (19.10.2001) to pay the assessed dues in instalments, accepted by the Executive Engineer with restoration of supply, rendered the earlier assessments final by his own conduct; a subsequent, undisputed third notice (based on actual meter inspection reports) stood in the same position. Para 3.1, Chapter 7 of the Commercial and Revenue Manual (read with Clause 6.8(c)(i) of the Code) required an opportunity of hearing before assessment/recovery, which was afforded pursuant to this Court's earlier order directing disposal of the consumer's 04.05.2005 objection within four weeks; the consumer was present at the hearing but failed to produce the documents (copy of his representation/receipt) he claimed supported his case, and his advocate's illness-based adjournment request on the last available date could not be granted without breaching the court's deadline. No ex parte order or breach of natural justice was made out.

cases.title: M/S Urmila Oil Industries v. U.P. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam & Ors.
cases.topic: An assessment based on mere 'possibility of theft' inferred from an MRI pattern, without Clause 6.8 procedure or reasoned analysis, cannot be sustained
cases.holding: No. The impugned notice itself stated only that the consumer's system 'has given rise to a possibility of direct theft of electricity' from the recorded nil night-time load; no specific reason was given for how the authorities concluded theft had occurred, nor was the manner of assessment disclosed, nor was the Clause 6.8 show-cause procedure followed. The consumer's explanation (that a transformer protection device disconnected supply at night as a safety measure during non-production hours) was rejected as 'unsatisfactory and illogical' without reasoned engagement. Following Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P., the assessment and demand were set aside for non-compliance with Section 126 read with Clause 6.8, with liberty to the Assessing Authority to pass a fresh order in accordance with law.

cases.title: Mohd Usman Ansari v. Chairman, Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Ltd. & 4 Others
cases.topic: A recovery certificate founded on an ex-parte provisional s.126 assessment, issued without following the Supply Code's assessment procedure, entitles the consumer to a hearing and a reasoned final assessment before coercive recovery
cases.holding: The Court directed that an opportunity of hearing be granted to the petitioner, with a final assessment to be carried out by the authorities within 12 weeks; until the final assessment order is passed, no coercive recovery measures may be taken against the petitioner.

cases.title: Mrs Rajendra Kumar Sharma v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.topic: A s.126 final assessment order that does not address the consumer's objections, fix a hearing date, or record theft findings breaches Clauses 6.8/8.1; the recovery citation founded on it must be withdrawn and a fresh assessment made after due notice and hearing
cases.holding: No — the licensee's own two-member inquiry committee found that Clauses 6.8 and 8.1 of the Supply Code had not been followed by the assessing Executive Engineer; the recovery citation founded on the impugned final assessment was directed to be cancelled, a fresh notice with objections and a hearing was issued, disciplinary show-cause proceedings were initiated against the officer, and a fresh final assessment order was to be passed within ten days. Pending that fresh assessment, the Court directed restoration of electricity supply on the petitioner depositing Rs. 25,00,000/- as security, subject to the outcome of the fresh assessment.

cases.title: M/S Om Ice Factory v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.topic: objections-to-provisional-assessment
cases.holding: Where a consumer has not yet objected to a provisional assessment notice, a writ seeking to quash that notice on alleged breaches of clauses 6.8 and 8.1 of the Supply Code, 2005, and on the assessment formula, is not decided on merits; the consumer may submit objections within the time allowed, which the assessing authority is to consider before finalising the assessment in accordance with law.

cases.title: Sadhana Mittal — demand notice relegated to Supply Code objection remedy
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: statutory remedy — objections to electricity bill or charges
cases.holding: Under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 the consumer has a statutory remedy of raising objections against an electricity bill or electricity charges; where that remedy is available, the writ court will not examine the demand and will leave the petitioner to avail it. The petition was disposed of with that observation.
cases.flag: Court cited the Supply Code 2005 generally for objections to bill/charges; clause 6.8 is inferred, not numbered in the order.

cases.title: Sandeep Kesarwani v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.topic: A final assessment order passed more than two years after the provisional assessment notice, without affording a fresh opportunity to object, violates natural justice and is liable to be set aside notwithstanding an available s.127 appellate remedy, where the assessing officer's jurisdiction itself is challenged
cases.holding: Section 126(3) contemplates a final assessment ordinarily within 30 days of the provisional assessment order; where, as here, more than two years elapsed between the provisional assessment notice (23.5.2011) and the final assessment order (21.6.2013) with no fresh notice or opportunity given, the final assessment order cannot be said to have been passed in consonance with natural justice, notwithstanding the petitioner's failure to object to the original provisional notice and the availability of an appeal under s.127. The recovery citation was set aside, and the petitioner was directed to file objections to the (revived) provisional assessment notice within 15 days, with the Executive Engineer to pass a fresh final assessment decision within one month, leaving the respondents free to proceed further in accordance with law thereafter.

cases.title: Sanjay Rizvi v. M.D. Kanpur Electricity Supply Co. & Others
cases.topic: A provisional assessment for alleged unauthorised use/theft, made without authentic verification data (e.g. MRI testing of the seized meter, despite the licensee's own procedure contemplating it and a specific court direction to obtain instructions on it), and without full compliance with the Clause 6.8 hearing procedure, is impugnable; the consumer is relegated to a fresh, properly-conducted departmental assessment process with preserved appeal rights, rather than a writ-court determination of the underlying factual dispute
cases.holding: The provisional assessment notice did not appear to have an authentic evidentiary basis; Clause 6.8 of the Supply Code requires that before concluding unauthorised use of electricity, the consumer be given an opportunity (inspection report communicated, show-cause notice with objections invited, personal hearing, then a speaking final order) — a requirement rooted in natural justice given the serious, offence-adjacent nature of the allegation. Given that an equally efficacious alternative remedy exists and the underlying factual/technical controversy (correctness of the alleged theft-detection method, given the absence of MRI verification) is better assessed by persons with technical expertise than by the writ court, the petition was disposed of by directing the petitioner to file a fresh representation (annexing the writ petition) before the licensee, to be decided by a reasoned, speaking order after a hearing addressing whether unauthorised use is established; if established, a final assessment order was to follow (for the full period per Clause 6.8(c)(iii)), appealable under s.127 read with Clause 6.8(d).

cases.title: Swati Kakkar v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited And Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: wrong-assessment alternative remedy
cases.holding: If the grievance is a wrong assessment, Clause 6.8 of the Code and the appeal provided in assessment matters must be exhausted before a writ is entertained.

cases.title: Gulajar Ahmad v. Executive Engineer, KESCO, Kanpur Nagar
cases.topic: relegation of reconnection and assessment after theft allegation
cases.holding: Without examining the merits, a writ seeking a direction to decide an application for reconnection and restoration of an LMV-2 connection, in a matter involving a theft allegation, an FIR, and pending assessment of charges, was disposed of by directing the competent authority under section 126 of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with clause 6.8 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 to decide the application preferably within two months of production of a certified copy.

cases.title: Vimal Gupta v. Executive Engineer, Dakshinanchal Electricity Dist. Nigam
cases.topic: A consumer challenging a provisional unauthorised-use assessment must pursue the Supply Code's own adjudicatory mechanism on the merits; pending that challenge, reconnection may be conditioned on deposit of 50% of the disputed demand as an equitable interim measure
cases.holding: The Court declined to adjudicate the merits, holding that the Supply Code, 2005 provides a detailed mechanism for adjudication and disposal of unauthorised-use assessment disputes which the petitioner must follow if he wishes to challenge the assessment. With the consent of both parties, the writ petition was disposed of with a direction that the petitioner deposit 50% of the total disputed amount within two weeks, upon which the licensee would consider the reconnection request in accordance with law, with expedition.

cases.title: Rustam Sahi v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: provisional assessment and objection after theft inspection
cases.holding: Where theft of electricity is found on a surprise inspection, provisional assessment is made under Clause 6.8 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and the consumer may object under the same clause. If the consumer has raised an objection before the competent authority, that authority shall examine all issues while making the final assessment. The writ was disposed of with that direction and without deciding the objection on the merits.
cases.flag: wrong_clause: Clause 6.8 (UUE) applied to theft; theft assessment is 8.1-8.2

cases.title: M/s Meher Chandra Sewal Das Rais Mill v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: uue-assessment-procedure-and-s127-appeal
cases.holding: Clause 6.8 is a complete unauthorised-use assessment procedure: site inspection and report under 6.8(a), notice requiring objections to the charges and provisional assessment under 6.8(b)(ii), and personal hearing followed by a speaking order under 6.8(c)(i) on whether unauthorised use is established and on quantum. The Assessing Officer's prima facie conclusion must be communicated to the consumer. Because an equally efficacious remedy exists, the writ is disposed without examining the ₹7,73,525 notice. The petitioners shall deposit ₹2,00,000 within two weeks; on that token deposit the connection shall be restored. The assessing authority shall decide the representation by a reasoned order after hearing and, if unauthorised use is established, pass a final assessment for the entire period of such use subject to the limitation in Clause 6.8(c)(iii). An appeal then lies within 30 days under Section 127 read with Clause 6.8(d).

cases.title: Ashok Kumar & Ors. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.topic: Mandatory Clause 6.8 procedure before an unauthorised-use assessment
cases.holding: No. Clause 6.8 requires the details/evidence substantiating unauthorised use to be recorded in the inspection report and stated in the assessment notice and order (6.8(a)(iv),(v)), 15 working days for reply (6.8(b)(i)), a fixed date on which the consumer is heard in person (6.8(b)(ii)), and a final order of assessment (6.8(c)) before a demand notice issues. Here the MRI report/findings were not shown to the consumers, the notice merely recited that theft/irregularities were found and gave seven days, and no final order preceded the s.3 demand. The provisional notices are wholly illegal for non-compliance with Clause 6.8 read with s.126.

cases.title: Kamil v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.topic: Mandatory Clause 6.8 procedure for a UUE assessment; bare deposit-demand notice is illegal
cases.holding: No. Clause 6.8 requires a site inspection report indicating conclusive evidence of UUE handed to the consumer (6.8(a)), a provisional assessment bill with a show-cause notice giving 15 working days to reply and a fixed date of hearing (6.8(b)), a personal hearing, and a speaking order on whether UUE is established and the quantum (6.8(c)). The notice dated 29.7.2005 offered no opportunity to object and fixed no hearing, merely demanding a deposit within seven days, and no final assessment order preceded the s.3 (1958 Act) demand. The entire procedure was de hors s.126 and Clause 6.8; the impugned order and the s.3 demand notice are quashed, with liberty to issue a fresh, compliant provisional assessment notice.

cases.title: Smt. Archana Prahladika v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: unauthorised use — writ not to try merits; restoration on 50% deposit
cases.holding: The U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 puts in place a detailed mechanism for adjudication of disputes over provisional assessment for unauthorised extraction of electricity, and that procedure must be followed if the consumer wishes to challenge the assessment on merits. A writ against such a demand was disposed of by consent directing deposit of 50% of the amount claimed within two weeks, after which the licensee may consider restoration of supply in accordance with law.
cases.flag: Order invokes the Code generally, without a clause number; keyed as 6.8 (unauthorised use / provisional assessment / 50% deposit for restoration).

cases.title: Suresh Kumar v. U.P. Power Corporation, Shakti Bhawan, Lucknow & Others
cases.topic: A 'provisional assessment' with no calculation or amount is not a valid provisional assessment
cases.holding: No. Such a document does not contain any calculation of the provisional assessment nor mention the amount assessed, and so cannot be a provisional assessment as contemplated by s.126 of the Act and the Code. The purported final assessment is therefore to be treated as the provisional assessment, and the consumer's objections must be decided by a speaking order after a reasonable opportunity of hearing; recovery under the citation stays meanwhile and abides that decision.

cases.title: Rakesh v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.topic: No recovery without a final assessment; provisional notice must conform to Clause 6.8 and Ashok Kumar
cases.holding: No. In the absence of any final order of assessment, no question of recovery arises; and the provisional assessment notice was not in conformity with Ashok Kumar and Clause 6.8 of the Code. The licensee must issue a fresh provisional assessment notice conforming to Ashok Kumar and Clause 6.8, give adequate opportunity of reply and oral hearing, and pass a speaking order; recovery stays suspended until then and abides the final assessment.

cases.title: Malti Devi v. Dakshinanchal Vidhut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: uue-objection-alternate-remedy
cases.holding: Where the allegation arising from a premises check is unauthorised use of electricity, clause 6.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 supplies the remedy of an objection against the Inspector’s assessment. A writ of mandamus to set aside the checking report is not entertained until that objection is filed; if filed, it is to be heard and disposed of in accordance with law.

cases.title: Dharam Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: theft-recovery-citation-remand-to-ee
cases.holding: Where a recovery citation for alleged theft dues after provisional assessment was challenged as issued without notice or Clause 6.8 assessment procedure, the Court did not examine whether the Code had been followed. It directed the petitioner to file his objection before the Executive Engineer (respondent no. 3) within ten days, the EE to examine the claim and pass an appropriate order within three weeks thereafter, and the recovery proceedings to abide that order, and disposed of the writ.

cases.title: Sunil Yadav v. State of U.P. (Clause 6.8 assessment — objections directed)
cases.topic: objections-to-provisional-assessment
cases.holding: Where a consumer challenges a consumption-bill assessment as having been made without following Clause 6.8—no proper provisional assessment and no final order after opportunity to object—and the licensee treats the provisional assessment as final for want of timely objection, the High Court may, without deciding those contentions, direct the consumer to file objections before the assessing officer, who shall pass an appropriate order in accordance with law, with recovery to abide that order, leaving any remaining grievance to an appeal under Section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003.
cases.flag: Court referred to 'Section 127 of the U.P. Electricity Act, 2003'; the appeal lies under s.127 of the Electricity Act, 2003.

cases.title: Ashok Kumar Awasthi v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: objections to provisional theft assessment; recovery to abide assessing order
cases.holding: On a challenge to joint recovery of two alleged theft assessments as violating Clause 6.8, the Court directed the consumer to file objections within ten days and the assessing officer to pass an appropriate order in accordance with law, with recovery proceedings to abide that order.

cases.title: Shiv Sharma v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: alternative-remedy-appeal
cases.holding: Assessment of electricity dues and theft of electric energy are separate: a final report, or a finding that a theft charge is not worth prosecuting, does not mean the consumer is not liable to pay assessed dues. A demand notice said to be incorrect or illegal may be challenged by appeal under Paragraph 6.8 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the writ was dismissed on that alternative remedy.

cases.title: M/s Meher Chandra Sewal Das Rice Mill v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: pending unauthorised-use final assessment — time-bound speaking order
cases.holding: Where a prior writ had directed a reasoned decision on unauthorised use of electricity and a final assessment if established, and the consumer had deposited the token amount, but no final order had been passed, the assessing officer shall, after the consumer appears with objections and evidence, pass a speaking final order within 45 days; coercive action is stayed for that period or until disposal of the objections, whichever is earlier. The subsequent notice is not quashed on merits.

cases.title: Riyazuddin v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: objections to provisional assessment
cases.holding: A consumer aggrieved by a provisional assessment of electricity dues has a right under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 to file objections; final assessment is made only after those objections are considered. The writ is disposed with liberty to object within two weeks, the Executive Engineer to pass the final assessment expeditiously in accordance with law (if possible within a month). A separate representation for restoration of supply, if moved, shall be considered by the Executive Engineer by a speaking order.
cases.flag: Court cited the 2005 Code generally, without numbering 6.8; 6.8 is the Code’s provisional/final assessment scheme.

cases.title: Jamshed Ali v. State of U.P. and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: objection before Executive Engineer against electricity dues recovery
cases.holding: A consumer facing recovery of electricity dues has a remedy of filing an objection before the Executive Engineer under clause 6.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ was disposed of with a direction that if such objection is filed within three weeks, the Executive Engineer shall consider and decide it in accordance with law within one month, and that no coercive step shall be taken on the recovery citation until that decision.

cases.title: Gyani Singh v. State of U.P. and Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: theft-notice-alternate-remedy-objection
cases.holding: A discrepancy between the inspection date in a theft-of-electricity notice and that in the FIR is for the Executive Engineer to decide. The petitioner’s remedy is to file an objection under Part 6.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; a writ to compel decision of a representation is not entertained when that objection is available.
cases.flag: Court applied Part 6.8 (UUE objection procedure) to a theft-of-electricity notice; catalog hit clause-8.1-8.2-govern-theft-assessment-not-6.8. Clause number not silently corrected.

cases.title: Mukul Pandey v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: mandatory provisional assessment notice and hearing before final assessment and recovery
cases.holding: Clause 6.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 must be strictly followed for making an assessment, including in a case of theft of electricity. Where nothing on record shows that a provisional assessment notice was issued or that the consumer was given an opportunity to object and to be heard, the final assessment and the consequential recovery are illegal. The demand is quashed; the licensee may prepare a fresh provisional assessment, serve it, consider objections with reasons, and then pass a final assessment in light of Ashok Kumar.

cases.title: Ram Prakash Yadav v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.topic: Unproved service + no recorded satisfaction of theft = denial of Clause 6.8(b) opportunity
cases.holding: No. Sending the provisional assessment by registered post, with nothing to show it was received and no positive reply on the method of service, means the consumer was denied the Clause 6.8(b) opportunity to reply and object; further, the provisional assessment gave no basis for the amount and the assessing authority did not record its satisfaction that theft was committed. Treating the unanswered provisional assessment as final and issuing a recovery certificate was therefore illegal; the demand and consequential proceedings are quashed and a fresh Code-compliant assessment (per Ashok Kumar) directed.

cases.title: Yogendra Singh v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitaran Nigam Ltd. & 3 Others
cases.topic: Unproved service + no recorded satisfaction of theft = denial of Clause 6.8(b) opportunity
cases.holding: No. Sending the provisional assessment by registered post, with nothing to show it was received and no positive reply on the method of service, means the consumer was denied the Clause 6.8(b) opportunity to reply and object; further, the provisional assessment gave no basis for the amount and the assessing authority did not record its satisfaction that theft was committed. Treating the unanswered provisional assessment as final and issuing a recovery certificate was therefore illegal; the demand and consequential proceedings are quashed and a fresh Code-compliant assessment (per Ashok Kumar) directed.

cases.title: Bharat Bhati v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.topic: Writ against a Clause 6.8(B) show-cause / provisional assessment notice is premature
cases.holding: No. Such a writ is premature; the consumer has ample opportunity to take all his pleas — including tenancy of the premises and the correct assessment period — before the appropriate authority. On the consumer filing objections within 15 days, the authority must decide them by a speaking order in accordance with law.

cases.title: Ram Bahadur v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.topic: The 365-day assessment period is a fallback, not a default; actual period must be determined
cases.holding: No. Under s.126(5) and Clause 6.8(c)(iii)/Annexure 6.3, the assessment is for the entire period of unauthorised use, and the 365-day period (criterion 'D') applies only when, on recorded satisfaction, the actual period cannot be ascertained. Here the connection was granted on 14.4.2015 and the use detected on 3.6.2015, so the period was ascertainable (at most from the date of connection); assessing 365 days mechanically — reaching back before the connection existed — without recorded satisfaction is patently erroneous. Assessment and recovery quashed; fresh assessment directed.

cases.title: Bhajan Lal and Anr. v. Executive Engineer, Electricity Distribution Khand-1, U.P. and Ors.
cases.topic: Provisional-assessment bill and show-cause notice must be served under proper receipt by an authentic mode; ordinary post insufficient
cases.holding: Ordinary post does not suffice. Clause 6.8(b) requires service of the provisional-assessment bill with a show-cause notice 'under proper receipt', giving 15 clear working days for reply and fixing a hearing; the assessing authority must ensure actual service by registered post and personal service simultaneously and, if both fail, by newspaper publication (after which it may proceed ex parte). Sending notice by ordinary post raises no presumption of service; non-compliance violates natural justice (Article 14) and vitiates the assessment. The Court directed the Chairman, U.P. Power Corporation to issue a circular ensuring such service.

cases.title: M/s Sangam Crusher Works & Another v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.topic: Once theft/UUE is not made out, the s.126 assessment (which the Court keyed to Clause 6.8) is unsustainable, and a s.127 order that affirms by a finding contrary to the inspection report is set aside
cases.holding: No. The second issue was framed as whether the assessment accorded with s.126 read with Clause 6.8. Because no unauthorised use was established, the s.126 assessment is unsustainable. The appellate authority failed to consider the grounds of appeal; its observation that the 17.12.2022 report recorded an energised 11 kV line with the jumper duly connected is contrary to that report (Annexure-9). Final assessment dated 05.07.2023 and the appellate order dated 14.03.2024 are set aside. Writ allowed. No costs. No remand.
cases.flag: The Court keyed issue (2) to Clause 6.8 but did not construe 6.8(a)–(c) (inspection report, 15-working-day notice, hearing, speaking order). The holding is that the assessment falls because UUE is not proved, not a free-standing construction of the Clause 6.8 procedure. Compounding (a s.135/s.152 incident) sat on a s.126 assessment; not separately analysed. Licensee's s.126(5) 12-month default period was not reached.

cases.title: M/s K.G.N. Stone Crusher Mill & Another v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.topic: Once theft/UUE is not made out, the s.126 assessment (which the Court keyed to Clause 6.8) is unsustainable, and a s.127 order that affirms by a finding contrary to the inspection report is set aside
cases.holding: No. The second issue was framed as whether the assessment accorded with s.126 read with Clause 6.8. Because no unauthorised use was established, the s.126 assessment is unsustainable. The appellate authority failed to consider the grounds of appeal; its observation that the 17.12.2022 report recorded an energised 11 kV line with the jumper duly connected is contrary to that report (Annexure-9). Final assessment dated 05.07.2023 and the appellate order dated 14.03.2024 are set aside. Writ allowed. No costs. No remand.
cases.flag: As in SCJ-285: the Court keyed issue (2) to Clause 6.8 but did not construe 6.8(a)–(c). The holding is that the assessment falls because UUE is not proved. Compounding (a s.135/s.152 incident) sat on a s.126 assessment; not separately analysed. Licensee's s.126(5) 12-month default period was not reached.

cases.title: Vishal Singh Batra v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: Alternative remedy — liberty to press cl. 6.8 after infructuous writ
cases.holding: On non-appearance of the petitioner the writ was dismissed as infructuous by efflux of time and any interim order was vacated. Without examining the merits, the Court recorded that cl. 6.8 of the Supply Code is an efficacious remedy and granted liberty to press relief under that clause if the petitioner feels the matter survives.

cases.title: Afzal Khan v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: hearing before final assessment
cases.holding: Where the licensee withdraws the recovery certificate and issues a fresh notice fixing a hearing, a writ seeking final assessment under clauses 6.8 and 8.1 is disposed of with a direction to grant the consumer an opportunity of hearing and thereafter pass a reasoned order in accordance with law within eight weeks.

cases.title: Sandeep Tiwari v. Executive Engineer, Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: recovery without final assessment
cases.holding: Recovery notices issued without a final assessment order under clause 6.8 of the Supply Code, 2005 cannot be sustained. On the licensee's concession that no final assessment had been passed, both citations were quashed; the consumer is to appear for personal hearing, after which the authority may pass a final assessment in accordance with law.
cases.flag: Petitioner cited clause 6.8(1)(b); the Code's 6.8 is not numbered as (1)(b).

cases.title: M/S Chakradhari Cold Storage Pvt. Ltd. v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited And Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: An assessment under s.135 read with clause 6.8(c) passed by the Executive Engineer (Revenue) is without competence and is quashed
cases.holding: The power was not with the Executive Engineer (Revenue) to pass the assessment bill and the demand notice; the power lies with the Executive Engineer (Distribution). Writ-C No. 14518 of 2006 is allowed and the revised assessment dated 17 December 2005 and the demand notice dated 20 December 2005 are quashed and set aside.
cases.flag: The 2005 papers were issued under s.135 r/w clause 6.8(c). The competence holding does not resolve that mix of a theft section with the unauthorised-use clause, nor whether the assessing officer is designated under s.126. Source PDF also contains listing orders of 4.3.2020 (Sudhir Agarwal and Rajeev Misra JJ.) and 18.7.2025 (same coram as the judgment).

cases.title: M/S Dev Cold Storage Pvt. Ltd. v. Dakshinachal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: assessing officer competence
cases.holding: Power to pass an assessment bill and demand notice — here the revised assessment dated 17.12.2005 and demand dated 20.12.2005 purported to be under s.135 of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with clause 6.8(c) of the Supply Code, 2005 — does not lie with the Executive Engineer (Revenue); it lies with the Executive Engineer (Distribution). The 2005 order and demand are quashed.
cases.flag: 2005 prayer cites clause 6.8(c); court did not apply a numbered sub-clause

cases.title: Uma Shankar v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: ex-parte assessment — hearing before Assessing Officer
cases.holding: Where provisional and final assessment of electricity dues were conducted and concluded ex parte, no useful purpose is served by keeping the writ pending. Subject to the consumer depositing Rs. 1,75,000 towards the disputed demand within one month and filing an application within a further week, the Assessing Officer shall decide the objection by a reasoned speaking order under Clause 6.8, after confronting the consumer with all adverse material and granting personal hearing, preferably within two months; non-compliance revives the recovery from that stage.

cases.title: Ashok Pathak v. State of U.P. and Another
cases.topic: assessment-hearing
cases.holding: Where it is unclear whether the assessment procedure was fully complied with and the consumer alleges denial of hearing, one opportunity of hearing is to be given before the Assessing Officer under Clause 6.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, who shall decide the objection by a reasoned and speaking order after confronting the consumer with all adverse material and giving a personal hearing; subject to deposit of part of the disputed demand and filing of an application, failing which recovery revives.

cases.title: Smt. Shashi Lata Tiwari v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: hearing-on-assessment-objection
cases.holding: Where compliance with assessment procedure is unclear and the consumer alleges no opportunity of hearing before the demand, the writ is disposed of directing that, subject to deposit of a specified sum towards the disputed demand and filing of an objection, the Assessing Officer shall decide the objection by a reasoned speaking order under Clause 6.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, after confronting the consumer with all adverse material and granting personal hearing.

cases.title: Petitioner v. State of Uttar Pradesh
cases.topic: opportunity of hearing on disputed electricity demand
cases.holding: Where it is unclear whether assessment procedure was completed and the consumer alleges that no hearing preceded an electricity demand, the writ court may dispose of the petition by directing the Assessing Officer, under Clause 6.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, to decide the objection by a reasoned speaking order after confronting the consumer with all adverse material and granting personal hearing, subject to a specified deposit towards the disputed demand.

cases.title: Malkhan Singh v. State of Uttar Pradesh
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: hearing before Assessing Officer on disputed electricity demand
cases.holding: Subject to depositing Rs. 50,000 towards the disputed demand within one month and filing an application before the Assessing Officer within a further week, the Assessing Officer shall decide the petitioners' objection under Clause 6.8 by a reasoned and speaking order strictly in accordance with law, after confronting them with all adverse material relied against them and granting personal hearing, preferably within two months of the application.

cases.title: Anshul Varshney v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: hearing on assessment objection
cases.holding: To the extent the petitioner may not have been given opportunity of hearing before the assessment demand, one opportunity is to be given before the Assessing Officer under clause 6.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Subject to deposit of Rs. 27,000 towards the disputed demand within one month and filing of an application within a further week, the Assessing Officer shall decide the objection by a reasoned speaking order after confronting the petitioner with all adverse material and giving personal hearing, preferably within two months.

cases.title: Petitioner v. State of U.P. and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: hearing before assessment of electricity dues
cases.holding: Where it is unclear whether assessment procedure was fully complied with and the consumer alleges want of hearing before a demand, the writ is disposed of by directing the Assessing Officer under clause 6.8 to decide the objection by a reasoned speaking order after confronting the consumer with all adverse material and granting personal hearing, subject to deposit of Rs. 10,000 towards the disputed demand and filing of an application.

cases.title: Petitioner v. State of U.P. and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: opportunity of hearing before recovery of assessment
cases.holding: Where it is unclear whether assessment procedure was complied with and the consumer alleges want of hearing before the electricity demand, the writ is disposed of with a direction that, subject to depositing Rs 1,50,000 towards the disputed demand within one month and filing an application within a further week, the Assessing Officer shall decide the objection under clause 6.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 by a reasoned speaking order after confronting the consumer with all adverse material and giving personal hearing, preferably within two months; non-compliance revives the recovery.

cases.title: Petitioner v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.topic: assessment-hearing
cases.holding: Where it is unclear that assessment procedure was fully complied with and the consumer claims he was given no hearing before a recovery citation for electricity dues, the writ court will not keep the petition pending. Subject to a deposit towards the disputed demand, the consumer may apply to the assessing officer, who shall decide the objection under Clause 6.8 by a reasoned speaking order after confronting the consumer with adverse material and granting personal hearing.

cases.title: Smt. Reeta Mishra v. State of U.P. and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: opportunity-of-hearing
cases.holding: Where it is unclear whether assessment procedure was fully complied with and the consumer claims no hearing before the demand, the writ may be disposed of directing that, subject to depositing Rs. 35,000 towards the disputed demand within one month and applying to the Assessing Officer within a further week, that officer shall decide the objection by a reasoned speaking order under Clause 6.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, after confronting the consumer with all adverse material and granting personal hearing, preferably within two months.

cases.title: Petitioner v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: Clause 6.8 hearing on assessment demand
cases.holding: Where it is unclear whether assessment procedure was fully complied with and the consumer claims no hearing before the electricity demand, the Assessing Officer shall, subject to deposit of Rs. 2,50,000 within one month and an application within a further week, decide the objection under Clause 6.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 by a reasoned speaking order after confronting the consumer with all adverse material and granting personal hearing, preferably within two months; the deposit remains subject to that final order.

cases.title: Kais Khan v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: hearing on disputed assessment
cases.holding: Where it is unclear whether assessment procedure was fully complied with and the consumer alleges that no opportunity of hearing was given before an electricity demand was created, the writ may be disposed of by directing that, subject to deposit of a specified amount towards the disputed demand, the consumer may apply to the Assessing Officer, who shall decide the objection by a reasoned speaking order after confronting the consumer with all adverse material and granting personal hearing, strictly in accordance with Clause 6.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: M/S R.D. Ice & Cold Storage (P) Ltd. v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited And Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: An assessment under s.135 read with clause 6.8(c) passed by the Executive Engineer (Revenue) is without competence and is quashed
cases.holding: The power was not with the Executive Engineer (Revenue) to pass the assessment bill and the demand notice; the power lies with the Executive Engineer (Distribution). Writ-C No. 6246 of 2006 is allowed and the revised assessment dated 16 December 2005 and the demand notice dated 20 December 2005 are quashed and set aside.
cases.flag: The 2005 papers were issued under s.135 r/w clause 6.8(c). The competence holding does not resolve that mix of a theft section with the unauthorised-use clause, nor whether the assessing officer is designated under s.126. Source PDF also contains listing orders of 9.9.2015 and 1.10.2015 (Krishna Murari and Amar Singh Chauhan, JJ.) and 18.7.2025 (same coram as the judgment).

cases.title: Suman Shukla v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad (Lucknow Bench)
cases.topic: opportunity to object to provisional assessment
cases.holding: Where a final assessment has been made without the consumer being able to submit objections to the provisional assessment, the final assessment and the consequent recovery demand are liable to be quashed. The consumer is to be given an opportunity to respond to the provisional assessment (here, within fifteen days after the inspection note is supplied), and a fresh final assessment is then to be made within three weeks as per law.

cases.title: Jiyauddin v. State of U.P. — s.126 recovery withdrawn; fresh Clause 6.8 order
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: fresh s.126 order after withdrawal of recovery
cases.holding: Recording the licensee’s withdrawal of the Section 126 recovery demand and its undertaking to pass a fresh order strictly in accordance with Clause 6.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, the Court disposed of the writ with liberty to the Electricity Department to pass a fresh order strictly in accordance with the procedure prescribed under the Code, without adjudicating the assessment.

cases.title: Sangram Singh Yadav v. State of U.P. and 3 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: Clause 6.8 requires the assessing officer to deal with objections at a hearing; confirming the provisional notice without applying the mind is not a technical error, and such an assessment may be withdrawn and redone
cases.holding: No. On 05.08.2024 the Division Bench (Manoj Kumar Gupta and Manish Kumar Nigam, JJ.) found sufficient force in the submission that the Assessing Officer had noted the petitioner's objections to the 14.03.2024 provisional assessment but had not dealt with them and had confirmed the notice. Clause 6.8 specifically provides that the consumer is entitled to file objection against the notice of provisional assessment and to a hearing so that those objections are dealt with. Respondent No. 4 admitted the 17.05.2024 final assessment was not in accordance with law and called it a technical error; the Court declined that explanation as total non-application of mind. Respondent No. 4 was permitted to withdraw the impugned assessment and proceed afresh strictly in accordance with law. The Managing Director was required to file a personal affidavit. On 27.11.2024 the writ was dismissed as infructuous after counsel agreed the assessed amount had already been adjusted.
cases.flag: Source PDF compiles orders of 24.07.2024, 05.08.2024, 29.08.2024, 10.09.2024, 01.10.2024, 18.10.2024, 12.11.2024, 26.11.2024 and 27.11.2024 (neutral citation on the last). Paras 3-7 are of the 05.08.2024 order (Gupta and Nigam JJ.). Coram of the 27.11.2024 disposal is Birla and Srivastava JJ. The 29.08.2024 order refers to the Electricity Supply Code, 2006 (catalog key remains UP-2005::6.8). SOP dated 16.04.2024 addressed theft and unauthorised use; this Court applied Clause 6.8.

cases.title: Suresh Chander v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: withdrawal of defective s.126 recovery; fresh 6.8 hearing
cases.holding: Where a recovery citation founded on a Section 126 assessment is issued without following Clause 6.8 of the Supply Code, the citation should be withdrawn forthwith so that the consumer is not driven to the High Court. Recording the Executive Engineer's withdrawal of the 29 June 2024 citation and the undertaking to grant a hearing and pass a fresh order, the Court permitted the licensee to proceed afresh and disposed of the writ subject to costs of Rs. 10,000 to the petitioner, the Managing Director to decide whether the DISCOM or the concerned Executive Engineer would bear the cost.

cases.title: Ram Prasad Gupta v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: independent findings on theft or UUE in final assessment
cases.holding: Paragraph 6.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 requires the assessing officer to record an independent finding relating to theft or unauthorized use of electricity; a final assessment lacking such findings is contrary to that paragraph and cannot stand.
cases.flag: Paragraph 6.8 applied to theft or UUE without distinguishing Clause 8 theft assessment.

cases.title: Uco Bank v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.topic: Written objection rejected without personal hearing cannot sustain a UUE assessment
cases.holding: No. After concluding unauthorised use, Clause 6.8(b)(i) requires a provisional assessment inviting objections, and Clause 6.8(c) requires the assessing officer to hear the consumer. The provisional order of 4 January 2006 was served; the bank objected on 9 January 2006 within time. The bank's assertion that no personal hearing was given, though denied in the counter-affidavit, was borne out on a perusal of the objection. The objection was rejected ex parte on 28 August 2006. The assessment therefore cannot be sustained and is quashed. The matter is remitted for a fresh order after hearing the petitioner, and the Nagar Nigam if necessary, within six weeks.
cases.flag: Petitioner also invoked Clause 6.8(c)(i) and Article 14. The Court applied Clauses 6.8(b)(i) and 6.8(c). Source PDF concatenates the 2.1.2017 listing order (Tarun Agarwala and Umesh Chandra Srivastava JJ.) with this unnumbered 9.1.2017 judgment (Tarun Agarwala and Abhai Kumar JJ.). Connected Writ-C No. 6116 of 2006 is disposed of in terms of the 31.1.2006 interim connection, with liberty to proceed in accordance with law if arrears after the fresh assessment are unpaid.

cases.title: Uco Bank v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.topic: Period of UUE must be ascertained; otherwise confined to twelve months preceding inspection
cases.holding: No. Clause 6.8(c)(iii) requires the assessing officer to ascertain the period of unauthorised use at the premises. It is settled that without that finding the period is confined to twelve months immediately preceding the date of inspection. Neither the provisional assessment nor the rejection of objections recorded such a finding. The bank's case was that as tenant it had paid electricity charges to the Nagar Nigam; the officer must consider payments made by the Nagar Nigam to the licensee and hear the Nagar Nigam if necessary.

cases.title: Shri Mahavir Rolling Mills v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: personal-hearing-before-assessment
cases.holding: An assessment of electricity dues passed without giving the petitioner an opportunity of personal hearing is violative of clause 6.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 and cannot be sustained. The assessment order dated 7 December 2006 is set aside. The Assessing Authority shall re-assess the electricity dues in accordance with clause 6.8 after giving the petitioner a hearing, and shall pass a fresh assessment order within one month of production of a certified copy of this order.

cases.title: M/S Sijaria Ice Gramodhyog Sultanpura & Others v. State Of U.P. & Others
cases.topic: Inspection report must be supplied and a 6.8(c)(i) hearing given before rejecting objections to a provisional bill
cases.holding: The Court found no material showing that a copy of the 26.06.2006 inspection report was made available, so an effective reply to the 30.06.2006 show-cause was not possible, and that no opportunity of hearing under paragraph 6.8(c)(i) was afforded before respondent no. 3 rejected the 15.07.2006 objections. Those were among the thirteen grounds of the Section 127 appeal. They were not used to quash the 23.02.2007 assessment; that order is left to the restored appeal.
cases.flag: Counsel invoked paragraphs 6.8(a)(v) and 6.8(c)(i). The Court named 6.8(c)(i) for the hearing and treated non-supply of the inspection report as a record finding (6.8(a)(v) is the Code clause for handing over the site report). An FIR under s.135 was lodged the day after inspection and the Court itself described the demand as for the period of 'theft of the electricity', yet applied Clause 6.8 (UUE) as argued, not Clauses 8.1–8.2. Keyed to catalog UP-2005::6.8; there is no 6.8(a) or 6.8(c) key. Cause title spells the firm Sijaria; the body spells Sijaoria. Licensee styled Dakshinanchal Vidhut Nigam Limited.

cases.title: Smt. Kalpana Agarwal v. Managing Director, Western Electricity & Others
cases.topic: Inspection, provisional assessment, hearing and speaking final order are mandatory before a theft or UUE assessment can stand
cases.holding: No. Assessment on an allegation of theft or unauthorised use must follow Clause 6.8: a site inspection report disclosing the irregularity, handed to the consumer or pasted/posted if refused (6.8(a)); a provisional assessment with show-cause giving 15 working days and a hearing date (6.8(b)); and after personal hearing a speaking order recording whether unauthorised use is established and the assessed amount (6.8(c)). The Executive Engineer issued the Rs. 15,20,828 demand straightaway. Licensee's counsel could not dispute that this procedure was not followed. The 02.11.2007 order is set aside, with liberty to proceed afresh in accordance with law, and costs of Rs. 10,000.
cases.flag: The checking report alleged theft under ss.135/138. The Court applied Clause 6.8 (UUE procedure) to that theft allegation, treating 6.8 as governing assessment of theft or UUE alike. Catalog distinguishes Clauses 8.1–8.2 as the theft-assessment procedure; the Court did not cite 8.1/8.2. Judgment states contracted load as '5 KV'.

cases.title: Krishan Kumar v. State of U.P. and others
cases.topic: Mandatory hearing before deciding objection to provisional assessment
cases.holding: Whenever the Court directs an authority to decide an objection or representation, the authority must act in accordance with law. Paragraph 6.8 C of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 mandates that a date of hearing be fixed. An order deciding an objection against a provisional assessment for alleged electricity theft, from which it is not clear that any opportunity of hearing was given, violates the principles of natural justice, cannot be sustained, and is quashed, with liberty to pass a fresh order after personal hearing.
cases.flag: Court cites paragraph 6.8 C; catalog lists UP-2005::6.8(d).

cases.title: Ganesh Agrawal v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: fifteen working days for reply to provisional UUE assessment
cases.holding: Pending consideration of whether a final assessment made before expiry of 15 working days from registered-post dispatch of the provisional assessment complied with Clause 6.8(b)(i), recovery on the citation was stayed and the licensee was left free to serve a fresh show-cause notice with the provisional assessment in accordance with the Supply Code. The writ was thereafter dismissed for want of prosecution, without a merits decision on that clause.
cases.flag: cited as 6.8(b)(i)

cases.title: Anwarul Haq v. State of U.P. and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: appeal against final assessment
cases.holding: Once a final assessment has been passed after an alleged Section 135 raid, the consumer's grievance that no provisional assessment notice under Clauses 6.8 and 8.1 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 was served, and the dispute over mixed domestic-commercial use, are to be raised in an appeal before the appropriate authority rather than in writ; that appeal is to be decided after a full hearing by a reasoned order.
cases.flag: order records assessment under Clauses 6.8 and 8.1 together; which procedure applied was not decided

UP-2005::6.8(b).topic: service of provisional assessment and opportunity to object

cases.title: Siddharth Rai v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: service of provisional assessment and opportunity to object
cases.holding: Notice of provisional assessment sent to an incorrect address and returned unserved is not valid service, so the consumer was not afforded the opportunity under para 6.8(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 to reply and object. The provisional assessment also did not disclose the basis of the demand of Rs.1,07,153/- and the assessing authority had not recorded satisfaction that the petitioner committed theft of electricity. The recovery citation dated 28 May 2014 and consequential proceedings are quashed. The licensee must prepare a fresh provisional assessment, serve it on the petitioner, and pass a reasoned final assessment after considering objections, in the light of Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P.
cases.flag: ambiguous: court applies 6.8(b) to a theft assessment

cases.title: Unserved theft provisional assessment: recovery quashed for want of 6.8(b) opportunity
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: opportunity to object to provisional assessment (theft)
cases.holding: Where a theft-based recovery is founded on a provisional assessment sent by ordinary post, and the record does not show service or any opportunity to object, the consumer has not been afforded the opportunity required by para 6.8(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The assessment is further vitiated if it does not disclose the basis of the amount demanded or record the assessing officer's satisfaction that theft was committed. The recovery and consequential proceedings are liable to be quashed, with a direction to issue a fresh provisional assessment, serve it, and pass a reasoned final assessment after considering objections, in the light of Ashok Kumar.

cases.title: Theft citation quashed for want of 6.8(b) opportunity
cases.topic: theft — provisional assessment — opportunity to object
cases.holding: A citation notice for alleged electricity dues cannot stand where the licensee does not show that the provisional assessment was served or that the consumer was afforded the opportunity under para 6.8(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 to object. The provisional assessment must also record the assessing authority's satisfaction that theft was committed and give the basis of the quantified demand. Failure on these counts warrants quashing of the citation and all consequential proceedings, with a direction to issue and serve a fresh provisional assessment and to pass a reasoned final assessment after considering objections, in the light of Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P., 2008 (6) ADJ 660 (DB).

cases.title: Veerendra Singh v. State of U.P. and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: provisional assessment — service and opportunity to object
cases.holding: Absent positive material that the provisional assessment was served, the consumer is denied the opportunity under para 6.8(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 to reply and object. A demand notice by registered post, without proof of service of the provisional assessment itself, does not cure that defect. The recovery certificate dated 2.9.2014 and consequential proceedings are quashed. Respondents must prepare and serve a fresh provisional assessment; the final assessment is to be made after considering objections, giving reasons to meet them, in light of Ashok Kumar.

cases.title: Akbar v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.topic: provisional assessment notice — hearing date and basis
cases.holding: The provisional assessment notice dated 11.6.2014 did not specify a date for hearing as required by clause 6.8(b)(1), and did not give the basis on which the petitioner was assessed at Rs.2,72,136. The petitioner was therefore not afforded the opportunity provided by clause 6.8(b). The notice and the recovery citation dated 15.6.2015 were quashed. Respondents were directed to prepare a fresh provisional assessment, serve it on the petitioner, and pass a final assessment after considering his objection, with reasons meeting the objections, in the light of Ashok Kumar (paras 56–64).
cases.flag: Court applied cl. 6.8(b)/(b)(1) while citing Ashok Kumar on theft assessment; catalog distinguishes theft assessment under 8.1–8.2 from 6.8.

cases.title: Bahabuddin @ Raju v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: provisional assessment notice — hearing date and basis of demand
cases.holding: Where the provisional assessment notice neither indicates a date for hearing as required by Clause 6.8(b)(1) nor gives the basis on which the consumer was assessed, the consumer is not afforded the opportunity provided in Clause 6.8(b). The notice and the recovery citation issued on it are liable to be quashed, and the licensee must prepare a fresh provisional assessment, serve it, and pass a reasoned final assessment after considering the consumer's objections.

cases.title: Manoj Singh v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: provisional assessment notice — hearing date and basis of demand
cases.holding: Clause 6.8(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 requires the provisional assessment notice itself to specify a date for hearing and to disclose the basis of the assessed amount. The 2 February 2016 notice demanding Rs.3,73,970/- did neither, so the consumer was not afforded the opportunity the clause requires. The notice is quashed; the licensee must issue a fresh provisional assessment and make the final order only after considering objections with reasons, following Ashok Kumar.

cases.title: Rakesh Khandelwal v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.topic: hearing and service before final theft assessment
cases.holding: Where recovery of alleged theft dues rests on a final assessment made without affording the consumer a hearing under Clause 6.8(1)(b) and without recording satisfaction that the provisional assessment notice was served, the demand and consequential recovery are unsustainable. A fresh provisional assessment must be prepared and served, and the final order made after considering objections with reasons, in the light of Ashok Kumar.
cases.flag: Order cites Clause 6.8(1)(b); catalog key is 6.8(b). Applied to theft assessment; catalog also tags 8.1–8.2 as the theft pathway rather than 6.8.

cases.title: Hanuman Prasad v. State of U.P. — Clause 6.8(b) notice must fix a hearing date
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: provisional assessment notice — hearing date and basis of demand
cases.holding: A provisional assessment notice under Clause 6.8(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 that neither specifies a date of hearing nor discloses the basis of the assessed amount is not in accordance with law and does not afford the consumer adequate opportunity. A recovery citation founded on such a notice is liable to be quashed; a reasoned final assessment must then be made after considering the consumer's objections.
cases.flag: Counsel cited Clause 6.8(b)(1); the Court applied para 6.8(b) to a theft-assessment recovery, following Ashok Kumar, without separating cl. 6.8 (unauthorized use) from theft procedure.

cases.title: Mohan Sharma v. Dakshinanchal Vidut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.topic: provisional assessment notice — hearing date and basis
cases.holding: Where a provisional assessment notice neither specifies a date for hearing as required by clause 6.8(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, nor discloses the basis of the assessed amount, the consumer is not afforded the opportunity the Code requires. A recovery citation founded on such a notice is liable to be quashed, and a fresh final assessment is to be made after considering the consumer's objections, with reasons meeting those objections.

cases.title: Pavan Kumar v. Dakshinanchal Vidut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.topic: provisional assessment notice — hearing date and basis
cases.holding: A provisional assessment notice that neither indicates a date for hearing nor discloses the basis of the assessed amount does not afford the opportunity required by Clause 6.8(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The recovery citation dated 21.05.2015 is quashed. Final assessment shall be made within six weeks after considering the petitioner's objections, with reasons meeting those objections, in light of Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P.

cases.title: Om Pal Singh v. Chairman/Managing Director, U.P.P.C.L.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: provisional assessment notice — hearing date and basis
cases.holding: A provisional assessment notice under Clause 6.8(b) that neither specifies a date for hearing nor gives the basis of the assessed amount is not in accordance with law and does not afford the opportunity that clause requires. Recovery founded on such a notice is quashed; final assessment must follow after considering the consumer's objections with reasons. Counsel had invoked Clause 6.8(b)(1); the Court applied para 6.8(b).

cases.title: Jagat Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: provisional assessment notice — hearing date and basis of demand
cases.holding: A provisional assessment notice under Clause 6.8(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 that neither specifies a date for hearing nor discloses the basis of the assessed amount is not in accordance with law, and the consumer has not been afforded the opportunity 6.8(b) requires. The notice and consequent recovery citations are liable to be quashed, with a direction to issue a fresh provisional assessment, consider the consumer's objections, and pass a reasoned final assessment in the light of Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P.

cases.title: Chhotu @ Arun Kumar Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: provisional assessment notice — hearing date and basis
cases.holding: A provisional assessment notice under Clause 6.8(b) must specify a date for hearing in the notice itself and must disclose the basis of the assessed amount. The notice dated 06.11.2015 neither indicated a hearing date nor gave the basis of the assessment of Rs.1,42,569, so the consumer was not afforded the opportunity Clause 6.8(b) requires. The notice is quashed. The licensee shall prepare and serve a fresh provisional assessment within 15 days of production of a certified copy; the final assessment shall be made after considering the petitioner's objections and giving reasons, in the light of Ashok Kumar.
cases.flag: Court cited both Clause 6.8(b)(1) and para 6.8(b), and invoked Ashok Kumar's theft-assessment discussion while applying 6.8(b).

cases.title: Smt. Geeta Maurya v. Poorvanchal Vidyut Vitran Khand-2
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: provisional-assessment-notice
cases.holding: A provisional assessment notice under Clause 6.8(b) must specify a date of hearing in the notice itself and must disclose the basis of the assessed amount. The notice dated 6 November 2013 assessing Rs.4,19,379 specified neither, so the consumer was not afforded the opportunity required by Clause 6.8(b). The notice and the recovery citation dated 23 July 2015 were quashed, with a direction to prepare and serve a fresh provisional assessment and to make the final assessment only after considering objections, with reasons, in the light of Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P.
cases.flag: Order cites Clause 6.8(b)(1) for the hearing-date-in-notice requirement; the operative finding is under para 6.8(b).

cases.title: Arjun Kumar v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: provisional assessment notice — hearing date and basis
cases.holding: A provisional assessment notice under clause 6.8(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 must indicate a date for hearing and the basis of the assessment. The Court found that the notice specified neither a hearing date nor the basis of the demand of Rs. 79,542, so it was not in accordance with law and the consumer was not afforded adequate opportunity under para 6.8(b). The notice dated 24 February 2016 and the recovery citation dated 11 January 2016 were quashed. The licensee was directed to prepare and serve a fresh provisional assessment within 15 days and to pass a reasoned final assessment after considering the consumer's objections, in the light of Ashok Kumar.

cases.title: Sudha Kashmiri v. Executive Engineer, Electricity Distribution Centre
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: provisional assessment notice — hearing date and basis
cases.holding: Where the provisional assessment notice does not indicate a date for hearing as required by Clause 6.8(b) and does not give the basis on which the consumer was assessed, the notice is not in accordance with law and the consumer is not afforded the opportunity Clause 6.8(b) provides. The notices are quashed; a final assessment is to be made after considering the consumer's objections, with reasons, in the light of Ashok Kumar.

cases.title: Gajendra Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: provisional assessment before recovery
cases.holding: In the absence of a provisional assessment and of compliance with clause 6.8(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, which is mandatory, a recovery certificate is not liable to be sustained and is quashed.

cases.title: Mohar Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: provisional assessment notice — date of hearing and basis of demand
cases.holding: Because the provisional assessment notice neither specified a date of hearing as required by clause 6.8(b) nor gave the basis on which the petitioner was assessed at Rs 1,18,201, it was not in accordance with law and did not afford the opportunity clause 6.8(b) requires. The recovery citation dated 25 February 2016 was quashed. Final assessment is to be made within six weeks after considering the petitioner's objections, with reasons meeting those objections, in the light of Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P.

cases.title: Smt. Afifa Fatima v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: provisional assessment notice and recovery
cases.holding: Provisional assessment and issuance of a recovery certificate without a notice shown to have been sent to the consumer and without specifying a date and time for hearing is de hors the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 and in gross violation of clause 6.8(b). The recovery citation cannot be sustained. The licensee may assess afresh after issuing a provisional notice, considering objections, and fixing a date for hearing with reasons.

cases.title: Shri Bholu v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: provisional assessment — notice and hearing
cases.holding: In the absence of notice and opportunity of hearing before making a provisional assessment, clause 6.8(b) being mandatory, the demand notice dated 13.03.2015 and recovery certificate dated 29.12.2015 cannot be sustained and stand quashed. The licensee remains free to make a fresh assessment after following the prescribed procedure.

cases.title: Brijendra Singh Tewatiya v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: provisional assessment — notice and hearing
cases.holding: Clause 6.8(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is mandatory. Where provisional assessment is made without issuing notice and without fixing a date of hearing, the demand notice and recovery certificate cannot stand and are liable to be quashed. The licensee remains free to make a fresh assessment after following the prescribed procedure.
