cases.title: Mohd. Javed Naiyer v. Kanpur Electricity Supply Co. Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: provisional-assessment-notice
cases.holding: A provisional assessment notice under Clause 6.8(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 that does not indicate a date for hearing, as Clause 6.8(b)(1) requires, and does not disclose the basis of the assessed amount is not in accordance with law. The consumer is not afforded the opportunity Clause 6.8(b) provides. The demand notice dated 25/26.2.2016 and bill dated 19.2.2016 are quashed. Final assessment shall be made within six weeks after considering the petitioner's objection, with reasons meeting those objections, in the light of Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P., 2008 (6) ADJ 660 (DB).

cases.title: Mahendra Dubey v. U.P.P.C.L.
cases.topic: provisional assessment notice — hearing date and basis
cases.holding: A provisional assessment notice under Clause 6.8(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 that does not indicate a date for hearing and does not give the basis on which the consumer was assessed does not afford the opportunity contemplated by para 6.8(b). The notice dated 28.02.2015 and the recovery citation dated 07.09.2015 are quashed. The licensee must prepare and serve a fresh provisional assessment within 15 days of production of a certified copy of the order, and must make the final assessment after considering the consumer's objections and giving reasons, in the light of Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P., 2008 (6) ADJ 660 (DB) (paras 56–64).

cases.title: Ved Prakash Soni v. Executive Engineer, Electricity Distribution Division
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: provisional assessment notice — hearing date and basis
cases.holding: A provisional assessment notice that neither specifies a date for hearing, as the Court read Clause 6.8(b)(1) to require, nor discloses the basis of the assessed amount does not afford the opportunity of hearing under para 6.8(b). Such a notice is not in accordance with law and is liable to be quashed, with a direction to serve a fresh provisional assessment and to pass a reasoned final assessment after considering the consumer's objections, in light of Ashok Kumar.
cases.flag: Court cited Clause 6.8(b)(1) for the hearing-date requirement and para 6.8(b) for opportunity; keyed to catalog hit UP-2005::6.8(b).

cases.title: Ajay Kasana v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: provisional assessment — notice and hearing
cases.holding: Clause 6.8(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is mandatory. A provisional assessment made without fixing a date of hearing and without issuing notice cannot support a recovery certificate, which is liable to be quashed, with liberty to the licensee to make a fresh assessment after following the prescribed procedure.

cases.title: Ram Sumer Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: provisional assessment notice (theft)
cases.holding: Provisional assessment and recovery under clause 6.8(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 are invalid where the notice is not shown to have been sent to the consumer and does not specify a date and time for hearing. The 21 April 2015 demand notice is quashed. The licensee must prepare a fresh provisional assessment, serve it, and pass a reasoned final order after considering the consumer's objections, in the light of Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P.

cases.title: Uma Shankar Yadav v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: provisional assessment notice — objections and hearing
cases.holding: Where the provisional assessment notice does not state the basis of the assessed amounts and does not invite objections with a date and time for hearing, a subsequent demand notice is de hors the Supply Code and in gross violation of clause 6.8(b), and must be quashed, leaving the licensee free to proceed in accordance with law.

cases.title: Harminder Singh v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: provisional assessment — notice and hearing
cases.holding: Provisional assessment without notice and without fixing a date of hearing violates the mandatory requirement of clause 6.8(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The electricity bill dated 10.05.2016 was therefore quashed, with liberty to the licensee to make a fresh assessment after following the prescribed procedure.

cases.title: Smt. Rajesh Kumari v. Secretary, Electricity Board
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: notice and hearing before provisional assessment
cases.holding: In the absence of notice and opportunity of hearing before making the provisional assessment, clause 6.8(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 being mandatory, the electricity bill dated 5.10.2016 cannot be sustained and is quashed; the licensee may make a fresh assessment after following the prescribed procedure.

cases.title: Ashish Gupta v. State of U.P. (Clause 6.8(b) notice without hearing date)
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: provisional assessment notice — hearing date and basis of assessment
cases.holding: A provisional assessment notice that neither specifies a date for hearing as required by Clause 6.8(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, nor discloses the basis of the assessed amount, is not in accordance with law and does not afford the consumer adequate opportunity under para 6.8(b). The notice dated 08.09.2014 and recovery citation dated 03.08.2016 are quashed; the licensee must prepare and serve a fresh provisional assessment and make the final assessment after considering the consumer's objections, with reasons, in the light of Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P., 2008 (6) ADJ 660 (DB).

cases.title: Shiv Shankar v. U.P. Power Corporation
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: mandatory hearing before UUE/theft recovery
cases.holding: Recovery of electric dues for alleged theft cannot be sustained where the consumer was not afforded the opportunity of hearing mandatorily warranted under Clause 6.8(1)(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
cases.flag: Order cites 'Clause 6.8 (1)(b)'; catalog key used is UP-2005::6.8(b). Numbering not silently corrected.

cases.title: Bachhan Pandey v. State of U.P. and others
cases.topic: provisional assessment before recovery
cases.holding: In the absence of provisional assessment in compliance with clause 6.8(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, which is mandatory, a recovery certificate is not liable to be sustained and is quashed. It remains open to the licensee to make a fresh assessment after following the prescribed procedure.

cases.title: Awadhesh Kumar Upadhyay v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.topic: provisional-assessment-notice-and-hearing
cases.holding: A recovery certificate that does not disclose the basis of assessment, and is issued without a provisional notice inviting objections and indicating a date and time of hearing, is de hors the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 and in gross violation of clause 6.8(b); it cannot be sustained and is quashed, without prejudice to the licensee proceeding afresh in accordance with law within three months.
cases.flag: Court applied cl. 6.8(b) (UUE assessment) while invoking Ashok Kumar, a theft-assessment precedent.

cases.title: Raju Jaiswal (Rajiv Jaiswal) v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: provisional assessment — service and hearing date
cases.holding: A demand notice and recovery citation cannot stand where the provisional assessment is not shown to have been served and does not indicate a date for hearing. Clause 6.8(b) requires the provisional notice to invite objections and to indicate a date and time for hearing of the consumer. Silence on the record as to the mode and manner of sending the provisional assessment yields a presumption that it was not sent. Following Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P., the demand dated 7 March 2017 and recovery citation dated 4 May 2017 were quashed, with liberty to proceed afresh in accordance with the prescribed procedure.
cases.flag: Court applied clause 6.8(b) while describing the assessment, via Ashok Kumar, as theft of electricity; theft assessment is governed by clauses 8.1–8.2, not 6.8.

cases.title: Satyanarayan v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: mandatory hearing and service of provisional assessment before final assessment
cases.holding: Because the petitioner was not afforded the opportunity of hearing mandatorily required by Clause 6.8(1)(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and no final assessment recorded the authority’s satisfaction that the provisional assessment notice had been served, the demand notice dated 26.9.2015 and recovery citation dated 8.11.2016 cannot stand and are quashed. The respondents must prepare a fresh provisional assessment, serve it on the petitioner, and make a final assessment after considering objections with reasons, following Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P., 2008(6) ADJ 660 (DB).
cases.flag: Court cited Clause 6.8(1)(b); catalog key is 6.8(b). The dispute was treated as theft of electricity, yet the Court applied Clause 6.8 (following Ashok Kumar) rather than cls. 8.1–8.2.

cases.title: Smt. Chhaya Gupta v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: provisional-assessment-notice
cases.holding: A provisional assessment notice under Clause 6.8(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 must indicate a date for hearing in the notice itself and disclose the basis of the assessed amount. A notice that does neither is not in accordance with law and does not afford the consumer the opportunity provided by Clause 6.8(b). The notice dated 27.03.2017 and recovery citation dated 18.11.2017 are quashed. The licensee must prepare and serve a fresh provisional assessment; the final assessment shall be made after considering the consumer's objections, granting hearing, and giving reasons meeting those objections, in the light of Ashok Kumar, 2008 (6) ADJ 660 (DB) paras 56-64.
cases.flag: Court referred to Clause 6.8(b)(1) and para 6.8(b); keyed to catalog UP-2005::6.8(b).

cases.title: Munna Lal v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: provisional assessment — mandatory hearing and proof of service
cases.holding: Where the consumer was not given an opportunity of hearing as mandatorily required by Clause 6.8(1)(b), and the final assessment does not record satisfaction that the provisional assessment notice was served, a recovery citation for alleged theft of electricity cannot be sustained. The demand of Rs. 57,044 dated 25 October 2016 and consequential proceedings were quashed; the licensee must prepare a fresh provisional assessment, serve it, and pass a reasoned final assessment after considering objections, in the light of Ashok Kumar (paras 56–64).
cases.flag: Court numbered the clause 6.8(1)(b) (catalog 6.8(b)) and applied it to theft; 8.1–8.2 ordinarily govern theft assessment.

cases.title: Prahlad Singh v. State of U.P. and another
cases.topic: provisional assessment notice — hearing date and basis of assessment
cases.holding: Where the provisional assessment notice neither indicates a date and time for hearing, as Clause 6.8(b)(1) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 requires, nor gives the basis of the assessed sum, the notice is not in accordance with law and the consumer is not afforded the opportunity provided in Clause 6.8(b). The consequent demand is liable to be quashed, and a reasoned final assessment is to be made after considering the consumer's objections in the light of Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P., 2008(6) ADJ 660.

cases.title: Virendra Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: provisional assessment notice — hearing date and basis
cases.holding: A provisional assessment notice under Clause 6.8(b) must specify the date and time for hearing and disclose the basis of the assessed amount. A notice that does neither does not afford the opportunity contemplated by Clause 6.8(b). The demand dated 08.01.2018 is quashed; final assessment shall be made within six weeks after considering the consumer's objections, with reasons meeting those objections, in the light of Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P., 2008(6) ADJ 660 (DB).

cases.title: Tilak Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: provisional assessment notice — hearing date and basis of demand
cases.holding: On the face of the provisional assessment notice, no date or time for hearing was indicated and the basis of the Rs.4,21,743 assessment was not given. Clause 6.8(b) requires both. The notice was therefore not in accordance with law, the consumer was not afforded the opportunity contemplated by Clause 6.8(b), and the demand notice dated 08.01.2018 was quashed. Final assessment is to be made within six weeks after considering the petitioner's objections, with reasons meeting those objections, in light of Ashok Kumar.

cases.title: Mahendra Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: provisional assessment notice — hearing date and basis
cases.holding: The provisional assessment notice did not indicate a date and time for hearing as Clause 6.8(b)(1) requires, and did not give the basis of the assessment of Rs.25,687. The petitioner was therefore not afforded the opportunity provided in Clause 6.8(b). The demand notice dated 8 January 2018 was quashed. Final assessment is to be made within six weeks after considering the petitioner's objections, with reasons meeting those objections in the light of Ashok Kumar.

cases.title: Ravi Prakash Tiwari v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: provisional assessment notice — date, time and basis
cases.holding: The provisional assessment notice did not indicate a date and time for hearing, as Clause 6.8(b)(1) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 requires, and did not give the basis on which the petitioner was assessed at Rs.6,17,752. The consumer was not afforded the adequate opportunity provided in para 6.8(b). The demand notice dated 15.03.2018 is quashed. Final assessment shall be made within six weeks after considering the petitioner's objections, giving reasons to meet those objections in the light of Ashok Kumar.
cases.flag: Court cited Clause 6.8(b)(1) for the date-and-time requirement and para 6.8(b) for opportunity of hearing.

cases.title: Shyam Kumar v. Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitaran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: provisional assessment notice — hearing fixture and basis
cases.holding: A provisional assessment notice that neither specifies the date and time for hearing nor states the basis of the sum assessed is not in accordance with clause 6.8(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Where the licensee then proceeds to a final assessment without any notice or opportunity of hearing, the consumer has not been afforded the opportunity required by para 6.8(b). The demand notice dated 24.11.2017 and the final assessment order dated 09.03.2018 are quashed; fresh assessment is to be carried out in the light of Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P., 2008 (6) ADJ 660 (DB) and the prescribed procedure within three weeks of production of a certified copy.

cases.title: Munna Lal v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: service of provisional and final assessment notices
cases.holding: On the licensee’s post-office dispatch receipts, the Court was satisfied that appropriate steps had been taken before the final assessment dated 6 November 2017: registered-post dispatch of the provisional assessment notice, of that final order (17 November 2017), and of the recovery notice dated 8 December 2017.
cases.flag: The 3 May 2018 listing order asked about Clause 6.8 (1) (b)(i). The 4 May disposal does not restate a numbered sub-clause. Catalog key 6.8(b) is the nearest hit; the court’s (1)(b)(i) numbering is not silently recast.

cases.title: Manoj v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: provisional assessment notice — hearing date and basis
cases.holding: Clause 6.8(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 requires adequate opportunity on a provisional assessment, including a date and time for hearing specified in the notice itself under Clause 6.8(b)(1) and disclosure of the basis of the demand. The notice dated 18.11.2017 did neither and was quashed. Respondents were directed to prepare and serve a fresh provisional assessment; the final order is to follow after considering objections, opportunity of hearing, and reasons meeting those objections, in light of Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P.

cases.title: Tariq v. Pashimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: date and time of hearing on provisional assessment
cases.holding: Clause 6.8(b) of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 requires the assessing officer to fix a date and time of hearing on a provisional assessment. A notice that merely allows 15 days to object, without appointing a hearing, is non-compliant. The Court did not restore supply or quash the assessment; it fixed 27.8.2018 at 11 a.m. for the consumer to appear with objections and directed the Executive Engineer to pass a speaking final order after considering those objections in accordance with law.
cases.flag: Court applied Clause 6.8(b) to an alleged theft assessment without addressing Clauses 8.1–8.2.

cases.title: Chandra Prakash Yadav v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: provisional assessment notice — hearing date and basis
cases.holding: A provisional assessment notice under Clause 6.8(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 must specify the date of hearing and the basis of the assessment. Counsel invoked Clause 6.8(b)(1); the Court applied para 6.8(b). A notice that omits both the hearing date and the basis is not in accordance with law and does not afford the opportunity Clause 6.8(b) contemplates. Such a notice is liable to be quashed; the licensee must issue a fresh provisional assessment and make the final assessment after considering the consumer's objections with reasons, in the light of Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P., 2008 (6) ADJ 660 (DB).

cases.title: Ram Prakash @ Pappu Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: theft provisional assessment — hearing date in notice
cases.holding: Where the provisional assessment notice in a theft case does not indicate a date for hearing, it is not in accordance with para 6.8(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and the consumer is not afforded adequate opportunity. A recovery citation issued on that process, without a final assessment after considering the pending objection, is liable to be quashed. The licensee must prepare and serve a fresh provisional assessment; the final assessment shall be made after considering the objection, giving reasons, in the light of Ashok Kumar.

cases.title: Sahabuddin v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: provisional assessment notice — hearing particulars and basis of demand
cases.holding: Clause 6.8(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 requires the licensee, when issuing a provisional assessment notice, to fix in the notice itself a date, time and place of hearing and to disclose the basis of the assessed amount. A notice dated 22.9.2017 that indicated neither hearing particulars nor the basis of a demand of Rs.1,13,624 was not in accordance with law, so the consumer was not afforded the opportunity Clause 6.8(b) provides. The notice and the recovery citation dated 13.11.2017 were quashed. The respondents were directed to prepare and serve a fresh provisional assessment and to pass a reasoned final order after considering objections and granting a hearing, in the light of Ashok Kumar (paras 56–64) on Supply Code, 2005 assessment procedure in theft cases.

cases.title: Meenu Gupta v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: theft provisional assessment — hearing date and basis of demand
cases.holding: A provisional assessment notice in a theft case that does not specify a date of hearing and does not disclose the basis of the assessed amount is not in accordance with para 6.8(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and does not afford adequate opportunity. Recovery citation issued on such a notice, without a final assessment considering the consumer's pending objection, is quashed. The licensee must prepare and serve a fresh provisional assessment; the final assessment shall be made after considering the objection and giving reasons, in the light of Ashok Kumar.

cases.title: Raj Bahadur v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: provisional assessment notice — hearing date and basis of demand
cases.holding: Clause 6.8(b) requires the licensee to afford the consumer an opportunity on a date specified in the provisional assessment notice itself and to disclose the basis of the assessed amount. A notice that indicates no hearing date and gives no basis for a demand of Rs.7,07,405 is not in accordance with law, so the consumer is not afforded the opportunity 6.8(b) contemplates. Such a notice and a recovery citation founded on it are liable to be quashed; a fresh provisional assessment must be served and a reasoned final order passed after considering objections and granting hearing.

cases.title: Ram Bihari v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: provisional assessment notice — date of hearing and basis of demand
cases.holding: Clause 6.8(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 requires that a provisional assessment notice afford the consumer an opportunity of hearing. The Court, citing Clause 6.8(b)(1), held that the notice must itself fix a date for hearing and must state the basis of the assessed amount. The notice dated 22.07.2017 specified neither a hearing date nor the basis of the Rs.59,898 demand; the consumer was therefore not afforded the opportunity Clause 6.8(b) provides. The notice and the recovery citation dated 08.12.2017 are quashed. Respondents must issue a fresh provisional assessment, consider the consumer's objections after an opportunity of hearing, and give reasons meeting those objections in the light of Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P., 2008 (6) ADJ 660 (DB) (paras 56–64).
cases.flag: Court cited Clause 6.8(b)(1) for the date-of-hearing requirement and para 6.8(b) for opportunity; catalog key is 6.8(b).

cases.title: Akhlak Ahmad @ Sundar v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: provisional assessment notice must indicate a hearing date
cases.holding: A provisional assessment notice in a theft-of-electricity matter that does not indicate a date for hearing does not afford the opportunity required by clause 6.8(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The recovery citation is quashed. The licensee must prepare and serve a fresh provisional assessment; the final assessment shall be made after considering the consumer's objection, with reasons meeting the objection, in the light of Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P.
cases.flag: Court applied clause 6.8(b) to a theft assessment; clauses 8.1–8.2 ordinarily govern theft (s.135) assessment.

UP-2005::6.8(c).topic: pending objection and personal hearing on theft recovery citation

cases.title: Mohammad Islam Rana v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: pending objection and personal hearing on theft recovery citation
cases.holding: Where a theft recovery citation is challenged for non-service of provisional-assessment notice and denial of the clause 6.8(c) personal hearing, and an objection to the Executive Engineer remains pending, the writ may be disposed by directing the Executive Engineer to consider a representation and pass appropriate orders within a stipulated time, with a limited stay of coercive recovery; the Court does not decide whether the Supply Code procedure was followed.
cases.flag: Petitioners invoked clause 6.8(c) on an allegation of electricity theft; the Court did not decide whether clause 6.8 or clauses 8.1–8.2 governed the assessment.

UP-2005::6.8(d).code: U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 (read with s.127, Electricity Act 2003)
UP-2005::6.8(d).topic: Remedy against a final theft assessment — statutory appeal under s.127 / Clause 6.8(d)

cases.title: Dr. Santosh Kumar Awasthi v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.topic: Remedy against a final theft assessment — statutory appeal under s.127 / Clause 6.8(d)
cases.holding: The remedy against a final order of assessment is the statutory appeal under Section 127 read with Clause 6.8(d) of the Code, on deposit of half the assessed amount; the writ court relegated the consumer to that appeal, directing it be entertained without a limitation objection, staying recovery for 30 days, and leaving the merits and any stay to the appellate authority.

cases.title: Jitendra Kumar Agnihotri v. State of U.P. — writ against final assessment relegated to s.127 appeal
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: statutory appeal against final assessment bill
cases.holding: A writ against a final assessment bill is disposed of by relegating the consumer to the statutory appeal under s.127 of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with clause 6.8(d) of the Supply Code, 2005. The Court recorded that the limitation for such appeal is 30 days, permitted filing within 15 days of the order, and directed the appellate authority to dispose of the appeal within six weeks.

cases.title: Smt. Babita v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: assessment-objections-and-appeal
cases.holding: If objections to a defective-meter demand remain pending, the Assessing Authority shall decide them and then issue a bill after complying with the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, subject to deposit of 50% of the demanded amount; if the objections have already been decided, the consumer is to be informed so that an appeal may be filed under Clause 6.8(d).

cases.title: M/s Kisan Chilling Plant v. Appellate Authority/Divisional Commissioner
cases.topic: appeal-disposal-timeline
cases.holding: Clause 6.8(d)(V) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 obliges the appellate authority to decide an assessment appeal within thirty days by a speaking order. Where the Divisional Commissioner had neither entertained the appeal nor fixed a date, the Court directed that authority to hear the appeal with fullest opportunity of hearing and dispose of it by a reasoned speaking order within thirty days of communication of this order.

UP-2005::6.9.code: U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 (with s.126, EA 2003 & Tariff Order)
UP-2005::6.9.topic: Excess load / appliance installation is not 'unauthorised use' under Section 126

cases.title: Kanpur Electricity Supply Co. Ltd. & Anr. v. U.P. Electricity Regulatory Commission & Ors.
cases.topic: Excess load / appliance installation is not 'unauthorised use' under Section 126
cases.holding: It is not Section 126 unauthorised use. Para 6.9 of the Code provides that excess load is not covered by Section 126; the use of an air conditioner is not prohibited but attracts an additional Fixed Charge under the tariff (Rs. 150 per ton, April-September). The CGRF/Ombudsman rightly disallowed the Section 126 assessment and permitted only supplementary Fixed-Charge bills.

cases.title: Kanpur Electricity Supply Co. Ltd. v. Permanent Lok Adalat
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: lok-adalat-bill-under-6.9
cases.holding: The High Court stayed, till the next listing, the Permanent Lok Adalat's direction to prepare a bill in terms of clause 6.9(B)(i) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The licensee's plea that the Lok Adalat lacked jurisdiction to adjudicate a complaint without offering a settlement was not decided. The writ was later dismissed for want of prosecution.

cases.title: Manish Rungta v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: theft-penalty notice — representation to assessing officer
cases.holding: The Court expressed no opinion on whether the 6.7.2018 theft-penalty notice complied with the Supply Code. On the petitioner confining his prayer, he was directed to appear before the Executive Engineer on 6.9.2018 and file a fresh representation/objection; if filed, that authority shall decide it by a speaking order after hearing, in accordance with law, preferably within 15 days. No coercive action shall be taken for 45 days or until disposal of the representation, whichever is earlier.

cases.title: Arvind Chaudhary v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: notice — relegated to representation
cases.holding: Without expressing any opinion on the merits of a challenge to an electricity-department notice alleged to have been issued in breach of the Supply Code, 2005, the writ was disposed of by directing the consumer to appear before the Executive Engineer on 6 September 2018 and file a fresh representation/objection, to be decided by a speaking order after hearing in accordance with law, preferably within 15 days; coercive action was stayed for 45 days or until that decision, whichever was earlier.
cases.flag: order cites the Supply Code 2005 generally; 6.9 is the catalog hit, not numbered in the order

cases.title: Petitioner v. U.P. Electricity Regulatory Commission
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: load enhancement
cases.holding: Without expressing any opinion on merits, the writ was disposed of with a direction to respondent No. 3 to decide the petitioner's pending application for enhancement of load from 80 HP to 140 HP under Clause 6.9 within four weeks of communication of the order; levy of excess demand penalty would abide that decision.

cases.title: Executive Engineer, Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. The Electricity Consumer Grievances Redressal Forum & Anr.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: Paragraph 6.9 overload assessment cannot be projected over 51 months from a short check-meter spell
cases.holding: No. The licensee invoked paragraph 6.9 to demand overload for 51 months. The Forum held that an average-overload assessment for 51 months (15.43 kW) was not in consonance with the rules, consumption varying month to month, and that excess load ought to have been billed in the monthly bills at the Commission tariff. The High Court, after also considering the Chief Engineer's 2 March 2013 letter reciting the Managing Director's direction that under the Supply Code, 2005, revenue assessment can be made for a maximum of one year, held it was not open to raise the overload demand for 51 months. Independently, the Chief Engineer's 9 March 2013 letter admitted the check meter was defective. There was no infirmity in the Forum's order setting aside the demand.
cases.flag: Source PDF page 1 is an 8.11.2013 listing order (V.K. Shukla and Suneet Kumar, JJ.). The operative disposal is 20.11.2025. The judgment labels the quoted provision 'Section 5.6 of the Electricity Act, 2003' but the extract is Section 56(2). The Forum's reference to the demand letter as dated 07.09.2022 is a slip for 07.09.2012 (para 1). Inspection figures '787 Kw' / '255 kw' are interrupted by a cause-title overlay; the Forum proceeded on an average overload of 15.43 kW.

cases.title: Babu Khan v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing dispute — statutory complaint
cases.holding: A writ petition that challenges the correctness of an electricity bill and a citation issued on that bill cannot be entertained; the remedy is an appropriate complaint under paragraph 6.9 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Writ against Clause 6.9 load-increase direction premature pending s.126(3) objection
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: writ-against-load-increase-premature-pending-s126-objection
cases.holding: A writ petition against a direction under Clause 6.9 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 to increase electricity load is premature while the consumer's objection under Section 126(3) of the Electricity Act, 2003 remains pending. Once that objection is decided, the consumer's remedy is an appeal under Section 127.

cases.title: Jai Vaishno Rice Mill v. Ram Sanehi Yadav
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
cases.topic: contempt-compliance
cases.holding: Where a writ court had directed the consumer to make a representation under Section 615 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, to be considered and decided on deposit of Rs 1,50,000 with restoration of supply, and the licensee showed that the complaint had been considered and decided, the civil contempt petition alleging non-compliance is dismissed and notices stand discharged.
cases.flag: ambiguous_clause

UP-2005::7(1)(3).topic: new connection — refusal for premises dispute — alternative complaint remedy

cases.title: Smt. Sushma Devi v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: new connection — refusal for premises dispute — alternative complaint remedy
cases.holding: Where the licensee has refused a prepaid electricity connection on the ground of a dispute regarding the premises, a writ of mandamus to compel the connection is not entertained. The consumer's remedy is a representation or complaint under Clause 7(1)(3) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, which the concerned authority is to decide preferably within 30 days of filing.
cases.flag: order cites 'Clause 7 (1) (3)'; numbering left as written

cases.title: Amit Gupta v. The Electricity Ombudsman
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: demand-charge-refund-writ
cases.holding: A writ seeking quash of Ombudsman and CGRF orders and mandamus for refund of excess demand charges under Annexure-7.1 of the Supply Code was dismissed: after perusing the record in the petitioner's absence, the Court found no case for interference and treated the petition as infructuous or not pressed.

cases.title: Pachani Devi v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: CGRF alternative remedy; writ withdrawn as not pressed
cases.holding: Where the licensee objects that the consumer has an alternative remedy before the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum under Clause 7.1 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and the writ petitioner withdraws with liberty to approach the Forum, the writ is disposed of as not pressed with that liberty, and the Forum shall consider and decide an application under Clause 7.1 within two weeks of presentation.

cases.title: Kanpur Electricity Supply Co. v. U.P. Electricity Regulatory Commission
cases.topic: meter-replacement-delay-penalty
cases.holding: Findings of fact that the change-of-meter fee was deposited on 4 March 2008 and the meter replaced only on 22 March 2011 after nearly three years admit of no interference; consequential action under Electricity Supply Code 7.1, including the Rs 50 per day fine on the Executive Engineer for that delay, does not warrant interference.

UP-2005::7.10.code: U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 (with s.42(5)-(7), EA 2003; UPERC (CGRF & Ombudsman) Regulations)
UP-2005::7.10.topic: Only the consumer, not the Distribution Licensee, may approach the Forum or the Ombudsman

cases.title: M.K. Pathak, Executive Engineer v. The Electricity Ombudsman & Ors.
cases.topic: Only the consumer, not the Distribution Licensee, may approach the Forum or the Ombudsman
cases.holding: No. Clause 7.10 of the Code and Section 42(5)-(7) of the Act, on a plain reading, entitle only the consumer to file a complaint before the Forum and, if aggrieved by non-redressal, a representation before the Ombudsman; this right is not given to the Electricity Distribution Licensee. The licensee/its officers therefore have no authority in law to approach the Ombudsman once the Forum has decided the consumer's complaint, and the Ombudsman commits no error of law in dismissing such a representation, even on its merits.

cases.title: M/S Three Star Paper Mills Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P. & 5 Ors.
cases.topic: A consumer who accepted a One Time Settlement covering 'all pending matters' is estopped from later reviving one of the settled disputes through the CGRF/Ombudsman route
cases.holding: No. The consumer's own representation accepting the One Time Settlement made clear it was 'ready to settle its ALL pending matters' by paying the agreed principal sum; the licensee accepted this and waived more than Rs. 78 lakh of accrued surcharge. Having obtained that benefit on the basis that all disputes stood settled, the consumer is estopped from raising the 10%-rebate dispute afresh before the Redressal Forum/Ombudsman; both correctly rejected the claim.

cases.title: Om Prakash v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.topic: A billing grievance pending before the District Consumer Forum should instead be routed through the licensee's Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum and, if unresolved, the Ombudsman under Clause 7.10
cases.holding: The petitioner was permitted to withdraw his writ petition and his pending District Consumer Forum complaint in order to approach the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum under Clause 7.10 of the Supply Code; the concerned authority was directed to decide the grievance, if presented within 15 days, as expeditiously as possible and not later than 8 weeks from presentation of a certified copy of the order.

cases.title: Basant Lal v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: statutory-remedy-billing-objections
cases.holding: A consumer who challenges an electricity demand notice or bill in writ must first avail the statutory remedy under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 of raising objections against the bill or charges; a request to deposit in installments may be considered by the Executive Engineer. The demand was not quashed.

cases.title: Parvez Akhtar v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing grievance — Clause 7.10 forum route after written reasons
cases.holding: Where a consumer challenges a modified electricity bill and the licensee undertakes to supply the calculations and reasons, the Executive Engineer is to inform the entire details through a written order within a week after considering the consumer's representation as earlier directed. After receipt of that communication, if still aggrieved, the consumer may approach the competent authority under Clause 7.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ is disposed without adjudicating the demand.

cases.title: Rais Ahmad v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: CGRF and Ombudsman as alternate remedy for billing grievance
cases.holding: The Court declined to entertain the writ because Clause 7.10 of the 2005 Code provides a consumer grievance redressal forum and a further route to the Ombudsman; if the petitioner files his grievance before the forum within 15 days, it shall be disposed of within six weeks.

cases.title: M/s Raja Ram Ispat Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: penalty dispute — CGRF
cases.holding: If the consumer disputes the factual imposition of penalty, the remedy is to approach the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum under clause 7.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the High Court will not entertain a writ for that cause of action. A complaint so filed is to be decided expeditiously.

cases.title: M/s Three Star Paper Mills Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: statutory-remedy-billing-grievance
cases.holding: Where a consumer seeks quashing of an electricity-bill order and a rebate, Clause 7.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is the statutory remedy; the writ petition is dismissed with liberty to pursue that forum.

cases.title: Ved Prakash v. President, U.P. Electricity Regulatory Commission
cases.topic: ombudsman-forum
cases.holding: A grievance of the kind raised in the petitioner's representation against the Consumer Forum decision is not for the U.P. Electricity Regulatory Commission; it is to be raised before the Ombudsman under clause 7.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ is disposed with liberty to apply to the Ombudsman, who shall dispose of the claim expeditiously, preferably within three months of production of a certified copy of this order.

cases.title: Om Prakash v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: alternative remedy — CGRF and Ombudsman
cases.holding: A consumer faced with a demand for electricity arrears and a recovery citation after a permanent disconnection has a statutory remedy before the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum and the Ombudsman under clause 7.10 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ petition was dismissed on that ground of alternative remedy.

cases.title: Ved Prakash v. State of U.P. — second writ against recovery citation dismissed after Clause 7.10 Ombudsman direction
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: ombudsman-forum-second-writ
cases.holding: Where the High Court has already directed the consumer to approach the Ombudsman under Clause 7.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, a second writ petition for the same cause of action challenging a recovery citation issued pursuant to the assessment order is not maintainable; the citation discloses no error.

cases.title: Chandra Shekhar Tiwari v. U.P. Power Corporation
cases.topic: forum for disputed dues and connection grievance
cases.holding: Where a consumer seeking an electricity connection contests the licensee's demand of arrears and a provisional theft assessment, the High Court will not decide the disputed quantum in writ jurisdiction and will permit the consumer to take recourse to the Consumer Dispute Redressal Forum constituted under Clause 7.10 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, which is expected to deal with the matter expeditiously and in accordance with law.

cases.title: Akhilesh Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: forum-ombudsman route for supply grievances
cases.holding: A grievance in respect of supply of electricity is to be taken to the Ombudsman/Consumer Dispute Redressal Forum constituted under Clause 7.10 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ was disposed of with liberty to approach that forum, which was to look into any complaint and decide it by a reasoned speaking order.

cases.title: Mithilesh Kumar v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: forum route for billing and recovery grievances
cases.holding: A writ challenging a recovery citation for electricity dues is not decided on merits where clause 7.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 affords an alternative remedy; the consumer is to take the grievance to the State Forum, which, if approached within fifteen days, shall decide the case within one month.

cases.title: Dharmendra Singh v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.topic: forum-route-for-billing-grievances
cases.holding: A writ challenging a recovery citation for electricity dues is disposed of because an alternative and efficacious remedy is available under Clause 7.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; if the consumer files his case before the State Forum within fifteen days, the Forum shall decide it within one month of filing.

cases.title: Surya Narayan v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: CGRF sequential after licensee decides complaint
cases.holding: Clause 7.10(ii)–(iii) require the licensee to decide a consumer's complaint first. Only if the licensee fails to settle within the Code time limits, or the consumer is dissatisfied with that decision, may the consumer approach CGRF. Where no order has been passed on a pending representation, the licensee cannot plead CGRF as an alternative remedy. Non-adjustment of Rs 27,530 already deposited against a later bill is not a clause 6.5 inaccuracy dispute. Executive Engineer, PuVVNL, Pipri directed to decide the representation dated 6.7.2015 within 15 days; if still aggrieved, the petitioner may then move CGRF under clause 7.10.

cases.title: Kanti Prasad v. Dakshinanchal Vidut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: forum-ombudsman-route-for-connection-denial
cases.holding: Where an Executive Engineer has refused a new electricity connection, the consumer's remedy is to approach the District Grievance Redressal Forum under Regulation 7.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 and thereafter the Ombudsman; a writ petition is dismissed on that alternative-remedy ground.

cases.title: Ram Bhawan Singh v. Chief Managing Director, U.P. Power Corp.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: CGRF as forum for grievance against further connections from a transformer
cases.holding: Where a consumer objects to the licensee releasing further connections from an installed transformer, that grievance is to be raised before the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum as contemplated in clause 7.10 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the High Court will dispose of the writ leaving that statutory remedy open.

cases.title: Brajesh Kumar v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing-grievance-forum
cases.holding: A writ petition challenging electricity bills is not entertained where the consumer has a remedy to raise the billing dispute under clause 7.10 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the petition is dismissed on that alternate remedy.

cases.title: Abdul Kalaam v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: CGRF and Ombudsman route for billing grievances
cases.holding: The U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is a self-contained code. Where a consumer is aggrieved by the licensee's action on a revised bill, including alleged non-adjustment of past deposits, the High Court will not enter disputed questions of fact and will leave the consumer to the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum and Ombudsman under clause 7.10. The licensee is obliged to set up that Forum in accordance with the UPERC (Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum & Ombudsman) Regulations, 2003, and the Forum was functional.

cases.title: Rajveer Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: alternative remedy before consumer forum
cases.holding: A writ petitioner who challenges an electricity recovery citation that has not been issued against him has no cause of action under Article 226. In any event, clause 7.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 furnishes an alternative and efficacious remedy before the appropriate forum, where all grounds taken in the writ may be raised, and the High Court will not interfere.

cases.title: Shyam Sunder Luthara v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: liberty to CGRF and Ombudsman on not-pressed writ
cases.holding: Where the petitioner does not press a writ and seeks liberty to approach the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum and the Ombudsman under clause 7.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, the High Court may dispose of the petition as not pressed and grant that liberty without deciding the merits of the supply dispute.

cases.title: Kaushal Kishor v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: new connection — disputed security — CGRF/Ombudsman
cases.holding: A dispute over the quantum of security demanded for grant of a new power connection cannot be entertained under Article 226. The consumer may approach the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum and the Ombudsman under clause 7.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If the petitioner deposits the demanded security of Rs.1,02,510, the licensee shall process the application for connection.

cases.title: Licensee has no para 7.10 appeal; CGRF prepaid-meter award stayed
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: licensee appeal from CGRF
cases.holding: Para 7.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 confers a remedy of appeal on the consumer, not on the licensee or a person standing in that position. Agra Development Authority, not being a consumer, had no such appeal against the CGRF award directing removal of a prepaid meter, and the writ was entertained.

cases.title: S.N. Singh v. State of U.P. and Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: cgrf-ombudsman-billing-grievance
cases.holding: Where a consumer remains dissatisfied with the Executive Engineer's disposal of a billing grievance (here, that check-meter and main-meter readings were identical), the writ court will not entertain the petition because clause 7.10 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 supplies a statutory remedy before the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum and the Ombudsman.

cases.title: Niho Scotish Garden Residents Welfare Association v. U.P. Electricity Regulatory Commission
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: Ombudsman jurisdiction
cases.holding: Prima facie, the controversy could not be considered by the Ombudsman under Clause 7.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ was later dismissed for want of prosecution without a merits ruling; any interim order stood discharged.

cases.title: Smt. Mona Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: cgrf-after-6.5-rejection
cases.holding: After rejection of a Clause 6.5 application for correction of electricity bills, the consumer’s remedy is a complaint before the Electricity Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum under Clause 7.10; a writ against the 6.5 rejection is not the proper course. The petition was dismissed, with a direction that if a Clause 7.10 complaint is filed and ₹50,000 is deposited with the licensee, the connection shall be restored within a week.

cases.title: M/s Pawan Putra Ice and Cold Storage v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: alternative remedy — CGRF and Ombudsman for recovery of electricity dues
cases.holding: A writ petition challenging recovery of outstanding electricity dues will not be entertained when the petitioner has a statutory alternative remedy under Clause 7.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 of approaching the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum and Ombudsman, before which the factual dispute can be effectively gone into; the petition is dismissed with liberty to invoke Clause 7.10 if so advised.

cases.title: Hariom v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: alternative remedy — CGRF and Ombudsman for billing grievance
cases.holding: The Court accepted the licensee's objection that a writ challenging an electricity notice and seeking a corrected bill is not maintainable because clause 7.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 provides an alternative remedy before the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum and the Ombudsman. Without expressing any opinion on merits, the writ was disposed of with liberty to approach the Forum; on such approach with a certified copy of the order, the Forum is to do the needful in accordance with law by a reasoned speaking order. The petitioner may also seek interim relief, which if applied for is to be concluded within three weeks of filing.

cases.title: Mahant Satyanam Das v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: cgrf-forum-route
cases.holding: A complainant may take the complaint before the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum under clause 7.10 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the High Court was not inclined to entertain the writ at that stage and dismissed it.

cases.title: Ejaj Ahmad v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: CGRF for urban-versus-rural tariff billing grievance
cases.holding: A grievance that the licensee is charging urban electricity rates for a business place claimed to be in a rural area is to be taken to the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum under clause 7.10 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If the consumer files an application or representation before the Forum within 15 days, it shall be decided in accordance with law, and no coercive action may be taken until that decision.

cases.title: Manoj Kumar Sharma v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: withdrawal of writ with liberty to CGRF
cases.holding: A writ petition may be dismissed as withdrawn where the consumer seeks, and is granted, liberty to approach the Consumer Redressal Forum under Clause 7.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, without a decision on the merits of the grievance.

cases.title: Kasturi Bai Gopi Babu Cold Storage Pvt. Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: cgrf-alternative-remedy-bars-writ
cases.holding: A writ challenging a licensee's order and demand notice and seeking a speaking order under the Supply Code is not maintainable where the consumer has the alternative remedy of approaching the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum under clause 7.10 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the petition is dismissed on that ground when the petitioner does not dispute the forum.
cases.flag: Order styles clause 7.10 as 'Section 7.10'.

cases.title: M/S Maa Narheji Agro Industries v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: CGRF and Ombudsman as alternate remedy for billing grievances
cases.holding: A consumer whose grievance of an incorrect electricity bill has been decided by the Executive Engineer may challenge that order before the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum in accordance with clause 7.10 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, with a further remedy of representation before the Ombudsman; the High Court will not exercise writ jurisdiction in the face of that alternate remedy and will dispose of the petition with liberty to avail those forums.

cases.title: Vipin Kalanamak Factory Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P. (demand notice / cl. 7.10 CGRF)
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: cgrf-route-for-billing-recovery
cases.holding: A consumer challenging a distribution licensee's demand notice and a Tehsildar recovery citation has an adequate remedy under clause 7.10 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 before the Consumer Redressal Forum, which may also grant interim orders. The writ was disposed of with a direction that if the petitioner approaches the Forum within 15 days, the Forum shall consider and decide the matter by a reasoned and speaking order within three months of production of a certified copy of this order.

cases.title: M/S Pawan Putra Ice And Cold Storage v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: Ombudsman as alternative remedy for billing dispute
cases.holding: A consumer disputing an electricity bill under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 has an efficacious remedy of approaching the Ombudsman under clause 7.10; the High Court will not entertain a writ while that remedy remains available.

cases.title: Raghuraj Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: CGRF route for disputed consumer identity and tube-well arrears recovery
cases.holding: Disputed questions of fact as to whether a family settlement transferred a tube-well electricity connection from the recorded consumer to the petitioner, and thus whether the petitioner is liable for arrears, cannot be decided in writ proceedings. The petitioner is to file a complaint before the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum under Clause 7.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the Forum shall decide after hearing both sides in accordance with law. Recovery pursuant to the impugned citation remains stayed for three months or until the Forum decides, whichever is earlier.

cases.title: Surendra Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: CGRF remedy for demand-notice grievance
cases.holding: A writ challenging a demand notice on the plea that final assessment was made without serving a provisional assessment or affording a hearing raises disputed questions of fact not suited to writ jurisdiction; the consumer's remedy is a representation to the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum under Clause 7.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The Forum was directed to decide such a representation, filed within two weeks, within a further four weeks after hearing all parties, and recovery under the 21.11.2017 demand was kept in abeyance for two months or until the Forum decides.

cases.title: Gaya Prasad v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & 3 Others
cases.topic: Disputed fact of post-disconnection usage belongs to the Clause 7.10 forum, not writ
cases.holding: It is a disputed question of fact (a spot inspection found the meter missing but the consumer residing and using supply) that the writ court will not decide. Clause 7.10 provides the first-instance CGRF/Ombudsman route for such billing grievances. The Court declined interference but gave liberty to approach the Executive Engineer with a Rs. 25,000 draft, on which the recovery would be stayed pending a reasoned decision, to be recovered only if usage is found.

cases.title: Veerendra Kumar Jain v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.topic: Billing grievance (duplicate bills) belongs to the Clause 7.10 CGRF/Ombudsman route
cases.holding: It is for the Clause 7.10 forum. The consumer is relegated to the CGRF/Ombudsman under Clause 7.10 (the forum being noted on the bill), his application to be decided on merits within 45 days; the interim order continues until then.

cases.title: Foran Singh v. Executive Engineer, Dakshiranchal Vidyut Vitaran Distribution Division, Firozabad and Another
cases.topic: Consumer relegated to the Code's complaint / CGRF grievance remedy against a recovery/representation order
cases.holding: The writ prayers become infructuous, and the consumer's remedy against the order deciding the representation lies under Clause 7.10 r/w Clauses 7.7.1 to 7.7.5 of the Code: a complaint to the licensee and, if the licensee fails to settle or the consumer is dissatisfied, a complaint before the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum. The Court disposed of the writ leaving that remedy open.

cases.title: M/S Ambuja Cements Limited v. Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Limited
cases.topic: Licensee's objection that a Code-imposed penalty must go to CGRF/Ombudsman under Clause 7.10, not to a s.11 arbitrator — raised, not decided
cases.holding: Not decided. The licensee so objected, invoking Clause 7.10 of the Code, Clauses 7.7.1–7.7.5 of the UPERC CGRF & Ombudsman Regulations, 2003, and the Cost Data Book. The Court, in a Section 11 proceeding confined to the existence of an arbitration agreement, appointed a sole arbitrator without ruling on that objection, and expressly left it open to the opposite party to raise all objections the Act permits before the arbitrator. This case is not authority that Clause 7.10 ousts contractual arbitration, nor that it does not.
cases.flag: Peripheral to the Supply-Code core: a s.11 appointment order. Indexed under Clause 7.10 only because that clause was the licensee's maintainability objection; the Court made no construction of it. Respondent also referred to 'U.P. Electricity Act, 2003' (the 2003 Act is the central Electricity Act) — recorded, not merged.

cases.title: Amar Nath Vidya Ashram & Anr. v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: Post-deposit technical billing dispute (MF change on amalgamation; mixed commercial/domestic load) belongs to the Clause 7.10 CGRF/Ombudsman
cases.holding: It is for the Clause 7.10 forum. After deposit of the amount claimed in the demand notice dated 18.10.2017, the remaining issue is a technical one best addressed by the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum / Ombudsman under paragraph 7.10 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The petitioner may file a complaint before that forum, which shall consider and decide it expeditiously, preferably within three months from the date a certified copy of the order is filed with the complaint. Subject to that, the writ petition stands disposed of.
cases.flag: Source PDF also contains listing orders of 19.3.2018 (interim non-disconnection if the stated Rs 20 lakh deposit was made), 13.3.2024, 22.4.2024 and 15.1.2025; the operative disposal is 7.2.2025.

cases.title: Ekta Malviya v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.topic: CGRF as forum for billing and meter grievances
cases.holding: Where a challenge to an Executive Engineer's order and a prayer to stop meter billing, install a new meter, and issue a correct bill raise several disputed questions of fact, the writ is not amenable to Article 226 jurisdiction. The consumer is to be relegated to the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum under clause 7.10 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and was directed to apply within two weeks, the Forum to decide within eight weeks after hearing.

cases.title: Harishchandra v. State of U.P. and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: alternative remedy — Clause 7.10 appeal; writ not maintainable
cases.holding: The Court held the dispute was not amenable to writ jurisdiction and relegated the petitioner to the alternative remedy under Clause 7.10 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, directing him to file an appeal within two weeks, to be decided within eight weeks after opportunity of hearing to the petitioner and other relevant persons.

cases.title: Sudhanshu Dhar Tripathi v. State of Uttar Pradesh
cases.topic: CGRF route after Clause 6.5 order
cases.holding: The petitioner was directed to approach the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum under Clause 7.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, within two weeks. If such an application is filed within that time, CGRF shall grant an opportunity of hearing and pass a reasoned order in accordance with law within eight weeks of filing.

cases.title: Madan Kumar Vishkerma v. State of U.P. & 4 Others
cases.topic: Second writ on a demand already relegated to CGRF; alleged non-functioning and misaddressed complaint; complaint placed before the sitting Forum
cases.holding: No. Instructions dated 06.02.2025 of the Presiding Officer showed the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum, Varanasi, sitting at 64-Chandrika Nagar, Sigra, Varanasi. The petitioner's complaint had been sent to a wrong address. Licensee's counsel was directed to place the complaint (Annexure-2) before that Presiding Officer; the petitioner to appear on 25.02.2025 and be heard; the Forum to endeavour to complete the hearing within one month. The writ petition was disposed of with those observations.
cases.flag: Source PDF contains the 22.1.2025 listing (neutral citation 2025:AHC:21619-DB) and this 14.2.2025 disposal. The listing quotes the 17.1.2024 order in Writ-C No. 27208 of 2023 (para 3 of the listing also calls that writ 37208 of 2023), which had classified carry-forward of erstwhile tenant dues as Clause 7.7.4 and dues/new connection as Clause 7.7.2 and relegated under Clause 7.10(ii)–(iii). This Court did not re-decide those classifications.

cases.title: M/s Akanksha Steels Pvt. Ltd. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Others
cases.topic: Billing grievance on a permanent-disconnection demand belongs to CGRF under Clause 7.10
cases.holding: No. Factual issues raised in the writ can more appropriately be examined by the competent forum under Clause 7.10. The writ is disposed of with liberty to the petitioner to approach the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum, with a certified copy of the order, within three weeks; if such a grievance is raised, the Forum shall pass appropriate orders in terms of the statutory scheme within two months thereafter.
cases.flag: Source PDF also contains listing and adjournment orders from 11.8.2010 through 2.5.2023 (illness slips; time for counter and rejoinder). The operative disposal is 11.7.2025 (neutral citation 2025:AHC:111280-DB).

cases.title: Leelawati Devi v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: forum-ombudsman-route
cases.holding: A writ petition may be disposed of as withdrawn with liberty to the petitioner to file an appeal under Clause 7.10 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Ghangas Breeding Farm And Hatchery v. State of Uttar Pradesh
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: forum-ombudsman-route-for-billing-grievances
cases.holding: Once a Clause 6.5 application has been rejected, the consumer's remedy against the bill is to approach the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum under Clause 7.10 of the Supply Code, 2005. The writ is dismissed with liberty to file before the Forum within two weeks; the Forum is to decide within three months; recovery under the impugned bill is stayed till disposal of that application, failing which the licensee may proceed in accordance with law.

cases.title: Ram Bhawan Singh v. Chief Managing Director, U.P. Power Corporation
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: CGRF/forum route for grievances
cases.holding: Where a similar grievance had already been directed to the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum under paragraph 7.10 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, the petitioner was permitted to withdraw the subsequent writ and avail that 7.10 remedy. If the grievance is raised within two weeks with a certified copy of the order, the competent authority shall take an appropriate decision in accordance with law, after notice to the party aggrieved, expeditiously.

cases.title: Arun Kumar Rai v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: cgrf-forum-as-alternative-remedy
cases.holding: A person aggrieved by disconnection or other action of the electricity department has a remedy before the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum under clause 7.10 of the Electricity Supply Code. Where that forum is available, and a civil appeal against the decree that prompted mutation and disconnection is also pending, the High Court will not interfere in writ jurisdiction.

cases.title: Babita Sharma v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: alternative remedy — CGRF and Ombudsman
cases.holding: Against an Executive Engineer's communication, Clause 7.10 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 supplies an efficacious alternative remedy before the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum and Ombudsman, including where facts are in dispute; Article 226 interference is declined. Subject to the consumer availing that remedy (styled as appeal) within three weeks, it is to be dealt with and decided without a limitation objection and as expeditiously as possible.

cases.title: M/S Devi Charan Cold Storage Tirwa v. Executive Engineer & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: accounting/payment dispute over dishonoured-cheque arrears is for the Clause 7.10 Forum/Ombudsman, not the writ court
cases.holding: No. The issue involves accounting and disputed questions regarding payment of electricity dues. The petitioner has a statutory alternative remedy before the District Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum as per Clause 7.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and if still aggrieved may approach the Electricity Ombudsman under the same provision. The writ is dismissed on the ground of alternative remedy and any interim order stands vacated.
cases.flag: Source PDF concatenates listing orders of 13.11.2018, 29.11.2018, 6.12.2018, 8.1.2019, 28.1.2019, 22.2.2019, 11.3.2019 and 25.3.2019; the operative disposal is 8.8.2019.

cases.title: The Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Anr. v. The Electricity Ombudsman of U.P. & Anr.
cases.topic: CGRF and Ombudsman are competent once a billing complaint to the licensee is not settled
cases.holding: No. Clause 7.10 obliges the licensee to set up CGRF; a consumer aggrieved by the licensee's action on matters in Clauses 7.7.1 to 7.7.5 may complain to the licensee; CGRF may be approached if the licensee fails to settle within the Code or Regulations time-limits or the consumer is not satisfied with the licensee's decision; and a representation then lies to the Ombudsman. After the supplementary counter affidavit it stood accepted that a 7 July 2007 request for two weeks' time was never acceded to, that a 29 July 2007 application for bill correction received no decision, and that a further complaint of 27 September 2007 was also undecided. The CGRF complaint of 2 February 2008 was therefore competent. CGRF, asked on 4 March 2008 to decide within the stipulated time, failed to do so; the 24 April 2008 representation to the Ombudsman was in order, and the Ombudsman's authority to decide the dispute cannot be disputed.
cases.flag: Source PDF concatenates listing orders of 19.2.2010, 8.3.2010, 23.4.2010, 30.4.2010, 7.5.2010, 8.7.2010, 15.7.2010 and 22.7.2010 (V.K. Shukla, J.); the operative judgment is 23.07.2010 (unnumbered 6-page body; paras assigned 1–12 in reading order). Internal date '02.02.2088' for the CGRF complaint is treated as 02.02.2008. Catalog false-positives (UP-2005::6.5(a)/(b)/6.5B; UP-2005::7.7 as a free-standing holding; clause-6.5-objection-must-be-in-proper-form; clause-6.5b-quantification-dispute) are not used.

cases.title: The Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Anr. v. The Electricity Ombudsman of U.P. & Anr.
cases.topic: Ombudsman may treat a meter as defective on consumption pattern without a Code testing request
cases.holding: No. The Ombudsman's authority is wide enough to pass an order on the facts. It considered the consumption pattern, found the recorded reading on the excessive side (more than ten times ordinary consumption), and noted that no commercial or industrial activity was carried on at the ashram and that no reason justifying such a rise had been given. The Code does prescribe a procedure for holding a meter defective and assessing bills where accuracy of readings is disputed, but the licensee never asked the Ombudsman to have the meter checked. On the record the petitioners themselves produced, the Ombudsman formed the opinion that the meter was defective on the face of it. A conscious, reasoned order is not interfered with. The writ petition is dismissed.

cases.title: M/s Gogi Ice & Cold Storage v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: alternative statutory remedy
cases.holding: A writ against the distribution licensee is dismissed where clause 7.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 affords a statutory alternative remedy, which the consumer must pursue first; any interim order stands discharged.

cases.title: Abdul Kalaam v. Purvanchal Vidhyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: excess billing — 30-day objection before writ
cases.holding: Para 7.10 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 provides that a consumer complaining of excess billing may raise an objection within 30 days of the alleged excess bill, which is then required to be corrected. A writ claiming refund of alleged overpayment over six years, without a stated calculation basis or departmental admission of excess, was dismissed. Any future billing complaint must first be protested under the Code before approaching the Court.
cases.flag: Court cited para 7.10 for the 30-day excess-bill objection (substance of cl. 7.10(i)).

cases.title: Shri H.C. Shukla v. KESCO
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: ombudsman-alternate-remedy
cases.holding: Where, after the writ was argued at some length, the petitioner elected to seek his remedy before the Electricity Ombudsman under clause 7.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 at the first instance, the Court dismissed the writ with liberty to pursue that remedy and discharged any interim order.

cases.title: Badri Prasad v. State of U.P. & Anr.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: CGRF as forum for supply grievances; writ declined for disputed facts
cases.holding: Relief sought in the writ can be gone into by the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum under clause 7.10 of the Electricity Supply Code. The petitioner is relegated to apply to the Forum. Without expressing any opinion on merits, the Court declined to interfere because disputed questions of fact were involved. Deposits already made shall be adjusted by the Forum, which shall also consider restoration of electricity after deposit of the amount it directs, in accordance with law.

cases.title: Jay Prakash v. Executive Engineer (City), U.P. Power Corp. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: grievance-redressal-committee-alternate-remedy
cases.holding: Where a Grievance Redressal Committee has been constituted under clause 7.10 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, a consumer writ petition is dismissed and the petitioner is relegated to file his case before that Committee.

cases.title: M. Das Binani (Binani Dharmshala) v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: CGRF as forum for billing grievances
cases.holding: Where a consumer who has paid a one-time settlement bill alleges excess charging and seeks refund, clause 7.10 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 supplies the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum as the forum for that grievance, and the writ court will not entertain the dispute on merits. If the petitioners approach the Forum within one month with a certified copy of the order, the Forum shall consider and decide the complaint expeditiously on merits without taking any objection as to delay.

cases.title: Smt. Vijai Laxmi v. State of U.P. and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: fresh connection on disputed existing service
cases.holding: On a consumer's claim that no electricity connection exists in her premises, a bill in her name recording disconnection is inconsistent with that claim. The Court will not mandamus a fresh connection on that disputed record and will instead require the consumer to apply under clause 7.10 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If the application is made within seven days of a certified copy, the authority must consider and dispose of it within fifteen days, and if it finds the cause genuine, give the connection immediately.

cases.title: Krishna Gopal Pandey v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: connection estimate — writ vs CGRF
cases.holding: A dispute over the licensee's estimate for an electricity connection cannot be decided on the writ side. Section 42(5) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with clause 7.10 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 (and the 2007 Regulations) is the appropriate forum for such factual grievances; the writ was dismissed with liberty to proceed in accordance with law.

cases.title: Ajay Kumar v. State of U.P. and others
cases.topic: consent payment of bill; future disputes to Consumer Redressal Forum
cases.holding: The writ is disposed of on the corporation's acceptance of the petitioner's offer: he shall pay the annexure-7 bill of Rs. 81,629 within one month of obtaining a certified copy. After payment, any future dispute may be taken to the Consumer Redressal Forum under clause 7.10. If no other bill is raised within one month after that payment, the corporation's claim is to be treated as settled fully and finally.
cases.flag: Order cites 'U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2001'; operative code is 2005. Clause 7.10 otherwise as numbered.

cases.title: Shashi Devi v. State of U.P. and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: disconnection-billing-grievance-forum
cases.holding: Because supply had been disconnected, the petitioner was entitled to hearing and disposal under Clause 7.10. The grievance was to be made within seven days of the certified copy; the authority was to decide within 15 days; and if the grievance was genuine and she deposited the sum payable, reconnection could be directed within 72 hours. The writ was disposed of at admission without costs.
cases.flag: Court directed the Regulatory Commission to decide a Clause 7.10 grievance (forum/ombudsman route).

cases.title: Shaphalata Jain v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: alternative forum — CGRF and Ombudsman
cases.holding: The Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum and Ombudsman under clause 7.10 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005, are an alternative forum for adjudication of the consumer's grievance; the High Court will not interfere in writ where that route is available, even if the authority has already considered the grievance. Dismissal of the writ does not affect the petitioner's right to approach the authority for early disposal, and that authority must carefully consider the civil court decree and the petitioner's possession.

cases.title: Devendra v. Superintendent Engineer
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: alternative remedy — CGRF and Ombudsman
cases.holding: Where the Executive Engineer has already considered the consumer's grievance, the High Court will not interfere in writ; the alternative forum is the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum and the Ombudsman under clause 7.10 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The dismissal does not affect the right to approach that forum for early disposal, and the forum must carefully go into any civil court decree and the petitioner's possession.

cases.title: Ram Shringar v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: CGRF for disputed bill after claimed permanent disconnection
cases.holding: The Court was hesitant to accept that permanent disconnection had not been effected when no bill was raised from 2004 until a sudden 2011 demand of Rs. 79,414, which did not appear reasonable. It declined to direct the petitioner to pay that amount, directed him to keep it in a separate account, and remitted the dispute to the Consumer Grievances Redressal Forum under clause 7.10 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005, for hearing and resolution within two months of communication of the order. The writ petition was disposed of without costs.

cases.title: Birendra Kumar Arya v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: consumer-redressal-forum
cases.holding: The Court disposed of the writ at admission without interfering with the Electricity Department's stand on disconnection, recording that the order would not affect the petitioner's right to apply to the Consumer Redressal Forum under clause 7.10 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Tej Ram Singh v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: consumer-forum-alternate-remedy
cases.holding: A writ attacking a licensee's disconnection order as illegal and dehors the Supply Code may be disposed of at admission without a merits determination against the department; that disposal does not affect the consumer's right to apply to the Consumer Redressal Forum under clause 7.10 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
