cases.flag: Para 8 cites the Supply Code as 2006; the Code is 2005.

cases.title: Neena Rani v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: indemnity bond as condition of new connection
cases.holding: On the licensee's statement, a new connection shall be released within two weeks of the applicant furnishing a bond in the proper format under Annexure 4.2 of the Supply Code. A later recall by a non-party claiming possession was refused: a pending title suit against the original allottee was not decided, and the connection direction did not itself confer any right on the consumer.

cases.title: Ramesh Chandra Chaurasia v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: billing-dispute-cgrf
cases.holding: A consumer disputing electricity bills and recovery on the ground of a meter fault must raise the dispute before the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum under the Electricity Act, 2003 read with the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the writ court will not decide such a billing dispute and will dispose of the petition by directing that a proper CGRF application, if filed, be decided preferably within two months.

cases.title: Hasmat Ullah v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: alternate remedy — Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum
cases.holding: Where an electricity grievance can be redressed by the Grievance Redressal Forum constituted under the Electricity Supply Code of the Power Corporation (framed under the Electricity Act), the High Court will not entertain a writ petition and will relegate the petitioner to that Consumer Redressal Forum.

UP-2005::additional-load.topic: unsanctioned additional load — objection and speaking order

cases.title: Unsanctioned additional load notice remanded for speaking order
cases.topic: unsanctioned additional load — objection and speaking order
cases.holding: Where an Executive Engineer concludes, without the consumer's written objections, that additional load is being used beyond what is sanctioned or permissible and directs completion of formalities on pain of coercive action, the consumer must be given an opportunity to file objection and the authority must deal with factual and legal points, including U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 contentions, by a speaking order. The writ court will not keep the petition pending; a short stay of coercive action may accompany the remand.

UP-2005::assessment.topic: consideration of objection before final assessment

cases.title: Suresh Singh v. Managing Director, Kanpur Electricity Supply Co. Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: consideration of objection before final assessment
cases.holding: When an objection is filed to a provisional assessment, the Executive Engineer is obliged to apply his mind to and consider that objection before finalizing the assessment. An assessment finalized on a printed proforma by merely filling figures, which acknowledges receipt of the objection but does not consider it, is a mechanical order without application of mind and cannot be sustained under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 mechanism for finalizing assessment. The 4 May 2013 assessment is set aside and the Executive Engineer is directed to consider the objection and decide the final assessment within four weeks of production of the order.
cases.flag: judgment invokes the 2005 Code mechanism for finalizing assessment without citing a clause number

cases.title: Madhu Tiwari v. State of U.P. — liberty to appeal final electricity assessment
cases.topic: final-assessment-appeal
cases.holding: A writ challenging electricity dues is not decided on merits once a final assessment has been completed; the consumer, having been given the assessment papers, is left to file an appeal or take other appropriate steps under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Mohd. Naeem v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: assessment; withdrawal with liberty; statutory remedy
cases.holding: On the petitioner's request, the writ concerning assessment is dismissed as withdrawn. Before any further challenge, he is to obtain the necessary documents from the Executive Engineer; if still aggrieved, he may avail the remedies under the Electricity Act, 2003 and the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The assessment is not examined on merits.
cases.flag: Order cites the 'U.P. Electricity Act 2003' (Electricity Act, 2003) and the Supply Code 2005 without a section or clause number.

cases.title: Jatin Kumar Modanwal v. State of Uttar Pradesh
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: hearing before final assessment on a provisional notice
cases.holding: Where a consumer challenges an inspection report and a provisional assessment notice under Article 226, and final assessment has not yet been made, the Court will not decide the merits. The consumer is directed to file objections to the report and the notice; the assessing authority must consider those objections, grant a hearing, and only thereafter take a final decision on assessment under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Coercive action is stayed for a limited period; current electricity bills remain payable.

cases.title: Shailendra Kumar v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: assessment notice, opportunity and recovery
cases.holding: The procedure for assessment in the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 had not been followed: the assessment notice dated 17.12.2007 did not give details or breakup of how the amount was arrived at, and the consumer was not given adequate opportunity to reply. Following Ashok Kumar, the assessment order and the recovery proceedings including the citation dated 15.9.2009 were quashed, with liberty to the assessing authority to proceed afresh after giving opportunity and to pass a fresh order in accordance with law.
cases.flag: order invokes Supply Code 2005 assessment procedure without numbering a clause

cases.title: M/s Raghu Prime Metal Pvt. Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: billing cycle
cases.holding: Without going into merits, the Court directed the licensee henceforth to issue bills as per the billing cycle in the Electricity Supply Code, provided the consumer makes no default in payment.
cases.flag: order cites the Supply Code billing cycle without a numbered clause

UP-2005::citation-objection-opportunity.code: U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 (objection/hearing procedure for recovery citations) read with Electricity Act, 2003 (s.127, appeal)
UP-2005::citation-objection-opportunity.clause: Objection/hearing opportunity before a recovery citation for theft dues is finalised, and s.127 appeal right against the resulting order
UP-2005::citation-objection-opportunity.topic: A recovery citation challenged on grounds of mistaken identity, where the petitioner has himself judicially admitted the disputed name is his own alias, must nonetheless be addressed through the Supply Code's objection/hearing procedure before the licensee, not resisted on identity grounds; interim protection from coercive recovery is granted pending that hearing, with a s.127 appeal available against the eventual order

cases.title: Vinay Kumar Singh v. State of U.P. And 2 Others
cases.topic: A recovery citation challenged on grounds of mistaken identity, where the petitioner has himself judicially admitted the disputed name is his own alias, must nonetheless be addressed through the Supply Code's objection/hearing procedure before the licensee, not resisted on identity grounds; interim protection from coercive recovery is granted pending that hearing, with a s.127 appeal available against the eventual order
cases.holding: No, the mistaken-identity objection is rejected as the petitioner had himself described himself as 'Rajje Pradhan alias Vinay Kumar Singh' in an earlier s.482 Cr.P.C. application seeking to quash the theft-case proceedings, judicially admitting the two names refer to the same person. However, since the citation had been issued and coercive measures contemplated without affording the petitioner a hearing on his objections under the Supply Code procedure, the Court, taking a lenient view, directed the petitioner to appear before the Executive Engineer with his objections and evidence, directed the Executive Engineer to pass a reasoned final order within four weeks thereafter, granted interim protection from coercive action for six weeks or until disposal of the objection (whichever is earlier), and preserved the petitioner's right to appeal any adverse final order under s.127 of the Electricity Act, 2003 — with the citation to stand automatically revived if the petitioner failed to appear.

UP-2005::compounding.topic: Theft (s.135) compounded through the Supply Code — theft/UUE-Code linkage

cases.title: Ajmal v. State of U.P. & 2 Ors.
cases.topic: Theft (s.135) compounded through the Supply Code — theft/UUE-Code linkage
cases.holding: The offence of electricity theft under Section 135 being compoundable, the accused's compounding remedy lies 'as provided under the provisions of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005' — the Code furnishing the machinery through which theft (Section 135) and, cognately, unauthorised use of electricity (Section 126) are assessed and compounded. Pending compounding, as the offence does not entail imprisonment beyond seven years, any arrest must comply with Section 41(1)(b) read with Section 41-A Cr.P.C.; the FIR, disclosing a cognizable offence, was not quashed.
cases.flag: Scope: the case's express Code engagement is the compounding remedy; the operative relief concerned arrest safeguards (s.41(1)(b)/41-A Cr.P.C.). Retained as a node in the theft / unauthorised-use line, which the Supply Code's assessment and compounding machinery governs.

UP-2005::connection-obtained-by-fraud.topic: No writ restoration of a connection alleged to be obtained by forged documents (matter sub judice)

cases.title: Dhyanendra Singh v. State of U.P. & 5 Others
cases.topic: No writ restoration of a connection alleged to be obtained by forged documents (matter sub judice)
cases.holding: No. Given the serious allegation that the connection was obtained on forged/fraudulent documents, and the matter being sub judice, the Court found no illegality in the authority's order refusing restoration and declined to interfere under Article 226. The petitioner was left at liberty to apply afresh for a connection under the Code, to be considered in accordance with law.

cases.title: Mohamad Gulshan v. Managing Director, Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.topic: bill-correction-complaint
cases.holding: A writ seeking quashing of a disconnection notice conditioned on payment of arrears, and correction of the electricity bill, is not decided on merits; the consumer has a remedy of an appropriate complaint for correction of bills under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and the Executive Engineer shall consider and decide that complaint in accordance with law.
cases.flag: Order cites the Supply Code 2005 generally, without a clause number.

cases.title: Gulab Singh v. State of U.P. — writ not a substitute for prescribed disconnection application
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: consumer-requested disconnection
cases.holding: Mandamus commanding the licensee to disconnect a consumer's supply is not available where the consumer has not applied in the prescribed format or completed the formalities under the Electricity Act, 2003 read with the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, which prescribe a full procedure for temporary and permanent disconnection. The consumer may still apply; the respondents shall then decide immediately in accordance with law.

UP-2005::disconnection-notice-requiremen.code: U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 (notice requirement for disconnection)
UP-2005::disconnection-notice-requiremen.topic: Permanent disconnection without prior notice, even where premised on alleged unauthorized use at another premises, is arbitrary and unauthorized under the Supply Code; reinstatement is directed, without prejudice to a subsequent show-cause notice

cases.title: Raju v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Another
cases.topic: Permanent disconnection without prior notice, even where premised on alleged unauthorized use at another premises, is arbitrary and unauthorized under the Supply Code; reinstatement is directed, without prejudice to a subsequent show-cause notice
cases.holding: No — the Supply Code does not permit disconnection of this nature without any notice whatsoever to the consumer. The licensee's own counsel conceded no show-cause notice had been given before the permanent disconnection (carried out 11.6.2024) on the stated ground of unauthorized use at another premises. The Court, without going into the merits of the unauthorized-use allegation, directed reinstallation of the permanently disconnected connection within 7 days, while leaving it open to the licensee to thereafter issue a show-cause notice and proceed in accordance with law, including against the petitioner on the complaint that had been filed.

cases.title: Smt. Krishna Devi Mishra v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: bill dispute — statutory forum
cases.holding: Once the representation on a bill dispute has been considered and an amended bill issued, a consumer still aggrieved of that bill must take the forum provided under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; a writ of mandamus to decide the representation does not survive.
cases.flag: court did not identify 6.5 or 6.8; referred only to the forum under the Supply Code, 2005

cases.title: Mahendra Nath v. State of U.P. — electricity recovery citation not quashed
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: recovery citation; incorrect bills
cases.holding: A writ to quash a citation for recovery of electricity dues cannot be granted where the citation is not challenged, the bills are not on record, and no good ground is shown. The petition is dismissed, with liberty to take steps under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 regarding incorrectness of the bills.
cases.flag: order invokes Supply Code 2005 on incorrect bills without numbering a clause

cases.title: Peetambar Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: increase and decrease of load
cases.holding: Without going into the merits, the writ is disposed of. The consumer may file a fresh representation before the Executive Engineer, Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited, Mathura, within one month; that officer shall consider and decide it in accordance with law after notice and hearing, preferably within one month thereafter.
cases.flag: Order names no numbered clause; an earlier listing referred only to unspecified Supply Code clauses on increase and decrease of load factor.

cases.title: Smt. Shailesh Mittal v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: independent agency meter testing
cases.holding: Where the consumer had opted under the Supply Code for the meter to be examined by an independent agency, the Court directed the licensee to get the meter checked by any independent agency at the consumer's cost: the department may make a provisional assessment of expenses, and after the agency's actual charge is known the consumer shall be intimated and must deposit that amount within fifteen days. In view of that direction, the consumer need not remain present as required by the letter dated 21.2.2013.
cases.flag: order invokes UP Electricity Supply Code, 2005 generally; no clause number

UP-2005::independent-feeder-definition.code: Tariff Order 2000-01 (issued under s.24, U.P. Electricity Reforms Act, 1999) read with the 'Independent Feeder' definitions in the Electricity Supply Code 2002 and Electricity Supply Code 2005
UP-2005::independent-feeder-definition.clause: 'Independent Feeder' and 'restricted/peak hours' surcharge provisions (HV-2 tariff category, rows 3 and 4 of the Tariff Order 2000-01 table)
UP-2005::independent-feeder-definition.topic: Interpretation of 'independent feeder' (pre-dating its Supply Code definitions) and whether restricted-hours and independent-feeder surcharges under a HV-2 tariff are cumulative

cases.title: Northern Coalfield Ltd. v. Chairman and Managing Director, U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Ors.
cases.topic: Interpretation of 'independent feeder' (pre-dating its Supply Code definitions) and whether restricted-hours and independent-feeder surcharges under a HV-2 tariff are cumulative
cases.holding: (a) Yes — the restricted-hours surcharge (row 3) and the independent-feeder surcharge (row 4) confer distinct benefits and are cumulative; a consumer availing both must pay a total 30% surcharge, and cannot avoid the restricted-hours surcharge merely by virtue of being on an independent feeder. (b) No — an independent feeder does not cease to be independent because other feeders (serving other consumers) also emanate from the same sub-station; it loses that character only if another consumer is tapped onto the very same feeder. Applying this, the NCL Bina connection (no other consumer on that feeder) was held an independent feeder from a 132 KV sub-station (both surcharges payable, 30% total), while the IWSS Khadia connection (power also tapped to a Kota Basti sub-station on the same feeder, without proven consumer consent) was held not an independent feeder (only the 15% restricted-hours surcharge payable, no independent-feeder surcharge; no penalty for want of prior permission, since the benefit had in fact been extended without objection).

UP-2005::new-connection.topic: Processing of application for fresh electricity connection

cases.title: Chandra Sein v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: Processing of application for fresh electricity connection
cases.holding: An application for grant of an electricity connection is to be processed under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Where the writ seeks only disposal of such an application, the Court may direct the licensee to scrutinize it and, subject to completion of required formalities, dispose of it expeditiously and preferably within one month; the connection is not granted on the writ.

cases.title: Movin v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: application for new connection or restoration
cases.holding: Where the consumer only sought consideration of an application for a new electricity connection or restoration of an old connection, and the licensee stated that a prescribed-format application completing 2005 Code formalities would be disposed of with expedition in accordance with law, the writ was disposed of by directing the consumer to apply under the Code within two weeks and, on such compliance, the third respondent to consider the application and pass appropriate orders within four weeks. No direction to grant or restore supply was issued.

cases.title: M/S Tulsi Castle v. Ashutosh Kumar Srivastava, G.M., Lucknow Electric Supply
cases.topic: Contempt — compliance with a direction to dispose of a new-connection application
cases.holding: A direction to the electricity authority to dispose of a new-connection application after affording an objector a hearing is complied with when the Sub-Divisional Officer rejects the application by a reasoned order after considering the objections; the contempt application is then dismissed, no contempt being made out, with liberty to the applicant to pursue redress before the competent authority or court.
cases.flag: Contempt-compliance disposal; the order construes no specific Supply Code clause, so keyed to the new-connection provision bucket. The merits of the SDO's rejection were not adjudicated.

UP-2005::permanent-disconnection.topic: permanent disconnection — prescribed application before mandamus

cases.title: Baljeet Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: permanent disconnection — prescribed application before mandamus
cases.holding: A writ of mandamus directing permanent disconnection of an electricity connection cannot issue where the consumer has not applied in the prescribed format after depositing the requisite amount under the Electricity Act, 2003 (styled in the order as the Electricity Supply Act, 2003) read with the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The consumer remains free to make a complete application, which must then be dealt with strictly in accordance with that law.

UP-2005::procedure-for-restoration.code: Electricity Act, 2003 (s.126) read with the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 (restoration-of-connection procedure)
UP-2005::procedure-for-restoration.clause: Restoration procedure following permanent disconnection for non-payment of s.126 dues
UP-2005::procedure-for-restoration.topic: Consent disposal permitting installment payment of s.126 assessment dues, with restoration of a permanently disconnected connection to follow a fresh application under the Supply Code's prescribed procedure

cases.title: Nadeem v. State of U.P. & 4 Others
cases.topic: Consent disposal permitting installment payment of s.126 assessment dues, with restoration of a permanently disconnected connection to follow a fresh application under the Supply Code's prescribed procedure
cases.holding: By consent of the parties, the petitioner was permitted to pay the outstanding sum under the recovery certificate in four equal monthly installments (15.8.2024 to 15.11.2024); it was left open to the petitioner to apply for restoration of the electricity connection as per the procedure prescribed under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, with any such application to be considered in accordance with law once the second installment is paid.

cases.title: Satish Kumar @ Yatish Sharma v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.topic: After deemed PDC, reconnection is by a fresh application considered in accordance with law, not by restoring the old connection
cases.holding: If the entire dues are cleared, it is open to the petitioner to apply afresh for an electricity connection; any such application is to be considered in accordance with law. The Court did not restore the disconnected tubewell.

UP-2005::supervision-charges.topic: supervision charges on a fresh connection

cases.title: M/S Sandeep Bobbins v. State of U.P. — no Supply Code concession on supervision charges for a fresh connection
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: supervision charges on a fresh connection
cases.holding: The U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 and the instructions relied on contain no provision granting a concession to a consumer who has applied for a fresh connection in relation to supervision charges; a writ seeking to limit such charges to 15% and to quash intimations to that effect is misconceived and is rejected.

UP-2005::supply-quality-no-imbalance.code: U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 (r/w Electricity Act, 2003)
UP-2005::supply-quality-no-imbalance.clause: duty to maintain supply / avoid imbalance
UP-2005::supply-quality-no-imbalance.topic: Licensee's duty to maintain supply and not create load imbalance; complaint to be technically audited

cases.title: Mohammad Rashid & Another v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.topic: Licensee's duty to maintain supply and not create load imbalance; complaint to be technically audited
cases.holding: The licensee is obliged under the Act and the Code to maintain the requisite supply and not create an imbalance. The complaint requiring a technical audit, the competent authority must assess it and report to the Managing Director, who is to examine it under the Act/Code and pass orders within three months after notice to the affected party.

UP-2005::tariff-feeder.clause: feeder-based tariff; set-off of repair cost
UP-2005::tariff-feeder.topic: Rural-feeder supply cannot be billed at urban rate; no self-help set-off

cases.title: Harihar Cold Storage v. P.V.V.N.L. & Another
cases.topic: Rural-feeder supply cannot be billed at urban rate; no self-help set-off
cases.holding: Supply made from a rural feeder cannot be billed at the urban-feeder rate schedule (conceded); the excess is refundable. A consumer who, without authorisation, gets the transformer repaired at his own cost cannot set off that cost against his bills — the remedy is a civil suit.

UP-2005::theft-assessment.topic: service of provisional assessment in theft cases

cases.title: Rakesh Kumar v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: service of provisional assessment in theft cases
cases.holding: Where a surprise-raid theft assessment was treated as final for want of objection and a demand issued under Section 3 of the U.P. Government Electrical Undertakings (Dues Recovery) Act, 1958, but the provisional assessment had been sent only by ordinary post with no record of actual service, the consumer was denied the opportunity to object. The demand notice dated 17.6.2014 is quashed. Respondents must issue a fresh provisional assessment, serve it, give fifteen days to file objection, fix a date and time for hearing, and then pass a reasoned final assessment after considering any objection, in light of the Supply Code, 2005 theft-assessment procedure considered in Ashok Kumar (paras 56–64).

cases.title: Vikramaditya Sharma v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: theft assessment — service of provisional assessment before recovery
cases.holding: Where the provisional assessment in a theft case is not served, the consumer is deprived of the opportunity to object; treating it as final and issuing a Section 3 recovery demand is unsustainable. The demand is quashed. The licensee must issue a fresh provisional assessment, serve it, give fifteen days to object, fix a date for hearing, and pass a reasoned final assessment after considering any objection, in light of the Electricity Supply Code 2005 theft-assessment procedure considered in Ashok Kumar (paras 56–64).
cases.flag: clause number not stated; court referred to ESC 2005 theft-assessment provisions as considered in Ashok Kumar paras 56–64

cases.title: Rakesh Sharma v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: theft assessment — service of provisional assessment
cases.holding: Where the provisional assessment for theft of electricity is not served, treating it as final and issuing a Section 3 Dues Recovery demand is unsustainable. The licensee must issue a fresh provisional assessment, serve it, allow fifteen days to object, fix a date for hearing, and then pass a reasoned final assessment after considering any objection, in light of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 as explained in Ashok Kumar.

cases.title: Rajesh Sharma v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: service of provisional assessment in theft cases
cases.holding: Because the provisional assessment dated 26.5.2014 was returned unserved, the consumer was deprived of the right to object and that assessment could not be treated as final. The demand notice dated 21.7.2014 under section 3 of the U.P. Government Electrical Undertakings (Dues Recovery) Act, 1958, is quashed. Respondents must issue a fresh provisional assessment, serve it, give fifteen days to file objection, fix a date for hearing, and then pass a reasoned final assessment after considering any objection, in light of Electricity Supply Code, 2005 as considered in Ashok Kumar paras 56 to 64.
cases.flag: order cites Supply Code 2005 theft-assessment procedure via Ashok Kumar paras 56-64 without a numbered clause

cases.title: Gaurav Gupta v. UPERC
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: meter testing after alleged tampering
cases.holding: With the parties' consent, the writ is disposed of directing that respondents 2 and 3 shall get the petitioner's meter tested in accordance with the Electricity Supply Code as interpreted in Smt. Amrawati Devi v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.flag: Order cites the Electricity Supply Code generally as interpreted in Amrawati Devi; no clause number.

UPDR1958::3.code: U.P. Government Electrical Undertaking (Dues Recovery) Act, 1958
UPDR1958::3.topic: Recovery demand presupposes a final assessment

cases.title: Dr. Munni Lal v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.topic: Recovery demand presupposes a final assessment
cases.holding: A demand under Section 3 of the 1958 Dues Recovery Act can be issued only after a final order of assessment is passed; a demand issued before final assessment is without authority and is quashed.

UPEDA1952::3(4).topic: Electricity duty realised during an exemption period is an excess realisation to be adjusted

cases.title: M/s Shri Radhey Iron (Pvt.) Ltd. v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.topic: Electricity duty realised during an exemption period is an excess realisation to be adjusted
cases.holding: The duty of Rs. 66,81,010 realised for October 2011 to May 2013 was an excess/unauthorised realisation, the unit being exempt from 9.10.2011; the licensee must adjust it against the bill dated 2.11.2013 (which is smaller than the amount already realised) rather than defer the adjustment to future bills, and could not disconnect for non-payment of that bill. Non-adjustment and disconnection were arbitrary and unsustainable.

cases.title: Harbansh Yadav v. State of U.P.
cases.topic: recovery notice without final assessment
cases.holding: Recovery power under Section 5 of the U.P. Government Electrical Undertakings (Dues Recovery) Act, 1958 cannot be invoked where, concededly, no final assessment order has been passed on alleged unauthorized use. The Department’s plea that the writ attacked only a provisional assessment, to be answered under Clauses 6.8/8.1 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, did not justify the Section 5 notice. The impugned bill was quashed, leaving the Executive Engineer free to proceed afresh in accordance with law.

cases.title: Awadhesh Pratap v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.topic: recovery certificates and attachment — writ will not try a disputed electricity account already partly in a civil suit
cases.holding: No. Counsel could not dispute that dues up to July 2001 were already the subject of Original Suit No. 255 of 2001. The 10.1.2002 certificate was a continuation of that cause of action. What was actually outstanding required investigation of payments, consumption and bills. The petitioner's own figures showed only ten payments totalling Rs. 2,30,890 over about 50 months of monthly billing, against a plausible range of Rs. 5–7.5 lakh, so he was in default. Having already gone to the civil court for part of the claim, he could take the entire accounting dispute there. The writ was dismissed and any interim order vacated.
cases.flag: Source PDF concatenates listing, pass-over, restoration and interlocutory orders from 27.2.2017 to 19.11.2019; the operative judgment is 5.12.2019 (Sudhir Agarwal and Rajeev Misra JJ., numbered paras 1–15). Caption is Awadhesh Pratap; para 2 of the 2019 order names him Awadhesh Prasad. Attachment was stayed on 12.4.2006. The Act is cited in the singular ('Undertaking'). Demand notice under s.3 (13.3.2001) and recovery certificates under s.5 (8.1.2002 for Rs. 3,38,167; 10.1.2002 for Rs. 1,87,348) are recited; the Court did not independently construe those sections.

UPGEU1958::2(b).code: U.P. Government Electrical Undertakings (Dues Recovery) Act, 1958
UPGEU1958::2(b).topic: Executive Engineer of DVVNL not a 'prescribed authority' unless notified; s.3 demand notices invalid

cases.title: Ashok Kumar & Ors. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.topic: Executive Engineer of DVVNL not a 'prescribed authority' unless notified; s.3 demand notices invalid
cases.holding: The Executive Engineer of DVVNL is not a 'prescribed authority' within s.2(b) of the 1958 Act so long as he is not notified as such thereunder; the demand notices issued under s.3 of the 1958 Act are therefore not legal and valid. A demand notice by the Executive Engineer describing himself as an officer of 'UPPCL' was additionally defective.
cases.flag: Recorded as an interplay node under the U.P. Government Electrical Undertakings (Dues Recovery) Act, 1958.

UPGEU1958::3.code: U.P. Government Electrical Undertakings (Dues Recovery) Act, 1958
UPGEU1958::3.topic: Validity of the s.3/s.5 demand notice and recovery certificate

cases.title: M/s Paliwal Alloys (Pvt.) Ltd. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Ors.
cases.topic: Validity of the s.3/s.5 demand notice and recovery certificate
cases.holding: The demand notice under the 1958 Act was not invalid: a registered notice is deemed sufficient service under s.3 Explanation (1), and the recovery certificate under s.5 was issued after the thirty-day period. That specific challenge to the recovery notice failed.

UPGEU1958::4.code: U.P. Government Electrical Undertakings (Dues Recovery) Act, 1958
UPGEU1958::4.topic: Deposit-under-protest and suit not directly applicable where recovery is already stayed

cases.title: Roop Narayan Tripathi v. Kanpur Electric Supply Company, Kanpur Nagar Thru' Its M.D.
cases.topic: Deposit-under-protest and suit not directly applicable where recovery is already stayed
cases.holding: No, not directly. Section 4 provides that where a dispute has been raised as to electricity dues, the disputed amount may be deposited under protest and a suit then filed for recovery of the amount so deposited. Recovery here had already been stayed on 31.3.2004, so Section 4 was not directly applicable.
cases.flag: The judgment cites the Act as 'U.P. Government Electrical Undertaking (Dues Recovery) Act, 1958' (singular). Stay date is 31.3.2004 in this passage and 31.4.2004 in the operative direction.

cases.title: Mahaver Cement Works Pvt. Ltd. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: civil-suit-bar-electricity-dues-recovery
cases.holding: Where electricity dues are being recovered as arrears of land revenue, a civil suit for permanent prohibitory injunction restraining disconnection and recovery is barred. The Court applied s.4 of the U.P. Government Electrical Undertaking (Dues Recovery) Act, 1958: after a s.3 demand notice, a consumer who denies liability may sue only for refund after depositing the dues under protest; the demand is conclusive and the appellant had not deposited, so an injunction suit was not maintainable. It also held the suit barred by s.331 of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950 (quoting s.330(c) on recovery as land revenue). First appeal dismissed and the 6 April 2006 interim order discharged, with liberty to approach UPPCL by representation before the appropriate forum under the Electricity Act, 2003 and the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
cases.flag: Court mixes UPZA&LR ss.330 and 331: the objection and operative holding cite s.331; the analysis quotes s.330(c); counsel's fallback referred to s.330.

URUA1966::4.code: U.P. Industrial Undertaking (Special Provisions for Prevention of Unemployment) Act, 1966
URUA1966::4.clause: ss.3-4 (relief-undertaking notification) r/w Clause 4.49, Supply Code 2005
URUA1966::4.topic: A relief-undertaking notification operates as a statutory stay of recovery satisfying Clause 4.49, and binds all instrumentalities of the State

cases.title: M/s L.M.L. Ltd. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.topic: A relief-undertaking notification operates as a statutory stay of recovery satisfying Clause 4.49, and binds all instrumentalities of the State
cases.holding: Yes. Under s.4 of the 1966 Act the rights, privileges, obligations and liabilities of a notified relief undertaking accruing before the relevant date stand suspended while the notification is in force, and all proceedings for their enforcement are stayed. As the petitioner was a notified relief undertaking when it applied on 31.3.2006, the recovery of its arrears is to be treated as stayed, and the respondents' contention that Clause 4.49 was inapplicable for want of a stay by any court or forum could not be accepted (following Modern Syntax (I) Ltd. v. DRT, Jaipur). The declaration binds all instrumentalities of the State, including the licensee, which cannot act so as to defeat the very object for which the company was declared a relief undertaking.

WB-2004::5.2.code: West Bengal Electricity Regulatory Commission (Electricity Supply Code) Regulations, 2004
WB-2004::5.2.topic: Disconnection procedure and the statutory route of objection/appeal under ss.126-127

cases.title: Chairman, West Bengal State Electricity Board & Ors. v. Syed Mukbul Hossain & Ors.
cases.topic: Disconnection procedure and the statutory route of objection/appeal under ss.126-127
cases.holding: Disconnection of supply on a theft allegation must follow the procedure of Regulation 5.2; the consumer's remedies are to object under Section 126(3) before the final assessment and to appeal the final order under Section 127. As the final assessment had already been made, the Court relegated the parties to the statutory appeal, to be decided on merits (including the maintainability/limitation objection), setting aside the costs and interim directions of the High Court and expressing no opinion on merits.
cases.flag: Multi-state: construes the West Bengal Supply Code (2004), not the U.P. 2005 Code. The Supreme Court expressly decided nothing on the merits.

cases.title: Rana Concast Limited v. PVVNL & Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.topic: additional security from consumers
cases.holding: A writ challenging additional security realised from consumers fails and is dismissed where that controversy stands concluded against the consumer by this Court's judgment dated 21.3.2017 in Writ-C No. 30898 of 2016 (M/s Dev Prayag Paper Mill (Pvt.) v. State of U.P.), counsel having fairly admitted that the challenge has been rejected.

cases.title: Executive Engineer, Southern Electricity Supply Co. of Orissa Ltd. (SOUTHCO) v. Sri Seetaram Rice Mill
cases.application: Foundational: Section 126 (civil, no mens rea, wider purposive 'unauthorised use' covering excess load/change of category under Explanation (b)(iv)) and Section 135 (criminal, mens rea) operate in different and distinct fields with no commonality; Sections 126-127 are a complete code, only the final Section 126(3) order is appealable, and Article 226 relief is confined to jurisdictional review.

cases.title: West Bengal State Electricity Distribution Co. Ltd. (WBSEDCL) v. M/s Orion Metal Pvt. Ltd.
cases.application: Theft (s.135) is a subset of unauthorised use (s.126); a s.126 assessment is available even in theft cases, requiring only civil proof (not proof beyond reasonable doubt/mens rea), and does not merge into or get ousted by the Special Court's s.154(5) civil-liability jurisdiction — both may run in parallel. Applies and extends Seetaram Rice Mill.

lead_authorities.name: Executive Engineer (SOUTHCO) v. Sri Seetaram Rice Mill

cases.title: M/S Beeco Electrical India & Anr. v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.application: Mens rea is irrelevant to a Section 126 civil theft-assessment; it is required only for Section 135 criminal prosecution (agreeing with Mohit Paper Mills Ltd. v. PVVNL).

lead_authorities.name: M/s Mohit Paper Mills Ltd. & Anr. v. PVVNL & Ors.

cases.title: Ajay Prakash Srivastava v. State of U.P.
cases.application: Theft compounding on the FIR, and the affidavit filed for that compounding, do not dispose of objections on the parallel section 126 assessment; the department cannot treat the compounding request as the assessment Aavedan.

cases.title: Subhashis Chatterjee v. U.P. Power Corporation Limited, Lucknow through Chairman and others
cases.neutral_citation: 2011 SCC OnLine All 611 : (2011) 89 ALR 888 : (2011) 6 All LJ 527
cases.application: The licensee's own election to proceed as UUE under s.126 (not theft under s.135) determines which Code powers apply; the theft-only disconnection power is unavailable.

cases.title: Sandeep Kesarwani v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.application: Confirms and extends this corpus's tracked doctrine (SCJ-069 Trikoot Iron & Steels) that theft-based assessment proceeds under s.126 (never under s.135 alone), clarifying (contra a misreading of Southco v. Seetaram Rice Mill's 'different fields' language) that s.126 assessment remains mandatory even where a s.135 FIR/Special Court trial is simultaneously pending — the two tracks (assessment for the civil dues, prosecution/civil-liability determination by the Special Court) run in parallel, not in the alternative.

lead_authorities.name: Executive Engineer, Southern Electricity Supply Company of Orissa Ltd. (Southco) v. Sri Seetaram Rice Mill
M/s Paliwal Alloys (Pvt) Ltd. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.

cases.title: Indian Oil Corporation Ltd. v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.application: Bars the consumer's refund of charges paid without demur and the licensee that only raised bills, never pursuing statutory recovery (s.52 noted).

cases.title: R.A. Castings Pvt. Limited v. PVVNL and Others
cases.application: Unpaid additional security cannot be classified as electricity arrears for the purpose of denying load-factor rebate, even if a UPERC Director (Licensing) letter so treats it.

lead_authorities.name: M/s K.L. Concast Pvt. Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.

cases.title: Barnala Steel Industries Ltd. v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. and Anr.
cases.application: Additional security on load enhancement is not a recoverable 'due'; Clause 4.49 is not attracted and a bank guarantee for it cannot be demanded.

lead_authorities.name: Tehri Girders Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.

cases.title: Tehri Girders Limited and another v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited and others (with R.A. Castings, Sikka Papers and connected petitions)
cases.application: Additional security is not a recoverable 'due'; Clause 4.49 (stay-of-recovery-of-dues) is not attracted and no bank guarantee for additional security can be demanded.

lead_authorities.name: Mirzapur Electric Supply Company Limited v. State of U.P.

cases.title: U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. v. Appellate Authority for Industrial & Financial Reconstruction & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Availability of a statutory appeal to the AAIFR under Section 25 SICA and a four-to-five-year delay were each a sufficient ground to decline writ jurisdiction.

cases.title: M/s Hind Industries Limited v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: A theft-assessment challenge is relegated to the statutory appeal under Section 127 and the Area Level Committee; a writ kept pending for nine years without using that remedy is an abuse of process. Same Section 127 cluster as SCJ-069, SCJ-163.

cases.title: Chotu Service And Washing Center v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Existence of the Section 127 appeal, read with the Supply Code 2005, was the sole ground for declining writ interference.

cases.title: M/s. Shree Gopala Iron (India) Ltd. & Anr. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: The onerous-deposit / limitation exceptions (J.M. Baxi, Shantilal & Co.) do not apply where the statutory forum requires no deposit of the whole demand (only 50% for interim relief) and the demand is not time-barred; the consumer is relegated to the forum. Same relegation-of-a-billing-dispute line as SCJ-636 and SCJ-1561.

lead_authorities.name: J.M. Baxi & Co. v. Commissioner of Customs, New Kandla

cases.title: Parmarth Steels & Alloys (Pvt.) Ltd. & Anr. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. (Transco) & Others
cases.application: A writ entertained with completed pleadings, an interim order and years of pendency should be decided on merits rather than dismissed for the statutory appeal; the alternative-remedy bar is self-imposed discipline, not a jurisdictional bar.

lead_authorities.name: Durga Enterprises (P) Ltd. v. Principal Secretary, Govt. of U.P.
Roshan Lal v. State of U.P.

cases.title: Managing Director, D.V.V. Nigam Ltd. & 2 Others v. Sri Kartar Singh & Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: The licensees' Clause 6.5(b) maintainability objection, even if technical, will not undo a CGRF billing order after nearly twelve years from the 2013 dispute when the order is unassailable on merits.

cases.title: Kapil Gupta v. U.P. Power Corpn. Ltd. & Anr.
cases.application: A writ against a Section 126 assessment is relegated to the Section 127 appeal unless the case falls within the jurisdiction / natural-justice / fundamental-rights exceptions; pure factual disputes go to the appeal.

lead_authorities.name: Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P.
M/s Popcorn Entertainment v. City Industrial Development Corporation

cases.title: M/S Om Ice Factory Thru' Its Partner Satyapal Singh v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Anr.
cases.application: Confirms and applies the alternative-remedy line (cf. SCJ-040 Kapil Gupta): a writ against a Section 126 assessment is entertained only on a genuine jurisdictional/natural-justice/fundamental-rights challenge; where objections have already been considered by the assessing authority and only the correctness of the assessment on facts/procedure is disputed, the petitioner is relegated to the Section 127 appeal, per Southco v. Sri Seetaram Rice Mill (SCJ-041).

lead_authorities.name: Executive Engineer, Southern Electricity Supply Company of Orissa Ltd. (Southco) v. Sri Seetaram Rice Mill
Ashok Kumar & Others v. State of U.P. & Others

cases.title: Moolchand Saini v. State of U.P. through Secretary, Power Corporation & Others
cases.application: Existence of a statutory appeal, though not an absolute bar to a writ, is a sufficient ground to decline to entertain the petition in an assessment matter of this nature.

cases.title: Gopali v. State of U.P. through Secretary and others
cases.application: The statutory appeal is the appropriate forum for a fact-heavy assessment dispute; existence of the remedy warrants declining the writ.

cases.title: Saurabh Agarwal v. State of U.P. And 3 Others
cases.application: A second writ against the assessing officer's rejection of a court-directed representation, after that representation had been substituted for an unused s.127 appeal, is declined because the statutory appeal remains available.

cases.title: M/S Chakradhari Cold Storage Pvt. Ltd. v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited And Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: The 2007 revised assessment passed by the Executive Engineer (Distribution) was not examined on the merits. The consumer was given four weeks to appeal without pre-deposit (substantial amount already deposited); the authority is to hear and pass a reasoned order within eight weeks of filing.

cases.title: Madan Kumar Vishkerma v. State of U.P. & 4 Others
cases.application: Alleged non-functioning of CGRF, disproved by the Presiding Officer's instructions, does not open the writ merits of a billing/new-connection dispute already sent to that Forum.

cases.title: Nagendra Singh Gautam v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: A writ challenging a Clause 4.9 new-connection estimate (Rs.35 vs Rs.70 after amendment) is disposed of by directing a representation to the Managing Director, to be decided after notice and hearing, without adjudicating the rate.

cases.title: M/s Akanksha Steels Pvt. Ltd. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Others
cases.application: The writ court will not decide a billing dispute once CGRF under Clause 7.10 is available; the consumer is given a timed liberty to approach that Forum.

cases.title: M/S R.D. Ice & Cold Storage (P) Ltd. v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited And Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: The 2007 revised ex-parte assessment passed by the Executive Engineer (Distribution) was not examined on the merits. The consumer was given four weeks to appeal without pre-deposit (substantial amount already deposited); the authority is to hear and pass a reasoned order within eight weeks of filing.

cases.title: Maula Bux v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.application: Where Clause 6.5, the consumer grievance forum and the Ombudsman can try the factual bill dispute and have not been used, Article 226 is declined and the writ is dismissed.

cases.title: Abdul Shakoor v. Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Ltd. And Others
cases.application: Review of a writ dismissed for an alternative appeal will not reopen a Clause 8.2(h) acquittal argument. The consumer remains relegated to the Commissioner; delay is not to bar the appeal where a wrong forum was first approached.

cases.title: Om Sons India Handicraft Manufacturers & Others v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.application: A 2006 writ challenging surcharge, pending without a counter, was disposed of by remitting the consumer's representations on levyability of surcharge to the Executive Engineer rather than deciding Clause 6.7 or the unnamed Supreme Court argument.

cases.title: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitaran Nigam Ltd. & Anr. v. Commissioner, Moradabad Region & Anr.
cases.application: On a limited remand, the appellate authority is confined to the remitted question and cannot reverse findings of the remanding court that have attained finality.

cases.title: M/s. Citi Hotel v. Commissioner, Lucknow Division, Lucknow & Ors.
cases.neutral_citation: 2009 SCC OnLine All 346 : AIR 2009 All 137 : (2009) 4 All LJ 741
cases.application: An appellate authority cannot dismiss the appeal without considering a final criminal acquittal or recording reasons for not agreeing with it; doing so is perverse.

cases.title: Palika Towns LLP v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.application: A party who accepts the beneficial parts of an instrument (here, a Transfer Memorandum/Sale Certificate incorporating lease covenants) cannot simultaneously repudiate its burdens — the doctrine of election/estoppel against approbating and reprobating.

lead_authorities.name: R.N. Gosain v. Yashpal Dhir

cases.title: Amrita Arya v. Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Ltd. & 2 Ors.
cases.application: A consumer cannot both contest liability before the CGRF and seek a mandamus to pay and restore; the inconsistent, simultaneous pursuit of two remedies for the same cause is not permitted.

cases.title: Spencer Retail Limited v. State of Uttar Pradesh And 4 Others
cases.application: A consumer who confined the earlier writ to instalments, and stood satisfied with the bill, cannot later attack the interest component of the same demand through the CGRF and a second writ. Interfering with the interest would review the consent judgment.

cases.title: Anubhav Jaiswal v. State of U.P. & 4 Others
cases.application: On a legal sub-division of a premises, outstanding electricity dues are divided pro-rata; a purchaser of a portion is liable only for that portion's share.

cases.title: Anand Kumar v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.application: The bar on a new connection for arrears attaches only to the specific premises in default, not to other portions of a building.

cases.title: Smt. Pawan Jha @ Priya Jha v. State of U.P. And Others
cases.application: Extends the DVS Steels/Hanuman Rice Mills arrears-transferee-liability doctrine (SCJ-099) from private-sale/purchase contexts to a statutory development-authority (ADA) EWS-flat allotment, holding the two contexts are not meaningfully distinguishable; part of this corpus's broader arrears/occupant-liability cluster (SCJ-090, SCJ-098, SCJ-124).

lead_authorities.name: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. DVS Steels & Alloys Pvt. Ltd.

cases.title: Special Officer, Commerce, North Eastern Electricity Company of Orissa (NESCO) & Anr. v. M/s Raghunath Paper Mills Private Limited & Anr.
cases.application: A landmark synthesis of the Supreme Court's own arrears-transferee-liability line (Isha Marbles, DVS Steels, Ahmedabad Electricity Co., Hanuman Rice Mills), crystallising that a fresh-connection applicant with no privity of contract is not liable for a previous occupant's arrears absent an express statutory/regulatory provision so authorising, distinguishing this from a mere transfer of an existing connection; a foundational precedent for this corpus's arrears/transferee-liability cluster (SCJ-031, SCJ-037, SCJ-054, SCJ-098, SCJ-099, SCJ-125).

lead_authorities.name: Isha Marbles v. Bihar State Electricity Board
Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. DVS Steels & Alloys Pvt. Ltd.
Ahmedabad Electricity Co. Ltd. v. Gujarat Inns Pvt. Ltd.
Haryana State Electricity Board v. Hanuman Rice Mills, Dhanauri

cases.title: Raman Ispat (Pvt.) Ltd. & Anr. v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.application: Past dues are not a charge on premises and cannot be foisted on a mere transferee, but a distributor may stipulate clearance of arrears as a condition of a fresh connection or load enhancement to the same premises.

lead_authorities.name: Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. DUS Steels & Alloys Pvt. Ltd.

cases.title: Smt. Soni Dwivedi v. Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. thru. its Chairman & Ors.
cases.application: A new connection to a purchaser of premises may be conditioned on clearing the previous consumer's arrears on those premises; a sale-deed clause shifting dues to the seller does not absolve the purchaser vis-a-vis the licensee.

cases.title: Kalawati Rana v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. Thru its M.D./Chairman and Another
cases.application: Past dues are not a charge on the premises, but a fresh connection to a purchaser may be conditioned on clearing them via a No-Dues Certificate; the sale-deed's inter-party allocation does not bind the licensee.

lead_authorities.name: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. DVS Steels & Alloys Pvt. Ltd.
Haryana State Electricity Board v. Hanuman Rice Mills, Dhanauri

cases.title: Amir Ahmad v. State of U.P. & 4 Others
cases.application: Electricity arrears create a statutory charge on the premises recoverable from a subsequent transferee, including an auction-purchaser on an 'as-is-where-is' basis.

lead_authorities.name: K.C. Ninan v. Kerala State Electricity Board

cases.title: Chandra Prakash Gupta v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.application: The 2005 Code creates the statutory charge that the pre-Code case law lacked: an auction-purchaser cannot escape the previous owner's arrears and must furnish a No-Dues Certificate for a fresh connection.

lead_authorities.name: Ahmedabad Electricity Co. Ltd. v. Gujarat Inns Pvt. Ltd.

cases.title: Haryana State Electricity Board v. M/s Hanuman Rice Mills, Dhanauri & Ors.
cases.application: Electricity arrears are not a charge on the premises; a transferee/auction-purchaser is liable for the previous owner's dues only where statutory rules or statutory conditions of supply expressly so provide (the refinement underlying the K.C. Ninan line).

lead_authorities.name: Isha Marbles v. Bihar State Electricity Board
Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Paramount Polymers (P) Ltd.
Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. DVS Steels & Alloys (P) Ltd.

cases.title: Jitendra Kumar Gupta & Anr. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.application: 'Outstanding dues' on a premises (including a theft assessment) attach to the premises and are recoverable from a subsequent purchaser, who must obtain a No-Dues Certificate — subject to adjustment against recovery from the original defaulter.

cases.title: K.C. Ninan v. Kerala State Electricity Board & Ors.
cases.neutral_citation: (2023) SCC OnLine SC 603; Civil Appeal Nos. 2109-2110 of 2004 (batch)
cases.application: Apex authority: the Supply Code (under s.50/s.181) can create a statutory charge on the premises for a previous owner's arrears recoverable from a new/subsequent owner; a condition requiring a new owner to clear such arrears is statutory and valid (confirming and extending Haryana SEB v. Hanuman Rice Mills; substantially qualifying Isha Marbles).

lead_authorities.name: Isha Marbles v. Bihar State Electricity Board

cases.title: M/S Dharti Agro Industries Pvt. Ltd. v. The Managing Director, Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & 2 Others
cases.application: IMPORTANT QUALIFICATION: the K.C. Ninan arrears-run-with-premises doctrine (SCJ-037) is confined to ordinary/non-insolvency transfers; where the premises were acquired through an IBC liquidation auction and the licensee has itself submitted a claim to the Liquidator for the same dues, IBC s.238 overrides the Electricity Act/Supply Code first-charge provisions and the licensee's sole recourse is the IBC waterfall mechanism, not withholding a fresh connection.

lead_authorities.name: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Raman Ispat Private Ltd. & Ors.
K.C. Ninan v. Kerala State Electricity Board & Ors.

cases.title: M/S Rayana Paper Board Industries Ltd. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Ors.
cases.application: Refines the cluster: absent an express Code provision authorising coercive recovery from a transferee, the licensee's leverage over unpaid dues on a transferred premises is limited to withholding a fresh connection (Clause 4.3), not issuing a land-revenue-style recovery citation against the non-consumer purchaser.

lead_authorities.name: Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. M/s Paramount Polymers Pvt. Ltd.

cases.title: Palika Towns LLP v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.application: Reinforces, by cross-domain analogy, the arrears-transferee-liability doctrinal cluster already tracked in this corpus (K.C. Ninan/SCJ-037 line): dues (whether electricity or, as here, lease rent) do not automatically constitute a charge on the property, but a specific statutory/regulatory stipulation or an express contractual/auction-notice clause can validly bind a subsequent purchaser to clear the predecessor's arrears as a condition of connection/transfer/recognition.

lead_authorities.name: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. DVS Steels & Alloys Pvt. Ltd.
Haryana State Electricity Board v. Hanuman Rice Mills

cases.title: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors. v. M/s DVS Steels & Alloys Pvt. Ltd. & Ors.
cases.application: The foundational SC statement of the doctrine underlying this corpus's arrears/transferee-liability cluster (K.C. Ninan/SCJ-037 line, and later applied/qualified in SCJ-054, SCJ-063, SCJ-090, SCJ-098): dues are not a charge on the property in the absence of a stipulation, but a distributor may lawfully condition supply/reconnection on clearance of a predecessor's dues via Clause 4.3(g)/(h)-type provisions, without that being arbitrary or unreasonable.

cases.title: Teena Sehgal v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.application: A new connection to a portion of premises is conditioned on payment of the electricity dues attributable to that portion; dues on the premises must be cleared before supply.

cases.title: Raman Ispat (Pvt.) Ltd. & Anr. v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.application: Under the amended Clause 4.3(f)(i), clearing the outstanding dues on the premises is a condition of a fresh connection/enhancement, the dues being a first charge on the company's assets and seller and purchaser jointly and severally liable.

cases.title: Smt. Soni Dwivedi v. Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. thru. its Chairman & Ors.
cases.application: Clause 4.1's provisos read with Clause 4.3(f) make a No-Dues Certificate / clearance of the premises' arrears a condition precedent to a new connection on the same premises.

cases.title: Kalawati Rana v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. Thru its M.D./Chairman and Another
cases.application: The third proviso to Clause 4.1 r/w Clause 4.3(f) makes a No-Dues Certificate a condition precedent to a new connection on premises carrying arrears.

lead_authorities.name: Smt. Pawan Jha @ Priya Jha v. State of U.P.

cases.title: M/S Sartaj Rice Mill Thru' Its Partner Maqsood Ali v. Paschimanchal Vidhyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.application: An assessment finalised by the consumer's own written offer to pay in instalments (accepted by the licensee) cannot later be disputed as never having been finalised; his conduct amounts to acceptance/waiver of a formal final-order requirement.

cases.title: M/S Chakradhari Cold Storage Pvt. Ltd. v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited And Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: A revised assessment bill and demand notice issued in purported exercise of s.135 read with clause 6.8(c) by the Executive Engineer (Revenue) were quashed. The power to pass the assessment lies with the Executive Engineer (Distribution).

cases.title: M/S R.D. Ice & Cold Storage (P) Ltd. v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited And Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: A revised assessment bill and demand notice issued in purported exercise of s.135 read with clause 6.8(c) by the Executive Engineer (Revenue) were quashed. The power to pass the assessment lies with the Executive Engineer (Distribution).

cases.title: M/S Kamakhya Steels Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.application: A final assessment that refers to each paragraph of the objection only to mark it 'not accepted', without reproducing or discussing the points, is non-speaking; a s.127 appellate order that likewise brushes aside the grounds of appeal is unsustainable. Both were quashed and the matter remitted for a speaking reconsideration.

cases.title: M/s Kamakhya Steels Pvt. Ltd. & Another v. PVVNL & Another
cases.application: As in the connected SCJ-273, the assessing authority did not consider the consumer's objections. The 23.10.2007 assessment and consequential orders were quashed and remitted for a fresh order under the Code after considering the objections.

cases.title: Saurabh Agarwal v. State of U.P. And 3 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: The order on the fresh representation must be a reasoned one.

cases.title: Mohammad Idrish v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.application: If the licensee cannot establish the mode of service of a provisional assessment, non-receipt is presumed and the consumer is treated as denied his s.126(3)/Clause 8.1(b)(iii) opportunity of hearing; objections must then be decided afresh by a speaking order.

cases.title: Ram Prakash Yadav v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.application: Without a positive reply on the method of service, the provisional assessment is presumed not received and the consumer is treated as denied his opportunity to object.

cases.title: Yogendra Singh v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitaran Nigam Ltd. & 3 Others
cases.application: Without a positive reply on the method of service, the provisional assessment is presumed not received and the consumer is treated as denied his opportunity to object.

cases.title: RKG Industries LLP v. Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Limited & 4 Others
cases.application: An auction purchaser buying on an "as is where is" basis is put to enquiry about, and takes the premises subject to, the erstwhile owner's outstanding electricity dues, which the licensee may recover from him.

lead_authorities.name: Telangana State Southern Power Distribution Co. Ltd. v. Srigdhaa Beverages

cases.title: Navi Hasan v. U.P. Power Corporation & Another
cases.application: A demand/assessment order must confront the consumer with adverse material, allow objections, and be a reasoned speaking order after a hearing; a pre-printed proforma order passed in disregard of these requirements (and of prior court directions to that effect) is vitiated for breach of natural justice.

lead_authorities.name: Uma Nath Pandey & Ors. v. State of U.P. & Anr.

cases.title: Prakash Chandra Gupta v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.application: CGRF's 26.9.2016 order on the check-meter slow-meter complaint was set aside for want of proper opportunity of hearing as well as for non-consideration of Clause 5.6(e). Fresh decision after hearing directed.

cases.title: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Anr. v. The Electricity Ombudsman & Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.date: 15 March 2023 (dismissed for want of prosecution; order-sheet 11.9.2012 to 15.3.2023; interim stay 17.2.2016)
cases.application: Prima facie, the correctness of a consumption / supplementary bill is challengeable only under clause 6.5 of the Supply Code; the CGRF and the Electricity Ombudsman lack competence over bill-correctness (Anis Ahmad). Same Anis Ahmad line as SCJ-1561; cf. SCJ-049 and SCJ-256 on the limits of CGRF / Ombudsman competence.

lead_authorities.name: U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. v. Anis Ahmad

cases.title: Ram Autar Singh v. U.P. Power Corporation
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Bill-correctness dispute relegated to Clause 6.5; writ not entertained because that statutory remedy was available.

cases.title: Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission v. Reliance Energy Ltd. & Ors.
cases.application: Metered consumption must be billed on actual meter readings; a licensee's supplementary/amended bill raised later on a presumed/average basis (e.g. suspected faulty meter) is not lawful absent due process — resonates with the Clause 5.6/5.9 defective-meter procedure line already established in this corpus (e.g. SCJ-058, SCJ-059, SCJ-071).

cases.title: Sudesh Mishra v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: The pending clause 6.5 objection to the revised bill was sent to the Executive Engineer for decision within two weeks; the Court did not itself decide the bill, disconnection, or demand.

cases.title: Rajveer Singh v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: The petitioner had already gone to the Executive Engineer for rectification of a disputed tube-well bill; the Court sent the disputed bill and arrears to be dealt with under Clause 6.5 and directed respondent no.2 to examine the request in accordance with law.

cases.title: Virendra Kumar v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: The pending 6.5 objection of 28.3.2016 was left to the licensee to decide within the Code's seven-day window; the Court did not restore supply or decide the bill.

cases.title: Ajay Kumar Jaiswal v. Uttar Pradesh Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Bill-and-arrears dispute after a recovery certificate was sent to the Executive Engineer under Regulation 6.5 rather than decided on the writ.

cases.title: Surendra Pratap Singh v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.application: Bill grievance already represented; court relegated the consumer to the Executive Engineer (Distribution) under clause 6.5 instead of examining the bill on merits.

cases.title: M/s S.R. Preservation Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: The Court left the pending Clause 6.5 objection, including alleged unadjusted cash deposits, to a time-bound speaking order of the Executive Engineer and kept the subsequent demand in abeyance.

cases.title: Sanjay Kumar Sharma v. State of U.P.
cases.application: The alleged unauthorized construction-use demand was treated as a billing issue arising out of assessment and sent to the Executive Engineer under cl.6.5 read with s.126, rather than being decided in writ.

cases.title: Smt. Rajkumari v. State of U.P.
cases.application: A consumer who disputes recovery of arrears on the ground of non-use after a pole-shifting application, and who relies on a civil court order about shifting of poles, must still take the billing objection to the Executive Engineer under clause 6.5.

cases.title: Ramesh Nath Pandey v. State of U.P. and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Challenge to a recovery-cum-disconnection notice for alleged arrears was sent to the Executive Engineer under clause 6.5 rather than decided on the writ.

cases.title: M/s Shree Radhey Ice Factory v. State of U.P. & 4 Others
cases.application: Disputes over incorrect/regular bills lie under Clause 6.5 before the Executive Engineer, who must pass a reasoned order on the objections.

cases.title: Shashi Bhushan Singh v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.application: A dispute over the correctness of a current/revised bill is to be raised by representation before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5, not adjudicated in writ jurisdiction.

cases.title: Buddhesh Patel v. State of U.P. and Another
cases.application: A disputed recovery (here on a direct-connection/theft finding) is to be pursued by objection before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5, with interim protection against coercive recovery.

cases.title: Smt. Mamata Verma v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.application: Clause 6.5(b) provides a self-contained pay-under-protest-and-complain mechanism for bill-accuracy disputes; a writ is not entertained where that remedy exists.

cases.title: Gul Mohammad v. U.P. Power Corporation and 2 Others
cases.application: A grossly-inflated-bill grievance is to be pursued through the Clause 6.5(b) pay-under-protest-and-complain mechanism, with recovery stayed pending decision.

cases.title: Mohammad Khalid v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Another
cases.application: A disputed demand is pursued by a Clause 6.5 representation (with a Clause 6.5(b) deposit under protest), to be decided within seven days.

cases.title: Chandrapal v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & 4 Others
cases.application: A disputed-arrears grievance pursued under Clause 6.5 must actually be decided by the competent authority before recovery is pressed.

cases.title: Executive Engineer, Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Riyasat Ali and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Interlocutory observation only: a consumer who disputed the genuineness of the licensee's bill had a Clause 6.5 remedy that was not used before approaching the Permanent Lok Adalat. The Court issued notice; it did not relegate or quash.

cases.title: Smt. Laxmi Chaurasiya v. Dakshinanchal Electricity Distribution Corporation Ltd. and 4 Others
cases.application: An apparent dispute over post-restoration electrical dues is a billing dispute for Clause 6.5. The writ court directs the concerned authority to furnish the liability, receive the consumer’s objection, and pass a reasoned order on a fixed timetable, without deciding the quantum.

cases.title: Petitioner v. Managing Director, Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
cases.application: The 5 July 2024 representation to the Executive Engineer was not treated as a paragraph 6.5(b) complaint; the Court directed a proper 6.5(b) complaint with the Code deposit, to be decided by the Executive Engineer.

cases.title: Abhishek Chand Kaushik v. State of U.P.
cases.application: The Court treated Chapter 6 as a detailed statutory mechanism for correction of bills and held that the AGA could not show a Class III PVVNL Executive Assistant was authorised to correct the complainant's bill. That want of authority, with load beyond his 9 kW competence, went only to whether a PC Act demand could be raised at the bail stage; the bill itself was not decided.

lead_authorities.name: Neeraj Datta v. State (NCT of Delhi)

cases.title: Vijay Shukla v. Shri Shadab Ahmad, Executive Engineer, Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. and Another
cases.application: The 10.08.2022 writ directed the Executive Engineer to decide a para 6.5 objection if filed. That duty is not engaged, and contempt does not lie, where no such objection was submitted.

cases.title: M/s Hotel Pride Inn v. Purvanchal Vidhut Vitrana Nigam Ltd. and Another
cases.application: A prior writ had already left the Rs. 2,02,581 billing dispute to Clause 6.5. This order does not reopen that path or decide the dues; it only enables the consumer to obtain M.R.I. readings so objections can be filed.

cases.title: Deo Dutt Kumar v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitaran Nigam Limited
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: A writ against a demand said to correct a mistake in a prior electricity bill was treated as a Clause 6.5 objection for the executive engineer (respondent No. 3), not a merits adjudication in writ.

cases.title: Roop Narayan Tripathi v. Kanpur Electric Supply Company, Kanpur Nagar Thru' Its M.D.
cases.application: A vendor billed for a connection released in his name after sale, and a dispute as to incorrect billing, must go to the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5. The writ is disposed of with a timed representation, a six-week decision, and a stay of coercive recovery only if the representation is filed within 15 days.

cases.title: Maula Bux v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.application: A dispute over billed arrears sought by a Section 3 recovery notice is for the supplier's competent authority under Clause 6.5, not a first-instance writ.

cases.title: M/S. Mohan Electrocasting Pvt. Ltd. And Another v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. And Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: A challenge to a check-meter recovery bill is treated as a dispute as to the correctness of the electricity bill. The writ is disposed of by permitting a Clause 6.5 objection before respondent no. 2, to be decided by a speaking order, with recovery stayed until that decision.

cases.title: The Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Anr. v. The Electricity Ombudsman of U.P. & Anr.
cases.application: Paragraph 6.5 supplies the seven-day time-limit in Clause 7.10(iii): if the licensee does not settle a billing complaint (here, a 29.07.2007 request to test the meter and recast the bill) within seven days, CGRF may be approached. Same cluster as SCJ-013, SCJ-234.

cases.title: Mohd. Azahar v. State of U.P.
cases.application: The petitioner had not represented the disconnection and meter-dismantling facts to the department; the Court required a para 6.5 objection to the Executive Engineer, then CGRF, before any writ to correct the bills.

cases.title: Islam v. State of U.P. & 4 Others
cases.application: In a theft/unauthorised-use assessment the burden is on the department to prove commercial or unauthorised use; a farmer need not disprove it where his use is ancillary agricultural use within the sanctioned load.

cases.title: M/s. Shree Gopala Iron (India) Ltd. & Anr. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: The CGRF under Section 42(5) EA2003 and the UPERC 2007 Regulations can decide a consumer's excess / wrong-billing and tariff-interpretation grievance; the restrictive 'grievance' definition in Reg. 2(n) does not oust it because 'complaint' in Reg. 2(e) is wide. Cf. the CGRF / Ombudsman-jurisdiction line in SCJ-256 and SCJ-049.

cases.title: Suresh Chand Bansal v. Electricity Ombudsman & Others
cases.application: The CGRF cannot award compensation for property loss from a transmission-line accident; its jurisdiction covers supply/billing/tariff grievances, not accident-related property damage.

cases.title: M.D., Pakshimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Electricity Ombudsman & Anr.
cases.application: CGRF/Ombudsman (creatures of subordinate regulation) have no jurisdiction to review a statutory Assessing Officer's Section 126 assessment or a Section 127 appellate order; the only remedy against such an assessment is under Sections 126/127 themselves. Anchors the later Full Bench holding (SCJ-043 Kisan Cold Storage) that the Ombudsman/CGRF scheme is a distinct consumer-grievance track confined to matters outside Sections 126/127/135 etc.

lead_authorities.name: Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Vidyut Lokpal, Lucknow

cases.title: Aruna Bhargava v. PuVVNL & Another
cases.application: A change of forum is not a matter of pure procedure; once proceedings are validly initiated before a forum, that vested right continues despite a later change of jurisdiction, unless the legislature clearly provides otherwise.

lead_authorities.name: CIT v. R. Sharadamma
CIT v. Dhadi Sahu

cases.title: KPB Metals Private Limited v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.application: Extending a sanctioned connection to a different/enlarged site is a change of site barred by Clause 4.8(d)(i), not an internal change under Clause 4.45(c); a fresh connection must be sought.

cases.title: Suman Engineering and Chemicals Pvt. Ltd. v. U.P.P.C.L. & 4 Others
cases.application: Liability for system-upgradation (the system-loading charge) accrues only on actual consumption; a prospective consumer who never draws supply bears no share of it.

cases.title: Executive Engineer, Electricity Urban Distribution Division v. The Electricity Ombudsman & 2 Others
cases.application: A tariff charge conditioned on the consumer opting for a facility (here, protective load) cannot be levied absent that option and the licensee's sanction; it cannot be imposed suo motu on an audit objection.

cases.title: Kanpur Electricity Supply Co. Ltd. and another v. Uttar Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission, Lucknow and others
cases.application: A charitable institution providing service free or at Government-rate charges is billed under LMV-4(A), not LMV-4(B).

cases.title: Parmarth Steels & Alloys (Pvt.) Ltd. & Anr. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. (Transco) & Others
cases.application: In a theft/UUE assessment, the reading of an outdoor check meter (found O.K.) and of the sub-station accounting meter (line-loss records tallying at both ends) are relevant factors the assessing officer must consider before concluding theft.

cases.title: M/S Krown Bakers India Pvt. Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam & Anr.
cases.application: The Clause 5.6 check-meter/testing procedure for a disputed meter is triggered only by the consumer's request; a consumer who has knowledge of a slow-meter finding and does not dispute it or seek testing cannot later invoke Clause 5.6 non-compliance to challenge the consequential bill.

cases.title: Executive Engineer, Distribution Division & Anr. v. Pacific Promoter
cases.application: Section 145 bars the civil court from entertaining a suit challenging a s.126 assessment; the Electricity Act is a complete Code and s.9 CPC excludes such jurisdiction.

cases.title: Sigma Castings Ltd. & Another v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Others (with Kundan Castings (P) Ltd.; PVVNL v. Vidyut Lokpal; M/s Shyam Ferrous Ltd.)
cases.application: Clause 3.4(a)'s mandatory independent-feeder requirement for the specified heavy industries applies to load-enhancement applications as well as new connections — a significant clarification refining SCJ-101 (Pawan Kumar Agarwal) and SCJ-094 (Northern Coalfield) on the scope of Clause 3.4.

cases.title: Pawan Kumar Agarwal s/o M.P. Agarwal v. State of U.P. thru. Secretary & Ors.
