cases.application: Clause 3.4(a)'s enumerated heavy-industry categories requiring mandatory independent-feeder supply are specific and restrictive, not illustrative; other consumers (even at higher loads) have only the Clause 3.4(b) option, not obligation, to seek an independent feeder — directly informs how 'Independent Feeder' provisions are to be read alongside the definitional line traced in SCJ-094 (Northern Coalfield).

cases.title: M/s Kesarwani Sheetalaya & Ors. v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.application: A conjoint reading of Clause 3.4 shows that sub-clause (d) governs tapping of an independent feeder in both category (a) (Arc/Induction furnaces, rolling/re-rolling/mini steel plants) and category (b) (townships/complexes, domestic, non-domestic, institutional); its conditions are not confined to steel/furnace plants and must be satisfied before any fresh consumer is tapped in.

cases.title: Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd., Bhikaripur & Anr. v. Vidyut Lokpal (Electricity Ombudsman) & Anr.
cases.neutral_citation: 2008 SCC OnLine All 376 : AIR 2008 All 127 : (2008) 5 All LJ 683
cases.application: Clause 3.4(d) allows tapping of an existing feeder for a similar-process consumer where an independent feeder cannot be constructed; a licensee cannot insist on 3.4(a) while ignoring the 3.4(d) exception.

cases.title: Ghanshyam v. State of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Energy Deptt. & 3 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad (Lucknow Bench)
cases.application: A 2016 receipt stamped 'P.D. Final Amount' for Rs 1,696, undenied and consistent with the licensee's admission that records are missing, is treated as Clause 4.14(g) termination and no-dues. A 2025 demand of Rs 1,66,916 on that connection is quashed; missing records cannot revive billing.

cases.title: M/S Atul Industrial Corporation And Another v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited And Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Clause 4.15(b) obliges HT/EHT consumers to provide independent entry to the meter or metering cubicle; Clause 4.15(a) lets the licensee fix the point of supply so meters remain unobstructed. An EE order to build a cubicle near the main gate with independent access is intra vires; a plea that access already exists goes to the EE, not the writ court.

cases.title: Smt. Beena Dubey v. M.D. Kanpur Electricity Supply Co. Ltd. & 4 Others
cases.application: A landlord's liability for a departed tenant's electricity dues is co-extensive under Clause 4.3(f)(vi), triggered once the connection was given with the landlord's consent (which a tenancy-agreement clause can itself evidence); this reinforces and extends this corpus's arrears/occupant-liability cluster (SCJ-090, SCJ-098) into the landlord-tenant context.

cases.title: Mohd. Asif v. Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: The licensee's power to permanently disconnect an existing connection is confined to the grounds in clause 4.38; a property-ownership dispute is not among them.

cases.title: Parvati Devi v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Another
cases.application: After temporary disconnection, Clauses 4.37(a) and 4.38 empower the licensee to move to permanent disconnection if the cause is not removed within six months; that power is the licensee's, and a bill-disputing consumer cannot compel its exercise in writ.

cases.title: Sagufta Ishrar v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.application: The Court gave effect to the consumer's request for permanent disconnection under clause 4.38 by directing the licensee to disconnect the line after on-site meter inspection and payment of pending dues.

cases.title: Petitioner v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. and Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: The petitioner invoked Clause 4.38(i)(b) as obliging the licensee to convert a six-month-old temporary disconnection into a permanent disconnection; the Court remitted that claim to the Executive Engineer without deciding the duty.

cases.title: Satish Kumar @ Yatish Sharma v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.application: Counsel admitted, and the Court recorded, that consecutive default in payment requires temporary disconnection followed by permanent disconnection within six months; the licensee billed only six months after the September 2022 TDC on the footing of deemed PDC.

cases.title: Anoop Goyal v. State of U.P.
cases.application: Auction purchase of an industrial plot still attracts clause 4.3(f) successor liability; the incoming occupier must search out and clear predecessor arrears before a fresh connection.

lead_authorities.name: Chandra Prakash Gupta v. State of U.P.

cases.title: RKG Industries LLP v. Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Limited & 4 Others
cases.application: The Clause 4.3(f)(i) duty to find out and clear outstanding electricity dues to obtain a no-dues certificate is co-extensive on seller and purchaser and applies to auction/distress sales, not only private sales.

cases.title: Sri Piyush Kumar v. State of U.P. Thru' Secretary Lucknow And Others
cases.application: Establishes that Clause 4.3(f)'s director-liability regime (first-charge-on-company-assets, then directors only if insufficient) does not apply retrospectively to dues/citations predating the 2005 Supply Code, and requires the licensee to first exhaust recovery against company assets before reaching directors personally — a limiting counterpoint to this corpus's broader arrears/occupant-liability cluster (SCJ-090, SCJ-098, SCJ-124, SCJ-125), here protecting a corporate agent from personal exposure absent an express undertaking.

lead_authorities.name: Adesh Kumar Jain v. U.P. State Electricity Board
M/s Meekin Transmission Ltd., Kanpur

cases.title: Mohd. Ashfaq Khan @ Ashfaq Khan v. State of U.P. thru. Addl. Chief Secy., Energy Deptt., Lucknow & 3 Others
cases.application: An occupant/tenant may obtain a fresh electricity connection under Clause 4.4 on furnishing an indemnity bond and proof of possession, even amid a dispute with the property's transferee-owner, subject to licensee verification and without prejudice to civil rights.

cases.title: Seema Mansoor v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & 3 Others
cases.application: A tenant/occupier may obtain a new electricity connection via the Annexure 4.2 indemnity-bond route where the landlord withholds consent; this reinforces and extends the Clause 4.4 occupant-connection principle already tracked in this corpus (SCJ-085, Mohd. Ashfaq Khan) to the new-connection (not just restoration) context, and explicitly holds that landlord-consent refusal cannot be an absolute bar.

cases.title: Vijay Kumar Tiwari v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Tenant at rented premises may furnish Annexure 4.2 indemnity if the landlord refuses the Clause 4.4 NOC; the Court did not itself grant the connection.

cases.title: Dr. Mamta Tripathi v. State of U.P. & 6 Ors.
cases.application: An occupier unable to produce the owner's consent (e.g. an owner-occupier dispute) is entitled to a connection on an Indemnity Bond under Clause 4.4, which serves the s.43 duty to supply; consent of the owner is not an absolute precondition.

lead_authorities.name: Smt. Sushama Chowdhary v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
Chandu Khamaru v. Smt. Nayan Malik

cases.title: Teena Sehgal v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.application: An occupier of a distinct portion may obtain a connection on an Indemnity Bond (Annexure 4.2) despite an owner-occupier dispute, subject to clearing the dues attributable to that portion.

cases.title: Deepak Jain v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.application: A tenant/occupier is entitled to a connection under Clause 4.4 on the owner's consent letter or, absent it, an Indemnity Bond (Annexures 4.2/4.3); want of the landlord's consent is no ground to refuse.

lead_authorities.name: Seema Mansoor v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.

cases.title: Smt. Sushama Chowdhary v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. thru. Chairman & 4 Ors.
cases.application: An occupier who cannot obtain the owner's consent — especially in an owner-occupier dispute — is entitled to a connection on an Annexure 4.2 indemnity bond; the licensee cannot insist on the owner's consent.

lead_authorities.name: Chandu Khamaru v. Nayan Malik

cases.title: Mohd. Rizvan v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.application: A genuine occupier who is not the owner may obtain a connection under the Code on an Annexure 4.2 indemnity bond in aid of Clause 4.4, without the owner's NOC.

lead_authorities.name: Gaurav Sharma v. State of U.P. & 4 Others

cases.title: Lalit Kumar Tripathi v. State of U.P. and 5 Others
cases.application: A co-possessor whose supply was cut at the instance of an SDM in s.145 CrPC proceedings, and who is not shown to be a tenant, may be considered for connection on the Clause 4.4 indemnity form; a rival occupant claiming sole ownership need not give consent. The connection abides the pending petition.

cases.title: Smt. Uma Chauhan v. State of U.P. And 2 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Clause 4.4 and Annexure 4.2 are quoted in full. Occupancy proof (rent receipt/lease) plus the indemnity-bond route where owner's consent is unavailable support a tenant's additional meter. The Code is treated as the self-sufficient forum for any landlady challenge to that connection; a parallel Section 420 complaint is quashed.

lead_authorities.name: Seema Mansoor v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.

cases.title: M/s Procapitus Business Park Pvt. Ltd. v. Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Ltd. & 4 Others
cases.application: A lessee disconnected at the owner's instance is not given mandamus for restoration or a new connection. The occupier must complete clause 4.4 / Annexure 4.2 formalities; the licensee then decides in accordance with law after hearing the lessor.

cases.title: Ashok Garg v. State of U.P. and Another
cases.application: Where no Clause 4.44 application for transfer or mutation was ever made, the connection remains in the recorded name. That recorded consumer cannot, at the section 482 stage, shed s.135 liability by asserting a prior resignation or corporate takeover; those facts go to trial or discharge.

cases.title: M/s. Suvidha Engineers India Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.application: Clause 4.49 is a valid protective provision (bank guarantee for a stayed amount as a condition of load enhancement), not a recovery mechanism, and is intra vires the Act.

cases.title: Priy Shankar Pandey v. State of U.P. & 4 Others
cases.application: A landowner's Clause 4.5(d) right to object to a supply line over his land is vindicated through the Clause 3, Works of Licensees Rules 2006 resolution mechanism before the District Magistrate/Commissioner of Police, balancing private property rights against public electrification interests.

cases.title: Shivmahraj v. State of U.P. & 6 Others
cases.application: Companion application of the same principle as SCJ-104 (Priy Shankar Pandey v. State of U.P.).

cases.title: Abhimanyu Singh v. State of U.P. & 7 Others
cases.application: When a third party objects to a supply line over its property, the applicant must obtain the no-objection or bear the cost differential of the alternate route; the direct-route cost is the licensee's.

cases.title: Kumar Ajay Singh v. State of U.P. & 10 Others
cases.application: Pending a live title dispute, Clause 4.5(d) is applied interlocutorily: no-objection from the authority in seisin of title, and parallel costing of an alternative route with the applicant to bear the differential if that route is used. No connection ordered yet.

cases.title: Smt. Mewati And Anr. v. Anil Kumar Singh, Executive Engineer, M.V.V.N.L., Tanda, Ambedkar Nagar
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
cases.application: The underlying writ required a Clause 4.5(d) decision on a landowner's objection to poles being erected on the farm. This Court did not apply or construe 4.5(d); it dismissed contempt once the 05.01.2022 connection-charge letter was revoked and that revocation was accepted as compliance. Same cluster as SCJ-104, SCJ-120, SCJ-169, SCJ-282.

cases.title: Smt. Vimla Tiwari v. State of U.P. And Others
cases.application: Reinforces this corpus's Clause 5.6 line (Smt. Amrawati Devi, Modern Rice Mill) requiring meter testing/verification before an assessment premised on a missing or defective meter is finalised.

lead_authorities.name: Smt. Amrawati Devi v. PuVVNL
M/s Modern Rice Mill v. MVVNL

cases.title: Saurabh Agrawal & Another v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.application: A theft finding premised on a defective/tampered meter requires compliance with Clause 5.6(d)'s testing procedure (notice, opportunity to be present, consumer's right to dispute per 5.6(c)); non-compliance (no MRI, no proper laboratory testing) undermines the evidentiary basis for both the assessment and any criminal prosecution.

lead_authorities.name: M/s Modern Rice Mill v. Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Another
Smt. Amrawati Devi v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.

cases.title: Rituraj v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.application: The Clause 5.6(d) procedure — advance intimation of the testing date, opportunity to be present, signature, right to dispute — is mandatory; an assessment on testing done without the 5.6(d)(i) intimation is illegal.

lead_authorities.name: Smt. Amrawati Devi v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.

cases.title: Shamsul Qamar v. PVVNL and Others
cases.application: Clause 8.1(vii) incorporates clause 5.6 testing. A provisional theft bill raised after the meter is removed for laboratory testing, without a testing date and without supplying the laboratory report that the inspection itself made binding, is illegal. Same 5.6 testing-before-theft-finding cluster as SCJ-114 and SCJ-161.

cases.title: Joginder Singh v. D.V.V.N. Ltd. thru' its Managing Director & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Para 6.15(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 was held to take colour from Section 56(1) and not to impose a stand-alone two-year limitation, even in a theft case. Same Clause 6.15 cluster as SCJ-113, SCJ-477.

cases.title: M/s Shri Radhey Iron (Pvt.) Ltd. v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.application: Clause 6.12's order of application applies to appropriating a consumer's bill payment, not to adjusting duty/amounts already realised from the consumer.

cases.title: Satya Narayan v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. thru. its Managing Director & Others
cases.application: The Clause 6.15/s.56(2) two-year recovery bar is not passive — it obliges the licensee to actively pursue notice-and-disconnection under Clause 4.36 within that window; prolonged inaction (here, ~12 years) forfeits recoverability, and Clause 4.38(c)'s permanent-disconnection-affidavit requirement cannot be read in isolation to override this.

cases.title: Muneshwar Prasad Baranwal v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Another
cases.application: A stale recovery for dues long after permanent disconnection engages the Clause 6.15 bar on belated recovery; prima facie such a demand (here ~19 years later) cannot stand, and recovery is stayed pending consideration.

cases.title: M/s Paliwal Alloys (Pvt.) Ltd. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Ors.
cases.application: Arrears (here a peak-hour penalty) cannot be recovered after two years from when they first became due (s.56(2)/Clause 6.15); recovery beyond two years requires a reasoned order adverting to the bar.

cases.title: M/s. Zaz Leather Complex Pvt. Ltd. v. Kanpur Electricity Supply Co. Ltd. and Another
cases.application: A licensee cannot recover, via a fresh bill, sums that became due more than two years earlier for its own metering error; the s.56(2)/Clause 6.15 bar applies.

cases.title: Executive Engineer, Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. The Electricity Consumer Grievances Redressal Forum & Anr.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: A 51-month overload assessment under paragraph 6.9 is not recoverable. The Forum applied Section 56 and Clause 6.15; the High Court held it was not open to raise the demand for 51 months. Same cluster as SCJ-113, SCJ-218, SCJ-406.

cases.title: Sm. Neelima Tiwari v. State of U.P.
cases.application: A Clause 6.5 challenge is competent only after the clause’s conditions, including deposit of the requisite amount, are satisfied.

cases.title: Mukesh Singh Chaturvedi v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.application: A billing objection triggers the licensee's duty to decide it only if it conforms to Clause 6.5 (particulars of amount deposited and the specific objection to the bill); a non-conforming representation need not be decided.

cases.title: Vijay Shukla v. Shri Shadab Ahmad, Executive Engineer, Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. and Another
cases.application: A 05.09.2022 application seeking One Time Settlement, with no endeavour to have the bill corrected under para 6.5, is not a Clause 6.5 objection. The Executive Engineer was not in contempt for not treating it as one; OTS is a government policy availed on UP.ENERGY.IN.

cases.title: Madarsa Dargah Aaliya Islamiya Shareef Nagar & Anr. v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.application: A dispute solely over quantification of a demand is relegated to the Clause 6.5B authority for a reasoned determination, rather than being adjudicated in writ jurisdiction.

cases.title: Petitioner v. Managing Director, Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
cases.application: Challenge to an allegedly exorbitant bill and a recovery citation of Rs.2,98,000 is a quantification dispute for paragraph 6.5(b), not for writ on merits.

cases.title: Sanjay Rizvi v. M.D. Kanpur Electricity Supply Co. & Others
cases.application: Before an assessing officer concludes that unauthorised use of electricity has occurred, Clause 6.8's inspection-report/show-cause/hearing/speaking-order procedure must be substantially followed, given the seriousness of the allegation; a provisional assessment lacking authentic verification data (e.g. unperformed MRI testing that the licensee's own procedure contemplates) is impugnable.

lead_authorities.name: Ashok Kumar & Others v. State of U.P. & Others

cases.title: Bahabuddin @ Raju v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: A UUE provisional assessment notice that specified no hearing date, and a recovery citation treated as final without a reply, were quashed for want of the Clause 6.8(b) opportunity.

lead_authorities.name: Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P.

cases.title: Ashok Kumar & Ors. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.application: Clause 6.8's requirements — evidence of unauthorised use recorded in the report and notice, 15 working days to reply, and a personal hearing — are mandatory; a bare notice reciting that irregularities were found, with 7 days to object, is non-compliant and the assessment is illegal.

lead_authorities.name: Maa Vind Vasini Industries v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.

cases.title: Shiv Shankar v. U.P. Power Corporation
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: The Court treated Clause 6.8(1)(b) hearing as mandatory even though the department had characterised the case as theft of electricity.

lead_authorities.name: Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P.

cases.title: Kamil v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.application: A provisional assessment must follow Clause 6.8 — site report of conclusive evidence, 15 working days to reply, a fixed hearing date, and a speaking order; a bare demand for deposit within seven days, with no objection/hearing opportunity, is de hors the Code and illegal.

lead_authorities.name: Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P.

cases.title: Rakesh v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.application: The fresh provisional assessment must conform to Clause 6.8 and Ashok Kumar — opportunity of reply and oral hearing, then a speaking order.

lead_authorities.name: Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P.

cases.title: Mahadev Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: The assessment was quashed because no hearing date was fixed and only seven days were given, contrary to the Code's 15-working-day notice-and-hearing requirement, though the Court named Clause 6.1(b) rather than 6.8.

cases.title: Mukul Pandey v. State of U.P.
cases.application: Quashed a final assessment and recovery certificate where the licensee produced the inspection report and final order but could not show any Clause 6.8 provisional-assessment notice fixing date, time and place for objections or hearing.

lead_authorities.name: Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P.

cases.title: Ram Prakash Yadav v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.application: A provisional assessment must give the basis of the amount and record the assessing authority's satisfaction of theft, and the consumer must get the Clause 6.8(b) opportunity to reply; absent these the assessment cannot be treated as final.

lead_authorities.name: Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P.

cases.title: Yogendra Singh v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitaran Nigam Ltd. & 3 Others
cases.application: A provisional assessment must give the basis of the amount and record the assessing authority's satisfaction of theft, and the consumer must get the Clause 6.8(b) opportunity to reply; absent these the assessment cannot be treated as final.

lead_authorities.name: Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P.

cases.title: Malkhan Singh v. State of Uttar Pradesh
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Want of hearing before the recovery citation was not decided on merits; the Court remitted the objection to the Assessing Officer under Clause 6.8, subject to a Rs. 50,000 deposit, for a speaking order after personal hearing and confrontation with adverse material.

cases.title: Sangram Singh Yadav v. State of U.P. and 3 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Clause 6.8 is not satisfied by reciting that objections were filed and then confirming the provisional notice. The assessing officer must apply his mind and deal with the objections at a hearing. An admission that the final order is not in accordance with law, explained as a technical error, does not save total non-application of mind.

cases.title: Uco Bank v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.application: A timely written objection to a Clause 6.8(b)(i) provisional UUE assessment does not satisfy Clause 6.8(c). The assessing officer must give a personal hearing; an ex parte rejection of the objection vitiates the assessment, which is quashed and remitted.

cases.title: M/S Sijaria Ice Gramodhyog Sultanpura & Others v. State Of U.P. & Others
cases.application: No material showed supply of the 26.06.2006 inspection report, and no paragraph 6.8(c)(i) hearing was given before objections to the provisional bill were rejected. Recorded as live grounds of the restored s.127 appeal; the 23.02.2007 assessment was not quashed on those defects.

cases.title: Smt. Kalpana Agarwal v. Managing Director, Western Electricity & Others
cases.application: Clause 6.8 inspection–notice–hearing–speaking-order sequence is mandatory before an assessment for theft or unauthorised use can stand. An EE demand issued straightaway, without that sequence, is set aside; the licensee may proceed afresh. Same cluster as SCJ-048.

lead_authorities.name: Ashok Kumar & Others v. State of U.P. & Others

cases.title: Om Prakash v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.application: Billing grievances against a licensee are to be routed through the Clause 7.10 Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum (and Ombudsman on appeal), a specific licensee-grievance mechanism distinct from and preferred over the general District Consumer Forum route — reinforcing the s.42(5)/(6)-equivalent individual-grievance routing principle already tracked in this corpus (SCJ-076, MERC v. Reliance Energy).

cases.title: Priya Prem v. Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Ltd. & 4 Others
cases.application: Companion application of the CGRF-routing principle already tracked in this corpus (SCJ-076, SCJ-096) — new-connection and delay-penalty grievances under s.43/Clause 4.4/7.7.2 are likewise routed through the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum rather than decided directly by the writ court.

cases.title: Basant Lal v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Writ against a demand notice and bill closed so the consumer must take the Supply Code objection route rather than High Court as a first forum.

cases.title: Parvez Akhtar v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: After directing the Executive Engineer to communicate full bill details by written order, the Court left the consumer to Clause 7.10 if still aggrieved, without deciding the demand on merits.

cases.title: Ved Prakash v. President, U.P. Electricity Regulatory Commission
cases.application: The Court treated a representation against a Consumer Forum decision as a clause 7.10 Ombudsman grievance and held the Regulatory Commission has no role.

cases.title: Chandra Shekhar Tiwari v. U.P. Power Corporation
cases.application: Disputed arrears and a provisional theft assessment, raised against a consumer seeking connection, were sent to the Clause 7.10 Consumer Dispute Redressal Forum instead of being decided on the writ.

cases.title: Dharmendra Singh v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.application: The Court accepted the licensee's plea that a recovery-citation dispute over electricity dues must go to the State Forum under Clause 7.10, and time-bound the Forum if the consumer files within fifteen days.

cases.title: Abdul Kalaam v. State of U.P.
cases.application: Revised bill after a court-directed representation, with a live dispute over adjustment of past deposits, sent to CGRF and Ombudsman; writ disposed without a merits determination.

cases.title: Santosh Stationary (P) Ltd. v. PuVVNL — CGRF order, Ombudsman under 7.10(iv)
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Even after the CGRF held the complaint outside Clause 7.10, the Court refused writ examination and relegated the consumer to the Ombudsman under Clause 7.10(iv).

cases.title: Kasturi Bai Gopi Babu Cold Storage Pvt. Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Challenge to the demand and the prayer for a speaking order were treated as grievances for which clause 7.10 CGRF is the prescribed route; the writ was dismissed when that remedy was not disputed.

cases.title: M/S Maa Narheji Agro Industries v. State of U.P.
cases.application: After the Executive Engineer had already decided the incorrect-bill grievance, the writ was not entertained and the consumer was sent to the Forum under clause 7.10, with the Ombudsman as the further Code remedy.

cases.title: M/S Pawan Putra Ice And Cold Storage v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Writ challenging a disputed electricity bill dismissed; petitioner directed to the Ombudsman under clause 7.10.

cases.title: S.N. Singh v. State of U.P. — recovery of disputed energy dues kept in abeyance pending CGRF stay application
cases.application: A prior writ on the same outstanding energy charges had already been dismissed because Clause 7.10 of the Supply Code required the consumer to approach the Forum and Ombudsman. With that complaint still pending, the Court again refused to decide the billing dispute on writ and sent the petitioner to the Forum for interim relief.

cases.title: Gaya Prasad v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & 3 Others
cases.application: A disputed billing grievance (here whether the consumer used electricity after disconnection) is for the Clause 7.10 CGRF/Ombudsman route in the first instance, not the writ court, which will not decide disputed facts.

cases.title: Veerendra Kumar Jain v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.application: A duplicate-billing grievance is for the Clause 7.10 CGRF/Ombudsman route in the first instance, not the writ court.

cases.title: Amar Nath Vidya Ashram & Anr. v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: A remaining technical billing grievance after deposit of the demand (multiplication-factor change on amalgamation of three connections; mixed commercial/domestic load on the single connection) is for the Clause 7.10 CGRF/Ombudsman in the first instance, not the writ court. Same cluster as SCJ-096, SCJ-197, SCJ-217.

cases.title: Madan Kumar Vishkerma v. State of U.P. & 4 Others
cases.application: A second writ repeating a 19.7.2023 challenge already relegated to CGRF is disposed of by placing the misaddressed complaint before the sitting Varanasi Forum (64-Chandrika Nagar, Sigra) with a one-month hearing, without examining tenant-dues or Section 56 issues. Same cluster as SCJ-096, SCJ-197, SCJ-217, SCJ-350.

cases.title: M/s Akanksha Steels Pvt. Ltd. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Others
cases.application: A challenge to a Rs. 8,54,004 demand towards permanent disconnection, on the ground that bills were incorrectly issued, is for CGRF under Clause 7.10 once that forum has been constituted, even where the writ has been pending since 2008. Same cluster as SCJ-096, SCJ-197, SCJ-217, SCJ-350, SCJ-384.

cases.title: M/S Devi Charan Cold Storage Tirwa v. Executive Engineer & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: A dispute over whether electricity arrears remain unpaid after cheques given towards dues were dishonoured, and over the Executive Engineer's rejection of a representation asserting that payment has already been made, is a billing/accounting grievance for the Clause 7.10 CGRF and then the Ombudsman, not the writ court.

cases.title: The Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Anr. v. The Electricity Ombudsman of U.P. & Anr.
cases.application: A bill-correction request to the licensee that is not decided is a Clause 7.10 complaint; CGRF then Ombudsman are competent, and the licensee's writ attacking their jurisdiction fails. Same cluster as SCJ-096, SCJ-197, SCJ-217, SCJ-350, SCJ-384, SCJ-400.

cases.title: M. Das Binani (Binani Dharmshala) v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Paid one-time-settlement excess-charge complaint sent to CGRF; delay waived if approached within one month.

cases.title: Shamshul Qamar v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.application: Because Clause 7.7.4 treats reduction or enhancement of load as billing, the writ court will not decide a load-enhancement communication and relegates the consumer to CGRF under Clause 7.10.

cases.title: Bhim Singh v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Rural-versus-urban tariff classification is a billing grievance for the Clause 7.10 Forum/Ombudsman route; the writ court will not try it as a disputed question of fact.

cases.title: M/S Ekdil Mini Floor Mill v. The Executive Engineer
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: A post-representation modified demand of Rs.1,71,121 was held to belong in CGRF and then the Ombudsman under para 7.10, not in a further writ.

cases.title: Kalwa Khan v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.application: Billing challenge after District Consumer Forum rejection still relegated to CGRF under clause 7.10.

cases.title: Shri Kunwar Sarvesh Kumar Singh v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.application: Confirms and applies the specific-over-general canon (from Mohit Paper Mills) that Clauses 8.1/8.2, not Clause 6.8, govern theft-based (s.135) assessment, including the mandatory 15-working-day notice and 1.5x (not 3x) tariff multiplier.

lead_authorities.name: M/s Mohit Paper Mills Ltd. & Another v. PVVNL & Others

cases.title: Shishir Jain v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Another
cases.application: After a consumer files objections to a theft-related provisional assessment, Clause 8.1(b)(iii) requires an actual personal hearing before any final assessment can be made; a bare 'final notice' reiterating the provisional figure, without a hearing or reasoned order, is unenforceable — reinforcing the corpus's cluster of s.126/Clause 8.1 procedural-strictness rulings (SCJ-069, SCJ-087, SCJ-092, SCJ-111).

lead_authorities.name: Ashok Kumar & Others v. State of U.P. & Others
Kamil v. State of U.P. & Others
Hazi Mohd. Yaseen v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.

cases.title: Arvind Kumar v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Another
cases.application: A final assessment under s.126(5)/Clause 8.1(b) is void without a prior opportunity of hearing; merely 'considering' written objections and communicating an order does not satisfy the mandatory hearing requirement.

cases.title: Latif v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.application: The Clause 6.8 inspection-notice-hearing-final-order sequence is mandatory before any unauthorised-use assessment; a demand raised by bypassing this procedure (e.g. directly under the 1958 Recovery of Dues Act) is illegal, following and applying Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P.

lead_authorities.name: Ashok Kumar & Others v. State of U.P. & Others

cases.title: M/S Kissan Chilling Udyog & Anr. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.application: Extends the Ashok Kumar/Clause 6.8 line: a theft assessment fails not only for skipping the prescribed procedure but also where the notice/final order misreads or mischaracterises the checking report itself (e.g. conflating a test/double meter's findings with the main meter's), since the consumer is thereby condemned on a factual basis the evidence does not support.

lead_authorities.name: Ashok Kumar & Others v. State of U.P. & Others

cases.title: Shri Kunwar Sarvesh Kumar Singh v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.application: A subsequent criminal acquittal on the s.135 charge, per Clause 8.2(X)(g)/(h), mandatorily requires withdrawal of the theft-based civil assessment and meter restoration — where such acquittal post-dates an appellate order, remand is required for the appellate authority to apply this clause.

cases.title: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitaran Nigam Ltd. & Anr. v. Commissioner, Moradabad Region & Anr.
cases.application: The effect of a criminal acquittal on a theft assessment is to be examined under Clause 8.2(X)(G)&(H) — the specific and only question remitted to the Commissioner.

cases.title: Smt. Urmila Devi v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & 3 Others
cases.application: A consumer exonerated of theft (here by an accepted police final report) claims the benefit of Clause 8.2(x)(h) to set aside the theft assessment; pending decision, recovery is stayed.

cases.title: M/s. Citi Hotel v. Commissioner, Lucknow Division, Lucknow & Ors.
cases.neutral_citation: 2009 SCC OnLine All 346 : AIR 2009 All 137 : (2009) 4 All LJ 741
cases.application: A criminal acquittal of theft after trial obliges the licensee/appellate authority to withdraw the theft assessment and restore supply through the original meter under Clause 8.2(x)(g)-(h).

cases.title: Akhalak Ahmad v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitaran Nigam Ltd. Thru' G.M. & Others
cases.application: The assessing officer was directed to pass a fresh order in the spirit of Clause 8.2(X)(h) after considering objections and a police final report in the theft FIR. That is consideration in spirit, not a holding that a closure report mandatorily withdraws the assessment as a court acquittal would.

cases.title: Shiv Shankar Giri v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Others
cases.application: A provisional assessment cannot be treated as final for want of objections unless the licensee can establish it was served in the manner Clause 9.3 prescribes; failure to do so, especially where the consumer denies receipt, deprives the consumer of the s.126(3)/Clause 8.1(b)(iii) objection right and vitiates a subsequent recovery based on that unserved assessment.

cases.title: Ramji Lal v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Because the checking report and provisional assessment were sent only under certificate of posting, they were not treated as duly served under 9.3; recovery under the citation was stayed until final assessment after registered-post service.

cases.title: Mohan Bajpai v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Ordinary post was held not to conform to Clause 9.3, so service of the provisional assessment could not be presumed. After actual service via the counter affidavit, the consumer was put to objections and recovery was stayed until those objections were decided.

cases.title: Mohamdabad Cold Storage Private Ltd. (& Anr.) v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.application: Clause 6.5(b)'s heading ('Disputed Bills and Arrears') does not confine its scope; a supplementary bill grounded in a disputed meter reading is a disputed bill within the clause — resonates with the marginal-heading-not-an-aid-to-construction principle already tracked in this corpus (SCJ-059/060, Chandler v. DPP line).

cases.title: Mother India Refrigeration Industries (& Anr.) v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.application: Companion application of the same principle as SCJ-083.

cases.title: Mohd. Sagir v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.application: The 'Defective Meters' marginal heading of Clause 5.6 does not confine the clause to non-tampered meters; the substantive words ('any meter' in 5.6(a); 'rendered defective due to tampering' in 5.9) govern, so tampering falls within the Clause 5.6 testing machinery.

cases.title: Vandana Srivastava v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.application: Suppression of a material fact — here an adverse civil-court finding on the petitioner's tenancy relevant to the connection claim — disentitles the petitioner to discretionary writ relief.

cases.title: Anil Shastri v. State of U.P. Thru. Principal Secy. Power & Others
cases.application: The Court found substance in the licensee's contention that the writ concealed the inspection at which the petitioner was found taking supply by a cable on the distribution line, with a site checking report and a provisional theft assessment. The petition was dismissed. Same cluster as SCJ-171.

cases.title: Joginder Singh v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.application: Clause 2.2(av) of the 2002 Code, and a Division Bench citation of 2009 (2) AWC 1189, cannot be used to defeat summoning under ss.135/138. The Code details licensee-consumer service obligations and has no relevance to the criminal prosecution.

cases.title: Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Others v. M/s Prakancha Metal Works Pvt. Ltd.
cases.application: The Code's grievance forum (CGRF/Ombudsman) and the Act's overriding clause do not cover a claim of tortious damages for wrongful disconnection; such claims lie before the Lok Adalat / consumer fora.

cases.title: Divisional Engineer, Electricity Distribution Division-I v. Raman Singh & Another
cases.application: The Supply Code and its CGRF/Ombudsman forum cover consumer grievances, not a non-consumer's tort-damages claim against the licensee; such claims lie before the Permanent Lok Adalat as a public-utility-service dispute.

lead_authorities.name: Bar Council of India v. Union of India
S.N. Pandey v. Union of India

cases.title: Executive Engineer, Electricity Distribution Division-II v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.application: The Supply Code/EA scheme (and the s.145 civil-court bar) govern consumer disputes; a non-consumer's tort-damages claim for electrocution is a public-utility-service dispute the Permanent Lok Adalat may decide.

lead_authorities.name: Bar Council of India v. Union of India
United India Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Ajay Sinha

cases.title: Jharkhand State Electricity Board & Others v. M/s Ramkrishna Forging Limited
cases.application: Supply Code regulations, being terms dictated by a monopoly supplier, are to be liberally interpreted in favour of the consumer; load-enhancement agreements are treated as continuations of the initial agreement.

cases.title: Ghanshyam v. State of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Energy Deptt. & 3 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad (Lucknow Bench)
cases.application: A disconnection application is not to be rejected for want of the prescribed format (Annexure 4.7) or the last receipt. The Code's 30-day Clause 4.14 process is to be applied in a consumer-friendly way; the application itself marks cessation of the supply relationship.

cases.title: M/s Baba Ice and Cold Storage Pvt. Ltd. v. Ram Chandar, Tehsildar, Kirawali, Agra
cases.application: Collection / recovery charges are leviable only where the dues are actually recovered by the Tehsil (revenue) authorities; where the consumer deposits the dues directly with the Electricity Department, no collection charges arise.

cases.title: M/s Baba Ice and Cold Storage Pvt. Ltd. v. Ram Chandar, Tehsildar, Kirawali, Agra
cases.application: A writ order granting instalments under Clause 6.14 and waiving collection charges on timely full payment bars recovery of collection charges once the dues are fully paid and the demand notice recalled; recovery thereafter, with arrest and without notice, is malafide and contumacious.

cases.title: Noida Power Company Ltd. v. State of U.P. & Anr.
cases.application: Once the regulatory commission is constituted, the statutory power to determine tariff/power-purchase price displaces the price mechanism agreed between the parties, even where the agreement is otherwise statutorily protected.

cases.title: Chandra Bhan Singh v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.application: The 22.11.2004 LMV-5 schedule was held to be a tariff fixed by UPERC under Section 24 of the Reforms Act, 1999 and Sections 62 and 64 of the 2003 Act. The consumer's case that the licensee had enhanced Bundelkhand private-tubewell rates on its own was rejected.

cases.title: Om Prakash s/o Gauri Shankar v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.application: Payment of a s.152(3) compounding fee for theft is distinct from, and does not extinguish, the consumer's separate civil liability for electricity actually consumed; recovery notices for consumption dues survive compounding — a companion principle to this corpus's theft/126 procedural-strictness line, clarifying that compounding addresses only the criminal offence.

cases.title: Om Prakash v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Others
cases.application: Payment of the compounding fee is a deemed acquittal of the theft offence but does not discharge the civil liability, which the Special Court adjudicates; the consumer is relegated to that statutory remedy.

cases.title: Kanpur Electricity Supply Company Ltd. & Another v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Releasing an electricity connection without installing a meter is illegal under the Electricity Act, 2003; the proviso to Section 55(1) even allows a consumer to install a purchased meter, so meter-unavailability is no excuse for a meterless release.

cases.title: Meva Ram v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.application: A connection can be transferred/mutated to a new holder only after all dues are cleared, by the Executive Engineer under Clause 4.44; the incoming holder here undertook the liabilities.

cases.title: Ganga Dayal v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.application: A connection is transferred/mutated to a new holder under Clause 4.44 only after all arrears are cleared and formalities completed, by the Executive Engineer of the Division.

cases.title: Mohammad Khalid v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Another
cases.application: A disconnection following the consumer's own delay in invoking the Clause 6.5 remedy is attributable to him, not the licensee.

cases.title: U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Ors. v. Anis Ahmad (with connected appeals)
cases.application: Landmark bar on Consumer Protection Act jurisdiction over Electricity Act s.126 assessment and s.135-140 theft/interference offences, distinguishing 'saving' of the CP Act's general applicability (ss.173-175) from an affirmative grant of jurisdiction over matters outside the CP Act's own 'complaint' definition — a foundational precedent for this corpus's forum-jurisdiction cluster, complementing SCJ-138's Ombudsman-status ruling and clarifying which remedies (appeal under s.127, not a CP Act complaint) properly lie against assessment/theft proceedings.

cases.title: Managing Director, D.V.V. Nigam Ltd. & 2 Others v. Sri Kartar Singh & Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Applied as the converse: a billing-arrears complaint before CGRF is maintainable because it is not a s.126 assessment or a s.135–140/150 complaint. Anis Ahmad was cited by the petitioners at admission against a 'District Consumer Forum'; the 2025 Court named the principle without the case name.

lead_authorities.name: U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. vs. Anis Ahmad

cases.title: Trimurti Concast Pvt. Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited
cases.court: National Company Law Tribunal, Allahabad Bench (Prayagraj)
cases.application: Extinguishment of the corporate debtor's pre-CIRP liability is distinct from the co-extensive personal liability of erstwhile directors as guarantors under an independent contract of guarantee.

lead_authorities.name: Narendra Singh Panwar v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.

cases.title: Kanpur Electricity Supply Company Ltd. & Another v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: A State instrumentality challenging a modest consumer-protection award for its own default, without any error apparent on the record, prosecutes frivolous and vexatious litigation liable to be dismissed with cost; departmental action against the defaulting officials is the proper course.

cases.title: M/s Hind Industries Limited v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Acquittal in the criminal theft case does not make the assessment order not survive; acquittal may rest on grounds unrelated to the assessment, and the assessment of charges on account of theft is provided under the Act.

cases.title: Torrent Power Limited v. U.P. Electricity Regulatory Commission & Ors.
cases.application: Cross-subsidisation of a franchisee's below-bulk-supply input rate by a licensee's other-area consumers is a legitimate feature of input-based franchisee models addressing high-loss areas, and is not by itself a ground to invalidate the arrangement absent evidence of illegality or misrepresentation.

cases.title: Kanpur Electricity Supply Company Ltd. & Another v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Concurrent DCGRF and Electricity Ombudsman findings of delay and laches justify damages under paragraph 7.7.2 of the Supply Code, 2005; Article 226 interference is refused absent an error apparent on the record. Same paragraph 7.7 cluster as SCJ-261 and SCJ-700.

cases.title: Ashok Kumar Ajmera v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: A deemed-disconnection plea under Clauses 4.36-4.38 does not, in a writ, negate a theft assessment where unauthorised drawing continued after disconnection; the point is for the Section 127 appeal.

cases.title: Shri Krishna Kumar Bhargava v. State of U.P. & 4 Others
cases.application: A defective meter, absent a finding that the consumer rendered it defective, is not per se theft/UUE under s.126 and is governed by the distinct defective-meter rules (Clauses 5.6/5.8), not the s.126 route.

cases.title: M/s Kamakhya Steels Pvt. Ltd. & Another v. PVVNL & Another
cases.application: Mere slow working of a meter with a lesser reading does not amount to theft. The assessing authority ought to have sent the meter for technical assessment to determine whether there was tampering or a manufacturing defect, instead of hypothetically charging the check-meter difference as theft units.

cases.title: M/S Three Star Paper Mills Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P. & 5 Ors.
cases.application: Delay/laches of decades bars a consumer from claiming the benefit of a favourable judgment obtained by other, timely litigants on the same point.

lead_authorities.name: New Delhi Municipal Council v. Pan Singh & Others
Yunus v. State of Maharashtra & Others

cases.title: Rameshwar v. DVVNL & Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: A demand notice recovering the amount assessed under the provisional assessment order is illegal once a final assessment order has been passed, and is quashed. Same Section 126 assessment cluster as SCJ-047 and SCJ-034.

cases.title: Satya Prakash Singhal v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Rather than ordering automatic reconnection, the court directs the competent authority to consider reconnection / fresh connection in accordance with law within a fixed period, conditioned on the consumer clearing all pending dues.

cases.title: Mukesh Kumar and 3 Others v. State of U.P. and 4 Others
cases.application: Recovery from directors under Clause 4.3(f)(v) is sequenced after recovery against the company's assets and, pending challenge, abides the outcome of the lead writ petitions.

cases.title: Rajee Steels Pvt. Ltd. & Anr. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Director not personally liable for the company's electricity dues absent a personal guarantee; unavailable here as the citation ran against the company through its Director.

cases.title: Assistant Engineer (D1), Ajmer Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Anr. v. Rahamatullah Khan alias Rahamjulla
cases.application: The two-year bar in s.56(2) restricts only the coercive remedy of disconnection; the licensee may still raise a supplementary demand and pursue other modes of recovery (including within limitation from discovery of a mistake).

cases.title: Devendra Sharma v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.application: A landlord-tenant or ownership dispute is not a ground to disconnect a validly sanctioned electricity connection; the Code's new-connection procedure cannot be turned to that use.

cases.title: Dipali Dey (Baxi) v. Mira Das
cases.application: A tenant in possession is not to be deprived of electric supply on account of a landlord-tenant dispute; supply is restored (here by civil injunction pending the suit).

cases.title: Divya Sahani v. State of U.P. & Another
cases.application: A pending ownership/property dispute is not a ground to refuse or disconnect a connection; a connection confers no title, so the supply question is independent of the title dispute.

cases.title: Ishwar Chandra v. U.P. Power Corporation Limited Thru' its M.D. & Another
cases.application: Where the licensee and consumer squarely dispute whether an objection was filed/considered, the writ court will not resolve it and directs the statutory appeal.

cases.title: Smt. Laxmi Chaurasiya v. Dakshinanchal Electricity Distribution Corporation Ltd. and 4 Others
cases.application: The licensee said only part of the dues after 2.4.2018 had been paid; the consumer said the entire amount had been deposited. The Court declined to enter that controversy and relegated the parties to Clause 6.5.

cases.title: Roop Narayan Tripathi v. Kanpur Electric Supply Company, Kanpur Nagar Thru' Its M.D.
cases.application: Whether the purchasers obtained the connection by a false declaration in the vendor's name is a disputed question of fact. Prima facie the sale deed supported the vendor, but the Court held it not prudent to decide the issue in writ jurisdiction.

cases.title: Awadhesh Pratap v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.application: Whether the ledger correctly reflected payments and consumption, and what sum remained outstanding, required investigation of facts. The writ court declined to try that accounting dispute, noting that part of the cause of action was already in Original Suit No. 255 of 2001, and dismissed the petition.

cases.title: M/S Devi Charan Cold Storage Tirwa v. Executive Engineer & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Whether the consumer had already paid the electricity dues, against a record of dishonoured cheques, is an accounting dispute of fact; the writ is dismissed without examining those questions.

cases.title: Smt. Amna Khatoon v. PVVNL & Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Whether the assessment was for 407 days instead of 180 days as contemplated under Clause 8.1 is a question of calculation the writ court cannot go into; it is left to objections before the assessing officer.

cases.title: Raj Kumar v. KESCO and Others
cases.application: Want of service of the provisional assessment and of an opportunity to object under s.126(3), not pleaded before the AO or in the appeal, involves investigation of facts and will not be entertained for the first time in writ.

cases.title: S.K. Construction Co. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.court: National Company Law Tribunal, Allahabad Bench (Prayagraj)
cases.application: On extinguishment of the right to recover, if a duty to supply is cast under the Electricity Act, 2003, the licensee cannot escape performing that duty and must energise the connection.

lead_authorities.name: West Bengal State Electricity Distribution Co. Ltd. v. Sri Vasavi Industries Ltd.

cases.title: HSA Traders v. Office of the Executive Engineer, Electricity Distribution Division, Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited & Anr.
cases.court: National Company Law Tribunal, Allahabad Bench (Prayagraj)
cases.application: On extinguishment of the right to recover, if a duty to supply is cast under the Electricity Act, 2003, the licensee cannot escape performing that duty and must energise the connection.

lead_authorities.name: West Bengal State Electricity Distribution Co. Ltd. v. Sri Vasavi Industries Ltd.

cases.title: Lakshmi Oil And Vanaspati Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.application: The Clause 4.1 obligation to supply is not displaced by the previous owner's arrears where the SFC sale certificate is free from encumbrances and Isha Marbles applies. Those arrears, if any, may be recovered from the previous owner in accordance with law.

lead_authorities.name: Isha Marbles v. Bihar State Electricity Board

cases.title: Trinmurti Buildwell Pvt Ltd v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd And Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: The Clause 4.1 obligation to supply is not displaced by the previous owner's arrears where the auction sale certificate is free from encumbrances and Isha Marbles applies. Those arrears, if any, may be recovered from the previous owner in accordance with law.

lead_authorities.name: Isha Marbles v. Bihar State Electricity Board

cases.title: Vijay Lakshmi v. Bihar State Electricity Board & Ors.
cases.application: Electricity arrears are not a charge on the premises; a transferee is liable for a predecessor's dues only where statutory rules or statutory conditions of supply so authorise.

lead_authorities.name: Haryana State Electricity Board v. Hanuman Rice Mills
Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. DvS Steels & Alloys (P) Ltd.

cases.title: Lakshmi Oil And Vanaspati Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.application: Following Isha Marbles, an SFC auction purchaser who had no prior connection or contract with the licensee is not a consumer or occupier and cannot be treated as a defaulter on the previous owner's arrears. A sale certificate transferring the premises free from all encumbrances is treated as the Clause 4.3(f) no-dues certificate.

lead_authorities.name: Isha Marbles v. Bihar State Electricity Board

cases.title: Trinmurti Buildwell Pvt Ltd v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd And Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Following Isha Marbles, a bank-recovery auction purchaser who had no prior connection or contract with the licensee is not a consumer or occupier and cannot be treated as a defaulter on the previous owner's arrears. A sale certificate transferring the premises free from all encumbrances is treated as the Clause 4.3(f) no-dues certificate. Same cluster as SCJ-655.

lead_authorities.name: Isha Marbles v. Bihar State Electricity Board

cases.title: Rajee Steels Pvt. Ltd. & Anr. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: A defaulting consumer could not shift its liability to the auction-purchaser via a sale deed it was not party to; dues are enforced under the supply contract and a transferee cannot be foisted with a predecessor's dues absent a contract to the contrary.

lead_authorities.name: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. DVS Steels & Alloys Pvt. Ltd.

cases.title: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Raman Ispat Private Limited & Ors.
cases.application: Electricity dues are not automatically a 'secured interest'/first charge under the IBC merely by virtue of a Supply Code recovery-as-arrears-of-land-revenue mechanism; secured-creditor status depends on whether a security interest was actually created (by contract clause or operation of law) and, if so, the claim is processed within the s.53 waterfall, not outside/above the IBC.

lead_authorities.name: State Tax Officer v. Rainbow Papers Ltd.

cases.title: U.P. State Cement Corporation Ltd. (In Liquidation), In re
cases.application: An electricity supplier's dues in a winding up do not rank pari passu with workmen and secured creditors under ss.529/529-A; only post-winding-up, court-ordered supply is recoverable — and only as a liquidation expense under s.457, not as a secured debt.

lead_authorities.name: Textile Labour Association v. Official Liquidator

cases.title: RKG Industries LLP v. Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Limited & 4 Others
cases.application: Electricity dues are statutory, not purely contractual; insisting on clearance of a premises' arrears as a condition of a fresh connection is not arbitrary or unreasonable.

lead_authorities.name: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. DVS Steels & Alloys (P) Ltd.
Hyderabad Vanaspathi Ltd. v. A.P. State Electricity Board

cases.title: U.P. Power Corporation Limited Thru' Executive Engineer v. Electricity Ombudsman & Ors. (M/S Suresh Automobiles)
cases.application: Establishes the Electricity Ombudsman's institutional character under s.42(6) as an ADR/quasi-judicial grievance-redressal mechanism, not an Appellate Authority or Tribunal, given the absence of finality (Regulation 12.8's 'any Court or Tribunal' access) and the absence of judicial 'trappings of a Court' — significant for characterising the Ombudsman's role and for procedural questions (appealability, superintendence) arising from Ombudsman awards throughout this corpus's Ombudsman-related cases (e.g. SCJ-128's Electricity Ombudsman appeal background).

lead_authorities.name: Union of India v. R. Gandhi, President, Madras Bar Association
Shiv Shakti Cooperative Housing Society v. Swaraj Developers

cases.title: Executive Engineer, Electricity Urban Distribution Division IInd v. Electricity Ombudsman, Lucknow & Ors.
cases.application: A sanctioned, fully-paid estimate must be honoured; the department's delay cannot be used to move the consumer to a costlier feeder or demand a fresh estimate (Clause 4.6(a)/(g)).

cases.title: Mohd Usman Ansari v. Chairman, Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Ltd. & 4 Others
cases.application: A recovery certificate founded on an ex-parte provisional s.126 assessment, made without following the Supply Code's assessment/hearing procedure, cannot be coercively enforced until the consumer is given a hearing and a reasoned final assessment is passed.

cases.title: M/s Shri Radhey Iron (Pvt.) Ltd. v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.application: Electricity duty realised during an exemption period is an excess recovery that must be adjusted against the consumer's current bill; the licensee cannot defer the adjustment or disconnect for a bill covered by the amount already held.

cases.title: Kanpur Electricity Supply Co. Ltd. & Anr. v. U.P. Electricity Regulatory Commission & Ors.
cases.application: Excess load or appliance installation within/around the contracted load is not 'unauthorised use' under Section 126 (para 6.9 of the Code); the remedy is the tariff's additional Fixed Charge, not a theft/UUE assessment.

cases.title: Nandu Engineering Works & Anr. v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.date: 22 February 2012 interim order (order-sheet 19.1.2012 to 8.1.2018; writ pending)
cases.application: The plea that an exorbitant re-assessment renders the statutory appeal onerous (50% pre-deposit) was held to need consideration; the writ was entertained and not thrown out at the interim stage on the alternative-remedy ground, though the respondents contended that an appeal lies.

cases.title: Abdul Gaffar @ G. Hussian v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Section 126(3) contemplates a Final Order of Assessment after a Provisional Assessment; a Provisional Assessment treated as Final without a specific order, on the footing that no objections were filed, is prima facie improper. Same Section 126 cluster as SCJ-047 and SCJ-034.

cases.title: Ashok Kumar Ajmera v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Once a theft case is registered and a final assessment order passed, the writ challenging the assessment is dismissed and the assessee relegated to the Section 127 appeal with all grounds open. Same Section 127 cluster as SCJ-1266, SCJ-047.

cases.title: Chotu Service And Washing Center v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: The Executive Engineer's final assessment dated 21.11.2016 was treated as attracting the Section 127 appeal, and the writ was disposed without examining the assessment.

cases.title: Vinod Kumar Agarwal v. State of U.P. And Others
cases.application: A systemic, State-wide compliance directive that no recovery citation under the 1958 Recovery of Dues Act may issue without a prior final s.126 assessment order (per Clause 6.8 of the Supply Code) following an opportunity of hearing — implemented via a compliance order from U.P. Power Corporation's Chairman & Managing Director binding on all Executive Engineers, reinforcing this corpus's procedural-fairness cluster around theft/unauthorised-use assessment (cf. SCJ-126's Clause 5.6/malice-in-law ruling).

cases.title: Rakesh v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.application: Recovery cannot issue without a final order of assessment; a recovery citation founded on a mere provisional assessment (or an unproved final order) cannot stand.

cases.title: Devi Lal @ Tutti Lal v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.application: Applied to stay the 1 March 2012 recovery citation because the 29 April 2010 demand was only a provisional s.126(1) assessment and the department produced no final order.

cases.title: Final s.126(3) assessment mandatory before recovery; notice-footer insufficient
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: A footer treating unanswered s.126(3) notice as the final assessment does not satisfy the statute; recovery under the Supply Code awaits a speaking final order after findings on service and, if filed, objections.

cases.title: Assistant Engineer (D1), Ajmer Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Anr. v. Rahamatullah Khan alias Rahamjulla
cases.application: Electricity charges become 'first due' when the bill is issued quantifying them, though liability to pay arises on consumption; the limitation clock under s.56(2) starts from billing.

cases.title: Executive Engineer, Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. The Electricity Consumer Grievances Redressal Forum & Anr.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: The explanation to Clause 6.15(b) was applied: inspection-based charges become first due from the due date of the bill, which must be given within two billing cycles, so a 51-month back-assessment of overload cannot stand.

cases.title: Torrent Power Limited v. U.P. Electricity Regulatory Commission & Ors.
cases.application: Establishes that a distribution franchisee under s.2(27)/seventh proviso to s.14 is the licensee's agent, insulated from direct ERC regulatory oversight; an ERC's s.128 investigation power reaches only the licensee, requiring a concrete showing of licence/Act non-compliance rather than a bare performance review — a significant precedent for this corpus's regulatory-architecture cluster (alongside SCJ-130's SERC-composition ruling and SCJ-106's APTEL-jurisdiction ruling), clarifying the limits of ERC oversight over distribution-delegation arrangements.

lead_authorities.name: City Corporation Limited v. Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission and Anr.

cases.title: M/s. Zaz Leather Complex Pvt. Ltd. v. Kanpur Electricity Supply Co. Ltd. and Another
cases.application: The relaxation for a supplementary bill (limitation running from discovery of a bona fide mistake) does not extend to a fresh bill for over two years; Clause 6.15 was not addressed in the Ajmer Vidyut line.

lead_authorities.name: Assistant Engineer (D1), Ajmer Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Rahamatullah Khan

cases.title: Chandrapal v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & 4 Others
cases.application: Issuing a fresh demand / recovery notice while a Clause 6.5 representation remains undecided is arbitrary; the representation must be decided first and recovery kept in abeyance.

cases.title: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Raman Ispat Private Limited & Ors.
cases.application: A distribution licensee's dues do not automatically rank as 'government dues' under s.53(1)(e)/(f) IBC merely because of state shareholding in the licensee; the licensee remains a distinct juristic entity in a liberalised, privately-contestable sector.

lead_authorities.name: Municipal Commissioner of Dum Dum Municipality v. Indian Tourism Development Corporation

cases.title: Divisional Engineer, Electricity Distribution Division-I v. Raman Singh & Another
cases.application: Electricity distribution is a hazardous activity; the licensee is under a statutory duty to maintain its installations and lines so that passers-by (human or animal) are not harmed.

lead_authorities.name: Shakuntala Devi v. Delhi Electric Supply Undertaking

cases.title: Executive Engineer, Electricity Distribution Division-II v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.application: A distribution company has an onerous duty to maintain its devices and to disconnect current from the sub-station in a storm; failure to do so is negligence founding a damages claim.

cases.title: Reliance Projects and Property Management Services Ltd. v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.application: The resolved debtor's liability crystallises from the plan's 'effective date' (actual transition of control), not the mere date of NCLT approval, especially where implementation was delayed by litigation; time excluded in litigation benefits the debtor, not the statutory creditors.

cases.title: Narendra Singh Panwar v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & 2 Others
cases.application: The s.14 IBC moratorium and a resolution plan's discharge of the Corporate Debtor do not extinguish a Director's independent personal-guarantor liability for the company's electricity dues under Clause 4.3(f)(v)/6.15 of the Supply Code — a distinct sub-doctrine within this corpus's IBC/electricity-arrears cluster (cf. SCJ-054 Dharti Agro Industries, where IBC s.238 barred recovery from the licensee itself post-liquidation; SCJ-063's PVVNL v. Raman Ispat line on arrears running with premises/against the Corporate Debtor). Here the qualification cuts the other way: IBC discharge of the Corporate Debtor does not reach a Director's separate, co-extensive personal guarantee.

lead_authorities.name: State Bank of India v. V. Ramakrishnan
Lalit Kumar Jain v. Union of India
Laxmi Pat Surana v. Union of India

cases.title: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Raman Ispat Private Limited & Ors.
cases.application: Once liquidation commences, IBC s.238 overrides the Electricity Act's ss.173/174 non-obstante recovery provisions and the Supply Code's Clause 4.3/6.15 mechanism; a licensee cannot independently attach/auction a corporate debtor's assets for electricity dues outside the IBC's collective process — directly confirms and elevates to Supreme Court authority the qualification to the arrears-run-with-the-premises doctrine already tracked via SCJ-054 (Dharti Agro Industries) and the NCLT/NCLAT ruling cited in SCJ-090 (Narendra Singh Panwar).

lead_authorities.name: Sundaresh Bhatt, Liquidator of ABG Shipyard v. Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
Duncans Industries Ltd. v. AJ Agrochem

cases.title: M/S Dharti Agro Industries Pvt. Ltd. v. The Managing Director, Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & 2 Others
cases.application: Section 238 of the IBC, being a later special enactment with a non-obstante clause, overrides sectoral statutes with their own non-obstante/first-charge provisions (Electricity Act ss.173-174; also applied to the Customs Act and the Tea Act in other SC rulings) once liquidation/moratorium proceedings are triggered and the sectoral authority has participated in them.

lead_authorities.name: Innoventive Industries Ltd. v. ICICI Bank & Anr.

cases.title: South East U.P. Power Transmission Company Ltd. v. Prescribed Authority & Ors. (with Tata Steel Ltd. v. State of U.P.)
cases.application: Section 238 IBC prevails over the Electricity Act, 2003, including its own overriding provisions (ss.173/174); electricity dues have no special immunity from the IBC framework.

lead_authorities.name: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Raman Ispat (P) Ltd.

cases.title: Reliance Projects and Property Management Services Ltd. v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.application: Section 238 IBC prevails over the Electricity Act; even arrears that would otherwise run with the premises cannot be demanded for the pre-effective-date period.

lead_authorities.name: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Raman Ispat (P) Ltd.

cases.title: M/S Mohit Paper Mills Ltd. & Anr. v. PVVNL & Ors.
cases.application: Where the consumer's own meter cannot yield a reading due to physical impossibility (fire, theft), a reliably maintained outside/check meter may exceptionally found billing, applying the impossibility maxims.

lead_authorities.name: Inter College Kusmaul, Gorakhpur & Anr. v. State of U.P. & Ors.

cases.title: M/S Shri Parasnath Alloys (Pvt.) Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.application: Clause 3.4(d)(ii)'s consent requirement for tapping an independent feeder runs to the consumer who funded the feeder's construction (the 'original consumer'), not to every downstream tapping consumer who paid only its own connecting-line cost; a downstream consumer can acquire a consent right only by itself having obtained the true original consumer's consent and shared the feeder's cost (Kesarwani Sheetalaya).

lead_authorities.name: M/s Kesarwani Sheetalaya & Others v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Others
M/s Shiv Flour and Rice Mills v. State of U.P. & Others

cases.title: Raj Narayan Singh v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.application: The Clause 3.4 protection (consent of the original consumer before tapping) attaches only to a genuine independent feeder; it does not arise for a small consumer supplied through ordinary lines/transformer.

cases.title: M/s Kesarwani Sheetalaya & Ors. v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.application: Tapping of an independent feeder requires the consent of the original consumer(s) who bore its cost. Here the petitioners had objected and never consented, so the direction to connect respondent no.4 to their cold-storage independent feeder was in breach of Clause 3.4(d).

cases.title: Northern Coalfield Ltd. v. Chairman and Managing Director, U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Ors.
cases.application: A feeder remains 'independent' notwithstanding other consumers being fed from other feeders off the same sub-station; it loses independence only if another consumer is tapped onto the very same feeder — the operative test for 'Independent Feeder' both under this pre-Code tariff interpretation and, by extension, informing how the term is later defined in the Electricity Supply Code 2002/2005.

cases.title: M/S Santosh Preservation Pvt. Ltd. & Anr. v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Anr.
cases.application: Clause 5.6(c)(iii)'s independent-laboratory option is triggered only when the tampering/defect finding is derived from a test report; it has no application where tampering is visibly patent at inspection, distinguishing Mohd. Sagir and Amrawati Devi (ambiguous, test-report-dependent tampering).

lead_authorities.name: Mohd. Sagir v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
K.C. Ninan v. Kerala State Electricity Board & Ors.

cases.title: Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission v. Reliance Energy Ltd. & Ors.
cases.application: A State Electricity Regulatory Commission cannot adjudicate individual consumers' billing grievances or issue a blanket refund direction without a proper s.128 investigation; individual grievances go through the s.42(5) Forum and s.42(6) Ombudsman.

cases.title: Obedue Rahaman Khan v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: An individual billing grievance over a DISCOM demand-cum-disconnection notice was sent to the s.42(5) CGRF rather than being decided on the writ side.

cases.title: Kripa Shanker v. State of U.P. Thru. Distt. Collector, Unnao & Ors.
cases.application: A consumer unable to pay an outstanding bill in one go may apply under Clause 6.14 of the Supply Code for installment payment; the Executive Engineer must consider and decide such an application expeditiously.

cases.title: Nawal Singh @ Lovil v. State of U.P.
cases.application: A writ offering to pay electricity arrears in installments is sent to the Executive Engineer under clause 6.14 rather than decided on the merits in the High Court.

cases.title: Rajveer Singh v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Liberty was reserved to seek installment payment of the disputed demand, with the Executive Engineer to invoke Clause 6.14 if permissible.

cases.title: Devendra Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.application: Clause 6.14 is the Code route for installment of an electricity bill; a writ seeking only that facility is declined so the consumer can apply to the competent authority.

cases.title: Iqbal Ahmad v. State of U.P.
cases.application: Writ seeking instalment deposit of Power Corporation bills was closed because Clause 6.14 is the Code remedy for that facility.

cases.title: Wahid Siddiqui v. State of U.P.
cases.application: Writ confined to paying Power Corporation bills in installments was disposed of by relegating the consumer to Clause 6.14 rather than granting the facility in the writ.

cases.title: M/S U.S. Foods Private Limited And Another v. State of U.P. And Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: The Court remitted the consumer's request for instalments of electricity dues to the Executive Engineer under clause 6.14 rather than granting instalments on the writ.

cases.title: Abdul Sattar v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Writ court channeled a request for breathing time on dues to the licensee's Clause 6.14 process instead of granting installments on the writ.

cases.title: Punit Kumar Gupta v. State of U.P. and others
cases.application: The Court treated clause 6.14 as the exclusive source of instalment relief and sent the petitioner to the Executive Engineer instead of granting a court-fashioned schedule.

cases.title: M/s Nutek Overseas Pvt. Ltd. v. Pachimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.application: The Court treated clause 6.14 as the proper channel for seeking time to pay disconnected-supply arrears and refused to grant that facility itself on the writ.

cases.title: S.S. Industries v. State of U.P.
cases.application: After the licensee ignored a prior 6.14 direction and disconnected despite a partial deposit, the Court itself fixed three equal instalments for the balance and tied restoration to the next deposit.

cases.title: Prime Gold International Ltd. v. State of U.P.
cases.application: Clause 6.14 is the statutory channel for seeking installment of electricity dues; the Court did not grant installments on the writ.

cases.title: Salman @ Salman Qureshi v. State of U.P. and Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Consumer relegated to a clause 6.14 installment application; the High Court declined to fix installment terms itself.

cases.title: Spencer Retail Limited v. State of Uttar Pradesh And 4 Others
cases.application: Confining an earlier writ to Clause 6.14 instalments, and taking a consent disposal (part-deposit, restoration, instalment application to be considered), is treated as acceptance of the bill. A later CGRF bid to waive interest on that demand is not a route to reopen it.

cases.title: Pratap Singh v. State of U.P. Electricity Deptt.
cases.application: Clause 6.14 is the Code forum for a written instalment request to the Executive Engineer; a writ mandamus to compel instalments was not granted on merits.

cases.title: Nawab Ali v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Payment of the recovery citation was structured as four equal instalments with stay of recovery continuing only so long as each instalment was deposited on time.

cases.title: Panna Lal v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Arrears of electricity bills directed to be paid in three equal instalments under clause 6.14, with stay of the recovery citation and 50% collection-charge waiver if paid on time.

cases.title: Installment facility under clause 6.14 for outstanding electricity bills
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Outstanding bills of Rs. 41,460 directed to be paid in three equal installments under clause 6.14, with default accelerating the entire amount and stay of recovery while installments were kept.

cases.title: Satyendra Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Court treated cl. 6.14 as the proper channel for a consumer seeking instalments for financial distress, and remitted the request to the prescribed authority instead of granting instalments in writ.

cases.title: M/S Savari Ice Factory v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
