cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Clause 6.14 permits installment facility where the consumer is in financial distress, but the High Court will not itself extend it; the consumer must apply to the authority concerned.

cases.title: Dinesh Chandra v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Clause 6.14 was treated as the statutory route for a consumer in financial distress seeking instalments against a recovery citation; the writ was disposed with a time-bound representation rather than a merits order on the citation.

cases.title: Natthoram v. State of U.P.
cases.application: Defaulting consumer relegated to a fresh 6.14 representation before the Executive Engineer, who must decide it by a reasoned speaking order.

cases.title: Gufran v. State of U.P. and others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Writ against electricity-charge recovery disposed by remitting a financially distressed consumer, who did not dispute liability, to the Executive Engineer under cl. 6.14, with a short stay of coercive process pending a speaking order.

cases.title: Harikesh Yadav v. State of U.P.
cases.application: Petitioner in financial distress seeking instalments against admitted arrears was sent to the Clause 6.14 licensee facility rather than given writ relief.

cases.title: M/S U.S. Foods Private Limited And Another v. State of U.P. And Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: The Court extracted clause 6.14, which confines the instalment facility to consumers in financial distress and bars waiver of surcharge, then left the request to the Executive Engineer.

cases.title: M/s Parmarth Steel & Alloys Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Counsel's request that the Court fix installments because the petitioners were facing financial hardship was refused in the writ and pointed to clause 6.14.

cases.title: Neeraj v. State of U.P. — recovery citation not quashed; Clause 6.14 installments
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Clause 6.14, not a writ quashing recovery, is the route when arrears are admitted and only easy installments are sought; the Executive Engineer applies the financial-distress, no-waiver, and rank/quantum limits.

cases.title: Mohammad Waseem v. State of U.P. & Another
cases.application: Instalments for electricity dues are a discretionary facility under Clause 6.14, confined to consumers in financial distress, granted only by an Executive Engineer or above within the prescribed tiers, with no surcharge waiver and a minimum 40% first instalment.

cases.title: Manveer Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Writ against recovery of undisputed dues was disposed of without granting instalments, because clause 6.14 already supplies that facility for consumers in financial distress and the application must go to the licensee.

cases.title: Sultan Khan v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.application: An instalment request for undisputed dues is for the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.14.

cases.title: Udayveer Singh v. State of U.P. and 3 Others
cases.application: A consumer in financial distress willing to clear the dues is entitled to easy instalments under Clause 6.15 r/w Clause 6.14, to be fixed by the competent authority.

cases.title: Usha Devi v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.application: A consumer in financial distress is entitled to seek easy instalments under Clause 6.14, to be decided sympathetically, with interim protection from coercive recovery.

cases.title: Nawab Ali v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Applied clause 6.14 because the consumer pleaded poverty and inability to pay the lump sum while remaining willing to clear the dues; the Court itself fixed four equal instalments rather than remitting him to apply to the Executive Engineer.

cases.title: Panna Lal v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Pleaded poor financial condition and readiness to pay, with the department's lack of objection, engaged clause 6.14's instalment facility for customers in financial distress; the Court itself scheduled three instalments rather than remitting the application.

cases.title: Installment facility under clause 6.14 for outstanding electricity bills
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Facility granted because the petitioner pleaded inability to pay the entire arrears at once due to poor financial condition, and clause 6.14 authorises the Executive Engineer or a higher officer to grant installments to consumers in financial distress.

cases.title: M/S Hind Industries Limited v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.application: Interest on a sum wrongfully retained/evaded (e.g. under Clause 8.1 of the Supply Code) is compensatory, not penal or confiscatory.

lead_authorities.name: Wig Brothers (Builders & Engineers) (P) Ltd. & Anr. v. Union of India & Ors.

cases.title: M/S Hind Industries Limited v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.application: A time-bound interim protection order automatically lapses on expiry of its term; a consumer cannot rely on its continued existence, or on an unrelated pending application, to justify years of non-payment of an assessed sum.

cases.title: Nandu Engineering Works & Anr. v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.date: 22 February 2012 interim order (order-sheet 19.1.2012 to 8.1.2018; writ pending)
cases.application: Pending a challenge that a re-assessment was not computed per clause 8.2 of the Supply Code, the court restored the disconnected supply on part-payment (Rs.10 lakh) and deposit of current bills, with no coercive action - an interim arrangement leaving the merits open. Same interim-restoration-on-deposit posture as SCJ-1063 and SCJ-206.

cases.title: Mrs Rajendra Kumar Sharma v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.application: Where a defective assessment is set aside for procedural non-compliance, the Court may order interim restoration of supply on the consumer furnishing security, subject to the outcome of a properly conducted fresh assessment.

cases.title: Vijay Krishna Agrawal & Anr. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Supply was restored on the consumer depositing the amount assessed for one year preceding the inspection (with liberty to pay current bills), pending final decision on the assessment's validity.

cases.title: RKG Industries LLP v. Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Limited & 4 Others
cases.application: Isha Marbles is confined to auctions with no clause dealing with electricity dues; where the auction is "as is where is" and the terms put the purchaser to notice of dues, the purchaser is liable.

lead_authorities.name: Isha Marbles v. Bihar State Electricity Board

cases.title: Radhe Shyam Singh v. State of U.P. & 2 Ors.
cases.application: Under the s.43 duty to supply to an owner or occupier, a tenant/occupier cannot be refused a new connection merely because the landlord objects or withholds consent.

lead_authorities.name: Chandu Khamaru v. Nayan Malik

cases.title: Smt. Sushama Chowdhary v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. thru. Chairman & 4 Ors.
cases.application: Clause 4.4 is in aid of the s.43 duty; refusal of a connection to an occupier for want of the owner's consent, by a reasonless order, breaches that duty.

cases.title: Abdul Waheed v. Smt. Fatima Begum And Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: The alleged owner's writ failed: lawful occupation, not title or an owner's NOC, is the predicate for supply; indemnity stood available even under old Regulation 3(i)(b).

cases.title: Mohd. Rizvan v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.application: A connection cannot be declined to a tenant merely because the landlord refuses a no-objection certificate, especially in a landlord-tenant dispute.

cases.title: M/s L.M.L. Ltd. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.application: A load-reduction application is governed by the Code as it stood when the application was made (here the unamended Clause 4.49 accepting a bond or any instrument), not by a later amendment introducing a bank-guarantee-only requirement; 'instrument' is wide enough to include an affidavit.

cases.title: Lalit Kumar Kapoor v. Kanpur Electricity Supply Company & Anr.
cases.application: For determining which version of Section 126 (deposit condition, assessment rate) applies, the operative date is the date of the FINAL assessment, not the provisional assessment or the date the cause of action arose.

lead_authorities.name: Sri Bhagwan Gupta v. Kanpur Electricity Supply Company Ltd.

cases.title: BSES Rajdhani Power Ltd. v. Delhi Electricity Regulatory Commission
cases.application: When the Supply Code / Section 126 deems assessed energy to be consumed, the fiction must be given full effect and the assessed units treated as sales.

cases.title: Tehsil Bar Association, Sadar Tehsil Parisar, Gandhi Nagar, Ghaziabad v. U.P. Power Corporation Limited And 3 Others
cases.application: Establishes that the legal profession, being a professional (not commercial) activity, cannot be billed under the non-domestic/commercial LMV-2 tariff merely because the current rate schedule lacks an express 'lawyers' chambers' category and a residuary clause would otherwise sweep it into LMV-2 — an important tariff-classification precedent extending Clause 3.3(e)'s residential-professional-use exemption to court-compound chambers, and a discrimination bar between districts served by different licensees under the same State ERC tariff.

lead_authorities.name: Dr. D.M. Surti v. State of Gujarat
M.P. Electricity Board and Others v. Shiv Narayan and Another
V. Sasidharan v. M/s Peter and Karunakar

cases.title: Suman Engineering and Chemicals Pvt. Ltd. v. U.P.P.C.L. & 4 Others
cases.application: Deposits taken as part of the estimate are refundable unless the licensee proves the actual expenditure reasonably incurred; unproved heads must be refunded.

cases.title: M/s Saini Alloys Pvt. Ltd. v. U.P. Power Corporation, Lucknow & Ors.
cases.application: Tariff is set by the regulatory commission; a distribution licensee has no power to alter it by executive circular, and a purported alteration not following the statutory procedure is void ab initio.

cases.title: U.P. Power Corp. Ltd. Through Executive Engineer v. Ombudsmen and 2 Others
cases.application: Minimum monthly/fixed charges form part of the Commission-notified Tariff Order under Section 24 of the Reforms Act, 1999 and paragraphs 3.8/3.9 of the Code. The licensee cannot waive them on a consumer request, and the Ombudsman cannot direct the licensee to ignore the Tariff Order.

lead_authorities.name: U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. v. Ombudsmen and 2 others (Writ-C No. 1003603 of 2008, 21.03.2023)

cases.title: U.P. Power Corp. Ltd. Through Executive Engineer v. Ombudsmen and 2 Others
cases.application: Minimum monthly/fixed charges form part of the Commission-notified Tariff Order under Section 24 of the Reforms Act, 1999 and paragraphs 3.8/3.9 of the Code. The licensee cannot waive them on a consumer request, and the Ombudsman cannot direct the licensee to ignore the Tariff Order.

lead_authorities.name: U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. v. Ombudsmen and 2 others (Writ-C No. 1003603 of 2008, 21.03.2023)

cases.title: U.P. Power Corp. Ltd. Through Executive Engineer v. Ombudsmen and 2 Others
cases.application: Minimum monthly/fixed charges form part of the Commission-notified Tariff Order under Section 24 of the Reforms Act, 1999 and paragraphs 3.8/3.9 of the Code. The licensee cannot waive them on a consumer request, and the Ombudsman cannot direct the licensee to ignore the Tariff Order.

lead_authorities.name: U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. v. Ombudsmen and 2 others (Writ-C No. 1003603 of 2008, 21.03.2023)

cases.title: U.P. Power Corp. Ltd. Through Executive Engineer v. Ombudsmen and 2 Others
cases.application: Minimum monthly/fixed charges form part of the Commission-notified Tariff Order under Section 24 of the Reforms Act, 1999 and paragraphs 3.8/3.9 of the Code. The licensee cannot waive them on a consumer request, and the Ombudsman cannot direct the licensee to ignore the Tariff Order.

lead_authorities.name: U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. v. Ombudsmen and 2 others (Writ-C No. 1003603 of 2008, 21.03.2023)

cases.title: U.P. Power Corp. Ltd. Through Executive Engineer v. Ombudsmen and 2 Others
cases.application: Minimum monthly/fixed charges form part of the Commission-notified Tariff Order under Section 24 of the Reforms Act, 1999 and paragraphs 3.8/3.9 of the Code. The licensee cannot waive them on a consumer request, and the Ombudsman cannot direct the licensee to ignore the Tariff Order.

lead_authorities.name: U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. v. Ombudsmen and 2 others (Writ-C No. 1003603 of 2008, 21.03.2023)

cases.title: Chandra Bhan Singh v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.application: Clauses 3.7 and 3.8 do not authorise the licensee to fix tariff without Commission approval. The published Commission schedule bound the consumer; the writ to restore the 2.12.2002 rates was dismissed.

cases.title: U.P. Power Corp. Ltd. Through Executive Engineer v. Ombudsmen and 2 Others
cases.application: Minimum monthly/fixed charges form part of the Commission-notified Tariff Order under Section 24 of the Reforms Act, 1999 and paragraphs 3.8/3.9 of the Code. The licensee cannot waive them on a consumer request, and the Ombudsman cannot direct the licensee to ignore the Tariff Order. Lead case later followed in SCJ-490 to SCJ-494.

cases.title: U.P. Power Corp. Ltd. Through Executive Engineer v. Ombudsmen and 2 Others
cases.application: Minimum monthly/fixed charges form part of the Commission-notified Tariff Order under Section 24 of the Reforms Act, 1999 and paragraphs 3.8/3.9 of the Code. The licensee cannot waive them on a consumer request, and the Ombudsman cannot direct the licensee to ignore the Tariff Order. Companion of SCJ-700 (Writ-C No. 1003603 of 2008, same date); later followed in SCJ-490 to SCJ-494.

cases.title: U.P. Power Corp. Ltd. Through Executive Engineer v. Ombudsmen and 2 Others
cases.application: Minimum monthly/fixed charges form part of the Commission-notified Tariff Order under Section 24 of the Reforms Act, 1999 and paragraphs 3.8/3.9 of the Code. The licensee cannot waive them on a consumer request, and the Ombudsman cannot direct the licensee to ignore the Tariff Order. Co-lead with SCJ-700 (Writ-C No. 1003603 of 2008, same date and bench); one of the 21.03.2023 Coordinate Bench trio later followed in SCJ-490 to SCJ-494.

cases.title: Northern Coalfield Ltd. v. Chairman and Managing Director, U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Ors.
cases.application: A licensee's own circular/notification cannot alter or vary a tariff duly approved by the Regulatory Commission; in case of inconsistency, the Commission-approved tariff order prevails.

lead_authorities.name: LML Ltd., Kanpur v. State of U.P.

cases.title: M/S Om Food Manufacturing Center v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: After due discharge of bills, a later demand on alleged licensee mistake is confined to Section 56 as read in Rahamatullah Khan: additional demand may be raised, disconnection may not, and the demand cannot be progressively increased. The licensee must particularise the mistake and calculation, then sue if unpaid.

lead_authorities.name: Assistant Engineer, Ajmer Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Rahamatullah Khan alias Rahamjulla

cases.title: Krishna Kant Dubey v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.application: Interlocutory. Where consumption bills were paid regularly and the licensee claims accumulated arrears on an earlier prepaid meter, the writ court did not relegate to Clause 6.5 and required the licensee to explain by affidavit how such arrears can arise on prepaid supply, with interim interference on omission.

cases.title: Ghanshyam v. State of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Energy Deptt. & 3 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad (Lucknow Bench)
cases.application: After due discharge of the Clause 4.14(g) final bill, a later unusual demand is quashed. The licensee showed no provision authorising reassessment of a permanently disconnected, no-dues connection, and missing records were not a substitute.

cases.title: Mohammad Rashid & Another v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.application: A licensee must maintain the requisite supply and not create a load imbalance; a technical complaint of over-loading is to be audited and decided by the competent authority after notice to affected parties.

cases.title: Gauri Prasad v. State of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Deptt. of Energy, Lko. & 4 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad (Lucknow Bench)
cases.application: A plea that the consumer's representation/appeal was not addressed to the proper authority does not justify inaction. The licensee must inform the consumer or re-direct the papers to the Appellate Authority.

cases.title: Smt. Madhu Rani Agrawal v. State of U.P. & 5 Others
cases.application: Installation of new-connection infrastructure (within 500 m) is done by the licensee, whose estimate under Clause 4.6 includes laying-line/mains/material charges; the consumer pays but cannot insist on supplying/installing the equipment himself.

cases.title: Raman Ispat (Pvt.) Ltd. & Anr. v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.application: Where a common controlling person uses a web of firms/companies and acquisitions to escape recovery, the veil may be lifted to hold the applicant entity liable for the defaulter's arrears as a condition of supply.

cases.title: M/s L.M.L. Ltd. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.application: Once the licensee's competent authority decides to reduce load on a complete application without pointing out any shortcoming, the reduction stands approved and only ministerial steps remain; the licensee cannot resile by later insisting on requirements not raised at the time.

cases.title: Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Permanent Lok Adalat and Another
cases.application: A Lok Adalat cannot direct the licensee to grant a connection in a manner contrary to the Act and the Supply Code.

cases.title: U.P. State Cement Corporation Ltd. (In Liquidation), In re
cases.application: Late payment surcharge under Clause 6.7 / the rate schedule cannot be charged where the payer was not a defaulter — here an Official Liquidator with no funds until realisation of assets, supplying under court order; actual bills admitted, surcharge disallowed.

cases.title: Smt. Vimla Tiwari v. State of U.P. And Others
cases.application: A s.126 assessment founded on a checking report shown (through compelled personal affidavits) to be internally contradictory/fabricated is vitiated by malice in law, applying the doctrine that malice in law requires no proof of personal ill-will, only action without just cause or on a misrepresented factual basis — a significant procedural-fairness precedent in this corpus's s.126/s.135 assessment cluster.

lead_authorities.name: S.R. Venkatraman v. Union of India
Mukesh Kumar Agrawal v. State of U.P.
Somesh Tiwari v. Union of India
HMT Ltd. v. Mudappa

cases.title: U.P. State Cement Corporation Ltd. (In Liquidation), In re
cases.application: A writ of mandamus or an Article 142 direction to supply/continue supply cannot displace the substantive priority scheme of ss.529, 529-A and 530; residuary powers are supplementary, not a means to ignore statute.

lead_authorities.name: Textile Labour Association v. Official Liquidator
Supreme Court Bar Association v. Union of India

cases.title: Dr. Mohammad Afsar Khan And Another v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited, Varanasi And Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Mandamus for a direct connection is refused where the Code as amended already supplies the conversion path (51% of single-point consumers applying together) and the petitioners do not satisfy it.

cases.title: M/S Venus Stone Crushing Co. & Anr. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Ors.
cases.application: The mandatory seven-day pre-testing notice requirement (Amrawati Devi) is now final law, the Supreme Court having dismissed the SLP against it; non-compliance renders the test report unusable.

lead_authorities.name: Smt. Amrawati Devi v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Anr.

cases.title: M/S Modern Rice Mill v. MVVNL & Anr.
cases.application: A clause's marginal heading (e.g. 'Defective Meters' for Clause 5.6) does not restrict its substantive scope; general principle of statutory construction applied to a Supply Code clause.

lead_authorities.name: Chandroji Rao v. CIT
Padmaraje R. Kadambande v. CIT
Guntaiah & Others v. Hambamma & Others

cases.title: Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. Through Its Executive v. Electricity Ombudsman, U.P., Lucknow and Others
cases.application: Paragraph 11 of the Commercial and Revenue Manual (the petitioner linked the exception to Clause 9.1 of the 2005 Code) withholds MCG for a disconnection period only if no dues are pending. An Ombudsman finding of pending bill dues leaves no occasion to waive MCG; the waiver is quashed. Distinct from SCJ-030 / SCJ-059 (fault for the interruption) and SCJ-490–494 (tariff-order non-waivability of minimum monthly charges).

cases.title: Ujala Kumar @ Ujala Singh v. State of Bihar & Ors.
cases.application: A mere signature of the owner on the tenant/lease-holder's connection application does not amount to consent unless expressed in such terms.

cases.title: U.P. Rajya Vidyut Parishad v. Panjab Corbohydrate
cases.application: Absent any allegation of theft or tampering, a dispute about whether a meter records correctly must be decided by the Electrical Inspector (s.26(6) IEA 1910), who alone may estimate consumption and fix the amount; the licensee cannot self-assess. The 2003 regime carries a parallel scheme (Code 2005, Clauses 5-6).

lead_authorities.name: Madhya Pradesh Electricity Board v. Smt. Basantibai

cases.title: Mohamdabad Cold Storage Private Ltd. (& Anr.) v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.application: Where a billing dispute turns on the accuracy of a meter/transformer reading, the consumer must first invoke the Clause 5.6 testing procedure (and thereafter the Electrical Inspector) rather than approach the writ court directly; the writ challenge is premature until that statutory route is exhausted.

lead_authorities.name: Bombay Electric Supply and Transport Undertaking v. Laffans (India) Pvt. Ltd.

cases.title: Mother India Refrigeration Industries (& Anr.) v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.application: Companion application of the same principle as SCJ-083.

lead_authorities.name: Bombay Electric Supply and Transport Undertaking v. Laffans (India) Pvt. Ltd.

cases.title: M/s Vikas Cool Industries v. Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: The Court did not test the meter or recast the bills on the writ; it sent the consumer to Clause 5.6 and directed the licensee to decide in accordance with law.

cases.title: Dinesh Kumar Gupta v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: The registered consumer in whose name the meter stands is liable for the charges; Clause 2.2(oo)'s 'Occupier' definition does not shift liability to a tenant in occupation. Cf. the definitional Clause 2.2 applied in SCJ-072.

cases.title: M/S Modern Rice Mill v. MVVNL & Anr.
cases.application: Testing of a disputed meter by its own manufacturer (e.g. Secure Meters Ltd.) does not satisfy the Code's requirement of testing at an 'independent laboratory'; such testing is inherently biased and cannot be relied upon to sustain an unauthorised-use assessment. Followed by later cases (see also SCJ-051 line applying the same technical background).

lead_authorities.name: M/s JMD Alloys Limited v. Bihar State Electricity Board

cases.title: M/S Venus Stone Crushing Co. & Anr. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Ors.
cases.application: Reaffirms (following Modern Rice Mill, SCJ-059, and JMD Alloys) that a meter manufacturer's own lab is not an 'independent laboratory'; extends the point with a burden-of-proof holding that the licensee must affirmatively prove the consumer (not an intervening cause after the meter left his custody) caused any tampering found.

lead_authorities.name: M/s Modern Rice Mill v. MVVNL & Anr.
M/s JMD Alloys Limited v. Bihar State Electricity Board

cases.title: Rituraj v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.application: A meter manufacturer's own laboratory (Secure Meters Ltd.) is not an 'independent laboratory' under Clause 5.6(b)(iii); its report cannot be relied upon because it has a commercial interest and cannot be a judge in its own cause.

lead_authorities.name: Modern Rice Mill v. Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.

cases.title: Lala Ram Batham v. U.P. Power Corporation Nigam & Ors.
cases.application: A disputed/implausible meter reading is to be resolved by a Clause 6.5 representation before the licensee, decided by a speaking order after inspection of the meter, rather than by the writ court on merits.

cases.title: M/s Hotel Pride Inn v. Purvanchal Vidhut Vitrana Nigam Ltd. and Another
cases.application: Want of M.R.I. readings is treated as a reason the consumer has not yet filed Clause 6.5 objections. The writ court facilitates supply of the readings (here, by e-mail once an ID is given) rather than quashing the reiterating demand or deciding the bill.

cases.title: M/S. Mohan Electrocasting Pvt. Ltd. And Another v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. And Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: A bill based on check-meter readings compared with an alleged defective main meter is a meter-reading/billing-correctness dispute for Clause 6.5, not a writ determination of whether independent laboratory testing or presence at meter removal was required.

cases.title: The Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Anr. v. The Electricity Ombudsman of U.P. & Anr.
cases.application: A dispute that billed units (24,400) did not match the licensee's later MRI/office reading (2,45,280) is a meter-reading/billing grievance first raised with the licensee under paragraph 6.5, then CGRF/Ombudsman. Same cluster as SCJ-046, SCJ-551.

cases.title: I.G. Shoes Pvt. Ltd. v. Kanpur Electricity Supply Co. Ltd. and Others
cases.application: A consumer who allows the meter to be removed/replaced without raising a s.26(6) dispute loses the material evidence and cannot later dispute past bills on meter-correctness grounds.

cases.title: Rituraj v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.application: The licensee must apprise the consumer of the Clause 5.6(c)(iii) right to choose the testing venue, including independent testing, before testing a sealed meter.

cases.title: Smt. Amrawati Devi v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Anr.
cases.application: Before a sealed meter is tested, the licensee must give the consumer a clear (bold-capitals) notice of the right to choose the testing venue — licensee's lab, an approved independent agency, or the electrical inspector; omitting it makes the testing illegal.

cases.title: M/S Modern Rice Mill v. MVVNL & Anr.
cases.application: Minimum consumption/guarantee charges for a disconnection period are chargeable only if the disconnection is attributable to the consumer's own fault; a licensee-caused or unresolved-fault disconnection cannot ground such a demand.

cases.title: Sigma Castings Ltd. & Another v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Others (with Kundan Castings (P) Ltd.; PVVNL v. Vidyut Lokpal; M/s Shyam Ferrous Ltd.)
cases.application: A mixed feeder serving multiple unrelated consumers is not an 'independent feeder' under Clause 2.2(ff); an Electricity Ombudsman award directing supply via a mixed feeder in derogation of Clause 3.4(a) exceeds Regulation 11 jurisdiction and is quashed.

lead_authorities.name: Punjab State Electricity Board v. Vishwa Calibere Builders Pvt. Ltd.

cases.title: Dhirendra Kumar Chaudhary v. State of U.P. & 5 Others
cases.application: The Establishment must prove disciplinary charges by evidence led through a Presenting Officer; charges are not proof of themselves, and material used behind the delinquent's back vitiates the inquiry.

lead_authorities.name: State of U.P. v. Saroj Kumar Sinha
Roop Singh Negi v. Punjab National Bank
State of Uttaranchal v. Kharak Singh

cases.title: Umesh Chandra Verma v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. and 3 Others
cases.application: In a major-penalty inquiry charges are not self-proving. The establishment must lead documentary and oral evidence through a Presenting Officer before an impartial inquiry committee; want of named witnesses in the charge-sheet, or a plea that documents were not disputed as to genuineness, does not relieve that burden when the delinquent has denied the charges.

lead_authorities.name: State of Uttar Pradesh v. Saroj Kumar Sinha
Roop Singh Negi v. Punjab National Bank
State of Uttaranchal v. Kharak Singh

cases.title: Tarun Kumar Pathak v. State of U.P. and others
cases.application: In a major-penalty inquiry charges are not self-proving. The Establishment must lead documentary and oral evidence through a Presenting Officer before an impartial inquiry committee; documents annexed to the charge-sheet are not evidence unless formally proved in the delinquent's presence. A namesake date of appearance, with no later date fixed, does not satisfy that procedure. Same cluster as SCJ-017 and SCJ-548.

lead_authorities.name: State of Uttar Pradesh v. Saroj Kumar Sinha
Roop Singh Negi v. Punjab National Bank
State of Uttaranchal v. Kharak Singh

cases.title: Virendra Kumar Mittal v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & 2 Others
cases.application: Supply on payment of the estimate is independent of an as-yet-undetermined theft-assessment liability; the licensee cannot withhold a new connection for such an amount under Clause 4.3, but may take security for it.

lead_authorities.name: Dr. Meena Chaudhary v. BSES Rajdhani Power Ltd.

cases.title: Shri Gautam Motors Pvt. Ltd. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Others
cases.application: A bill/demand cannot be raised on the basis of a check meter, there being no such provision in the Code or the Act.

cases.title: Harihar Cold Storage v. P.V.V.N.L. & Another
cases.application: Minimum-guarantee (and like) charges cannot be levied for a period in which supply failed for a reason attributable to the licensee; the obligation to pay is tied to the licensee's maintaining the minimum standard of supply.

lead_authorities.name: Raymond Ltd. v. M.P. Electricity Board

cases.title: M/s Rukmani Ferro Pvt. Ltd. v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: As only a provisional assessment had been made, the Court held there was no occasion for coercive action and declined interim protection.

cases.title: Subhashis Chatterjee v. U.P. Power Corporation Limited, Lucknow through Chairman and others
cases.neutral_citation: 2011 SCC OnLine All 611 : (2011) 89 ALR 888 : (2011) 6 All LJ 527
cases.application: Code Clause 8.1 disconnection applies only to theft (s.135); a UUE case (s.126) does not attract it, and a domestic connection cannot be disconnected for UUE.

cases.title: Abdul Gaffar @ G. Hussian v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Where no Final Assessment Order under Section 126 is passed, the assessee is prima facie deprived of the Section 127 appeal, warranting interim protection against recovery. Related to the Section 127 remedy considered in SCJ-1266.

cases.title: Smt. Shanti Devi v. Managing Director, Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran & Anr.
cases.application: A consumer who consumed electricity must clear the bills; non-payment justifies disconnection, and the absence of a raised bill is no licence for free consumption - the remedy is to resolve the billing dispute under the Code.

cases.title: I.G. Shoes Pvt. Ltd. v. Kanpur Electricity Supply Co. Ltd. and Others
cases.application: A writ court will not issue a mandamus to enforce an order that is without jurisdiction and a nullity.

cases.title: Sigma Castings Ltd. & Another v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Others (with Kundan Castings (P) Ltd.; PVVNL v. Vidyut Lokpal; M/s Shyam Ferrous Ltd.)
cases.application: A licensee's prior mistaken/inadvertent supply of another similarly-situated consumer via a non-compliant route cannot be invoked to compel repetition of that illegality for a different consumer — Article 14 does not guarantee negative equality.

lead_authorities.name: Chandigarh Administration v. Jagjit Singh
State of Orissa v. Mamata Mohanty

cases.title: Ram Charan v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Where the assessee files no objection to a provisional assessment order for unauthorised use, the recovery proceedings are rightly initiated and a writ against the citation fails; the remedy is the Section 127 appeal. Same Section 126/127 cluster as SCJ-1269, SCJ-1266, SCJ-047.

cases.title: M/s Saini Alloys Pvt. Ltd. v. U.P. Power Corporation, Lucknow & Ors.
cases.application: The licensee could not be held to a surcharge-exemption promise that would breach Section 24 of the Reforms Act; there is no estoppel against a statute, and a concession can be withdrawn in public interest.

lead_authorities.name: Sharma Transport v. Government of A.P.

cases.title: Tehsildar v. State of U.P. and others
cases.neutral_citation: 2009 SCC OnLine All 1931 : (2009) 83 AIC 493 : (2010) 1 All LJ (NOC 84) 22
cases.application: Theft recovery cannot precede a final assessment under Clause 8.1(b); a final assessment must be made (recording service of the provisional assessment) even where the consumer files no objection.

cases.title: Rajendra Prasad v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.application: Recovery of Rs.40,856 on a provisional theft assessment, without a speaking final assessment, was stayed as contrary to clause 8.1(b).

cases.title: Rajesh Kumar v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Provisional theft assessment had been served and recovery of Rs 40,856 begun without a final assessment; recovery stayed until that step is completed, whether or not objections were filed.

cases.title: Rajendra Kumar Gupta v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: The 16.8.2010 bill was treated as a final theft assessment issued without a Clause 8.1(b) provisional bill, notice or objections; it was quashed, leaving the licensee to pass a proper final assessment after that process.

cases.title: Raman Ispat (Pvt.) Ltd. & Anr. v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.application: A petitioner who withholds material facts and obtains an interim order by painting a false picture is not entitled to discretionary relief.

cases.title: Vijay Lakshmi v. Bihar State Electricity Board & Ors.
cases.application: A Supply Code clause cannot be applied retrospectively to fasten liability arising from a disconnection that pre-dates the Code's coming into force.

cases.title: Vineet Plastics Ltd. v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. and Another
cases.application: Provisional assessment bills cannot be issued serially in the absence of a provision in the Act or the Code; provisional billing under Clause 6.2(b) is confined to cases where the meter reading cannot be taken, and regular-bill disputes lie under Clause 6.5.

cases.title: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Appellate Authority/Addl. Commissioner & Anr. (Sunita Spat Pvt. Ltd.)
cases.application: Even a finding of 'no theft' by the appellate authority remains subject to the Special Court's determination of civil liability for theft under Sections 154(5)-(6) read with Sections 153 and 155; the licensee's revenue interest being thereby protected, the finding is no ground to interfere in writ.

cases.title: M/s L.M.L. Ltd. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.application: The Code does not require the U.P. Electricity Regulatory Commission's approval of a licensee's decision to reduce load; the reference to the Commission was a redundant exercise that could not defeat rights accrued on the licensee's own decision.

cases.title: Shri Krishna Kumar Sharma v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: A writ at the proposed-assessment / calculation-sheet stage is not entertained; the consumer is relegated to file objection before the Executive Engineer, the calculation sheet being only a call for his response. Same objection-stage / relegation line as SCJ-1270, SCJ-1271, SCJ-032.

cases.title: Mahboob Ahmad v. Commissioner, Moradabad & Another
cases.application: The writ court will not re-examine the quantum of a s.126 assessment that the s.127 appellate authority has considered and reduced; the consumer's remedy is to comply, not to re-litigate the amount in writ.

cases.title: Dhyanendra Singh v. State of U.P. & 5 Others
cases.application: The writ court will not restore an electricity connection under Article 226 where it is seriously alleged, in pending proceedings, to have been obtained by forged/fraudulent documents; the remedy is a fresh application or the outcome of the criminal case.

cases.title: Suresh Chand Bansal v. Electricity Ombudsman & Others
cases.application: Transmission lines are not part of a licensee's distribution system (s.2(72)), so a person affected by a transmission-line accident is not a 'consumer' (s.2(15)) for that purpose.

cases.title: Raju v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Another
cases.application: Permanent disconnection of electricity supply — even where grounded in an allegation of unauthorized use — requires prior notice/show-cause opportunity under the Supply Code; disconnection without notice is arbitrary and unauthorized, warranting reinstatement without prejudice to a subsequent lawful show-cause process.

cases.title: M/s Rukmani Ferro Pvt. Ltd. v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: The objection to the very competence to issue the Section 126(2) notice was directed to be raised before, and decided by, the competent authority in a reasoned order after hearing, rather than by the writ court.

cases.title: Gaurav Sharma v. State of U.P. & 4 Others
cases.application: A genuine occupier (including a family member in separate possession) has a statutory right under s.43(1) to a connection and may furnish an indemnity bond (Annexure 4.2) where the owner's NOC is unavailable; the bond only excludes trespassers/house-grabbers.

lead_authorities.name: Seema Mansoor v. U.P. Power Corporation
Chandu Khamaru v. Nayan Malik

cases.title: Husna Bano v. State of U.P. & 9 Others
cases.application: A tenant/occupier unable to obtain the owner's NOC may obtain a connection on an indemnity bond (Annexure 4.2); the bond is not a title document, and a landlord-tenant/succession dispute is no ground to deny the basic necessity of electricity.

lead_authorities.name: Gaurav Sharma v. State of U.P.
Chandu Khamaru v. Nayan Malik

cases.title: Smt. Uma Chauhan v. State of U.P. And 2 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Applied in a criminal-revision setting: a tenant in occupation is entitled to an electricity connection under Clause 4.4 and Annexure 4.2; getting an additional meter in the tenanted premises through the electricity department is not Section 420 fraud. Same cluster as SCJ-115 (Seema Mansoor), SCJ-006, SCJ-212, SCJ-265.

lead_authorities.name: Seema Mansoor v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.

cases.title: Dr. Ashok Kumar Sharma & Another v. State of U.P. & 4 Others
cases.application: The right of a tenant/occupier to a connection under the Code presupposes authorised occupation; it does not extend to a person against whom an unstayed eviction decree operates. (Qualifies the tenant-occupier entitlement recognised in Anand Kumar / SCJ-006.)

lead_authorities.name: Anand Kumar v. State of U.P.

cases.title: Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Permanent Lok Adalat and Another
cases.application: A non-owner occupier may obtain a connection on an indemnity bond (Annexure 4.2) in lieu of owner's consent, but only on producing proof of occupancy (PoA / rent receipt / registered lease).

cases.title: Jayant Singh v. Pradeep Kumar Verma
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
cases.application: An indemnity bond under Clause 4.4 is not enough. The occupier must also furnish an occupancy certificate under Clause 4.4 read with Annexure 4.2. Until that is done, non-release of the connection is not contempt of a writ that directed supply only if formalities were completed. Same cluster as SCJ-249.

cases.title: Executive Engineer, Electricity Urban Distribution Division IInd v. Electricity Ombudsman, Lucknow & Ors.
cases.application: An Electricity Ombudsman's award is akin to an arbitral award and may be interfered with only on grounds similar to s.34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.

lead_authorities.name: Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Vidyut Lokpal (Electricity Ombudsman)

cases.title: Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd., Bhikaripur & Anr. v. Vidyut Lokpal (Electricity Ombudsman) & Anr.
cases.neutral_citation: 2008 SCC OnLine All 376 : AIR 2008 All 127 : (2008) 5 All LJ 683
cases.application: An Electricity Ombudsman's award is akin to an arbitral award, challengeable only on grounds similar to s.34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996; a conciliated settlement is challengeable only for want of jurisdiction or fraud.

cases.title: U.P. Power Corp. Ltd. Through Executive Engineer v. Ombudsmen and 2 Others
cases.application: An Electricity Ombudsman award that waives tariff charges, or otherwise directs the licensee to act against the Electricity Act, 2003 and the Supply Code, 2005, is without authority and is set aside. Applied via Narinder Chand Hem Raj: no direction against the provisions of the Act and the Code.

cases.title: Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. Through Its Executive v. Electricity Ombudsman, U.P., Lucknow and Others
cases.application: An Electricity Ombudsman award under s.42(6) that waives MCG contrary to paragraph 11 of the Commercial and Revenue Manual (and the Clause 9.1 exception the licensee invoked) cannot stand. Same cluster as SCJ-490–494, on a pending-dues rather than tariff-order footing.

cases.title: U.P. Power Corp. Ltd. Through Executive Engineer v. Ombudsmen and 2 Others
cases.application: An Electricity Ombudsman award that waives tariff charges, or otherwise directs the licensee to act against the Electricity Act, 2003 and the Supply Code, 2005, is without authority and is set aside. cases.application: An Electricity Ombudsman award that waives tariff charges, or otherwise directs the licensee to act against the Electricity Act, 2003 and the Supply Code, 2005, is without authority and is set aside. Applied via Narinder Chand Hem Raj: no direction against the provisions of the Act and the Code.

lead_authorities.name: Narinder Chand Hem Raj v. Lt. Governor, Himachal Pradesh

cases.title: Prakash Chandra Gupta v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.application: On a consumer's representation, the Electricity Ombudsman cannot take away part of the relief CGRF had granted when the licensee filed no appeal. Unchallenged CGRF relief is final between the parties (Authorised Officer (Land Reforms)); CGRF on remand is equally barred from withdrawing it.

lead_authorities.name: Authorised Officer (Land Reforms) v. M.M. Krishnamurthy Chetty

cases.title: The Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Anr. v. The Electricity Ombudsman of U.P. & Anr.
cases.application: Where the licensee never asked the Ombudsman to have the meter checked, the Ombudsman may still treat the meter as defective on the licensee's own records and an unexplained more-than-tenfold consumption spike, and direct average billing; the writ court will not interfere with that reasoned award.

cases.title: Kisan Cold Storage & Ice Factory v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors. (Full Bench reference)
cases.application: Foundational Full Bench ruling: the Section 42(5)-(7) Forum/Ombudsman grievance scheme is for the consumer alone; a Regulation cannot extend the Ombudsman remedy to the Distribution Licensee, as that would make the subordinate regulation inconsistent with the parent Act.

lead_authorities.name: Jindal Poly Films Limited v. U.P. Electricity Regulatory Commission

cases.title: M.K. Pathak, Executive Engineer v. The Electricity Ombudsman & Ors.
cases.application: Confirms, on Clause 7.10 of the Supply Code and Section 42(5)-(7), that only the consumer (not the licensee) may approach the CGRF/Ombudsman — an independent DB ruling reaching the same conclusion later confirmed by the Full Bench in Kisan Cold Storage (SCJ-043) construing the parallel UPERC Regulations, 2007 provision.

cases.title: M/S Three Star Paper Mills Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P. & 5 Ors.
cases.application: Acceptance of a licensee's One Time Settlement covering all pending disputes estops the consumer from later reviving any one of those disputes.

cases.title: Chunni Lal Gupta v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.application: A final theft/assessment bill cannot be raised without the Code's mandatory provisional-bill notice, 15-day reply window and hearing; a same-day 'revised bill' is only provisional.

cases.title: Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Others v. M/s Prakancha Metal Works Pvt. Ltd.
cases.application: The Code's billing/disconnection timeline (15-day bill dispatch plus notice) is mandatory; a truncated bill and premature disconnection are illegal.

cases.title: Dr. Munni Lal v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.application: A final theft assessment requires the Code's mandatory 15-working-day show-cause notice and a hearing; recovery cannot precede a final assessment.

cases.title: Gauri Shankar Gupta v. State of U.P. & 4 Others
cases.application: A proper Section 126 / Clause 8.1 assessment made after notice and hearing is a precondition to any recovery of theft dues; recovery under the 1958 Act cannot precede a valid final assessment.

cases.title: Hazi Mohd. Yaseen v. P.V.V.N.L. & Another
cases.application: In the consumer/electricity-theft context, the statutory 'reasonable opportunity of hearing' (s.126(3)) includes a personal hearing before a final assessment; taking note of written objections alone is insufficient.

lead_authorities.name: Transmission Corpn. of A.P. Ltd. v. Sri Rama Krishna Rice Mill
Khem Chand v. Union of India

cases.title: Mohd. Sagir v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.application: A s.126(3) final assessment made without deciding the consumer's objection and without allowing even minimal time to be heard — and before the statutory one-month window closed — is void for breach of natural justice; set aside on that ground alone.

cases.title: Arup Kumar Mitra v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.application: A final assessment passed before the revised provisional notice was even transmitted/served, and without considering the objection, violates natural justice.

cases.title: Kamil v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.application: A recorded conclusion of UUE reached without a fair opportunity of hearing cannot support an assessment; natural justice applies to the serious charge of unauthorised use, which may also be a s.135 offence.

cases.title: Suresh Kumar v. U.P. Power Corporation, Shakti Bhawan, Lucknow & Others
cases.application: Objections to the (re-characterised) provisional assessment must be decided by a speaking order after a reasonable opportunity of hearing before recovery proceeds.

cases.title: Tehsildar v. State of U.P. and others
cases.neutral_citation: 2009 SCC OnLine All 1931 : (2009) 83 AIC 493 : (2010) 1 All LJ (NOC 84) 22
cases.application: Clause 8.1(b) contemplates notice, hearing and a speaking final assessment in theft cases before recovery is initiated.

cases.title: Bhajan Lal and Anr. v. Executive Engineer, Electricity Distribution Khand-1, U.P. and Ors.
cases.application: Actual service of the provisional assessment and a real opportunity to object are essential to natural justice before recovery in a UUE case.

cases.title: Shahvez Abdullah v. State of U.P. & 6 Others
cases.application: Service of the provisional assessment must be shown (a receipt on the record); a recital that the consumer did not object, without proof of service, will not support a 'final' assessment or recovery. The 'final' order is demoted to a provisional one and objections are to be heard. Same cluster as SCJ-014, SCJ-022, SCJ-028, SCJ-117.

cases.title: M/s S. Milan Agro Industries & 2 Others v. State of Uttar Pradesh & 4 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: The Code sequence is provisional assessment, objections and hearing, then a completed final assessment. A further hearing granted after that final order is not a Code step and puts the entire assessment under a cloud. Same cluster as SCJ-014, SCJ-022, SCJ-028, SCJ-032, SCJ-117, SCJ-280.

cases.title: Saurabh Agarwal v. State of U.P. And 3 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: The assessing authority must grant a proper opportunity of hearing on a fresh representation and pass a reasoned order, which is to be treated as the final assessment. Same cluster as SCJ-014, SCJ-022, SCJ-028, SCJ-117, SCJ-280, SCJ-351.

cases.title: M/S I.G. Shoes Pvt. Ltd. v. U.P. Electricity Corporation Ltd. & Others
cases.application: Ashok Kumar's requirement of notice and a speaking assessment, and a reasoned appellate order, applied to a 2002-Code theft assessment. Absence of notice, a non-speaking Executive Engineer order, and an Appellate Committee order that only reiterated the 2002 Code without discussing the grounds, vitiated both; remitted for fresh assessment after show-cause and hearing. Same cluster as SCJ-014, SCJ-048, SCJ-280.

lead_authorities.name: Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P.

cases.title: Akhalak Ahmad v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitaran Nigam Ltd. Thru' G.M. & Others
cases.application: Where the 2005 Code was not yet in force at the date of checking, natural justice still required supply of the survey/checking report so the consumer could object to the provisional assessment. An appellate order that dismissed the appeal solely on the unserved report is quashed; the provisional assessment is left to a fresh decision after objections. Same cluster as SCJ-014, SCJ-022, SCJ-028, SCJ-117, SCJ-280.

cases.title: Uco Bank v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.application: Service of the provisional assessment and a written objection are not enough. Clause 6.8(c) still requires a personal hearing before the objection can be rejected and the assessment treated as final. Same cluster as SCJ-014, SCJ-022, SCJ-028, SCJ-117, SCJ-280.

cases.title: Smt. Amna Khatoon v. PVVNL & Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: The consumer is left to file objections to the 7.3.2008 provisional assessment within 15 days; the respondents then proceed to a final order in accordance with law. The writ court does not short-circuit that two-stage process.

cases.title: M/S Mayur Sheetgrah Pvt. Ltd. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. And Others
cases.application: A theft assessment is vitiated if the MRI report, which clause 8.1(a)(vii) requires to be supplied where tampering is alleged, is furnished only along with the final order. Same MRI/testing-before-assessment cluster as SCJ-682.

cases.title: Kerala State Electricity Board & Ors. v. Thomas Joseph Alias Thomas M.J. & Ors. (with connected appeals)
cases.application: Extends and crystallises Seetaram Rice Mill's core holding: excess-load consumption is 'unauthorised use of electricity' under Explanation (b)(iv) to s.126 in every case, independent of whether it changes tariff category or causes revenue loss, because the harm targeted by s.126 is systemic (grid integrity, voltage stability) not merely pecuniary — the single most significant s.126/Explanation(b) doctrinal clarification in this corpus, directly governing every 'excess load' assessment case in the collection (cf. SCJ-042, SCJ-061, SCJ-111, SCJ-123's Clause 3.4 independent-feeder line, SCJ-121, SCJ-126, SCJ-139, SCJ-145).

lead_authorities.name: Executive Engineer, Southern Electricity Supply Co. of Orissa Ltd. (Southco) v. Sri Seetaram Rice Mill

cases.title: Indian Oil Corporation Ltd. v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.application: Applied against a distribution licensee: the procedural prerequisite (amending the agreement) is deemed waived within a reasonable time of the consumer's request.

lead_authorities.name: M.K. Shah Engineers & Contractors v. State of M.P.
Kusheshwar Prasad Singh v. State of Bihar
Mrutunjay Pani v. Narmada Bala Sasmal
Chairman, SBI v. M.J. James
Nirmala Anand v. Advent Corporation (Pvt.) Ltd.

cases.title: Managing Director, D.V.V. Nigam Ltd. & 2 Others v. Sri Kartar Singh & Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Applied against the licensees: having produced no bills or ledgers before February 2009, they cannot recover earlier arrears or take the benefit of that default under Section 56(2). Same cluster as SCJ-001.

cases.title: Iftakhar Ahsan v. State of U.P. and others
cases.application: A new connection to an occupier/tenant requires the owner's consent under Clause 4.4(a)(vi); absent that consent no mandamus to connect can issue.

cases.title: Vijay Lakshmi v. Bihar State Electricity Board & Ors.
cases.application: Clause 4.15(vi) of the Bihar Supply Code makes the owner liable for a tenant's arrears only where the connection was given with the owner's consent; without proof of consent the clause cannot be invoked to deny a fresh connection.

cases.title: Ujala Kumar @ Ujala Singh v. State of Bihar & Ors.
cases.application: Clause 4.15(vi) fastens liability for a lease-holder's arrears on a person only where the connection was given with the house-owner's consent.

cases.title: Ashok Kumar Ajmera v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: The liability for dues under the demand notice and citation was fixed on the owner/lessor in whose name the connection stood, notwithstanding termination of the dealership and Hindustan Petroleum's running of the outlet.

cases.title: Shri Kunwar Sarvesh Kumar Singh v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.application: The s.2(15) 'consumer' definition's broad second limb (premises connected for receiving electricity) extends civil assessment liability for theft to a property owner even where an unsubstantiated tenancy is claimed, though criminal mens rea remains a separate question — an important gloss on who bears assessment liability, complementing this corpus's transferee/occupant-liability cluster (SCJ-090, SCJ-098).

cases.title: Daya Nand Sharma v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.application: Where an owner objects to a licensee laying/supplying over his premises, the licensee must obtain the DM's/Commissioner's permission under the proviso to Rule 3(b) of the Works of Licensees Rules, 2006; a connection cannot be forced over the objection without it.

cases.title: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitaran Nigam Ltd. & Anr. v. Commissioner, Moradabad Region & Anr.
cases.application: The owner of premises falls within 'consumer' (s.2(15)) and can be subjected to a s.135 theft assessment for revenue purposes even if the premises were let out; criminal mens rea is a separate trial question.

cases.title: Anil Shastri v. State of U.P. Thru. Principal Secy. Power & Others
cases.application: Applied to the Secretary of a registered society who occupied the premises of the society's connection. Consumer (s.2(15), followed in the 2005 Code) plus occupier (Clause 2.2(oo)) plus person (s.2(49)) made him liable for the theft assessment on a direct cable to the distribution line. Same cluster as SCJ-121 / SCJ-179 (owner as consumer), here occupier-secretary rather than owner.

cases.title: M/s Kesarwani Sheetalaya & Ors. v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.application: 'Service line' (Clause 2.2(vv)) and 'independent feeder' are separate concepts; paras 4.29 and 3.4 are harmonised so that para 4.29 cannot be used to supply other consumers through an independent feeder while bypassing the Clause 3.4 conditions, which would otherwise be rendered redundant.

cases.title: Ram Charan v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Recovery under the citation was stayed on a part-deposit (Rs.35,000 against Rs.75,220) without prejudice to the parties' rights; the interim indulgence did not entitle the petitioner to a merits adjudication in the writ.

cases.title: Sri Chandu Khamaru v. Smt. Nayan Malik & Ors.
cases.application: A pending private/ownership dispute between the applicant and third parties is not a ground to deny the owner/occupier his statutory right to supply under s.43.

cases.title: Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Permanent Lok Adalat and Another
cases.application: A Permanent Lok Adalat may entertain a consumer's grievance over refusal of an electricity connection; its jurisdiction is in addition to, not in derogation of, the Act's fora.

lead_authorities.name: Bar Council of India v. Union of India

cases.title: Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Permanent Lok Adalat, Moradabad & Anr.
cases.application: A Permanent Lok Adalat may conciliate but cannot adjudicate on merits a dispute relating to electricity theft; s.22-C(8) ousts adjudicatory jurisdiction over any offence-related dispute regardless of compoundability or whether an FIR was lodged.

lead_authorities.name: Torrent Power Ltd. v. State of U.P.

cases.title: Executive Engineer, Distribution Division & Anr. v. Pacific Promoter
cases.application: A plea that the civil court lacks jurisdiction (here under s.145) can be raised at any stage of the proceedings, even after years, since every court must satisfy itself of its jurisdiction.

cases.title: S.K. Construction Co. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.court: National Company Law Tribunal, Allahabad Bench (Prayagraj)
cases.application: The licensee is a secured operational creditor recovering pre-CIRP dues only through the Section 53 waterfall, not from the auction purchaser; on liquidation the right to recover from the premises/purchaser is extinguished.

lead_authorities.name: West Bengal State Electricity Distribution Co. Ltd. v. Sri Vasavi Industries Ltd.

cases.title: HSA Traders v. Office of the Executive Engineer, Electricity Distribution Division, Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited & Anr.
cases.court: National Company Law Tribunal, Allahabad Bench (Prayagraj)
cases.application: The licensee is a secured operational creditor recovering pre-CIRP dues only through the Section 53 waterfall, not from the auction purchaser; on liquidation the right to recover from the premises/purchaser is extinguished.

lead_authorities.name: Eastern Power Distribution Co. of Andhra Pradesh Ltd. v. Maithan Alloys Ltd. (NCLAT)
West Bengal State Electricity Distribution Co. Ltd. v. Sri Vasavi Industries Ltd.

cases.title: Iftakhar Ahsan v. State of U.P. and others
cases.application: A judgment delivered under the provisions in force before the 2005 Code does not aid an applicant where the Code has since introduced a new mandatory requirement.

lead_authorities.name: Rajesh Kumar Gupta v. State of U.P.

cases.title: M/s Rukmani Ferro Pvt. Ltd. v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: The Court refused to entertain a writ against a provisional assessment notice under Section 126(2), holding the challenge premature and relegating the consumer to file a detailed objection which the assessing authority could modify, confirm or discharge.

lead_authorities.name: GKN Driveshafts (India) Ltd. v. Income Tax Officer & Ors.

cases.title: M/S Birla Aircon v. District Magistrate, Meerut & Ors.
cases.application: The Supply Code's 'premises' definition (area/portion sanctioned to a single consumer) bounds the scope of recovery/sealing against a defaulting consumer; disputes about whether a third party's distinct premises were wrongly included are fact-specific and go to the recovery authority (Collector), not the writ court.

cases.title: KPB Metals Private Limited v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.application: 'Premises' is the specific area/khasra for which a single consumer's connection was applied for or sanctioned; later-acquired contiguous plots are not part of it merely by adjacency.

cases.title: M/S Dev Prayag Paper Mill (Pvt.) & Ors. v. State of U.P. & Ors. (batch of ~90 connected writ petitions)
cases.application: The s.47(5)/Clause 4.20(l) security exemption for consumers willing to take supply through a prepayment meter operates only once such meters are actually available for that consumer category; unavailability (as for HT consumers) leaves the licensee's ordinary power to demand security under s.47(1)-(4) intact. Followed and agreed with the Telangana/AP High Court's parallel ruling in Sarwottam Ispat.

lead_authorities.name: Sarwottam Ispat Ltd. v. Southern Power Distribution Company of Telangana Ltd. & Ors.

cases.title: Ashok Kumar & Ors. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.application: An officer can exercise recovery powers as a 'prescribed authority' under the U.P. Government Electrical Undertakings (Dues Recovery) Act, 1958 only if notified as such; absent notification, s.3 demand notices are invalid.

cases.title: Vinay Kumar Singh v. State of U.P. And 2 Others
cases.application: A consumer's own prior judicial admission (in a separate proceeding) that a disputed name is his alias precludes a later mistaken-identity defence against a recovery citation issued in that name — an evidentiary/estoppel point in the theft-recovery enforcement context.

cases.title: Bhajan Lal and Anr. v. Executive Engineer, Electricity Distribution Khand-1, U.P. and Ors.
cases.application: A Clause 6.8(b) provisional-assessment/show-cause notice must be served by an authentic mode (registered post + personal service, then newspaper publication); ordinary post does not establish service.

cases.title: M/s. Suvidha Engineers India Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.application: A bank-guarantee condition that operates only because the consumer voluntarily sought enhanced load does not nullify or override the court's stay of the underlying assessment.

lead_authorities.name: Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal, In re

cases.title: Dinesh Kumar Gupta v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: After a provisional assessment the authority must give the meter-holder notice to object before a final assessment; a simultaneous provisional-cum-final assessment is treated as merely provisional and reopened. Same 126(3) objection-stage line as SCJ-032, SCJ-898.

cases.title: Suresh Kumar v. U.P. Power Corporation, Shakti Bhawan, Lucknow & Others
cases.application: A provisional assessment must contain the calculation and the amount assessed; a document lacking these is no assessment at all, and the consumer is entitled to have objections decided by a speaking order after hearing.

cases.title: Shri Krishna Kumar Sharma v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Under the Supply Code, 2005 the Executive Engineer holds the provisional-assessment power; an Assistant Engineer (Revenue) calculation sheet issued on the EE's behalf is not the assessment, so a 'wrong officer / bad in law' challenge fails.

cases.title: Lalit Kumar Kapoor v. Kanpur Electricity Supply Company & Anr.
cases.application: Reasonable opportunity of hearing before a theft-based Section 126 assessment is governed by Clauses 6.8(b)(i)/6.8(c)(iii)/8.1(b) of the Supply Code; substantial compliance (even via a court-directed representation) condones a procedural defect at the provisional stage.

lead_authorities.name: Khem Chand v. Union of India
Transmission Corporation of A.P. Ltd. v. Sri Rama Krishna Rice Mill

cases.title: M/S Mayur Sheetgrah Pvt. Ltd. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. And Others
cases.application: Supplying the MRI with the final order, while the order itself says clause 8.2(i) remains uncomplied and further proceedings are to be taken, is not a reasonable opportunity before a theft assessment is finalised.

cases.title: Noida Power Company Ltd. v. State of U.P. & Anr.
cases.application: A licensee is entitled to a reasonable return; where the purchase price is disputed, reverse application of the Sixth Schedule principles is an appropriate method of determining the rate.

cases.title: Navi Hasan v. U.P. Power Corporation & Another
cases.application: An assessing officer who withdraws/recalls a demand order during pending litigation must disclose the statutory power (under the Electricity Act or Supply Code, 2005) exercised to do so; failure to do so is prima facie misconduct.

cases.title: Satya Prakash Singhal v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Clause 4.39 of the Supply Code r/w the second proviso to Section 135(1A) EA2003 makes reconnection or fresh connection available even after a permanent disconnection ('PDC final') recorded on theft allegations; the authority is directed to consider the request. Interplay of the Supply Code and the theft provision of the Act. Same Clause 4.39 reconnection route as SCJ-1138 and SCJ-1143.

cases.title: Mohd. Asif v. Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Having held that clause 4.38 did not authorise disconnection for a title dispute, the Court directed the consumer to apply for reconnection under clause 4.39 rather than restoring supply itself.

cases.title: Dinesh Kumar Gupta v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: On reopening the assessment for objection, the recovery citation was kept in abeyance for two months or till the authority's final decision, which the citation is to abide.

cases.title: Arup Kumar Mitra v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.application: When the final assessment is set aside, the recovery/citation must be withdrawn, not merely 'kept in abeyance' or deferred; deferring it is not compliance with the order.

cases.title: Rameshwar v. DVVNL & Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Recovery under Section 126 must be founded on the final assessment order, not the provisional assessment; quashing the demand notice leaves the assessee at liberty to challenge the final assessment order separately. Companion to the provisional/final-order point in SCJ-1267.

cases.title: Heera Lal v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.application: An objection to the correctness of an electricity demand lies before the assessing/electricity authority (or on appeal), not before the executing Tehsildar, who is confined to execution and cannot vary the demand.

lead_authorities.name: Chandra Kishore Jha v. Mahabir Prasad

cases.title: M/s Paliwal Alloys (Pvt.) Ltd. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Ors.
cases.application: Where an earlier order permitted a s.127 appeal on a part-deposit and restrained recovery pending the appeal, the licensee cannot recover the assessment while the appeal is undecided and no stay has been granted against that restraint.

cases.title: Saurabh Agarwal v. State of U.P. And 3 Others
cases.application: Till disposal of the Section 127 appeal, no coercive action is to be taken on the impugned Executive Engineer order.

cases.title: Gauri Prasad v. State of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Deptt. of Energy, Lko. & 4 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad (Lucknow Bench)
cases.application: Recovery against the petitioner is stayed for six weeks or until the decision on the fresh appeal, whichever is earlier.

cases.title: M/S Sijaria Ice Gramodhyog Sultanpura & Others v. State Of U.P. & Others
cases.application: Until the restored Appeal No. 03/2006-07 is decided afresh, recovery of electricity dues from the petitioner remains stayed.

cases.title: Shyam Ferrous Ltd. Gopal Nagar v. State of U.P. & 6 Others
cases.application: Service of a demand notice by registered post to the address on the licensee's records is deemed sufficient under Explanation 1 to s.3 of the 1958 Dues Recovery Act, regardless of a bare denial of receipt.

lead_authorities.name: Vishanji Tokarsi v. Collector, Kanpur Nagar

cases.title: BSES Rajdhani Power Ltd. v. Delhi Electricity Regulatory Commission
cases.application: A Regulator cannot, at the truing-up stage, change the methodology or principles of the initial tariff determination; doing so is an impermissible retrospective revision of a quasi-judicial tariff order.

lead_authorities.name: PTC India Ltd. v. CERC

cases.title: Chairman, West Bengal State Electricity Board & Ors. v. Syed Mukbul Hossain & Ors.
cases.application: Where the statutory appeal under Section 127 against a final assessment is available and has been invoked, the parties are relegated to it (with maintainability/limitation left to the appellate authority) rather than to writ/appellate interference on merits.

cases.title: Chandrika v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.application: A billing-correctness dispute is to be pursued through the Code's grievance channel (Clause 6.5) before the Competent Authority, not by writ, the writ court granting only interim protection on part-deposit.

cases.title: Dr. Santosh Kumar Awasthi v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.application: Against a final theft-assessment order, the consumer is relegated to the s.127 / Clause 6.8(d) appeal (with the half-deposit), the writ court giving only limitation protection and a short recovery stay.

cases.title: Jai Laxmi Cement Company Ltd. v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.application: A writ against a provisional assessment notice is premature; the consumer must file objections under s.126(3) and is relegated to the statutory assessment process, interference being confined to the Whirlpool exceptions.

lead_authorities.name: Executive Engineer, SOUTHCO v. Sri Seetaram Rice Mill

cases.title: Mohd. Daud v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.application: A billing-correctness grievance is relegated to the Clause 6.5 competent authority; the writ court will not entertain it at the first instance.

cases.title: Bharat Bhati v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.application: A writ against a Clause 6.8(B) show-cause/provisional assessment notice is premature; the consumer is relegated to file objections before the authority, which must decide by a speaking order.

cases.title: Smt. Mamta Devi Srivastava v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.application: A dispute about whether bills were sent is a disputed fact for the Clause 6.5 remedy, not the writ court.

cases.title: Ram Padarath Gupta v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & 4 Others
cases.application: A rate-category/billing grievance and the consumer's objections are for the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 r/w s.126; recovery abides that decision.

cases.title: Awadhesh Kumar Yadav v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.application: A disputed factual billing dispute is for the Clause 6.5 Executive Engineer or the Consumer Forum, not the writ court.

cases.title: Vikas Gupta & Another v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.application: A disputed question of service of the assessment notice is for the s.127 appeal against the final assessment, not the writ court; instalments are for the Clause 6.14 Executive Engineer.

cases.title: Moolchand Saini v. State of U.P. through Secretary, Power Corporation & Others
cases.application: A writ against a final s.126 assessment order is not entertained where the s.127 appeal (r/w Clause 6.8 of the Code) is available and untried.

cases.title: Shashi Bhushan Singh v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.application: Writ court declines to fix the bill and relegates the consumer to the Clause 6.5 mechanism, conditioning restoration of supply on a part-deposit.

cases.title: Foran Singh v. Executive Engineer, Dakshiranchal Vidyut Vitaran Distribution Division, Firozabad and Another
cases.application: Against an order deciding a recovery representation, the consumer is relegated to the Code's grievance mechanism (complaint to licensee, then CGRF) under Clause 7.10 r/w Clauses 7.7.1-7.7.5.

cases.title: Smt. Mamata Verma v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.application: A bill-accuracy dispute is dismissed in writ jurisdiction and relegated to the Clause 6.5(b) statutory forum.

cases.title: Ishwar Chandra v. U.P. Power Corporation Limited Thru' its M.D. & Another
cases.application: A disputed factual challenge to a final s.126 assessment is not entertained in writ jurisdiction; the consumer is relegated to the s.127 appeal.

cases.title: Gopali v. State of U.P. through Secretary and others
cases.application: A factual challenge to a final s.126 assessment is not entertained in writ jurisdiction where the s.127 appeal (r/w Clause 6.8) is available.

cases.title: Smt. Jama Begum v. Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & 2 Others
cases.application: Confirms (by reciting and refusing to treat as a mandatory direction) the writ court's relegation of a billing dispute to Clause 6.5; contempt does not lie to compel a 'correct bill' after such a disposal.

cases.title: Devendra Nath Dubey v. Executive Engineer, Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
cases.application: Recites the writ court's relegation of a dues/correctness dispute to Clause 6.5 (time-bound EE decision + limited stay of coercive recovery). Contempt does not survive once that representation has been decided.

cases.title: Sanjay Kumar v. State of U.P. & Another
cases.application: A writ seeking transfer of a connection on a representation to the supply company is disposed of by directing a prescribed-form application to the Executive Engineer under Clause 4.4; the Court does not itself transfer.

cases.title: Saurabh Agarwal v. State of U.P. And 3 Others
cases.application: The consumer is directed to appeal under Section 127 to the Divisional Commissioner within three weeks, with a bank draft of Rs. 10 lakhs in addition to the 25% already deposited, the appeal to be decided preferably within two months.

cases.title: Gauri Prasad v. State of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Deptt. of Energy, Lko. & 4 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad (Lucknow Bench)
cases.application: Without examining merits, the consumer is directed to file a fresh appeal before the competent appellate authority within ten days; if filed, it is to be heard and decided within four further weeks.

cases.title: Smt. Amna Khatoon v. PVVNL & Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: A writ challenging a Section 126(4) provisional assessment is disposed of with liberty to file objections within 15 days; the assessing officer proceeds in accordance with law to a final order, after which Section 127 is the appeal. The Court did not quash or uphold the 7.3.2008 order.

cases.title: Ram Charan v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: On relegating a belated assessee to the Section 127 appeal, the writ court may fix a time to appeal and direct the appellate authority to decide on merits without going into limitation, neutralising the delay.

cases.title: M/s L.M.L. Ltd. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.application: A notification under ss.3-4 of the 1966 Act suspends pre-notification liabilities and stays their enforcement, satisfying the stay condition of Clause 4.49 without any court order.

lead_authorities.name: Modern Syntax (I) Ltd. v. Debts Recovery Tribunal, Jaipur

cases.title: Trimurti Concast Pvt. Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited
cases.court: National Company Law Tribunal, Allahabad Bench (Prayagraj)
cases.application: On approval of a resolution plan under s.31 IBC, pre-CIRP claims not in the plan are extinguished; the corporate debtor under new management cannot be denied a fresh electricity connection for those dues.

lead_authorities.name: Ghanshyam Mishra & Sons (P) Ltd. v. Edelweiss Asset Reconstruction Co. Ltd.

cases.title: South East U.P. Power Transmission Company Ltd. v. Prescribed Authority & Ors. (with Tata Steel Ltd. v. State of U.P.)
cases.application: Electricity dues for the pre-CIRP period, not claimed during CIRP and not in the approved resolution plan, stand extinguished under s.31 IBC; the resolved entity takes over on a clean slate and statutory recovery cannot revive them.

lead_authorities.name: Ghanashyam Mishra & Sons (P) Ltd. v. Edelweiss Asset Reconstruction Co. Ltd.
CoC of Essar Steel India Ltd. v. Satish Kumar Gupta

cases.title: Reliance Projects and Property Management Services Ltd. v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.application: An approved and implemented resolution plan binds statutory authorities and extinguishes all pre-effective-date claims not filed during CIRP or not in the plan; a claim cannot be resurrected after implementation.

lead_authorities.name: Ghanshyam Mishra & Sons (P) Ltd. v. Edelweiss Asset Reconstruction Co. Ltd.

cases.title: Devendra Sharma v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.application: Supply of electricity is necessary for a life with dignity; disconnection for reasons not authorised by the Act/Code, for malafide purposes, violates Article 21.

cases.title: Divya Sahani v. State of U.P. & Another
cases.application: Supply of electricity to an occupant is fundamental to living with dignity under Article 21; refusal/disconnection on extraneous grounds offends it.

cases.title: M/S Ambuja Cements Limited v. Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Limited
cases.application: A Section 11 court does not decide whether a Supply Code penalty must go to the Clause 7.10 CGRF/Ombudsman; it only asks whether an arbitration agreement exists, leaving the Code-forum objection to the arbitrator.

lead_authorities.name: M/S Mayavati Trading Pvt. Ltd. v. Pradyuat Deb Burman
Duro Felguera, S.A. v. Gangavaram Port Ltd.
GOQII Technologies Pvt. Ltd. v. Sokrati Technologies Pvt. Ltd.

cases.title: Satyam Shukla v. State of U.P. and 3 Others
cases.application: Section 126 requires the assessing officer to conduct the inspection and then provisionally assess. A provisional assessment by the Executive Engineer founded on a Junior/Assistant Engineer's checking report is set aside; the licensee may initiate assessment afresh in accordance with that procedure.

lead_authorities.name: Executive Engineer v. M/s Sri Seetaram Rice Mill
