cases.title: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Appellate Authority/Addl. Commissioner & Anr. (Sunita Spat Pvt. Ltd.)
cases.application: 'Unauthorised use of electricity' in Explanation (b) to Section 126 is comprehensive enough to cover theft under Section 135; the scheme of the 2003 Act (with the third proviso to Section 135(1A)) contemplates assessment under Section 126 for all categories of unauthorised use, including theft.

cases.title: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Appellate Authority/Addl. Commissioner & Anr. (Sunita Spat Pvt. Ltd.)
cases.application: A final order of assessment under Section 126 that has attained finality cannot be re-opened by the assessing authority, save under inherent authority in cases of fraud or misrepresentation and after affording an opportunity of hearing.

cases.title: Sandeep Kesarwani v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.application: An inordinate gap between provisional and final assessment (here, over two years) requires a fresh notice/hearing before the final assessment is passed; failure to do so violates natural justice regardless of the consumer's earlier default in objecting.

cases.title: Mrs Rajendra Kumar Sharma v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.application: A final assessment under s.126 must engage with the consumer's objections and record findings after a fixed hearing date, per Clauses 6.8/8.1; failure to do so vitiates the assessment and any recovery founded on it — reinforcing the procedural-strictness line already tracked in this corpus for theft/final-assessment orders (e.g. SCJ-069, SCJ-071).

cases.title: Jagat Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.application: Section 126 recovery cannot rest on a provisional assessment notice that omits a Clause 6.8(b) hearing date and the basis of the demand; the notice and citations fall.

lead_authorities.name: Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P.

cases.title: Shiv Shankar v. U.P. Power Corporation
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Division Bench quashed a theft-labelled recovery because no Section 126 provisional assessment was on record and no hearing had been given, and sent the matter back for a served provisional assessment and reasoned final order.

lead_authorities.name: Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P.

cases.title: Gauri Prasad v. State of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Deptt. of Energy, Lko. & 4 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad (Lucknow Bench)
cases.application: An unexplained three-month gap between making a provisional assessment (24.02.2023) and sending it by registered cover (08.05.2023), with no shown final assessment and incomplete instructions, was treated as a breakdown of communication: the consumer had not been served with the assessment or demand in accordance with law.

cases.title: Saurabh Agarwal v. State of U.P. And 3 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Section 126 provisional notices and a purported final assessment, followed by a demand, are not left to stand as concluded. The matter is heard de novo after a 25% deposit, and a reasoned order is to be treated as the final assessment within six weeks.

cases.title: Smt. Ranjana Gupta v. Executive Engineer (Distribution), Asst. General Manager & Anr.
cases.application: A theft bill and s.3 recovery notice issued without show-cause, provisional assessment or final assessment violate s.126(3) and are quashed.

lead_authorities.name: Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P.

cases.title: M/S Mahavir Iron Foundry And Another v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. And Others
cases.application: Provisional assessment without a prior show-cause is per se illegal. Combined with absence of a designated assessing officer until 27.6.2006, the 12.9.2005 inspection assessments cannot stand. Licensee may proceed afresh after opportunity.

lead_authorities.name: Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P.
A.K. Kraipak v. Union of India

cases.title: Smt. Kalpana Agarwal v. Managing Director, Western Electricity & Others
cases.application: Section 126 read with Clause 6.8 requires inspection report, provisional assessment with show-cause, personal hearing and a speaking final order. Non-compliance, which licensee's counsel did not dispute, vitiated the 02.11.2007 assessment.

lead_authorities.name: Ashok Kumar & Others v. State of U.P. & Others

cases.title: Shamsul Qamar v. PVVNL and Others
cases.application: A licensee cannot meet a challenge to a provisional theft bill merely by pointing the consumer to section 126(3) objections when the laboratory report of the removed meter has not been supplied. Those objections cannot then be filed.

cases.title: M/S Mayur Sheetgrah Pvt. Ltd. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. And Others
cases.application: Where the MRI was not supplied before the assessment was finalised, the writ is maintainable despite the statutory appeal. Whirlpool: alternative remedy is no bar on a breach of natural justice.

lead_authorities.name: Whirlpool Corporation v. Registrar of Trade Marks

cases.title: Smt. Vimla Tiwari v. State of U.P. And Others
cases.application: Because s.126 assessment often shares its factual predicate with s.135 theft and carries comparable reputational/character consequences, the same procedural rigour and honest fact-recording expected in quasi-criminal proceedings must govern s.126 assessments.

cases.title: Ashok Kumar & Ors. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.application: s.126 requires a hearing at two distinct stages — before the assessing officer records the conclusion of unauthorised use (guilt), and before final assessment (quantum); the recorded conclusion of unauthorised use is the jurisdictional condition precedent to a provisional assessment.

cases.title: Smt. Ranjana Gupta v. Executive Engineer (Distribution), Asst. General Manager & Anr.
cases.application: Ashok Kumar paras 58-60 applied: dual opportunity — first on unauthorised use, then provisional assessment and objection before final assessment — directed to be completed within two months.

lead_authorities.name: Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P.

cases.title: M/S Mahavir Iron Foundry And Another v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. And Others
cases.application: Ashok Kumar para 58 applied: opportunity before concluding unauthorised use (which confers jurisdiction to issue the provisional notice) and a distinct opportunity before final assessment on quantum. No show-cause before the 24.9.2005 provisional assessment; assessment illegal.

lead_authorities.name: Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P.

cases.title: Smt. Kalpana Agarwal v. Managing Director, Western Electricity & Others
cases.application: Ashok Kumar paras 56–64 applied: opportunity before concluding unauthorised use (which confers jurisdiction to issue the provisional notice) and a distinct opportunity before final assessment on quantum. Straightaway demand of Rs. 15,20,828 without either stage cannot sustain.

lead_authorities.name: Ashok Kumar & Others v. State of U.P. & Others

cases.title: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Appellate Authority/Addl. Commissioner & Anr. (Sunita Spat Pvt. Ltd.)
cases.application: An appeal under Section 127 is maintainable only against a final order under Section 126; a provisional assessment (even a revised one issued during the appeal, on which no final order is passed) is not appealable, requires no amendment of the memo of appeal, and does not render the pending appeal infructuous.

cases.title: Smt. Vimla Tiwari v. State of U.P. And Others
cases.application: Structural critique: a s.127 Commissioner who mechanically defers to the Superintending Engineer technical member without independent application of mind fails the statutory purpose of an appeal — a notable institutional-design observation in this corpus.

cases.title: Smt. Ranjana Gupta v. Executive Engineer (Distribution), Asst. General Manager & Anr.
cases.application: An Appellate Committee that does not decide the checking report or the assessment, and rests the appeal on a counsel's concession of theft recorded only in the operative portion and disputed as unauthorised, has not independently adjudicated; the order is quashed.

lead_authorities.name: Himalayan Coop. Group Housing Society v. Balwan Singh

cases.title: M/S Venus Stone Crushing Co. Thru' Partner & Another v. The U.P. Power Corpn. Ltd. Thru' Chairman & Others
cases.application: An appellate order that recites facts and the assessing officer's findings without discussing any ground of appeal is not an order in the eye of law. Quashed and restored for a reasoned decision (later by the Divisional Commissioner, Jhansi).

cases.title: M/S Sijaria Ice Gramodhyog Sultanpura & Others v. State Of U.P. & Others
cases.application: An appellate order that recites facts and the inspection team's finding of unauthorised use, without considering any ground of appeal, is not an order in the eye of law. Quashed and restored to the Commissioner, Jhansi Division, for a reasoned decision after hearing. Same cluster as SCJ-640.

cases.title: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Appellate Authority/Addl. Commissioner & Anr. (Sunita Spat Pvt. Ltd.)
cases.application: As Section 127 prescribes no parameters for deciding the appeal, the appellate authority's power is co-extensive with the assessing authority's and it is competent to decide whether the case is one of theft (para 8.1, Supply Code 2005) or unauthorised use (para 6.8); a reasoned finding is not disturbed in writ merely because a second view is possible.

cases.title: Satish Kumar Bharti alias Chhotu v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.application: s.135(1)(a)–(e) define theft and share one punishment; omitting the sub-clause from the FIR/charge-sheet/cognizance is not fatal if the narration is complete.

cases.title: Satish Kumar Bharti alias Chhotu v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.application: The 24-hour police-complaint rule in s.135(1-A) second proviso, reinforced by Clause 8.2 of the Code and s.57 consequences, is mandatory; a theft FIR lodged four days after inspection vitiates the criminal case. Indresh Patel (DB, directory) is treated as per incuriam; Varun Kumar Yadav (coordinate Bench; SLP pending) is followed.

lead_authorities.name: Varun Kumar Yadav v. State of U.P. & Others
Indresh Patel @ Indreshwar Singh v. State of U.P. & 4 Others
Dr. Arun Kumar v. Nagar Nigam, Bareilly

cases.title: Pawan Kumar Laur v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.application: An officer of a distribution licensee authorised under s.135(2) is competent to lodge an FIR for theft of electricity under s.135(1); this authority is not displaced by unproven allegations of malafide timing.

lead_authorities.name: State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal

cases.title: Mobin Ahamad v. State of U.P. & 2 Ors.
cases.application: A cognizable s.135 FIR will not be quashed, but arrest must comply with Cr.P.C. s.41(1)(b)/41-A safeguards where the offence carries under 7 years, and a compoundable s.135 offence's remedy lies via the Supply Code/s.152 route rather than quashing.

cases.title: Mohamad Aslam v. State of U.P. & 2 Ors.
cases.application: Companion application of the same principle as SCJ-081.

cases.title: Mohd. Rashid v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: s.135 FIR left standing; arrest, if at all, under CrPC 41/41-A; compounding pointed to the Supply Code rather than granted.

cases.title: Tinku Bhati alias Tinku Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Quash of a s.135 FIR refused; any arrest for a sub-seven-year offence must follow CrPC 41(1)(b)/41-A, and compounding if available is to be sought under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Riyazuddin v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.application: Applied to a pending s.135 FIR: no quash, but CrPC 41/41-A before arrest (max sentence not over seven years) and compounding left to the Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Alok Kumar Mishra v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Applied to refuse quashing of a s.135 FIR that disclosed a cognizable offence, while directing that any arrest comply with Cr.P.C. 41(1)(b) and 41-A and leaving compounding to the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Latoori Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Applied to a s.135 FIR writ: quash refused because the FIR disclosed a cognizable offence; arrest, if made, directed under CrPC 41(1)(b)/41-A; compounding left to the Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Nityanand Prajapati v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Applied to a pending s.135 FIR where arrest had not been effectuated; quash refused and compounding left to the Supply Code if available.

cases.title: Rakesh Kumar Shukla v. State of U.P.
cases.application: Quash of the s.135 FIR refused because it disclosed a cognizable offence; any arrest for an offence not carrying more than seven years must follow CrPC 41(1)(b)/41-A; compounding, if available, is to be sought under the 2005 Code.

cases.title: Vinay Pandey v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Quash of the s.135 FIR refused because it disclosed a cognizable offence; any arrest for an offence not entailing more than seven years' sentence must follow CrPC 41(1)(b)/41-A; compounding, if available, is to be sought under the Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Ikram v. State of U.P.
cases.application: Quash of a s.135 FIR refused because a cognizable offence was disclosed; CrPC 41/41-A arrest discipline applied and compounding, if available, left to the 2005 Code.

cases.title: Suresh Singh Sengar v. State of U.P.
cases.application: FIR under s.135 left standing; arrest, if any, tied to CrPC 41(1)(b)/41-A, and compounding left to the Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Mahboob v. State of U.P. — s.135 FIR disclosing cognizable offence not quashed
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Quash of the s.135 FIR refused because it disclosed a cognizable offence; prospective arrest confined to CrPC 41(1)(b)/41-A; compounding left to the Supply Code, 2005 if available.

cases.title: s.135 FIR not quashed; CrPC 41/41-A and Supply Code compounding
cases.application: Quash refused on a s.135 FIR; arrest, if at all, under CrPC 41(1)(b)/41-A; compounding to be sought under the 2005 Supply Code.

cases.title: Brij Mohan v. State of U.P. — s.135 FIR not quashed; arrest safeguards and compounding
cases.application: Quash of a s.135 FIR refused as it disclosed a cognizable offence; arrest, if at all, tied to CrPC 41(1)(b)/41-A because sentence cannot exceed seven years; compounding left to the Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Magister Tiwari @ Uday Pratap Tiwari v. State of U.P.
cases.application: s.135 FIR left intact; arrest, if made for an offence not exceeding seven years' sentence, must follow CrPC 41(1)(b)/41-A; compounding left to the Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Suresh v. State of U.P. and others
cases.application: Quash of a cognizable electricity FIR refused, but arrest (if any, for an offence not exceeding seven years) directed to follow CrPC s.41(1)(b)/41-A, with compounding left to the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 if the offence is compoundable.

cases.title: Awadhraj v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Quash of the s.135 FIR was refused because it disclosed a cognizable offence; the Court directed CrPC 41(1)(b)/41-A compliance if arrest were made (sentence not exceeding seven years) and pointed the petitioner to compounding under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 if the offence is compoundable.

cases.title: Ashok Kumar Gupta v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: s.135 FIR stands if it discloses a cognizable offence; arrest attracting ≤7 years must follow CrPC 41(1)(b)/41-A; compounding, if available, is under the Supply Code rather than by quashing the FIR.

cases.title: Sharafat v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Applied after refusing to quash: no arrest yet, so CrPC 41(1)(b)/41-A binds any future arrest for a sub-7-year s.135 offence; compounding is a Supply Code 2005 remedy, not a ground to quash.

cases.title: Kripa Shanker @ Kripal Pathak v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Quash of the s.135 FIR refused; future arrest, if made, tied to CrPC 41(1)(b)/41-A because sentence cannot exceed seven years; compounding left to the Supply Code 2005 if the offence is compoundable.

cases.title: Smt. Leelawati Sharma v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Quash refused because the s.135 FIR disclosed a cognizable offence; arrest, if made, confined to CrPC 41(1)(b)/41-A; compounding left to the Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Parvez v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Applied where a s.135/138 FIR was left standing: arrest, if at all, must follow CrPC 41/41-A, and compounding is for the Supply Code 2005, not the writ.

cases.title: Ajit Singh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Quash refused because the s.135 FIR disclosed a cognizable offence; arrest had not been made, so only a prospective CrPC 41(1)(b)/41-A direction issued; compounding left to Supply Code, 2005 if available.

cases.title: Manish Sharma v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: s.135 FIR left standing; arrest, if at all, under CrPC 41(1)(b)/41-A; compounding pointed to Supply Code 2005.

cases.title: Mangal Singh v. State of U.P. — s.135 FIR not quashed
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Applied to a s.135 FIR that disclosed a cognizable offence: quash refused; CrPC 41(1)(b)/41-A directed if sentence will not exceed seven years; compounding left to the accused under the 2005 Code and s.152.

cases.title: Avdhesh v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Quash of the s.135 FIR refused; arrest, if at all, under CrPC 41(1)(b)/41-A; compounding left to the Supply Code 2005 if the offence is compoundable.

cases.title: Smt. Chanda Devi v. State of U.P. and others
cases.application: Quash refused because the s.135(1)(c) FIR disclosed a cognizable offence; compounding directed to Supply Code 2005 and s.152; arrest, if any, confined to CrPC 41(1)(b)/41-A because sentence cannot exceed seven years.

cases.title: Jagdish Kaushik v. State of U.P.
cases.application: s.135 FIR disclosing a cognizable offence left intact; any arrest must follow CrPC 41(1)(b)/41-A; compounding, if available, to be sought under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Smt. Suman Devi v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: FIR left standing; arrest if any to follow CrPC 41(1)(b)/41-A because sentence cannot exceed seven years; compounding left to Supply Code 2005 and s.152.

cases.title: Smt. Meena Verma v. State of U.P.
cases.neutral_citation: Crl. Misc. Writ Petition No. 15715 of 2015
cases.application: FIR quash refused on the cognizable-offence test; arrest, if at all, tied to CrPC 41(1)(b)/41-A because the s.135 sentence cannot exceed seven years; compounding left to the Supply Code, 2005 and s.152.

cases.title: Babu Ram v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Where arrest under s.135 has not yet been made and the offence cannot attract a sentence exceeding seven years, police must follow CrPC s.41(1)(b) read with s.41-A. If the offence is compoundable, the accused may seek compounding under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 and s.152 of the Act.

cases.title: Mohammad Ali v. State of U.P.
cases.neutral_citation: Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. 2725 of 2015
cases.application: Quash of a s.135 FIR refused because it disclosed a cognizable offence; any arrest for an offence not entailing more than seven years must follow CrPC 41(1)(b)/41-A; compounding, if available, is to be sought under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Sunil Kumar Pal v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Applied to refuse quashing of a s.135 FIR while directing that any arrest for an offence not exceeding seven years follow CrPC 41(1)(b)/41-A and leaving compounding to the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

cases.title: Rajendra Kumar @ Raju v. State of U.P.
cases.application: FIR under s.135 left standing; police directed to CrPC 41(1)(b)/41-A if arresting because the offence cannot carry more than seven years; compounding left to the Supply Code, 2005 and s.152 rather than granted on the writ.

cases.title: Husain Ameer @ Bade Miyan v. State of U.P.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Quash of the s.135 FIR refused; arrest, if made, tied to CrPC 41(1)(b) and 41-A; compounding left to the Supply Code, 2005 if the offence is compoundable.

cases.title: Vijay v. State of U.P. (s.135 FIR; compounding and arrest)
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Writ to quash a s.135 FIR refused; compounding left to Code and s.152; CrPC ss. 41(1)(b) and 41-A directed if arrest is to be made for an offence not exceeding seven years.

cases.title: Jalaluddin v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.application: For a s.135 electricity-theft offence (≤7 years), arrest must follow the s.41(1)(b)/41-A Cr.P.C. safeguards and cannot be mechanical; the accused may compound under the Supply Code.

cases.title: Santosh Pathak v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.application: For a s.135 electricity-theft offence (≤7 years), arrest must follow the s.41(1)(b)/41-A Cr.P.C. safeguards and cannot be mechanical; the accused may compound under the Supply Code.

cases.title: A.K. Dixit @ Avdhesh Kumar Dixit v. State of U.P. & 4 Others
cases.application: For a s.135 electricity-theft offence (≤7 years), arrest must follow the s.41(1)(b)/41-A Cr.P.C. safeguards and cannot be mechanical; the accused may compound under the Supply Code.

cases.title: Kanchan Singh v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.application: For a s.135 electricity-theft offence (≤7 years), arrest must follow the s.41(1)(b)/41-A Cr.P.C. safeguards and cannot be mechanical; the accused may compound under the Supply Code.

cases.title: Santosh Pathak v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.application: For a s.135 electricity-theft offence (≤7 years), arrest must follow the s.41(1)(b)/41-A Cr.P.C. safeguards and cannot be mechanical; the accused may compound under the Supply Code.

cases.title: Anuradha v. State of U.P. & 4 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: A cognizable Section 135 FIR is left standing. Because the offence is punishable with seven years or less, arrest is not mechanical: notice under Section 35 BNSS, cooperation in investigation, and arrest only on credible material with reasons, following Arnesh Kumar and Md. Asfak Alam. This order applied the arrest-safeguard limb only; it did not mention compounding under the Supply Code.

lead_authorities.name: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar
Md. Asfak Alam v. State of Jharkhand

cases.title: Joginder Singh v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.application: At the Section 204 CrPC stage, a court summoning under ss.135/138 need not examine whether the act was dishonest. Section 39 of the repealed 1910 Act and Ram Chandra Prasad Sharma do not apply. Intention, if it emerges, is for trial.

cases.title: Shailendra Kumar v. State of U.P. & Another
cases.application: Prosecution for unauthorised reconnection under s.138 is independent of any billing/arrears dispute under Chapter 6 of the Code; a favourable consumer-forum order on a bill does not bar the s.138 prosecution.

cases.title: Sunil Todi & Ors. v. State of Gujarat & Anr.
cases.application: Company-director liability under s.141 NI Act (whether the accused was 'in charge of and responsible for' the company's business) is ordinarily determined at trial; sufficient prima facie averments in the complaint preclude quashing at the summoning stage.

lead_authorities.name: Sunil Bharati Mittal v. CBI
SMS Pharmaceuticals Ltd. v. Neeta Bhalla

cases.title: Ashok Garg v. State of U.P. and Another
cases.application: Unamended section 151's complaint route does not exclude FIR, investigation or a police charge-sheet for section 135. Following Vishal Agrawal, Cr.P.C. procedure governs; a charge-sheet for theft of electricity is competent.

lead_authorities.name: Vishal Agrawal v. Chhattisgarh State Electricity Board

cases.title: I.G. Shoes Pvt. Ltd. v. Kanpur Electricity Supply Co. Ltd. and Others
cases.application: The Electrical Inspector's s.26(6) jurisdiction is limited to a live meter-correctness dispute; it does not extend to disputes over bills or to theft/fraud/tampering assessments.

lead_authorities.name: Bombay Electricity Supply and Transport Undertaking v. Laffans (India) (P) Ltd.

cases.title: Western Electricity Supply Co. of Orissa Ltd. & Ors. v. M/s Baba Baijanath Roller and Flour Mill Pvt. Ltd.
cases.application: Confirms the well-settled distinction (M.P. Electricity Board v. Basantibai; Rupa Ice Factory; Sub-Divisional Officer (P), UHBVNL v. Dharam Pal) that s.26(6) of the 1910 Act, confined to genuine meter-correctness disputes referable to an Electrical Inspector, has no application to fraud/tampering allegations, which are instead governed by the licensee's own statutory Supply Code tampering provisions — directly relevant to this corpus's meter-tampering/theft-assessment cluster.

lead_authorities.name: Madhya Pradesh Electricity Board & Ors. v. Smt. Basantibai
State of W.B. v. Rupa Ice Factory (P) Ltd.

cases.title: Sri Chandu Khamaru v. Smt. Nayan Malik & Ors.
cases.application: Sections 42(1)/43(1) impose a duty to supply an owner or occupier on application and confer a correlative statutory right to obtain supply.

cases.title: M/S Prem Steels (Pvt.) Limited v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Others
cases.application: s.47(4) (in force 10.6.2003) requires interest on security at bank rate. The licensee cannot keep paying the 2002-Code rate for want of a SERC notification or because the deposit predated the 14.6.2008 insertion of Clause 4.20(i). The Code clause supplies the RBI bank rate; the start date is the Act.

cases.title: M/S Madhu Roller Flour Mills Pvt Ltd v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: 4.20(1)'s 3% credit is read down; interest on security is payable at the s.47(4) bank rate or more from 10 June 2003, for the period the sub-clause operated.

cases.title: Smt. Mamta Devi Srivastava v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cases.application: The s.56(2) limitation protects against belated first demands, not the ongoing accrued bills of a continuing consumer still being supplied; a gross defaulter who paid nothing while consuming cannot invoke it.

cases.title: Shyam Ferrous Ltd. Gopal Nagar v. State of U.P. & 6 Others
cases.application: The s.56(2)/Clause 6.15 two-year recovery-limitation bar applies only prospectively to post-2003-Act liabilities; pre-2003-Act liabilities remain governed by s.24 of the 1910 Act (no limitation on demand/recovery power) via s.6 of the General Clauses Act — an important temporal-scope qualification on the recovery-limitation doctrine tracked elsewhere in this corpus (SCJ-111, SCJ-113, SCJ-119), distinguishing and narrowing the Paliwal Alloys/Satya Narain line where the underlying liability predates the 2003 Act.

lead_authorities.name: Kusumam Hotels (P) Ltd. v. Kerala State Electricity Board
M/s Isha Marbles v. Bihar State Electricity Board

cases.title: M/S. Kamla Cold Storage And Ice Factory v. M.V.V.N.L. & Anr.
cases.application: Section 62(6) interest is confined to genuine overcharging above the determined tariff; a rebate under the tariff order is a bill-level concession, and its delayed crediting does not attract s.62(6) interest.

cases.title: Sri Chandu Khamaru v. Smt. Nayan Malik & Ors.
cases.application: Where a line must cross land whose owner objects, the licensee must find an alternative route or follow the s.67(2) permission procedure, causing least damage and paying compensation.

cases.title: Sri Chandra Mohan Goyal v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Others
cases.application: Reaffirms, in an electricity-penalty-circular context, the general rule that judicial precedent (including a Supreme Court ruling correcting a High Court's erroneous statutory/circular interpretation) applies retrospectively to pending disputes unless the deciding court expressly limits it to prospective operation.

lead_authorities.name: U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. v. Lohia Brass (P) Ltd.
Union of India v. Mohd. Ramzan Khan

cases.title: Subhashis Chatterjee v. U.P. Power Corporation Limited, Lucknow through Chairman and others
cases.neutral_citation: 2011 SCC OnLine All 611 : (2011) 89 ALR 888 : (2011) 6 All LJ 527
cases.application: The lawful response to a device used for unauthorised use is search and seizure under Clauses 4.33-4.34 (in the person's presence, with a signed seizure list), not disconnection.

cases.title: M/s Hind Industries Limited v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Section 127(6) provides interest at 16% per annum compounded every six months on the assessed amount; interest is a necessary corollary to retention of the amount, neither penal nor confiscatory (Wig Brothers).

lead_authorities.name: Wig Brothers (Builders & Engineers) (P) Ltd. & Anr. v. Union of India & Ors.

cases.title: S.K. Construction Co. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.court: National Company Law Tribunal, Allahabad Bench (Prayagraj)
cases.application: Section 238 IBC overrides Clause 4.3(f) of the U.P. Supply Code where inconsistent; a fresh connection to an auction purchaser cannot be conditioned on clearing the corporate debtor's pre-CIRP dues.

lead_authorities.name: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Raman Ispat Pvt. Ltd. (NCLAT)

cases.title: HSA Traders v. Office of the Executive Engineer, Electricity Distribution Division, Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited & Anr.
cases.court: National Company Law Tribunal, Allahabad Bench (Prayagraj)
cases.application: Section 238 IBC overrides Clause 4.3(f) of the U.P. Supply Code where inconsistent; a fresh connection to an auction purchaser cannot be conditioned on clearing the corporate debtor's pre-CIRP dues.

lead_authorities.name: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Raman Ispat Pvt. Ltd. (NCLAT)

cases.title: Trimurti Concast Pvt. Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited
cases.court: National Company Law Tribunal, Allahabad Bench (Prayagraj)
cases.application: Section 32A(2) bars action against the corporate debtor's property for pre-CIRP liabilities once an approved plan changes control to an unconnected person.

cases.title: Shailendra Kumar v. State of U.P. & Another
cases.application: The inherent power under s.482 Cr.P.C. is used sparingly and not to appreciate evidence or test the genuineness of allegations at the pre-trial/summoning stage; where a prima facie offence is disclosed, the proceedings are not quashed.

cases.title: Natthi Prasad v. State of U.P. and Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Section 528 BNSS treated as the inherent-power vehicle. The Court restated that s.482 Cr.P.C. at the pre-trial stage is used sparingly, not to appreciate evidence or try disputed defences, and dismissed the application because the FIR, statements and charge-sheet disclosed a prima facie ss.409/420 embezzlement case after departmental enquiry. Same cluster as SCJ-173, SCJ-142.

lead_authorities.name: R.P. Kapur v. State of Punjab
Manik B. v. Kadapala Sreyes Reddy
State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal
State of Bihar v. P.P. Sharma
Zandu Pharmaceutical Works Ltd. v. Mohd. Saraful Haq

cases.title: Syed Avesh Ahmad v. State of U.P. and Another
cases.application: At the s.482 stage only a prima facie case is seen; disputed facts (wrong implication after objecting to a neighbour's checking; additional L.T. cable besides connection no. 172337) cannot be adjudicated. Applying Bhajan Lal, Neeharika, R.P. Kapur, P.P. Sharma and Zandu Pharmaceutical, the charge-sheet and summoning in the s.135 case were not quashed. Same cluster as SCJ-173, SCJ-343, SCJ-538.

lead_authorities.name: State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal
M/s Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Maharashtra
R.P. Kapur v. State of Punjab
State of Bihar v. P.P. Sharma
Zandu Pharmaceutical Works Ltd. v. Mohd. Saraful Haq

cases.title: Ashok Garg v. State of U.P. and Another
cases.application: Resignation as director, takeover of the company, and absence from the raid are factual pleas. They are for the trial court or a discharge application, not for quashing a s.135 charge-sheet and summoning order under section 482. Same cluster as SCJ-173, SCJ-343, SCJ-539.

cases.title: Joginder Singh v. D.V.V.N. Ltd. thru' its Managing Director & Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: The consumer's plea that recovery beyond two years was barred by Section 56(2) was rejected prima facie: the sub-section addresses default in payment of charges, not theft. Same Section 56(2) cluster as SCJ-001, SCJ-406, SCJ-477.

cases.title: Sunil Todi & Ors. v. State of Gujarat & Anr.
cases.application: Establishes that a 'security' cheque issued at the outset of a Power Supply Agreement matures into an instrument for a legally enforceable debt once electricity is actually supplied and billed and payment defaults, distinguishing Indus Airways (no debt ever arose) and aligning with the Sampelly/Sripati Singh line — a significant precedent for electricity-dues enforcement via s.138 NI Act prosecutions, complementing this corpus's civil arrears-recovery cluster (SCJ-098, SCJ-124, SCJ-125, SCJ-127) with a criminal-law enforcement mechanism.

lead_authorities.name: Sampelly Satyanarayana Rao v. Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency Ltd.
Sripati Singh v. State of Jharkhand
Indus Airways Private Ltd. v. Magnum Aviation Private Ltd.

cases.title: Tehri Girders Limited and another v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited and others (with R.A. Castings, Sikka Papers and connected petitions)
cases.application: A security/additional-security deposit is an advance payment (depositor-depositee), not a debt owed to the licensee, and is not recoverable as arrears of land revenue.

lead_authorities.name: Ferro Alloys Corporation Limited v. A.P. State Electricity Board

cases.title: R.A. Castings Pvt. Limited v. PVVNL and Others
cases.application: Additional security under s.47 is not dues and is not arrears of electricity dues. A licensee cannot treat it as arrears so as to withdraw load-factor rebate under the tariff condition that a consumer with arrears is ineligible. Same characterisation as SCJ-252 (Tehri Girders) and the coordinate holding in K.L. Concast (Writ-C 7764 of 2011).

lead_authorities.name: Tehri Girders Limited v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited
The Mirzapur Electric Supply Company Limited v. State of U.P.
M/s K.L. Concast Pvt. Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.

cases.title: Sunil Todi & Ors. v. State of Gujarat & Anr.
cases.application: Whether a cheque was truly non-presentable security or secured an existing/maturing liability is a disputed question of fact for trial, not resolvable in a s.482 Cr.P.C. quashing petition.

lead_authorities.name: HMT Watches v. M.A. Habida
M/s Womb Laboratories Pvt. Ltd. v. Vijay Ahuja

cases.title: State of Gujarat & Ors. v. Utility Users' Welfare Association & Ors.
cases.application: Landmark Electricity Act institutional-architecture ruling: s.84(2) enabling (not mandatory) as to a judicial Chairperson, but mandatory legal/judicial Member requirement for any SERC exercising adjudicatory functions — foundational for any future case in this corpus touching SERC composition or the validity of Commission-level adjudicatory orders.

lead_authorities.name: Union of India v. Madras Bar Association (MJ-I)
Madras Bar Association v. Union of India (MJ-II)
Tamil Nadu Generation and Distribution Corporation Ltd. v. PPN Power Generating Company Pvt. Ltd.

cases.title: Arup Kumar Mitra v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.application: An assessment quashed by the writ court is non est; on remand the authority must pass a fresh reasoned/speaking order dealing with the objection, and cannot merely reaffirm or treat the quashed order as alive.

lead_authorities.name: Ashok Kumar v. State of U.P.

cases.title: M/s S. Milan Agro Industries & 2 Others v. State of Uttar Pradesh & 4 Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: The 28.12.2023 final assessment and all proceedings against the consumer are quashed. On 50% deposit the consumer may file a fresh objection, must be heard, and a fresh order is to be passed in accordance with law within eight weeks. Same cluster as SCJ-154.

cases.title: U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. v. Appellate Authority for Industrial & Financial Reconstruction & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: A licensee heard during and consenting to a BIFR-sanctioned scheme (Sections 19(2) and 32(1) SICA) is bound by its demand-charge waiver and cannot invoke its Electricity Act tariff-recovery obligation to escape it.

lead_authorities.name: M/s Indian Maize and Chemical Ltd. v. State of Uttar Pradesh

cases.title: M/s L.M.L. Ltd. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.application: A loss-making unit notified a 'Relief Undertaking' cannot be saddled with billing at the pre-reduction 8 MVA load after production has stopped; the declaration binds the licensee and continued 8 MVA billing was unjust and unfair.

cases.title: Kanpur Electricity Supply Co. Ltd. & Anr. v. M/s L.M.L. Limited & Ors.
cases.application: A licensee must give protective, fair treatment to a Relief Undertaking / Sick Industrial Company (current dues only, arrears in instalments, no coercive disconnection) and cannot defeat an agreed load reduction by legalese; the Supply Code is applied to aid revival.

lead_authorities.name: Modern Syntax (I) Ltd. v. Debts Recovery Tribunal, Jaipur

cases.title: Dr. Mohammad Afsar Khan And Another v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited, Varanasi And Others
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Conversion of an existing single-point supply in a multi-storey building to individual connections requires an application by 51% of the consumers drawing from that single point (Electricity Supply Code (Thirteenth Amendment), 2018). A shop-buyer with 10% support, whose sale deed accepted the vendor's one-point connection and a prepaid meter, has no cause of action for a direct connection. Writ dismissed.

cases.title: M/s Madhuvan Properties (P) Ltd. v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Another
cases.application: Under Clause 5.6(c)(ii) the difference for a slow/defective meter is chargeable only for the previous three months, and testing must be in the consumer's presence with an opportunity to object; a multi-year slow-meter demand cannot stand.

cases.title: Saurabh Agrawal & Another v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.application: Where a licensee itself assesses and fully recovers disputed consumption as slow-metering charges under Clause 5.6(c)(ii) (a civil, non-theft remedy), and a s.127 appellate authority conclusively finds s.135 inapplicable on the same facts, a parallel/continuing s.135 theft prosecution on the identical inspection report is an abuse of process.

cases.title: Kanpur Electricity Supply Co. Ltd. and another v. Uttar Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission, Lucknow and others
cases.application: A State-owned licensee filing a meritless writ against its own correct billing determination is liable to costs, recoverable from the officials responsible for advising the filing.

cases.title: M/S Modern Rice Mill v. MVVNL & Anr.
cases.application: Where the Supply Code's assessment-rate provision is discrepant with the governing statute (Section 126(6)), the statute prevails.

cases.title: M/S Venus Stone Crushing Co. Thru' Partner & Another v. The U.P. Power Corpn. Ltd. Thru' Chairman & Others
cases.application: Section 126(6) prevails over paragraph 6.17.2 of the 2002 Code on the assessment rate. Followed from Sri Bhagwan Gupta.

lead_authorities.name: Sri Bhagwan Gupta v. Kanpur Electricity Supply Company Ltd.

cases.title: Raj Kumar v. KESCO and Others
cases.application: Section 126(6) as it stood prevails over Clause 6.17.2 of the 2002 Code on the assessment rate. Followed from Pankaj Kumar.

lead_authorities.name: Pankaj Kumar v. Kanpur Electric Supply Company and others

cases.title: The State of Haryana & Ors. v. M/s Faridabad Gurgaon Minerals & Anr. (with M/s Ganpati Enterprises Slate Mines)
cases.application: General administrative-law doctrine (statutory power survives contractual silence, subject to the Indian Aluminium exception for express valid fetters) with potential cross-application to electricity tariff/circular-enhancement disputes in this corpus (cf. SCJ-128's retrospective-circular-application doctrine, SCJ-123's clause-enforcement holding).

lead_authorities.name: Indian Aluminium Co. v. Kerala State Electricity Board
State of Rajasthan v. J.K. Synthetics

cases.title: Executive Engineer, Electricity Urban Distribution Division v. The Electricity Ombudsman & 2 Others
cases.application: A statutory consumer grievance forum (CGRF/Ombudsman) must decide the consumer's dispute on merits and cannot abdicate by relegating the parties to an arbitration clause; the statutory remedy is additional, by right of election, not ousted by the agreement.

lead_authorities.name: Gujarat Urja Vikas Nigam Ltd. v. Essar Power Ltd.

cases.title: U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad & Anr. v. U.P. Power Corpn. Ltd.
cases.application: A statutory Electricity Supply Code (framed under the ERC's statutory mandate) overrides and supersedes a pre-existing administrative office memorandum on the same subject, from the Code's effective date, given the Code's statutory character versus the memorandum's mere administrative character — a useful precedent on the hierarchy between statutory Supply Code provisions and non-statutory licensee circulars/memoranda, complementing this corpus's Clause-precedence doctrine.

cases.title: Shyam Ferrous Ltd. Gopal Nagar v. State of U.P. & 6 Others
cases.application: For limitation purposes, an electricity charge/penalty 'first becomes due' only when a bill/demand is actually raised (and unpaid), not from the date of the underlying default/violation — a licensee's delayed billing (for legitimate reasons, e.g. awaiting correction of an earlier erroneous waiver) does not by itself extinguish recovery rights.

lead_authorities.name: MCD v. H.D. Shourie
NDMC v. Karam Chandra Thapar & Brothers Pvt. Ltd.

cases.title: M/s. Suvidha Engineers India Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.application: The Supply Code is regulation-making under s.181 (and s.86(1) 'supply'), not limited to the subjects listed in s.50; fiscal/protective provisions are within power.

cases.title: Satya Narayan v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. thru. its Managing Director & Others
cases.application: Provisions of the Supply Code must be construed together, in context, not in isolation — a specific clause (Clause 4.38(c)) cannot be relied upon divorced from the licensee's parallel obligations (Clause 4.36/6.15).

lead_authorities.name: Grasim Industries Ltd. v. Collector of Customs
Zameer Ahmed Latifur Rehman Sheikh v. State of Maharashtra

cases.title: Vijay Pal Singh & Another v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. and Others
cases.application: The Supply Code is subordinate legislation framed under the Electricity Act; by s.174 the Act overrides and the Code cannot travel beyond the Act's assessment limits.

cases.title: Vijay Pal Singh v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. and Others
cases.application: The Supply Code is subordinate legislation framed under the Electricity Act; by s.174 the Act overrides and the Code cannot travel beyond the Act's assessment limits.

cases.title: M/S Sri Dauji Cold Storage Pvt Ltd And Another v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd And Others
cases.application: Vijay Pal Singh applied: by s.174 the Act overrides; a Code three-times theft-assessment rate cannot travel beyond s.126(6)'s 1.5-times cap. Licensee's counsel could not dispute that holding.

lead_authorities.name: Vijay Pal Singh & Another v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd & others

cases.title: Raj Kumar v. KESCO and Others
cases.application: By ss.174 and 175 the 2003 Act overrides inconsistent law or instruments. s.185(3) saves the 1999 Reforms Act only if consistent. Clause 6.17.2's thrice rate cannot travel beyond unamended s.126(6).

lead_authorities.name: Pankaj Kumar v. Kanpur Electric Supply Company and others

cases.title: Kerala State Electricity Board & Ors. v. Thomas Joseph Alias Thomas M.J. & Ors. (with connected appeals)
cases.application: A landmark, sharply-reasoned ultra vires ruling: a State Commission's Supply Code, being delegated legislation under s.50/s.181(2)(x), cannot create a substantive carve-out from Section 126 liability that the parent Act's self-contained assessment code does not itself provide — reinforcing and extending Anis Ahmad's holding (already in this corpus at SCJ-139) that Supply Codes 'do not relate to' s.126 assessment, into an affirmative invalidation of a specific Regulation. This is the leading authority in this corpus on the limits of Supply Code rule-making power vis-a-vis the parent Electricity Act.

lead_authorities.name: U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Ors. v. Anis Ahmad
Sukhdev Singh & Ors. v. Bhagatram Sardar Singh Raghuvanshi & Anr.

cases.title: Northern Coalfield Ltd. v. Chairman and Managing Director, U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Ors.
cases.application: Where power is taken during restricted hours with (implicit or express) permission/acquiescence of the licensee, only the tariff surcharge applies; taking power surreptitiously/by theft during restricted hours instead attracts penalty under the theft provisions, not merely a surcharge.

lead_authorities.name: Prachi Leathers v. UPPCL

cases.title: Raj Narayan Singh v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.application: Even absent a right to object, tapping is permissible only where technically feasible and the licensee records that the original consumer's supply is not affected.

cases.title: M/s. Shree Gopala Iron (India) Ltd. & Anr. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: A challenge framed as 'beyond the scope of Section 45' to a demand-charge / 75% billable-demand levy for a disconnection period is really tariff interpretation, not want of jurisdiction; it does not attract the 'wholly without jurisdiction' exception to the alternative-remedy rule. Applied with Whirlpool and Gujarat Ambuja.

lead_authorities.name: Whirlpool Corporation v. Registrar of Trade Marks, Mumbai
State of H.P. v. Gujarat Ambuja Cement Ltd.

cases.title: M/S Shokumbhari Pulp & Paper Mills Ltd. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & 3 Others (with connected petitions)
cases.application: A revised tariff takes effect only from seven days after its publication (Clause 3.8 of the Supply Code / s.24(7) Reforms Act / Regulation 139); it cannot be applied retrospectively to an earlier date, following Binani Zinc's presumption against retrospective statutory/regulatory effect.

lead_authorities.name: Binani Zinc Ltd. v. Kerala State Electricity Board & Ors.

cases.title: Kerala State Electricity Board & Ors. v. Thomas Joseph Alias Thomas M.J. & Ors. (with connected appeals)
cases.application: Confirms, via s.45(3)(a)'s definition, that 'tariff' for s.126(6) purposes includes both fixed charges and energy charges, foreclosing any judicially- or regulation-created category of unauthorised-use assessment limited to fixed charges alone.

cases.title: Hyundai Engineering and Construction Co. Ltd. v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.application: Supply for construction/civil work is 'temporary' under LMV-9 Part C by reason of its purpose and defined period, not its load or how long it actually ran; it attracts the appropriate schedule's rate plus 25%.

cases.title: M/S Trikoot Iron & Steels Castings Ltd. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.application: Foundational clarification for the corpus: a theft-based assessment (Clause 8.1-8.3 of the Code) remains a Section 126 assessment appealable under Section 127; it is never treated as a non-appealable Section 135 order. Confirms and extends SCJ-011 (Chairman, WBSEB v. Syed Mukbul Hossain) and the Clause 6.8/8.1 line (Ashok Kumar, Mohit Paper Mills).

lead_authorities.name: Chairman, West Bengal State Electricity Board & Ors. v. Syed Mukbul Hossain & Ors.
Ashok Kumar & Others v. State of U.P. & Others

cases.title: Sunder Lal Chaubey v. State of U.P.
cases.application: Unauthorised L.T. line cut treated as a theft-case assessment (calculation under the Supply Code); after the Executive Engineer decided objections, the Court pointed the consumer to a Section 127 appeal rather than writ merits.

cases.title: Ram Kumar v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: The 24 May 2008 theft assessment was treated as a final assessment for which the only remedy was a Section 127 appeal; criminal acquittal did not convert the dispute into a writ for bill correction.

cases.title: M/S Urmila Oil Industries v. U.P. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam & Ors.
cases.application: An assessment cannot be grounded merely on the 'possibility' of theft inferred from a load pattern (e.g. MRI-recorded nil night load); the assessing authority must give specific, disclosed reasons and follow the Clause 6.8 procedure, engaging with the consumer's explanation on its merits (cf. SCJ-060 Mohit Paper Mills: theft must be established, not presumed).

lead_authorities.name: Ashok Kumar & Others v. State of U.P. & Others

cases.title: M/S Kamakhya Steels Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.application: Extends the SCJ-070 line from an MRI-pattern 'possibility of theft' to a checking report that itself records that no direct theft was detected and infers possibility only from CT/PT-chamber seals and mixed-feeder line losses: those facts cannot, without reasoned analysis converting possibility into a proved case of theft under s.135, support a Code assessment. A tampered outer/CT-PT seal without a finding that the meter itself was tampered or bypassed is not enough.

lead_authorities.name: Modern Terry Towels Ltd. v. Gujarat Electricity Board

cases.title: M/s Sangam Crusher Works & Another v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.application: Extends the SCJ-070 / SCJ-273 line from MRI-pattern or mixed-feeder 'possibility of theft' to a restart-inspection that finds an 11 kV cable on the floor and infers that the consumer could connect it to an energised line by artificial means. Without artificial means found on the spot, the s.135(1) proviso presumption is misplaced; a cable in the premises cannot indict on the hypothesis that theft is possible. Unlike SCJ-273 there is no remand: assessment and appeal are set aside.

lead_authorities.name: Ashok Kumar & Others v. State of U.P. & Others

cases.title: M/s K.G.N. Stone Crusher Mill & Another v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.application: Twin of SCJ-285, same day: a restart-inspection that finds an 11 kV cable on the floor and infers that the consumer could connect it to an energised line by artificial means does not make out theft. Without artificial means found on the spot, the s.135(1) proviso presumption is misplaced. Assessment and appeal set aside; no remand.

lead_authorities.name: Ashok Kumar & Others v. State of U.P. & Others

cases.title: M/s Kamakhya Steels Pvt. Ltd. & Another v. PVVNL & Another
cases.application: Companion to SCJ-273 (connected, same Bench and date): the checking report itself records that no direct theft was detected and infers only a possibility of theft from CT/PT-chamber seals and mixed-feeder losses. That possibility cannot, without a finding of actual theft, support an assessment of additional units. This record adds that a check-meter finding of slow running, with a lesser reading, is not theft.

cases.title: M/S Mohit Paper Mills Ltd. & Anr. v. PVVNL & Ors.
cases.application: A theft assessment under para 8.1(b)(iv) of the Code requires cogent, disclosed evidence of unauthorised use; an unexplained late-period divergence between the billing meter and untested outside check-meters (which otherwise tracked the billing meter closely) does not suffice, and an unsupported technical suggestion at hearing cannot cure the evidentiary gap.

cases.title: Mohan Dairy & Cold Storage Bulandshahar v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Others
cases.application: A 2002-Code para 6.17 theft finding cannot be presumed from a higher-capacity transformer and cable. Para 2.2(av) requires bypass, meter-tampering, or illegal tapping; absent those facts, and with the MDI in order, the case is excess sanctioned load under para 6.18. Same cluster as SCJ-060.

cases.title: M/S Mahavir Iron Foundry And Another v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. And Others
cases.application: Independent witnesses were not present at the inspection, and the licensee had been issuing minimum-consumption bills, so it could not be presumed that electricity was being used illegally. The 180-day formula assessment could not rest on that presumption.

cases.title: Ajmal v. State of U.P. & 2 Ors.
cases.application: A compoundable Section 135 theft offence is to be compounded under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 procedure; the Code supplies the enforcement / compounding machinery for theft (and, cognately, unauthorised use under Section 126).

cases.title: Anil Kumar Upadhyay v. State of U.P. & 6 Others
cases.application: A thin node: payment of the s.135-linked assessment and a proposed compounding report to the police station led the consumer to give up the writ; the Court did not itself apply the Code’s compounding machinery or decide that it had been followed.

cases.title: M/S Beeco Electrical India & Anr. v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.application: Where full arguments on the underlying theft assessment have already been made and the 'without jurisdiction' exception is invoked, the Court may examine the record on merits (checking report, MRI report) to see if the assessment is patently illegal, rather than mechanically relegating to the s.127 appeal; physical/MRI indicators of direct extraction, even without a red-handed catch, satisfy Ashok Kumar's notice-of-manner requirement.

lead_authorities.name: Ashok Kumar & Others v. State of U.P. & Others

cases.title: Rajee Steels Pvt. Ltd. & Anr. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.application: Recovery initiated in 2010 for a 1997 disconnection was quashed as barred by Clause 6.15(b) of the Supply Code, the Corporation having failed to establish that the dues were continuously shown as recoverable.

cases.title: Kerala State Electricity Board & Ors. v. Thomas Joseph Alias Thomas M.J. & Ors. (with connected appeals)
cases.application: Applies Punjab SEB v. Vishwa Caliber Builders' holding that a licensee's inability to timeously release a sanctioned enhancement does not excuse a consumer's overdrawal in the interim, and that an Ombudsman/adjudicatory authority commits jurisdictional error by directing regularisation/refund of amounts properly charged for such overdrawal absent statutory authorisation — reinforcing this corpus's Ombudsman-jurisdiction-limits cluster (cf. SCJ-123's citation of the same case; SCJ-138).

lead_authorities.name: Punjab State Electricity Board v. Vishwa Caliber Builders Private Limited

cases.title: U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad & Anr. v. U.P. Power Corpn. Ltd.
cases.application: A party that unilaterally accepts a charge/obligation under a successor Supply Code cannot consistently dispute an analogous charge under the code's statutory predecessor for the same underlying reasons.

cases.title: Ramveer Singh v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Another
cases.application: Under Annexure 6.3 (Clause 2) of the Code, a s.126 unauthorised-use assessment is charged at 1.5 times the applicable tariff; assessing at a higher multiple (thrice) is illegal.

cases.title: Vijay Pal Singh & Another v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. and Others
cases.application: Section 126(6) fixes assessment at 1.5 times the tariff; a Code provision assessing theft/UUE at three times is ultra vires and cannot be enforced.

cases.title: Vijay Pal Singh v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. and Others
cases.application: Section 126(6) fixes assessment at 1.5 times the tariff; a Code provision assessing theft/UUE at three times is ultra vires and cannot be enforced.

cases.title: Tejinder Singh v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Others
cases.application: Section 126(6) (unamended) fixes assessment at 1.5 times the applicable tariff. Computing a s.126 penalty on excess load at thrice that tariff is illegal; the assessment is set aside and a fresh order at the statutory 1.5-times rate is directed. Same cluster as SCJ-059, SCJ-188, SCJ-227.

cases.title: M/S Venus Stone Crushing Co. Thru' Partner & Another v. The U.P. Power Corpn. Ltd. Thru' Chairman & Others
cases.application: Sri Bhagwan Gupta applied: s.126(6) (unamended) fixes theft assessment at 1.5 times the tariff; computing thrice the units under 2002-Code paras 6.17.1 and 6.17.2 is illegal. Observation for the restored appeal; the assessment was not itself quashed. Same cluster as SCJ-059, SCJ-227, SCJ-638.

lead_authorities.name: Sri Bhagwan Gupta v. Kanpur Electricity Supply Company Ltd.

cases.title: M/S Sri Dauji Cold Storage Pvt Ltd And Another v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd And Others
cases.application: On a 1.11.2004 check, unamended s.126(6) fixes assessment at 1.5 times the tariff. A later Executive Engineer demand at three times is quashed. Same cluster as SCJ-227, SCJ-228, SCJ-638, SCJ-640.

lead_authorities.name: Vijay Pal Singh & Another v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd & others

cases.title: Raj Kumar v. KESCO and Others
cases.application: Unamended s.126(6) fixes a 26.10.2004 theft/UUE assessment at 1.5 times the tariff. Charging thrice under 2002-Code Clause 6.17.2 is illegal; assessment and appeal are quashed and the AO is to re-determine at the statutory rate. Same cluster as SCJ-059, SCJ-227, SCJ-228, SCJ-638, SCJ-640, SCJ-678.

lead_authorities.name: Pankaj Kumar v. Kanpur Electric Supply Company and others

cases.title: Ram Bahadur v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.application: The 12-month/365-day period for a UUE assessment is a fallback used only when the actual period cannot be ascertained on recorded satisfaction; where ascertainable (e.g. from the date of connection) it must be used, and the period cannot predate the connection.

cases.title: Uco Bank v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.application: Under Clause 6.8(c)(iii) the assessing officer must ascertain the period of unauthorised use. Absent that finding, the period is confined to twelve months immediately preceding inspection. A demand from 1974 to 2005 with no period finding cannot stand; payments through the landlord meter must be considered on remand. Same cluster as SCJ-211.

cases.title: Aruna Bhargava v. PuVVNL & Another
cases.application: The right of appeal is a substantive right that vests when the original (here, assessment) proceedings are initiated, governed by the law then in force, and is not taken away by a later statute unless expressly or by necessary intendment; a new pre-deposit condition cannot be imposed on such a vested appeal.

lead_authorities.name: Garikapati Veeraya v. N. Subbiah Choudhry
Ramesh Singh v. Cinta Devi
Shiv Shakti Coop. Housing Society v. Swaraj Developers

cases.title: Narendra Singh Panwar v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & 2 Others
cases.application: A challenge to the vires of a Supply Code clause (here Clause 4.3(f)(v), on the ground Directors fall outside the s.2(15) 'consumer' definition) cannot be entertained where raised only in oral rejoinder submissions without any foundation laid in the writ petition itself.

cases.title: Abhinav Seva Sansthan Mahavidyalaya v. U.P. Power Corporation Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.application: A compounding/assessment amount paid without protest or contemporaneous objection cannot later be assailed as realised under coercion.

cases.title: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors. v. M/s DVS Steels & Alloys Pvt. Ltd. & Ors.
cases.application: A consumer who voluntarily pays disputed dues as a condition for obtaining a benefit (here, a fresh connection), pursuant to its own undertaking, cannot later claim a refund based on a subsequent regulatory order that merely restrains future demands, absent an express refund direction — the payment remains refundable only per the terms of the original undertaking.

cases.title: Mohd. Sagir v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.application: A consumer who was never informed of the Clause 5.6(c)(iii) testing option cannot be deemed to have waived it; waiver is an intentional act done with full knowledge of the right, and there is no presumption that everyone knows the law.

lead_authorities.name: M/s Moti Lal Padampat Sugar Mills Ltd. v. State of U.P.

cases.title: Smt. Amrawati Devi v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Anr.
cases.application: A consumer not informed of the Clause 5.6(c)(iii) option cannot be deemed to have waived it; waiver is an intentional act with full knowledge of the right, and there is no presumption that everyone knows the law.

lead_authorities.name: Moti Lal Padampat Sugar Mills Ltd. v. State of U.P.

cases.title: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Anr. v. The Electricity Ombudsman & Another
cases.court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
cases.date: 15 March 2023 (dismissed for want of prosecution; order-sheet 11.9.2012 to 15.3.2023; interim stay 17.2.2016)
cases.application: A writ pending for a decade in which the petitioner-licensee is not interested in arguing is dismissed for want of prosecution and the interim stay of the impugned order stands vacated - no merits decision, the Ombudsman's order reviving.

cases.title: Sanjay Rizvi v. M.D. Kanpur Electricity Supply Co. & Others
cases.application: The availability of a statutory appeal (s.127/Clause 6.8(d)) does not bar writ entertainment where natural justice is violated, the action is without jurisdiction, or fundamental rights are enforced — though on the facts here, the underlying technical/evidentiary controversy was left to be resolved through the departmental process rather than adjudicated directly by the writ court.

cases.title: Mohd. Sagir v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cases.application: A s.127 appeal is no bar to a writ where the assessment is challenged for violation of natural justice; alternative remedy is a rule of discretion, not an absolute bar (fundamental rights, natural justice, want of jurisdiction, vires).

lead_authorities.name: Whirlpool Corporation v. Registrar of Trade Marks, Mumbai

cases.title: Jai Laxmi Cement Company Ltd. v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cases.application: Interference with a provisional assessment despite the statutory remedy is available only within the Whirlpool exceptions (jurisdictional challenge, vires, natural justice); absent these, the writ is not entertained.

lead_authorities.name: Whirlpool Corporation v. Registrar of Trade Marks, Mumbai

cases.title: Kamil v. State of U.P. & Others
cases.application: An assessment passed in breach of natural justice falls within the Whirlpool exceptions, so the s.127 appeal is no bar to the writ; long pendency reinforced the refusal to relegate.

lead_authorities.name: Whirlpool Corporation v. Registrar of Trade Marks, Mumbai

cases.title: Satyam Shukla v. State of U.P. and 3 Others
cases.application: A writ against a Section 126 provisional assessment is entertained on the inspection-competence infirmity despite delay, unused objections, and Section 127. Seetaram Rice Mill: Section 127 lies only against a final assessment; the High Court may decide the jurisdictional/procedural point and must remand merits to the assessing officer.

lead_authorities.name: Executive Engineer v. M/s Sri Seetaram Rice Mill

cases.title: M/S Mahavir Iron Foundry And Another v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. And Others
cases.application: Extreme violation of natural justice (no show-cause before the provisional assessment) makes the writ maintainable; the consumer is not relegated to a Section 127 appeal.

cases.title: Tehri Girders Limited and another v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited and others (with R.A. Castings, Sikka Papers and connected petitions)
cases.application: A load-factor rebate given in the bill and later withdrawn becomes a 'due', so a bank-guarantee demand for that amount is permissible (unlike additional security).

cases.title: Vimal Gupta v. Executive Engineer, Dakshinanchal Electricity Dist. Nigam
cases.application: Reinforces that challenges to Supply Code assessments should ordinarily proceed through the Code's own adjudicatory mechanism rather than direct writ adjudication on the merits, with interim reconnection conditioned on partial deposit — a recurring pattern in this corpus's disconnection/reconnection interim-relief cluster.

cases.title: Parvati Devi v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Another
cases.application: A surcharge / Clause 6.5(b)(i) grievance will not be examined in writ if the consumer refuses to deposit the billed amount less the disputed surcharge, as previously directed.

cases.title: Awadhesh Pratap v. State of U.P. and Others
cases.application: On the petitioner's own showing, only Rs. 2,30,890 was paid over about 50 months of monthly ice-factory billing whose range the Court put at more than Rs. 8,000–12,000 a month (about Rs. 5–7.5 lakh). That default was treated as a reason not to enter the accounting controversy in writ.

cited_in.title: Rajendra Kumar Gupta v. DVVNL

2009 (2) AWC 1189 (DB).name: 2009 (2) AWC 1189 (DB)
2009 (2) AWC 1189 (DB).proposition: Not stated in this judgment; cited with the 2002 Code theft definition.

cited_in.title: Joginder Singh v. State of U.P. and Others
cited_in.how_treated: Held to have no relevance once the Supply Code itself was held irrelevant to the criminal revision.

A.I. Champdany Industries Ltd. (municipa.name: A.I. Champdany Industries Ltd. (municipal dues case)
A.I. Champdany Industries Ltd. (municipa.proposition: Municipal dues, being unsecured and not within the purview of Crown debt, do not have priority/charge over a company's assets on liquidation sale.

cited_in.title: Palika Towns LLP v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Distinguished — concerned unsecured municipal dues without a charge, unlike the lease deed's express first-charge clause here.

1396480.name: A.I.S.B. Officers Federation & Others v. Union of India & Others
1396480.proposition: A petitioner cannot raise mala fide allegations against persons who have not been impleaded as respondents.

cited_in.title: M/S Beeco Electrical India & Anr. v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on to the same effect.

A.K. Kraipak & Ors. v. Union of India an.name: A.K. Kraipak & Ors. v. Union of India and others
A.K. Kraipak & Ors. v. Union of India an.proposition: Principles of natural justice supplement the statute; an opportunity of hearing is required even where the statute is silent.

cited_in.title: M/S Mahavir Iron Foundry And Another v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. And Others
cited_in.how_treated: Applied with Ashok Kumar for the holding that no show-cause before the provisional assessment violated natural justice.

1353689.name: A.R. Antulay v. R.S. Nayak and 38 further authorities on statutory interpretation, precedent (sub silentio/per incuriam), vires of delegated legislation, and harmonious construction (incl. Kunj Behari Lal Butail v. State of H.P.; Global Energy Ltd. v. CERC; State of T.N. v. P. Krishnamurthy; J.K. Cotton Spinning & Weaving Mills v. State of U.P.; PTC India v. CERC)
1353689.proposition: General canons of statutory interpretation and administrative law (reading a statute as a whole vs. section-by-section; ultra vires/consistency of subordinate legislation with the parent Act; precedential weight of a decision not engaging a specific provision) cited in support of the rival vires arguments.

cited_in.title: Kisan Cold Storage & Ice Factory v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors. (Full Bench reference)
cited_in.how_treated: Not individually discussed — the Court held the text of Section 42(5)-(7) and Rule 7 to be clear and unambiguous, so canvassing the case law would 'unnecessarily burden' the judgment.

A.V. Venkateswaran, Collector of Customs.name: A.V. Venkateswaran, Collector of Customs v. Ramchand Sobhraj Wadhwani
A.V. Venkateswaran, Collector of Customs.proposition: The exceptions to the alternative-remedy rule are not exhaustive; a discretion vests in the High Court to entertain a petition and grant relief notwithstanding an adequate alternative remedy.

cited_in.title: Mohd. Sagir v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Noticed within the quoted Whirlpool extract.

cited_in.title: M/S Mayur Sheetgrah Pvt. Ltd. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. And Others
cited_in.how_treated: Noticed within the quoted Whirlpool extract.

1358956.name: Abdul Gani & Anr. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
1358956.citation: Civil Misc. Writ Petition No. 15498 of 2008
1358956.proposition: An assessment made only on the allegation of a tampered meter seal, without any evidence of how the seal was tampered or theft was effected, cannot stand.

cited_in.title: M/S Beeco Electrical India & Anr. v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Distinguished on facts — unlike Abdul Gani, here there was affirmative evidence (naked conductor, MRI anomalies) of the manner of theft.

Abdus Salam @ A. Salam v. Election Commi.name: Abdus Salam @ A. Salam v. Election Commission of India
Abdus Salam @ A. Salam v. Election Commi.proposition: There is nothing rigid about natural justice; the duty to hear does not always mean affording a personal hearing.

cited_in.title: Hazi Mohd. Yaseen v. P.V.V.N.L. & Another
cited_in.how_treated: Referred (respondent's line).

Abhimanyu Mazumdar v. Superintending Eng.name: Abhimanyu Mazumdar v. Superintending Engineer
Abhimanyu Mazumdar v. Superintending Eng.proposition: A person in settled possession is entitled to electricity.

cited_in.title: Neelam Gupta v. Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Ltd.
cited_in.how_treated: Court noted the view (judgment dated 11 February 2011) but held the settled-possession controversy could not be resolved because the petitioner herself obstructed spot inspection.

ABL International Ltd. & Anr. v. Export.name: ABL International Ltd. & Anr. v. Export Credit Guarantee Corporation of India Ltd. & Ors.
ABL International Ltd. & Anr. v. Export.proposition: A writ petition against the State or its instrumentality arising out of a contractual obligation is maintainable, and a consequential monetary claim does not bar it; but the High Court imposes self-restraint and will normally not exercise the power unless the action is arbitrary or unreasonable in violation of Article 14.

cited_in.title: M/s. Shree Gopala Iron (India) Ltd. & Anr. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Referred.

Additional District Magistrate (Rev.), D.name: Additional District Magistrate (Rev.), Delhi Admn. v. Siri Ram
Additional District Magistrate (Rev.), D.proposition: Conferment of rule-making power does not enable the delegate to make rules travelling beyond, inconsistent with, or repugnant to the enabling Act.

cited_in.title: Kerala State Electricity Board & Ors. v. Thomas Joseph Alias Thomas M.J. & Ors. (with connected appeals)
cited_in.how_treated: Followed.

Adesh Kumar Jain v. U.P. State Electrici.name: Adesh Kumar Jain v. U.P. State Electricity Board
Adesh Kumar Jain v. U.P. State Electrici.proposition: Directors of a company cannot be made personally liable for the company's electricity dues unless the director gives an undertaking or personal guarantee for recovery from his personal assets.

cited_in.title: Sri Piyush Kumar v. State of U.P. Thru' Secretary Lucknow And Others
cited_in.how_treated: Followed.

Ahmedabad Electricity Co. Ltd. v. Gujara.name: Ahmedabad Electricity Co. Ltd. v. Gujarat Inns (P) Ltd.
Ahmedabad Electricity Co. Ltd. v. Gujara.proposition: Past electricity dues are not a charge over the property; the auction-purchaser may seek supply of energy without being saddled with the previous owner's dues.

cited_in.title: Raman Ispat (Pvt.) Ltd. & Anr. v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Ors.
cited_in.how_treated: Cited by the petitioner alongside Isha Marbles; not applied to defeat the licensee's stipulation given DUS Steels.

28246.name: Ahmedabad Electricity Co. Ltd. v. Gujarat Inns Pvt. Ltd. & Ors.
28246.proposition: In the absence of any statutory provision, an auction-purchaser applying for a fresh connection cannot be fastened with the previous owner's electricity dues, and a fresh connection cannot be denied on that ground.

cited_in.title: Chandra Prakash Gupta v. State of U.P. & 3 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Distinguished — held inapplicable after Clause 4.1 of the 2005 Code supplied the statutory provision it presupposed to be absent.

cited_in.title: M/S Dharti Agro Industries Pvt. Ltd. v. The Managing Director, Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & 2 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Relied on by the petitioner as foundational auction-purchaser precedent.

cited_in.title: Special Officer, Commerce, North Eastern Electricity Company of Orissa (NESCO) & Anr. v. M/s Raghunath Paper Mills Private Limited & Anr.
cited_in.how_treated: Followed.

1638274.name: Ajit Singh @ Muraha v. State of U.P. & Others
1638274.proposition: Reiterates the Bhajan Lal/Satya Pal standard that FIR quashing/stay of arrest is warranted only where no cognizable offence is ex-facie discernible or a statutory restriction on investigation exists.

cited_in.title: Pawan Kumar Laur v. State of U.P. & Others
cited_in.how_treated: Followed as the controlling Full Bench authority.

Ajmer Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Rahama.name: Ajmer Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Rahamatullah Khan
Ajmer Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Rahama.proposition: Invoked in the reproduced 17.1.2024 order for the contention that dues more than two years old cannot be recovered under Section 56.

cited_in.title: Madan Kumar Vishkerma v. State of U.P. & 4 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Cited by the petitioner in the earlier writ quoted in the 22.1.2025 listing; not applied in this disposal.

139734870.name: Aleque Padamsee & Others v. Union of India & Others
139734870.proposition: Where the police fail to act on information about a cognizable offence, the remedy is to file a complaint before the Magistrate under s.190/200 Cr.P.C., not a writ petition seeking a direction to register an FIR.

cited_in.title: Shiv Murti Yadav v. State of U.P. & 6 Others
cited_in.how_treated: Applied to hold the revisionist had no separate ground for interference given this remedy.

316379.name: Bombay Electric Supply and Transport Undertaking v. Laffans (India) Pvt. Ltd. & Anr.

cited_in.how_treated: Applied by analogy to hold that s.162 of the Electricity Act, 2003 is the modern successor forum for such meter-accuracy disputes (companion citation to SCJ-083).

1029167.proposition: Where a body performs both advisory/regulatory and adjudicatory functions, it may be appropriate (though a matter for legislative wisdom) to create two separate bodies.
